title: An Inductorless Downconversion Mixer with 24.2-dB CG, 8.2-dB NF, 350-μW Power, and 50-Hz Flicker-Noise Corner Frequency at -5-dBm LO.
abstract: This paper presents an inductorless downconversion mixer that achieves high conversion gain, low noise, and an ultra-low flicker-noise corner frequency with sub-mW power consumption. Designed and laid out in a 65-nm CMOS, the proposed architecture reuses current in complementary branches and employs a dedicated current-bleeding path whose noise is actively canceled by the switching devices. Thus, the presented structure achieves low noise while facilitating high gain performance. Moreover, by turning off the switches at local oscillator (LO) zero crossings, both direct and indirect flicker-noise mechanisms are attenuated without requiring inductors. Post-layout simulations at 2.4 GHz show a conversion gain of 24.2 dB, a noise figure of 8.2 dB with a flicker noise corner frequency of ~50 Hz, an IIP3 of −20 dBm, while operating with a −5-dBm LO, from a 1.5-V supply and consuming 350 μW. The design has compact active area of 0.0234 mm2.

title: Exploration of a Multi-Bit TDC-based PLL-SAR ADC with Dynamic Settling.
abstract: This paper investigates a phase-locked loop (PLL)-based successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC), referred to as the PLL-SAR—a time-domain architecture that operates similarly to a digital PLL (DPLL). It proposes and analyzes a dynamic settling scheme inspired by ring amplifiers to accelerate settling speed, and it shows how output filtering can improve accuracy when longer conversion times are allowed. These techniques are demonstrated through VerilogA-based simulations.

title: Variability Aware Design of Memristor-based Gene Implementation in Cellular Neural Networks.
abstract: As conventional computers based on von Neumann architecture approach their physical and performance limits, unconventional computing paradigms such as Cellular Neural Networks (CellNNs) have emerged as promising platforms for real-time, massively parallel analog computation. However, conventional analog CellNNs suffer from scalability and power constraints due to large cell hardware overhead. This work investigates the integration of memristor-based crossbar arrays into CellNN architectures to address these limitations by exploiting their analog tunability, high density, and low power operation. A 1-Transistor-1-Memristor (1T1R) crossbar is proposed for implementing the coupling weights defining the CellNN gene. Device nonlinearity, asymmetry and stochastic variability are incorporated using the physics-based JART VCM memristor model, enabling accurate mapping of target weights onto memristor conductances through numerical optimization and differential-pair encoding. Simulations of edge detection tasks confirm high functional accuracy and robustness, while Monte Carlo analysis reveals variability’s impact, underscoring the need for variability-aware design of reliable memristor-CNN hardware.

title: An ISFET Pixel Array with Random Access Analog Floating-Gate Calibration.
abstract: We have designed an 8×8 CMOS micro sensor array comprised of ISFET pixels and photo pixels. The ISFETs’ floating gates store analog bias/calibration charge and are individually programmable by bi-directional Fowler–Nordheim tunneling, thus enabling fixed pattern noise compensation and point of operation adaptation. We present 1) silicon verification of the ISFET pixel’s core on a first 180nm CMOS test chip, and 2) the design of the array that is in production on a second chip. That chip measures 1520×1520μm, and the pixel pitch is 80μm.

title: Wideband Cartesian RF-DAC-Based Predistorter using Nonlinear RF-DACs and IQ Expansion.
abstract: We here present an RF-DAC-based PD featuring IQ expansion, a linearization concept using segmented non-linear RF-DACs combined with increased expansion in the IQ direction. The proposed predistorter, realized within the RF-DACs themselves, is very hardware efficient, only requiring a small amount of additional hardware compared to a conventional RF-DAC. The proposed RF-DAC-based PD, realized in a 22nm CMOS technology, is used to linearize a PA integrated on the same chip. With IQ expansion, we measure a peak compression ripple of ±0.2dB across the full range with a peak output power <2.3dB below the PA Psat. Modulated measurements with up to 4GSym/s 64QAM SC signals show an EVM <4.05% and ACPR <−30.1dBc, achieving an EVM improvement of >0.3percent unit.

title: Low-Complexity and Resource-Efficient Design of a Streaming Channel Estimation for ZP-OTFS.
abstract: This work presents a low-complexity and resource-efficient hardware architecture for Channel Estimation (CE) in Zero-Padded Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (ZP-OTFS) systems. The proposed design reconstructs the channel impulse response in the delay–time domain through a partially parallel interpolation scheme, enabling continuous streaming while exploiting matrix sparsity to reduce computational overhead. The architecture is implemented at the Register Transfer Level (RTL) in VHDL, with functional validation performed via FPGA-in-the-Loop (FIL). A prototype on the AMD ZCU111 board demonstrates high efficiency in terms of area and power, with 44.10μs latency and 1.45μJ per-frame energy, quantifying performance unavailable in prior SDR-only implementations. These results confirm the suitability of the proposed architecture for integration into complete OTFS receivers that target high-mobility wireless communication scenarios.

title: EvoGabor: Hierarchical Clustering and Evolutionary Algorithms for Area-Power Efficient Gabor Design.
abstract: This paper introduces EvoGabor, a hardware-efficient approach for implementing Gabor filters (GFs) in resource-constrained medical image processing applications. While GFs effectively extract orientation- and frequency-selective features, they require high-precision multipliers, making implementation computationally demanding. To address this problem, We propose an evolutionary optimization framework that explores different precision levels for Gabor kernel coefficients, reducing hardware complexity while preserving image quality measured by Structural Similarity Index (SSIM). We quantized the original full-precision fixed-point 16 (FI-16) bit coefficients with graded precision to significantly reduce dynamic power consumption, silicon footprint, and design delay. Additionally, we employ clustering techniques to reduce the effective dimensionality of Gabor kernels, thereby reducing hardware redundancy and enabling kernel reuse. The proposed architecture, characterized on standard-cell synthesized in NANDgate 45 nm PDK, reported area and power savings of 79% and 6%, respectively, compared to the conventional baseline FI-16 precision-based GF architecture. This work successfully bridges the gap between algorithmic accuracy and hardware feasibility by combining optimization strategies with architectural simplification. The hardware design files are made freely available for further usage to the research and design community.

title: Fast Frequency Response of Distribution Feeders Equipped with CIGs: An MRAC Based Approach.
abstract: The renewable energy source-fueled grid-following and/or grid-forming converter-interfaced generators in distribution feeders allow the provision of fast frequency response.Their contribution to this ancillary service can differ from the wanted one since converter-interfaced generators may not be always available and they are spread in the feeder, leading to different contributions to a power disturbance.To achieve the desired fast frequency response at the point of common coupling, it is necessary to implement a proper control strategy to dynamically regulate the inertia and load damping contributions by at least a subset of converter-interfaced generators.This paper proposes a strategy based on a direct model reference adaptive controller (MRAC) to achieve this target.To evaluate the performance of the proposed controller, simulation results obtained by applying it to a modified version of the IEEE 13-node feeder are presented.

title: A Fast TX/RX Switching Power Management Unit with Capless Sink/Source LDO for Heterogeneous mmWave Phased Arrays.
abstract: This paper proposes a fast TX/RX switching power management unit (PMU) for mmWave phased array heterogeneous chiplet integration. The chip supports fast TX/RX power switching for decreasing power consumption in a time division duplex (TDD) system with a switching time of less than 300 ns, satisfying the 5G New Radio TDD standard. It can control 4 GaN transceivers, enabling PMU and GaN transceiver integration for 24 GHz half-wavelength placement. The chip combines the gate biasing ranging from -3.4 to -1.7 V, with a 10 mA bidirectional current capability, and drain biasing up to 15 V 100 mA for the GaN HEMT power supply in a 180 nm BCD process. The Gate bias is implemented with a capless sink/source LDO with adaptive biasing frequency compensation. The LDO exhibits a voltage droop of 380 mV for a step of -2 to 4 mA with a 20 ns edge time, and the settling time is 150 ns. Its start-up time is less than 270 ns. Drain bias is provided by a PMOS high-side load switch with an on/off time of less than 300 ns.

title: Live Demonstration: A Portable Pressure Imaging System for Convenient and Ubiquitous Lumbar Disc Herniation Screening.
abstract: Early screening for lumbar disc herniation (LDH) remains challenging due to the high cost and limited accessibility of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). To address this issue, we develop an automated screening system based on seated biomechanical analysis, capable of performing seated pressure acquisition, feature analysis, and LDH risk assessment. The system first captures a pressure map of the user’s buttocks in a standardized seated posture using a custom-designed, highly sensitive flexible pressure array. Mechanical and statistical features that characterize seated asymmetry and balance are then extracted from the pressure map. These features are subsequently fed into a trained machine learning model to predict and display risk assessment results. This approach enables large-scale, low-cost lumbar health screening and provides a practical tool for the early detection of LDH risk. Key technical specifications of the system are as follows: sensor dimensions: 40 cm × 40 cm; array configuration: 32 × 32; measurement range: 1 – 50 kg; sampling frame rate: 3.3 fps; prediction duration: 30 s; weight: 2 kg; thickness:100Ω. A demo video of the proposed pressure imaging system, including recordings of both real-world usage and screen output, is available at: https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.30225178

title: Screening of Lumbar Disc Herniation Using Buttock Pressure Imaging System.
abstract: Lumbar disc herniation (LDH) diagnosis relies on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which is costly and not widely accessible. This paper presents a cost-effective screening alternative based on buttock pressure distribution. We develop a custom flexible pressure imaging system with a novel parallel readout circuit, which is validated to exhibit high linearity (R2=0.999), excellent spatial consistency, and stable performance over 1,000 loading cycles. Using this system, buttock pressure distribution characteristics (PDC) are modeled by an α-stable distribution to extract features quantifying asymmetry (β), center (μ), and dispersion (σ). These features are used to train a classifier that achieved 85.71% accuracy in identifying LDH on a clinical cohort.

title: Urban Traffic Short-Term Flow Prediction Based on the Fusion of Multiple Correlations.
abstract: To accurately model the influence of diverse spatiotemporal correlations in complex traffic networks, this study proposes an adaptive feature aggregation mechanism that integrates multi-level node representations for enhanced traffic flow prediction. The method effectively captures intricate spatiotemporal dependencies by jointly modeling path-wise correlations among road segments, inter-segment feature relationships, and regional spatial associations. Specifically, a unified framework incorporating path transitivity, regional spatial dependencies, and road segment features is designed to fully exploit traffic flow characteristics across multiple scales. Experiments on the SUMO-SY and Taxi-BJ datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing baselines. It achieves approximately 12.9% and 14.0% improvements in RMSE and MAE on the SUMO-SY dataset, respectively, and yields a 1.3% enhancement in MAE on the Taxi-BJ dataset, indicating strong robustness and generalization across different traffic scenarios.

title: A Single-Stage Class-AB OTA with 100-dB Gain Driving 20-pF to 8-nF Capacitive Loads.
abstract: This work presents a single-stage operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) with high DC gain for driving nano-farad capacitive loads. The circuit employs two conjugated current mirrors to form high-impedance nodes, enhancing transconductance and driving capability. Flipped-voltage follower (FVF) cells act as variable tail current sources to boost transconductance and generate a dynamic current larger than the bias current during slewing, enabling a faster transient response. The FVFs also allow additional folded drivers on the cascode stage for further improvement. To integrate these techniques, both n- and p-channel differential pairs are used at the input. Implemented in TSMC 0.18-μm CMOS, the OTA achieved a simulated DC gain above 100 dB and a measured gain of 95 dB, validating the proposed design. It shows a unity-gain bandwidth of 5.85 MHz and a slew rate of 0.347 V/μs while driving a 2×4 nF load at 1.8 V.

title: Triple-Packed Posit MAC: Low-Bitwidth Inference via Tri-Product DSP48E2 Overpacking for CNNs.
abstract: We present Triple-Packed Posit MAC, an FPGA accelerator that packs Xilinx UltraScale+ DSP48E2 blocks to execute three exact 4-bit posit multiplications per cycle, tripling throughput while using only one DSP. The design supports Posit(8,1), Posit(8,2), and Posit(8,3) with just 14 LUTs for carry correction. Integrated into a matrix-multiplication and convolution pipeline on a ZCU104 board, it targets LeNet-5 inference on MNIST. Compared to a baseline posit engine, this approach reduces LUT usage by 25%, frees two DSPs per MAC, and increases convolution-layer MAC throughput by 3× with identical accuracy. RMSE analysis shows Posit(8,1) is within 0.02 of FP16 for 3-MAC operations, and layer-level RMSE remains under 0.5 for both Conv2D and Dense layers. In MNIST inference, Posit(8,1) achieves FP32 Top-1 accuracy within 0.3% (90.5% vs. 90.8%) and 99% Top-5 accuracy. This demonstrates up to 3× higher compute density and 15–25% logic savings without compromising numerical fidelity.

title: Probabilistic Sensing: Intelligence in Data Sampling.
abstract: Extending the intelligence of sensors to the data-acquisition process - deciding whether to sample or not - can result in transformative energy-efficiency gains. However, making such a decision in a deterministic manner involves risk of losing information. Here we present a sensing paradigm that enables making such a decision in a probabilistic manner. The paradigm takes inspiration from the autonomous nervous system and employs a probabilistic neuron (p-neuron) driven by an analog feature extraction circuit. The response time of the system is on the order of microseconds, over-coming the sub-sampling-rate response time limit and enabling real-time intelligent autonomous activation of data-sampling. Validation experiments on active seismic survey data demonstrate lossless probabilistic data acquisition, with a normalized mean squared error of 0.41%, and 93% saving in the active operation time of the system and the number of generated samples.

title: Double-Clock Architecture for Small-Duty-Cycle DC-DC Converters.
abstract: Many applications pose stringent requirements on the voltage-conversion-ratio (VCR) that a DC-DC converter should cover, requiring it to reliably synthesize very small duty-cycles. One of such applications is the power management of Li-ion battery powered Active Matrix Organic Light Emitting Diode (AMOLED) displays. In this article a double-clock architecture for current-mode DC-DC converters is proposed, which guarantees high-quality regulated rails. By means of a small-signal model it is shown that the proposed architecture also provides benefits in terms of jitter sensitivity. Measurements of a fabricated boost converter in a 180nm technology validate the architecture.

title: Adaptive Federated Learning Defense Against Byzantine Attacks and Concept Drift in IIoT.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative intrusion detection in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments without compromising data privacy. However, FL systems face critical challenges from Byzantine attacks, where malicious clients send poisoned model updates, and concept drift, where data distributions evolve over time. Existing defenses typically force a trade-off between security and efficiency, employing either computationally expensive robust aggregation methods or fast but vulnerable approaches. This paper proposes an adaptive defense framework that dynamically responds to the threat landscape using lightweight statistical detection mechanisms. The system defaults to efficient Federated Averaging (FedAvg) aggregation and switches to robust methods only when attacks or drift are detected. We validated the framework through experiments on the Edge-IIoTset dataset and real-world deployment on five Raspberry Pi 3B devices. Results show the adaptive approach maintains F1=0.828 under 40% malicious clients and remains robust up to the 50% threshold.

title: LiDAR-based Framework for Detecting Suspicious Human Activities.
abstract: This study explores the development of Human Activity Recognition (HAR) systems capable of identifying suspicious activities to enhance security in public spaces. We propose an innovative solution that integrates LiDAR sensors with deep learning technologies. Our method employs advanced models operating on LiDAR point cloud, PV-RCNN for human detection, and LidarGait++ for classifying activities into categories such as standing or walking (non-suspicious) and sneaking or fighting (suspicious). Due to the scarcity of suitable real-world datasets for training such systems, we utilize a 3D simulation tool, Blender, to create realistic environments and generate labeled point cloud data. This synthetic dataset allows us to train our models effectively under controlled yet near-realistic conditions. Preliminary results from this approach are promising, demonstrating accurate localization and classification of human activities and highlighting the potential of our system to contribute significantly to proactive security measures.

title: Efficient On-the-Fly Twiddle Factor Generation for Falcon PQC NTT/INTT.
abstract: Efficient hardware implementations are crucial for post-quantum cryptography (PQC) algorithms like FALCON. A key challenge in FALCON key generation is performing polynomial modular multiplications using the Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) across hundreds of prime moduli. Conventional designs precompute and store twiddle factors (TFs) in ROM, demanding substantial on-chip memory. This paper proposes an on-the-fly TF generation architecture for FALCON-oriented NTTs supporting multiple polynomial sizes. The design significantly reduces ROM storage, cutting memory by 99%, area by 95%, and power by 87%, while achieving a higher frequency of 500 MHz with only 3.82 mW power consumption and no latency penalty. The proposed approach enables scalable, full-hardware deployment of FALCON in ASIC implementations.

title: A 6.5nV/√Hz Chopper Stabilized Amplifier with Dead-Time Ripple Compensation (DT-RC) Technique for Precision Data Acquisition.
abstract: This paper presents a high-precision, energy-efficient capacitively-coupled chopper gain amplifier (CCGA) employing a novel dead-time ripple correction (DT-RC) technique. The proposed DT-RC scheme significantly enhances attenuation of offset-induced ripple and output drift while introducing minimal area and zero power overhead. By strategically implementing switch-based dead-time control, the technique effectively suppresses the dominant first-stage offset without compromising noise performance. Implemented in a 180 nm CMOS process, the amplifier operates from a 1.8 V supply while consuming 0.5 mA current. Measurement results demonstrate an input-referred noise density of 6.5 nV/√Hz and a competitive noise efficiency factor (NEF) of 3, establishing the proposed architecture as a compelling solution for high-precision, low-power sensor interface applications.

title: A 3-day ASIC Design Hands-on with the Minimal Fab.
abstract: Because ASIC design and fabrication require substantial cost and long lead times, they are not suitable for student laboratory courses; this has become one reason the number of students aspiring to enter the semiconductor field has not grown. Using a short-turn, low-cost Structured-ASIC design and fabrication approach we call the Agile-Chip Platform, we proposed a student experiment that can be completed quickly and inexpensively, and we piloted an exercise to design and fabricate a simple ring oscillator. Although this experiment requires relatively little knowledge of electronic circuits and allows students to easily experience chip implementation, it remains far from the full design process of a practical digital IC. In this paper, we report on an experiment in which we used the Agile-Chip Platform to implement digital logic circuits on a gate array, connect them to an embedded RISC-V CPU, and build a small-scale system-on-a-chip (SoC) that can be powered on and functionally verified. The circuits to be implemented on the gate array can be designed using a standard flow — from HDL description, through logic synthesis, to automatic layout. Because the current Agile-Chip Platform performs interconnect wiring using only five metal layers, some challenges arise during the automatic routing stage; however, these can be resolved with a few hours of work. In a trial conducted in August 2025, six participants independently designed and implemented their own circuits within three days. Two weeks later, the packaged chips were tested on a dedicated debug board, and five different chips were confirmed to operate as designed.

title: Training slow silicon neurons to control extremely fast robots with spiking reinforcement learning.
abstract: Air hockey demands split-second decisions at high puck velocities, a challenge we address with a compact network of spiking neurons running on a mixed-signal analog/digital neuromorphic processor. By co-designing hardware and learning algorithms, we train the system to achieve successful puck interactions through reinforcement learning in a remarkably small number of trials. The network leverages fixed random connectivity to capture the task's temporal structure and adopts a local e-prop learning rule in the readout layer to exploit event-driven activity for fast and efficient learning. The result is real-time learning with a setup comprising a computer and the neuromorphic chip in-the-loop, enabling practical training of spiking neural networks for robotic autonomous systems. This work bridges neuroscience-inspired hardware with real-world robotic control, showing that brain-inspired approaches can tackle fast-paced interaction tasks while supporting always-on learning in intelligent machines.

title: Efficient VLSI Architecture for Finding Maximum Value and Its Corresponding Index.
abstract: This paper proposes an area and power-efficient VLSI architecture for finding the maximum value from an array of inputs using bitwise parallel AND (BPA) operations. The proposed BPA architecture has a fixed critical delay path independent of input size, ensuring a scalable operating frequency, with a trade-off in latency compared to existing architectures. ASIC synthesis results show that the proposed BPA design achieves a reduction of 6% to 13% in area delay product and 10% to 21% in power delay product for 16-bit and 6-bit fixed-point implementations, respectively. These results confirm that BPA architecture provides improved efficiency with lower area and power consumption compared to state-of-the-art designs.

title: An ASIC Implementation of a Generalized Galois RO-PUF for Edge Device Identification.
abstract: This work presents the preliminary results from the first ASIC implementation of a Physically Unclonable Function (PUF) based on Generalized Galois Ring Oscillators (GenGAROs) designed for device identification in edge computing environments. The GenGARO-PUF presents no spatial correlations, unlike the conventional Ring Oscillator PUF (RO-PUF), making this proposal more resistant to modeling attacks. Two PUFs with GenGAROs of 3 and 11 stages have have been full-custom designed in ASIC 65 nm CMOS technology. The proposed PUF has been experimentally tested in terms of uniqueness, uniformity, identifiability and reliability facing voltage and temperature variations. Experimental results show a near-ideal uniqueness (average inter-HD higher than 49 %), high reliability (above 98 % in the worst case scenario), and a uniformity close to 50 %. Furthermore, an Equal Error Rate (EER) on the order of 10-15has been achieved in both cases. We will demonstrate that this proposal also outperforms other ASIC and FPGA-based PUF solutions reported in the literature. Moreover, the results confirm the feasibility of ASIC-based GenGARO-PUFs as a root-of-trust for edge authentication.

title: A 10-bit 6.4-GS/s Current Steering DAC with -163.7 dBm/Hz Noise Spectral Density for DPD-Based D-Band Backhaul Transmitters.
abstract: This paper presents a 6.4-GS/s digital-to-analog converter (DAC) designed for D-band backhaul transmitters employing digital pre-distortion (DPD). A comprehensive noise analysis to optimize the DAC performance within the noise-power trade-off is proposed; in addition, optimal segmentation selection is discussed to address dynamic linearity under area and digital complexity constraints. The DAC was fabricated in a 55-nm BiCMOS process, and both experimental and post-layout Monte Carlo results are presented. With a 10-bit resolution, it achieves a -163.7-dBm/Hz noise spectral density (NSD), measured at 1 GHz. The DAC SFDR is >51.2 dBc, while its IM3 is <-60.6 dBc. With a state-of-the-art 22-mW total power consumption, the proposed DAC achieves a remarkable figure-of-merit (FoM) of 194 PHz/W.

title: Stereo-NeRF: Efficient Stereo Neural Rendering via Feature Reuse.
abstract: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) achieve high-fidelity view synthesis, making them highly desired for Augmented Reality applications. However, current NeRF implementations remain computationally and memory challenging for real-time use on low-power hardware. We present Stereo-NeRF, a stereo feature caching approach that reuses grid-encoded features between stereo viewpoints in Instant-NGP, avoiding redundant hash-grid evaluations. By leveraging spatial and sampling locality between adjacent camera views, Stereo-NeRF reduces encoder computation and memory traffic by up to 52%, corresponding to higher estimated frame rate and lower energy per frame. Across NeRF-Synthetic scenes, the method maintains perceptual similarity with mean ΔLPIPS (Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity) [1] ≈ 0.05 and scene-dependent ΔPSNR (Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio) of 1–6dB, demonstrating a practical path toward real-time, energy-efficient neural rendering on Augmented- and Virtual-Reality and mobile platforms.

title: A 4 nW 114 dB DR Electrochemical Sensing Interface IC with Digital-Intensive Regulation Loop.
abstract: This paper introduces an ultra-low-power amplifier-less front-end architecture for amperometric electrochemical sensing. The proposed architecture can simultaneously regulate the potential difference between the required electrodes and perform current readout for an electrochemical sensor. A dual-side potentiostat regulation loop comprising dynamic latched comparators in conjunction with digital loop filters and current-steering DACs is proposed, with its detailed operation discussed in this paper. Implemented in a standard 180 nm CMOS process, this design achieves a current measurement range of 114.3 dB. It can operate over a wide range of sampling frequencies FS (100 Hz ~ 100 MHz) and supply voltages (1 V ~ 1.8 V). The whole interface IC consumes only 3.50 nA current at 1.2 V supply at a clock frequency of 1-kHz.

title: Accurate and Efficient Seizure Prediction Using Legendre Memory Units.
abstract: This study introduces an LMU-based model for seizure prediction using scalp EEG signals. It captures long-term patterns with minimum parameters and is comprised of EEG preprocessing, spectral feature extraction, and LMU-based classification of preictal and interictal states. Using data from eight patients in the CHB-MIT EEG database, preictal segments (30 minutes before seizures) and equal-length interictal samples were analyzed. The model reached 95.92% sensitivity and a 0.0833 false detection rate, matching or surpassing CNN and LSTM models with lower complexity. These results show the LMU’s promise for lightweight, real-time seizure prediction in portable or implantable devices.

title: An Elzakker Dynamic Comparator with Improved Speed and Rejection to Meta-Stability.
abstract: Elzakker dynamic comparator is a well-known low voltage comparator with fine trade-off between power and speed. The speed and rejection to meta-stability are improved in the proposed one, which incorporates a pair of second latches and minimizes the turn-on time. Taking a comparison delay of 500ps as the criterion, with an input of 0.1 μV, the probability of meta-stability is 100 percent for the classic Elzakker dynamic comparator, but is just 1.4 percent for the proposed one.

title: Live Demonstration: Low-Power Wearable System for Real-Time Myopia Prevention and Monitoring.
abstract: Myopia is a growing public health issue, especially among children and adolescents. We demonstrate a wearable smart device that monitors reading distance, ambient light, and head posture using integrated digital sensors. The system is built on a low-power CC2640R2L MCU with 16 Mbit flash for storing 6300 records and BLE communication for stable data transfer within 10 m. A vibration motor provides real-time reminders to correct unhealthy eye behaviors, while a WeChat miniprogram enables data visualization and personalized settings. With 66 hours of continuous operation and up to 13 days standby, the device offers flexible forms such as smart glasses and handheld sticks,showing strong potential for collaborative myopia prevention and daily monitoring. The demo video is available at: https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.30338845.v1.

title: A Low-Power, High-Resolution Capacitance to Digital Conversion Mechanism for Invasive attacks.
abstract: Micro-probing is an invasive attack that targets smart devices, such as IoT (Internet of Things) devices and similar low-power devices, to extract sensitive information from their on-chip data wires and inject faults to change their functionality. In this study, a new approach for detecting micro-probing using capacitance changes is presented, i.e., a capacitance-to-digital conversion mechanism. In this method, capacitance variations are detected by monitoring the amplifier’s higher cut-off frequency in two phases. In the first phase, the higher cut-off frequency is detected. The second phase converts the detected frequency to a digital quantity. The required readout building blocks are discussed, and the results are verified using post-layout simulations in TSMC 180nm CMOS process, with a power consumption of 13.42μW from a 1.8V power supply, and a minimum detectable capacitance of 100aF. In addition, Monte Carlo simulation results showcase mismatch variations and noise analysis to prove its reliability. The proposed architecture is a promising candidate for low-power, portable, capacitive sensors and invasive-attack detection applications.

title: A stimulus-free foreground calibration technique for correction of feedback DAC element mismatch in ∆Σ-A/D converters.
abstract: Element mismatch in the feedback DAC of multi-bit ∆Σ analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) severely degrades linearity and elevates the in-band noise floor. Prior calibration approaches typically rely on spectrally pure full-scale sinusoidal excitation, which is challenging to generate on-chip or a full-scale out-of-band sinusoidal signal with relaxed spectral purity requirements. In addition, the full-scale sinusoidal signal may introduce additional non-linearities from the loop filter and quantizer. This work introduces a stimulus-free foreground calibration technique that enables accurate estimation and correction of DAC element mismatches even under idle channel conditions. By leveraging pseudo-random element randomization and a variance-minimization algorithm, the proposed method avoids external tones, reduces hardware overhead, and ensures robust convergence. Simulation results on a 4-level 4th-order ∆Σ modulator demonstrate full recovery of SNDR from 67 dB (with 0.5% element mismatch) to the ideal 84 dB, confirming the efficacy and practical viability of the approach.

title: On the Degradation of Alias Rejection in Continuous-time Incremental ∆Σ Modulators.
abstract: This paper discusses about the degradation of alias rejection in continuous-time incremental delta sigma modulator (CTIDSM). It is shown that the prized property of inherent anti-aliasing in continuous-time delta sigma modulator (CTDSM) degrades when it is operated in incremental mode. The paper presents a detailed mathematical analysis deriving the signal transfer function (STF) of CTDSM and CTIDSM. It further discusses the influence of potential aliased tones on the in-band performance of the modulator. The analysis is supported by behavioral and transistor level simulations of CTIDSM using CMOS 65 nm process. Measurement results from a fabricated CTIDSM are also presented to validate the observations made regarding degradation of alias rejection property in CTIDSM.

title: No Gate-keeping: Teaching Novice Engineering Students To Build a CPU on FPGA.
abstract: Computing today is an integral part of engineering, and an understanding of how a computer works at a low level is imperative to utilize computing to its fullest extent. As such, many students choose to pursue a minor or second major in Computing to augment their skills. We introduce CS2100DE Computer Organization, a 13-week course designed for such engineering students with no background in electrical engineering other than introductory Python programming. The course teaches the basics of digital design and computer organization, culminating in a project where students implement their own functional CPU on a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) board. We present the assessment results from this course, as well as feedback from students, to demonstrate the effectiveness of the course in achieving the desired learning outcomes.

title: Adiabatic Energy-Recycling Charge-Redistribution Array for Ultra-Low Power Massively Parallel Cross-Correlation.
abstract: We present a mixed-signal Compute-in-Memory (CIM) circuit for XNOR-and-Accumulate (XAC) that uses adiabatic charge redistribution to reduce switching loss and noise while recycling energy during computation. For bipolar 256-dimensional vectors in 22nm fully depleted silicon-on-insulator (FD-SOI) simulations, the array core achieves an energy efficiency exceeding 1500 TOPS/W at 29.1aJ per XAC and supports 8-bit quantization. The cell comprises 14 minimum-size transistors and two small unit capacitor, yielding a compact, energy-efficient, and high-throughput solution suitable for AI and signal-processing tasks in power- and thermal-constrained settings.

title: A 0.3-nA Quiescent Current CMOS-Only Undervoltage Lockout Circuit with Dual-Mode Operation for Energy Harvesting Systems.
abstract: We propose an ultra-low-power, CMOS-only under-voltage lockout (UVLO) circuit designed for energy-harvesting applications. The proposed UVLO operates in a dual-mode configuration, which is essential for energy-autonomous power switching converters, while consuming significantly less area and power compared to conventional bandgap-based UVLOs that require multiple resistors and BJTs. The design is fabricated in a 0.18 µm CMOS technology and occupies an active area of 0.0066 mm2. The measured low-to-high trip voltage (LHTV1) and high-to-low trip voltage (HLTV1) for the first mode are 1.362 V and 1.018 V, respectively, while the LHTV2and HLTV2for the second mode are 1.608 V and 1.492 V, respectively. The circuit consumes a quiescent current (IQ) of 300 pA at room temperature under a 1.8 V supply.

title: Live Demonstration: A 0.787pJ/bit, 25 Mbps True Random Number Generator based on Analog Chaotic Tent Map.
abstract: We demonstrate a true random number generator based on simulating chaotic tent circuits. The demonstration platform includes TRNG chips, test circuit boards, and a series of experimental results. The proposed true random number generator chip achieves high throughput, low power consumption, and very high reliability. The measurement results indicate that the proposed TRNG only consumes 19.68 µ W at a throughput of 25 Mbps, equivalent to an energy efficiency of 0.787 pJ/bit. In addition, the random bit sequence generated by TRNG successfully passed the NIST and AIS randomness tests without any post-processing. During the demonstration, we also found that the ratio of '1' and '0' can be adjusted by adjusting the voltage and temperature, gradually deviating by 50%.

title: A Scaling Annealing Method for Combinatorial Optimization in Asynchronous Memristive Hopfield Network.
abstract: The memristive Hopfield neural networks (HNNs) can greatly accelerate the solving of combinatorial optimization problems. However, efficient annealing methods are required to prevent HNNs from converging to sub-optimal solutions. In this paper, we propose a novel scaling annealing (ScA) method and circuit design using the intrinsic stochasticity of the memristors to mitigate the local minima problem. Specifically, asynchronous updates are employed with the ScA method to prevent the hardware overhead from going out of control as the problem size grows. Based on the classical max-cut problems, simulation results show that on a 60-node problem, ScA finds the global minimum with 5.4× higher accuracy than the HNN without annealing. In addition, compared to the prior annealing schemes for memristive HNNs, the ScA method exhibits a better overall solution performance, and achieves 9.5× reduction in the annealing circuit area overhead for a 60-node problem.

title: Robust Compression Circuit for Real-time Read-out of 320x240 SPAD Array Based on FPGA.
abstract: LiDAR systems based on single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) are capable of picosecond-accurate temporal resolution through detecting individual photon arrivals, resulting in massive data rates exceeding the bandwidth of data-transfer buses. While state-of-the-art compressive methods have demonstrated significant success in reducing bandwidth requirements, their reconstruction accuracy remains compromised under challenging conditions, including long-range imaging and low-light scenarios. In this paper, we propose an FPGA-based compression circuit capable of achieving more accurate depth reconstruction results under various photon count levels compared to state-of-the-art non-learning method, while maintaining 32x compression for data volume. Moreover, the latency is significantly reduced, making the real-time read-out of large SPAD arrays possible on edge devices.

title: A Reconfigurable VCO-Ringamp Based Pipeline ADC.
abstract: A low-power two-stage pipeline-SAR ADC is demonstrated featuring a reconfigurable VCO-ringamp in the first stage. The quantization and residue amplification of a pipeline stage can be achieved by first operating the VCO-ringamp in a unity feedback configuration and subsequently reconfiguring it to act as a residue amplifier. This eliminates the need for a dedicated quantizer in the first stage. The VCO output phases are captured by dynamic latches commonly used in high-speed SAR logic. Transistor-level simulations are used to validate the operation of the pipeline ADC in a 16nm CMOS technology. The proposed ADC is able to operate up to a sampling rate of 625 MS/s achieving an SNDR of 66 dB and SFDR of 80 dB while consuming only 4.4 mW of power.

title: A Synthesizable Mixed-Precision DCIM Macro with Parallel Write and Compute.
abstract: Language models (LMs) have achieved remarkable success but continue to face high computational and memory demands. Mixed-precision quantization has emerged as a promising approach to mitigate these challenges by multiplying low-bit integer weights by higher-precision floating-point activations, thereby reducing computational cost while preserving accuracy. However, existing hardware platforms such as GPUs and TPUs lack native support for FP×INT computation, resulting in costly dequantization overhead. In this work, we present a synthesizable mixed-precision digital compute-in-memory (DCIM) macro that performs direct FP8×INT2/4/6 multiplications. We explore both bit-serial and parallel-input architectures and analyze their performance trade-offs. The proposed design employs double-buffered storage to overlap weight loading with computation, improving throughput and hardware utilization. Implemented in TSMC 65nm technology, the mixed-precision FP8×INT macro achieves up to an 8.77× reduction in power-delay-area (PDA) product compared to an FP8×FP8 baseline design at the macro level. When evaluated on end-to-end LLaMA3.2 inference workloads, the proposed architecture delivers 4-6× higher throughput and energy efficiency, while reducing area by up to 5× relative to FP8×FP8 computation.

title: SlimTTS: Parameter- and Compute-Efficient Neural Text-to-Speech Synthesis for Real-Time Inference.
abstract: Neural text-to-speech (TTS) systems have achieved remarkable naturalness and fidelity but remain computationally intensive, limiting their deployment on resource-constrained devices. This paper presents SlimTTS, a parameter- and compute-efficient neural TTS pipeline designed for real-time inference. The proposed approach applies hardware-aware optimisations to both stages of a two-part TTS architecture: a phoneme-to-mel model based on EfficientSpeech and a HiFi-GAN-based vocoder. Computationally expensive components such as LayerNorm, SoftMax, and GeLU are replaced with lightweight, hardware-friendly alternatives, including Dynamic Tanh (DyT), ReLU, and hardtanh. In parallel, systematic architectural simplifications are applied to the HiFi-GAN vocoder, reducing channel and kernel sizes while preserving perceptual quality. These optimisations yield a reduction from 1.2M to 562k parameters and a 3.5× decrease in computational cost per second of generated audio from 3.24 to 0.92 GFLOP with negligible accuracy loss. The resulting model is suitable for on-device TTS synthesis and future custom hardware design. Synthesised audio samples are available at: https://arnedebeer.github.io/optimised-tts-demo.

title: Lightweight Multi-View EEG Seizure Detection with a Two-Stage Low-Power BFP FFT-NN Accelerator.
abstract: Epilepsy, affecting more than 60 million people worldwide, is characterized by recurrent, unpredictable seizures that jeopardize patient safety and quality of life. Accurate, real-time detection is therefore of substantial clinical and societal significance. We present a lightweight, multi-view seizure-detection model together with a corresponding hardware implementation. The framework integrates temporal, spectral, and time–frequency features via three subnetworks and achieves an accuracy of 99.06% on the CHB-MIT dataset. A two-stage, low-power optimization strategy performs rapid prescreening with a compact network and, when a seizure is suspected, triggers refined analysis using a larger network. By employing depthwise-separable convolutions, the model substantially reduces both the number of parameters and the computational cost. On the hardware side, we implement an engine with a customized block floating-point (BFP) compute unit that accelerates fast Fourier transform (FFT) and neural-network (NN) operations, reducing silicon area by 24% and power consumption by 47% relative to a bfloat16 (BF16) baseline. Compared with prior designs, the system reduces energy per inference by approximately 1.8× to 13.7×. The proposed solution offers an efficient foundation for wearable, real-time seizure-detection systems.

title: Residual-Free Image Reconstruction from HEVC for Compressed-Domain Visual Analytics.
abstract: Conventional video analytics systems require full pixel-domain decoding before object detection or classification, incurring significant computational overhead. This study introduces a novel method for reconstructing images directly from HEVC bitstreams without residual data, enabling efficient compressed-domain processing. We propose a Gaussian-based random perturbation technique that substitutes residuals during intra-frame reconstruction, generating structurally meaningful images suitable for machine learning tasks. Our approach reconstructs images using only prediction metadata and statistically generated perturbations, bypassing the most computationally intensive component of HEVC decoding. Applied to the BIT-Vehicle dataset, our method achieves 35.60% reduction in reconstruction time compared to full decoding, while achieving near-perfect vehicle detection and 96.84% classification accuracy. By eliminating residual decoding, the proposed approach enables faster and more lightweight video analytics pipelines. Although not visually interpretable by humans, the reconstructed images retain sufficient structure for deep learning models, potentially offering benefits in privacy-conscious scenarios. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first method to fully eliminate residual decoding in HEVC for compressed-domain image reconstruction supporting object classification tasks.

title: Planting CRYSTALS-Kyber Acceleration Seeds.
abstract: CRYSTALS-Kyber (FIPS203) was one of the first post quantum cryptography schemes to be standardized by the National Institute of Standards and Technology; CRYSTALS-Kyber utilizes Montgomery reduction at the heart of the modulo reduction. Montgomery reduction traditionally is suited to computing moduli much larger than 32/64-bits. Recently a new modulo reduction method was published named Plantard reduction which allows for one less multiplication at the reduction stage. However, this does require doubling the word size of the values being calculated, in the case of CRYSTALS-Kyber increasing from 16-bit to 32-bit. In this paper we present the worlds first Plantard ISE on the Ibex RISC-V core and investigate the impact Instruction Set Extensions can have utilizing this new modulo reduction method over original methods such as Montgomery and Barrett reduction. Utilizing Plantard reduction as a set of Instruction Set Extensions, we are able to reduce the cycle counts required to compute the entire CRYSTALS-Kyber algorithm by up to 21% and reduce the cycle counts of the NTT by 1.7x and the INTT by 2.6x against the reference implementation.

title: TAuC-SoC: A 0.36 mm2 In-Yarn Integrable Tiny Audio Compressor SoC for E-Textile Based Audio Recording Applications.
abstract: This paper presents a 0.36 mm2(die area)/0.2 mm2(core area) Tiny Audio Compressor System on Chip (TAuC-SoC) for direct in-yarn integration to perform audio compression and recording in E-textiles. This work addresses the unmet need for a tiny, programmable, audio-compression SoC which can operate in unison with other TAuC-SoCs on a distributed computing in-yarn network to perform excellent quality (based on Speech Transmission Index for Public Address (STIPA) score) audio recording (in compressed or uncompressed mode), useful in a noisy environment. It has a Cortex M0+ CPU, 8kB SRAM, I2C host and device interfaces, and Cascaded-Integrate-Comb (CIC)-Adaptive Delta Pulse Code Modulation (ADPCM) based audio compressor accelerator. It boots up automatically from an external flash memory, supports multiple programmable compression options to tradeoff recording quality vs. recording size, performs CRC-based robust audio recording retrieval and other relevant programmable tasks. Implemented in 65nm, it has a minimum operating power of 39.2 µW, 2.7 pJ energy/bit and STIPA score of over 0.77.

title: A Graph-Based Methodology for Dynamic KV-Cache Compression in Transformer Inference.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) face significant challenges when deployed in edge and resource-constrained environments due to the heavy memory and compute demands of the Key–Value (KV) cache during autoregressive inference. This work introduces a graph-based KV cache compression framework that models cache entries as nodes in a dynamic similarity graph and performs centroid-based merging guided by a tunable distance threshold. This enables dynamic compression while preserving contextual fidelity, effectively balancing model accuracy and efficiency. Experimental evaluation demonstrates up to 97% memory reduction while maintaining high throughput retention. Crucially, this is achieved with only a modest and stable increase in perplexity on benchmark GPT-2 and TinyLlama models, validating that the proposed methodology delivers a highly favorable trade-off between extreme memory savings and model fidelity. The results establish this approach as a practical and scalable solution for efficient LLM deployment in edge AI systems.

title: A Pico-Watt, Supply-Insensitive All-CMOS Voltage Reference, from -30°C to 160°C for Ultra Low Power IoT Applications.
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-low-power CMOS voltage reference (VR) design that achieves very low line sensitivity and a wide temperature range of operation. The core architecture consists of only four transistors and employs a dual regulation loop topology to enhance the line sensitivity. A gate-source shorted PMOS serves as the main current source of the core. An additional proportional to absolute temperature (PTAT) generator connected to the body of the PMOS current source to modulate Vthat subzero temperatures while bulk diode leakage control is utilized to ensure reliable operation at higher temperature. Simulated in a 0.18µm CMOS process, the proposed VR delivers a reference voltage of 451.6 mV while consuming only 37.6 pW power. It has a line sensitivity (LS) of 0.009%/V and operates over a temperature range from -30°C to 160°C with temperature coefficient (TC) of 70.2 ppm/°C.

title: Cross-Resolution Transfer Learning in Pixelated RF Filter Inverse Design.
abstract: Addressing the contradiction between resolution and electromagnetic (EM) simulation dataset collection efficiency in pixelated RF circuit design, this paper proposes a cross-resolution transfer learning approach for pixelated circuit design. The method achieves lossless cross-resolution migration of circuit layouts through edge anti-aliasing pixelated configurations, establishing a complete technical framework from low-resolution EM surrogate model training to high-resolution circuit design. Experimental results demonstrate that, starting from a 16×16 training dataset, the proposed method requires only an additional 13% of 32×32 samples to accurately predict arbitrary 32×32 layouts, achieving a mean squared error below 0.0032. In the validation of the 1.8-2.7GHz bandpass filter design, after migrating the low-resolution design to a 32×32 high-resolution design and further optimization, the filter performance is significantly improved. Harmonic control and roll-off characteristics are substantially enhanced, with stopband suppression superior to -17 dB up to the 4th harmonic, validating the effectiveness and practicality of this method in reducing data requirements while improving design performance.

title: Heteroclinic Bifurcations Reveal Virtual Inertia-Damping Limits for Grid Stability.
abstract: Modern electrical grids are witnessing an increasing share of inverter-based resources (IBRs) at generation and load side, while conventional generators and loads are being displaced.The resulting reduction in inertia and load damping exacerbates stability issues, particularly frequency and synchronization stability.To address this issue, the concept of virtual inertia and load damping has emerged, provided by the IBR control logic.This raises the question of how much intervention from IBRs is actually necessary, and if a too high contribution may yield adverse effects.We consider an aggregated model of a power-grid area, compact enough to be fully analyzed through the tools of nonlinear dynamics, to identify the key parameters influencing frequency and synchronization stability.We derive an operational expression showing that the ratio of grid area damping to inertia is of paramount importance rather than their individual values.These results are validated by simulating a well known benchmark electrical grid in different scenarios.

title: Ising-ReRAM: A Low Power Ising Machine ReRAM Crossbar for NP Problems.
abstract: Computational workloads are growing exponentially, driving power consumption to unsustainable levels. Efficiently distributing large-scale networks is an NP-Complete problem equivalent to Boolean satisfiability (SAT), making it one of the core challenges in modern computation. To address this, physics and device inspired methods such as Ising systems have been explored for solving SAT more efficiently. In this work, we implement an Ising model equivalence of the 3-SAT problem using a ReRAM crossbar fabricated in the Skywater 130 nm CMOS process. Our ReRAM-based algorithm achieves 91.0% accuracy in matrix representation across iterative reprogramming cycles. Additionally, we establish a foundational energy profile by measuring the energy costs of small sub-matrix structures within the problem space, demonstrating under linear growth trajectory for combining sub-matrices into larger problems. These results demonstrate a promising platform for developing scalable architectures to accelerate NP-Complete problem solving.

title: Live Demonstration: A self-adapting randomness extractor for a monolithic QRNG.
abstract: This live demonstration shows a monolithic quantum random number generator (QRNG) fabricated in a 22-nm standard CMOS technology and based on the dark events generated by a Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD). The random number generator relies on a novel methodology for random bit extraction based on an on-the-fly median estimation of the inter-arrival times between consecutive events. Thanks to this self-adapting mechanism, the quality of the output sequence is kept constant regardless of the working conditions.

title: Design of a compact QRNG in 22nm standard CMOS technology.
abstract: In this work we present a quantum random number generator (QRNG) based on Single-Photon Avalanche Diodes (SPADs) implemented in 22-nm CMOS technology. A new approach for quantum random number generation is presented, based on the median estimation of the times between pulses defined by endogenous generation processes. The proposed methodology allows for a random number generation efficiency near to one, as well as randomly generated strings of bits that pass common randomness tests without the need for post-processing. Thanks to the use of standard CMOS technology for both the detection and the logic, our QRNG is suitable for a highly scalable solution.

title: In Simplicity There Is Strength: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of XGBoost for Generalizable SRAM Stability Prediction.
abstract: Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) is a key element in modern electronics, and predicting its stability often motivates the use of increasingly complex models. In this work, we challenge this trend by showing that simpler approaches can be highly effective. Through a series of experiments, we demonstrate that a well-tuned Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model achieves strong in-domain prediction accuracy for critical SRAM metrics including Access Disturb Margin (ADM), Write Margin (WRM) and Ireadmin. More importantly, the same model also delivers robust performance in cross-domain prediction, a task typically viewed as more challenging. To further test whether added complexity improves generalization, we design a parameter-sharing neural network (PS-NN) tailored for cross-domain transfer. Our results show that the PS-NN does not outperform the simpler XGBoost model. Taken together, these findings support a "simplicity-first" approach in electronic design automation, where the strengths of efficient models like XGBoost should be fully assessed before turning to more complex architectures. Ultimately, such prediction capabilities have the potential to transform the design process and accelerate decision-making for circuit designers.

title: Distributed Instrumented Paddle for Real-Time Kayak Performance Analysis: IACF-Based Cadence Estimation.
abstract: Real-time performance analysis in elite kayaking requires precise, on-water measurement systems that bridge the gap between laboratory biomechanics and field conditions. We present a distributed instrumented paddle system featuring a dual-node architecture with optimized analog front-end for high-fidelity force and kinematic data capture. Our key contribution is the Incremental Autocorrelation Function (IACF), a novel algorithm for real-time cadence estimation that reduces computational complexity by 75% while maintaining superior resolution compared to FFT methods. Experimental validation on-water with video ground truth demonstrates strong correlation (r > 0.84) and low RMSE (< 3.3 SPM), confirming the effectiveness of the proposed system for field-based performance analysis.

title: Energy-Efficient Epileptic Seizure Prediction Using Spiking Neural Networks.
abstract: Early, reliable prediction of epileptic seizures from scalp EEG can materially improve patient safety, as well as enable responsive interventions. The low energy consumption of Spiking Neural Networks (SNN) makes them good candidates for wearable devices implementation. In this paper, we propose an energy-efficient seizure prediction method compatible with resource-constrained wearable devices. We developed a patient-specific SNN-based model trained and tested on the CHB-MIT scalp EEG dataset. The proposed model combines two convolutional layers with Leaky Integrate-and-Fire spiking neurons, a recurrent neural network to capture temporal dependencies, and surrogate-gradient training. A seizure-wise leave-one-out protocol is used for development and assessment. Our experimental result indicates that the proposed model attains a mean Accuracy of 93.60%, Sensitivity of 88.91%, Specificity of 98.29%, F1-Score of 91.85%, and AUROC of 0.9360, indicating accurate pre-ictal brain state detection compared to the state-of-the-art algorithms while consuming much less energy. The event-driven nature of SNNs supports the long-term goal of power-constrained, on-device seizure prediction in wearable/IoT settings.

title: Configurable p-Neurons Using Modular p-Bits.
abstract: Probabilistic bits (p-bits) have recently been employed in neural networks (NNs) as stochastic neurons with sigmoidal probabilistic activation functions. Nonetheless, there remain a wealth of other probabilistic activation functions that are yet to be explored. Here we re-engineer the p-bit by decoupling its stochastic signal path from its input data path, giving rise to a modular p-bit that enables the realization of probabilistic neurons (p-neurons) with a range of configurable probabilistic activation functions, including a probabilistic version of the widely used Logistic Sigmoid, Tanh and Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) activation functions. We present spintronic (CMOS + sMTJ) designs that show wide and tunable probabilistic ranges of operation. Finally, we experimentally implement digital-CMOS versions on an FPGA, with stochastic unit sharing, and demonstrate an order of magnitude (10x) saving in required hardware resources compared to conventional digital p-bit implementations.

title: A Stable Approximate Pruning Framework with Heuristic Optimization.
abstract: With the growing demand for energy-efficient computing, approximate computing has emerged as a promising solution. However, the number of approximable components rises exponentially with system complexity, making it challenging to explore the design space effectively. This paper proposes a Heuristic Pruning Approach (HPA) to address this issue through multi-circuit replication and adaptive pruning strategies. Inspired by particle swarm optimization and backtracking algorithms, HPA introduces a global wire selection mechanism that prioritizes overall optimization rather than local improvements in each iteration. Compared with existing methods, HPA achieves more stable error growth and tighter convergence toward predefined tolerance thresholds, enabling more efficient exploration of the approximate design space. Experimental results show that HPA consistently outperforms prior techniques across multiple arithmetic architectures, achieving up to 15.48% lower power-delay-area product in multiply accumulate implementations.

title: HQC Post-Quantum Cryptography Decryption with Soft-Decision Reed-Solomon Decoder.
abstract: Hamming Quasi-Cyclic (HQC) has been selected in the last round of the post-quantum cryptography standardization. The HQC decryption involves decoding a concatenated Reed-Muller (RM) code and Reed-Solomon (RS) code. The error-correcting capability of the decoding algorithms decides the codeword length, which in turn determines the key size and the ciphertext size, and affects the implementation complexity. Previous HQC instantiations have adopted hard-decision RS decoding, which is straightforward but offers limited error-correcting performance. This paper proposes soft-decision RS decoding for HQC in order to improve the correction capability and accordingly reduce the codeword length. Soft information is extracted from intermediate results of RM decoding to determine the reliability of RS decoder input symbols with small hardware overhead. The trade-off between error-correcting performance gain and implementation complexity is analyzed across various soft-decision decoding schemes, and erasure-only RS decoding is selected. Furthermore, low-complexity hardware architectures are developed for the soft information extraction and erasure-only RS decoder. For HQC-128, the proposed soft-decision decoding achieves a 13% reduction in codeword length compared to the current HQC specification with smaller estimated logic area and shorter latency for overall HQC decryption module.

title: A Compact-Area Digital-Output CMOS Test Module for Random Telegraph Noise Characterization.
abstract: This work presents a CMOS test module for the characterization of random telegraph noise (RTN) that can be integrated into regular scribe lines. The proposed module incorporates a novel low-noise current-mode IAF ADC and a standard I2C digital backend for addressing and reading each DUT. A set of 1024-DUT modules has been integrated in the 0.18μm Modular Mixed-Signal HV CMOS technology from X-FAB (XH018). Preliminary experimental results are presented in terms of RTN patterns, spectra, power distributions, spatial mappings for two NMOS transistor types and sizes. The test module can be used to investigate RTN bias dependencies and, with minimal modifications, to speed up testing through RTN subsampling techniques.

title: A Full-Custom Time-Domain Unary Sorter for Soft-Information Decoding in 65 nm CMOS.
abstract: We present a full-custom time-domain (TD) unary sorter for soft-information decoding with 5-bit quantized inputs. The design exploits a time-domain unary representation combined with a bitonic sorting network to efficiently order large numbers of log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) while outputting only their indices. Implemented in a 65 nm CMOS process, the proposed sorter achieves substantially lower latency compared to conventional digital and unary designs, while also reducing area and power relative to digital implementations, making it well-suited for efficient ultra-low-latency soft-decision decoding. Furthermore, the time-domain unary representation allows trading a small amount of sorting accuracy for even lower latency, which is acceptable in many soft-decision decoding applications such as ordered reliability bits guessing random additive noise decoding (ORBGRAND) and Chase-type error-correcting decoders.

title: Analytical Derivation of Quantization Error in Threshold Level Quantizers Using Bipolar PFM.
abstract: Uniform quantization is a topic that has been extensively studied. However and although an analytical description of quantization noise has been proposed, most descriptions of the spectral properties of quantization error resort to statistical descriptions. In this paper, we show that the spectrum of a quantized signal can be expressed using pulse frequency modulation. We first establish the equivalence of a uniform quantizer with a system based on the bipolar pulse frequency modulation and we define afterwards the Fourier transform of the quantized signal using pulse frequency modulation properties. This model brings a more intuitive understanding of the spectral structure of quantization noise and complements prior research in the topic. The results of the paper can be directly applied to level crossing ADCs with zero-order-hold interpolators, giving an accurate estimation of their performance.

title: A Low-Power 4x Multiplier Based on Current-Reuse Complementary Push-Push Doublers.
abstract: This paper presents a frequency quadrupler targeting the 60-GHz band, designed in a 28-nm bulk CMOS technology. The proposed architecture consists of two cascaded doublers based on common-gate (CG) stage with capacitive cross-coupling and integrated LC tanks, enabling efficient generation of the fourth harmonic of the 15-GHz input signal. The 60-GHz signal is further increased by a pseudo-differential cross-coupled cascode amplifier, while an output buffer is added for on-wafer measurement purposes. Electromagnetic (EM) and circuit-level simulations show effective input/output matching and a maximum power conversion gain of −2.6 dB at 0-dBm input power. The total power consumption is as low as 16 mW with a 0.9-V supply, resulting in a total efficiency (ηTOT) of approximately 3.15%.

title: Ultra Low-Power CMOS Voltage References Designed with Automated Flow.
abstract: This paper presents three-transistor CMOS voltage references (3T-VRs), automatically designed and optimized by means of a CAD framework, the OptiGap. This toolbox, based on Matlab-Spectre co-simulations, has been developed for the automated design of several classes ultra low-power (ULP) VRs, in multiple technology nodes. We report the implementation on silicon of three 3T-VR circuits in TSMC 130-nm BDC technology. The circuits have been designed for minimum temperature coefficient (TC), minimum spread on process corners, and large power supply rejection (PSR), at 1 nanoAmpere of current consumption.In measurements, the 3T-VRs show output voltages well aligned with the simulations, at the specified current consumption. Good metrics in terms of average TC, spread on multiple samples, and PSR are achieved with respect to the state-of-the-art. The reported results demonstrate the high potential for automated design for this class of circuits.

title: Cryo-CMOS Antenna for Wireless Communications within a Quantum Computer Cryostat.
abstract: Scaling quantum computers from a few qubits to large numbers remains one of the critical challenges in realizing practical quantum advantage. Multi-core quantum architectures have emerged as a promising solution, enabling scalability through distributed quantum processing units (QPUs) interconnected via classical and quantum links. However, the bottleneck of wired connections persists, as densely packed wired interconnects, both vertically across temperature stages and horizontally within the same layer, introduce spatial constraints, power dissipation, and latency, which could hinder performance as the number of QPUs increases. To overcome these limitations, this work proposes a cryo-compatible on-chip differential dipole antenna operating at 28 GHz to enable short-range wireless communication within a quantum computer cryostat. Temperature-dependent material properties are incorporated to accurately capture antenna behavior at 4 K. Moreover, by embedding the antenna in a realistic cryostat structure, we evaluate the feasibility of antenna operation within the cryogenic environment. The proposed antenna achieves a reflection coefficient of -20.8 dB in free space and -18.38 dB within the cryostat, demonstrating efficient impedance matching.

title: FastDEP: A CMOS DEP Chip with Frequency and Voltage Scaling for Cell Biology Applications.
abstract: CMOS-based dielectrophoresis (DEP) is a vital tool for high-precision cell manipulation, but its efficiency is limited by restricted waveform and voltage control. FastDEP is a programmable CMOS platform with two chips and a velocity-tracking system for quantitative evaluation. One chip integrates a 30 MHz on-chip DCO for square-wave excitation, and the other supports dynamic voltage scaling up to 3.6 V. The image-based tracker measures cell and particle velocity under various conditions. Results show that a 1.8 V square wave achieves the same transport speed as a 3.6 V sine wave, and increases particle velocity from 0.9 µm/s to 20.53 µm/s, a 22.8× improvement compare to 1.8 V sine wave. iPSC experiments reveal an optimal 5 MHz frequency and a migration speed increase from 27.8 µm/s to 83.7 µm/s. FastDEP enables efficient, low-voltage, and high-speed DEP manipulation for cell biology applications.

title: A Single-Ended Tri-Mode PAM2/3/4 Transceiver Front-End Achieving 0.437/0.302/0.314 pJ/bit Energy Efficiency for D2D Interconnection.
abstract: This paper reports a single-ended tri-mode PAM2/3/4 transceiver front-end to support multiple signaling formats. A voltage mode (VM) driver is introduced in the transmitter (TX), paired with a dedicated PAM2/4 encoder and a separate PAM3 encoder to support tri-mode signaling. The receiver (RX) front-end comprises a reference level selector (RLS), a sampler, and decoders. Prototyped in 28-nm CMOS technology and operating at 14 Gbaud, the proposed transceiver front-end achieved the energy efficiency of 0.437 pJ/bit for PAM2, 0.302 pJ/bit for PAM3 and 0.314 pJ/bit for PAM4, respectively. The transmitter driver occupies an area of 693 μm2, and the receiver front-end occupies an area of 650 μm2.

title: A Profit Guranteed Dynamic Dual-pricing Model and robust scheduling approach for Electric Vehicle Charging in Microgrid.
abstract: Utilizing Dynamic Pricing schemes for Electric Vehicle (EV) charging has attracted much interest during the last decades. However, ensuring profitability in microgrid operations amid load and renewable fluctuations is a significant challenge. To this end, we propose a novel consumer-oriented dual-pricing scheme for EV charging and microgrid optimal scheduling approach. It utilizes EVs as dynamic loads and a robust scheduling scheme that adjusts the EVs to match the base load demand. Moreover, a novel dual-pricing scheme comprising guaranteed and non-guaranteed contracts for selling electricity to the EVs and other loads in the microgrid sustaining profitability. The non-guaranteed contracts help to deal with the intermittent nature of the renewable. Simulation results show that the proposed approach can meet the guaranteed profit from 5% to 30% renewable penetration. The EV owners are charged 6% to 18% cheaper than the utility with increasing penetration of renewable.

title: A Front-End for Parkinsonian Tremor Detection Using Memristive Spike Encoding.
abstract: Real-time detection of Parkinsonian rest tremor is vital for assessing disease severity and evaluating therapeutic interventions such as medication and deep brain stimulation (DBS). Conventional digital pipelines often rely on microcontrollers and power-intensive processing, making them unsuitable for compact or low-power continuous monitoring applications. In this context, memristive circuits offer a promising alternative, enabling simplified and fully analog processing. This work proposes an analog front-end architecture that extracts the envelope of the tremor velocity signal through rectification, low-pass filtering, and signal conditioning. The resulting signal modulates a memristive-based oscillator (MBO), producing spike trains whose temporal structure encodes the input amplitude for downstream detection. Evaluation on representative patient recordings demonstrates that the oscillator output varies systematically across therapeutic states using the bio-inspired depolarization blocking concept, thus enabling detection directly in the analog domain. The proposed system provides a low-complexity framework for signal-driven tremor analysis.

title: ElecThinker: A Three-Stage Framework to Enhance Electronic Diagram Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs.
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) show significant potential to revolutionize electronic engineering by automating circuit analysis and design. However, their application is hindered by challenges in reasoning specific to this domain, particularly when solving problems presented in diagrams. To overcome this limitation, we introduce ElecThinker, a framework designed to elicit the intrinsic reasoning potential of MLLMs. This work is supported by our new dataset ElecVerse, which contains 8276 samples with annotations provided by experts. ElecThinker first sharpens the visual grounding of MLLMs using Perception Calibration, then synergistically employs supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for Knowledge Injection and reinforcement learning (RL) for Application Optimization. This approach systematically enhances the model’s ability to solve complex problems. Experiments show our 7B model improves the pass@1 score by approximately 37.5% over the baseline, significantly outperforming larger open-source models and offering a powerful solution for LLM-assisted electronic engineering.

title: High-speed Bufferless NoC-based LLM Accelerator with Distributed Ring-Shaped Buffer.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success in natural language processing, but their massive computation and memory demands create severe bottlenecks in inference for hardware acceleration. The core challenge lies in sustaining high throughput under limited on-chip bandwidth and energy constraints, particularly when scaling matrix multiplications and attention operations across large models. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a distributed ring-shaped buffer topology and a high-performance bufferless NoC-based hardware accelerator tailored for LLM inference. The proposed design integrates innovations across computation, communication, and memory. By leveraging a specific dataflow, the proposed bufferless router supports high-speed data exchange while minimizing router area and link width. Furthermore, the proposed Distributed Ring-Shaped Buffer (DRB) offers unified memory banking and alleviates congestion during inter-core data movement. Compared to prior works, the proposed architecture demonstrates 2.53×–3.13× higher energy efficiency and 1.43×–2.64× greater area efficiency.

title: Neuromorphic Sensing-and-Computing for Multi-Panel Cancer Diagnostics by Memristive Biosensors.
abstract: The investigation of memristors has promoted the development of neuromorphic devices, which play a key role in in-memory computing and brain-inspired computation. In this work, we propose, for the first time, the concept of neuromorphic sensing-and-computing out of several cancer markers by memristive biosensors. Building upon memristive biosensors, each detecting a different cancer biomarker, our design directly converts biomolecular concentrations into spiking signals by employing a unipolar volatile memristor (UVM). These spikes can then serve as the input layer of a spiking neural network (SNN). Unlike conventional single-marker assays, the proposed approach supports multi-marker integration and multi-strategy analysis. Using dual-markers assessment of prostate cancer as an example, we provide preliminary validation of cancer risk prediction, highlighting the potential of neuromorphic sensing-and-computing as a new paradigm for disease diagnosis.

title: A 4x106 Gb/s PAM4 Current-Reuse VCSEL Driver with a High-Bandwidth VGA in 130 nm BiCMOS.
abstract: This work presents a 4x106 Gb/s four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM4) vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL) driver designed for 400G/800G pluggable modules. Compared with conventional variable-gain amplifiers (VGAs) used in VCSEL drivers, the proposed high-bandwidth VGA achieves a 9 dB dynamic range while maintaining a 38 GHz bandwidth, thereby enhancing the VCSEL driver’s operational data rate. In addition, a current-reuse technique is implemented in the output stage to effectively reduce power consumption. A negative-feedback loop incorporating an error amplifier is employed to stabilize the bias current delivered to the VCSEL. The prototype is fabricated in a 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS process and evaluated using a commercial 850 nm anode-driven VCSEL. Measurement results show that the proposed VCSEL driver achieves an extinction ratio (ER) of 3.1 dB and an optical modulation amplitude (OMA) of 1.26 mW at a 106 Gb/s PAM4 data rate, corresponding to an energy efficiency of 1.1 pJ/bit.

title: A Reinforcement Learning Co-Simulation Platform for Event-Triggered and Variable-Frequency Power Converter Control.
abstract: Matlab and Simulink offer a solution for reinforcement learning (RL) in industrial control. RL agents are configured in Matlab, while interactive environments are developed in Simulink. However, the Simulink RL modules cannot implement variable-frequency and event-triggered mechanisms due to the fixed-step decision feature. The closed-source Matlab RL algorithms prevent customization and debugging. These limitations constrain previous studies to simple topologies and fixed-frequency control. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a RL co-simulation platform to implement advanced mechanisms in power converter control. The platform respectively implements the agent, environment, and signal transmitter in Python, Simulink, and C. On the proposed platform, the agent can dynamically adapt the control frequency to match the variable switching frequency and conduct event-triggered operations. The proposed platform is validated on the double-clamp zero-voltage-switching (DCZVS) flyback converter, a resonant topology requiring multi-mode control. The experiment results demonstrate that the proposed platform can effectively manage event-triggered sampling and variable-frequency control.
