title: A Dual-Stage ZOOM2 Light-to-Digital Converter for High-Dynamic-Range PPG Readout.
abstract: This paper presents a low-power, high–dynamic-range Photoplethysmography (PPG) readout front end based on a dual-stage ZOOM2light-to-digital converter (LDC). The proposed architecture performs two sequential successive-approximation-register (SAR) assisted coarse quantization steps within a single LED activation cycle. The first SAR stage (8-bit) cancels the dominant DC component, while the second SAR stage (5-bit), combined with a second-order sigma–delta (ΣΔ) modulator, digitizes the residual AC signal. Behavioral-level simulations show that the design achieves a signal-to-quantization-noise ratio (SQNR) of approximately 107.4 dB within a 20 Hz bandwidth, while the single-cycle conversion time is shortened to 39.8 µs including decimation, which is only approximately one-third that of conventional incremental sigma–delta modulator (ISDM)-based LDCs without digital filtering.

title: A Sparsity-Aware Reconfigurable Sensing-Quantization Circuit for RRAM-Based Analog Compute-in-Memory.
abstract: Resistive random-access memory (RRAM)-based analog compute-in-memory (CIM) architectures utilize Ohm’s law and Kirchhoff’s law to accelerate neural network computations. However, the large area and power overhead of peripheral sensing circuits significantly limit integration density and energy efficiency. In addition, the restricted quantization resolution constrains computational flexibility, posing challenges for scalable and reconfigurable edge deployment. This work presents a sparsity-aware reconfigurable sensing-quantization circuit featuring: 1) a sparsity-aware capacitor-hold integrating readout unit (SA-CHIRU) that relieves op-amp loading and enables adaptive multi-cycle accumulation by exploiting weight sparsity. 2) a reconfigurable 5-10-bit pipelined SAR/single-slope analog to digital converter (ADC) that dynamically adjusts resolution to satisfy layer-specific precision requirements. Designed in 40nm CMOS, the SA-CHIRU achieves 76.8% power and 47.6% area reductions, while the ADC attains 9.74 bits ENOB and 42.8% smaller capacitor array. These results demonstrate a compact, energy-scalable, and precision-configurable circuit for high-performance RRAM-based CIM.

title: Source Free Domain Adaptation For 3D Cross-modal Semantic Segmentation.
abstract: 3D cross-modal semantic segmentation (CMSS) is crucial for autonomous driving and robotics. Existing unsupervised domain adaptation methods align domain and modal features to handle source-target distribution differences. However, in privacy-preserving scenarios where source data is inaccessible, these methods suffer significant performance degradation. In this paper, we explore the challenging task of source free domain adaptation for 3D cross-modal semantic segmentation. We propose cross-modal matching knowledge distillation for accurate 2D-3D transfer learning by leveraging prediction consistency between point clouds, pixels, and pixel neighbors. To address prediction inconsistencies caused by different domain gaps in 2D and 3D modalities, we introduce a hyperparameter-free Modal Adaptive Pseudo-label Fusion (MAPF) that adaptively fuses 2D-3D predictions to generate accurate pseudo-labels. Experiments on three cross-modal adaptation datasets demonstrate our method achieves superior performance and surpasses datadependent UDA approaches.

title: Broadband Microfluidic Coplanar Waveguide Biosensor for Position-Dependent Cell Detection.
abstract: Recently, Coplanar Waveguide (CPW), easily integrated with microfluidics and offering wide bandwidth for rapid cellular frequency characterization, shows great potential in electrical property-based cell detection and biosensing applications. This study focuses on investigating the sensitivity of CPW in cell detection. We designed an integrated structure combining a novel blocking-capture microfluidic channel with a CPW, enabling effective cell capture on the sensing region. Simulation results reveal stronger localized electric fields near 22 GHz and 40 GHz. HepG2 tumor cells were experimentally characterized over a frequency range of 0.1–50 GHz. Accumulated S21 variations were also obtained during measurements of 15 tumor cells. Results indicated that the CPW device achieved optimal sensitivity to HepG2 cells at 40 GHz, with sensitivities of 6.52 × 10−7dB/μm3on the signal line and 1.36 × 10−6dB/μm3at the gap, corresponding to a 2.09-fold enhancement. System noise characterization further verified measurement reliability. This work broadens CPW applications in cell detection, demonstrating great potential in biomedical sensing.

title: FlexCNN: Design of a Universal and Easy-to-Deploy CNN Acceleration System.
abstract: The widespread application of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) has driven the development of dedicated accelerators. However, existing CNN accelerators still face two major challenges in practical applications: limited hardware versatility to support diverse convolution and activation operators, and high barriers to software–hardware collaborative deployment. To address these issues, this paper proposes FlexCNN, a CNN acceleration system that is both highly universal and convenient for deploying models. The system features a hardware architecture incorporating an image to column based general matrix multiplication (im2col-GEMM) unit compatible with multiple convolution types, a vector ALU supporting various activation functions, and a reconfigurable pooling unit. In addition, a customized toolchain based on the NCNN inference engine is developed to facilitate end-to-end deployment. Implemented on a Xilinx XCZU15EG FPGA, FlexCNN achieves an energy efficiency of 67.07 GOPS/W when executing YOLOv3 and demonstrates competitive performance across multiple network architectures.

title: A Synchronous Switch Multi-shot Energy Extraction Circuit for Electromagnetic Energy Harvesting.
abstract: In the studies of piezoelectric energy harvesting (PEH), synchronous switching actions at the zero-crossing points of the equivalent current help enhance the harvested capability. By referring to the design principles of capacitive PEH systems, the harvested power from an inductive source can also be enhanced by taking a complementary topology design. This paper proposes a synchronous switch multi-shot energy extraction (SSMEE) circuit for electromagnetic energy harvester (EMEH). It realizes energy extraction at the zero-crossing instants of the electromotive force, i.e., equivalent source voltage. Experimental results demonstrate that, under the same rotational excitation condition, the harvested power using the proposed SSMEE circuit is 30% higher than that using the state-of-the-art synchronous switch energy extraction (SSEE) circuit.

title: TFAF: Temporal-Frequency Attention Fusion for Transformer Pretraining in Time Series Forecasting.
abstract: Multivariate time-series forecasting is hard due to non-stationarity, multi-scale seasonality, and long-range dependencies. Recently, transformer-based methods have been proposed to integrate frequency-domain-based modules, yet they most rely on linear layers to learn frequency-domain representations and adopt a supervised training mechanism. In this paper, a Temporal–Frequency Attention Fusion method (TFAF), is proposed for Transformer pretraining in multivariate time series forecasting across multiple datasets, which augments a PatchTST-style encoder with a time-frequency branch and a multi-layer perceptron(MLP) head, and a Timer-style two-layer MLP replaces the linear head to capture residual nonlinearities. The pretrained model is then finetuned on specific datasets to achieve forecasting. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art models on most classical real-world benchmarks with lower errors, and maintains trend stability across varying pretraining data proportions. Notably, it also consistently improves the scalability of classical supervised Transformer-based forecasters.

title: SegSEM: Enabling and Enhancing SAM2 for SEM Contour Extraction.
abstract: Extracting high-fidelity 2D contours from Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) images is critical for calibrating Optical Proximity Correction (OPC) models. While foundation models like Segment Anything 2 (SAM2) are promising, adapting them to specialized domains with scarce annotated data is a major challenge. This paper presents a case study on adapting SAM2 for SEM contour extraction in a few-shot setting. We propose SegSEM, a framework built on two principles: a data-efficient fine-tuning strategy that adapts by selectively training only the model’s encoders, and a robust hybrid architecture integrating a traditional algorithm as a confidence-aware fallback. Using a small dataset of 60 production images, our experiments demonstrate this methodology’s viability. The primary contribution is a methodology for leveraging foundation models in data-constrained industrial applications.

title: Fully Parallel Ising Machine with MRAM based p-bit Probabilistic Simulated Annealing.
abstract: We present a hardware-friendly Ising machine using voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA)-MTJ based p-bits for combinatorial optimization problems (COPs). The proposed system implements probabilistic simulated annealing (pSA) with discretized scaling factors via lookup table (LUT), eliminating multiplication operations, it also features a scaling back-off (SBO) mechanism to prevent stagnation. Moreover, benefiting from the intrinsic stochastic nature of VCMA-MTJ, a 16 PE array is constructed to achieve fully parallel one-cycle-one-iteration updates for Bernoulli sampling. Accordingly, the circuit simulation of the designed Ising hardware demonstrate 99.7% convergence probability for solving the Max-Cut problem, featured by 129 ns solution time, and 549.5 pJ/solution energy at 1 GHz. Our work delivers O(N) scalability without invoking external random sources, offering improvements over digital annealers in speed and energy efficiency.

title: A Mixed-Signal Gaussian-Based Super-Resolution Sensor Interface Circuit for High-Density Tactile Perception.
abstract: This paper presents a super-resolution sensor interface circuit for high-density tactile perception. A mixed-signal Gaussian-based super-resolution algorithm suitable for sampling rate reduction and energy-efficient processing is presented. Based on a 4×4 capacitive pressure sensor arrays covered with flexible material on a 4cm×4cm substrate, the effective resolution is boosted to 16 pixel/cm2by the proposed super resolution algorithm and experimentally verified by printed circuit boards. The achieved frame rate is 11.9kHz with a 1Mhz system clock. An integrated-circuit version of the proposed sensor interface is designed in a 180-nm CMOS technology, which occupies layout area of 0.276mm2.

title: A Collaborative Adversarial Purification Framework with Perturbation-Insensitive Semantics-Guidance.
abstract: Neural networks have been widely used, which are known to be vulnerable to well-designed adversarial attacks. However, existing purification methods are inefficient in generalizing unknown attacks and tend to destroy useful texture content. To address these issues, we propose a multi-view collaborative purification framework against adversarial examples based on perturbation-insensitive semantics-guidance, which jointly considers multiple purifiers for semantic-view and texture-view representations via semantics-guided collaboration. Specifically, we first explore the sensitivity of multimodal models with image and text alignment learning against perturbations and leverage it to construct a semantic-view purifier. Besides, to retain useful texture details, a texture-view purifier is constructed, where purification is formulated as a corrupted image-inpainting task. Finally, a collaborative purification strategy with semantic guidance is developed to conduct adaptive purification. Extensive experiments are conducted on various adversarial attacks to verify our purification ability against unknown adversarial attacks.

title: A 5MHz-Bandwidth CMOS Hall Current Sensor with Non-spun Voltage-biased Hall Plates and SAR-Accumulator Offset Calibration.
abstract: Advanced high-voltage power electronics demand low-cost isolated current sensors with wide bandwidth and high accuracy that support increasing switching frequencies. However, existing high-performance solutions rely on costly architectures. To address this, this work presents a low-cost yet high-performance Hall-based current sensor. By employing non-spun voltage-biased Hall plates as well as an inverter-based input stage, the proposed design provides a more than 3× improvement in resolution versus other wideband Hall sensors, achieving a 42 µTrmsresolution over a 5 MHz bandwidth. A SAR-accumulator offset calibration scheme cancels the large offset of non-spun Hall plates, reducing it to only 30.5 µT at room temperature. Temperature-dependent resistor compensation limits Hall sensitivity drift from 49% to 2% across 0 °C–125 °C. This design achieves a 150 dB FoM that represents a 3 dB improvement compared to prior art, enabling high-precision wideband current sensing at low cost.

title: A Lightweight RISC-V Multiply-Accumulate Extension with Data Preloading Scheme.
abstract: With the continuous development of internet-of-things (IoTs), edge devices are now expected to perform certain data processing tasks for better overall performance. Due to the highly limited area and power constraints, employing the existing general-purpose processor (GPP) with custom instruction set architecture (ISA) extension is a promising solution to enhancing the computation efficiency of domain-specific tasks. In this brief, a lightweight multiply-accumulate (MAC) extension featuring a data preloading scheme is proposed to support efficient MAC computation for emerging machine learning (ML) applications. With the proposed ISA extension, the GPPs can retain their flexibility while realizing enhanced processing performance and efficiency on MAC-relevant computation tasks. A RISC-V processor with the proposed MAC ISA extension was implemented in 28nm CMOS technology. The measurement results show that the proposed design achieves 47.6–62.3% run time reduction and a peak energy saving of 60.33% when running MAC-relevant tasks. The lightweight feature of the proposed design results in small area and power overhead of 10.93% and 4.95%, respectively. Compared to the state-of-the-art designs, the proposed design realizes 1.29× lower implementation cost in area and 1.84× lower implementation cost in power.

title: A Symmetrical RHP-Zero-Free Hybrid Boost Converter With Eliminated Flying Capacitor Inrush Current and Enhanced Output Current Continuity.
abstract: In this paper, a symmetrical right-half-plane zero free (SRZF) hybrid boost converter with four-phase operation is proposed, which can obtain a higher system robustness and a faster load transient response. The SRZF converter has a hybrid architecture of one inductor and two flying capacitors, which solves the inrush current problem of the flying capacitor under extreme duty cycle, therefore a arbitrarily wide output voltage conversion range is achieved, the continuity of output current is enhanced and the output voltage ripple is reduced. An experimental prototype with switching frequency of 200 kHz is designed to verify the performance of the proposed converter. The measurement results demonstrate that the SRZF converter achieve a peak efficiency of 94.8% and a maximum output voltage ripple of 34 mV. The recovery time is less than 110 µs when the load transient between 0 and 500 mA.

title: MK-Net: A Multi-Scale Semantic Propagation and Base-Channel Distillation Network for Multi-Class Kidney Ultrasound Segmentation.
abstract: Multi-class kidney ultrasound image segmentation suffers from low contrast, speckle noise, and class imbalance that affect the depiction of small structures. To address these challenges, we propose MK-Net with the following novelties: 1) A Multi-scale Semantic Propagation (MSP) module at the encoding stages is proposed, which perform cross-scale semantic fusion via channel-aware gating and residual connection, and convey high-level semantics into low-level features while retaining spatial details. 2) A Base-Layer Distillation (BD) block that strengthens the fundamental/base channels in the UNet representations and produces teacher logits for knowledge distillation is proposed. 3) A combined multi-scale and the distillation loss is proposed to enhance the perception ability of microstructures. The MK-Net is evaluated on the multi-class (Cortex, Medulla, Capsule, and Central echogenic complex) kidney ultrasound dataset, KidneyUS. MK-Net demonstrates superior performance over UNet and its advanced segmentation variants, and the ablation study has confirmed the effectiveness of the components introduced. MK-Net also incorporates a lightweight backbone network with only 12.9M. Its low computational complexity makes it an attractive framework for deployment in clinical settings.

title: Accelerating Entropy Coding via Probability State Caching Mechanism (PSCM).
abstract: With the continuous expansion of real-time transmission scenarios involving 4K and 8K videos, entropy coding, as a crucial stage in video compression systems, has become a major bottleneck in the coding process. Although Context-based Adaptive Binary Arithmetic Coding (CABAC) significantly improves coding efficiency, its inherent serial dependency limits throughput, since the probability state update relies on the previously coded bin value. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel entropy coding acceleration method that introduces a probability state caching mechanism (PSCM) to mitigate the strong serial dependency of context model update. Based on this mechanism, two methods, namely the parity caching method and the temporal caching method, are proposed, achieving throughput improvements of approximately 1.5× and 1.3×, respectively. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed methods incur only a marginal coding efficiency loss of about 0.23% and 0.15% for LDB configuration.

title: DPAM: A Dual-Path Protected Approximate Multiplier for Reliable Neural Network Acceleration.
abstract: Neural networks (NNs) deployed in energy- and safety-critical applications demand hardware that is both efficient and reliable. While approximate multipliers have emerged as a promising means to reduce the cost of multiply-accumulate operations, their reliability is severely challenged by soft errors, voltage fluctuations, and other perturbations. This paper proposes a novel fault-tolerant approximate multiplier based on the Mitchell logarithmic principle. The design integrates approximate triple modular redundancy (ATMR) in the exponent path and a truncated self-detecting adder in the mantissa path, enabling hybrid protection with low hardware overhead. The proposed design achieves fault tolerance comparable to TMR-hardened counterparts while significantly reducing area by 26.6% and power-delay product by 21.4% on average compared to state-of-the-art multipliers, demonstrating superior hardware efficiency and reliability.

title: A 23μW 158.4dB FoM Triple-Slope Current-to-Digital Converter with Digital Thermal Noise Reduction for Electrochemical Current Readout.
abstract: This paper presents a Triple-Slope Current-to-Digital Converter (TS-CDC) for high-sensitivity readout of electrochemical sensors, featuring a digital domain thermal noise reduction (DTNR) technique that enhances signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) by reconfiguring the CDC control logic. The TS-CDC comprises an integrating amplifier, a dynamic comparator, coarse/fine integration current sources, and dedicated control logic. While multi-slope operation inherently achieves low quantization noise, the overall system noise is typically dominated by the thermal noise of the integrating amplifier. The proposed technique reduced thermal noise by extending the final integration phase and modifying counter logic. Post-layout simulations of the TS-CDC, implemented in a 65nm CMOS process, demonstrate a 6dB improvement in SNR when DTNR is enabled. The converter achieves a peak SNDR of 75.1dB while consuming only 23μW at a 10kS/s sampling rate, making it well-suited for low-power, high-precision sensor interfaces.

title: Automatic Circuit Topology Generation on a Reconfigurable Analog Array.
abstract: In this paper, a framework is proposed to automatically generate circuit topologies on a Field-Programmable Analog Array (FPAA) based on user-provided specifications. A Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) algorithm is utilized to optimize device selection, transistor pair topology selection, and routing. During the device selection stage, the algorithm determines whether to expand the number of devices used for implementation of a circuit. In the topology selection stage, the structured configuration of the selected devices is finalized, while in the routing selection stage the connections between devices are established. A Bayesian optimization algorithm is executed to determine the transistor sizes of the circuit topologies generated by the MCTS algorithm, which optimizes the performance of each generated topology with feedback provided through SPICE simulation. Experimental results demonstrate that execution of the proposed flow successfully results in the creation of different circuit topologies of an operational amplifier (op amp) that meet the specifications and constraints provided by the user. After 23 executed iterations, the proposed MCTS algorithm generates circuits that achieve a 26% higher performance score than circuits generated with a random tree search (RTS) algorithm.

title: Accelerating Audio-driven 3D Facial Animation Training with a Compressive Sensing Framework.
abstract: The training of end-to-end models for audio-driven 3D facial animation is often hindered by the significant computational overhead of direct loss computation on high-dimensional 3D mesh data. To address this efficiency bottleneck, we propose a novel compressed-domain training framework. Our method leverages the principles of Compressive Sensing to shift the loss computation from the high-dimensional vertex space to a compact, low-dimensional signal space. Extensive experiments on multiple state-of-the-art architectures demonstrate that our framework significantly accelerates the training process, with speedups ranging from 1.52x to a remarkable 9.57x, while maintaining generation quality comparable to SOTA methods. Our findings establish a superior solution that achieves an exceptional trade-off between computational efficiency and final animation quality.

title: A Clock-Independent, Time-Domain Rapid Calibration Method for Memristor-based Analog Computing AI Processors.
abstract: Memristor-based analog computing shows promising energy efficiency compared to digital counterparts. High- performance memristor-based AI processor has multi-level memristors, combined with the effect of device retention and ageing, the memristor readout system has tight readout margin to accurately determining the state of the memristor. Because the accuracy of the readout comparator determines the maximum accuracy the system can achieve. To address this, we proposed a high precision, clock-independent offset calibration scheme. The calibration scheme uses edge-triggered pulse-based calibration signal that makes the calibration accuracy independent of clock speed. The coarse-fine calibration steps are used to rapidly converge to minimum offset with high precision. A built-in digital calibration flag indicates the calibration status, that enables the synchronisation across arrays of comparators to facilitate scaling. The comparator is designed, laid out and simulated using 12 nm FinFET process. The comparator achieves average input voltage offset of 120 μV with 50 μV standard deviation after calibration, while the conventional method has the offset of 1.35 mV with standard deviation of 390 μV.

title: A Multi-Precision Tensor Processing Unit for Accelerating Matrix Computations.
abstract: Matrix multiplication serves as a fundamental operation across various computational domains, including scientific simulations, computer graphics, signal processing, and machine learning, driving the development of specialized hardware processing units to accelerate its computation. Traditional high-precision data formats incur substantial power consumption and latency, creating challenges for edge devices that require high performance under strict resource constraints. Quantization to low-precision representations mitigates these issues while preserving accuracy, but existing accelerator designs often lack flexibility, focusing narrowly on fused multiply-add units without holistic system integration. This paper proposes a multi-precision tensor processing unit (MPTPU) with compact hardware architecture for edge inference, featuring an 8x8 systolic array with resource-multiplexed processing elements that achieve variable parallelism: lx for FP16/TF32, 2x for BF16/INT8, and 8x for FP8/INT4. The MPTPU is implemented on FPGA, achieving throughput of up to 214 GFUOPS at 209 MHz, demonstrating its efficacy in balancing performance and flexibility for diverse low-precision workloads.

title: A Smart Ring for Long-term Blood Pressure Monitoring.
abstract: Traditional cuff-based blood pressure (BP) monitoring methods suffer from inherent limitations in user discomfort and intermittent measurement. In contrast, photoplethysmography (PPG)-based BP estimation provides a promising alternative. However, several critical challenges remain in PPG-based BP estimation. First, prior evidence indicates that finger-worn devices can yield signals with higher feasibility and quality than wrist-worn devices. Second, long-term variations in blood pressure have not been sufficiently investigated in this field. To address these challenges, this study develops a novel smart ring platform and collects samples to train and evaluate the proposed model. A large-scale dataset comprising 116,995 samples from 96 subjects is constructed to evaluate long-term performance. The trained model achieves mean absolute errors (MAE) of 11.20 mmHg for systolic blood pressure (SBP) and 7.51 mmHg for diastolic blood pressure (DBP). These results demonstrate that a smart ring provides a comfortable and practical solution for continuous blood pressure management in personalized healthcare.

title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Optimal Scheduling for Virtual Power Plant Participation in Energy and Regulation Markets.
abstract: This paper addresses the day-ahead joint optimization problem of a virtual power plant (VPP) that participates in both the energy and regulation markets, and formulates a day-ahead scheduling model that explicitly captures the coupling among multiple markets. Considering that traditional analytical model-based optimization approaches suffer from high modeling complexity and limited generalization capability when facing high-dimensional decision spaces, strong nonlinear couplings, and uncertainties, a reinforcement learning-based solution is introduced to solve the proposed optimization model. Building upon the Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) framework, a Dueling network architecture is further incorporated to decouple the state value function from the action advantage function, thereby enhancing learning efficiency and decision-making stability under diverse operating conditions.

title: Top-V: A Flexible and Programmable Top-K Acceleration Framework Based on the RISC-V ISA.
abstract: The efficient deployment of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models on edge devices is hindered by the Top-K expert selection bottleneck, where latency can exceed matrix multiplication by up to 27× on specialized hardware. Software algorithms suffer from poor parallelism due to conditional branches and data dependencies, while hardware designs face trade-offs among flexibility, programmability, and compatibility. To address these challenges, this work proposes Top-V, a flexible and programmable Top-K acceleration framework based on the RISC-V Vector (RVV) Extension. Top-V introduces a Reconfigurable Reduced Bitonic Sorter (R-RBS) generator that automatically produces energy-efficient sorting structures for diverse configurations. A custom VTOPK instruction is proposed to provide an efficient software interface supporting INT4/8/16 and FP16/32 data types. A dedicated Top-K hardware unit is integrated into the open-source Ara RISC-V vector processor, realizing a hardware-software co-design solution. FPGA evaluations show up to 3.07× and 5.24× speedups over the min-heap and standard RVV-based sorting, respectively, offering both efficiency and programmability for edge MoE deployment.

title: A Yield-enhanced and Highly Reliable 512k-bit HZO-based 2T2C FeRAM Chip Enabled with Charge Pump.
abstract: In this work, we present a low-power and high-yield 2D FeRAM test chip based on Hf0.5Zr0.5O2(HZO) thin films for advanced embedded nonvolatile memory (eNVM) applications. A novel ferroelectric capacitor (FeCAP) with a capacitor-under-bitline (CUB) configuration is introduced to effectively mitigate the fatigue phenomenon and enhance device endurance. A 512 kb 2T2C FeRAM test chip was developed by integrating the high-performance FeCAP with an 8.5 nm HZO film in a 2D MFM structure on a 180 nm CMOS platform. Moreover, a charge pump-assisted design enhances the read and write yield, decreasing the bit-error rate (BER) from 25% to 0%. The proposed design achieves an additional yield improvement of about 30% under wide temperature and voltage. The results demonstrate the high reliability and strong potential of the proposed FeRAM architecture, paving the way for large-scale, high-performance, and highly reliable FeRAM applications.

title: TurboRANSAC: A Fully GPU-Accelerated RANSAC Framework for Robust Estimation.
abstract: Robust model estimation plays a central role in geometric computer vision, enabling applications such as camera localization, motion estimation, and 3D reconstruction. Among many techniques, Random Sample Consensus (RANSAC) is widely adopted for its robustness to outliers. However, existing RANSAC variants commonly rely on CPU-based sequential processing, leading to computational inefficiency that limits their suitability for real-time and large-scale scenarios. This challenge is heightened by the rise of learning-based pipelines optimized for GPU acceleration, where CPU-bound RANSAC becomes a bottleneck within predominantly GPU-centric workflows. In this paper, we propose TurboRANSAC, a fully GPU-accelerated framework that parallelizes all key stages, including sampling, hypothesis generation, scoring, and refinement, directly on the GPU. Unlike methods that optimize isolated components, TurboRANSAC provides a unified and scalable solution applicable to a broad spectrum of geometric estimation problems.

title: An Efficient Optimization Framework for Netlist Partitioning by Co-optimizing Moves and Replications.
abstract: The evolution of 2.5D multi-die FPGA architectures presents significant timing closure challenges due to large inter-die communication delays. To address this, we propose an automated Electronic Design Automation (EDA) framework that transforms standard design files into a timing-aware hypergraph. Our framework then minimizes inter-die delays by synergistically co-optimizing node movement and logic replication, guided by a unified, hop-aware gain model. Experimental results on large-scale benchmarks demonstrate an average 27% reduction in total hop distance, validating the effectiveness of our partitioning strategy.

title: HOLMES: Hierarchical Optimization with poLygonal ModEling for Large-Scale AMS Placement.
abstract: Physical placement is a critical determinant of analog/mixed-signal (AMS) circuit performance. For large-scale designs, existing hierarchical methods lose accuracy due to oversimplification of subcircuits, while flat approaches become computationally infeasible for large circuits. In this paper, we propose HOLMES, a hierarchical placement framework that systematically addresses this accuracy-efficiency trade-off. HOLMES maintains hierarchical design representations with tree-based optimization structures and performs bottom-up refinement to model subcircuits using polygonal representations. For device-level optimization, the framework provides a delayed decision strategy that co-optimizes critical parameters such as the number of fingers (NF) in MOS transistors. Experiments show that our framework achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods on smaller circuits while delivering excellent placement quality for large circuits.

title: UniOOD: A Unified Framework for Domain Generalization and Out-of-Distribution Detection in Time Series.
abstract: Time series modeling faces two challenges: out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization to correctly classify sequences from distribution shift domains, and OOD detection to identify anomalous or previously unseen sequences. Existing methods usually address these separately, which limits their applicability in real-world scenarios. In this work, we propose UniOOD, a unified framework that tackles both challenges simultaneously. UniOOD divides sequences into patches, encodes each as a latent Gaussian distribution, and aggregates them into a sequence-level posterior via learned weighting. By aligning sequence posteriors with learnable class priors while maintaining inter-class separation, UniOOD learns representations that are both generalizable and discriminative. The distance between posteriors and class priors provides an intrinsic OOD score, enabling detection of unseen sequences without prior exposure. Experiments show UniOOD achieves state-of-the-art classification, strong OOD generalization, and effective OOD detection within a single unified model.

title: An RRAM-based Neuromorphic Sleep Monitoring System for Energy-efficient Edge Healthcare Applications.
abstract: Sleep monitoring is essential for assessing human health, but existing sleep stage classification methods based on deep learning still demand high computational resources and energy, limiting their deployment on wearable and edge devices. To address this challenge, we propose an RRAM-based in-memory computing architecture that integrates EEG signal preprocessing with spiking neural network (SNN) inference. A precision-preserving mapping strategy, termed Split Kernel Value Mapping, is developed to improve the accuracy of analog FIR-Hilbert filtering in the presence of device non-idealities such as conductance drift and read noise. Fabricated in a 180 nm process, the proposed system achieves a 0.99 correlation between hardware and software filtering results, and attains 85.3% on-chip classification accuracy comparable to its software counterpart, demonstrating the potential of RRAM-based sleep monitoring for energy-efficient edge healthcare applications.

title: Enhancing SPAD HDR Imaging via Cross-Modality Frequency-Spatial Fusion.
abstract: High dynamic range (HDR) imaging with single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) opens new possibilities for passive imaging under extreme illumination owing to their single-photon sensitivity. However, SPAD images often suffer from low resolution, high noise, and spectral imbalance, leading to structural degradation and detail loss. To address these issues, a cross-modality frequency–spatial fusion framework is proposed for SPAD HDR imaging. First, a Frequency-Domain Fusion Module (FDFM) aligns frequency spectra to mitigate spectral inconsistencies, enhancing textures and suppressing noise. Second, a structure-aware modulation mechanism injects high-resolution structural priors from CMOS into SPAD features to guide spatial fusion and enhance fidelity. Finally, a luminance-guided multi-directional refinement block (MADB-L) adaptively separates and aggregates illumination features along distinct orientations, reducing cross-boundary mixing and suppressing artifacts. Experiments show a 2.02 dB mean PSNRµgain over state-of-the-art methods on simulated datasets and the best visual results on both simulated and real-captured data with clearer, artifact-free HDR reconstructions.

title: Optimizing the Energy Efficiency in SAR ADCs with Linear/Exponential Comparator Biasing.
abstract: This paper presents comparator biasing techniques for energy-efficient optimization in successive-approximation-register (SAR) analog-to-digital converters (ADCs). The proposed approaches leverage the non-uniform decision complexity across SAR conversion cycles by employing a biasing-pattern register (BPR) to dynamically adjust the bias current of the comparator preamplifier through a current-mode digital-to-analog converter (IDAC). Four BPR-driven biasing profiles - namely dual-mode, linear, exponential, and hybrid are introduced and evaluated against the conventional uniform one. Simulations and analysis of an 8-bit SAR ADC demonstrate that the hybrid biasing scheme achieves approximately a 67% improvement in the normalized Walden figure of merit (FoMWN) compared to the static biasing scheme. Notably, this implies that the improvement in-terms of power reduction is achieved with sub 1 dB degradation in signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR).

title: Multimodal Smart Insole with Crossbar Crosstalk Compensation for Fall-Risk Prediction.
abstract: Gait analysis has always relied on latent indicators that can provide early warnings about underlying health conditions. Fall-risk prediction is one of the most important applications. In this paper, we present a portable smart insole system that couples a 253-sensor plantar pressure array with a 6-DoF IMU and an end-to-end deep learning fall-risk prediction pipeline. A double-frame sensing scheme expands the sensor's dynamic range under different pressure loadings. To suppress sneak-path crosstalk, a compact U-Net (33×15 input) reconstructs a crosstalk-free matrix from a cross-bar array, achieving R2= 0.9307. The clean pressure map and IMU signals are input into a 3D-CNN + Transformer encoder for joint pose regression (13×3) and fall-risk prediction, achieving accuracy of up to 91%. With this indicator, we can determine whether the cumulative probability of a person falling is steadily increasing over time. This further suggests that their physical health status may warrant additional examination, allowing the system to issue an early warning to the user. Fall itself is instantaneous, but the factors that lead to a fall are issues worth monitoring over the long term.

title: An All-NMOS Adaptive Active Gate Driver with Detection-Free CSIV Spike Suppression.
authors: L. S. S. Pavan Kumar Chodisetti
abstract: This paper presents a novel SiC MOSFET gate driver designed using TSMC 0.18-µm CMOS HV technology, featuring a fully NMOS output stage with self-triggered oscillation suppression and adaptive drive currents. The Boost-Damp buffer activates only during Common Source Inductance Voltage (CSIV) spike events using intrinsic low-pass filtering, avoiding extra detection circuits. An Active Float Bridge enables safe signal transfer across multiple floating grounds, while a feedback mechanism dynamically adjusts the drive current during switching, including the Miller plateau. Post-layout simulations show 28.9 ns rise time, 20.5 ns fall time, 138 mW power @ 500 kHz, 983 µm × 1678 µm overall chip area, and a core area of 678.31 µm × 1451.9 µm, making it compact and efficient for high-speed SiC applications.

title: Fast and Accurate SystemVerilog Framework for Mixed-Signal Modeling of PAM-4 Wireline Transceivers.
abstract: This paper presents a SystemVerilog-based modeling and simulation methodology for a 4-level pulse-amplitude-modulation (PAM-4) transceiver. The framework is developed to address verification challenges in complex analog-to-digital converter (ADC)-based mixed-signal systems, where conventional circuit-level simulations suffer from prohibitively long execution time. Two key modeling techniques to significantly improve simulation efficiency are introduced in this work. For the time-interleaved ADC (TI-ADC), a counter-based equivalent circuit model is employed to capture dominant rank-1 mismatch errors while substantially reducing modeling complexity. In addition, for digital clock and data recovery (CDR), a statistical bit-error-rate (BER) evaluation approach based on XMODEL primitives is adopted as an alternative to conventional time-domain analog-mixed-signal (AMS) simulations. This modeling framework enables accurate verification of critical transceiver performance metrics, such as jitter tolerance (JTOL), within a 30-minute simulation window. Compared to conventional timedomain simulations, which require more than 12 hours to perform, the proposed approach achieves approximately a 24× improvement in simulation speed.

title: Hardware-Efficient Softmax and Layer Normalization with Guaranteed Normalization for Edge Devices.
abstract: In Transformer models, non-GEMM (non-General Matrix Multiplication) operations—especially Softmax and Layer Normalization (LayerNorm)—often dominate hardware cost due to their nonlinear nature. To address this, previous approximation studies mainly target rank-oriented tasks, which is acceptable for classification. However, edge Natural Language Processing (NLP) applications and edge generative AI are largely evaluated based on score-oriented tasks, so normalization-guaranteed nonGEMM operations are essential. We propose a hardware-efficient Softmax and LayerNorm with Guaranteed Normalization for Edge devices. Our design employs hardware-efficient approximation methods while preserving the normalization (Softmax: Σp=1, LayerNorm: σ =1). Our architecture is described in Verilog HDL and synthesized using the Samsung 28nm CMOS process. In accuracy evaluation, we achieve high accuracy with minimal degradation; GLUE +0.07%, SQuAD -0.01%, perplexity -0.09%. Implementation results show that our architecture is small; 942µm2for Softmax, 1199µm2for LayerNorm. Compared to the state of the art, we achieve up to 11x and 14x reduction in area, respectively.

title: SeVeDo: A Heterogeneous Transformer Accelerator for Low-Bit Inference via Hierarchical Group Quantization and SVD-Guided Mixed Precision.
abstract: Low-bit quantization is a promising technique for efficient transformer inference by reducing computational and memory overhead. However, aggressive bitwidth reduction remains challenging due to activation outliers, leading to accuracy degradation. Existing methods, such as outlier-handling and group quantization, achieve high accuracy but incur substantial energy consumption. To address this, we propose SeVeDo, an energy-efficient SVD-based heterogeneous accelerator that structurally separates outlier-sensitive components into a high-precision low-rank path, while the remaining computations are executed in a low-bit residual datapath with group quantization. To further enhance efficiency, Hierarchical Group Quantization (HGQ) combines coarse-grained floating-point scaling with fine-grained shifting, effectively reducing dequantization cost. Also, SVD-guided mixed precision (SVD-MP) statically allocates higher bitwidths to precision-sensitive components identified through low-rank decomposition, thereby minimizing floating-point operation cost. Experimental results show that SeVeDo achieves a peak energy efficiency of 13.8TOPS/W, surpassing conventional designs, with 12.7TOPS/W on ViT-Base and 13.4TOPS/W on Llama2-7B benchmarks.

title: A Compute-in-Memory Based on Approximate Multiplication with a Calibration Adder.
abstract: This paper presents an energy-efficient compute-in-memory (CIM) architecture with approximated multiplication and a calibration adder. The proposed CIM applies Mitchell’s approximate multiplication to implement multiply-accumulate (MAC) with a single addition operation for multiplication, regardless of input precision, thereby reducing both latency and power consumption of arithmetic operations. Furthermore, the precision degradation caused by approximate multiplication can be improved by approximately 3.4% on average using the proposed calibration adder (C-Adder). Each computing element utilizes an 8T-SRAM-based structure with separate local and global read bit lines to enable parallel MAC operations and further enhance computational throughput. Implemented in a 28-nm CMOS process, the proposed CIM achieves 38.65 TOPS/W energy efficiency, 0.05003 TOPS/mm2area efficiency, and 91.86 % inference accuracy on ResNet-20 with CIFAR-10.

title: PRIMAL: Processing-In-Memory based Low-Rank Adaptation for LLM Inference Accelerator.
abstract: This paper presents PRIMAL, a processing-in-memory (PIM) based large language model (LLM) inference accelerator with low-rank adaptation (LoRA). PRIMAL integrates heterogeneous PIM processing elements (PEs), interconnected by 2D-mesh inter-PE computational network (IPCN). A novel SRAM reprogramming and power gating (SRPG) scheme enables pipelined LoRA updates and sub-linear power scaling by overlapping reconfiguration with computation and gating idle resources. PRIMAL employs optimized spatial mapping and dataflow orchestration to minimize communication overhead, and achieves $1.5\times$ throughput and $25\times$ energy efficiency over NVIDIA H100 with LoRA rank 8 (Q,V) on Llama-13B.

title: STEAM-SSM: A Streaming-Tiled Efficient Accelerator for Mamba-2 SSM on FPGA.
abstract: This paper proposes STEAM-SSM, a Streaming-Tiled Efficient Accelerator for Mamba-2 SSM. Recently, the state space models (SSMs) like Mamba have shown excellent performance for long sequence modeling. However, an SSM block introduces unique computing patterns, such as element-wise operations or non-linear activations, which cause sub-optimal performance on general-purpose hardware like CPUs or GPUs. To address the problem, this work presents an FPGA-based accelerator for SSM blocks. Specifically, STEAM incorporates three key features: (i) forwarding intermediate results on-chip to avoid off-chip materialization, (ii) optimizing tiling to maximize performance-per-resource, and (iii) selecting an HP-major for contiguous DDR bursts and on-chip reuse. Modeled with Verilog HDL and implemented on a Xilinx Alveo U250 FPGA board, STEAM achieves a latency of 6.49 µs for a single-layer SSM block of the Mamba2-130M with half precision (FP16), yielding a speedup of 31.2× compared to that of an Nvidia RTX 4070 Ti SUPER GPU.

title: Analytical Origin and Mitigation of Third-Order Tones in 4-Phase BLE Backscatter.
abstract: This paper reports a repeatable spectral artifact observed in 4-phase (I/Q) BLE backscatter transmitters operating with single-sideband modulation. Despite nominal 90° Hilbert phasing, a dominant third-order spur appears near the image sideband. We show that this artifact originates from the four-step phase staircase combined with the short periodicity of the {2,3}-tick fractional-divider dwell pattern used for BLE subcarrier generation. While the fundamental tone is mapped to the desired sideband, the third harmonic is deterministically placed on the opposite sideband. To mitigate this effect without disturbing BLE timing or CPFSK modulation, a frame-dithered 2/3-dwell mapping technique is proposed. It preserves the exact per-bit dwell budgets while breaking frame-to-frame phase coherence. Measurement results demonstrate a reduction of the third-order spur from −61.8/−63.5 dBm to −66.9/−66.6 dBm and corresponding improvements in SFDR to 15.7/15.5 dBc and IRR to 15.5 dB, with negligible impact on the fundamental tone.

title: A Perturbation-Based Low-Overhead IQ Calibration Scheme for RF Receivers.
abstract: This paper presents a low-complexity IQ (in-phase and quadrature) mismatch calibration scheme for direct-conversion RF receivers. Accumulated phase and gain mismatches in the IQ receive path degrade the receiver’s ability to reject interference at image frequencies. We propose a generic, digital-domain, perturbation-based calibration scheme that samples the receiver’s ADC outputs to autonomously estimate and apply gain and phase compensation in the digital back-end. Power, timing and area efficiency of the proposed digital calibration scheme are demonstrated by implementation in a 1V 65 nm CMOS process. The design achieves a compact on-chip area of 155x500 µm2. Assuming 9-bit ADC outputs, the proposed scheme corrects raw image rejection ratios (IRR) to better than -44 dB, from uncorrected values as high as -25 dB, with a worst-case calibration time of 16 µs and power consumption of 1.89 mW (using a 100 MHz clock). In comparison with existing IQ calibration approaches, the proposed method offers a faster and computationally efficient on-chip implementation without requiring external spectrum measurements or compute resources.

title: High-Performance AES-GCM Hardware via Circuit and Architecture Co-Design of AES and GHASH.
abstract: Advanced Encryption Standard in Galois/Counter Mode (AES-GCM) is one of the most widely deployed authenticated encryption schemes, offering both confidentiality and integrity. With the rapid growth of data-intensive applications, encryption systems must enhance their throughput and hardware efficiency to prevent performance bottlenecks in overall system. In the AES datapath, we adopt redundant-basis Substitution Box (S-Box) for SubBytes and integrate two parallel AES modules to improve frequency and throughput. In the Galois Hash (GHASH) module, we design a two-stage pipelined multiplier based on the Overlap-Free Karatsuba (OFK) algorithm, which shortens the critical path and reduces the number of required hash key precomputations. The proposed architecture is implemented in Verilog and synthesized using Synopsys Design Compiler with TSMC 130 nm and 180 nm standard cell libraries. The results show that the proposed design achieves an operating frequency of up to 625 MHz and 160 Gbps throughput at 130 nm, corresponding to a 2.68× improvement in hardware efficiency compared to the best previous implementation. At 180 nm, the proposed design achieves 1.22× higher hardware efficiency than the state-of-the-art work. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed Circuit and Architecture Co-Design for high-performance cryptographic applications.

title: A Membrane Potential Communication-based Network-on-chip for Merge-core-free Spiking Neural Network Deployment.
abstract: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) on multi-core neuromorphic hardware often rely on split-and-merge strategies that require dedicated merge cores and model retraining due to the non-summable nature of discrete spike signals. This paper presents a high-efficiency network-on-chip (NoC) architecture that eliminates merge cores by transmitting and summing continuous membrane potentials (MP) instead of spikes. We design a heterogeneous SNN core with time-division multiplexing (TDM) that natively consumes and produces MP data, and a fully-connected router that integrates addition units on output channels to perform lossless, parallel MP summation in flight. The co-designed system supports multi-core collaborative deployment and cross-layer MP residual connections without model retraining. Implemented in 28 nm CMOS, the proposed core achieves a peak energy efficiency of 0.379 pJ/SOP at 100 MHz and 0.72 V, which is 23.25% of that reported in related works. The approach achieves a maximum 65% core count reduction compared to traditional solutions when deploying SNNs on NoC.

title: A Low Noise Electronic Platform for monitoring and stimulation of Biohybrid Machines.
abstract: Biohybrid machines (BHMs) integrate living actuators with artificial components to achieve biologically inspired motion and adaptive behavior. One of the main challenges is precisely detecting the electrical response of soft biological actuators using compact, low-noise electronics. In this work, we present a custom PCB-based acquisition platform employing organic field-effect transistors (OFETs) as strain sensors. The system features a dual-stage amplification circuit allowing independent selection of the transistor bias voltages via a programmable digital-to-analog converter. A dedicated drift current compensation unit ensures low-noise operation and prevents amplifier saturation during long-term measurements. The design integrates a programmable stimulation unit that enables controlled actuation of the BHM. Experimental validation showed a Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of up to 42 dB for 2 nA input signals and the ability to acquire the mechanical deformations detected through the OFET strain sensor. Combining low-noise signal acquisition with programmable current stimulation, the proposed platform lays the foundations for future bidirectional interaction with biohybrid actuators.

title: UniMAC: Multi-Precision MAC with a Unified Computing Architecture for Efficient Large Language Model Inference.
abstract: Quantization techniques vary considerably in their requirements for computational precision. Although prior works have introduced various multi-precision multiply-accumulate (MAC) units, most offer limited precision coverage. Moreover, most designs focus on standard arithmetic and lack optimizations for inference in large language models (LLMs). To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes UniMAC, a multi-precision MAC architecture that unifies integer, floating-point, and FP-INT operations within a single computing datapath by employing a new General-Purpose Data Partitioning (GPDP) method and an Iterative Neighbor Grouping Scheduling (INGS) strategy. In addition, we implement two acceleration modes for FP16 guided by an on-the-fly activation-to-activation (act-to-act) search (OAS) algorithm to improve throughput and efficiency in act-to-act computations, a dominant contributor to inference latency in LLMs with long contexts. Compared with prior works, the proposed design supports a wider range of precision formats while delivering up to 3.9× higher energy efficiency in FP8 and 2× for act-to-act computations in FP16.

title: A High Dynamic Range and Energy-Efficient Readout Circuit for Versatile Electrochemical Sensing.
abstract: This paper presents the design and hardware verification results of a readout circuit that is suitable for versatile electrochemical sensing. The circuit can perform high dynamic range direct digitization of sensor currents using a Delta-Delta-Sigma modulator readout architecture. A return-to-zero (RTZ) feedback structure is used which allows duty cycling the currents from both the sensor and the feedback current-steering digital-to-analog converter (IDAC) in the modulator. A prototype chip was fabricated using 130nm standard CMOS process, and the chip measurement results verify that the readout circuit achieved a peak signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) of 59.31dB. Covering a wide current range of 0-120 µA, the circuit is feasible for a variety of electrochemical sensors. As an example, the chip was tested in an electrochemical testing experiment together with a commercially available graphene field effect transistor (GFET). The results show that the chip achieved accurate measurement results that are consistent with results obtained from a full-size precision lab instrument, making it a good candidate for portable electrochemical sensing applications.

title: A Dual-Output Resonant Current-Mode Wireless Power Receiver With Shared-Inductor Energy Replenishing for Neuron Stimulation.
abstract: This paper presents a resonant current-mode (RCM) wireless power receiver achieving both normal dual-output regulation and shared-inductor energy replenishing for implantable neuron stimulation. By introducing a shared-inductor boost-converter configuration, the energy stored in one output can be directly shared to another output in proposed RCM receiver without wireless power waste. Therefore, only three transistors and three off-chip capacitors are adopted, which optimizes the efficiency and compactness. The proposed wireless power receiver is designed in a 0.18-μm BCD process and regulates two output voltages of 5V and 3V. Simulation results show that the peak power conversion efficiency reaches 90.8%. Thanks to the proposed shared-inductor energy replenishing method, the receiver extended the peak output power range by 9.4x with a maximum output power of 51mW. For a high-voltage output load switching between 0.2mA and 4mA, the transition between the normal voltage regulation and the energy replenishing is fast and smooth.

title: A Power-efficient 5x Compressive Sensing Readout IC for 3D-stacked CMOS Image Sensor.
abstract: This paper presents a power-efficient compressive sensing (CS) readout integrated circuit (IC) for 3D-stacked CMOS image sensors (CIS). The proposed readout architecture consists of a dynamic source follower (SF), a switched-capacitor (SC) multiplier, and a two-step coarse-fine SAR-SS ADC. To improve energy efficiency while ensuring image reconstruction quality, the following techniques have been introduced: First, the dynamic SF decouples its power consumption from the high pixel supply voltage, while eliminating static power during ADC conversion. Second, a deterministic measurement matrix eliminates column weight wiring and the global pseudo-random number generators (PRNG), which reduces the power and area overhead. Third, the two-step coarse-fine quantization scheme reduces the SS ADC’s input range by a factor of 8, significantly lowering the counter toggle frequency and corresponding dynamic power. Additionally, the sampling capacitors of the dynamic SF are repurposed as both the computation capacitors in the SC multiplier and the capacitive digital-to-analog converter (CDAC) of the SAR ADC, enhancing the area efficiency of column readout circuits. The proposed CS readout IC achieves 5× image compression at 60 fps while maintaining high reconstruction quality (PSNR>33.2 dB, SSIM>0.91). With a total power consumption of 268 uW, the design achieves an overall energy efficiency of 66 pJ/pixel•frame.

title: FlexMulSim: A Full-Precision Hardware Reuse Simulator for Power, Area, and Utilization Efficiency.
abstract: The increasing adoption of low-bit and mixed-precision arithmetic in AI accelerators demands hardware that is both flexible and energy-efficient. Conventional architectures using dedicated multipliers for each precision (e.g., INT8, FP16) suffer from poor utilization and excessive area and power overhead. This paper presents FlexMulSim, a simulator for evaluating hardware reuse in multi-precision multiplier arrays. FlexMulSim provides unified analysis of Power, Performance, and Area (PPA) across reuse strategies, including INT–INT, INT–FP, and FP–FP sharing. By reusing low-bit multipliers (e.g., 4-bit) for higher-precision computations, FlexMulSim achieves significant improvements in area, power, and utilization efficiency, offering a practical framework for designing next-generation reconfigurable AI accelerators.

title: A 2RW Dual-Port 8T-SRAM Macro with Bitline Leakage Current Tracking and Read-Write Arbitration.
abstract: Dual-port static random-access memory (SRAM) is often adopted to maximize data throughput for high-bandwidth applications like registers and caches. However, conventional dual-port SRAM suffers from inherent bitline leakage current and read-write disturbance issues. This work presents a highly stable dual-port 8T-SRAM macro design. The macro uses a one-sided leakage compensation circuit (LCC) module to enhance the tolerable ability of bitline leakage current. The macro uses a double pump CLK generation to achieve dual-port read and write operations through a time-sharing scheme. A read-write arbitration circuit is proposed to solve the potential read-write disturbance issues in dual-port SRAMs. Under 28 nm CMOS process, simulation results manifest the maximum tolerable leakage current is 240 μA and maximum operating frequency can reach 1.6 GHz at 0.9 V.

title: High-Throughput and Configurable Modular Multiplier Using Extended Montgomery Reduction.
abstract: The growing demand for information security and privacy protection has prompted the development of post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and homomorphic encryption (HE) schemes. A fundamental operation in these algorithms is the computation-intensive modular multiplication, necessitating hardware optimization. This paper presents an eXtended Montgomery modular reduction (X-MR) algorithm designed to reduce complexity and enhance the reconfiguration capabilities of the hardware implementations. Using the X-MR algorithm, two modular multiplier hardware architectures—an iterative version and an unfolding version—are proposed and evaluated to explore the area-throughput trade-off under various parameters. The experimental results demonstrate improvements in areanormalized throughput (TP/Area) of 2.09×, 5.64× and 1.22× for 32/60/64-bit parameter settings, respectively, compared to prior art. To further evaluate the performance of X-MR algorithm, the number theoretic transform (NTT), a dominant subroutine in lattice-based PQC and HE algorithms, is implemented as a use case. The FPGA implementation of the NTT achieves a high throughput of 15.6 Gbps at (N, ⌈log2q⌉) = (4096, 60).

title: VCCU: A RISC-V-based Edge Computing Processor Capable of General-Purpose Computing and Infrared Image Processing.
abstract: Since neural network algorithms based on infrared images have been applied in many fields, the demand for edge computing devices tailored for infrared images has increased significantly in recent years. To simultaneously achieve general-purpose computing and infrared image processing in edge computing devices, we can use RISC-V as the CPU for edge computing and realize various customized data processing through instructions. Therefore, this paper proposes a RISC-V-based coprocessor named Vector Computing Co-Unit (VCCU) which integrates four core functional modules: 1) a Convolution Unit with FIFO modules for efficient data reuse and parallel convolution operations; 2) a Dot Product Unit with multi-precision Processing Elements (PEs)—each PE contains 64 4-bit multipliers configurable into 8/16/32-bit multipliers; 3) a Quantization Unit that directly quantizes 14–16-bit infrared images from the Read-Out Integrated Circuit to 8-bit; and 4) a Vector Mapping Unit that maps 3D multi-channel feature images and convolution kernels to 2D vectors. Synthesized with the 55nm process, VCCU achieves a peak performance of 168 GOPS and a peak energy efficiency of 1193 GOPS/W, while supporting 4-32-bit multi-precision computation. Its peak performance is 2.26×-34.7× higher and energy efficiency is 1.05×-2.09× higher than those of similar RISC-V edge devices.

title: A power-and-area efficient AFE with continuous time-gain compensation of 48 dB gain range and ±0.6 dB gain error for Miniature Ultrasound Probes.
abstract: This manuscript presents an analog front-end (AFE) with dB-linear continuous time-gain compensation (TGC) for miniature ultrasound probes. The AFE is composed by a single-stage resistor-feedback amplifier. To obtain the fourth-order dB-linear time-gain compensation, a dual T-Network TGC(DTN-TGC), both the input and feedback resistor dividing into T-type resistor network, is proposed. By employing MOSFET-based resistors, the closed-loop gain exhibits a dB-linear dependence on their gate voltages. These gate voltages are generated by charging and discharging capacitors using nanoampere-level currents, with the slopes meticulously designed to match the attenuation characteristics of echoes. This AFE is fully integrated without external ramp control signals. It was fabricated in 180 nm CMOS process, achieving a gain range of 48 dB with ±0.6 dB gain error and a minimum input-referred noise density of 12.3 ${\mathbf{nV}}/\sqrt {{\text{Hz}}} $. The AFE occupies a core area of only 0.0085 mm2and consumes 0.65 mW power, achieving significant improvements in both area and power efficiency compared to the state-of-the-art designs.

title: Visual Geometric 6-DoF Grasping: A Multi-View Framework with Sparse RGB Observations.
abstract: Current robotic grasping systems predominantly rely on single-view RGB-D grasp detection, which critically necessitates a depth sensor. While pure multi-view RGB estimation methods have emerged recently, those largely based on Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) often confront the challenge of inaccurate geometric reconstruction, which subsequently reduces grasp prediction reliability. To address these limitations, we propose a novel Visual Geometric 6-DoF Grasping framework (VG-Grasp) that integrates sparse-view 3D reconstruction with heatmap-guided grasp generation. Leveraging transformer-based cross-view attention, our method reconstructs dense point clouds from a few RGB images and predicts stable grasp poses without requiring direct depth input. Evaluated on the GraspNet-1Billion dataset, our approach significantly outperforms existing RGB-based 6-DoF Grasping methods, especially on seen and similar objects. Real-robot experiments demonstrate a 61% grasp success rate and 83% completion rate, validating the effectiveness and practicality of our depth-free solution.

title: An Ultra-Low Power Data Retention Flip-Flop with 25.8 pW Leakage in 28 nm CMOS.
abstract: Data retention flip-flops (DR-FFs) can help processors in duty-cycled battery-powered IoT devices to maintain the state data during sleep mode, helping them quickly recover from the previous state upon wake-up to reduce latency. This paper introduces a new ultra-low-leakage balloon-based DR-FF that implements data retention using ultra-low-power (ULP) diodes with transistors biased in the super-cut-off region. Implemented in both 180 nm and 28 nm CMOS technology, the proposed DR-FF shows a 0.04 pW / 25.8 pW in sleep mode leakage power, which is more than 3× lower than prior CMOS DR-FFs. Also, it shows faster and more energy-efficient mode transitions than other balloon-based DR-FFs. The overall performance of the proposed DR-FF makes it a promising solution for low-power, duty-cycled IoT processors that require low wake-up latency.

title: A PN-Assisted Dynamic-Window Interstage Gain Calibration for Pipeline-SAR ADCs.
abstract: This paper presents an input dither injection combined with a dynamic window technique for inter-stage gain calibration in pipeline-SAR ADCs. Foreground calibration is performed by matching two pseudo-random injection signals, where inter-stage redundancy is utilized only near full-scale input, effectively overcoming the amplitude limitation imposed by comparator offset in conventional methods. This allows the use of larger pseudo-random signals, significantly accelerating convergence. A dynamic window further filters valid samples, minimizing the influence of input signal and capacitor mismatch on the calibration process. Simulation confirms effective inter-stage gain correction after 5×105points. Fabricated in 65nm CMOS, a 12-bit 200-MS/s prototype achieves 58.66dB SNDR and 73.6dB SFDR, representing 8.4dB and 12.5dB improvements after calibration.

title: A 1GS/s 8b 2× Time-Interleaved SAR ADC with Speed-Enhanced Techniques in 65nm CMOS.
abstract: A 1GS/s 8b 2-way time-interleaved (TI) SAR ADC with several optimization techniques is presented. First, a two-stage comparator with complementary input pairs and bootstrapped interstage connection mitigates common-mode variation, clock feedthrough, and a long latch-setup, thereby shortening the comparison cycle. An asynchronous clock generator with separated edge-control paths precisely adjusts delay and shortens the critical path for speed-matching. Second, a bridge-structure with a novel VCM-based switching circuit is employed to accelerate DAC settling. Third, a correlation-based feedforward detection is proposed to speed up the timing skew estimation in the digital domain mismatch calibration. The prototype TIADC fabricated in 65nm CMOS achieves 41.69dB SNDR and 59.54dB SFDR at Nyquist input and 1.2V supply, consuming 7.85mW and occupying a 0.037-mm2core area.

title: A ML-based Robust Channel Estimation Enhancer Against Multi-Tone Jamming in OFDM systems.
abstract: Orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) systems rely critically on accurate channel estimation to ensure reliable communication but are highly susceptible to jamming attacks. Multi-tone jamming is particularly challenging as it provides a unified representation of diverse interference patterns through adjustable tone spacing and power allocation. Existing works, including neural network (NN)-based techniques, primarily target individual tasks such as channel estimation, jamming detection, or mitigation, rather than addressing them jointly. To overcome these limitations, we propose a two-stage convolutional neural network (CNN)-based variational autoencoder (VAE) framework for joint channel estimation and jamming robustness. The proposed method refines the least square (LS) estimates while generalizing effectively across both jammed and unjammed conditions. Unlike conventional approaches, it achieves accurate and resilient channel estimation without explicit jamming detection or prior knowledge of the jammer. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework maintains robust performance under multi-tone jamming, achieving a bit error rate (BER) of 1% with only a 0.7 dB increase in Eb/N0compared to unjammed operation conditions.

title: A Dual-Mode Dual-Band RTWO Covering X and K Bands with Phase Interpolation Based Phase Calibration Achieving 180.4 dBc/Hz FoM.
abstract: This work proposes a dual-mode, dual-band RTWO architecture implemented in 22-nm FDSOI CMOS. The design achieves stable operation across both the X-band (10.06–11.69 GHz) and K-band (19.77–22.75 GHz) through symmetric mode switching, while exhibiting improved phase noise performance. A phase interpolator is incorporated to enable precise calibration of multi-phase outputs, effectively mitigating phase errors inherent in direct RTWO sampling. Measurement results show phase noise of -111.5 dBc/Hz at 10.06 GHz and -107.6 dBc/Hz at 19.77 GHz @ 1-MHz offset, corresponding to Figures-of-Merit up to 180.4 dBc/Hz.

title: IDIM: In-situ DRAM-based Ising Machine with All-to-All Connectivity.
abstract: Ising machines offer a promising hardware solution to combinatorial optimization problems but still face scalability and cost challenges. In this work, we present IDIM, an in-situ DRAM-based Ising machine that exploits in-memory computing within DRAM subarrays to enable large-scale, fully connected spin updates with lightweight hardware overhead. By introducing lightweight logic into sense amplifiers and redesigning an in-memory DRAM adder, IDIM minimizes data movement and significantly improves area utilization. Prototyping results show that IDIM achieves over 166× speedup in annealing time compared to conventional computational substrates, while the additional peripheral circuitry only accounts for 3.6% of the baseline area.

title: SPPA: A Self-Adaptive Pruning and Parallel Annealing Algorithm for Ising Computing.
abstract: The simulated annealing (SA) algorithm is a widely used reference method for iterative Ising annealers, but its sequential spin updates restrict parallelization and lead to slow convergence in large fully connected systems. Parallel annealing algorithms accelerate convergence by updating multiple spins simultaneously, but this requires evaluating spin-flip probabilities for all spins at every step, leading to redundant computations and substantial hardware demand. We introduce Self-Adaptive Pruning and Parallel Annealing (SPPA), a parallel algorithm that incorporates spin inertia through a candidate spin set to reduce unnecessary probabilistic spin-flip computations. SPPA achieves convergence speed comparable to state-of-the-art methods while improving solution accuracy by 0.9%–7.8%. Furthermore, by pruning redundant evaluations, SPPA reduces the number of required spin update units (SUUs) by up to 75%.

title: A Unified Queueing-Based Runtime Evaluation Framework with Uncertainty Modeling for Heterogeneous Computing Platforms.
abstract: With the rapid advancement of intelligent computing and high-performance applications, accurately evaluating system execution time under heterogeneous computing resources has become a critical challenge. This paper proposes a Unified Queueing-based Runtime Evaluation (UQRE) framework that integrates uncertainty modeling with queueing network analysis to perform hierarchical modeling of data access, computation, and communication delays. The framework characterizes the pipelined execution of FPGA, multicore parallelism of DSP, and sequential processing behavior of ARM architectures. Experiments conducted on a heterogeneous computing platform in five types of information processing systems demonstrate that the average prediction error is 5.69%, remaining within 7%, validating the precision and generality of the proposed method. The results confirm that UQRE provides a theoretical foundation for algorithm deployment and system-level performance optimization on heterogeneous platforms.

title: PVT Robust LDO with Curvature Compensated BGR over wide Temperature Range -55°C to 170°C.
abstract: This paper presents a low-dropout regulator (LDO) designed and implemented in TSMC 180 nm CMOS process, incorporating a curvature-compensated band-gap reference for precision voltage regulation. The LDO delivers a stable 1.8V output from 2–3.3V supply while operating reliably across PVT variations from -55°C to 170°C. The design achieves a quiescent current of 35 µA and supports a maximum load current of 20mA with 99.9% current efficiency and 70 µW power consumption. The results demonstrate a DC PSRR of -81dB, a phase margin of 65°under full load, and a startup time of 1.79 µs. Monte Carlo analysis reveals that Vref has a standard deviation of 0.87 mV, and the worst-case temperature coefficient across process corners is 27 ppm°/C. This architecture is suitable for low power and wide temperature range based applications.

title: Hierarchical Fault Mitigation Architecture in Radiation-Hardened STT-MRAM.
abstract: Spin-transfer torque magnetic random-access memory (STT-MRAM) offers inherent radiation tolerance from its magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) structure, but remains susceptible to total ionizing dose (TID) degradation and single event effects (SEE) in CMOS circuitry. To enhance overall reliability, this work proposes a hierarchical fault mitigation architecture that dynamically distinguishes and mitigates transient and permanent faults through coordinated ECC correction and redundancy mapping. A radiation-hardened standard cell library is further incorporated to reinforce vulnerable control logic, complementing the proposed architecture for enhanced robustness. Circuit-level simulations and layout evaluation based on a 28 nm CMOS process demonstrate significant improvements in radiation robustness, maintaining stable functionality up to 70 MeV•cm2/mg and 450 krad(Si) with only 15% area overhead.

title: Implementation of Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity for epileptic seizure recovery on neuromorphic memristive hardware.
abstract: Neuromorphic engineers have spent decades developing efficient, brain-inspired computing hardware. This field was significantly advanced by the emergence of nanoscale memristors, which emulate synaptic connections and enable insitu learning algorithms like Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity (STDP). However, the widespread application of current memristors is hindered by limited reliability, particularly their difficulty in stably storing analog resistive values. This limitation can be overcome by exploiting a binary-weight stochastic STDP learning rule that leverages the more reliable binary memory capability of memristors. In this work, we implement this stochastic binary STDP algorithm on a neuromorphic hardware platform intended for real-time processing of brain Local Field Potential (LFP) signals, allowing the system to sense epileptic activity and prevent seizures in a closed-loop setup. Using synthetic signals generated by a hippocampal loop model, we demonstrate that a memristive crossbar can use STDP to learn neural correlations to detect and eventually prevent seizures. This outcome serves as a proof of concept for implanting a neuromorphic chip to inhibit epileptic seizures in the brain.

title: A 40 μW 8-bit Accelerator Wake-Up Circuit for Always-on Smart IoT Sensor Monitoring.
abstract: IoT sensors and devices rely heavily on cloud-based processing, especially in healthcare monitoring, for sensor data analysis, incurring high data transfer costs and energy consumption. To reduce constant data transmission, always-on smart sensors can use lightweight brain-inspired Hyperdimensional computing (HDC) models to efficiently classify sensor data that requires further resource-intensive cloud processing. We propose an all-digital CMOS always-on smart sensor accelerator for energy-constrained smart sensing applications. The proposed wake-up circuit architecture maintains HDC inference accuracy with INT-8 precision for complex datasets, where 1-bit quantization is not feasible. We introduce a novel systolic similarity search unit that utilizes a small systolic array to calculate hypervector cosine similarity metrics, and an energy-efficient near-memory fused item memory + multiply-accumulate systolic array encoder. This work achieves extremely low power consumption of 39.21-92.59 μW in typical applications, consuming only 120.01 nJ/inference.

title: A Memory-Efficient NTT Accelerator with a Highly Parallel Memory Mapping Scheme.
abstract: Number Theoretic Transform (NTT), a polynomial multiplication algorithm, is the computational bottleneck of lattice-based cryptography, such as post-quantum cryptography (PQC). Designing a high-performance NTT hardware accelerator can effectively enhance computational speed. However, existing mainstream designs often introduce significant memory overheads in pursuit of high throughput, resulting in poor throughput-per-area. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a memory-efficient NTT accelerator with a highly parallel memory mapping scheme. A 10T SRAM cell structure is presented that supports precise bit-level addressing and read/write access. Exploiting this cell, the design achieves high-throughput, in-place parallel data migration within a single SRAM array during butterfly computations. Furthermore, a glitch generator is incorporated into the near-memory computing unit, significantly reducing the latency of butterfly operations. Evaluation results show that the proposed NTT accelerator achieves a significant improvement in throughput(up to 7.3×) over the state-of-the-art.
