title: An IZO-Based 2T0C Compute-in-Memory Array with Adaptive Read Voltage Boosting for Energy-Efficient Edge AI.
abstract: Oxide-semiconductor (OS) thin-film transistor (TFT)-based 2T0C eDRAM cells are promising for energy-efficient compute-in-memory (CIM) owing to their ultra-low leakage, high ION/IOFFratio, and long data retention. However, conventional OS devices suffer from low drive current and threshold-voltage (VTH) shift, leading to high operating voltages and accuracy degradation in large-scale CIM arrays. In this work, we fabricate a 64×64 indium–zinc–oxide (IZO) TFT CIM array using a BEOL-compatible self-aligned top-gate (SATG) process. The array achieves sub-0.1 V analog computation with data retention exceeding 120 s. To address VTHshift, an adaptive read-voltage boosting (ARVB) scheme is proposed, which expands the CIM operating window by 5.63× and improves VGG-16 inference accuracy to 92.15%. A PCB-based evaluation platform is developed for chip-level evaluation. The fabricated IZO CIM array achieves a peak energy efficiency of 34.75 TOPS/W@8bIN8bW, demonstrating the strong potential of IZO-based CIM for low-power AI deployment.

title: A 15-Bit 22-μW 3.91-aF Power/Measurement-Time Scalable Direct Capacitance-to-Digital Converter with Closed-Loop Ratio-Based Floating Inverter Dynamic Amplifier.
abstract: This paper presents a 15-bit direct capacitance-to-digital converter (CDC) based on a switched-capacitor (SC) incremental delta-sigma (ΔΣ) modulator. A two-stage closed-loop (CL) ratio-based (RB) floating inverter dynamic amplifier (FIDA) is proposed to mitigate gain sensitivity to process, voltage and temperature (PVT) variations. It stabilizes the DC gain via inherent compensation between the transconductance (gm) and the output resistance (ro) of the FIDA, while ensuring sufficient phase margin (PM) through self frequency compensation. Correlated-level-shifting (CLS) technique is also employed to further boost the DC gain. To verify the linearity, the proposed CDC integrates a dual-modal reconfigurable sampling network to support voltage and capacitance measurement without additional hardware overhead. Fabricated in a 180-nm CMOS process, the prototype CDC consumes 22 μW from a 1.8-V supply and occupies an active area of 0.19 mm2. It achieves a capacitance resolution of 3.91 aF at 1.28 MS/s with a measurement time of 100 μs in free-running mode and exhibits a FoMW of 98 fJ/conv. step.

title: A Novel Frequency Detection Method Based on Aliasing Sampling System.
abstract: In response to the evolving demands of spectrum sensing technology, this paper proposes a new method for the sparse signal frequency detection under aliasing sampling system, which is based on asynchronous time-interleaved (ATI) architecture. This method effectively detects frequency aliasing by delay relationships between different channels, enabling the precise estimation of frequencies, even under multi-signal aliasing conditions. A four-channel simulation was conducted to evaluate the method's performance, successfully recovering all original frequencies aliasing together, which validates the method's effectiveness.

title: A Reconfigurable Multi-Precision MAC with Bin-Based FP8 Accumulation for Edge AI.
abstract: The deployment of large-scale Transformer models on edge devices requires hardware that can dynamically balance numerical precision and computational efficiency. This paper introduces FMMAC, a lightweight, reconfigurable Fixed point multi-precision Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) engine that efficiently supports INT4, INT8, and both E4M3/E5M2 FP8 computations within a unified datapath. Our key innovation is a fixed point bin-based accumulator that eliminates the complex mantissa alignment shifters found in conventional floating-point adders and larger systolic array designs. This unified approach results in a highly efficient design, demonstrating a 77.5% area reduction, a 41.9% power reduction, and a 3.86× improvement in energy per operations over state-of-the-art MACs when synthesized in 16nm. System-level simulations further validate our architecture, showing that it maintains accuracy and perplexity on par with both FP32 baseline and NVIDIA’s Transformer Engine. FMMAC is thus a viable and powerful building block for future resource-constrained, mixed-precision edge AI accelerators.

title: OptHQC: Optimize HQC for High-Performance Post-Quantum Cryptography.
abstract: As post-quantum cryptography (PQC) becomes increasingly critical for securing future communication systems, the performance overhead introduced by quantum-resistant algorithms presents a major computing challenge. HQC (Hamming Quasi-Cyclic) is a newly standardized code-based PQC scheme designed to replace classical key exchange methods. In this paper, we propose OptHQC, an optimized implementation of the HQC scheme to deliver high-performance cryptographic operations. Our approach provides a comprehensive analysis of each computational blocks in HQC and introduces optimizations across all three stages: key generation, encryption, and decryption. We first exploit data-level sparsity in vector multiplication to accelerate polynomial operations during vector generation. We then leverage instruction-level acceleration (e.g., AVX2) in hash computation to further improve performance. Last, we transform multiplication into lookup table indexing and optimize memory access patterns in syndrome computation and error vector recovery, which are the most computationally intensive operations in HQC. Overall, OptHQC achieves an average 55% speedup over the reference HQC implementation on CPU.

title: PathDiff: Efficient Patch-Level Histology Image Synthesis with Pathology-Prior Guided Diffusion.
abstract: To address the challenge of data scarcity and high computational cost in digital pathology, we introduce PathDiff. It is an efficient adaptation framework for diffusion-based patch-level image synthesis that, for the first time, explicitly integrates pathology-specific priors to ensure diagnostic fidelity. Unlike existing approaches that require large-scale datasets or heavy computation, PathDiff combines LoRA, Textual Inversion, and a Q-Former within a pathology-guided denoising process, which emphasizes diagnostically critical regions such as nuclei and glandular structures. This design enables faithful and diverse patch generation with only limited training data and modest resources. Extensive experiments on PCam and TCGA-BRCA demonstrate that PathDiff consistently outperforms representative GAN-and diffusion-based baselines in both visual fidelity and semantic alignment, while achieving comparable classification improvements to foundation-scale models at a fraction of the cost. These results highlight PathDiff as a practical and domain-aware solution for data augmentation in computational pathology.

title: A 0.07-mm2 32.7-kHz Frequency Reference with Aging Calibration Embedded 1-second Timer Scoring 22% Residual Error After 500-Hour Aging at 150°C in 28-nm CMOS.
abstract: This paper presents a frequency reference, embedded 1-second timer, featuring pioneering aging calibration for kilohertz RC oscillators. An aging-resilient reference branch incorporating a current-reuse N-diffusion resistor is proposed, complemented by aging calibration circuits using current-supply and level-shifting technologies. A leakage-current-assisted gate-source-voltage ratio scheme is employed for high-order temperature compensation. Fabricated in 28-nm CMOS technology, the 32.7-kHz prototype, occupying 0.07 mm2, achieves frequency stabilities of 2400 ppm/V and 27.6 ppm/°C across 1.2-1.8 V and -40-125 °C. After aging at 150 °C for 500 hours with the following calibration, it maintains merely 22% residual frequency error compared with the pre-aging error.

title: Hybrid-Domain STT-MRAM Compute-in-Memory Scheme for Quantized Deep Neural Network.
abstract: The escalating parameter scale of neural networks intensifies the memory wall challenge in von Neumann architectures, spurring the exploration of non-volatile memory-based computing-in-memory (NVM-CIM) architectures. This work presents an spin-transfer toque(STT)-MRAM-based computing-in-memory (CIM) macro that addresses key challenges in supporting quantized neural networks, including bit-level sparsity variation, signed-number operations, and hardware-software co-optimization. The design introduces three key innovations: a multi-domian CIM macro that eliminates dequantization overhead, a sign-bit replication strategy for efficient signed-number computation, and a dynamically adjustable accumulation-length scheme for sparse workloads. Implemented in 28nm technology, the 192Kb CIM macro achieves 24.15 TOPS/W energy efficiency. When evaluated on MNIST with LeNet-5, the system maintains 94% accuracy while consuming 2.69 nJ per inference, representing a 2.6× improvement over full-digital scheme.

title: Silicon-Based Evaluation of CSD Arithmetic in a RISC-V Processor Using Open-Source ASIC Flow.
abstract: This paper presents the ASIC implementation of NOVACore, a high-performance embedded RISC-V processor that integrates Canonical Signed Digit (CSD) arithmetic to enable carry-free addition and subtraction within its execution pipeline. This architectural enhancement significantly improves computational efficiency in arithmetic-intensive embedded workloads. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first silicon-based evaluation of CSD arithmetic in a RISC-V core, implemented using a fully open-source ASIC flow targeting the IHP 130 nm technology. Experimental results show that NOVACore, leveraging its CSD-based pipelined execution unit, achieves up to 31% higher throughput than the widely used VexRiscv at the same frequency. This performance comes with 43% area and 82% power overheads, primarily due to the redundant nature of the CSD representation, which increases routing complexity and placement density in NOVACore’s execution stage. These results validate the practical viability of CSD arithmetic for improving arithmetic performance in RISC-V processors while contributing to the broader goal of supporting open and accessible ASIC design using open-source toolchains.

title: Quantum Circuit Pruning: Improving Fidelity via Compilation-Aware Circuit Approximation.
abstract: This work presents a routing-aware pruning strategy for quantum circuits executed on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices. We propose a method to remove parametric controlled rotations whose small rotation angles do not justify the routing overhead required for their implementation. By selectively pruning such gates, the method mitigates fidelity loss arising from additional SWAP operations introduced during compilation. Our approach evaluates whether executing a gate leads to greater fidelity loss than omitting it. Simulations on benchmark circuits with realistic noise models show that the method reduces two-qubit gate counts (up to 48.6%) while improving final state fidelity (up to 47.7%), especially for larger circuits where routing costs dominate.

title: A Low-Power CMOS-Spintronic Neuromorphic Network Based on Vortex Oscillators.
abstract: This paper presents a low-power CMOS interface for magnetic tunnel junction-based vortex oscillator (MTJ-VO) devices, suitable for neuromorphic networks. In the proposed approach, a rectified linear unit (ReLU)-like function is implemented by exploiting the dependence of the MTJ-VO frequency on its bias current (MTJ-ReLU). Compared with prior works, the proposed MTJ-VO-based neuron offers the distinct advantage of directly connecting multiple neurons to realize more complex neural networks. The CMOS interface was designed and verified through transistor-level simulations in a 65 nm CMOS technology using MTJ-VO data obtained from device measurements. Finally, the functionality of the MTJ-ReLU neuron was validated by implementing a 784×256×10 artificial neural network (ANN), achieving a test accuracy of 94%.

title: A 40 nm integrated cryo-CMOS 120 MHz switching power converter for power management at 4 K aiming large-scale quantum computers.
abstract: Quantum computers require a complex cryogenic electrical interface to avoid the wiring bottleneck between the cryogenic qubits and the room-temperature controllers. Such cryogenic electronics are typically supplied through long cables that introduce significant resistive and thermal losses, hindering efficiency and scalability. To circumvent this hurdle, this work presents a fully integrated cryo-CMOS synchronous buck converter operating at 4 K that enables the use of a high-voltage low-current supply to reduce resistive losses in the cables. Implemented in 40 nm CMOS, the converter targets a 7 V input, a 1.1 V output, and load currents of 100–300 mA, while achieving 63% efficiency by exploiting the cryogenic behavior of active and passive CMOS devices. These results pave the way for the power-management systems required in the cryo-CMOS SoC controlling future large-scale quantum computers.

title: SPEAR: Spike-Aware Point Pruning and Fused FPS-KNN Sampling for Spiking Point Transformer Acceleration Co-Design.
abstract: Point cloud data are inherently sparse and irregular, leading to high computational, power, and latency costs in sampling and neighborhood search. The Spiking Point Transformer (SPT) has recently demonstrated strong potential for energy-efficient spatiotemporal modeling by leveraging event-driven computation. Yet efficient hardware acceleration remains constrained, as sampling and neighborhood search incur substantial computational and memory overheads, GPU-based implementations fail to exploit the energy efficiency of spiking attention, and existing neuromorphic processors lack effective mapping for structured point-level sparsity. This paper presents SPEAR, an algorithm–hardware co-design framework tailored for SPT. It integrates a spike-aware point pruning mechanism for structured sparsity generation and a fused FPS-KNN engine for efficient data reuse, together with a Spiking Feature & Attention Engine enabling event-driven convolution and attention computation. Experimental results show that SPEAR achieves up to 24.3–135.3× speedups and 154.4–845.3× energy efficiency improvements over GPU baselines for large- and small-scale point cloud inference, respectively, while maintaining accuracy. It further attains 4.9× and 2.4× higher energy efficiency compared to prior point cloud and spiking Transformer accelerators.

title: Phase-Change Memory Based Passive Timing Circuits for DRAM Refresh Management.
abstract: Timers play a crucial role in integrated circuit design. Cycle-based stamp counters are commonly used in various applications, such as CPU timing management and DRAM refresh operations. However, precise counting with digital counters comes with significant overhead. We propose a novel Phase-Change Memory (PCM) based passive timer for efficient timing. The passive and spontaneous conductance drift effect of PCM makes the timer highly energy-efficient. Through experiments using measured PCM conductance drift data, we compare our proposed PCM-based passive timer with traditional timers implemented in CMOS circuits. Our design achieves 121× better area efficiency and 8125.7× higher power efficiency compared to previous solutions. In the context of DRAM refresh management, the proposed solution requires only 0.1% area overhead and 0.14% power overhead, showcasing its practicality and efficiency.

abstract: This paper presents a "Practice-Driven" teaching model for electronic circuit education, shifting from traditional teacher-centered instruction to student-led learning. The model emphasizes hands-on experiments, fostering active engagement and problem-solving skills. A revised assessment system prioritizes practical abilities and learning processes, resulting in improved student learning outcomes and engagement.

title: A 6.78MHz Dual Output Wireless Power Transfer System With Fast Transient Response And Adaptive Global Power Control.
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-output wireless power transfer system operating at 6.78MHz. Both output voltages are regulated by PWM controllers, so that the transient response can be faster than that controlled by only global power control loop. To ensure the shortest 0x mode duration, an LSK is employed between the transmitter and receiver. When the transmitter detects excess or deficiency of the output current, it will adaptively adjust the output power to minimize the energy consumption during the 0x mode. A pulse width detector is employed within this system to determine whether the receiver's energy meets the load requirements. The maximum energy output of this wireless power transfer system is 1W, designed in a 180nm process. The peak efficiency of the receiver is 93%. Compared to conventional WPT systems, the efficiency of this system is improved by 15.1% at the power of 400mW. The fastest response time reaches 15 μs.

title: A Static-Gradient, IC-Based 0.5-T NMR Spectrometer for 2D Diffusion-Relaxation Analysis of Solid Peanuts.
abstract: We present a compact, IC-based low-field NMR spectrometer that achieves diffusion-sensitive measurements without bulky gradient hardware, by using the inherent static magnetic gradient of a 0.5-T Halbach magnet. A custom 180-nm CMOS NMR ASIC integrates an arbitrary pulse sequencer, an RF transmitter, and a low-noise receiver within a die area of 5 mm2, enabling fully portable operation. Using the static gradient (gavg= 0.5 T/m), we demonstrate two-dimensional (2D) diffusion–relaxation (D–T2) experiments on solid peanuts during drying at 60°C. These measurements reveal oil molecular mobility and moisture loss without oil extraction. The system maintains a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 29 dB and stable operation across off-center regions with strong static gradients. These results establish a chip-scale, gradient-electronics-free NMR platform that bridges integrated-circuit design and magnetic resonance sensing, enabling field-deployable, non-destructive analysis of agricultural, food, and biological materials.

title: MDM: Manhattan Distance Mapping of DNN Weights for Parasitic-Resistance-Resilient Memristive Crossbars.
abstract: Manhattan Distance Mapping (MDM) is a post-training deep neural network (DNN) weight mapping technique for memristive bit-sliced compute-in-memory (CIM) crossbars that reduces parasitic resistance (PR) nonidealities.PR limits crossbar efficiency by mapping DNN matrices into small crossbar tiles, reducing CIM-based speedup. Each crossbar executes one tile, requiring digital synchronization before the next layer. At this granularity, designers either deploy many small crossbars in parallel or reuse a few sequentially—both increasing analog-to-digital conversions, latency, I/O pressure, and chip area.MDM alleviates PR effects by optimizing active-memristor placement. Exploiting bit-level structured sparsity, it feeds activations from the denser low-order side and reorders rows according to the Manhattan distance, relocating active cells toward regions less affected by PR and thus lowering the nonideality factor (NF).Applied to DNN models on ImageNet-1k, MDM reduces NF by up to 46% and improves accuracy under analog distortion by an average of 3.6% in ResNets. Overall, it provides a lightweight, spatially informed method for scaling CIM DNN accelerators.

title: An Ultra-Low-Power IR-UWB Energy-Harvesting Tag for Unsynchronized Multi-User Transmission.
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-low-power wireless tag for kHz-rate sensing in unsynchronized energy-harvesting wireless sensor networks (EHWSNs). The tag implements a multiuser time-hopping impulse-radio ultra-wideband (TH-IR-UWB)-based scheme that enables the simultaneous and unsynchronized operation of 64 tags transmitting asynchronously to a single base station. The SoC is fabricated in a low-cost 180-nm 1P6M CMOS process. It integrates a digital core, a packet generator, a pulse generator, a UWB transmitter, an XO-based clock generator, and a power management unit that includes an energy harvester for direct over-the-air powering or wireless battery charging. The proposed TH-IR-UWB uses packets of 255bits each, consisting of a preamble, data bits, and CRC at a transmit rate of 256Hz which can be increased to 4096Hz by reducing the payload length. A sequence set with bounded correlation is constructed through a systematic and exhaustive search to support reliable multi-user detection. Measurements confirm correct packet timing and an effective data rate of 57.34kbs-1per tag. At a 1-V supply, the pulse generator consumes 18.9µW on average, and the transmitter consumes 29µW during operation with −1dBm RF output power, occupying an area of 1.5mm2. The results demonstrate a scalable, energy-efficient telemetry platform suited for dense EHWSNs.

title: A High-Efficiency Buck-Boost Converter with a Wide Load Range for Neural Stimulators.
abstract: To satisfy the stringent safety and performance requirements of multi-channel neural stimulators, the power system must deliver high efficiency across a wide output-voltage and load range, provide fast transient response with robust charge-delivery capability, and incorporate reliable protection mechanisms. This paper presents a wide-output-range, high-efficiency power converter fabricated in TSMC 0.18-μm BCD technology, employing a four-switch buck–boost topology and a V2constant on-time (V2-COT) control strategy. To support V2-COT, we propose a cooperative multi-module architecture: a three-segment ramp generator that ensures loop stability across operating conditions; a zero-current detection (ZCD) circuit that enables accurate identification of inductor current zero-crossings, guaranteeing reliable operation in discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) and seamless transitions between continuous (CCM) and discontinuous modes; an over-current protection (OCP) module to safeguard the system; and an on-time generation block fundamental to the COT framework. Measured results demonstrate a peak efficiency of 87.8% at a 15-V output with a 10-mA load, along with stable operation and automatic frequency adaptation under varying stimulator load conditions, thereby sustaining high overall efficiency.

title: Lightweight Recaptured Image Detection Model with Gradual Unfreezing and Structured Pruning.
abstract: Detecting recaptured images is vital in digital forensics, as such images can fabricate evidence or bypass verification systems. These images introduce subtle high-frequency artifacts that are hard to detect using conventional tools. Traditional handcrafted methods struggle to generalize across devices and lighting conditions, while deep learning models, though more robust, are often computationally intensive and require significant computational and memory resources, making them unsuitable for real-time or resource-constrained applications. To overcome these challenges, we propose a lightweight, interpretable deep learning framework that integrates Laplacian-based high-frequency enhancement with a MobileNetV2 backbone for efficient feature extraction. We evaluate three fine-tuning strategies: classifier-only (FT-C), full architecture (FT-A), and top-to-bottom gradual unfreezing (FT-GU), and show that FT-GU achieves the best accuracy and efficiency trade-off. Structured pruning is subsequently applied to the FT-GU model to further reduce its complexity, yielding a compact yet high-performing detector. Experiments on the ROSE and custom LCD datasets demonstrate that the pruned FT-GU model achieves 91% accuracy while being over 10x smaller and 20% faster than the full model.

title: Patch Size-Considered Incremental Learning for Video Compression Artifact Reduction.
abstract: In this paper, we propose patch size-considered incremental learning for video compression artifact reduction based on quantization parameter (QP) distance. Patch size represents the block size in a frame for training, while QP distance represents the difference between the input QP and its label QP. The relationship between the patch size and QP distance enables the high-performance operating point (HOP) in-loop filter for VVC to learn both local features and global structure in a frame. Thus, the proposed patch size-considered incremental learning based on QP distance strengthens the learning ability of the HOP in-loop filter and enhances its performance, while accelerating the training time. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves average Bjøntegaard-Delta rate (BD-rate) gains of {-8.25% (Y), -17.31% (U), -18.67% (V)} and {-8.82% (Y), -16.70% (U), -16.70% (V)} over VTM_11.0-NNVC_3.0 in AI and RA configurations, respectively. Moreover, the proposed method remarkably reduces the training time to about 8 days without the training sets compressed by the HOP-embedded VTM.

title: PipeInfer: A pipelined inference framework for U-Net like neural networks.
abstract: U-Net and its variants are widely used in many fields, and some of their applications are even latency and power-sensitive. This paper presents a low-latency inference framework for U-Net-like neural networks. The framework decomposes models into multiple sub-models executed in parallel and introduces a device-side zero-copy shared-memory mechanism to enable efficient inter-stage data exchange. By integrating NVIDIA TensorRT and Multi-Process Service (MPS) for optimized computation and concurrency, the proposed approach achieves up to 70% and 54% performance improvement over PyTorch and TensorRT, respectively, demonstrating its effectiveness for high-efficiency U-Net-like neural networks inference, especially in scenarios with latency and power limitations.

title: A 91.4-dB SNDR 200-kSPS Exponential-Incremental ADC with an Open-Loop Ratio-Based Floating Inverter Dynamic Amplifier.
abstract: This paper presents a 16-bit fully dynamic exponential-incremental (EI) analog-to-digital converter (ADC). Capacitor stacking and dynamic buffering techniques with an open-loop (OL) ratio-based (RB) floating inverter dynamic amplifier (FIDA) are employed to achieve near-fourth-order noise-shaping (NS) capability with only first-order hardware cost. Verified in a 180-nm CMOS process, the proposed ADC achieves a signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) of 91.4 dB under a 1.8-V supply over a 100 kHz bandwidth with an oversampling ratio (OSR) of 10. The power consumption of the proposed ADC is 126.3 μW, demonstrating a Schreier figure of merit (FoMS) of 182.1 dB.

title: Robust Data-Driven Distributed Control Strategy for Dynamic Energy Scheduling in Hybrid Energy Systems.
abstract: This paper proposes a robust data-driven distributed control strategy for dynamic energy scheduling in hybrid energy storage systems (HESSs) comprising fuel cells (FCs) and lithium-ion batteries. The proposed framework integrates a robust recurrent deep network (R2DN)-based controller that enables fully distributed coordination among heterogeneous energy sources without relying on centralized communication. By embedding degradation indicators of FCs and virtual state-of-charge (SoC) variables of batteries into the control design, the strategy achieves adaptive power allocation among multiple FCs, SoC equalization of batteries, and fast DC-bus voltage regulation under dynamic operating conditions. The R2DN controller provides intrinsic stability guarantees through contraction and Lipschitz constraints, ensuring robustness against parameter variations and external disturbances. Simulation in MATLAB/SIMULINK verified the performance of proposed control method.

title: Live Demonstration: A Photovoltaic Asynchronous Time-Based Image Sensor.
abstract: Over the past decade, there has been a remarkable surge in industrial interest in Dynamic Vision Sensors (DVS). Leading multinational companies to integrating DVS technology into their product portfolios. Building upon previous work by the authors [1] , a Photovoltaic Asynchronous Time-Based Image Sensor (PVATIS) has been implemented. Unlike the well-known pixel-level ATIS architecture [2] , which implements temporal contrast detection and exposure measurement using two photodiodes and a logarithmic receptor per pixel, the proposed approach employs a single photodiode operating in photovoltaic mode [3] . This novel topology offers several advantages: it reduces both pixel area and power consumption, while the higher integrated capacitance lowers noise power at the photoreceptor stage, thereby increasing dynamic range and improving temporal variation detection under low illuminance. This comes at the cost of reduced bandwidth. Additionally, the use of an external positive-slope ramp is particularly beneficial for dim-light operation, as it minimizes latency.

title: Neuromorphic Spiking Ring Attractor for Proprioceptive Joint-State Estimation.
abstract: Maintaining stable internal representations of continuous variables is fundamental for effective robotic control. Continuous attractor networks provide a biologically inspired mechanism for encoding such variables, yet neuromorphic realizations have rarely addressed proprioceptive estimation under resource constraints. This work introduces a spiking ring-attractor network representing a robot joint angle through self-sustaining population activity. Local excitation and broad inhibition support a stable activity bump, while velocity-modulated asymmetries drive its translation and boundary conditions confine motion within mechanical limits. The network reproduces smooth trajectory tracking and remains stable near joint limits, showing reduced drift and improved accuracy compared to unbounded models. Such compact hardware-compatible implementation preserves multi-second stability demonstrating a near-linear relationship between bump velocity and synaptic modulation.

title: An Efficient On-chip Adaptation Technique for MAML models on Memristive Hardware.
abstract: In-memory computing based on memristive devices is highly promising, yet the overheads of gradient-based learning pose challenges for post-deployment adaptation/finetuning or on-chip training. Model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) overcomes this challenge by providing a good initialization of the memristive conductances, which can be further tuned online to suit a particular task. We propose an efficient on-chip adaptation technique for finetuning MAML models on the memristive hardware. We first prepare the models for on-chip deployment by training on high-precision hardware. Further, we simplify the on-chip adaptation process by using the delta learning rule, which updates only the last layer of the model. We tested our approach on the DoubleMNIST and Omniglot datasets on non-ideal memristive hardware. Our methods for on-chip adaptation reduce area, latency, and energy by up to 18%, 61%, and 90%, respectively, while reducing accuracy by < 1.0%.

title: Bandpass Incremental Delta-Sigma ADCs.
abstract: This work presents the first proof of concept and derivation of the bandpass incremental delta-sigma modulator (BP-I-ΔΣM). The theory behind the bandpass sampling I-ΔΣM is mathematically derived, explained, and exemplarily validated by high-level circuit-level simulations. The reconstruction filter of the BP-I-ΔΣM is particularly important because it plays a pivotal role in reconstructing the output stream. It is shown that the output of a BP-I-ΔΣM can be directly reconstructed by a matched reconstruction filter, while utilizing chain-of-integrator (CoI) filters for the direct conversion is futile. Furthermore, the reconstruction of the BP-I-ΔΣM is optimized by demodulation of the I- and Q-channel before using lowpass reconstruction filters, then also including CoI filters. In our exemplary system, this optimization increases the signal-to-noise and distortion ratio (SNDR) by up to 7dB. This proposed filter optimization increases the resolution and also simplifies the circuit implementation of the decimation filter for BP-I-ΔΣMs.

title: High Performance Fault-Tolerant Control for DC-DC Buck-Boost Converters: An Unsupervised Learning-based Approach.
abstract: This paper introduces an advanced learning-based fault-tolerant control strategy for DC-DC buck-boost converters, demonstrating significant improvements over classic approaches under challenging operating conditions. The proposed Learning-based Fault-Tolerant Control PI (LFTC-PI) integrates Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) clustering with adaptive parameter adjustment to enable fault detection and mitigation dynamically. In contrast to fixed-parameter robust controllers, which often depend on conservative designs, the LFTC-PI adaptively adjusts its control parameters based on operational data, allowing for prompt adjustments in response to component degradation and external disturbances. Comprehensive simulation studies demonstrate substantial performance improvements: reduced settling time, lower overshoot, and diminished steady-state error compared to classic fault-tolerant control strategies. Moreover, the proposed controller ensures stable operation even under simultaneous 40% inductance and capacitance degradation, with concurrent voltage and load disturbances. An analysis of computational complexity demonstrates the algorithm's suitability for implementation on standard embedded systems. This approach represents a transition from reactive to proactive fault mitigation in power electronics, with potential applications in electric vehicle charging infrastructure and renewable energy systems, where reliability is critical.

title: A 74.5-dB DR 1.25-MHz BW Continuous-Time Delta-Sigma ADC Using Low-Noise Feedback DAC with Optimized Barrel Shifter.
abstract: This paper presents a 4-bit, 3rd-order continuous -time (CT) delta-sigma modulator (DSM) for through-wall radar (TWR) applications, achieving a 1.25-MHz bandwidth. A low-noise, current-steering digital-to-analog converter (DAC) is proposed, which employs source degeneration and noise filtering to reduce its output current noise power by 2.6 dB. To further enhance linearity, an optimized barrel shifter is implemented to perform a data-weighted averaging (DWA) algorithm based on a modulo-15 element rotation scheme. Additionally, power-efficient operational amplifiers (OPAs) utilizing a hybrid Miller and feedforward compensation scheme are employed in the second and third integrators. Fabricated in 40-nm CMOS process, the proposed Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) achieves a measured dynamic range (DR) of 74.5 dB and a spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) of 80.1 dB. It consumes 6.5mW from a 1.2-V supply and occupies a core active area of 0.1 mm2.

title: Live Demonstration: An Event-Driven E-Skin System with Dynamic Binary Scanning and real time SNN Classification.
abstract: This demonstration presents a novel hardware sys-tem for high-speed, high-data-efficiency tactile sensing and real-time classification. The system uses a 16×16 high-impedance tactile sensor array and an event-driven strategy with a dynamic binary scanning algorithm to classify the digits. This approach leverages 99% data sparsity to achieve a 12.8× reduction in scan counts and a 38.2× data compression rate and a 28.4× dynamic range increase, significantly lowering system energy consumption. The resulting sparse data streams are processed by a multi-layer Convolutional Spiking Neural Network (Conv-SNN) on FPGA, which requires only 65% of the computation and 15.6% of the weight storage relative to a CNN, while maintaining 92.11% accuracy for real-time handwritten digit recognition. This live demo showcases a complete pipeline from analog tactile sensing to neuromorphic classification, highlighting the efficiency of event-driven systems for next-generation robotic perception and human-computer interaction.

title: A 1-10.7GHz Low-Jitter 8-Phase Injection-Locked Clock Generator with Supply-Voltage Feedback in 28 nm CMOS.
abstract: With the advancements in high-speed integrated circuits, the demand for compact-area, high-performance multi-phase clock generation is increasing. This paper presents a small-area, low-jitter 8-phase injection-locked clock generator with supply-voltage feedback. The proposed delay-locked loop (DLL) employs a low-dropout regulator (LDO) to directly control the supply voltages of both the delay line and ring voltage-controlled oscillator (RVCO). This design effectively suppresses noise coupling into the RVCO and minimizes replica control-loop-induced mismatches, thereby achieving both an enhanced locking range and reduced output jitter. Fabricated in 28–nm CMOS process under 0.9–V supply, the design achieves an ultra-wideband locking range of 8-phase clock output spanning 1–10.7GHz. At 7 GHz, the measured jitter is 26 fs (integrated from 100 Hz to 1 GHz ), while occupying an area of less than 0.012 mm2. The compact area, high performance, and wide locking range make this solution highly suitable for integration with high-speed ADC and other mixed-signal systems requiring precise timing synchronization.

title: Detector-in-Memory for Massive MIMO Detection.
abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) signal detection is essential for 6G and beyond. However, current detectors, both digital and in-memory computing (IMC)-based, suffer from high energy and latency overheads. We propose the Detector-in-Memory (DiM) architecture to overcome these challenges. DiM is an IMC-based architecture that employs symbol slicers instead of column ADCs, and an intrinsically complex-valued IMC bitcell (BC) to realize a high-dimensional complex-valued matrix-vector multiplication (C-MVM). The use of symbol slicers results in a 128× reduction in the number of quantizations per symbol, while the use of a 28T4C complex-valued IMC BC reduces the transistor count by 30% compared to real-valued BCs. Simulations in a commercial 28nm CMOS indicate that DiM achieves an 11× higher energy efficiency and 7× greater area efficiency than state-of-the-art MIMO detectors, while meeting the QPSK 3GPP error vector magnitude (EVM) specification of -15.15dB.

title: Memory-Efficient In-Sensor Event Denoising with a Lightweight Point-Cloud Network.
abstract: Dynamic vision sensors (DVS) offer high dynamic range and microsecond latency but suffer from background-activity (BA) noise that degrades perception and wastes band-width and power. We target in-sensor denoising to reduce bus and host energy, using a memory-efficient, lightweight point-cloud network. For each event, we query a small spatio-temporal neighborhood from a FIFO of length L, apply simple spatial/temporal normalization, and process the at-most-M neighbors with two shared MLP layers and max/mean pooling, followed by a compact classifier. This design uses ${\mathcal{O}}(L)$ storage (about 5 KB feature map + 2.5 KB weights in our setting) rather than a full-resolution timestamp surface (e.g., 131 KB at 128 × 128), and requires fewer than 72k operations per event. Experiments on open source DND21 dataset show strong accuracy with a tiny footprint. Across 30,000 test samples, the model attains 91% mean accuracy and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.957. The ${\mathcal{O}}(L)$ memory, small parameter count, and parallel-friendly computation make the method well suited for ASIC implementation and in-sensor deployment.

title: RISC-V and SHA-256 Accelerator Hackathon: A Problem-Based Learning Approach to Hardware-Software Co-Design.
abstract: Hackathons have emerged as a powerful Problem-Based Learning (PBL) approach in engineering education, fostering active engagement, teamwork, and problem-solving under real-world constraints. This paper presents an educational hackathon in which students designed a RISC-V core based on the Imagination University Program and a SHA-256 cryptographic accelerator, implemented on a Xilinx Nexys A7-100T FPGA board. The hackathon was integrated into a VLSI course with three preparatory workshops—focused on FPGA setup, accelerator interfacing, and software co-design—culminating in a final open-ended challenge. The goals of the hackathon were fourfold: (1) apply PBL in hardware/software co-design, (2) enhance practical FPGA and RISC-V skills, (3) develop collaboration and creativity under time constraints, and (4) increase motivation toward VLSI careers. Survey results revealed increased motivation, enhanced technical and collaborative skills, and strengthened career interest. This work demonstrates the value of hackathons as a PBL methodology for advancing practical skills and professional readiness in computer engineering education.

title: An Event-Driven E-Skin System with Dynamic Binary Scanning and real time SNN Classification.
abstract: This paper presents a novel hardware system for high-speed, event-sparse sampling-based electronic skin (e-skin) that integrates sensing and neuromorphic computing. The system is built around a 16×16 piezoresistive tactile array with front-end and introduces a event-based binary scan search strategy to classify the digits. This event-driven strategy achieves a 12.8× reduction in scan counts, a 38.2× data compression rate and a 28.4× equivalent dynamic range, a 99% data sparsity, drastically reducing the data acquisition overhead. The resulting sparse data stream is processed by a multi-layer convolutional spiking neural network (Conv-SNN) implemented on an FPGA, which requires only 65% of the computation and 15.6% of the weight storage relative to a CNN. Despite these significant efficiency gains, the system maintains a high classification accuracy of 92.11% for real-time handwritten digit recognition. Furthermore, a real neuromorphic tactile dataset using Address Event Representation (AER) is constructed. This work demonstrates a fully integrated, event-driven pipeline from analog sensing to neuromorphic classification, offering an efficient solution for robotic perception and human-computer interaction.

title: A Low-Power 2-bit Full Adder realized with Three-Independent-Gate Reconfigurable FETs.
abstract: Reconfigurable Field Effect Transistors are emerging nano-electronic devices providing controllable n-type/p-type operation, that can be fabricated on industrial processes such as 22nm FDSOI. These multi-gate devices are based on Schottky barriers and therefore well-suited for low-power applications because of their superior control on the leakage current. In this paper, we demonstrate on 22nm FDSOI hardware a 2-bit full adder digital circuit completely realized with RFETs operating at 1.8 V. The circuit presents a calculated maximum simultaneous switching power in a full ripple-carry propagation event of 3.024 µW and a minimum global leakage power of only 5.04 pW. When compared to CMOS 2-bit adder designs on the same 22nm FDSOI technology baseline operating at 0.8 V, the RFET-based 2-bit full adder shows a reduction of the calculated maximum simultaneous switching power and for the global leakage power by factors 103and 102, respectively. Finally, we demonstrate in simulations that if the more scaled version of the same circuit operating at 0.8 V is considered, a power-delay-product of only 5.97 fJ can be obtained with less than 50A of the area required by other CMOS standard designs.

title: A 445pW, 28Hz Gate-Leakage based Relaxation Oscillator.
abstract: This paper presents a sub-nW relaxation oscillator without using large resistors to achieve low area, thereby making it suitable for IoT applications. Gate-leakage-based voltage and current references have been used to achieve an effective resistance of Vref/Iref, thereby scaling down the power consumption to the pW level while consuming low area. The oscillator is designed in 65 nm process and occupies an area of 0.007 mm2. It generates a clock of 28 Hz and post-layout simulations show a temperature coefficient (TC) of 56 ppm/°C in the temperature range of −55°C to 80°C. It exhibits a line sensitivity of 1.83%/V in the supply range of 1.2 V to 2.5 V and consumes 445 pW power at 1.2 V supply. The power efficiency is observed to be 15.9 pW/Hz.

title: 3D Monolithic Integrated Indium Tin Oxide-Silicon Hybrid Leaky Integrate and Fire Neuron.
abstract: Neuromorphic circuits offer energy and area-efficient operation for edge applications. Being inspired by the massive connectivity of biological neural networks, these would also require dense connectivity that can be achieved by 3D integration. Conventional analog subthreshold neuron circuits are implemented in Si-CMOS technology and require a capacitor to integrate the incoming synaptic inputs, which tend to occupy a larger area. In this paper, we demonstrate a Leaky Integrate and Fire (LIF) neuron in Amorphous Oxide Semiconductor (AOS) technology using Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) channel nFET. By exploiting its low off-state leakage in a 2T gain-cell integrator that allows long charge retention, we show a capacitor-less circuit. We propose an ITO-nFET neuron circuit and also a 3D hybrid neuron circuit that combines Si-pFET along with ITO-nFET, which can be potentially fabricated in a Monolithic 3D IC technology to reduce overall footprint. The circuits are demonstrated based on a compact model calibrated to experimental ITO-nFET data. The proposed ITO-nFET neuron circuit is designed with 65nm technology design rules and consumes an energy of 12.95pJ/spike at a supply voltage of 1.2V with a spiking frequency of 166.66kHz and utilizes 96.7µm2area. The hybrid circuit is shown to operate at much reduced energy of 9.58pJ/spike at a spiking frequency of 125kHz for the same conditions. Furthermore, our neurons are evaluated in a convolutional spiking neural network (CSNN) and demonstrate a high inference accuracy of >97% on the N-MNIST dataset.

title: A 0.562 mm2 MTJ-Based Ising Machine for 48-bit Integer Factorization in 40 nm CMOS.
abstract: Combinatorial Optimization Problems (COPs) are recognized for their complexity and difficulty in finding quick solutions. An Ising machine with an annealing strategy effectively solves these COPs but often incurs low speed and high resource costs. To mitigate the challenges, we have developed a Magnetic Tunnel Junction (MTJ) technology-based CMOS Ising Machine to achieve high speed and area efficiency in solving COPs. Our main contributions include: (a) A gradient-guided strategy that shortens search times, avoiding falling into local optimal solutions; (b) A probability-based random number generator using MTJ switches to replace the high-area-cost Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) circuits; (c) A digital pseudo-annealing circuit can generate interaction coefficients on-site. Fabricated with 40 nm CMOS technology, our design can achieve 48-bit (or 32-bit) integer factorization in 500 ms (or 3-5 ms) at 10-20 MHz with 1.1 V supply voltage, occupying a 0.562 mm2core area and achieving an area efficiency of up to 3846.98 mm-2.

title: Identification of ADHD Biological Subtypes with Variational Autoencoder Network.
abstract: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) diagnosis using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data has grown increasingly prevalent with advances in deep learning. However, most research has focused on symptom-based subtyping of ADHD, which fails to address the intrinsic heterogeneity of this disorder. To address this limitation, we propose an end-to-end deep learning framework for ADHD biotype identification, which integrates feature learning and the clustering process by combining a variational autoencoder model with pseudo-label assignment modules. This unified architecture facilitates mutual reinforcement between feature learning and clustering optimization. Two distinct ADHD biotypes cluster with clear separation from healthy controls and from each other. Meanwhile, linear regression tests reveal significant associations between these biotypes and symptom-based subtypes, enhancing the understanding of the biological mechanisms underlying symptomatic manifestations. The proposed framework offers an effective solution for ADHD biotype identification, providing valuable insights for personalized ADHD treatment.

title: A 25kHz-BW 115-dB SNDR Zoom Incremental ADC with Two-step Extended-Counting Technique for Audio Applications.
abstract: This article presents a high dynamic-range (DR) high signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) zoom incremental analog-to-digital converter (ADC) for audio applications. The prototype operates in a two-step time division multiplexed (TDM) manner to perform extended counting (EC), which enables an improved signal-to-quantization noise ratio (SQNR). Furthermore, the digital coefficient determined by clock cycle eliminates quantization noise leakage when combing the results from two-step operation. The prototype has been implemented with 180-nm BCD process, occupying an active area of 0.24 mm2. The simulation results show that it achieves a dynamic range of 115.4 dB, and an SNDR of 115 dB in a 25 kHz bandwidth while dissipating 1.8 mW, corresponding to a competitive Schreier FoM (FoMS,DR) of 186.8 dB and SNDR FoM (FoMSNDR) of 186.4 dB. The prototype is the first reported hybrid ADC integrating zoom and two-step EC IADC, which paves the way for precision audio signal chains with high energy efficiency.

title: Highly Energy-Efficient In-Memory Computing Architecture Based on VGSOT-MRAM for Reconfigurable BNN/TNN Acceleration.
abstract: In-memory computing (IMC) significantly accelerates neural networks by addressing the von Neumann bottleneck. Among the various emerging technologies for IMC, voltage-gated spin-orbit torque magnetic random-access memory (VGSOT-MRAM) stands out due to its high resistance and ultra-low power consumption. While binary neural networks (BNNs) leverage IMC for extreme energy efficiency, their accuracy often falls short. Ternary neural networks (TNNs) offer improved accuracy but typically demand dedicated circuitry, leading to considerable hardware overhead. To leverage the advantages of both, we propose a VGSOT-MRAM IMC architecture delivering extreme BNN energy efficiency while natively supporting TNN computation with near-zero hardware overhead, which is achieved by reconfiguring operational bit-width: a single two-magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) bit-cell performs 1-bit BNN operation, while two adjacent BNN-cells are collaboratively used for TNNs. Furthermore, a time-to-digital converter (TDC) quantization circuit is integrated to ensure accurate and low-power readout. Evaluated at the 28 nm CMOS node, the proposed architecture achieves 6799.16 and 3012.22 TOPS/W for BNN and TNN modes, demonstrating a versatile solution for energy-efficient edge AI.

title: Area-Efficient In-Memory Computing for Mixture-of-Experts via Multiplexing and Caching.
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers activate a subset of model weights, dubbed experts, to improve model performance. MoE is particularly promising for deployment on process-in-memory (PIM) architectures, because PIM can naturally fit experts separately and provide great benefits for energy efficiency. However, PIM chips often suffer from large area overhead, especially in the peripheral circuits. In this paper, we propose an area-efficient in-memory computing architecture for MoE transformers. First, to reduce area, we propose a crossbar-level multiplexing strategy that exploits MoE sparsity: experts are deployed on crossbars and multiple crossbars share the same peripheral circuits. Second, we propose expert grouping and group-wise scheduling methods to alleviate the load imbalance and contention overhead caused by sharing. In addition, to address the problem that the expert choice router requires access to all hidden states during generation, we propose a gate-output (GO) cache to store necessary results and bypass expensive additional computation. Experiments show that our approaches improve the area efficiency of the MoE part by up to 2.2x compared to a SOTA architecture. During generation, the cache improves performance and energy efficiency by 4.2x and 10.1x, respectively, compared to the baseline when generating 8 tokens. The total performance density achieves 15.6 GOPS/W/mm2. The code is open source at https://github.com/superstarghy/MoEwithPIM.

title: CHiP-NoC: A Congestion-Adaptive Dual-Mode Neuromorphic NoC with Hybrid Spike Compression.
abstract: Neuromorphic systems promise high energy efficiency by leveraging sparse, event-driven computation. As neuromorphic computing advances, its scalability is bottlenecked by communication infrastructure that struggles to keep pace with increasing inter-layer spike traffic, irregular spatiotemporal firing activity, and tight power constraints. This work presents CHiP-NoC, a network-on-chip (NoC) tailored for neuromorphic workloads, with cross-layer co-optimization to achieve high throughput and energy efficiency. It incorporates a hybrid spike compression scheme that dynamically selects between bitmap and zero-run encoding, a fully adaptive congestion-aware routing algorithm, and a dual-mode dataflow architecture with multi-level clock gating. Compared to the baseline, our design reduces latency by 38% and lowers power by 8.3×. Furthermore, the proposed router achieves a peak throughput of 44.8 Gbps at 100 MHz, which is the highest among existing designs, while maintaining ultra-low energy consumption of 1.5×10-2pJ/bit.

title: Variance-Aware Quantized Multi-Scale Conformer for Efficient ECG Rhythm Classification on Resource-Constrained Devices.
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) rhythm classification is vital for the early detection and continuous monitoring of cardiac disorders. To address this, we propose a Conformer-based architecture that effectively models both local waveform morphology and long-range temporal dependencies in ECG signals. However, deploying deep learning models on resource-constrained devices is challenging due to their high computational and memory demands. To address this, we introduce an adaptive layer-wise quantization framework driven by layer importance estimation. The sensitivity of each layer is quantified using a combination of parameter density, weight variance, and kurtosis, capturing both scale and higher-order distributional characteristics of network weights. This formulation enables fine-grained bit-width allocation across layers, applying conservative quantization to diagnostically critical modules while allowing aggressive quantization for redundant ones. Extensive experiments on the Chapman dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves up to 9.52× compression, consistently outperforming fixed-precision baselines. A comprehensive ablation study further validates the individual and joint contributions of each sensitivity component to overall performance.

title: harDyT: A Post-Training Hardware-Aware LayerNorm Replacement.
abstract: Layer Normalization (LayerNorm) is essential in modern deep learning models like vision transformers, but its computational overhead and non-linear operations hinder efficient deployment on hardware accelerators like FPGAs. In this paper, we present harDyT, a novel hardware-aware post-training replacement for LayerNorm designed for efficient FPGA deployment. Our approach substitutes standard LayerNorm with a simplified functional formulation that relies exclusively on comparison and clipping operations, augmented by multiplication with per-channel learnable parameters alongside conventional channel-wise shift and scale operations. Unlike existing methods that require extensive large-scale training, our technique achieves effective replacement with only 5 epochs of fine-tuning and 20k calibration samples on pre-trained models. We evaluate harDyT across ConvNeXt, Swin Transformer, DeiT, and Vision Transformer (ViT), demonstrating performance preservation and significant reduction in computational complexity by eliminating costly operations such as divisions and square roots. Our results show that attention-based models can adopt harDyT with minimal accuracy degradation, making it a practical drop-in replacement for LayerNorm in hardware-constrained environments. This work highlights how hardware-aware functions can enable scalable and high-performance deep learning inference on resource-constrained devices.

title: Design and validation of a clocked gm-C bandpower extraction circuit for biosignal analysis.
abstract: This paper presents a compact and hardware-efficient bandpower extraction circuit for analog spectral analysis of local field potentials (LFPs), enabling robust real-time biomarker detection for closed-loop deep brain stimulation (DBS). A clocked-transconductor architecture provides digitally tuneable low-frequency filtering with minimal capacitance and a fixed bias current, followed by a cross-coupled full-wave rectifier for highly power-efficient envelope detection. The circuit is designed and simulated in a 65 nm CMOS process and cross-validated using off-the-shelf components in a board-level implementation, enabling realistic in vitro emulation prior to silicon fabrication. The prototype achieves a tuneable centre frequency of 4 to 33 Hz, a quality factor of 0.7 to 9.4, and fine frequency steps down to 1%, meeting the requirements of neural biomarkers used clinically in closed-loop neuromodulation.

title: Approximate Reciprocal-based Divider.
abstract: Recent years have seen a growing demand for smart, portable, and high-speed processing systems, posing significant challenges for digital circuit design in terms of power consumption, silicon area, and latency. Approximate Computing (AC) has emerged as an effective approach to address these challenges by allowing controlled computational errors in error-tolerant applications. In this paper, a novel approximate divider architecture based on a reciprocal algorithm is proposed. The proposed design achieves improvements of 86% in area, 92% in delay, and 79% in power consumption compared with an exact divider. The accuracy of the proposed divider is evaluated in image and signal processing applications. For change detection, it achieves a Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) of 0.99 and a Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) of 55 dB, compared with average values of 0.97 and 47.5 dB in state-of-the-art designs. In foreground extraction, the average SSIM and PSNR are 0.96 and 37.54 dB, respectively. For heartbeat QRS detection using the Pan–Tompkins algorithm, the proposed divider achieves a PSNR of 60 dB, demonstrating its suitability for error-resilient applications.

title: Towards Practical Reliability Assessment of RF-based Heartbeat Sensing with Multi-Domain Analysis.
abstract: Reliable cardiac monitoring is critical for ubiquitous health sensing. While RF-based contactless cardiac sensing enables comfortable and continuous monitoring, its reliability degrades in practice due to motion artifacts, multipath interference, and non-ideal sensing angles. We present Heartbeat Signal Quality Assessment (HSQA), an unsupervised framework that quantifies the reliability of each heartbeat without relying on the ground-turth measurements. HSQA assesses how faithfully cardiac motion is embedded in reflected RF echoes by extracting multi-domain features and fusing them via an entropy-based strategy. The resulting HSQA score provides per-sample confidence estimation, allowing unsupervised signal quality assessment and adaptive data filtering. Extensive experiments conducted in real clinical environments demonstrate that HSQA consistently improves heartbeat sensing accuracy across diverse algorithms and facilitates large-scale data cleaning, thereby enhancing the robustness of RF-based ubiquitous cardiac sensing systems.

title: Toward Backpropagation-Free On-Chip Training: Circuit-Algorithm Co-Design of a Goodness-Based Learning Tile.
abstract: Training neural networks on edge devices remains challenging due to the substantial computational and memory overheads of the backpropagation (BP) algorithm. This work introduces ASGE-Lite, a hardware-algorithm co-design that builds upon the layer-wise training algorithm, Adaptive Spatial Goodness Encoding (ASGE) to overcome these limitations. By algorithmically replacing multiplications with simpler operations, ASGE-Lite achieves a significant reduction in computational complexity. A hardware prototype, the ASGE-Lite Tile, is implemented and integrated into the training framework. Experimental results demonstrate that ASGE-Lite Tile preserves training accuracy while achieving a compact area, low power consumption, and high throughput, confirming its efficacy for on-chip learning in resource-constrained edge environments.

title: PacViT: An Efficient ViT Accelerator with Native Dynamic Pruning and Sliding Cache Attention.
abstract: Vision Transformers have become foundational for various visual tasks. However, their intensive computational and memory requirements impede deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. To address this, we propose PacViT, a hardware-algorithm co-designed accelerator for efficient edge vision applications. PacViT introduces two key innovations: (1) Native Dynamic Pruning (NDP) leverages intrinsic attention matrices to prune redundant vision tokens with zero overhead; and (2) Sliding Cache Attention (SCA) exploits hardware local buffers as resource-aware KV caches to enhance window-based attention accuracy. Co-optimized with a dedicated architecture and dataflow, the 28 nm PacViT processor achieves a 403× gain (5.58 mJ/frame) in energy efficiency over an Nvidia V100 GPU, while maintaining comparable inference speed (9.31 ms/frame) and accuracy (2% Top-1 drop).

title: Res-P4DGS:Enhancing 4D Gaussian Splatting Compression with Scene-Depth Prior.
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has attracted significant attention for its superior scene representation fidelity and real-time rendering capability, particularly in dynamic 3D scene reconstruction (4D reconstruction). Recent work has attempted to compress 4D scene data more efficiently, with some approaches achieving high compression ratios but at the cost of degraded reconstruction quality. Striking a balance between storage efficiency and reconstruction fidelity thus remains a critical challenge. To address this, we present Res-P4DGS, a residual-augmented version of 4DGS for compact dynamic scene modeling. Our method first compares rendered views with ground-truth images to identify regions that are reconstructed poorly. We then use depth maps to guide the addition of residual Gaussian primitives to improve those areas. To avoid large extra storage, we design a dedicated compression strategy for these residual Gaussians. Experiments on real-world datasets show that Res-P4DGS improves reconstruction quality while keeping storage extremely low and maintaining real-time rendering speed.

title: A Double-Node-Upset Tolerant Latch for Enhanced Reliability in Radiation-Prone Environments.
abstract: With the continuous scaling down of transistors, soft errors caused by high-energy particles have become increasingly critical, particularly the Multi-Node Upset (MNU) phenomenon in sequential elements. Existing mitigation techniques, especially conventional Double-Node Upset (DNU)-tolerant latches, suffer from significant power and area overheads, which limits their practical applicability. To address these limitations, we propose a highly reliable, non-redundant DNU-tolerant latch implemented in 28 nm CMOS technology. The proposed Low-Complexity High-Reliability Latch (LCHRL) eliminates redundant structures found in traditional designs. By integrating a specially designed inverter with Muller C-elements, LCHRL ensures robust data retention during DNUs while achieving an impressive 3193% reduction in Power-Delay-Area Product (PDAP) compared to state-of-the-art DNU-tolerant latches.

title: An ASIC Emulated Oscillator Ising/Potts Machine Solving Combinatorial Optimization Problems.
abstract: Oscillator-based Ising/Potts machines (OIMs/OPMs) are promising hardware accelerators for NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems using coupled oscillator synchronization dynamics. Analog OIMs/OPMs offer speed advantages but have limited coupling resolution, process variation susceptibility, and scalability issues, while digital GPU/CPU emulations provide flexibility but suffer from irregular memory access patterns and energy inefficiency. This work presents a custom ASIC architecture that digitally emulates OIM/OPM dynamics using simplified fixed-point Kuramoto model equations. The scalable design features processing elements with direct interconnections, eliminating shared memory bottleneck while maintaining digital programmability and precision. A 20×20 processing element array with king’s graph connectivity is prototyped and evaluated via post-layout simulations on unweighted/weighted max-cut and graph coloring problems, achieving 97-100% maximum accuracy with significant speed and energy improvements over general-purpose platforms, demonstrating the viability of algorithmically codesigned ASICs.

title: The Hacker Fab: An Open-Source Initiative for Nanofabrication Education.
abstract: Teaching nanofabrication to undergraduates can be challenging due to the limited availability and high cost of processing equipment and infrastructure, such as cleanroom facilities. The Hacker Fab, an initiative launched in 2023 at Carnegie Mellon University, seeks to lower these barriers by developing innovative, low-cost, open-source semiconductor fabrication tools and processes. The initiative breaks traditional models by introducing students to the fundamental principles of semiconductor device fabrication in an affordable and accessible manner through a project-based course that provides opportunities to engage in hands-on projects that directly contribute to the advancement of the laboratory infrastructure. The unique, scalable model is also highly adaptable, enabling the ability to follow industry and research trends.

title: Design and Validation of a Wireless System for Bokashi Compost Monitoring.
abstract: Bokashi composting is an anaerobic fermentation process that offers a sustainable alternative for organic waste management by preserving nutrients and reducing gaseous emissions associated with aerobic composting. However, the lack of practical and energy-efficient monitoring tools limits its optimization and broader adoption under real-world conditions. This paper presents a low-power, LoRa-enabled IoT platform designed for autonomous, real-time monitoring of Bokashi fermentation processes. The proposed system demonstrates the feasibility of long-range, ultra-low-power wireless sensing to observe anaerobic fermentation dynamics while operating under constrained energy resources. Experimental operation shows that the platform can achieve 38 hours of standalone autonomy on a compact Li-ion battery. An on-board solar panel can further extend this autonomy based on solar radiation levels. Overall, this work highlights the potential of low-power LoRa-based IoT architectures to support climate-smart agricultural practises and sustainable waste management through real-time monitoring of anaerobic bio-processes.

title: Verification of Quantum Fourier Transform and Its Inverse via Rotational and Superposition Abstraction.
abstract: In this work, we present a scalable formal verification method for the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) and its inverse (iQFT). A novel bit-vector-based abstraction that models both superposition and rotational behaviours of quantum gates is employed to achieve efficiency and scalability. Abstraction-aligned formal properties are introduced that capture functional correctness for QFT and iQFT. The approach is able to verify both QFT and iQFT circuits with 50,000 qubits in under 25 minutes.

title: A Low Power Single Sampler based PAM3 Error Receiver using Incoming Error Signal Information.
abstract: Advanced graphics double data rate (GDDR) standard is adopting multi-level signaling with increased data rate to foster to the demands of the next generation graphics processing unit (GPU). The next generation GDDR supports a separate error correction mechanism in the form of an error receiver for reliable data transfer, unlike previous generation of GDDR(s) where error detection code (EDC) is used for this purpose. This error information is coded in pulse amplitude modulation 3 (PAM3) levels instead of the traditional non-return to zero (NRZ). Conventional PAM3 receiver design involves linear equalizer or variable gain amplifier (VGA) followed by two high-speed samplers. However, these designs are not power and area efficient from a PAM3 error receiver perspective. A low pJ/bit is a key performance parameter to be met in any competitive design. Accordingly, in this paper, a power and an area efficient PAM3 error receiver architecture employing a single sampler is proposed. Proposed error receiver architecture utilizes the PAM3 coded information to reduce the overall error receiver power. A single sampler design using dynamically switchable reference voltage along with the single-phase clock based deserializer utilizing local single-2-differential (S2D) clock generator is proposed. Implemented in 3nm FinFET technology, the proposed techniques reduce the overall receiver power by at least 50% across PAM3 error symbols when compared with the conventional error receiver design. Further, single sampler design lowers kickback noise observed on sampler’s input.

title: FIR Feedback in Incremental ∆Σ Modulators with Feedback-Assisted Input-Stage Linearization.
abstract: Finite-impulse-response (FIR) feedback in Delta-Sigma (∆Σ) converters allows to combine benefits of single-and multi-bit feedback, e.g. inherent linearity, low sensitivity to clock jitter, and smooth feedback waveforms. The latter can e.g. be employed for a global feedback linearization of Gm-input Delta-Sigma-Modulators (DSMs). In incremental Delta-Sigma modulators (I-DSMs), however, the reset of all memory elements poses significant challenges toward the use of a FIR-digital-to-analog converter (DAC) in the feedback due to a temporary loss of input tracking needed for such Gminput-stage linearization. In this work, an existing method to restore the input tracking after the reset by presetting the FIR feedback is enhanced. Through analysis of the error, a correction method is proposed, which is robust against coefficient mismatch. Furthermore, a simplification to presetting by simply omitting the reset of the feedback path is introduced. The effectiveness of the techniques is demonstrated with an exemplary 3rd-order I-DSM.

title: An Autonomous Wireless Biosensor Node for multi-seasonal in-vivo Crop Monitoring.
abstract: This paper presents an autonomous wireless biosensor node for in-vivo and real-time plant monitoring in crops. An organic electrochemical transistor nested in the plant stem is used to detect variations in the concentration of cations in the xylem sap. A battery life-time as long as four years was estimated in spite of the high bias current of the sensor and the long observation time frame, thanks to sensor duty cycling and signal post-processing combined with low-cost energy harvesting.

title: A Hyper-Extended Dual-path Quadrature Sub-Sampling Phase Detector with Double-Cycle (720°) Phase Ambiguity Resolution.
abstract: The sub-sampling phase-lock loop (SSPLL) has been widely researched for its low phase noise and high operating frequency. However, its sub-sampling phase detector (SSPD) suffers from a limited detection range. Conventional SSPDs have a sinusoidal characteristic curve, which restricts the positive-gain phase detection range to [-π/2, π/2] and the overall phase detection range to [-π, π]. This limitation narrows the loop’s lock-in range, necessitating an auxiliary frequency-lock loop (FLL). Nevertheless, false locking can still occur in the phase frequency detector (PFD) phase-flipping intervals and be taken over by sub-sampling loop (SSL). To address these issues, this paper proposes a dual-path quadrature sub-sampling phase detector (D-QSSPD). By optimizing the sub-sampling topology, the proposed design expands the positive-gain phase detection range to [-π, π] and the overall phase detection range to [-2π, 2π]. This significantly broadens the lock-in range of the SSPLL, which accelerate the locking speed, reduce reliance on auxiliary FLL, mitigate false locking and finally advance the SSPLL performance for high-frequency applications.

title: A 442.42 TOPS/W RRAM-based Digital Computing-in-Memory Accelerator for BF16×1-bit Vision Transformer.
abstract: RRAM-based Computing-in-Memory (CIM) architectures are promising for efficient Transformer inference, yet analog approaches suffer from circuit non-idealities and limited precision, leading to accuracy degradation. In this paper, a fully digital CIM accelerator based on RRAM is proposed to achieve a better trade-off between accuracy, energy, and area. Firstly, a hardware-oriented W1A16 quantization strategy is proposed, incorporating the architectural enhancements of BinaryViT to compensate for the capacity loss of 1-bit weights. By maintaining activations in Brain-Floating Point-16 (BF16) format and utilizing hard distillation, the quantized Vision Transformer achieves competitive accuracy with minimized memory footprint. Then, a fully digital RRAM-based CIM accelerator is designed with an area-efficient 4T-XOR and a fine-grained mantissa shifter. Implemented on 28nm technology node, the proposed design achieves a peak normalized energy efficiency of 442.42 TOPS/W.

title: Spectral Impact of Mismatches in Interleaved ADCs.
abstract: Interleaved ADCs are critical for applications requiring multi-gigasample per second (GS/s) rates, but their performance is often limited by offset, gain, and timing skew mismatches across the sub-ADCs. We propose exact but compact expressions that describe the impact of each of those non-idealities on the output spectrum. We derive the distribution of the power of the induced spurs and replicas, critical for yield-oriented derivation of sub-ADC specifications. Finally, we provide a practical example in which calibration step sizes are derived under the constraint of a target production yield.

title: A Multiplier-Free Similarity Metric for Token Merging in Vision Transformers.
abstract: Token Merging (TM) has become an effective and widely adopted strategy for accelerating Vision Transformers (ViTs), reducing computational cost by merging similar tokens without requiring model retraining. However, the metric used to compute this pairwise similarity suffers from an accuracy-cost dilemma. Cosine similarity, despite being the de facto standard, is computationally expensive for hardware implementations, while existing lightweight metrics yield only moderate performance. To resolve this, we introduce the Transform-Domain L1 Distance (TDL), a multiplier-free similarity metric with competitive model accuracy. This paper first proposes an automated search strategy using Simulated Annealing (SA) to discover optimal transform kernels. With these SA-found kernels, TDL allows the host model to sustain or surpass task accuracy compared with cosine similarity. Then, through comprehensive comparison, we identify the Hadamard kernel as a highly effective universal transform kernel. By exploiting the Fast Hadamard Transform (FHT), TDL with Hadamard kernel delivers exceptional hardware efficiency while maintaining almost the same accuracy with (and often exceeding) cosine similarity, establishing a new Pareto-optimal solution for hardware-efficient TM design.

title: HHGC: High-Throughput High-Accuracy Gradient Data Compression.
abstract: The growing scale of deep neural networks (DNNs) necessitates distributed training, yet data parallelism introduces communication bottlenecks. While gradient compression mitigates bandwidth demands, existing lossy methods compromise accuracy and increase computation. We propose HHGC, a high-precision compression framework for floating-point gradients that strategically optimizes FP32 components: (1) sign-bit retention preserves directional integrity, (2) two-phase prediction-encoding for exponents reduces redundancy, and (3) 14-bit adaptive mantissa truncation allows accuracy to be maintained with maximum compression. Experimental results show that we can significantly improve the compression ratio by 10% compared to existing floating-point compression techniques, while training accuracy is consistent with or even exceeds the baseline. Furthermore, we co-design an efficient hardware architecture, validated on an FPGA prototype, which achieves a throughput of 120 Gbps, far higher than existing lossless compression hardware.

title: A High dv/dt-Tolerant Level Shifter with Sub-Nanosecond Delay Using Dummy Pulse Protection.
abstract: This paper presents two Pulse Triggered Level Shifters (PT-LS) that use a dummy pulse to increase tolerance to HVSS slewing (dv/dt). An IO (5V) device based design provides high dv/dt tolerance. Another core (1.8V) device based design achieves lower transition energy ET, and lower propagation delay TP. Both designs are implemented in a 180nm process. These Dummy Pulse Level Shifters (DP-LS) use an additional dummy current path compared to other PT-LS designs to mitigate glitches or flips caused by high dv/dt, common in GaN-based power systems. The IO design maintains output integrity under dv/dt conditions up to 5000 V/ns, achieves a TPof 0.98ns, and ETof 80.23pJ in post-layout simulations. The core design demonstrates dv/dt tolerance of 40 V/ns, TPas low as 0.42ns, and ETas low as 10.79pJ in post-layout simulations. Compared to state-of-theart LS architectures with the highest dv/dt, the IO based DP-LS shows a reduction in Figure of Merit (FoM) by almost 2x due to lower ETand lower TPwhile maintaining the same dv/dt.

title: An Enhanced-Bandwidth Noise-Shaping SAR ADC Using RC-Tracking Circuit as Amplifier.
abstract: This paper presents a noise-shaping (NS) successive-approximation register (SAR) ADC with an enhanced bandwidth of 200 MHz. The ADC incorporates a 2b/cycle architecture using voltage-domain and time-domain comparators. The ADC accomplishes 4th-order noise shaping using a novel RC-tracking circuit as a passive amplifier. Implemented in a 28-nm CMOS process, simulations show that the ADC achieves a 67.7-dB signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) while consuming 2.73 mW of power. It achieves a FoMWof 3.3 fJ/conv.-step and FoMSof 179 dB.
