title: RCW-CIM: A Digital CIM-based LLM Accelerator with Read-Compute/Write.
abstract: Digital computing-in-memory (DCIM) has emerged as a promising solution for large language model (LLM) acceleration by minimizing data transfers between external DRAM and on-chip accelerators while maintaining high precision for superior accuracy. However, existing CIM architectures often overlook weight update latency, which becomes critical as LLM weights are far larger than a single CIM macro’s capacity. To address this issue, this paper proposes a read-compute/write (RCW) architecture that effectively minimizes weight update latency, along with a nonlinear operator fusion that further mitigates dependency-induced latency. The proposed RCW reduces decoding computing latency by 21.59% on the Llama2-7B model. In addition, the nonlinear operator fusion mechanism achieves a 69.17% latency reduction through efficient partial accumulation and group-based approximation. Furthermore, a weight-stationary and output-column-stationary (WS-OCS) dataflow is introduced to reduce both external DRAM access and internal CIM weight updates—by 51.6% and 87.6%, respectively—during the prefill phase of 1024 tokens, leading to an overall 49.76% latency reduction. Fabricated using TSMC 22 nm CMOS technology and operating at 100 MHz, the proposed RCW-CIM achieves 3.28 TOPS and 42.3 TOPS/W, enabling 4.2 ms prefill latency and 26.87 decoded tokens per second for the INT4-weight Llama2 model with dual DDR5-6400 memory.

title: Balancing Speed and Accuracy for Robust Analog-Mixed Signal Circuit Design using Closed-Loop Reinforcement Learning with Ensemble Neural Network Surrogates.
abstract: Analog/mixed-signal (AMS) circuit sizing requires exploring high-dimensional, constrained design spaces under expensive SPICE simulations, while maintaining robustness to out-of-distribution (OOD) parameter proposals. We propose a fidelity-aware reinforcement learning framework (RL-PPO-Online) that unifies (i) SPICE-in-the-loop verification and (ii) ensemble neural network guided regularization for surrogate-assisted optimization. Another PPO policy (RL-PPO-Offline) is trained using an ensemble neural network for fast performance prediction, while a discriminator penalizes OOD actions to stabilize surrogate-only updates. We further introduce RL-PPO-Blend, which schedules a small fraction of SPICE queries (0.2–5%) on top of RL-PPO-Offline to provide a tunable speed–fidelity trade-off. On challenging ADC front-end sizing tasks in 28 nm (bootstrapped sampling switch and input buffer + switch), the proposed method improves pass rates over DDPG and LLM baselines, and achieves near-online accuracy with substantially reduced simulation cost.

title: GenFall: A Configurable Fall Dataset Generated via Text-to-Motion Models for Wearable Fall Detection.
abstract: Reliable wearable fall detection requires large-scale and diverse datasets of falls and activities of daily living, yet collecting real-world falls from the elderly is ethically and practically challenging. We propose GenFall, a configurable synthetic fall dataset generated via diffusion-based text-to-motion models trained on large-scale human motion corpora. Virtual inertial signals, comprising triaxial accelerometer/gyroscope data, are computed from generated 3D trajectories to emulate sensors at arbitrary body positions. Each motion sequence undergoes rigorous quality control to ensure biomechanical plausibility and temporal continuity, resulting in a physically consistent dataset. Using GenFall, we evaluate the influence of dataset scale on fall-detection performance through representative neural architectures, including an LSTM baseline and a CNN–LSTM hybrid. Results demonstrate that training with larger-scale synthetic data improves model robustness and generalization, with the CNN–LSTM structure capturing superior spatiotemporal patterns. GenFall provides a scalable foundation for developing and benchmarking wearable fall-detection algorithms based on generative data.

title: A Hybrid Quantization Method for FMCW Radar Data Compression.
abstract: FMCW radar is widely used in the field of autonomous driving. However, the high-resolution signal processing in FMCW radar presents challenges for on-chip memory and transmission bandwidth. Thus, We propose a compression method that integrates a lattice vector quantization scheme with non-uniform amplitude quantization, while employing uniform quantization for phase. During amplitude quantization, the algorithm first performs grouped quantization on spectral data to mitigate the impact of high-amplitude values on quantization accuracy. It then applies vector normalization to reduce the hardware resources required for storing shared parameters, and selects the quantization approach based on the numerical distribution characteristics. All modules are implemented with hardware-friendly operations to strike a balance between efficiency and feasibility. The experimental results demonstrate that our algorithm achieves a 74.8% reduction in storage usage while maintaining a reconstructed signal PSNR of 40 dB, and requires only a minimal amount of additional computational resources to ensure its object detection performance.

title: LUT-SNN: Efficient Spiking Neural Networks with Fast Parallel Inference.
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have shown great potential for low-power intelligent sensing and edge computing due to their sparse and event-driven nature. However, inference in conventional Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) models requires sequential membrane potential updates across time steps, hindering parallel execution. To overcome this limitation, we propose a lookup-table-based parallel LIF neuron model (LUT-SNN) and an algorithm–hardware co-optimization framework for acceleration. For the algorithm, by precomputing threshold boundaries, the temporal recurrence is transformed into a spatial lookup operation, achieving constant-time parallel inference. Based on this model, we design a systolic-array accelerator that employs comparator trees and on-chip LUT modules for efficient neuronal computation. Experimental results show that, compared with standard LIF-based SNNs, LUT-SNN achieves up to 2.89× speedup on the proposed accelerator for ResNet-18 model on TinyImageNet datasets with 4 timesteps, while maintaining comparable accuracy. This work provides a new perspective for efficient and parallel SNN inference and hardware implementation.

title: SNTT: A Sparsity-aware NTT Accelerator Based on FPGA for Zero-Knowledge Proof.
abstract: Zero-knowledge proofs (ZKP) have been widely adopted in verifiable computing and privacy-preserving computing. Efficient generation of ZKP relies heavily on large-scale polynomial multiplications, which are typically accelerated using Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) techniques. NTT has been the second bottleneck for the proof generation. The existing NTT accelerators are not suitable for ZKP settings due to poor support to the large size and overlook to the inherent sparisty in ZKP setting.In this work, we propose a sparsity-aware NTT acceleration scheme based on an optimized algorithm, SMD-NTT, which exploits the inherent sparsity in ZKP settings. In addition, By incorporating the Winograd NTT (WNTT) and the Multipath Delay Commutator (MDC), the resource consumption of the NTT computation core is reduced. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed accelerator achieves 42.13% latency reduction for sparse NTT computations. Compared with existing designs, it also achieves 24.79% reduction in the area-time product (ATP), highlighting its superior performance and resource efficiency.

title: Performance Pragma-Based Design Space Pruning and Exploration for High-Level Synthesis.
abstract: High-level synthesis (HLS) tools are widely used to design field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) and application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) using high-level languages like C/C++. Existing tools typically provide a set of directives for optimizing generated designs, necessitating exploration of the vast design space formed by directive combinations to obtain satisfactory designs. To tackle this, numerous HLS design space exploration (DSE) frameworks have been proposed in recent years. However, these frameworks either inadequately prune the design space or lack pruning method, leading to excessively long exploration time. This work replaces traditional pragma combinations with the newly released PERFORMANCE pragma in Vitis HLS. Our approach eliminates unreasonable pragma combinations and substantially reduces the total number of pragmas employed. It also prunes pragma parameter values to exclude redundant designs, thereby further shrinking the design space. The proposed framework employs graph neural networks (GNNs) to predict the quality of results (QoR) of candidate designs and adopts Bayesian optimization (BO) for efficient exploration. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves a Pareto front comparable to the state-of-the-art (SOTA) with a 38.30% improvement in ADRS.

title: A Fully Integrated Gate Driver With Closed-Loop Feedback Achieving Wide Output Range Using Low-VGS Devices.
abstract: This paper presents a fully integrated high-voltage gate driver architecture that achieves an extended output range while exclusively employing low gate-source voltage (low-VGS) devices, thereby eliminating the requirement for thick-gate-oxide transistors. The proposed architecture incorporates an adaptive closed-loop feedback control mechanism to ensure precise regulation of the driver output voltage. The control scheme operates by amplifying the error between the sampled output voltage and a predetermined reference voltage, which subsequently modulates the gate potential of the pull-up transistor to establish accurate control over the driver output voltage. Designed in a 0.18 μm BCD process, the gate driver demonstrates a maximum output voltage of 20 V with simulated rise and fall time of 37 ns and 24 ns. Moreover, the design exhibits exceptional thermal stability, maintaining output voltage variation within ±5% across the industrial temperature range of -40°C to 125°C, validating its robustness for deployment in harsh operating environments.

title: RRAM-as-Reference Sensing with Parallelogram Crossbar Architecture for Large-Scale Arrays.
abstract: This paper proposes a reading scheme for RRAM devices that employs an RRAM as the reference element utilizing its multi-level, which reduces the sense margin issue in large-scale crossbars, especially for distant RRAM cells, relative to the traditional resistor-based reference. Furthermore, a parallelogram-shaped crossbar architecture is introduced, enabling all cells to share a single sense amplifier while mitigating the imbalance of parasitic resistances along the sensing current path.

title: A 97.4% Efficiency IoT Buck Converter With Adaptive On-Time and Quasi-V2 Control.
abstract: This paper presents a DC-DC buck converter based on Quasi-V2control topology, which is specifically designed to meet the low-power and high-efficiency power supply demands of Internet of Things (IoT) devices and implemented in a 0.18-μm BCD process. Under heavy and light load conditions, Continuous Conduction Mode (CCM) and Discontinuous Conduction Mode (DCM) with Adaptive On-Time (AOT) are employed; whereas in ultra-light loading conditions, Hiccup mode (HM) is adopted to reduce quiescent current and improve efficiency. This converter operates with an input voltage range of 3-5 V and an output voltage range of 0.9-1.5 V, maintaining high efficiency across the entire operating range. When converting from 3 V to 1.5 V, the converter maintains an efficiency of over 90% across a load current range of 10 μA to 1 A; furthermore, when the load current is 100 mA, the converter achieves a peak efficiency of 97.4%. The maximum output voltage ripple is 19.5 mV with 5 V input, 0.9 V output, and 10 μA loading condition.

title: A Post-Fabrication Tunable TDC-PUF Using VG-SOT MRAM for Robust Hardware Security.
abstract: The demand for secure and energy-efficient hardware authentication in resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) devices continues to rise. This brief presents a voltage-gated spin–orbit torque (VG-SOT) MRAM-based physically unclonable function (PUF) with a time-to-digital converter (TDC) readout. The proposed design converts intrinsic resistance variations of VG-SOT cells into discharge-time differences, enabling one-bit-per-cell output without complex reference-voltage circuits. An externally controlled delay chain allows post-fabrication tuning of sampling time, enhancing adaptability to process, voltage, temperature variations. Fabricated in 28 nm CMOS and evaluated through Monte Carlo simulations with 3% MTJ diameter variation, the PUF achieves near-ideal uniformity (50.02%) and uniqueness (50.66%), with reliability above 99.37% from -40 °C to 125 °C and 0.8–1.2 V. NIST SP800-22 randomness tests and autocorrelation analysis confirm strong statistical randomness. Compared with SRAM-, STT-MRAM-, and prior VG-SOT-based PUFs, the proposed design delivers higher CRP density, robust environmental stability, and post-fabrication tunability, making it an attractive solution for lightweight and secure embedded identification.

title: A 96.8% Peak Efficiency Dual-Path Hybrid Step-Down Converter With Full Voltage-Conversion Ratio and Reduced Inductor Current.
abstract: This paper proposes a full conversion ratio dual-path (FCR2-DP) hybrid step-down DC-DC converter, which achieves voltage regulation across the full range from 0 to VIN. The converter consists of five power transistors and a single inductor, which employs three working phases and operates in three distinct modes, enabling precise output voltage adjustment. To minimize inductor current and DC resistance (DCR) losses, the converter employs a dual-path structure comprising inductors and capacitors in all operating modes. Additionally, the converter ensures the inductor currents remain below the load current in all three modes, thereby enhancing efficiency. An experimental prototype for 5 V input to 0.6-4.5V output has been developed, demonstrating excellent performance of FCR2-DP hybrid converter topology in reducing inductor current and achieving high efficiency. The prototype has been measured at a switching frequency of 1 MHz and achieves a full voltage-conversion range of 0-1 and a maximum load current of 2A. The peak efficiency reaches 96.8% at VOUT=4V and ILOAD=1.2A, validating the effectiveness of the proposed topology.

title: MeritFL: Self-Regulating Federated Learning via Merit-Gated Communication.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training on decentralized data while preserving privacy. However, communication inefficiencies remain a significant challenge, as existing protocols allow clients to participate without evaluating their learning progress or update quality. Current approaches waste bandwidth on redundant or low-quality updates, risk destabilizing the global model, and fail to adapt to client heterogeneity in diverse federated environments. In this paper, we propose MeritFL, a self-regulating framework that transforms FL communication from a schedule-based to a value-based paradigm. MeritFL introduces a client-side merit assessment mechanism based on normalized loss reduction that autonomously gates low-quality updates before transmission. Additionally, a server-side proportional control mechanism dynamically adjusts participation thresholds, creating a closed-loop feedback system that intelligently allocates communication resources to clients providing the most valuable contributions. Experiments on CIFAR-10 show MeritFL achieves 87.53% accuracy, outperforming FedAvg by 2.88%. It converges 1.47× faster while reducing communication by 47.3%, demonstrating superior efficiency and performance in federated learning scenarios.

title: FPGA-Based Hardware Optimization for Low-Power High-Speed NLM Algorithms.
abstract: Denoising algorithms play a critical role in eliminating image noise and enhancing video quality for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and Internet of Things (IoT) applications. Existing denoising approaches typically rely on computationally intensive designs implemented on Graphics Processing Units (GPUs), which are ill-suited for the stringent constraints of both UAV and IoT edge devices requiring low latency and minimal power consumption. Meanwhile, conventional hardware-based denoising circuits often exhibit prohibitively high power consumption and excessive resource utilization for these resource-constrained systems. To overcome these limitations, we present a hardware-optimized low-power Non-Local Means (NLM) algorithm specifically designed for visual processing in UAV and IoT environments. We streamline the algorithm by replacing squared and exponential operations with absolute value and customizable multi-linear function. This enhances adaptability for diverse UAV and IoT scenarios. Deployed on hardware, it processes 1080P@60FPS video at an ultra-low latency of 14.68 us while consuming only 0.077W, ideal for power-constrained devices.

title: A Low-IF GFSK Demodulator Achieving 0.1% BER under ±450 kHz Frequency Offset via Dynamic Fractional Delay Calibration.
abstract: This paper presents a low-IF GFSK demodulator with enhanced robustness against intermediate-frequency (IF) offset. The proposed architecture integrates a controllable Farrow-based fractional delay line for precise digital delay tuning and a dynamic IF-offset calibration (IF-OC) loop for real-time frequency offset tracking. This adaptive mechanism effectively stabilizes the recovered baseband envelope under large IF deviations. Implemented in 55nm CMOS technology with a 0.8V supply, simulation and post-layout estimation indicate that the demodulator achieves a BER of 0.1% with a minimum SNR of 10dB, and tolerates up to ±450kHz IF offset at 15dB SNR. The design consumes 68μW and occupies 0.009mm2, demonstrating high efficiency and suitability for robust, low-power wireless communication systems.

title: Delta-Sigma Modulator-Based Compute-in-Memory Neural Network with Analog Feature Extraction and Classification for Edge Sensors.
abstract: This work presents an on-chip feature extractor and classifier that reduces sensor transmission by >1000× through on-chip data analysis. The classifier includes reservoir computing (RC) layer for unsupervised feature extraction followed by an artificial neural network (ANN) layer for supervised classification. The RC layer is implemented using switched-capacitor circuits, while the ANN uses a delta-sigma modulator-based 9T1C compute-in-memory (CIM) macro that supports variable-resolution precision. A test chip, fabricated in a 28nm process, is demonstrated for stress and seismic event detection. The test-chip achieves mean classification accuracies of 97.0% for stress detection and 95.8% for seismic event detection, with energy consumption of 1.3nJ/classification for stress and 4.25nJ/classification for seismic events.

title: Respiratory Disease Prediction from Lung Sounds Using Reservoir Computing.
abstract: Respiratory diseases are among the leading causes of mortality worldwide, including in the United States. Respiratory sounds provide critical insight into pulmonary health, as they are directly influenced by airflow dynamics, changes in lung tissue, and the presence of secretions within the tracheobronchial tree [1]. In this work, we present an artificial intelligence (AI)–based approach for predicting respiratory diseases from lung sounds, integrated into a wearable platform for on-device monitoring. Using the ICBHI 2017 Respiratory Sound Database [2], our method demonstrates strong performance in both binary classification (Healthy vs. Unhealthy) and multiclass classification (six respiratory diseases). The proposed solution employs an analog reservoir computer (RC) fabricated in a 28 nm CMOS process, achieving energy-efficient operation with a consumption of only 12.9nJ per prediction for multiclass and 7.4nJ per prediction for binary class, while reaching 91% accuracy for binary classification and 89% accuracy for multiclass classification.

title: A 16-Channel Rapid On-Chip Seizure Classifier With Online Re-Training for Closed-loop Neuromodulation.
abstract: Closed-loop neuromodulation-based deep-brain stimulation devices are increasingly used for treating neurological disorders such as epilepsy. These systems require on-chip intelligence for reliable seizure onset detection under strict power and area constraints. Achieving low-latency detection while adapting to the dynamic nature of neural signals remains a major challenge. This paper presents an on-chip seizure detection framework based on online re-training. The proposed system continuously adapts to variations in neural recordings through a two-step self-labelling and balancing mechanism that ensures stable and unbiased model updates. A logistic regression classifier enables efficient real-time inference, and a stochastic gradient descent-based balanced re-training engine enables adaptation over time. The 16-channel prototype achieves a sensitivity of 95.3%, specificity of 95.2%, a rapid inference time of only 240 ms, an energy efficiency of 1.83 nJ/classification and a compact area of 0.017 mm2.

title: A Synchronous EEG-fNIRS BCI: A Proof-of-Concept for Multimodal Avalanche Analysis of Motor Cognition in Older Adults.
abstract: This proof-of-concept study introduces a novel multimodal framework combining synchronized EEG-fNIRS modalities with neuronal avalanche analysis to identify early network dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease. The approach leverages complementary neural signals to examine motor network dynamics during execution and imagery tasks within an interactive task environment. Preliminary analysis of a small pilot cohort (N=4 subjects, including one with Mild Cognitive Impairment) validated the technical feasibility of the multimodal framework and revealed observable condition-dependent patterns in network organization. Two primary observations emerged: a reduced neural contrast between motor execution and imagery states, and increased trial-to-trial variability in network organization in the MCI participant. These initial results successfully validate the technical pipeline and provide hypothesis-generating observations for future statistically powered studies. The convergence of findings across modalities suggests that multimodal assessment of network flexibility may help detect functional changes in early Alzheimer’s continuum, supporting the future development of this BCI-inspired framework into an engaging diagnostic tool.

title: A Near-Sensor Image Compression Architecture with RRAM-based Hyperdimensional Encoder for Smart Vision.
abstract: Image compression is crucial for edge vision systems, but traditional human vision-optimized methods are inefficient for machine tasks and raw data transmission faces bandwidth constraints. To tackle these issues, this paper exploits the compatibility between brain-inspired hyperdimensional computing (HDC) and in-memory computing, proposing an RRAM-based HDC architecture for near-sensor image compression. This architecture encodes images into high-dimensional vectors near sensor, enabling direct feature extraction and compression for downstream tasks on a host processor. The proposed method achieves a bitrate of 0.361 bpp, improving compression efficiency by 39.8% compared to existing machine vision compression approaches. Benefiting from the parallel computing capability of the RRAM-based in-memory architecture, the system enables highly energy-efficient implementation of HDC. Simulated using the 28 nm CMOS process at 100MHz, the system consumes 5.44 mW, representing a 9.4× power reduction over ASIC systems. The proposed all-in-memory encoding module achieves a system latency of 3.53 ms, which is 202× lower than the multi-cycle approach.

title: A 0.69-pJ/bit 16/24/32-Gb/s/pin NRZ/PAM-3/PAM-4 Multi-Mode Transmitter with Power-Optimal Rx Termination and Clock-Embedded DBI.
abstract: This paper presents a high-energy efficiency and high-bandwidth single-ended multi-mode transmitter for memory interfaces. This design supports three modes: non-return-to-zero (NRZ), three-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-3) and four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4). The power-optimal receiver (Rx) termination for power-isolated low-voltage swing terminated logic (PI-LVSTL) driver is analytically derived as 0.5VDDQ, minimizing the total expected signaling current. A clock-embedded data bus inversion (DBI) technique is proposed for PAM-3 and PAM-4 to attain the maximal theoretical I/O bandwidth. Implemented in 40-nm CMOS, the transmitter achieves 16/24/32 Gb/s over a 5.57-dB loss channel, with energy efficiencies of 0.89, 0.76, and 0.69 pJ/bit for NRZ, PAM-3 with DBI, and PAM-4 with DBI, respectively and occupying a core area of 0.447 mm2.

title: Mixed-signal implementation of feedback-control optimizer for single-layer Spiking Neural Networks.
abstract: On-chip learning is key to scalable and adaptive neuromorphic systems, yet existing training methods are either difficult to implement in hardware or overly restrictive. However, recent studies show that feedback-control optimizers can enable expressive, on-chip training of neuromorphic devices. In this work, we present a proof-of-concept implementation of such feedback-control optimizers on a mixed-signal neuromorphic processor. We assess the proposed approach in an In-The-Loop (ITL) training setup on both a binary classification task and the nonlinear Yin–Yang problem, demonstrating on-chip training that matches the performance of numerical simulations and gradient-based baselines. Our results highlight the feasibility of feedback-driven, online learning under realistic mixed-signal constraints, and represent a co-design approach toward embedding such rules directly in silicon for autonomous and adaptive neuromorphic computing.

title: A Two-Stage Capacitive Readout ASIC for High-Resolution Surface Characterisation With Adaptive Tuning.
abstract: Rapid acquisition of high-resolution capacitive sensors limits the allowable input range, resulting in a low tolerance to parasitic effects. Time-based capacitance front-ends present a low sensitivity to environmental effects, while supporting a wide input range. However, manual tuning is often necessary to adjust the sensor’s dynamic range to the application needs. This paper presents a two-stage, differential capacitive readout circuit with adaptive tuning for dynamic shear sensing applications, where micromotion-induced capacitance variations must be detected with high resolution. A versatile solution that combines a configurable pulse-width modulation stage and a programmable pulse extension stage is described for achieving 0.29-fF resolution with a wide input range up to 360 pF at the nominal 20 kHz excitation frequency. The circuit was implemented in a low-power mixed-signal ASIC using a standard 65-nm CMOS process. Post-layout simulations demonstrate adaptive, real-time tuning of the input capacitance range for single and differential-mode sensing. The front-end achieves a maximum sensitivity of 6.84 ns/fF while operating with a digital clock frequency of 10 MHz and requiring a total power of 19−73 μW under a 1.2-V supply.

title: Internet of Drones System for Water Quality Sensing, Sampling, 2-D Mapping, and 3-D Profiling.
abstract: This paper presents an Internet-of-Drones (IoD) platform for real-time, in-situ water quality sensing, sampling, and high-resolution 3-D modeling. The system employs a modular IoD network with dual-mode LoRa/LoRaWAN and 4G LTE communication for adaptive sampling and cooperative mapping. A single-actuator multi-sampler collects four 50mL water samples, while integrated sensors measure pH, temperature, turbidity, TDS, and depth. The circuit enables low-power telemetry, GPS geo-tagging, RTC synchronization, and SD local data logging. UAV-assisted transects reconstruct volumetric water quality fields through interpolation of spatial and vertical gradients. Field results validate robust operation and accurate 3-D water profile reconstruction, offering a scalable, cost-effective solution for high-resolution environmental monitoring.

title: Power-Efficient and Reconfigurable Compute Unit for Multi-Precision AI Inference at the Edge.
abstract: Hardware computation units require support for multi-precision calculations to run modern applications. Implementing more than one fixed-precision multiplier and using only one at a time is inefficient as the larger multiplier would dominate the critical path and slow down the maximum operating frequency. We propose two power-efficient and scalable multiplier architectures with run-time reconfigurability in this paper, namely R4RC16, and R4RC32. Each of them can operate in two modes: low-power (8-bit) and default (16-bit for R4RC16 and 32-bit for R4RC32). The two proposed reconfigurable multipliers running in low-power mode have higher energy efficiency compared to the state-of-the-art approximate logarithmic multipliers (by up to ×7.6) and the state-of-the-art approximate Booth-based multipliers (by up to ×13.8). The proposed reconfigurable multipliers have a ×2 throughput (16-bit) and a ×4 throughput (32-bit), in low-power mode, compared to an exact 8-bit multiplier. The proposed reconfigurable multipliers’ overhead, in the low-power mode, is not dependent on the multipliers’ full bit-width, so the proposed reconfigurable 16-bit and the 32-bit multiplier have a near-constant power-delay product.Through the proposed reconfigurable multiplier, the maximum operating frequency and the throughput can dynamically change in the run-time with a negligible area overhead of less than 1%.

title: CIM-Pruner: A Dual-Mode Compute-In-Memory Macro for Efficient VLMs with Intra-Chunk Token Pruning and Merging.
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities under various downstream tasks but incur significant computational overhead, especially during edge deployment. While text-guided vision token pruning algorithm effectively reduces redundancy, existing hardware architectures lack tailored support for such dynamic patterns, especially for token-level pruning and merging. We propose CIM-Pruner, a hardware-algorithm co-design framework for efficient VLM inference on digital compute-in-memory architectures. CIM-Pruner introduces: (1) an intra-chunk token pruning and merging algorithm that eliminates expensive global top-k sorting by intra-chunk incomplete sorting, (2) an early-quit bitonic sorting circuit for sorting and labeling different input tokens with reasonable area and power consumption, and (3) a dual-mode token processing unit featuring a dual-mode Booth multiplier and accumulator for differentiated token processing. Implemented in 28nm CMOS, evaluation results show that the proposed CIM-Pruner macro achieves an energy efficiency of 25.64 TOPS/W (@200MHz) featuring INT8 data precision.

title: Cross-Platform Low Operation Point In-Loop Filter for VVC Using Integer Operations.
abstract: The low operating point (LOP) loop filter has been integrated into the Neural Network-Based Video Coding (NNVC) reference software in VVC. After continuous development, the latest LOP6 brings average Bjøntegaard Delta rate (BD-rate) gains of 8.59% and 8.01% for NNVC-14.0 in Y component under all intra (AI) and random access (RA) configurations, respectively. In this paper, we propose a cross-platform LOP in-loop filter for VVC using integer operations. We replace the original structure of the LOP6 luma branch with five TwinBlocks (x) and that of the LOP6 chroma branch with five backbone blocks (BBB(x)). Compared with the original LOP6 structure, the 1×5 and 5×1 depthwise convolutions increase the receptive field of the LOP6 BBB and reduce the number of times that LOP6 BBB(1) are used once, thereby reducing the complexity of the LOP6 network. For over-parameterized training, we expand the 1×5, 5×1, 1×3, and 3×1 depthwise convolutions into multi-branch structures to enhance their multi-scale feature extraction capabilities. Moreover, we employ variable channel configurations in the chroma branch to enrich its input information while reducing network complexity. Therefore, the proposed method enhances BD-rate performance while reducing the LOP network complexity from 16.60 kMAC/pixel to 16.56 kMAC/pixel. Experimental results show that compared with the NNVC-14.0 anchor, the proposed method achieves average BD-rate gains of {-0.05% (Y), -0.55% (U), -0.07% (V)} under AI configuration and {-0.13% (Y), -0.70% (U), 0.23% (V)} under RA configuration.

title: VecIntrinBench: Benchmarking Cross-Architecture Intrinsic Code Migration for RISC-V Vector.
abstract: Intrinsic functions are specialized functions provided by the compiler that efficiently operate on architecture-specific hardware, allowing programmers to write optimized code in a high-level language that fully exploits hardware features. Using Single Instruction, Multiple Data (SIMD) intrinsics to vectorize core code blocks is a standard optimization method in high-performance libraries, often requiring specific vector optimization implementations for multiple mainstream architectures. The promising RISC-V software ecosystem has a significant demand for algorithm library migration and adaptation. Translating existing intrinsic functions to RISC-V Vector (RVV) intrinsic functions across architectures is currently a mainstream approach. Rule-based intrinsic mapping methods and LLM-based code generation can help developers address the code migration challenge. However, existing intrinsic code benchmarks focus on mainstream SIMD intrinsics and lack support for the emerging RISC-V architecture. There is currently no benchmark that comprehensively evaluates the intrinsic migration capabilities for the RVV extension. To fill this gap, we propose VecIntrinBench, the first intrinsic benchmark encompassing RVV extensions. It includes 50 function-level tasks from open source repositories, implemented as scalars, RVV intrinsics, Arm Neon intrinsics, and x86 intrinsics, along with comprehensive functional and performance test cases. We systematically evaluated various code migration approaches on VecIntrinBench, yielding a series of insightful findings. The results demonstrate that advanced Large Language Models (LLMs) achieve a similar effect as rule-based mapping approaches for RISC-V code migration, while also delivering superior performance. We further analyze the reasons and identify future directions for LLM development in the code migration field. The VecIntrinBench is open-sourced to benefit the broader community and developers.

title: A 17.28-Gb/s Transceiver With Hybrid Phase-Interpolated Clock and Data Recovery in 40-nm CMOS.
abstract: This paper presents a 17.28-Gb/s NRZ transceiver for short-reach chip-to-chip interconnects on PCB. A 17.28-GHz phase-locked loop (PLL) generates quadrature clocks shared by the transmitter and the receiver for timing recovery. The transmitter adopts a low-swing voltage-mode LVDS driver with passive RC pre-emphasis to reduce channel loss, output swing, and dynamic power consumption. The receiver employs a phase-interpolator (PI)-based clock-and-data-recovery (CDR) circuit integrating a bang-bang phase detector, majority-vote control, and an injection-locked multi-phase clock network to achieve accurate phase alignment and low jitter. Fabricated in 40-nm CMOS and operating at a 1-V supply, the prototype achieves 17.28 Gb/s with an energy efficiency of 1.4 pJ/bit. The PLL output exhibits –97.9 dBc/Hz phase noise at a 1-MHz offset and an integrated RMS jitter of 509.5 fs (1 kHz–100 MHz). The recovered data shows an RMS jitter of 6.93 ps and a 786-mV peak-to-peak swing, while the 4.32-GHz recovered clock demonstrates an RMS jitter of 998 fs on the measured real-time eye diagram.

title: A 19.43-bit Effective Resolution and 3.9 kSPS SAR-Based Integrator-Residue Extended Counting First-Order ΔΣ ADC.
abstract: This work proposes a high precision analog-todigital converter (ADC) with fast conversion time and low power consumption, which is widely used in recent high performance sensor designs. Combining a first-order ΔΣ-modulator (ΔΣM) with a parallel digitization for an internal integrator residue using a 12-bit SAR ADC, this extended counting (EC) ADC shows an effective resolution (ER) of 19.43bit within 257 μs conversion time with extra pipelining, which matches the noise analysis result within the paper. This work achieved dynamic range Schreier figure-of-merit (FoM) of 173.9 dB with a wide input voltage range of 5.8 V.

title: A 112Gb/s DAC-Based PAM-4 Transmitter with Fast Automatic Retiming Clock Phase Optimization and 6-Tap FFE in 28nm CMOS.
abstract: This paper presents a 112 Gb/s digital-to-analog (DAC)-based transmitter (TX) with a 6-tap feed-forward equalizer (FFE). The proposed fast automatic retiming clock optimization technique is built on the phase rotator (PR) and inverse-PR based phase detector (PD), ensuring rapid convergence with low hardware overhead. Fabricated in a 28- nm CMOS technology, the TX prototype achieves the fastest clock optimization speed of only 8/16 UI with 5.5 mW and 0.002 mm2extra power and area, respectively. The total TX consumes 237 mW at 112-Gb/s four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) signaling with 97.2 % RLM in 0.18 mm2area.

title: A D-Band Power Amplifier with A Novel Gain-Boosting Structure Achieving 15.8-dB Gain and 23.9-GHz Bandwidth in 65-nm CMOS.
abstract: This paper presents a D-band power amplifier (PA) employing a triple-coil transformer (XFMR)-based gain-boosting structure. The proposed gain-boosting structure, featuring a triple-coil XFMR embedded in a common-source (CS) PA core, facilitates wideband impedance transformation and cross-coupled neutralization, enhancing gain, bandwidth, and stability simultaneously. The complete D-band PA consists of three CS stages, utilizing the triple-coil technique to achieve efficient impedance matching in the first two stages and load impedance transformation in the final stage. Designed in a 65-nm CMOS process, the D-band PA demonstrates a peak gain of 15.8 dB at 127 GHz, with a wide bandwidth of 23.9 GHz in post-layout simulations. With the concise three-stage implementation, the overall PA occupies a compact area of 0.034 mm2and delivers a saturated output power of 10.4 dBm, resulting in a figure-of-merit (FoM, Power×Bandwidth×Gain/Area) of 121.78 W•GHz•dB/mm2. Additionally, a peak power added efficiency of 7.8% has been achieved at 127 GHz.

title: A Low Noise Active Pixel Circuit Using Dual Correlated Double Sampling for Dynamic TFT Integrated X-Ray Imaging.
abstract: Active pixel sensors (APS) based on thin-film transistors (TFTs) show great potential for low-dose and high–signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) X-ray imaging. However, a considerable amount of pre-amplification reset noise is a major concern. In this work, a novel 4T-2C APS circuit implementing a dual correlated double sampling (D-CDS) technique is proposed, which can simultaneously suppress pre-amplification reset noise and post-amplification low-frequency flicker noise. The current-integration readout mode provides a low-pass filtering effect, effectively reducing the thermal noise caused by the conduction of the reset transistor. The APS circuit implemented with oxide TFTs achieves a charge-to-current conversion gain of 7.28 μA/pC and a nonlinearity of 0.42%. Compared with the conventional CDS-based 3T-1C pixel, the proposed circuit reduces the pre-amplification noise by 46.7%, demonstrating its suitability for low-dose, high-SNR dynamic X-ray medical imaging.

title: GreenMorph: Sustainable Neuromorphic Computing through Energy-Harvesting and Energy-Driven Online STDP Learning.
abstract: In recent years, the rapidly increasing computational demands of artificial intelligence (AI) have underscored the need for more sustainable and energy-efficient computing solutions. This paper introduces GreenMorph - a carbon-aware Spiking Neural Network (SNN) framework that relies on energy harvesting and can be driven by the energy level. GreenMorph dynamically adjusts timesteps and employs similarity-based neuron pruning to optimize energy consumption to achieve carbon neutrality during operation. Experimental evaluations on benchmark datasets show that timestep adaptation reduces training energy by 15.15% without accuracy degradation, while combining timestep adaptation with neuron pruning achieves an 88.10% reduction in training energy at the cost of only 3.01% accuracy loss. During inference, similarity-based neuron pruning reduces computation energy by 27.18% with just 0.35% accuracy loss, and by up to 88.32% with 8.81% accuracy loss.

title: A Gate-Biased Wide-Range Rectifier for Neural Stimulation.
abstract: Intra-body power transfer (IBPT) emerges as a flexible wireless power transfer (WPT) method for neural stimulation. However, the dynamic range (DR) of the rectifier requires an extension to accommodate diverse transmission conditions and application demands. This paper introduces a 180 nm CMOS NMOS-sided biased (N-BIAS) rectifier employing area-efficient feedback transistors for gate voltage biasing and an optimized capacitance network to mitigate phase delay. Thus, the forward conduction and reverse leakage currents are effectively balanced. The optimized measurement setup shows that a peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 87% and a DR of 6 dB with PCE> 70% can be achieved at a frequency of 10 MHz and a 2 kΩ load. The proposed wide-range high-efficiency rectifier provides a favorable solution for neural stimulation.

title: A Multi-Stage SiC Gate Driver Utilizing Peak/Valley Miller Plateau Voltage Tracking for 48.4% Switching Loss Reduction.
abstract: The inherently fast switching speed of SiC MOSFETs induces significant voltage/current oscillations. Conventional suppression methods suppress the oscillations through increased gate resistance, which inevitably increase switching losses. To minimize switching losses, this paper proposes an adaptive multi-stage gate driver (AMSGD) for SiC MOSFETs that regulates dV/dt during switching transient, achieving minimum switching loss under peak dV/dt limits. Peak/valley Miller plateau (MP) tracking circuits and a drain voltage tailing detection circuit are proposed to dynamically optimize switching sequences of multi-stage drive currents in real time. With the proposed AMSGD, a near-constant dV/dt is achieved, which minimizes the extra losses caused by voltage tailing effect and reverse recovery current are minimized under dynamic operation conditions. Fabricated in a 0.18-μm BCD process, the proposed driver achieves 58.0% and 48.4% reduction in turn-on and turn-off losses compared with conventional drivers, under 400V/40A operation with 20V/ns peak dV/dt limit.

title: Unified Architecture of Random Sampler for Fully Homomorphic Encryption.
abstract: Random sampling is a critical primitive in Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) schemes based on the ring learning-with-errors (RLWE) problem. Existing hardware implementations target a single distribution—typically the discrete Gaussian sampler—while other required distributions such as uniform and ternary remain software-based, creating performance imbalance and redundant logic. This paper proposes a unified random-sampler architecture capable of generating uniform, ternary, and discrete Gaussian outputs. The design reuses arithmetic components to reduce resource cost while maintaining timing constancy. An implementation on a Xilinx Kintex–7 target board demonstrates that the unified sampler achieves 2.98× higher throughput for Gaussian sampling (122.6 Msps vs. 41.13 Msps) compared to the best prior single-distribution Gaussian sampler on the same platform (Yang et al.), while using comparable slice resources (146 vs. 150 slices). For uniform and ternary sampling, throughput reaches 184 Msps (4.47× improvement). The unified architecture also achieves a 63.5% reduction in area-time product (Slice•Cycles = 438 vs. 1200) compared to prior art. The architecture provides a compact, secure, and reconfigurable randomness core for hardware-accelerated FHE systems.

title: Reconfigurable SRAM-CAM for Similarity Index Computation in 22-nm FDSOI.
abstract: Content addressable memories (CAMs) enable fast parallel search and are widely used in networking, associative learning, and pattern classification. However, conventional CAM architectures are limited to exact match operations and incur high area and power overheads. Existing solutions that enable similarity search often rely on non standard memory technologies or modified SRAM cells, which compromise scalability and process compatibility. In this work, we present a fully CMOS compatible 6T SRAM-based CAM that introduces a similarity index feature by leveraging intrinsic bitline voltage behavior during mismatches, digitized using a compact 3 bit ADC. Post-layout simulations in 22nm FDSOI confirm energy-efficient approximate search, with 0.44 fJ/search/bit at VDD = 0.5V and operation up to 1 GHz. The array preserves the unmodified 6T cell and co-supports SRAM/BCAM/TCAM, enabling approximate search and ranked retrieval for in-memory AI workloads.

title: CxlRatioOpt : A Predictive Optimizer for Performance Trade-offs in CXL-Tiered Memory.
abstract: CXL (Compute Express Link) offers flexible memory tiering, but optimizing its resource allocation for specific performance targets under multiple workloads presents a complex challenge that has not been fully addressed by previous simulation-based or hardware-based studies. To address this gap, we systematically characterize a commercial CXL server, revealing its nonlinear saturation bounds and counterintuitive phenomena. These findings motivate our core contribution, CxlRatioOpt, an optimizer that derives the optimal DRAM:CXL configuration from high-level performance targets. CxlRatioOpt employs a two-stage workflow: it first builds a highly accurate prediction model from empirical data and then uses this model to perform a backward search to find the optimal configuration. Our evaluation on real hardware demonstrates that CxlRatioOpt consistently outperforms traditional fixed-ratio policies. It achieves up to 10.2% latency reduction in latency-sensitive scenarios and 22.2% stability improvement under high stress, providing a key tool for designing predictable, high-performance CXL systems.

title: HLC: A High-Quality Lightweight Mezzanine Codec Featuring High-Throughput Palette.
abstract: Existing mezzanine image codecs lack specialized screen content coding tools and therefore struggle to maintain high image quality under bandwidth constraints, especially in areas with dense text. Although distribution codecs offer advanced screen content compression techniques, their high computational complexity makes them impractical for mezzanine coding. To address this shortfall, we introduce the High-quality Lightweight Codec (HLC), a solution centered on enabling a practical, high-throughput palette tool for mezzanine coding. The core innovation is a novel data-dependency-free palette that eliminates the throughput bottlenecks. To ensure its effectiveness across all content, a co-designed rate-distortion optimization module arbitrates between the palette and traditional prediction modes, while a data reuse strategy between rate estimation and entropy coding minimizes the overall hardware resources required for the system. Experimental results show that, compared with a 4K@120fps JPEG-XS encoder, HLC achieves the same throughput while using only half the LUT resources and delivers BD-PSNR improvements of 3.461dB, 3.299dB, and 5.312dB on gaming, natural, and text content datasets, respectively.

title: A 40-nm Resilient MLC RRAM Macro with Self-Referenced Time-Based Readout and 3-Bit Interleaved ECC Achieving 0.22 pJ/bit Read Energy.
abstract: Multi-level-cell (MLC) resistive random-access memory (RRAM) has emerged as a promising candidate for high-density compute-in-memory and neuromorphic systems. However, the accuracy of MLC read operations is commonly degraded by process variations and parasitics, especially in time-based sensing schemes. This paper proposes a self-referenced time-based readout circuit for 3-bit MLC 1T1R RRAM arrays, featuring a replica bitline (RBL) calibration technique and a 3-bit interleaved Hamming-code-based error correction (ECC) scheme. The proposed RBL dynamically tracks parasitic delay and process variations, enabling accurate sensing without additional analog circuitry. Furthermore, the lightweight 3-bit ECC further enhances read reliability with minimal area overhead. Post-layout simulations in a 40-nm CMOS process show an improvement in read symbol-error ratio (SER) from 16.44% to 0.63% after replica calibration and to below 10-4after ECC correction, with 0.22 pJ/bit energy consumption at a 9.2-ns read clock period and 1.2-V supply, demonstrating superior robustness and energy efficiency over prior RRAM readout schemes.

title: CIMS: A CAM-based In-Memory Sorting Architecture for Efficient Top-K Ranking.
abstract: This paper presents a novel Content-Addressable Memory (CAM)-based in-memory sorting architecture. By enhancing sorting parallelism and narrowing search scope, our design optimizes ranking energy efficiency and throughput while minimizing data movement. A Parallel Sorting Unit (PSU) is introduced in the CAM, utilizing transistors with high, standard, and low threshold voltages, with carefully configured sizes to control Match Line (ML) discharge rates, reflecting the numerical magnitude of stored data. The proposed two-stage sorting strategy combines comparison-free in-memory sorting with Compare-And-Swap (CAS) unit-based sorting to narrow the search range and skip redundant operations. Simulated in a 22 nm CMOS process, CIMS achieves a throughput of 157M to 631M numbers per second for databases of 1k and 1M scales. Compared to the stae-of-the-art work, our design delivers a 1.3× to 1.7× improvement in throughput and a 1.8× to 9.4× enhancement in energy efficiency, paving the way for future research into scalable in-memory sorting systems.

title: SCAR: A Neural Rendering Accelerator with Sparse-aware Sampling and Conflict-Free Encoding.
abstract: Neural rendering, which bridges computer vision and graphics, has garnered significant attention for its ability to deliver high-quality rendering and rapid reconstruction. However, deploying neural rendering on resource-constrained devices remains challenging due to its substantial computational and memory demands. In this paper, we present SCAR, a specialized accelerator optimized for implicit neural representation-based rendering applications. To address bottlenecks in the sampling and encoding stages, SCAR introduces two key innovations: 1) a sparsity-aware sampling scheduler that combines iterative preprocessing with density-aware sampling to significantly enhance ray casting efficiency, and 2) a renumbered block-based memory access strategy that eliminates bank conflicts during feature encoding, thereby maximizing memory throughput. We implement SCAR in VerilogHDL and evaluate it using 40 nm CMOS technology with scheduling executed on the host. SCAR achieves a 36× speedup over the Jetson Xavier NX baseline while consuming only 4.8% of its energy, demonstrating state-of-the-art efficiency and rendering performance compared to existing neural rendering accelerators.

title: A Fully Open-source Implementation of an Analog 8-PAM Demapper for High-speed Communications.
abstract: Spectrally-efficient communication systems rely on the use of multi-level modulation formats. At the receiver side, a demodulator is often used to extract soft information about the transmitted bits. Such a demodulator is typically implemented in the digital domain. However, analog implementations of such demodulators are also possible. In this paper, we design and simulate an analog 8-ary pulse-amplitude modulation (8-PAM) demapper in IHP SG13G2 SiGe BiCMOS technology. We generalize and improve a design available in the literature for 4-PAM. A fully MOSFET-based 8-PAM design is proposed. Our simulations and design are completely based on open-source IC design tools. Our results show an energy efficiency of 0.33 pJ/bit for a data rate of 1Gbit/s.

title: E2Detect: Object Detection from Event Camera via Sparse Feature Pyramid Recovery.
abstract: Event cameras offer high dynamic range, no motion blur, and very high temporal resolution—capabilities that conventional RGB cameras lack and can be crucial for many vision tasks. Existing computer vision approaches struggle to operate directly on event streams due to the asynchronous and sparse nature of event data. Event-driven pipelines often require intensity image reconstruction or retraining on event-based object detection datasets, increasing the computational complexity and limiting the reusability of existing pretrained frame-based object detectors. We present E2Detect, a learning-based framework that performs object detection directly from event streams without dense intensity image reconstruction or detector retraining. Our Event Feature Pyramid Network (E-FPN) recovers a Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD)-compatible feature pyramid directly from event data. The recovered feature pyramid is plug-and-play compatible with the SSD detection head without requiring retraining. Experiments on ESIM-simulated event data from the REDS 120fps dataset demonstrate that our method achieves competitive AP@0.5 as compared with RGB image–based detection results.

title: An Ultra Low-Power True Random Number Generator for RFID Systems in 65nm CMOS.
abstract: In this paper, a True Random Number Generator (TRNG) based on a dual amplifier-comparator architecture is presented. The circuit uses intrinsic noise to generate random bits without the need for additional pseudo-random post-processing stages. Extensive Monte Carlo and post-layout simulations show an almost evenly split bit distribution of 50% ones and 50% of zeros. There is no observable bias or correlation in the output bit streams, and the different runs show that the outputs follow uniform distributions. Standard statistical metrics (mean, variance and p-value χ2) have been evaluated, and the results are compatible with an unbiased bitstream. The average power consumption of the duty-cycled circuit is below 200nW and occupies an area of 1μm2. The proposed TRNG has been applied to a Wi-Fi-based RFID device anticollision protocol to randomize the selection of transmission slots. The results shown in this paper suggest that this TRNG can be used as a power and area-efficient solution for wireless IoT systems.

title: A 0.74 pJ/bit 10 Gbps PAM-4 Transceiver with Triple TIA Termination and Power-saving Addition-only Driving for Parallel Memory Interface Channels.
abstract: This paper presents a 10Gbps 0.74pJ/bit PAM-4 transceiver using a triple transimpedance amplifier (TIA) termination receiver with a power-saving addition-only driving. The proposed addition-only main driver removes the large static current for the intermediate-level generation and reduces the total transmitter power by 36.33%. This work also utilizes an addition-only feed-forward equalizer (A-FFE) for further power reduction. In the receiver, a triple TIA with symmetric threshold voltages is proposed to enhance the eye height by separating the three eyes. The total eye height is improved by a factor of 6.53. Moreover, a RZ (return-to-zero) decoder is employed to remove the RZ-to-NRZ (non-return-to-zero) converters for power-saving. The proposed transceiver was fabricated in a 65 nm CMOS process and achieves an energy efficiency of 0.74pJ/bit at 10 Gbps.

title: A Crossed Bond-Wire Structure for High-Speed Differential Interconnects Achieving 27% Reduction in Insertion Loss at 56 GHz.
abstract: This paper proposes a crossed bond-wire (CBW) structure for high-speed differential interconnects, achieving a 27.3% reduction in insertion loss at 56 GHz compared with the parallel bond-wire (PBW) structure. The CBW increases the mutual inductance between two bond-wires, thereby reducing the differential-mode inductance. A lumped circuit model for CBW is developed and validated by vector network analyzer (VNA) measurements. Measured results confirm that the CBW has similar self-inductance but larger mutual inductance. For 112-Gbps PAM-4 transmission, the CBW exhibits a 45% larger eye height, demonstrating its potential in high-speed wireline communication.

title: Electronic-Photonic Hybrid CIM-based Ising Machine with Interaction-Aware Update Strategy for Combinatorial Optimization Problems.
abstract: Ising machines present a promising solution for tackling NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems (COPs). While Compute-in-Memory (CIM) architectures enhance performance by minimizing data movement and enabling efficient multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) operations, their scalability is hindered by IR-drop issues, and their speed is limited by the sequential nature of simulated annealing (SA). This work introduces an electronic–photonic hybrid CIM Ising machine to address these limitations. The design leverages discharge based 4-bit FeFET compute cells to reduce power consumption and optical bitlines to perform lossless summation through phase modulation, thereby eliminating IR-drop. An interaction-aware update (IAU) strategy is further proposed to enable parallel spin updates. Evaluated on a 1024-node Max-Cut problem and a 29-city TSP under a fully connected Ising model, the design achieves 99% and 98% of the theoretical optima, respectively. Compared to baseline implementations, our work delivers >26 × speedup and a >1.5× improvement in figure-of-merits which reflects the capability and energy consumption of Ising machine.

title: Hybrid Dynamic/SRAM based TCAM Cell with Self-Gating Match Line and Adaptive VSS.
abstract: Ternary content-addressable memory (TCAM) is widely adopted in modern network routing applications due to its fast parallel matching capabilities. However, traditional TCAMs face optimization bottlenecks in terms of area, static leakage power, and dynamic power consumption. This paper proposes a novel hybrid dynamic/SRAM based TCAM cell design. This approach integrates a dynamic gain cell with SRAM within a single TCAM cell, achieving area and transistor count reduction. Moreover, leveraging the continuity characteristic of mask data, the mask data is segmented into multiple sections. This enables self-gating during ML pre-charge and adaptive VSS for SRAM, thereby reducing dynamic and static power consumption respectively. A 32×128 TCAM array is simulated in a 65nm CMOS process. Results demonstrate that compared to conventional approaches, the proposed design achieves 36.6% area optimization, 75.2% static leakage power reduction, and 18.5% dynamic power reduction. This work provides a viable solution for high-performance, low-power storage systems.

title: Vision-Language Modality Prompt Classification Method for Image Quality Assessment.
abstract: Image Quality Assessment (IQA) is an essential component of image processing. Prompt learning methods on multimodal vision-language models (e.g., CLIP) show strong generalization in IQA, yet existing approaches lack semantic classification of prompts in each modality, limiting semantic expressiveness. This study proposes a vision-language modality prompt classification method for IQA that semantically classifies learnable prompts within the visual and language modalities, respectively. In the visual modality, learnable prompts are divided into CLS prompts and patch prompts, and global and local information is captured separately via an attention-mask mechanism. In the language modality, a five-point quality scale serves as the original prompts, and learnable language prompts are divided to guide the global and local cues of the visual modality. Through the proposed vision-language modality fusion and global-local information aggregation method, quality prediction is achieved. Experiments on multiple IQA datasets verify that, with almost no additional trainable parameters compared with the baseline, performance is significantly improved.

title: Three-Level GaN HEMT Gate Driver with Negative VGS Pulse and Integrated Overcurrent Protection.
abstract: In this work, a compact gate driver IC is presented that introduces a negative VGSpulse generation circuit to avoid parasitic turn-on due to low threshold voltage and low Cg/Cgdratio, during fast switching transients of GaN HEMT’s. The circuit produces a short negative bias at the gate output during turn-off without an additional negative supply. To achieve this a chargepump with external capacitors is included. A new levelshifter strategy is applied to automatically adapt to the output gate voltage domain and eliminate the need for a two stage down–up levelshifting. Additional features include 90 ns overcurrent detection and active gate turn-off, as well as 6 V capable output devices to interface directly with external GaN transistors. A prototype IC was fabricated in 0.18 μm SOI CMOS and experimentally validated in a GaN half-bridge, demonstrating robust negative gate voltage biasing and reliable operation under high-frequency switching and short circuit fault conditions.

title: A Feedforward-Feedback Reconfigurable Switched-Capacitor DC-DC Converter with One-Step VCR Transitions Achieving 9.6V/μs under 5MHz Fast DVS for Edge AI Applications.
abstract: This paper proposes a feedforward-feedback reconfigurable switched-capacitor (FFRSC) DC-DC converter designed to enable single-step transitions for each voltage conversion ratio (VCR) adjustment. The proposed design facilitates near-soft-switching and seamless transitions, substantially reducing power consumption during dynamic voltage scaling (DVS) to meet the demands of AI edge computing applications. The FFRSC achieves a high DVS slew rate and enhances efficiency at elevated DVS frequencies. Implemented in a 28nm process, it demonstrates a 9% improvement in efficiency compared to existing solutions at a DVS frequency of 1 MHz. Besides, it achieves an average efficiency of up to 86% at a 5 MHz DVS frequency, operating 5–10 times faster, with a maximum slew rate of 9.6 V/μs.

title: A Lightweight Speaker Verification Processor based on Large-Scale Dataset.
abstract: This paper presents a low-power neural-network (NN)-based speaker verification (SV) processor, the first processor developed and evaluated on the large-scale speaker verification benchmark VoxCeleb1-E. The proposed memory-efficient attention, multi-level model compression flow, and optimized hardware architecture effectively minimize the model size and feature memory size, enabling a fully-integrated low-power SV processor without off-chip memory resources. The proposed design techniques attain 8.2× parameter reduction and 1.5× feature memory reduction with minimal degradation of 0.672% in equal error rate (EER). The proposed SV processor in 28 nm CMOS technology consumes 9.158 mW at 0.9V, with enhanced robustness compared to previous works.

title: Indirect Multi-Domain Characterization of 25 GHz 5G Amplifiers Using a Low-Cost SDR and IF-Loopback Testbed.
abstract: Characterizing 5G NR mmWave power amplifiers typically requires cost-prohibitive equipment, hindering academic research. This paper validates a low-cost, reconfigurable testbed using a novel indirect IF-loopback methodology. By utilizing a single sub-6 GHz SDR for 5G-compliant waveform generation and analysis at a 5 GHz IF, the system achieves multi-domain characterization (ACPR, EVM, and transient power) at 25 GHz without expensive mmWave analyzers. The platform’s efficacy is proven through the characterization of a 25 GHz amplifier chain, successfully capturing the EVM ’bathtub’ curve and defining the linear dynamic range for 256-QAM signals. Results demonstrate that this approach offers a high-fidelity, accessible alternative for RF engineering and education, effectively balancing setup complexity with 5G-compliant measurement accuracy.

title: Direction-based Route Integrity Validation for Eavesdropping Prevention in NoC Systems.
abstract: Modern computing platforms increasingly rely on System-on-Chip (SoC) architectures, where Network-on-Chip (NoC) frameworks provide scalable and efficient interconnects for multi-core systems. However, the integrity and confidentiality of NoC communications can be compromised by design flaws or malicious attacks, leading to performance degradation and leakage of sensitive information. In particular, eavesdropping attacks may introduce anomalous traffic patterns that burden the network with extra load while exposing critical data. To address these challenges, this work proposes a lightweight and hardware-friendly validation scheme to secure NoC communication. The proposed Direction-based Route Integrity Validation for Eavesdropping (DRIVE) is embedded within routers to detect and discard invalid packets at an early stage, thereby alleviating the performance impact of attack-induced traffic. To further strengthen protection, a complementary Hop-Count Check (HCC) mechanism is deployed at the Network Interface (NI) to block residual invalid packets that may bypass DRIVE, minimizing potential information leakage. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves up to 89.0% reduction in average packet leakage when DRIVE alone is employed in routers. In terms of latency, the proposed defense reduces attack-induced delay by 73.8% to 90.1%, thereby mitigating the incidental performance degradation that can accompany eavesdropping attacks.

title: Debiasing Diffusion Model: Enhancing Fairness through Latent Representation Learning in Stable Diffusion Model.
abstract: Diffusion-based models excel at synthesizing realistic images but often inherit and amplify societal biases from their training data, leading to unfair group representations. Existing debiasing methods typically rely on predefined sensitive attributes, external classifiers, or large language models, which limits their applicability to complex, continuous demographic variations. To overcome these limitations, we propose the Debiasing Diffusion Model (DDM), a novel framework that fine-tunes a Stable Diffusion Model to learn fair latent representations. DDM integrates a temporary indicator module during training, which guides the model to become invariant to sensitive attributes without requiring explicit attribute labels at inference time. This approach not only ensures a balanced distribution for neutral prompts but also minimizes performance disparities when attributes are specified. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DDM through comprehensive experiments, showcasing its ability to enhance fairness beyond the scope of conventional techniques.

title: A Low-Complexity Peak Search Method for MUSIC Based on FFT and Early-Terminated Goertzel Algorithm.
abstract: Spectral peak search is critical for implementing the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm in hardware systems. This paper proposes a hardware-oriented method that can find the spectrum peaks precisely and efficiently. The small-point fast Fourier transform (FFT) is applied initially to roughly identify the peaks. For each of the peaks, the precision is further refined by examining adjacent points progressively using the Goertzel algorithm. In particular, it is shown that the Goertzel iteration can be early terminated since the searching process only needs the magnitude of the spectral points. Compared with existing methods, the proposed method can reduce the computational complexity significantly without lowering the precision.

title: An Area-latency-balanced Hardware Design for the Reference Pixel Management of VVC Intra Coding.
abstract: In video encoding, prediction plays a crucial role in reducing redundant information. For intra block encoding, accurate prediction relies on the availability of reconstructed neighboring pixels as reference pixels. However, in hardware encoders, the rate-distortion optimization (RDO) process continuously updates the optimal reconstructed pixels during partition decisions, requiring a dedicated design for their real-time management. This challenge is further exacerbated by the Quad-Tree with nested Multi-Type Tree (QTMTT) partitioning scheme introduced in the Versatile Video Coding (VVC) standard, which significantly increases the complexity of reference pixel management. To address this, we propose an area-latency-balanced reference pixel management (RPM) design supporting QTMTT in VVC. This design integrates register-based and SRAM-based buffers to achieve an optimal trade-off between latency and area. The proposed hardware design is implemented using GF 28nm technology, achieving zero SRAM data transfer latency, with a hardware area cost of 62295 µm2.

title: EM-Aware Physical Synthesis: Neural Inductor Modeling and Intelligent Placement & Routing for RF Circuits.
abstract: This paper presents an ML-driven framework for automated RF physical synthesis that transforms circuit netlists into manufacturable GDSII layouts. While recent ML approaches demonstrate success in topology selection and parameter optimization, they fail to produce manufacturable layouts due to oversimplified component models and lack of routing capabilities. Our framework addresses these limitations through three key innovations: (1) a neural network framework trained on 18,210 inductor geometries with frequency sweeps from 1-100 GHz, generating 7.5 million training samples, that predicts inductor Q-factor with less than 2% error and enables fast gradient-based layout optimization with a 93.77% success rate in producing high-Q layouts; (2) an intelligent P-Cell optimizer that reduces layout area while maintaining design-rule-check (DRC) compliance; and (3) a complete placement and routing engine with frequency-dependent EM spacing rules and DRC-aware synthesis. The neural inductor model demonstrates superior accuracy across 1-100 GHz, enabling EM-accurate component synthesis with real-time inference. The framework successfully generates DRC-aware GDSII layouts for RF circuits, representing a significant step toward automated RF physical design.

title: S2PUF: A <1.77E-8 BER Schmitt Effect SRAM PUF with Load Tilt Masking for Resource-Constrained systems.
abstract: Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) have emerged as a promising solution for resource-constrained key generation and authentication. However, PUFs are highly sensitive to voltage and temperature variations, making it difficult to achieve 100% reliability throughout their entire lifecycle. Existing solutions often require large overhead in terms of masking or error correction codes (ECC) to ensure reliability. This work proposes S2PUF, a schmitt effect SRAM PUF that successfully eliminates all unreliable bits without the need for expensive temperature sweeps. By using an all-NMOS structure and leveraging hysteresis to achieves both high native reliability and low power. Additionally, a load tilt masking technique is employed to precisely adjust controllable loads for identifying unreliable bits, further enhancing PUF reliability to ~100%. The S2PUF is fabricated in 180-nm standard CMOS and achieves "0" bit error rate (BER) (BERpes, <1.77E−8) by masking 8.52% of PUF bits. It also shows 0.391%/10 ℃ and 0.398%/0.1 V native bit error across temperature variations of −40 ℃ to 120 ℃ and voltage variations from 0.6 V to 2.0 V. The core energy per bit at 0.6 V is 12.56 fJ.

title: UMDAM: A Unified Data Layout and DRAM Address Mapping for Heterogeneous NPU-PIM.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed on edge devices with Neural Processing Units (NPUs), yet the decode phase remains memory-intensive, limiting performance. Processing-in-Memory (PIM) offers a promising solution, but co-executing NPU-PIM systems face challenges such as data layout mismatches, bandwidth loss, and redundant storage. To address these issues, we propose UMDAM, a unified memory-affinity data layout and DRAM address mapping scheme tailored for NPU-PIM co-execution. UMDAM employs a column-major, tile-based layout and a configurable DRAM mapping strategy to ensure compatibility with NPU computation while maximizing PIM efficiency – without introducing extra memory overhead or bandwidth loss. Comprehensive evaluations on OPT models demonstrate that UMDAM reduces time-to-first-token (TTFT) by up to 3.0× and time-to-last-token (TTLT) by 2.18×, significantly improving end-to-end LLM inference efficiency on edge devices.

title: A Miniaturized Wireless Multimodal Physiological In-Vivo Monitoring Platform Featuring Power-Efficient Photoelectrochemical Sensing.
abstract: The increasing diversity of sensing mechanisms has created a growing demand for compact and versatile readout platforms that can support multiple modalities under strict power constraints. Conventional photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems, in particular, rely on bulky optical setups and continuous high-power illumination, making them unsuitable for portable or in-vivo applications. To address these challenges, this work presents a miniaturized and reconfigurable sensing platform that integrates current, voltage, resistive and electrochemical measurement capabilities—along with an on-board current source for light-stimulated applications—within a 21 mm × 17 mm, 0.9 g hardware implementation. Compared with existing sensing systems, the proposed design achieves multimodal functionality, miniaturized implementation, and power-efficient operation within a fully integrated platform. To verify the system’s multimodal capability, synchronous measurement experiments were conducted, demonstrating the ability to accurately capture signals across all sensing modalities while maintaining milliwatt power operation. Furthermore, a power-efficient PEC measurement method based on duty-cycled optical modulation is experimentally validated, demonstrating a feasible approach toward fully integrated, low-power PEC sensing suitable for wearable and in-vivo bioelectronic applications.

title: Live Demonstration: Hardware-Bound IP Protection for OWL-ViT on Edge Devices.
abstract: We demonstrate a hardware-bound Intellectual Property (IP) protection scheme for transformer models on edge devices. Our method binds the OWL-ViT [1], an open-vocabulary object detection model, to specific hardware using a Physical Unclonable Function (PUF). The model weights are reversibly obfuscated using PUF-derived cryptographic keys, catastrophically degrading the performance of unauthorized devices and thus preventing IP theft. The proposed method incurs only a moderate inference overhead on the authorized target for real time applications.

title: An Asynchronous Ripple-Based SIMO Buck Converter with 10mV/A Cross Regulation and 1500× Unbalanced Load Current Ratio.
abstract: This paper presents a single-inductor multiple-output (SIMO) buck converter with asynchronous ripple-based control (ARB). In traditional synchronous SIMO buck converters, the power distribution stage and the power generation stage are driven by a common clock signal and coordinated at precise intervals. However, in the proposed asynchronous SIMO buck converter, the power distribution stage is decoupled from the power generation stage, which intrinsically alleviates the cross regulation and greatly increases the unbalanced load current ratio (ULCR). Moreover, ripple-based control is adopted to enhance output regulation. The proposed SIMO buck converter is designed with a 180-nm BCD technology, aimed at delivering four outputs ranging from 2.5 V to 4.2 V, with 12-V input. Simulation results show a ULCR up to 1500× with a load range of 1 mA-1500 mA. The proposed asynchronous SIMO buck converter realizes a cross regulation of 10 mV/A with a 1 A/100 ns load current change and achieves a peak efficiency of 95.6% at a 3.94 W output power.

title: A Half-Cell-Activation Search Scheme for Low-Power and High-Reliability TCAM Design.
abstract: In recent years, magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) has been used for non-volatile ternary content addressable memory to reduce search static power. However, MTJ-based TCAM still suffers from high dynamic power and low reliability during search operations due to its fully parallel search feature. To address this issue, we propose a half-cell-activation search scheme based on spin transfer torque MTJ (STT-MTJ). Hybrid simulation is obtained by utilizing a STT-MTJ compact model and the CMOS 28 nm design kit. The results demonstrate that the half-cell-activation search scheme reaches 36.95% dynamic power reduction and 46.62% search-error-rate decrease compared with conventional designs.

title: Discrete high-gain observer based epileptic seizure prediction by single-lead ECG.
abstract: Generalized tonic-clonic seizure (GTCS) is a typical epilepsy, sudden and unpredictable, which may increase the risk of fatalities. As a non-invasive physiological electrical signal, electrocardiograph (ECG) is easy to access and can be applied for seizure prediction. In this paper, a seizure prediction model based on deterministic learning and dynamical pattern recognition (DLDPR) is proposed using single-lead ECG. The discrete high-gain observer (DHGO) is used to estimate the state of ECG and the dynamical Radial-Basis Function Networks (RBFN) is constructed to obtain the internal dynamics of ECG. Besides, the pattern library is constructed by three kinds of normal patterns and one "seizure omen" pattern for calculating residual and further predicting seizure. Experiments are performed on the ECG signals of 7 GTCS subjects from CHZU database. The proposed DLDPR can achieve accurate early warning time before the seizure onset.

title: A High-Compression SISO CNN Accelerator Chip for Low External Memory Access.
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are essential in modern AI. However, redundant operations and excessive memory access cause high energy consumption. Conventional compression methods often rely on on-chip SRAM to store intermediate results, limiting efficiency. Additionally, prior works introduced kernel-based compression schemes. However, this approach causes unstable compression efficiency, as the sliding window may repeatedly compress the same data. To address these issues, this paper proposes a sparsity-optimized single-input single-output (SISO) compression scheme for energy-efficient CNN acceleration. Our architecture uses dedicated encoder and decoder modules for real-time, on-the-fly data compression and decompression. This reduces data volume and external DRAM access while avoiding redundant internal computations. The results show our scheme reduces external memory access to 52% and achieves 3.61x higher energy efficiency compared to traditional architectures, demonstrating significant energy efficiency and performance improvements for CNN acceleration.
