title: A 40 μV VRipple, 0.1-ps FoM Output-Capacitor-Less Fully Time-Domain Digital LDO With a VCO-Assisted Dual Loop.
abstract: This paper presents an output-capacitor-less fully time-domain digital low-dropout regulator (DLDO) with a voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO)-assisted dual-loop structure for enhanced power supply rejection ratio (PSRR), targeting sub-1-V applications. The proposed architecture employs a 4-bit time-to-digital converter (TDC) to leverage key advantages of DLDOs—fast transient response and low voltage droop. To reduce steady-state voltage ripple (VRipple) and improve PSRR, a VCO-assisted dual-loop technique is introduced without employing any analog circuit blocks. The DLDO was implemented in a 28-nm CMOS process and operates within a supply voltage range of 0.7–1 .3 V. It achieves a voltage ripple of 40 μ V and a PSRR of -58 dB at 1 kHz. Moreover, the design consumes 450 μA of quiescent current and exhibits a voltage droop of only 50 mV with a settling time of 210 ns under a load current step from 1 mA to 100 mA within 200 ns, resulting in a figure-of-merit (FoM) of 0.1 ps.

title: A 24-29.5-GHz Phased-Array Receiver with Subdegree RMS Phase Errors and Wide Gain Tuning Range in 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS.
abstract: This paper presents a wideband 28-GHz phased-array front-end in 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS. Attenuation-based current compensation technique and amplitude compensation unit are employed in the vector-modulated phase shifter (VMPS) to realize 6-bit phase resolution. A two-stage digital-control VGA with a gain compensation unit is utilized to realize 31.5 dB gain tuning and 0.5-dB gain step. A wideband two-stage LNA is employed for high gain and low noise figure (NF). A compact high-linearity asymmetric single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switch is implemented for asymmetric requirements. The phased-array RX demonstrates a peak gain of 31 dB with a 3-dB bandwidth of 22.2-29.5 GHz and dc power consumption of 74 mW. The measured NF is 4.6-5.5 dB within 24-30 GHz. The measured IP1dBat the highest gain state is -22 dBm at 28 GHz. For phase control, a 6-bit full 360° phase shifting with sub-degree rms phase error is achieved within 24-30 GHz. For gain control, a 6-bit 31.5-dB gain tuning with <0.12 dB rms gain error is achieved within 24-30 GHz.

title: A 24.3MHz RC Relaxation Oscillator with a FoM of -153.05 dBc/Hz achieving 63ppm/°C from -40 to 125°C.
abstract: This paper describes an RC relaxation oscillator operating in the MHz range. The design uses capacitor stacking technique and a polarity-controllable chopped comparator to boost the initial discharge voltage to enhance Phase noise performance. To enhance the temperature stability of the circuit, this design employs resistors with opposite temperature coefficients for first-order temperature conpensation. Post-layout simulation was accomplished using the 28nm process technology of TSMC. The post-layout simulation results showed 24.3 MHz output frequency, -117.56dBc/Hz phase noise at 1 MHz offset, and 167.4 µW power consumption under 0.9 V supply voltage. The frequency variation is 1.2% for supply within 0.78 V to 1 V, and 63 ppm/°C for temperature across -40°C to 125°C. The overall circuit performance is compared favorably to the state-of-art designs, with a Figure of Merit (FoM) of 153.05 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz.

title: A New Triple-Quadrature Image-Rejection Architecture for mm-Wave Applications.
abstract: Image rejection over an ultra-wideband frequency range is a key function for millimeter-wave up/down-converters. This paper first presents a triple-quadrature image-rejection architecture supporting ultra- wideband millimeter-wave image rejection. Compared with conventional single-quadrature and double-quadrature architectures, the proposed triple-quadrature architecture exhibits stronger tolerance to amplitude and phase errors of quadrature networks, enabling further cancellation of path mismatches and achieving a higher image rejection ratio (IRR). To verify the proposed concept, ultra-wideband image rejection was realized through transformer-based quadrature networks and eight passive mixers. Prototypes have been realized in a 65-nm CMOS process. The simulated IRR is higher than 40 dB over a bandwidth from 12.5 to 84.5 GHz and higher than 50 dB over a bandwidth from 23.5 to 47.5 GHz without any calibration. The simulated LO-to-RF isolation is better than 55.7 dB from 12.5 to 84.5 GHz. Compared with previously reported quadrature architectures, the proposed design achieves a competitive advantage by offering a high fractional bandwidth of 146.6% at operating frequencies above 10 GHz.

title: A High Full-scale Range High-linearity 9.76-ps Resolution Time-to-Amplitude Converter for TCSPC Applications.
abstract: This paper presents a multi-ramp, high-precision time-to-amplitude converter (TAC) based on an integration approach. The proposed architecture converts input time intervals into multiple ramp signals and employs dual quantization channels together with multi-threshold comparators, enabling overlapping ramp generation in the time domain. This approach significantly relaxes the conventional trade-off between resolution and full-scale range (FSR). The linearity of the converter is further enhanced by selectively utilizing the effective quantization range while avoiding nonlinear regions (tuning points) of the ramp signal. Implemented in a 180 nm CMOS process, the prototype chip occupies an active area of 0.033 mm2. Measurement results show a power consumption of 14.71 mW under a 3.3 V supply. When combined with a 12-bit analog-to-digital converter (ADC), the TAC achieves a theoretical timing resolution of approximately 9.76 ps and a FSR of about 2 us.

title: A 55-dB Range, 0.87-dB Step Decibel-linear Mixed Structure Programmable Gain Amplifier Based on R-2R Resistor Array for Sensor System.
abstract: This paper presents a wide gain range, high accuracy mixed structure decibel-linear programmable gain amplifier (PGA) used in sensor System. The PGA consists of a coarse stage controlled by a true exponential function using a 2-bit one-hot code and a precision stage controlled by an exponential function using a 4-bit binary code. The fine gain stage consists of two cascade R-2R pseudo-exponentialgain stage. Under the 180nm process, the post simulation results of the proposed PGA show that the gain range is 0 ~ 55 dB and the maximum gain error is 0.23 dB. At the maximum gain, the -3dB bandwidth is 5.39 MHz and the input reference noise is 20.15 nV/√Hz. The SNR measured by dynamic simulation is 90.69 dB at the highest gain. The static power consumption at the 1.8 V voltage domain is 4.34 mW and the core area is 0.2 mm2.

title: A Passive-LoRa Tag Chip Achieving 78m Battery-Free Bidirectional Communication with Standard LoRa Devices.
abstract: The massive deployment of the next-generation Internet of Things (IoT) requires node chips with ultra-low power consumption, low cost, protocol compatibility, and long-range communication. Although the recent passive-BLE/Wi-Fi tags based on wireless power harvesting and backscattering communication present a potential solution, their limited communication range remains a major bottleneck. To address this challenge, this paper presents a crystal-less passive-LoRa tag that achieves battery-free bidirectional communication with standard LoRa devices: 1) A LoRa-shaping backscattering technique based on beat-frequency wireless clock recovery is proposed, enabling the battery-free uplink signal to be received by standard LoRa devices. 2) A beat-splitting self-downconversion technique is proposed to enable the battery-free tag to demodulate standard LoRa signals. The proposed techniques are implemented into a passive-LoRa chip fabricated in a 65nm CMOS process. Measured results show that the chip achieves battery-free bidirectional LoRa communication with an equivalent range up to 78m.

title: A Reconfigurable Audio Analog Front-End with Hardware-Aware Transfer Learning for Task-Adaptive Keyword Spotting.
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable audio analog front-end (AFE) using hardware-aware transfer learning (TL) for task-adaptive keyword spotting (KWS). In current practice, AFEs and classifiers are designed separately, and the fabricated AFE typically keeps all bandpass filter (BPF) channels enabled across downstream tasks. However, software-only channel pruning ignores hardware resource constrains such as power and memory budget, also degrades classification performance. We proposes a three-stage architecture: (i) train a multi-channel analog BPF in tandem with a classifier on 35-keyword KWS task to learn circuit parameterization; (ii) for downstream tasks, freeze the AFE and learn a cost-weighted channel-importance vector that maps to per-channel switching controls; and (iii) prune low-importance channels and perform few-shot classifier finetuning to recover accuracy. Implemented in SKY130 130nm CMOS process, the model achieves 89.8% accuracy with full 16-channel BPF. After transfer to a 10-keyword task, pruning from 16 to 8 channels attains 92.1% with a DSCNN while reducing SPICE-simulated AFE power from 132.5 nW to 76.1 nW and halving spectrogram memory. Moreover, TL on a personalized spoken-digit dataset, pruning from 16 to 10 channels yields 93.5% accuracy with <1% loss after finetuning and a 39.5% AFE power reduction. These results demonstrate a reconfigurable AFE via guided channel pruning to cut power and memory while improving task-adaptive KWS accuracy.

title: FinFET-Based High Performance Radiation-Hardened SRAM Cell Design with Optimized Layout for Commercial Aerospace.
abstract: A novel optimized layout high reliability radiation hardened SRAM cell is designed based on 16nm FinFET process. The proposed cell achieves significant improvement in single-event upset (SEU) immunity by employing innovative backup storage nodes and interlocking structures. TCAD and SPICE co-simulation results demonstrate that specifically implemented optimized layout design contributes significantly to the SEU tolerance by substantially boosting the critical charge at sensitive nodes. The proposed cell also features excellent speed, with a write time of 21.6ps and a read time of 7.62ps. A comprehensive evaluation indicates that its outstanding EQM metric is significantly superior to traditional radiation-hardened cells. Consequently, the proposed SRAM is ideally suited for critical roles such as register files in commercial spaceborne CPUs and configuration memory (CRAM) for FPGAs, while also showing great potential for emerging applications like AI accelerators in near-Earth orbit and deep-space exploration.

title: Reliable and Trustworthy Learning Prototype: Insight from POCUS.
abstract: Deep learning models often lack the interpretability and trustworthiness required for clinical use. This paper proposes a prototype-regularised training method to analyse 1,208 lung ultrasound images, with a focus on B-line artefacts. A ConvNeXt-Tiny architecture is used, adding a novel reconstruction loss to the standard classification loss. The model is trained to extract meaningful prototypes and to use them to classify ultrasound images. To prevent these constraints from hindering generalisation, it is used in pairs with the proposed reconstruction loss, a set of plausible data augmentation of the ideal researched prototypes, and a geometry-aware network, a spatial transformer network, to measure which solutions help the network towards outputting the most reliable outcomes. The resulting models are precise, lightweight and interpretable, indicating that the proposed solution can be embedded in an ultrasound device to assist healthcare specialists in point-of-care applications.

title: Energy-Efficient Compute-in-Memory Macro for BNNs in Edge AI using NV-SRAM.
abstract: In this paper, an area and energy efficient in-memory binary neural network (BNN) accelerator is proposed by employing the CMOS-compatible non-volatile (NV) SRAM. The developed NV-SRAM provides the on-chip non-volatile storage for weights and feature maps without off-chip reload, achieving robust data retention and mitigating information leakage. The proposed NV-SRAM design utilizes less transistors and lower operating voltage 800 mV as compared with the existing nonvolatile SRAM with tunneling effect. In a case study to support binarized 20×20 MNIST image processing, a (400×200) SRAM array is designed to efficiently map for the 400-bit feature data using dedicated peripheral circuits. The chip design has been implemented in GlobalFoundries 22 nm FDSOI technology and verified by Monte Carlo analysis. Results show very high energy efficiency of 5 fJ per logic operation with around 20% area saving as compared to the state-of-the-art. It also demonstrates the suitability of such an accelerator for edge AI applications with low-power by holding the inference accuracy which reaches 94.78% on MNIST dataset.

title: Learning-Based CU Splitting in VVC: A ConvNeXt Approach for Intra-Mode Acceleration.
abstract: The rapid rise in multimedia content consumption has pushed current communication technologies to their limits, necessitating more advanced video compression solutions like the Versatile Video Coding (VVC) standard. While VVC provides approximately 40% bitrate savings over High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC), it significantly increases encoding complexity. To address this, we propose a ConvNeXt-based convolutional architecture for efficient Coding Unit (CU) partitioning, aiming to reduce computational overhead during the encoding. This model predicts CU split decisions with high accuracy, enabling the encoder to avoid the computationally intensive Rate-Distortion Optimization (RDO) typically required by VVC. The proposed method accelerates the decision-making process while preserving Rate-Distortion (RD) performance. In contrast to conventional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based strategies, the ConvNeXt framework leverages design elements inspired by vision transformers to better capture spatial and contextual information across entire frames. Empirical evaluations show that our method reduces encoding time by an average of 50.66% with negligible increases in bitrate and minimal losses in perceptual quality, as measured by Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Video Multi-Method Assessment Fusion (VMAF), and the Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM), relative to the standalone VVC encoder.

title: A Differential Capacitive Sensor for Transluminal Shear Wave Elastography.
abstract: Shear wave elastography (SWE) is a valuable technique for mechanical tissue characterisation, particularly for detecting tumours and assessing organ health. Transluminal SWE approaches require compact sensors capable of detecting propagating mechanical waves at tissue interfaces from within body lumens. This paper presents a differential capacitive sensor designed to capture and quantify dynamic shear excitation in SWE-based tissue characterisation applications. The design presented offers simple, low-cost fabrication and easy configuration. The sensor consists of three main components: a printed circuit board (PCB) substrate, a laser-cut plastic spacer, and a deformable polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) structure comprising a membrane topped with a block serving as the contact interface with the surface of interest. The paper details the sensor’s design, optimised by finite element modelling, its fabrication, and its electronic readout. Preliminary experiments demonstrate the sensor’s capability to detect shear excitation over a frequency range of 0-1000Hz. The sensor resolved an oscillating displacement range of 2-100µm, yielding differential capacitance outputs of 1-30fF.

title: A Shared-TDC Architecture for Large-Scale SPAD Arrays Enabling Range-Gated Timing in Flash LiDAR Sensors.
abstract: In direct time-of-flight (d-ToF) light detection and ranging (LiDAR) systems employing single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) arrays, precise timing is essential for high-resolution depth measurement. However, scaling time-to-digital converters (TDCs) across large arrays poses significant power and area challenges. This work presents a shared-TDC architecture for large-scale SPAD-based flash LiDAR sensors, enabling accurate multi-event timing with reduced circuit overhead. The architecture integrates the TDC with a pixel-wise range-gating technique, which is desired for filtering out background noise without compromising the sensor’s frame rate. A prototype SPAD-based d-ToF sensor fabricated in 180-nm CMOS technology with a 68×40 pixel array achieves 156.25-ps timing resolution, robust operation under 79-klux background illumination, and improved noise rejection through adaptive pixel-wise range gating at 20-fps imaging. The proposed design offers a scalable, power-efficient, and high-performance solution for next-generation SPAD-based LiDAR sensors operating under realistic illumination conditions.

title: GT2N: An Open-Source 2nm Nanosheet PDK Enabling Multi-Width/VT Benchmarking.
abstract: This work introduces GT2N, an open-source, process-aware 2nm nanosheet PDK with wrap-around contact, integrated backside power delivery and buried power rail support. Leveraging 10 nanosheet width and 10 threshold voltage variants, a comprehensive DTCO study was conducted using full-chip benchmarks. Results demonstrate that a configuration using 2 specific W and 5 VT flavors achieves near-optimal PDP, within 3.7% of the full 10W×10VT baseline in the worst case, while significantly reducing library complexity. GT2N provides an accessible, realistic platform for 2nm DTCO exploration.

title: FPGA-Based Spiking Neural Network AutoEncoders for Real-Time Anomaly Detection in LHC Physics.
abstract: Real-time anomaly detection at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) requires ultra-low-latency inference under strict computational constraints. This paper presents the FPGA implementation of Spiking Neural Network AutoEncoders (SNN-AEs) for anomaly detection at the trigger level. Multiple SNN-AE architectures are synthesized on Xilinx UltraScale+ FPGAs and their resource utilization is characterized. Event-based spike processing reduces DSP usage by 67% and LUT usage by 53% compared to conventional Deep NN implementations while maintaining Area Under Curve (AUC) = 0.899 for charged Higgs-like scalar (h+) detection. The smallest SNN-AE architecture consumes only 1.99% LUTs and 1.94% DSPs, enabling viable integration into existing L1 trigger systems. Using the Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) ADC2021 dataset, hardware resource comparisons are provided with FPGA-deployed DNN AutoEncoders across multiple signal models and architectural configurations.

title: HGEN: A Hierarchical Layout Framework for Automated IP Integration.
abstract: The reuse of pre-verified Intellectual Property (IP) is essential in modern Analog and Mixed-Signal (AMS) design. However, conventional layout automation frameworks are not equipped to integrate this IP directly, often requiring its procedural re-implementation. This paper presents HGEN, a hierarchical layout framework that addresses this challenge through a "place-and-abstract" methodology. HGEN directly utilizes original IP layouts, abstracting their physical data to create a foundation for automation tasks such as placement-aware grid generation and geometry-driven pin access. Interconnects are then completed by a hybrid engine that combines an A* search for pathfinding with manual specifications for critical nets. We validate HGEN’s effectiveness through an industrial Digitally Controlled Delay Line (DCDL) generator, which demonstrates the generator’s portability by producing DRC/LVS clean layouts across multiple process technologies from a single script. The results show that HGEN reduces design cycle time while preserving layout quality and electrical performance.

title: A Fully Digital and Bias-Free Ternary Bus for Energy-Efficient On-Chip Interconnects.
abstract: This paper presents a fully digital and bias-free Ternary Bus (T-Bus) for energy-efficient on-chip interconnects. The proposed architecture employs a triode-stack-based Ternary Driver (T-Driver) and a T-CMOS based Ternary Receiver (T-Receiver), enabling self-balanced mid-level generation and robust detection without analog biasing. These bias-free circuit techniques simultaneously reduce voltage swing and effective wiring capacitance, achieving substantial dynamic-power savings while preserving full binary compatibility. Fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS process, the prototype demonstrates clear three-level signaling and stable mid-level transitions at a 1.0 V supply. Post-layout simulations achieve up to 77% dynamic power reduction compared with a binary repeater bus, reaching 22.9 Gb/s and 49 fJ/bit/mm. The T-Bus also validates protocol-level scalability through AMBA AHB-Lite integration, providing a compact and technology-portable solution for next-generation SoC and chiplet interconnects.

title: A 9-bit 1.2GS/s Gain-Programmable Stochastic Time-to-Digital Converter with Sub-ps Resolution.
abstract: This paper presents a 9-bit gain-programmable stochastic time-to-digital converter (GP-STDC) achieving sub-picosecond resolution and a high conversion rate. To overcome the limited dynamic range and nonlinearity of conventional STDCs, the proposed architecture uses a parallel topology of multiple arbiter groups with programmable input delay. Furthermore, the input delays are generated by digitally-controlled delay elements (DCDEs) to enable a programmable gain (KTDC) with a tuning range of 271%. Implemented in a 28-nm CMOS process, the GP-STDC operates at a conversion rate from 100MS/s to 1.2GS/s. A resolution of 225fs and a linear dynamic range exceeding 100ps are achieved at its minimum KTDC. At its maximum KTDC, the resolution improves to 61fs, resulting in a figure-of-merit (FoM) of 0.011pJ•ps/step at 1.2GS/s.

title: SEGA-PointNet: A Semantic Enhancement and Global Aggregation Network for Maize Organ Segmentation from 3D Point Clouds.
abstract: Accurate segmentation of crop organs from three-dimensional (3D) point clouds is critical for intelligent perception in precision agriculture. Existing point cloud networks have limited ability to jointly capture local geometric features and global semantic structures. To address this limitation, this study proposes SEGA-PointNet (Semantic Enhancement and Global Aggregation PointNet), an improved architecture built upon PointNet++. SEGA-PointNet integrates three core modules: SPSA (Semantic-Perceptual Spatial Attention) for multi-scale spatial enhancement, KAN (Kolmogorov-Arnold Network) for nonlinear feature modeling, and GLSFA (Global-Local Semantic Feature Aggregation) for semantic fusion across scales. Experiments on the syau_single_maize dataset demonstrate that SEGA-PointNet achieves higher overall accuracy and mean intersection over union compared with existing point cloud models. Ablation studies verify the positive contribution of each module. SEGA-PointNet provides an effective and extensible framework for 3D semantic segmentation of complex crop structures.

title: A 98.3dB-SNDR 100kHz-BW 4th-CIFF Noise-Shaping SAR ADC Using Source Degeneration Floating Inverter Amplifier.
abstract: This paper presents a 16-bit noise-shaping successive approximation register (NS-SAR) ADC that employs a fourth-order cascade-integrator-feed-forward (CIFF) loop filter based on source-degeneration floating inverter amplifier (SD-FIA). The SD-FIA optimizes the linearity of the traditional FIA structure, enabling the NS SAR ADC to improve accuracy while maintaining high energy efficiency. The proposed architecture utilizes passive charge summation combined with dynamic amplifier to achieve high-order noise shaping. The prototype was implemented in a 180 nm CMOS technology, occupying an active area of 0.195 mm2. It operates at a 5 MHz sampling rate under a 1.8 V supply. Measured results under off-chip LUT-based calibration indicate an SNDR of 98.3 dB, an SNR of 104 dB, an SFDR of 99.6 dB, and an ENOB of 16.0 bits for a 100 kHz signal bandwidth, corresponding to a Schreier FoM of 181.5 dB. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed SD-FIA-based architecture for high-resolution, medium-bandwidth applications.

title: A Vertically Stacked CMOS-MEMS Temperature/Humidity Sensor System for Real-Time Respiration Monitoring.
abstract: This paper presents a vertically stacked micro temperature/humidity sensor fabricated using a standard 0.18 μm 1P6M CMOS-MEMS process, followed by a bulk silicon release post-processing step. The humidity-sensing unit adopts an interdigitated electrode (IDE) configuration coated with a PEDOT:PSS thin film, which effectively enhances moisture adsorption and improves sensing sensitivity. Capacitance characterization using a LCR meter indicates an average sensitivity of 11.4 fF/%RH over the 10%–95% RH range, with a hysteresis of 18.5% of the full scale. Besides, the temperature-sensing element exhibits a linear resistance sensitivity of 12.9 Ω/°C across the 0-50 °C range. Based on the proposed sensor, a fully integrated temperature–humidity sensing system incorporating a custom interface circuit was developed and experimentally evaluated. The sensing system demonstrates fast response, high sensitivity, and can accurately distinguish various human breathing patterns. Moreover, the biocompatibility of the PEDOT:PSS layer makes the proposed sensor system well suited for wearable physiological monitoring, particularly for real-time respiration detection applications.

title: 64-Point Radix-4 fast Fourier transform (FFT) Implementation in an 8 × 4 1T1R RRAM Array.
abstract: The 1-Transistor-1-Resistor (1T1R) Redox-based resistive random-access memory (RRAM) array enables computation-in-memory (CIM) owing to the non-volatile characteristic of RRAM devices, which helps overcome the von Neumann bottleneck. Benefiting from its intrinsic parallelism, the array reduces the complexity of vector-matrix multiplication (VMM) and consequently enhances computational efficiency. As the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) relies on VMM operations, it can be naturally implemented within RRAM arrays. However, as the transformation matrix of DFT increases and its coefficients more complex, larger arrays and highly precise multi-level switching devices are required, posing significant implementation challenges. To overcome these challenges, we propose a concept base on radix-4 fast Fourier transform (FFT) implemented on an 8 × 4 1T1R RRAM array. The array is partially reused to map the transformation matrix, with RRAM devices operated in binary states. Input data with FP16 precision are first bit-sliced into binary, then encoded into different voltage levels and applied on the RRAM array. To further reduce the latency and energy consumption, the input data are either truncated of some least significant bits (LSBs) or bit-sliced into 2-bit segments. This approach is validated by simulation in Cadence Spectre and the results demonstrate consistency with the computations obtained from algorithmic implementation.

title: A 6.86Tb/s Bandwidth SOT-MRAM Sensing Scheme with Configurable Full-Column Over Frequency Technique for Near Memory Computing.
abstract: The proliferation of multimodal systems, which heavily rely on efficient visual backbone networks like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), is driving the adoption of Computing-in-Memory (CIM) architectures for edge deployment. Magnetoresistive RAM (MRAM) is an attractive weight storage medium for such systems due to its non-volatility, inherent radiation hardness, and high-speed read/write potential. However, the computational performance of digital MRAM-CIM chips is bottlenecked by the MRAM read bandwidth, thereby precluding full utilization of its non-volatility and limiting overall energy efficiency, especially as network depth scales. To this end, we introduce a compact, dual-path-optimized full-column-readout sense amplifier (SA) for reliable reading, complemented by a stage-aware over-frequency scheme with algorithm retraining to preserve inferency accuracy. Simulation results of our Spin-Orbit-Torque (SOT)-MRAM design in a 32-channel CIM architecture show a bandwidth of 6.86 Tb/s and a read energy efficiency of 34.5 fJ/bit. This represents a 33.9× improvement in normalized bandwidth over previous cutting-edge designs.

title: RACP: An Efficient RISC-V Domain-Specific Processor for Arbitrary-Size Kernel CNNs.
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are widely used in various fields where the kernel size directly influences both the model expressiveness and inference performance. However, existing accelerators struggle with trade-offs among DSP utilization, computational efficiency, and architectural flexibility for arbitrary-size kernel. To address this issue, we present RACP, a domain-specific, RISC-V processor that leverages its instruction extensions and modular advantages for efficient acceleration. Firstly, we propose a small-kernel fusion (SKF) method for convolution decomposition to reduce redundant computational overhead. On this basis, the processor integrates dedicated customized instructions and a reconfigurable convolution engine with flexible data mapping, thereby reducing unnecessary stalls and preserving pipeline execution. Furthermore, we employ a stacked dataflow scheme combined with a three-level hierarchical memory organization to mitigate memory access bottlenecks. The experimental results show that compared to the baseline, RACP reduces inference latency by over 55.2%. The prototype achieves a peak performance of 417.8GOPS and delivers DSP efficiency improvements of 2.18× over prior FPGA-based accelerators.

title: A 28-Gbps 28-nm CMOS Wireline Receiver Analog Front End With An Adaptive CTLE Enabled By A Hexagonal Mask Eye-Opening Monitor.
abstract: This paper introduces a 28 Gbps high-speed wireline receiver front-end with a continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE) that adapts to channel conditions. It employs a hexagonal mask eye-opening monitor that is proposed in this work to accurately profile the eye diagram by simultaneously constraining data-edge and sampling-clock jitter. Combined with a novel three-phase fast search methodology, this enables rapid CTLE adaptation through a synthesizable control loop. Designed in a 28 nm CMOS, the proposed CTLE consumes 55.8 mW when operating with a 1.0 V supply and occupies an active area of 0.078 mm2. Post-layout simulation results show that it effectively enhances the area of eye diagram by 48.6%, 11.7%, and 686% when tested with three different channels with 14 GHz insertion losses of 6.3 dB, 12.6 dB, and 18.9 dB, respectively.

title: A CMOS E-band Noise-canceling Low Noise Amplifier with 4.5 dB Noise Figure.
abstract: This paper presents an E-band CMOS two-stage low noise amplifier (LNA) with noise-canceling (NC) technology. The proposed LNA employs a tri-coil transformer in the input matching network to simultaneously achieve noise cancellation and impedance matching. Operating at a 1.1 V supply, the LNA achieves a 3-dB bandwidth of 10 GHz (72.3–82.3 GHz), a minimum noise figure (NF) of 4.5 dB, and a peak gain of 13.3 dB, with a power consumption of 18.1 mW. The core area of the LNA is only 0.308 × 0.135 mm2.

title: Dynamic Phased Pruning with Similarity-Aware Filter Selection.
abstract: While importance-based metrics are standard in convolutional neural network (CNN) compression, they often fail to preserve the diversity of the feature space, leading to the retention of redundant information. To overcome this, we introduce a novel framework based on dynamic pruning with similarity-aware filter selection (DPSAFS). Unlike static methods, DPSAFS employs a triple-pool architecture that dynamically sorts filters into retained, optional, and pruned categories. We introduce a composite similarity metric that weighs both the directional alignment (cosine similarity) and magnitude differences (L1-norm) to rigorously identify redundancy. Experimental results on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet demonstrate that DPSAFS effectively balances model compactness with representational power, achieving over 90% parameter sparsity on VGG16 with improved accuracy.

title: Live Demonstration: A Flexible and Upgradable GNSS Receiver on Venus Architecture.
abstract: As Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) advances toward multi-system and multi-frequency operation, modern receivers require greater flexibility and scalability. The Venus architecture, built on RISC-V instruction extensions, effectively meets these demands. This live demonstration presents a software-defined receiver based on the Venus architecture. Implemented in a domain-specific language, the GNSS receiver uses vectorized parallelism to accelerate preprocessing, correlation/integration, and FFT, achieving real-time performance. In addition, acquisition and tracking are optimized for the Venus architecture, improving overall efficiency. The demonstration visualizes the GNSS receiver outputs and real-time positioning results.

title: Experimental Validation of Irradiance Reconstruction and MPPT Performance for Offshore Floating Photovoltaic Systems.
abstract: This study presents an integrated experimental-simulation framework for validating irradiance reconstruction models and evaluating maximum power point tracking (MPPT) performance in offshore floating photovoltaic (FPV) systems. A six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) motion platform was used to replicate wave-induced module motion and verify the irradiance reconstruction accuracy. Experimental results showed strong consistency between measured and simulated irradiance variation curves, confirming the reliability of the proposed method. Further simulations demonstrated that both IP&O and GWO-P&O algorithms achieved high tracking precision and stability, with average MPPT efficiencies of 99.87% and 99.85%, respectively. The proposed approach effectively supports performance evaluation and control optimization for FPV systems operating under dynamic marine conditions.

No degeneration of performance has been presented. Besides, normalized transconductance is considered as a clear signal for the onset of direct tunneling current at cryogenic temperatures.

title: Exponential Distribution of DVS Events and High Latency under Low Light.
abstract: Dynamic vision sensor (DVS) generates high-speed asynchronous event streams via event-driven sparse encoding. However, event-triggering delays induce motion artifacts, which worsen under low light. Our experiments reveal for the first time that the temporal event distribution follows an exponential distribution. Theoretical modeling shows the time constant is inversely related to light intensity. Furthermore, we also establish for the first time that an exponential relationship between this time constant and the event threshold. Measurements confirm the temporal decay depends on both light intensity and threshold. This work clarifies the critical role of these factors in DVS motion artifacts under low light conditions, deepening the understanding of high latency mechanism and supporting physics-based artifact suppression.

title: A 3.4-MHz Class-A Operational Amplifier in GaN Monolithic Technology with 80 dB Open-Loop Gain.
abstract: Monolithic integration is essential to fully exploit the advantages of Gallium Nitride (GaN) technology, particularly its fast-switching capability. However, because of the significant limitations of this emerging technology, including the absence of p-channel transistors, realizing general-purpose building blocks like operational amplifiers (op-amps) remains challenging. This paper presents a two-stage op-amp with a Class-A output stage, implemented fully with n-channel transistors in STpGaN monolithic technology. The proposed design achieves a measured DC gain of 80 dB and a gain-bandwidth of 3.4 MHz for a capacitive load of 100 pF. Measured slew rates in unity-gain configuration are 1.8 V/µs (rising) and –0.2 V/µs (falling) for a 1 V input step. The measured PSRR is 63 dB at 10 kHz and 37 dB at 1 MHz. The op-amp occupies an area of 0.0889 mm2and draws a quiescent current of 150 µA. A detailed comparison with the state-of-the-art is presented and discussed.

title: Library Index Optimization Through Diffusion Model for Accurate Timing Interpolation.
abstract: Timing behaviors of standard cells are modeled using two-dimensional lookup tables. Missing timing values are typically obtained through bilinear interpolation, which can introduce large errors due to the nonlinear characteristics of cell timing. Although interpolation accuracy strongly depends on index values, conventional libraries determine them in a fixed and pre-defined manner, without considering cell-specific nonlinear behavior. To address this limitation, this paper formulates library index optimization as a diffusion-model-based problem. The index set is represented as a vector and iteratively refined through a diffusion process guided by interpolation error, enabling the discovery of index configurations that better capture nonlinear timing behavior. Experimental results show that the proposed method reduces the maximum interpolation error by 9.1% compared to the conventional approach, leading to path delay error reductions of up to 1.7% and 92 ps for the maximum and minimum delays, respectively.

title: Memory-Efficient Twiddle Factor Generator in Parallel NTT Accelerators for FHE Applications.
abstract: In this paper, we present a memory-efficient twiddle factor (TF) generator for number theoretic transform (NTT) accelerator architecture in fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) schemes such as CKKS, where large polynomial degrees (up to 216) lead to substantial TF memory overheads. To address this, we introduce a TF decomposition method that stores only a compact set of seed values, enabling efficient on-the-fly TF generation regardless of NTT parallelism. We then analytically quantify the TF storage requirements in block-parallel NTT architectures, demonstrating the efficiency of the proposed method. Implemented in a 28nm CMOS technology, the proposed accelerator prototype demonstrates support for practical FHE parameter sets while reducing TF memory overhead by up to 78% compared to prior solutions, thus significantly improving the hardware efficiency of high-degree NTT for emerging FHE applications.

title: Frequency Channelized Filtering by Aliasing.
abstract: The Filtering by Aliasing (FA) technique employs periodically time-varying circuits to achieve sharp, linear, integrated filters but the filter sharpness and stop band attenuation is still insufficient for many RF applications. This paper proposes a variant that decomposes the time-varying filter into multiple parallel frequency channelized components potentially enabling arbitrarily sharp filter responses. A brief theoretical analysis, corroborating simulation results, and a discussion on implementation tradeoffs are presented.

title: LSMC Meets GPU Acceleration: Scalable and High-Quality Multi-Row Detailed Placement.
abstract: Detailed placement is a crucial stage in VLSI physical design, optimizing wirelength, timing, routability and power under complex constraints such as edge spacing, site alignment and fence regions. With the aggressive increase of design utilization and adoption of multi-row height cells in advanced technology nodes, existing detailed placers struggle with efficiency and quality, often becoming trapped in local minima. In this work, we develop GPU-DPO, a fast and high-quality GPU-accelerated detailed placement framework built on top of the OpenROAD infrastructure, which leverages Large-Step Markov Chain techniques to escape local optima and improve placement quality. GPU-DPO is the first GPU-accelerated detailed placer with the capability of fully supporting movable and reorderable multi-row height cells. Experimental results on testcases with varying utilization demonstrate that, in comparison with DPO [42] (the default detailed placer in OpenROAD) and ABCDPlace [27] (the state-of-the-art GPU-accelerated detailed placer), our approach achieves an average reduction of post-detailed placement half-perimeter wirelength (HPWL) by 1.71% and 3.5% respectively, while consuming similar runtime as ABCDPlace.

title: A 41-62.4 GHz CMOS Frequency Doubler with Peak 30.79% Drain and 13.7% Total Efficiency.
abstract: A conventional push-push frequency doubler (CPFD) is simple to implement but suffers from limited total efficiency (ηtotal) at millimeter-wave (mm-wave) frequencies due to negative feedback introduced by the gate–drain capacitance (Cgd). To overcome this limitation, a 41-62.4 GHz mm-wave FD is proposed in which the NMOS CPFD employs cross-coupled gate-source feedback that generates an in-phase gate second-harmonic voltage with the drain’s second-harmonic current. This feedback effectively mitigates the inherent Cgdfeedback and doubles the fundamental gate-source voltage, Vgs[f0]. As a result, the drain 2f0current generated by the nonlinear second-harmonic transconductance gm2,nonlinearof the active core’s NMOS is increased, leading to enhanced drain efficiency (ηD) and ηtotal. The proposed FD is designed in a 65 nm CMOS process. Post-layout simulations demonstrate a peak ηDof 30.79%, a peak ηtotalof 13.7%, and a peak 2f0output power of 5.8 dBm at 46 GHz, with a 12 dBm local oscillator (LO) input and 12.66 mW DC power consumption. The FD achieves a 3 dB bandwidth of 41-62.4 GHz (41.4%) and an efficiency bandwidth of 42.3–56GHz (27.7%), where ηtotal≥ 10%.

title: A High-Performance and Area-Efficient Unified Butterfly Module for ML-KEM Polynomial Computations.
abstract: With the rapid advancement of quantum computing technology, traditional public-key cryptographic algorithms are gradually losing their security guarantees. To address this challenge, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) announced the Module Lattice-based Key Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM) in 2022, whose security is based on the computational hardness of the Module Learning with Errors (MLWE) problem. This makes it resistant to quantum attacks in the foreseeable future. In this paper, we propose a high-performance and area-efficient butterfly computation unit that supports various polynomial operations in ML-KEM, including the Number Theoretic Transform (NTT), Inverse NTT (INTT), and Point-wise Multiplication (PWM). The proposed butterfly unit is constructed from basic modular arithmetic submodules and incorporates a rescheduled Karatsuba algorithm to enhance the efficiency of polynomial multiplication without incurring significant hardware overhead.

title: Educational Perspectives on LLM Architectures: Analyzing Code Generation for Circuits and Systems.
abstract: We present a systematic analysis of large language models (LLMs) tailored for circuit and system synthesis. The paper is structured as a pedagogical resource for graduate and advanced undergraduate students in machine learning, offering insights into the interplay between LLM architectures and domain-specific performance. Toward that end, we propose a taxonomy of architectural aspects that differentiate LLM suitability across domain, in particular for hardware design versus broader tasks such as image/video generation and conversational assistance. We examine how the stringent requirements of hardware design—ranging from bit-accurate synthesis to performance-critical logic—have motivated specialized innovations in attention mechanisms, training objectives, and context windows. To complement this analysis, we also provide a codebase that enable hands-on insights for students by inspecting LLM architectures and comparing model performance before/after parameter updates and fine-tuning for circuit and system synthesis.

title: Dynamic GNNs for Continual Learning on Circuits.
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown strong potential for analyzing circuits, enabling tasks such as node classification for reverse engineering. However, when trained with a fixed architecture in a continual learning (CL) setting, GNNs can suffer from catastrophic forgetting (CF), where performance on earlier tasks deteriorates as new tasks are introduced. To address this challenge, we propose dynamic architecture expansion that incrementally grow the model while freezing previously learned weights, thereby preserving past knowledge. We investigate two mechanisms for expansion: (i) widening through concatenated encoders with task-specific heads, and (ii) deepening through stacked layers. To determine the optimal expansion size, we explore multiple hyperparameter tuning strategies. Experiments across four prominent GNN backbones (GCN, GraphSAGE, GIN, GAT) on ISCAS85 and EPFL netlists demonstrate that dynamic expansion significantly mitigates CF, ensuring fair and reproducible benchmarking for both node classification and link prediction tasks. title: A 30.4 dB Dynamic Range Pulse-Modulated Class-E RF PA with 11-bit Digital Pulse Modulation Unit Achieving 25.3 dBm Psat and 32.3% Peak PAE.
abstract: This paper presents a compact pulse-modulated Class-E RF Power Amplifier (PA) integrating an 11-bit Digital Pulse-Modulation (DPM) unit in 22 nm FD-SOI CMOS. The proposed high resolution RF-PWM generation circuit segments the rising and falling time of the generated pulses in coarse and fine delay steps with the use of high-speed digital logic and Digital-to-Time converters (DTCs). Measurements show 25.3 dBm Psatand 32.3% peak PAE at 1.75 GHz, with operation from 1.4–1.85 GHz and 0.65 W/mm2power density. The DPM adds only 0.026 mm2(≈5%) area and ≤2% efficiency overhead, yet expands output-power dynamic range to 30.4 dB and digitally compensates nonlinearities: static LUT-based predistortion reduces AM–AM and AM–PM RMS errors to 12 mV and 1.5°, respectively (14.5×/15.1× improvement). Compared with a conventional Class-E PA, the proposed PA improves PAE by 5.5%, 5.2%, and 3.8% at 3, 6, and 9 dB back-off; it also achieves 6.2% higher PAE than a Class-B PA at 6 dB back-off.

title: DirectGeMM: Eliminating the GeMV Bottleneck in Analog In-Memory Computing.
abstract: General matrix–matrix multiplication (GeMM) dominates 40-95% of AI workload execution time, but existing in-memory computing (IMC) architectures suffer from a fundamental cycle bottleneck, decomposing GeMM into sequential general matrix-vector multiplications (GeMV) requiring O(M) cycles. In this paper, we propose DirectGeMM, a direct GeMM architecture for analog crossbar arrays that eliminates this bottleneck for the prevalent K ≪ M, N regime through FP8 pre-alignment (shared-exponent extraction for analog-compatible floating-point) and outer-product accumulation (in-situ conductance updates across K phases). Experimental results show that our architecture reduces compute cycles from O(M) to O(K) for AI workloads where K ≪ M, N (K: inner dimension, M: output rows, N: output columns), achieving 58-847× cycle and 12-47× energy reduction across Transformer and CNN models, with 90% classification accuracy on MNIST.

title: A 5V swing, 20GS/s, 6-bit Current Steering DAC utilizing LDMOS in 22nm FDSOI CMOS.
abstract: This paper proposes a 6 bit, 20 GS/s current steering DAC achieving 5 V and 4 V swing at 6.3 GHz and 10 GHz respectively, while consuming 900 mW power. Lateral diffused MOSFET cascodes enable the DAC to operate at high voltages in a power efficient CMOS technology. The presented architecture is designed as an energy efficient Mach-Zehnder-Modulator driver to accommodate low power electro-optical data conversion. To support the high current load, which is required to provide 5 V swing over the 50 Ohm matched output, PMOS current sources are connected in parallel to the analog core’s load resistors. The DAC employs inductive peaking and a negative capacitance generator as bandwidth extension techniques and is segmented for better linearity. Therefore, it achieves 35.6 dBFS SNDR near Nyquist and can generate a 56 Gbit/s PAM16 eye diagram with 150 mV vertical eye margin.

title: A Novel Segmentation Approach Based on Analog LSB for High-Resolution mmWave Digital TXs.
abstract: This paper proposes a new segmentation approach for digital Mixing-DACs (MXDAC) that can enable high-resolution wireless transmitters at mmWave frequencies. The MSB part is realized with unary MXDAC 1-bit slices for their high accuracy, while the LSB part is realized as an analog power mixer for its area efficiency. In fact, the D/A function for the LSB part takes place in the baseband domain, and not in the mmWave domain. This method enables enhanced resolution while minimizing physical area and the impact of associated mmWave effects, and consequently preserving low error vector magnitude (EVM). The new segmentation approach is implemented in two exemplary designs in 28 nm bulk CMOS, a 140 GHz real MXDAC and a 140 GHz I/Q modulator. Both designs have 3 MSB and 3 LSB segmentation. The real MXDAC shows that up to 5 effective number of bits (ENOB) is possible in a 10 GHz signal bandwidth. The I/Q modulator achieves a dynamic EVM of -34.30 dB for QAM 1024. This simulated performance, with layout-extracted parasitics, is shown to be possible thanks to the small area that the new segmentation approach allows.

title: CryHop: Baby Cry Classification on Dunstan Dataset using Transfer Learning and Ensembling.
abstract: Identifying the cause of infant crying is essential for new parents, particularly since the task is challenging amid sleep deprivation and disrupted routines. Prior infant-cry studies often report high accuracies without accounting for variable audio durations or biases from audio resizing (cropping, padding, or resampling), which distort temporal–spectral structure and inflate performance. We circumvent these biases and present a reliable baby-cry classification method using Dunstan Baby Language (DBL), which defines five cry types: belly pain, need to burp, discomfort, hunger, and tiredness. To remove length bias while producing fixed-size inputs, we compute Mel-spectrograms with a variable hop length, yielding a constant number of time frames for the classifier. We apply Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (GCAM) heatmaps to show our method avoids biased learning and use ensemble softmax averaging for inference. Lastly, top-2 predictions improve parental guidance, achieving 94.88% top-1 and 99.49% top-2 accuracy on the five Dunstan classes, enabling parents to address infants’ needs in at most two tries.

title: Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning Accelerators: Balancing Efficiency and Security.
abstract: Privacy-preserving machine learning (PPML), particularly based on differential privacy (DP) as the gold standard, has become essential for deploying AI in sensitive domains such as healthcare, finance, and edge intelligence, where user data must remain secure. However, the computational overhead of DP-ML mechanisms far exceeds the capacity of conventional processors, motivating the need for specialized accelerator designs. This paper reviews recent advances in DP training from both hardware and software perspectives. Whereas software-level strategies reduce computational cost while maintaining rigorous privacy guarantees, hardware-focused approaches address efficiency, scalability, and energy challenges in DP training. By examining these complementary approaches, the review illustrates how hardware and software innovations in accelerators can collectively enhance the feasibility and performance of DP systems for practical PPML. These insights bridge the gap between current accelerator capabilities and the realization of secure, efficient, and trustworthy AI, pointing toward future architectures that enable safe and scalable deployment of PPML in real-world applications.

title: Circuit Similarity Based Initial Parameter Sampling for Tool Parameter Exploration.
abstract: Tool parameters in logic synthesis and physical design tools significantly affect the design implementation and ultimately determine the quality of the resulting design. Each circuit has its own optimal set of tool parameters to achieve the best design quality, and various global optimization methods, such as Bayesian optimization, genetic algorithms, and reinforcement learning, are commonly employed to find them. However, these methods often require long runtimes to explore numerous parameter combinations. In this paper, we accelerate the optimization process by leveraging pre-optimized tool parameter sets from other circuits, under the assumption that circuits with similar designs exhibit comparable optimal tool parameter configurations. Experimental results show that the proposed method consistently outperforms conventional approaches, achieving an average of 14.3% greater improvement in energy–delay product within the same runtime, and requiring 2.8× smaller runtime to reach the same level of improvement.

title: MEGA.mini-S: A 1.9-to-15.0 TOPS/W Generative AI Processor with Bit-serial Weight Scalability and Bank-Conflict-free Sparsity Compression.
abstract: This paper presents an energy-efficient generative AI processor that extends the prior MEGA.mini by introducing three key innovations: 1) a 2’s complement-based bit-serial MAC that supports weight precision scalability from 1 to 8 bits, 2) a conflict-free tile-based compressed sparse row (T-CSR) encoding for sparsity-aware processing, and 3) an upgraded dual-core design that maximizes parallelism while eliminating bank conflicts in weight and activation memory access. The MEGA-S core adopts a novel FXP bit-serial MAC with a low-power accumulation scheme, while the mini-S core employs a DFP-to-FP16 bit-serial MAC with efficient exponent handling for sparse outliers. To further improve scalability, the proposed T-CSR format encodes the output activation tile-wise and enables tile-level input channel partitioning, effectively avoiding both WMEM and IOMEM bank conflicts. Implemented in 28nm CMOS technology, MEGA.mini-S achieves up to 15.0 TOPS/W and demonstrates 54.5% higher throughput than prior zero-RLE-based single-core designs across various generative AI tasks including diffusion model-based image generation, and low-bit LLM inference.

title: A 20 Gb/s All-Digital CDR with Fast Locking and Improved PI Linearity Using an Injection-Locked Ring Oscillator.
abstract: This paper presents a 20 Gb/s all-digital clock and data recovery (AD-CDR) circuit implemented in a 28-nm CMOS process. The proposed architecture integrates a fast frequency acquisition loop using an injection-locked ring oscillator (ILRO) and a phase acquisition loop based on a 64-step phase interpolator (PI). A bang-bang phase detector (BBPD) detects phase errors, and a digital loop filter (DLF) with a continuously tunable integral gain KIensures stable phase convergence while meeting jitter tolerance and output jitter specifications. A Booth-encoded unsigned multiplier is employed for fine gain control with minimal hardware overhead. The half-rate reference clock is injected into the ILRO to rapidly generate 8-phase clock signals at 10 GHz, and the PI achieves fine phase resolution of π/32, defined as 1 LSB (l.5625ps). The proposed CDR core occupies 0.203mm2, consumes 112.8mW from a 1 V supply, and achieves a BER of 10-12with an input pulse amplitude of 600m Vpp,diffat 20Gb/s. Post-layout simulations show a frequency lock time of 840ps, with RMS and peak-to-peak jitters of 7.32 fs and 24 fs, respectively, and PI DNL within 0.28 LSB.

title: A 26 Gb/s/pin Single-Ended Transceiver With Adaptive Switched-Capacitor-Based Simultaneous Switching Noise Compensation.
abstract: Dense die-to-die (D2D) interfaces employing single-ended signaling with 32+ parallel lanes face severe simultaneous switching noise (SSN) challenges. title: Low-Latency Software-Defined 5G NR PUSCH Receiver with Mixed-Precision SIMD Acceleration.
abstract: This paper presents a low-latency software-defined 5G New Radio physical uplink shared channel receiver optimized on general-purpose processors. The proposed receiver exploits a cutting-edge single-instruction multiple-data (SIMD) vectorization with mixed-precision computations, applying 32-bit floating-point only to precision-sensitive computations while using 8-bit integer arithmetic for latency-critical stages. To further reduce demodulation latency, we develop an unrolled equalizer to minimize control overhead and employ lookup-table-based implementations. Experimental results show that the proposed design achieves a 76% reduction in equalization latency compared to a high-precision baseline and a 3× faster demodulation processing compared to the previous SIMD-accelerated receiver.

title: Design of Switch-Free Bias-Current-Free ∆Σ Fractional-N PLLs with Calibration-Free Quantization Noise Reduction.
abstract: This paper describes a low-voltage ∆Σ fractional-N PLL architecture that does not require complex calibration. To reduce quantization noise, both overclocking and hybrid finite impulse response (FIR) filter techniques are employed with multiphase phase detectors (PDs) and dividers. The hybrid FIR filter lowers the oversampling ratio (OSR), which helps alleviate not only the maximum speed limitation of the ∆Σ modulator under low supply voltage but also the limited linear range problem of the multiphase PD, particularly in fractional-N PLLs. With the proposed quantization reduction method, a switch-free bias-current-free fractional-N PLL with a voltage-mode PD is realized. The proposed architecture operates from a 0.5 V supply voltage and consumes a total power of 1.202 mW. Phase noise analysis is performed with variation combinations of OSR and FIR taps. Simulation results show that a 2-phase PD with a 2-tap FIR filter achieves significant quantization noise reduction without any calibration. Owing to the switch-free voltage-mode operation, the proposed calibration-free fractional-N PLL has reduced sensitivity to circuit nonlinearity, enabling robust frequency synthesis under low supply voltage.

title: BRAM-Free ML-KEM NTT with SRL-Based Reordering Unit.
abstract: The module-lattice-based key encapsulation mechanism (ML-KEM), standardized by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), is a key encapsulation scheme based on module learning with errors (MLWE). Its core computation relies on polynomial multiplication using the number theoretic transform (NTT), which is executed as a sequence of NTT–point-wise multiplication (PWM)–inverse NTT (INTT). This work presents a BRAM-free NTT architecture employing a shift-register lookup table (SRL)-based Reordering Unit (RU) to eliminate memory access and address-generation overheads. The RU consists of seven SRL-based clusters that enable conflict-free data reordering across stages, while the Butterfly Unit (BU) adopts a BRAM-free datapath to remove on-chip memory latency along the BU–RU–BU critical path. The proposed design was implemented on a Xilinx Artix-7 (AC701) platform, achieving 294 MHz operating frequency using 1132 LUTs, 561 FFs, 346 slices, 0 BRAMs, and 2 DSPs. For NTT/INTT/PWM operations, the design requires 458/458/275 cycles, and demonstrates 11–89% improvement in area-time product (ATP) compared with representative Artix-7 designs. The proposed SRL-based, BRAM-free datapath effectively eliminates data conflicts and provides a compact and high-throughput hardware solution for ML-KEM.

title: A16K: 1.6nm NSFET, FSFET, and CFET Technology Libraries for Chip-Level VLSI Prediction.
abstract: Semiconductor process is evolving more than ever before. Major foundries plan to mass-produce the 2nm process, while academia continues to announce devices for even more advanced nodes. Despite the continuous scaling in technology nodes, it remains uncertain to what extent digital VLSI can further improve in advanced and future nodes. Therefore, we present A16K: the first public 16 Angstrom (Å) technology library and report the following results. 1) It is crucial to design standard cells with fewer tracks compared to the 2nm library for better PPA (power, performance, and area) improvement. 2) Increasing usable signal tracks by adopting Buried Power Rail (BPR) guarantees substantial PPA improvement. 3) 3T CFET library shows -35.5% power, -44.1% area, and +2.84% effective frequency enhancement compared to the 2nm counterpart. Based on these results, we emphasize that design technology co-optimization (DTCO) is essential for process development in addition to native transistor scaling.

title: Memory-Efficient Partially Self-Corrected Min-Sum LDPC Decoder for 5G NR Applications.
abstract: This paper presents a memory-efficient partially self-corrected min-sum (PSCMS) decoding algorithm and its hardware implementation for 5G NR LDPC codes. The proposed PSCMS algorithm selectively applies the self-correction mechanism and reconstructs variable-to-check (V2C) signs on the fly, thereby removing the need for additional sign and zero-flag memories required by the previous SCMS approach. As a result, the proposed work attains memory usage equivalent to the baseline MS algorithm while maintaining a strong error-correction capability. Implemented in a 65-nm CMOS technology, the PSCMS decoder achieves a throughput of 5.3 Gb/s at 400 MHz, with 34.5% smaller area, 39.2% lower power, 1.92× higher area efficiency, and 52.0% lower energy per bit than the conventional SCMS design, achieving an attractive trade-off between error-correction performance and hardware efficiency.

title: A Scalable Dual-Input/Output Heap-Based Top-K Unit for Vector Search Accelerators.
abstract: Modern vector search accelerators require efficient top-K maintenance to process massive similarity scores generated by distance computation units. As the number of candidates (K) increases, conventional architectures such as a systolic priority queue and a pipelined heap face a trade-off between throughput and hardware complexity, often becoming a primary bottleneck in large-scale search systems. To address this limitation, we propose a dual-input/output heap-based top-K unit that achieves high throughput with low hardware overhead. The proposed top-K unit processes two input elements simultaneously using a hierarchical sub-heap structure, enabling continuous dual-element insertion and extraction every two cycles. This design achieves logarithmic scaling in the number of required comparators with respect to K, enabling efficient operation for large-K configurations. Furthermore, a large portion of flip-flop-based storage is replaced with high-density SRAM at deeper heap levels, mitigating register overhead while preserving the top-K candidate set. Synthesized in a Samsung 28 nm CMOS process, the proposed architecture demonstrates strong scalability and hardware efficiency for large-K vector search accelerators.

title: An 80 Gbit/s NRZ 100 Gbit/s PAM4 Highly-Efficient Voltage-Mode VCSEL-Driver in 22nm FDSOI CMOS.
abstract: This paper presents the realization of a DC-coupled 80Gbit/s (NRZ), 100Gbit/s (PAM4) energy-efficient voltage-mode VCSEL driver implemented in 22nm FDSOI CMOS, utilizing an accurate electro-optical (E/O) VCSEL model. The driver architecture comprises a subtractive-type continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE) that compensates for the complex-conjugate pole-pair characteristic of the optical VCSEL response, together with an inductively peaked Cherry–Hooper (CH)-based programmable gain amplifier (PGA) that enables broadband signal amplification. A super source-follower (SSF)–based output stage directly drives the VCSEL by modulating the voltage at its anode. Simulation results of the complete driver system demonstrate an energy efficiency of 0.33pJ/bit and 0.25pJ/bit at 80Gbit/s (NRZ) and 100Gbit/s (PAM4), respectively, when operating from a dual 0.9V and 1.1V power supply.

title: Energy Function Choice for Training Nonlinear Resistive Neural Networks with Equilibrium Propagation.
abstract: Equilibrium Propagation (EqProp) is an alternative to backpropagation for minimizing an energy function. Existing EqProp implementations for nonlinear resistive networks typically rely on a pseudo-power formulation, defined as the integral of the local current-voltage characteristic. However, pseudo-power is only applicable to two-terminal components and cannot be extended to dependent or multi-terminal elements, limiting its conceptual consistency across the circuit. This work proposes using the true electrical power, defined as I • V , as the governing energy function for analog resistive networks. Theoretically, the true electrical power satisfies the equilibrium condition ∂P/∂V = 0 and aligns with Kirchhoff’s laws across both linear and nonlinear devices. Ngspice and PySpice simulations of the XOR task, averaged over 100 randomly initialized resistance values, show that the true-power formulation achieves stable convergence to approximately −7dB error, compared to −4dB for pseudo-power. When controlled-source or diode contributions were excluded, both formulations failed to learn and diverged toward +10dB. These results demonstrate that EqProp learning in analog hardware requires an energy function that accounts for all circuit components; in addition, the true electrical power provides a physically consistent formulation with lower computational overhead than pseudo-power.

title: An Isomorphic Transformation for Hardware Implemented Non-negative Neural Networks.
abstract: High speed and efficient accelerators such as neuromorphic photonics are becoming increasingly popular, as they can significantly improve the computation speed and energy efficiency of matrix-based calculations, leading to femtojoule per MAC efficiency. However, deploying existing DL models on such platforms is not trivial, as a wide range of photonic neural network (PNN) architectures relies on incoherent setups and power-adding operational schemes that cannot natively represent negative quantities. This results in additional hardware complexity that increases costs and reduces energy efficiency. To overcome this, we can train non-negative neural networks and potentially exploit the full range of incoherent neuromorphic photonic capabilities. However, the existing non-negative training approaches cannot achieve the same level of accuracy as their regular counterparts. To this end, we introduce a methodology to obtain the non-negative isomorphic equivalents of regular artificial neural networks (ANNs) that meet the requirements of neuromorphic hardware, as it allows one to perform inference with non-negative-only parameters.

title: Open and Accessible Workflows for the education and Prototyping of Nanoelectronic Devices.
abstract: Modern semiconductor design is organised into a layered hierarchy of abstraction that governs the progression from device-level modelling to complete system realisation. This paper examines the methods and software tools used at each stage, spanning technology computer-aided design for device simulation, through mixed-signal and circuit-level verification, and culminating in FPGA prototyping and ASIC implementation. It places particular emphasis on the rising role of open-source electronic design automation ecosystems, which are increasingly complementing or displacing conventional proprietary solutions. The study shows how such tools enable educational and research institutions to undertake end-to-end semiconductor design using transparent, reproducible workflows. Open PDks, cloud-hosted automation frameworks, and shared community fabrication shuttles reduce cost and complexity, making silicon prototyping more accessible for students and investigators. Together, these innovations foster the democratisation of nanoelectronic and VLSI design by supporting open, interoperable processes that connect theoretical work, experimental validation, and physical fabrication.

title: A 0.58 Ops/Trans Analog Compute-in-Memory Macro with Input Operand Generator Supporting Wide Boolean Operations for Enhanced Versatility.
abstract: Compute-in-memory (CIM) has emerged as a promising solution to mitigate the bandwidth bottleneck by performing computations directly inside memory arrays. However, most prior CIM designs have been optimized primarily for multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) operations, restricting their applicability to a wider range of tasks. To address this limitation, this paper presents an analog CIM (ACIM) macro that extends functionality beyond MAC operations through a 10T1C SRAM cell and an input operand generator (IOG). By converting input values into two signals applied to the bitcell, the IOG enables six Boolean logic operations (AND, NAND, OR, NOR, XOR, XNOR) with minimal area overhead of the peripheral circuitry, yielding an efficiency of 0.58 Ops/Trans. Meanwhile, the 10T1C bitcell performs charge-domain MAC operations via capacitive coupling, which ensures high linearity. Furthermore, a quaternary-search analog-to-digital converter (ADC) mitigates area overhead by sharing one ADC among three columns through time-interleaving operation. The increased latency from time interleaving is compensated by converting two bits per cycle. Designed in a 28-nm CMOS technology, the proposed ACIM macro achieves an energy efficiency of 33.8 TOPS/W and an inference accuracy of 89.81% for ResNet-18 model on the CIFAR-10 dataset.

title: A Digitally Controlled Delay Line with Delay Calibration in Phase-Interpolator.
abstract: This paper proposes an expandable digitally controlled delay line (DCDL) to improve the linearity of the delay value corresponding to the digital code. The proposed DCDL consists of two delay lines, i.e., a coarse delay line and a fine delay line, which together achieve a wide delay range and high resolution. To enhance the linearity of the DCDL, the minimum delay value of the coarse delay line and the maximum value of the fine delay line should be precisely matched because of a cascade connection of the delay lines. In other words, if there is a mismatch between these delay values, significant degradation of linearity occurs when switching between the coarse and fine delay lines. In the proposed DCDL, this mismatch is automatically suppressed by the Self-Calibration scheme of phase interpolator (PI) in the fine delay line, regardless of PVT variations. A prototype chip was fabricated using an 0.18 μm CMOS process, and measurement results confirmed that the proposed method effectively eliminates the delay nonlinearity. The proposed DCDL exhibits a quarter of the DNL/INL compared to previous work and compared to other chips in the same generation process, it also shows approximately half the DNL and equivalent INL despite a wide delay range.

title: Multi-Source Localization in High-Noise Mixed Fields: A Logarithmic Spacing Multi-Concentric Circular Array and Conical Gridding Method.
abstract: In industrial production and maintenance, Sound Source Localization is a common method for monitoring and rapidly identifying fault points such as gas leaks and bearing damage. With the proliferation of embedded hardware supporting efficient matrix operations, methods based on Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA) for spatial reconstruction are gradually being replaced by those utilizing steering vectors derived from wave propagation models in irrotational fluids. Steering vector-based methods are often more sensitive to array geometry, which has led to the development of improved arrays based on compressed sensing theory, such as the logarithmic spiral array. However, in our practical evaluations, the logarithmic spiral array demonstrated poor performance in localizing far-field sources within hybrid near-field and far-field scenarios under high noise and struggled with designing effective spatial filters for low-frequency imaging tasks prone to high sidelobe contamination. To address these issues, we propose a modified multi-concentric circular array with logarithmic spacing and equal angular rotation, inspired by the design principles of the logarithmic spiral array. Concurrently, we introduce a non-uniform conical gridding method tailored to this array's characteristics to better facilitate spatial filtering. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed array design achieves superior performance in terms of sidelobe reduction, on-grid error, and off-grid error compared to the logarithmic spiral array in FISTA-based sparse reconstruction tasks involving high white noise and mixed-field sources. Furthermore, the proposed gridding method significantly outperforms traditional gridding techniques in sidelobe level, on-grid and off-grid errors, and computational cost.

title: An RTL-based CNN Inference Module for Low-Power Edge Vision Applications.
abstract: In this paper, by quantifying the perception RTL design, an efficient CNN accelerator architecture optimized for FPGA-based edge vision systems is proposed. This framework integrates convolution, activation, pooling, flattening and fully connected modules into independently synthesized Verilog entities, achieving high parallelism and scalability. Each module is optimized using a Boolean multiplier and a forward adder to achieve a balance between computational throughput and hardware resource efficiency. The accelerator adopts an INT8 quantization scheme to minimize memory usage while ensuring inference accuracy. This design is implemented on Xilinx Zynq-7020 FPGA, achieving real-time classification of road sign images. It has low power consumption, low hardware utilization rate and does not require a dedicated DSP module. The experimental results confirmed the feasibility of deploying quantized CNNS on resource-constrained embedded platforms, demonstrating an end-to-end software and hardware collaborative optimization solution suitable for low-latency and energy-efficient edge applications.

title: Hardware-Friendly Machine-Learning-Based Fast AV1 Overlapped Block Motion Compensation.
abstract: The AV1 video codec was defined by major technology players as an efficient, royalty-free video codec. AV1 delivers substantial compression gains over other codecs, such as VP9, at the cost of significantly increased computational effort. A notable contributor to this computational effort is the Overlapped Block Motion Compensation (OBMC) tool, which is used to mitigate blocking artifacts at prediction boundaries. This paper introduces FastOBMC, a hardware-friendly Decision Tree (DT) method to reduce the computational effort of OBMC by selectively skipping its execution in scenarios where it is unlikely to provide a rate-distortion benefit. To accomplish this, a simple hardware-friendly DT was trained. Experimental results carried out in the AV1 reference software show that the method reduces the execution time of the OBMC by an average of 74.68% while incurring a negligible loss of coding efficiency of only 0.07% in BD-BR. To our knowledge, this is the first work in the literature to address the reduction of computational effort of the OBMC tool in AV1.

title: A 2-GHz 5.06-mW Phase Accumulator Employing Dynamic Regulation for High-Speed Direct Digital Frequency Synthesizers in 65-nm CMOS.
abstract: This paper proposes a low power phase accumulator (PACC) for high speed direct digital frequency synthesizers(DDFS). First, a dynamic control technique for the rows and columns of a flip-flop array is proposed, significantly reducing power consumption. Second, a signal delay chain is introduced to replace the flip-flop chain, thus greatly saving the required flip-flop hardware. Post-layout simulations in a 65-nm low-power CMOS process demonstrate that proposed PACC with a word length of 32 bits, consumes only 5.06mW, and has a maximum clock frequency of 2GHz.

title: Mitigating Conductance Drift via In-Situ Calibration for Reliable RRAM-Based CIM Edge Inference.
abstract: Edge-AI systems based on resistive random-access memory (RRAM) compute-in-memory (CIM) hardware suffer from conductance drift induced by intrinsic device non-idealities such as relaxation and read-disturb effects, leading to gradual degradation of inference accuracy. Existing calibration methods either reprogram all RRAM weights at the cost of endurance degradation or depend on off-chip retraining, preventing fully autonomous on-chip learning. This work presents an on-chip-integrable, zero-RRAM-write conductance drift calibration method that combines a low-rank-adaptation (LoRA)-based CIM architecture with a layer-wise distillation-based weight update scheme. The proposed approach reduces the number of updatable weights to below 5% and performs in-situ LoRA computation within the RRAM CIM array via pseudo-RRAM cells, eliminating RRAM rewriting and additional hardware overhead. It also eliminates cross-layer backpropagation and lowers the calibration dataset requirement to fewer than five samples, enabling low-cost on-chip self-calibration with a total area of 1.422 mm2in 22 nm CMOS. Simulation results based on measured RRAM conductance drift data demonstrate that, using only 4 samples for calibration, the inference accuracy of ResNet-20 is recovered from 68.77% (46.41%) to 86.54% (62.06%) on CIFAR-10 (CIFAR-100) dataset.

title: InFuzz: An Efficient and Lightweight In-Memory-Computing Cryptographic Fuzzy Extractor for IoT Security.
abstract: As a vital cryptographic primitive for IoT security, the fuzzy extractor is capable of deriving uniformly random and precisely reproducible keys from noisy sources. However, conventional hardware implementations are critically limited by the "von Neumann bottleneck": large parity-check matrices must be repeatedly shuttled between memory and processing units, which causes significant energy consumption and latency. In this work, we introduce InFuzz, the first in-memory cryptographic fuzzy extractor architecture. Our design realizes an in-situ fuzzy extractor using Quasi-Cyclic Low-Density Parity-Check (QC-LDPC) codes directly within an SRAM array, eliminating costly data movement. Evaluated in a 28nm process, InFuzz achieves a total latency of 9.93 μs and an energy consumption of 8.43 nJ, improving energy efficiency by up to 68.0× over prior implementations. By integrating storage and computation, this work presents a novel, ultra-low-power pathway for secure key generation on resource-constrained edge devices.

title: Implementation and Evaluation of a Cryogenic DSP in 22-nm with Floating-Point Arithmetic for Estimating Qubit States.
abstract: Recent advancements in quantum computing have emphasized the need for scalable quantum–classical interfaces (QC-IFs) capable of controlling a huge number of qubits efficiently. Conventional QC-IFs, implemented at room temperature, face wiring and thermal challenges that limit system scalability as the number of qubits increases. To address these issues, we propose a cryogenic digital signal processor (DSP) architecture capable of performing qubit readout and control operations inside the dilution refrigerator. We implemented the DSP which replaced wide fixed-point operations by floating-point ones in a previous study. An ASIC was fabricated using a 22-nm CMOS bulk process. Compared with the previous study, power consumption and area increased at room temperature due to additional circuits. We conducted a leakage power analysis on this design based on transistor leakage characteristics at 25 °C and −73 °C. The results demonstrated a reduction of 96.6% compared to leakage power at 25 °C. These results demonstrate the feasibility of low-power, compact control electronics for future Cryo-CMOS control SoCs and fault-tolerant quantum computing systems.
