title: On Resistor Nonlinearity Modeling for Low-Distortion Analog Circuits.
abstract: The nonlinearity of resistors can cause distortion in circuits such as amplifiers, filters, and delta-sigma modulators. Models commonly used by many foundries use first and second-order voltage coefficients for the resistance value. This model is unphysical. Though it can match the resistor I-V characteristics over a limited voltage range, the nonlinear distortion products calculated using them can be very inaccurate, especially at low distortion levels. If the model overpredicts the nonlinear products, designers must choose larger resistors whose parasitics negatively affect other performance measures. It is shown here that, for accurate modeling, only even-order voltage coefficients of resistance should be used for a two-terminal resistor, or a complete three-terminal model must be used. Nonlinear coefficients should be extracted in a symmetric voltage range around zero.

title: From RTL to Prompt Coding: Empowering the Next Generation of Chip Designers through LLMs.
abstract: This paper presents an LLM-based learning platform for chip design education, aiming to make chip design accessible to beginners without overwhelming them with technical complexity. It represents the first educational platform that assists learners holistically across both frontend and backend design. The proposed approach integrates an LLM-based chat agent into a browser-based workflow built upon the Tiny Tapeout ecosystem. The workflow guides users from an initial design idea through RTL code generation to a tapeout-ready chip. To evaluate the concept, a case study was conducted with 18 high-school students. Within a 90-minute session they developed eight functional VGA chip designs in a 130 nm technology. Despite having no prior experience in chip design, all groups successfully implemented tapeout-ready projects. The results demonstrate the feasibility and educational impact of LLM-assisted chip design, highlighting its potential to attract and inspire early learners and significantly broaden the target audience for the field.

title: A 7×25Gb/s Transceiver Using Codebook-Based CNRZ-7 for High-Density Transmission.
abstract: This paper presents a 7 × 25Gb/s wireline transceiver (TRX) for high-density transmission. A codebook-based correlated none-return-to-zero (CNRZ-7) modulation scheme is employed to achieve high output bandwidth while maintaining strong immunity to crosstalk (XT), simultaneous switching noise (SSN), and common-mode noise (CMN). In the receiver (RX), a single-ended Q-shaped continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE) replaces the conventional multi-input equalizer to suppress additional noise introduced by finite common-mode gain (ADM-CM). The proposed TRX is fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS process. Measurement results show that the TRX achieves a vertical eye opening of 90 mV and a horizontal eye opening of 27 ps at 25 Gb/s per lane, corresponding to a bit-error rate (BER) o 1 x 1012.

title: A 0.35 mm2 Fully Pipelined JPEG Encoder for Monolithic CMOS ISFET Array Integration.
abstract: This paper presents a fully pipelined and synthesisable JPEG baseline encoder, tailored for on-chip image compression in monolithically integrated systems with CMOS ISFET arrays. Motivated by the increasing feasibility of on-chip digital processing enabled by continued CMOS scaling, this work highlights new opportunities to embed complex processing engines directly within the sensing front end. The developed encoder IP features a separate and vectorised transform pipeline, enabling a hardware-efficient architecture that achieves continuous one-pixel-per-cycle throughput (II=1) while maintaining scalability and configurability for different block sizes and transform variants, rather than arithmetic-specific optimisations. A coordinate-driven zigzag sequencer computes indices on the fly, eliminating the need for LUTs, thereby reducing memory usage and enhancing scalability. The system is first implemented and validated on an FPGA, demonstrating a PSNR deviation of less than 0.01% compared to images compressed by a standard library. It is then optimised via fully synthesisable arithmetic units for ASIC implementation. Fabricated in a 65 nm CMOS process, the encoder consumes 35.89 mW at 100 MHz. It occupies a die area of 0.35 mm2, representing approximately 1.4% in the state-of-the-art sensing SoC, demonstrating its suitability for on-chip integration in future smart-sensing front ends.

title: BrainRead: Multi-Sensor Earable System for Continuous Physiological Sensing.
abstract: We present BrainRead, a multimodal earable system designed for continuous physiological sensing through an integrated architecture spanning signal acquisition, on-device storage and processing, and wireless communication. The platform incorporates EarEEG, EarECG, EarPPG, a 6-axis IMU, and a IR temperature sensor within earbuds, supported by a modular neckband and chestbud subsystem housing dual MCUs, power management, storage, audio interfaces, and a BLE communication module. Hardware and functional validation confirms reliable neural, cardiac, and vascular signal acquisition, including alpha attenuation response during eyes-open or closed conditions and consistent ECG and PPG morphology. These results establish BrainRead as a versatile platform for continuous, multimodal physiological assessment, suitable for non-clinical tracking with potential applications in clinical settings and research.

title: On Evaluating the Security of Complete Access Protocol of IJTAG Architecture.
abstract: Modern System-on-Chips (SoCs) incorporate a diverse array of on-chip instruments and proprietary data to support functions such as testing, diagnosis, post-silicon debugging, in-field monitoring, authentication, and counterfeit detection. To provide flexible access to these instruments, testing infrastructure such as IEEE Std. 1687 (IJTAG) is embedded into the ICs. However, such broad access can be exploited by adversaries to facilitate side-channel attacks. To address this concern, a complete security protocol has been recently proposed, which aims to protect IJTAG against both internal and external attacks by encrypting the Test Mode Select (TMS) signal, responsible for controlling the JTAG TAP controller, through specialized access software. In this work, a comprehensive security analysis of the IJTAG framework is presented. It is demonstrated that the proposed complete security protocol remains vulnerable to a chosen-plaintext attack initiated by an untrusted tester. The attacker can exploit the communication channel between the tester and the access software to compromise the system. Notably, even under the assumption of a high-security environment, the attack enables successful recovery of the templates used for TMS encryption in under 2 milliseconds. Additionally, we propose a session-bound obfuscation in which all TMS bits are embedded sequentially, yielding strong resistance to the proposed attack.

title: Split Reservoir Capacitor Stacking for Correlated-Level-Shifting in Floating Inverter Amplifiers.
abstract: In this brief, we present a technique to increase the settling speed when correlated-level-shifting (CLS) is used in floating inverter amplifiers (FIA). In dynamic amplifiers like the FIA, CLS is not as effective as it is in static amplifiers. This is because, in an FIA, the transconductance reduces with time during the amplification phase, while CLS requires sufficient transconductance during the latter half of the amplification phase. To boost the transconductance in the latter half of the amplification phase, we propose the following. The reservoir capacitor is split into two equal halves and used in parallel during the first half of the amplification phase. During the latter half, the two capacitors, which are partially discharged, are stacked to boost the gate-source voltage and, hence, the transconductance of the FIA. Compared to earlier works that used a dual reservoir capacitor, the proposed technique has better linearity, without compromising on the settling speed and the power consumption. Simulation results confirm the efficacy of the proposed technique.

title: Improved Query by Humming Using Conformer-based Network with Harmonic-Aware Mechanism.
abstract: Query by Humming (QBH) systems allow users to retrieve music by humming a melody when conventional search information, such as lyrics or song titles, is unavailable. Traditional QBH approaches, which rely on note segmentation, pitch estimation, and symbolic sequence matching, often struggle with pitch instability, tempo variations, and the scarcity of large labeled datasets. To address these challenges, we proposed a conformer-based QBH architecture. As the conformer is effective for speech, we believe that it can also well address the QBH problem. We reformulate QBH as a special case of cover song identification and propose a deep learning-based system that converts audio into high-dimensional embeddings. By performing similarity-based retrieval in the embedding space, our method improves accuracy, scalability, and robustness over conventional pitch-based pipelines.

title: A 16-nm 24.8 Mbps/mJ Utilization-Aware Dynamic Allocation Read Mapping Accelerator for Next-Generation Sequencing.
abstract: This paper presents the first utilization-aware dynamic allocation accelerator for short-read mapping in next-generation sequencing. The BITAP algorithm is employed and optimized to reduce computational complexity while deriving both edit distance and the actual mismatch pattern of the sequence alignment. The proposed architecture integrates a Dynamic BITAP Engine that achieves 95.3% utilization through horizontal and vertical dynamic allocation. Dual-Base Alignment and Exact-Match Detection are incorporated to minimize redundant operations. A novel Banded Backward Searching scheme tailored for the BITAP algorithm further reduces on-chip SRAM usage by 85% through shared state-vector reconstruction with banded scheme. Designed in TSMC 16-nm, the accelerator occupies 0.48 mm2, operates at 526 MHz, and consumes 162 mW, delivering 4.02 Gbps/s throughput and 24.8 Mbps/mJ energy efficiency. It achieves 8.65× area efficiency and 14.33× energy efficiency improvements over state-of-the-art designs while maintaining 99.7% accuracy compared with BWA-MEM. The results demonstrate a scalable and energy-efficient architecture for real-time portable data analysis for genome sequencing.

title: Fixed-Point Implementation Analysis of MLSE Receiver DSP for High-Speed Wireline Transceivers.
abstract: This paper analyzes the fixed-point (FXP) implementation of the maximum-likelihood sequence estimation (MLSE) engine for high-speed PAM-4 wireline transceivers (TRXs). Quantization effects in the ADC/FFE output, branchmetric (BM), and path-metric (PM) computations are systematically evaluated through end-to-end BER simulations at 118Gb/s over a 28.5dB-loss channel. Comprehensive precision sweeps show that insufficient quantization at early DSP stages, particularly in the FFE output and BM computation, causes irreversible BER degradation even when later stages maintain high precision. The analysis identifies the dominant precision bottlenecks and provides quantitative design guidelines for balancing BER performance and hardware efficiency in MLSE receiver DSP implementations for future high-speed wireline transceivers.

title: A Low-Power PWM-ASK Receiver Supporting High Supply Variation Tolerance and High Order Modulation for Wireless Implantable Applications.
abstract: This paper presents a low-power pulse-width modulated amplitude shift keying (PWM-ASK) receiver with high supply variation tolerance for wireless implantable applications. The proposed RC integration-based demodulator eliminates supply dependency, ensuring stable data detection under varying supply voltages. A two-stage integration scheme further enables 4-level PWM-ASK demodulation, doubling data throughput without increasing hardware complexity. Implemented in 28-nm FDSOI CMOS, the receiver occupies 0.0348 mm2and consumes 0.336 μW at 0.7 V while achieving a 20 kbps data rate. Measurement results verify robust operation and reliable data recovery, demonstrating the proposed receiver’s effectiveness for energy-efficient wireless implant systems.

title: Neural Network-Based Contiguous Carrier Aggregation Digital Predistortion Design for Sub-THz Power Amplifier in Baseband Transmitter.
abstract: This work presents the design and evaluation of a neural network based digital predistortion scheme for four-band intra-band contiguous carrier aggregation in sub-THz systems. To define a feasible operation scheme, we investigate the limitations of key circuit components, and propose a system-level transceiver solution for future high-throughput communication. Traditional polynomial-based DPD models suffer from exponential growth in complexity with multiple carriers, making them impractical. By adopting real-valued time-delay neural networks, nonlinear PA behavior and memory effects are effectively modeled with significantly lower complexity. Simulation results show that the proposed DPD significantly improves constellation quality, suppresses AM/AM and AM/PM distortions, and meets the IEEE Std. 802.15.3d transmitter EVM requirement of –22 dB, and achieving an overall data rate of 84.48 Gbps. Hardware implementation in 16 nm FinFET CMOS achieves 330.8 K equivalent gates, 0.098 mm2area, and 75 mW power.

title: ADC-Based Nonlinear Quantization for In-Memory Computing using FeFETs.
abstract: This work presents a hardware-driven nonlinear quantization (NLQ) approach inspired by the current characteristics of ferroelectric FETs (FeFETs) used in in-memory computing (IMC) arrays. The proposed method models the nonlinear transfer behavior of a single-slope ADC interfacing the FeFET-based crossbar, where the quantization levels are redistributed to match the inverse relationship between the FeFET input current and the digital output code. By assigning denser quantization steps near zero current, the ADC effectively provides higher precision in sparse activation regions while reducing the effective resolution for large-weight activations, thereby improving energy efficiency without accuracy loss. To validate this concept, a dedicated PyTorch framework was developed to integrate the nonlinear ADC model directly into the neural inference flow. Simulation results on CIFAR-10 show that the proposed NLQ achieves 85.58% accuracy at 4-bit resolution, compared to 82.99% for uniform quantization, demonstrating that hardware-inspired nonlinear mapping can enhance accuracy while enabling lower-resolution, energy-efficient FeFET-based IMC operation.

title: CLOAQ: Combined Logic and Angle Obfuscation for Quantum Circuits.
abstract: In the realm of quantum computing, quantum circuits serve as essential depictions of quantum algorithms, which are then compiled into executable operations for quantum computations. Quantum compilers are responsible for converting these algorithmic quantum circuits into versions compatible with specific quantum hardware, thus connecting quantum software with hardware. Nevertheless, untrusted quantum compilers present notable threats. They have the potential to result in the theft of quantum circuit designs and jeopardize sensitive intellectual property (IP). In this work, we propose CLOAQ, a quantum circuit obfuscation (QCO) approach that hides the logic and the phase angles of selected gates within the obfuscated quantum circuit. To evaluate the effectiveness of CLOAQ, we sample the input state uniformly from the Hilbert space of all qubits, which is more accurate than prior work that use all-|0〉 inputs. Our results show that CLOAQ benefits from the synergy between logic and phase protections. Compared with prior QCO approaches using only one perspective, the combined method is more resilient to attacks and causes greater functional disruption when the unlocking key is incorrect.

title: LIRL-NoC: Long-Range Link Insertion Using Reinforcement Learning for Network-on-Chips.
abstract: Network-on-Chip (NoC) is a key technology for communication in chip multiprocessors and multiprocessor system-on-chips. However, traffic in Network-on-Chip is often unevenly distributed, which may lead to congestion on certain links while leaving others underutilized. Inserting long-range links into NoC topologies can help balance traffic by diverting packets away from congested regions. However, the effectiveness of this approach strongly depends on the position, length, and combination of these links, which together constitute a large and complex design space. To address this issue, this paper introduces LIRL-NoC, a reinforcement learning-based method for long-range link insertion. LIRL-NoC leverages a graph convolution network to encode the NoC architecture and a deep reinforcement learning agent to effectively explore the extensive design space. In addition, it performs buffer capacity allocation to balance performance against power consumption. Experimental results show that compared to the baseline mesh topology, LIRL-NoC reduces latency by 21.00% at the cost of a 2.25% increase in power consumption; compared to state-of-the-art work, it achieves a 5.59% reduction in latency with similar power consumption.

title: PhySeqForm: A Data-Driven, Physical Synthesis Sequence Former.
abstract: In the flow of digital IC design, physical synthesis optimizes a post-mapping design for subsequent physical design stages. During physical synthesis, netlist and layout information are modified to minimize leakage power while achieving timing closure. In practice, physical synthesis relies on discrete operators like buffer insertion and gate resizing, where the order of operators significantly impacts the optimization outcome. In this paper, we propose PhySeqForm, a data-driven, physical synthesis sequence spawner, which integrates a sampling-based estimation algorithm with a dynamic sequence generation strategy to customize efficient physical synthesis operator sequences. Our implementation outperforms the first-place results of MLCAD Contest 2025 by 6.3%.

title: nanoHEENS: Biomimetic Near-Memory-Computing 16-Core SIMD Processor Node for Evolutive Spiking Neural Networks.
abstract: The design of a digital spiking neural processor (NP) ASIC for biomimetic evolutive applications is reported. The architecture is briefly described, highlighting its fundamental characteristics, namely: Near-Memory Computing (NMC), efficient Single-Instruction Multiple-Data (SIMD) computation, multi-model support, 16-bit precision, axonal delay support and on-the-fly reconfiguration. A sub-mm2, 16-core NP testchip has been designed in 28 nm CMOS and sent to manufacture. A post-implementation simulation, including a controller and two NPs, is shown to demonstrate the system’s correct operation and capabilities.

title: A Unified Quantum Circuit Framework for Grover Search and Quantum Walks in NISQ Cryptanalysis.
abstract: This paper explores the use of quantum search in symmetric cryptanalysis within the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) regime, introducing a unified quantum circuit framework that expresses Grover’s algorithm as a coined quantum walk. This enables a direct comparison of the two approaches, previously treated separately, under a common model of circuital resources and noise. The framework is implemented and tested on cyclic permutations and AES-like primitives. Experiments show that, in the ideal case, the walk exhibits the familiar Grover amplification curve although, under realistic depolarizing and readout noise, the peaks are damped and the optimal number of steps falls below the theoretical value. In the AES examples, the probability of recovering the key remains negligible. Taken together, these results extend earlier analyses and suggest that symmetric encryption maintains classical-level security in the NISQ era of quantum circuits, while also providing a reproducible testbed for future studies.

title: Additive Resource Scaling in Quantum Circuits for Search in Cryptanalysis.
abstract: Quantum search algorithms are often analyzed in idealized, isolated models, yet real hardware and cryptanalytic applications involve communication channels and residual entanglement. We develop a unified circuit framework that models these effects explicitly, introducing a controllable quantum-channel interaction between system and environment registers. The resulting non-isolated circuits exhibit additive time-space behavior, instead of standard multiplicative scaling. We provide circuit schematics, simulation data, and performance visualization demonstrating how a single-qubit environment modifies Grover oscillations and success probability trajectories of cryptographic attacks. The proposed framework connects algorithmic tradeoffs with measurable circuit phenomena, offering a practical methodology for quantum-classical hybrid circuits design.

title: Compact Inverter-Triggered SCR for ESD Protection in Broadband Communication Circuits.
abstract: This work presents a silicon-controlled rectifier (SCR) design optimized for broadband electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection in high-speed communication interfaces. Fabricated in a 0.18-µm CMOS process, the proposed circuit employs a power-clamp-based trigger mechanism to achieve a reduced turn-on voltage without increasing layout complexity. To ensure superior signal transparency and impedance matching, an inductor is integrated above the SCR structure to compensate for the parasitic capacitance from the SCR device. Experimental results confirm that the device has an HBM robustness of up to 2.1 kV and maintains a signal bandwidth of 60 GHz, validating its suitability for advanced communication systems.

title: A 1.12 μJ/pixel Omnidirectional Image Perception Processor Using Planar-figure-based Memory-efficient Icosphere Mapping.
abstract: Omnidirectional vision enables full 360° perception for autonomous and mobile systems but poses severe computational and memory challenges due to irregular spherical data representation and massive neighbor-search operations. Conventional icosphere-based transformers suffer from irregular memory access, large intermediate feature maps, and high external memory access (EMA), which prevent efficient on-chip inference. This paper presents a 1.12 μJ/pixel processor for omnidirectional image perception via memory-efficient icosphere mapping. First, a planar-figure-based line indexing method regularizes the icosphere structure into a 2D addressable form, eliminating 76.7% of memory access and enabling fully on-chip execution. Second, a neighbor search controller dynamically manages boundary-edge cases in which duplicated nodes violate regular access patterns, ensuring continuous dataflow without conditional branching. Finally, 3-core pipelined architecture streams node subsets through each stage to minimize external memory access. Implemented in 28 nm CMOS, the proposed processor achieves 99.26% lower energy consumption and 6.5% lower latency compared to conventional architectures, delivering real-time 360° image perception for mobile and embedded vision systems.

title: A 66.15 TFLOPS/W RRAM-based Near-memory-computing Macro using Log-multiplication and Error-aware Adaptive Adder Structure with 2-D Pipelined CNN Dataflow.
abstract: We propose a low-power floating-point near-memory-computing (FP-NMC) resistive random-access memory (RRAM) macro. RRAM devices are well-suited for weight storage because of their high density and non-volatility. Our design features a lookup table (LUT)-based alignment unit that reduces power consumption during the alignment process and increases zero sparsity through data gating. Furthermore, we implement an error-aware adaptive adder structure that identifies outliers, thereby minimizing hardware overhead in the adder components. To overcome the bottleneck caused by single-row RRAM reads in our design, we introduce a novel two-dimensional (2-D) pipelined convolution neural network (CNN) dataflow that significantly enhances throughput for CNN accelerators. Our design, fabricated using a 40nm process, achieves 66.15 TFLOPS/W while maintaining high accuracy on the CIFAR-10 dataset (VGG-16: 90.26%, ResNet-18: 88.12%), demonstrating its potential for energy-efficient artificial intelligence (AI) accelerations.

title: A 2-GS/s 6-bit 2b/conv. Single-channel SAR ADC with comparator offset calibration in 28-nm CMOS.
abstract: This paper presents a 2 GS/s, 6-bit, single-channel SAR ADC using a 2bit/conversion architecture, implemented in 28-nm CMOS for use as a sub-ADC in time-interleaved systems. By maximizing single-channel speed, the design reduces the number of interleaved paths, easing clock distribution and input loading while lowering overall size and power. With on-chip comparator-offset calibration, the prototype achieves measured 31.98 dB SNDR and 36.84 dB SFDR near Nyquist at 2 GS/s. The ADC core consumes 14.07 mW and occupies 0.0077 mm2, demonstrating a compact, non-interleaved solution for multi-GHz front-ends.

title: High Energy Efficiency TCAM In-Memory Search Architecture with Pre-Determined Short-Circuit Current Cutoff.
abstract: Mismatch-dominated search operations in SRAM-based ternary content-addressable memories (TCAMs) incur excessive short-circuit currents, leading to significant energy overhead in in-memory search (IMS) applications. This paper presents a high-energy-efficiency TCAM architecture that suppresses unnecessary short-circuit currents by disabling invalid or masked conduction paths prior to the search operation. Fabricated in 28-nm CMOS technology, the proposed TCAM achieves a 96% reduction in short-circuit current and an energy efficiency of 1.87 fJ/bit/search at 400 MHz. By further reducing the number of active search lines through position encoding, the proposed design improves the figure-of-merit (FoM) by 65.7%. Measured results demonstrate stable, data-independent energy behavior under mismatch-dominated workloads, making the proposed TCAM well suited for high-speed and energy-efficient IMS applications.

title: A Novel CRP-Space-Extended RO-PUF Based on LFSR and FNV-1a Implemented in 90nm CMOS for IoT Security.
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a 90nm CMOS ring-oscillator physically unclonable function (RO-PUF) that combines an 8-bit Galois linear feedback shift register (LFSR) for challenge diversification with a lightweight Fowler–Noll–Vo hash function version 1a (FNV-1a) post-processing hash. A BufferXOR stage mixes the LFSR output, PUF buffer, and the external challenge to inject nonlinearity and positional entropy before hashing, expanding the effective challenge–response space to 256nfor n-length sequences with minimal overhead. To validate the proposed RO-PUF design, this work presents simulation results based on the TSMC TN90GUTM process, as well as measurement results from fabricated chips. The core design occupies 50,301 μm2, operates at 100 MHz, and consumes 0.854 mW of core power, resulting in an energy efficiency of 12.3 pJ/bit. The PUF passes the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) statistical tests. Statistical quality is near-ideal: the average bit error rate (BER), uniqueness, uniformity, and bit-aliasing of the generated responses are 2.83%, 50.26%, 50.49%, and 49.11%, respectively. These results indicate that the proposed architecture delivers stable, high-entropy responses suitable for ultra-low-power Internet-of-Things (IoT) device authentication.

title: A Compact Low-Voltage and Low-Power Flip-Flop with Static, Contention-Free, and Redundant-Transition-Free Operation.
abstract: This paper presents a compact 22-transistor flip-flop (FF) optimized for low-voltage and low-power operation. By eliminating unnecessary pull-down paths, the proposed FF maintains static and contention-free operation, thereby ensuring reliability in the near-threshold voltage (NTV) region. The reduced transistor count improves area efficiency and lowers leakage current and parasitic capacitance, enhancing both energy efficiency and speed. Furthermore, the design eliminates redundant transitions and suppresses glitches through transistor stacking and the removal of noise paths. Consequently, the proposed FF significantly reduces both dynamic power under various switching activities and static power across a wide range of supply voltages. Pre-layout simulations in a 45-nm CMOS process show that the proposed FF consumes only 2.67 nW at 1.0 V and 10 MHz with 10 % switching activity, representing an 81.7 % reduction compared to conventional transmission gate flip-flops (TGFFs). Monte Carlo simulation results demonstrate stable operation down to 0.4 V. These results indicate that the proposed FF is a highly efficient solution for ultra-low-power compact digital systems.

title: Close-Loop Controlled RC Parameter Damping-Based Multiplier for Wind Farm Equivalent Modeling.
abstract: Equivalent modeling serves as a vital tool for analyzing wind farms, with current multiplication being one of its key methodologies. Addressing the inefficiencies of traditional detailed wind farm models and the insufficient accuracy of existing current multiplication approaches, this paper proposes an adaptive multiplication method (AMM). This method improves upon conventional schemes by employing variable RC damping elements instead of fixed components, combined with a close-loop control algorithm to achieve intelligent dynamic parameter adjustment. Three-phase short-circuit fault experiments were conducted on a wind farm model comprising 25 turbines. Results demonstrate the method’s exceptional tracking capability, achieving a balance between simulation efficiency and model accuracy. This approach holds significant practical promise for wind farm equivalent modeling.

title: An Asynchronous Mixed-Signal Resonate-and-Fire Neuron.
abstract: Analog computing at the edge is an emerging strategy to limit data storage and transmission requirements, as well as energy consumption, and its practical implementation is in its initial stages of development. Translating properties of biological neurons into hardware offers a pathway towards low-power, real-time edge processing. Specifically, resonator neurons offer selectivity to specific frequencies as a potential solution for temporal signal processing. Here, we show a fabricated Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) mixed-signal Resonate-and-Fire (R&F) neuron circuit implementation that emulates the behavior of these neural cells responsible for controlling oscillations within the central nervous system. We integrate the design with asynchronous handshake capabilities, perform comprehensive variability analyses, and characterize its frequency detection functionality. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of large-scale integration within neuromorphic systems, thereby advancing the exploitation of bio-inspired circuits for efficient edge temporal signal processing.

title: Probabilistic-Based Complementary Logic Gate Design.
abstract: When downscaling integrated circuits with a low supply voltage, noise can cause computing errors which decrease the reliability directly. Previous noise-tolerant designs trade too much reliability for area. In this paper, a probabilistic-based complementary logic gate design is proposed. It separates logic "1" and "0" signals into either robust bits and weak bits from the perspective of probability. The design tolerates errors from noise in terms of probability. By only choosing robust bits, the proposed logic gates can generate high quality output signals. Also, a general mapping rule is deduced to allow the idea to be easily implemented automatically within the existing Electronic Design Automation flows.

title: Data-driven Parameter Design Method for Memristive LIF Neuron Circuits.
abstract: Memristive leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron circuits have attracted considerable interest due to their compact size, structural simplicity, and low power consumption. However, existing parameter design methods for such circuits heavily rely on accurate mathematical models of the memristive device, which can be difficult to obtain. This paper presents an experimental data-driven approach for parameter design of memristive LIF neuron circuits. The proposed method begins by applying voltage and current sweeping to the memristors to characterize their static operating ranges and control types based on the Edge of chaos (EOC) definition. Subsequently, an AC small-signal excitation superimposed on a suitable DC bias is applied to analyze the frequency-domain response, enabling the determination of the type and parameters of additional circuit elements required for the neuron. To validate the method, a simple memristor model and its corresponding emulator circuit are implemented, confirming the correctness and feasibility of the proposed design strategy.

title: An 89.3 dB SNDR MASH 1-2 Pipelined SAR ADC Using Stacking FIA with Extended Voltage Domain.
abstract: This work presents a stacking floating inverter amplifier (SFIA) with an extended voltage domain. By leveraging a four-fold current-reuse factor and doubled voltage range, the proposed amplifier achieves higher gain, improved energy-efficiency, better noise performance and increased output swing. By employing a single proposed closed-loop amplifier, the 16x residue integration and 1-order active noise-shaping can be simultaneously realized in a multi-stage-noise-shaping (MASH) successive-approximation register (SAR)-assisted analog-to-digital converter (ADC). Verified by simulation in 65-nm CMOS process, the prototype archives a signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) of 89.3 dB over 0.625-MHz bandwidth (BW) with an over-sampling ratio (OSR) of 8. Under 1.2-V supply voltage, the ADC consumes 0.582 mW and exhibits a Schreier figure of merit (FoMS) of 179.6 dB.

title: Reinforcement-Learning-Based Multiport Circuit Topology Derivation with No Cross Regulation.
abstract: This paper presents a novel methodology that leverages deep reinforcement learning to streamline the design of multi-output converters for renewable energy applications. On the basis of the presented current-source-mode cells, connection principles, and environment construction in this paper, the proposed algorithm will derive multiport converter topologies and identify those featuring extendable port number and no cross regulation. This approach facilitates the integration of various sources and loads, simplifies control schemes, and maintains a straightforward design process. Moreover, by incorporating dense reward features into the reinforcement learning framework, the proposed method ensures effective guidance and optimization of intermediate design progress, thereby improving training efficiency and convergence stability. The reinforcement-learning-based method for deriving converters efficiently and rapidly produces converters with desired functionalities, offering a wide array of choices for progressively intricate new energy supply systems.

title: An RRAM-based Multi-Timescale Spiking Processor with Reconfigurable Neurons.
abstract: Real-world temporal data often exhibit multi-timescale dynamics. Liquid State Machine (LSM), as a type of Spiking Neural Networks, show remarkable ability in processing multi-timescale data with high performance and efficiency. However, LSMs inherently suffer from lack of flexibility caused by the fixed architecture. In this work, we demonstrate a novel LSM architecture for multi-timescale signal processing. This work captures both transient and long-term temporal characteristics in data with multiple timescales through a reconfigurable framework. The key innovation lies in both the algorithmic model with trainable neuron decay constants and physical implementation with resistive random-access-memory (RRAM) array. This work achieves significant benchmarks for edge deployment with RRAM array, delivering 97.6% 5-class ECG signal classification accuracy on the MIT- BIH database. It bridges the gap between algorithm and hardware, enabling effective and hardware-efficient multi-timescale data processing in real-world applications.

title: Efficient Top-k Sorter through Runtime Lane Selection of Priority Queues on a Directed Ring.
abstract: Top-k computation, the process of identifying the k largest or smallest elements from an N-element dataset, serves as a fundamental operation in recommendation systems, data mining, and machine learning. Existing top-k sorters face a fundamental trade-off. Those employing parallel sorting networks achieve high throughput but are prohibitively resource-intensive, thus supporting only small k. Alternatively, those using input-filtering priority queues can handle larger k but are inherently non-scalable and deliver suboptimal performance for small N.This paper presents DirRing-TopK, which employs a ring topology to interconnect priority queues, enabling scalable parallelism. Furthermore, a Min-Max Lane Selection Mechanism is proposed, achieving superior throughput in small-N scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed selection mechanism achieves higher throughput than fixed lane assignment in the most cases. DirRing-TopK achieves a throughput of 33.71 GB/s and when compared to state-of-the-art designs exhibits superior scalability and enhanced capability for large k.

title: Bridging Trust and Efficiency: TEE-Accelerated Nonlinear Evaluation in Multiparty Computing.
abstract: Secure multiparty computation (MPC) enables edge devices to query cloud-hosted models while preserving the privacy of both client data and server parameters. However, current MPC systems rely heavily on communication-intensive primitives—such as oblivious transfer (OT) and Beaver triples—for nonlinear operations, which are often impractical on resource-constrained platforms with limited compute and challenging network conditions. In this work, we propose a trusted execution environment (TEE)-assisted polynomial multiplication scheme that leverages TEEs to optimize the dominant secure-comparison overhead in nonlinear evaluation. Evaluated on a low-end edge profile (500MHz single-core CPU, 256MB RAM), our approach achieves up to 5.82× and 4.00× speedup on SqueezeNet and ResNet-50, resprctiely, compared with state-of-the-art MPC systems such as CryptFlow2 and Cheetah.

title: Efficient Video Compression with Hierarchical Motion Representation and Attentive Compensation.
abstract: The proliferation of high-resolution video applications demands more efficient compression technologies. Existing methods often suffer from inaccurate motion estimation and inadequate temporal modeling. In this paper, we propose a novel framework with two key innovations: a feature-domain motion offset refinement module that corrects alignment errors through residual learning, and an attention-based compensation mechanism that leverages multi-frame references to generate high-quality contextual features, which work synergistically to improve motion accuracy and temporal consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves 7.19% BD-rate gain compared with the lasted neural codec, establishing a novel perspective for video compression.

title: One-Bit DOA Estimation for Partially Calibrated Arrays with Unknown Uncertainties.
abstract: Combining multiple distributed sub-arrays can create an array with a much larger aperture, achieving significant improvement in direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation performance. In this paper, one-bit DOA estimation for partially calibrated arrays (PCAs) is investigated, in the presence of imperfections with unknown inter-subarray displacements and amplitude-phase uncertainty. Toward this end, the DOAs are decoupled with these imperfections, forming a decoupled array signal model after one-bit quantization. Then, based on the group-sparsity (GS) concept, a one-bit sparse representation of array covariance vectors (SRACV) framework is formulated, exploiting information from all sub-arrays jointly. Besides, the pessimistic Cramér–Rao Bound (CRB) for one-bit measurements is derived to provide a benchmark for evaluating the performance. Simulation results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness and improved performance of the proposed method.

title: Live Demonstration: A 1TX/4RX Radar with Frequency-Dimension Virtual Aperture Expansion.
abstract: This demonstration presents a 15/30/60-GHz 1TX/4RX radar chipset with frequency-dimension virtual aperture expansion. By stimulating the radar array with three different frequencies, we diversify electrical distances under a fixed physical distance across antenna elements to expand the virtual aperture. As a proof-of-concept, we demonstrate a single-channel TX chip and a dual-channel RX chip in 65-nm CMOS technology. We use one TX chip and two RX chips to form a 1-TX and 4-RX demonstration board. With only 1 TX and 4 RX, we can achieve 6° angular resolution, which is 4-times better than the conventional 1-TX and 4-RX radar array.

title: TF-MV SwAV++: Subject-Invariant Time-Frequency Prototype Learning for Cross-Subject sEEG Seizure Detection.
abstract: Cross-subject sEEG seizure detection often degrades on unseen subjects due to inter-subject heterogeneity and electrode-layout disparities. We introduce TF-MV SwAV++ (Time–Frequency Multi-View SwAV++), a purely algorithmic, prototype-consistent self-supervised framework that learns subject-invariant seizure representations by coupling (i) multiview, multi-scale consistency across temporal and time–frequency domains, (ii) a lightweight dual-branch backbone, and (iii) three prototype-level mechanisms—adversarial de-identification, prototype uniformity, and cross-modal prototype alignment. On a de-identified hospital sEEG cohort with 33 two-hour recordings (two 10s ictal episodes per recording) from 20 patients (12 male, 8 female), under strict LOSO our method attains AUROC=0.88, AUPRC=0.64, and Balanced Accuracy=0.80, outperforming vanilla SwAV by +8.2/+9.1/+6.4 percentage points and a supervised 1D-TCN by +11.6/+12.7/+8.0. Cross-center zero-shot AUROC reaches 0.84 and improves to 0.86 with light test-time adaptation. Event-level performance achieves Sensitivity=90.7% at 0.18 FP/h. These results indicate that prototype-consistent self-supervision and time–frequency multi-view learning effectively reduce subject bias and significantly improve cross-subject generalization for sEEG seizure detection.

title: A 60-GHz Transformer-Based Broadband 3-way Quadrature-Phase Coupler in 65-nm CMOS.
abstract: This paper proposes and analyzes a transformer-based broadband 3-way quadrature phase coupler implemented using 65nm CMOS process. The proposed passive coupler can split the input signal into three balanced outputs with relative phase of 0°, 90°, and 180°, respectively. Post-layout electromagnetic simulations indicate that the coupler exhibits an insertion loss less than 1.5dB and the power and phase imbalance is less than 0.4dB and 8°, in range of 57GHz to 66GHz, covering the entire 60GHz unlicensed millimetre-wave band. At 60GHz, the three output ports demonstrate a power imbalance of less than 0.1dB and a phase imbalance of less than 0.1°. Furthermore, the relative bandwidth within 1dB power imbalance is 40%. Compared to conventional branch-line couplers and Lange couplers, the proposed design achieves broader 1dB power imbalance bandwidth and lower insertion loss. To the best of authors’ knowledge, this is the first 3-way quadrature phase coupler operating at 60GHz frequency band reported to date.

title: A Battery Management System Applied to Critical Remote Devices, Featuring High Transient Response and Battery-System Separate Charging.
abstract: This paper presents a battery management system (BMS) that extends battery lifespan for long-endurance applications such as satellites, remote IoT sensor nodes, and implantable medical devices. The proposed BMS employs a dual-mode control strategy: a four-switch buck-boost mode with fast load-current feedback for enhanced transient response, and a separated power-path mode employs dedicated paths for the system load and the battery that prevents battery charge-discharge cycling caused by system power fluctuations. The control IC is fabricated in a 0.18 μm BCD process. Simulation results demonstrate that the converter supports a wide input voltage range from 2.7 V to 18 V and an output range from 3 V to 18 V, utilizing a 2.2 μH inductor at a switching frequency of 600 kHz. With the load-current feedback mechanism, output voltage overshoot and current ripple are significantly reduced, achieving a V drop/I step ratio of 0.058 even at moderate switching frequencies. Moreover, the system delivers a maximum load current of 5 A with a peak efficiency of 96.74%.

title: HippNet: A Hippocampus-Inspired Architecture for Spatial Memory and Inference Using CMOS Oscillator Networks.
abstract: We present HippNet, a hippocampus-inspired spatial memory architecture implemented with CMOS oscillator networks. Each map location is represented by an oscillator, and Hebbian-trained couplings are realized through resistive interconnects. A super-harmonic injection enforces bistable phase states, enabling Hopfield-style associative recall in continuous time. Through this mechanism, HippNet reconstructs stored trajectories from partial or random cues and performs path inference in unexplored regions via localized reweighting and boundary anchoring. MATLAB simulations confirm robust trajectory recall and inference, and transistor-level simulations in a 28 nm CMOS process validate circuit feasibility. A 26-node array converges within 6 ns and consumes less than 8 pJ per recall, demonstrating that HippNet is a compact and energy-efficient neuromorphic substrate for spatial memory, inference, and cognitive-map-inspired computation.

title: High-accuracy and Energy-efficient RRAM-based Real-time Object Detection System for Thermal Infrared Imaging Applications.
abstract: The ambiguity of thermal imaging and the complexity of thermal infrared (TIR) object detection hamper conventional processors from accurately and rapidly processing video streams. Integrating analog compute-in-memory (CIM) can substantially reduce energy consumption and latency whereas sacrificing detection accuracy due to the computation errors. To address these issues, this work proposes an RRAM-based real-time TIR object detection system featuring: (1) a salient object detection unit (SODU) and a pre-judgment mechanism to reduce the system latency by skipping redundant computations in trivial pixels and frames; (2) a hardware-software co-optimized RRAM-CIM macro enabling low-power, high-accuracy analog CIM operations; (3) a dual-contrast-multi-pixel scheme in SODU and a temporal fusion module for mitigating the effects of low-quality TIR images and computation errors by spatiotemporal correction. Implemented using a 28 nm RRAM-CIM macro integrated with FPGA, the PCB system achieves 60 fps real-time detection on a self-built 6-class 384×288 TIR video dataset, attaining over 96% recognition accuracy and mIoU above 0.6. The proposed system demonstrates 45× and 12× energy reductions, and 13× and 42× latency improvements compared with GPU and pure FPGA-based counterparts, respectively, highlighting the potential of RRAM-based CIM for efficient edge intelligence in TIR vision systems.

title: HiMARS: High-Performance Inference for Multi-Modal/Model AI Assistant via Runtime Scheduling.
abstract: After years of rapid development, AI techniques have been gradually brought into applications across diverse fields, transforming the landscape of many workflows. One promising application is AI assistant, which consists of multiple multi-modal models. Unlike traditional AI computing, AI assistants exhibit unprecedented inter-model heterogeneity and dynamism at runtime, involving complex dependencies and interactions between models. This unique computing scenario introduces new challenges, including graph modeling, scheduling overhead, and increased optimization complexity, which lead to utilization and contention issues. In this work, we present a comprehensive analysis of the emerging multi-modal/model AI assistant scenarios, highlighting both the challenges and opportunities in this field. Based on our analysis, we propose HiMARS, a runtime scheduling framework for AI assistant applications. Experiments on different application scenarios show that HiMARS can deliver up to 2.1× performance gain, compared with multiple baselines.

title: A 0.1-V Transformer-Based Class-D VCO Achieving 0.9-V Output Swing and >193.8-dBc/Hz FoM at 10-MHz Offset.
abstract: This work presents a compact 0.1-V transformer-based Class-D voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) for ultra-low voltage (ULV) applications. A high start-up loop gain of 10 and a 0.9-V output swing are achieved through a 1:4 transformer with optimized gate biasing, enhancing the VCO’s phase noise (PN), start-up robustness, and drive strength. Fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS process and occupies a core area of 0.075mm2, the prototype achieves a PN of193.8 dBc/Hz, and a FoMA > 205 dBc/Hz at a 10-MHz offset, normalized to a 5-GHz oscillation frequency. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, the measured FoM and FoMA are the best reported among recently published state-of-the-art ULV VCOs.

title: A Multiplication-Free Floating-Point CIM Architecture with a 5-Bit Approximate Squaring Circuit.
abstract: This paper proposes an optimized 5-bit approximate squaring circuit-based, multiplier-free floating-point in-memory computing architecture. Via mathematical transformations, the design converts mantissa multiplication into low-cost squaring operations, eliminating conventional multipliers while retaining high computational precision. The proposed squaring circuit employs a modular combinational logic structure to minimize hardware complexity. Fabricated in a 28 nm CMOS process, the 4 Kb macro operates at 200 MHz. Under FP16 precision, simulation results show a peak energy efficiency of 21.84 TFLOPS/W, with a maximum absolute error of 0.03 and a relative error of 3.07%. These outcomes indicate that the architecture not only significantly improves energy efficiency but also offers a viable solution for high-precision floating-point computing.

title: HOPESim: A Lightweight and Modern C++ based Accelerator Simulation Approach.
abstract: The design of XPU-PIM integrated Domain-Specific Accelerators relies heavily on high-performance simulators. However, existing simulation tools often suffer from limited integration capability and insufficient simulation speed. To address these challenges, this paper proposes HOPESim, a lightweight and fast simulator specifically designed for XPU-PIM accelerators. We introduce a Register Synchronous Simulation Model (RSSM), which abstracts multiple Processing Elements (PEs) and their interconnections into parallel blocks, enabling seamless integration with third-party simulators through a modular structure. A non-global timestamp strategy is proposed to break cycle dependencies between components, while a decoupled lightweight coroutine library leveraging modern C++ features is adopted to enhance large-scale simulation performance. Experimental results demonstrate that HOPESim achieves over 27× speedup compared to RTL simulation while maintaining compatibility with third-party simulation tools.

title: Energy-Efficient Fall Detection Using Conditional Dual-Path Spiking Neural Networks with Hierarchical Temporal Dynamics.
abstract: Falls remain one of the leading causes of injury and mortality worldwide, underscoring the need for accurate and energy-efficient wearable detection systems. Existing deep neural networks achieve high recognition accuracy but require dense, always-on computation that is impractical for continuous monitoring. Meanwhile, current fall detection frameworks process all activities with the same high-resolution pipeline, wasting energy on steady daily motions that dominate most of the time. To address these challenges, we propose a conditional dual-path spiking framework based on Adaptive Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (ALIF) neurons. A steady-state path continuously monitors low-frequency daily activities at reduced sampling, while a transient-response path activates only when high-frequency motion or low-confidence predictions occur. This event-driven design dynamically allocates computation to salient motion periods, ensuring efficient and responsive operation. The proposed model achieves 98.6% overall accuracy on the KFall dataset, while reducing computation by 56.8% compared to dense ANN baselines.

title: Live Demonstration: A Dual-modal Neural Sensing Array System with Back-end Neural Signal Processing.
abstract: This live demonstration shows a dual-modal neural sensing array system with back-end neural signal processing. The implemented system includes a front-end 32×32 pixels LabOn-Chip array and a back-end python-based data sorting and processing engine to examine. Within the array, a dual mode recordings pixels is capable to capture both electrical recording channel and three chemical recording channels, with integrated sensors/electrodes, amplifiers and digitization circuits. The spacing between active pixels is only 100μm. The 1024 electrical recording channels and 3072 chemical recording channels can simultaneously collect electrical and chemical signals for in-vitro brain slice at the sampling rates of 10kHz and 3.3kHz. The back-end data processing engine collect the data, analysis the correlation between recording sites.

title: An Area-Efficient Neural Stimulator Chip Achieving 23V Voltage Compliance by 180nm BCD CMOS process.
abstract: Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) ameliorates pathological neural activity through the delivery of precisely regulated electrical impulses to targeted subcortical structures, thereby modulating aberrant neural circuit function and restoring normative physiological dynamics. One of the design challenges of DBS circuits is to fit the variable impedance of the electrode-tissue interface (ETI) by a high voltage compliance. Traditional neural stimulator ICs try to increase the voltage compliance by using either high-voltage (HV) process or a stacked configuration of standard MOSFETs, which lead to large chip areas or potential transistor breakdown. To address the issue, a current-steering shifter technique is proposed to offer the neural stimulator a high voltage compliance at the cost of a small chip area. The proposed technique is implemented into a neural stimulator chip fabricated in 0.18μm BCD CMOS technology. The measured results show that the proposed chip achieves 23V voltage compliance with 1.77mA maximum stimulation current, which takes a small chip area of only 0.2mm2per channel.

title: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Tracking Control under Multiple Safety Constraints via Linearly Combinable Control Barrier Functions.
abstract: In this paper, we develop a safe tracking control strategy for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), enabling them to perform tracking tasks while avoiding multiple airborne obstacles. The method treats these obstacles as safety constraints for the UAV system and ensures that it remains within the safe set by constructing a novel control barrier function (CBF). Given that the UAV may be subject to multiple safety constraints, we introduce a Lyapunov function as a slack term for the safety conditions to render the CBFs linearly combinable. As a result, the proposed CBFs can be directly combined into a single unified function when handling multiple safety constraints. Simulation results verify the effectiveness and adaptability of the proposed method in environments with multiple airborne obstacles.

title: ICDL: Inverse Compensation Direct Learning with Model-Accelerator Co-Optimization enabling Real-time Inference in Precision Motion Control.
abstract: Neural network-based feedforward (NN-FF) compensation has emerged as a promising solution in precision motion control due to the strong generalization, yet its key pain point is reliance on iterative learning control (ILC)-constructed dataset—constrained by limited answer precision and cumbersome operation. Furthermore, fast and lightweight requirements for real-time inference have never been addressed in prior art. Here, we propose Inverse Compensation Direct Learning (ICDL), directly catching the nonlinear relationships between reference trajectory and output, instead of indirect learning for errors between them, and theoretical analysis confirms zero-error trajectory tracking. Additionally, we develop a lightweight model Causal Dilated Convolution-based Trajectory Predistorter (CDTP), inherently supporting our circuit implementation of a compressed and parallel computing accelerator. For the first time, ICDL-CDTP demonstrates end-to-end real-time validation, achieving a ~20% accuracy improvement over indirect learning, alongside a low latency of 0.32 µs and a power consumption of 0.5 W, outperforming prior NN-FF methods in both efficiency and accuracy.

title: A KT/C-Noise-Cancelled Charge-Sharing Sampling Pipeline ADC Front-End with Parallel Operation Timing and Substrate-Tracking Technique.
abstract: This paper proposes an improved charge-sharing sampling pipeline ADC front-end achieving high conversion rate, low noise and high linearity. The charge-sharing sampling stage integrated with bottom-plate tracking is implemented by introducing a tracking capacitor to facilitate a much smaller CDAC, which alleviates the input driving, shortens the acquisition time and reduces the reference load. Leveraging the replicability of the proposed front-end, an efficient parallel operation timing is introduced to enable multiple circuit modules in each stage of pipeline ADC to operate simultaneously and thus improve the conversion rate. Moreover, the KT/C noise cancellation is achieved while alleviating the constraints on input frequency and amplitude as well as the Auto-Zero bandwidth of residual amplifier. To further improve the charge-sharing sampling linearity, a Substrate-Tracking technique is proposed to suppress the nonlinear variation of parasitic capacitance at the charge-sharing sampling node. The proposed circuit is implemented and verified in 180nm CMOS process, achieving 98.6dB SNDR and 107.2dBc SFDR with a 1.1MHz, 8.8Vpp differential input at 20MSPS sampling rate.

title: A 267-mV input and 122-ns fall time, pre-charged cross-coupled pulse voltage doubler for low-voltage thermoelectric energy harvesting.
abstract: This paper proposes a pre-charged cross-coupled doubler (PCCD) that enhances output voltage and pulse fall time in TEG boosting circuits, while reducing rush-current-induced power loss and waveform degradation observed in the double cross-coupled doubler (DCCD). Simulations demonstrated a 457-mV output from a 267-mV input, with a 122-ns pulse fall time and 3.9 pJ/bit energy, enabling efficient boosting for thermoelectric generators.

title: A Fewer-Cycles, Resource-Efficient Concurrent Calibration Method for Compact Transmon Qubit Control and Readout Circuit.
abstract: To overcome the resource and time bottlenecks of conventional calibration, this paper proposes a resource-efficient, fewer-cycles concurrent calibration method designed for cryogenic ASICs. The core innovation is the introduction of two mutually decoupled metrics, a separability metric (Dsep) for readout optimization and a |1⟩-state probability metric (Pdis) for control optimization. The insensitivity of Dsepto π-gate precision, combined with the independence of Pdisfrom readout distinguishability, enables the control and readout calibration to be performed concurrently. Efficiency is further improved using a dynamic grid mapping algorithm for dimensionality reduction, and simplifying metric calculations via a PCA-inspired approach. Additionally, a simulated annealing (SA) algorithm is incorporated to accelerate the global search for optimal readout parameters. Compared to conventional approaches, our method reduces memory and computational resources by 81% and 50%, respectively, and decreases the calibration cycles from ~108to ~105. Crucially, the concurrent workflow allows for multi-round iterative optimization of control parameters, boosting theoretical gate fidelity by 0.99% while improving readout fidelity to 99.9%. This work presents a path toward autonomous and continuous calibration in large-scale, high-fidelity quantum computers.

title: FireFly-P: FPGA-Accelerated Spiking Neural Network Plasticity for Robust Adaptive Control.
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer a biologically plausible learning mechanism through synaptic plasticity, enabling unsupervised adaptation without the computational overhead of backpropagation. To harness this capability for robotics, this paper presents FireFly-P, an FPGA-based hardware accelerator that implements a novel plasticity algorithm for real-time adaptive control. By leveraging on-chip plasticity, our architecture enhances the network’s generalization, ensuring robust performance in dynamic and unstructured environments. The hardware design achieves an end-to-end latency of just 8 µs for both inference and plasticity updates, enabling rapid adaptation to unseen scenarios. Implemented on a tiny Cmod A7-35T FPGA, FireFly-P consumes only 0.713 W and ∼10K LUTs, making it ideal for power- and resource-constrained embedded robotic platforms. This work demonstrates that hardware-accelerated SNN plasticity is a viable path toward enabling adaptive, low-latency, and energy-efficient control systems.

title: Spatio-Temporal Power Flow Forecasting During Cascading Failure Propagation in Power Systems.
abstract: Accurate power flow forecasting is crucial for enabling timely interventions to prevent cascading failure events from escalating into large-scale outages. In this paper, we propose a spatio-temporal learning model specifically designed for forecasting power flow redistribution during cascading failure events. The model combines a transformer-based temporal encoder with a graph attention network (GAT) to jointly capture the temporal evolution and spatial dependencies within the grid, thereby enhancing robustness under rapidly changing operating conditions. The proposed model is evaluated on the IEEE 118-bus system and compared against several state-of-the-art baselines, demonstrating superior forecasting accuracy across both short-and long-term horizons.

title: Adaptive All-Digital Clock Data Calibration Circuit for Chiplet Interfaces.
abstract: Die-to-Die (D2D) parallel interconnections play a crucial role in data transmission of the chiplet-based system, yet they are confronted with severe clock-data skew and delay mismatch issues. Existing methods primarily rely on phase interpolator structures and additional monitoring channels, which not only increase design complexity and area overhead but also exhibit limited calibration capability under runtime Voltage-Temperature (VT) variations. This paper proposes an adaptive all-digital calibration circuit based on a high-resolution Digitally Controlled Delay Line (DCDL), enabling precise delay adjustment. Furthermore, by designing a dynamic calibration mechanism, the circuit can mitigate the impact of runtime VT variations, thereby significantly enhancing system robustness. Simulation results based on the SMIC 55nm CMOS process demonstrate that the proposed circuit achieves a delay resolution of 2.25 ps. Under VT variations, the dynamic calibration maintains an eye diagram opening of 0.88 UI, representing an improvement of approximately 120% compared to existing schemes.

title: Volumetric Video on Demand System Based on Scalable Spacetime Gaussian Splatting.
abstract: Volumetric video, by offering users an immersive experience, is becoming an important part of future video technologies. The primary challenge is handling the massive data volume of volumetric video representation, which poses significant storage and distribution difficulties. Recent advancements demonstrate that dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) shows promise as an efficient volumetric video representation. However, current dynamic 3DGS-based transmission architectures suffer from two critical shortcomings: (1) fixed-rate representations are ill-suited to cope with fluctuating network conditions, and (2) there are no transmission systems and quality-of-experience (QoE) optimization methods designed for scalable representation. To address these challenges, we first proposes a scalable spacetime Gaussian Splatting representation that leverages the inherent scalability of Gaussian primitives. We progressively organize Gaussian primitives into multiple levels of detail according to their importance, and we apply layer-wise optimization to improve reconstruction fidelity at each quality level. Building on this representation, we further develop a volumetric video-on-demand system that uses a QoE driven utility function to guide the hierarchical transmission of Gaussian primitives. Experimental results demonstrate that our scalable representation achieves superior rate-distortion performance compared to existing methods. The proposed system effectively adapts to network bandwidth fluctuations while attaining significantly higher QoE scores than conventional approaches.

title: A Wavelet-Enhanced Neural Network with Knowledge Distillation for MCU-Based Fingerprint Liveness Detection.
abstract: This paper presents a wavelet-enhanced lightweight neural network with knowledge distillation for MCU-based fingerprint liveness detection (FLD). To address the deployment challenges of CNN-based FLD on resource-limited microcontrollers—large feature maps, high parameters, and long run-time—we integrate discrete wavelet transform (DWT), depthwise separable convolutions, and knowledge distillation. A fast ROI localization using image moments extracts 224×224 patches to standardize inputs and reduce redundancy. Haar-based DWT provides four multi-scale frequency components; low-frequency maps are progressively fused with convolutional features to improve representation at minimal computational cost. The student model is trained with KL-divergence to MobileNetV2 logits, enhancing performance without architectural overhead. On LivDet2015 (excluding Biometrika), the proposed model achieves an average ACE of 3.18% across Crossmatch, GreenBit, and DigitalPersona, competitive with state of the art. It attains the fewest parameters (0.01M), the smallest maximum feature map (61.25K), and fastest GPU inference (0.78 ms), while satisfying typical MCU limits (Flash 1 MB, SRAM 320 KB).

title: SLaB: Sparse-Lowrank-Binary Decomposition for Efficient Large Language Models.
abstract: The rapid growth of large language models (LLMs) presents significant deployment challenges due to their massive computational and memory demands. While model compression, such as network pruning, offers potential solutions, most existing methods often fail to maintain good performance at high compression ratios. To address this, we propose SLaB, a novel framework that decomposes each linear layer weight into three complementary components: a sparse matrix, a low-rank matrix, and a binary matrix. SLaB eliminates the need for retraining and leverages activation-aware pruning scores to guide the decomposition process. Experiments on Llama-family models demonstrate that SLaB achieves state-of-the-art performance, reducing perplexity by up to 36% compared to existing methods at 50% compression and improving accuracy by up to 8.98% over the baseline on zero-shot tasks.

title: A ReMOS Cross-Coupled Charge Pump Achieving 0.62-V VDR and 81.5% Peak PCE for Micro Energy Harvesting Applications.
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable CMOS (ReMOS) cross-coupled charge pump (CCCP) that widens the input voltage (Vin) dynamic range (VDR) while maintaining high power conversion efficiency (PCE) for battery-assisted IoT/WSN applications. Fabricated in 130-nm CMOS technology, the proposed CCCP operates in 5 reconfigurable modes via a transistor reconfigurable method. Conduction efficiency (low ON-resistance) is enhanced in the low-power zone (LPZ) by increasing the effective width of the device dynamically, while leakage is effectively suppressed in the highpower zone (HPZ) by increasing the effective length of the device dynamically. Measured results show 81.5% peak PCE at 400-mV Vininto RL= 500 kΩ and a 623-mV VDR at PCE ≥ 30%. Compared with prior CMOS CCCPs, the proposed prototype demonstrates a wide efficient VDR and competitive peak efficiency.

title: A 8-40 GHz SPDT Switch with 1.24-dB Insertion Loss and 25.5-dBm IP1dB in CMOS SOI.
abstract: This work presents a 8-40 GHz ultra-wideband single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switch in 0.13-μm CMOS SOI technology. Based on the series-shunt structure with negative bias control circuit, the insertion loss, isolation and IP1dBare significantly improved. To broaden the bandwidth without significantly increasing chip area, the structure with series inductor at the RF port is adopted. The measured SPDT switch features 25.5 dBm IP1dBat 24 GHz, lowest insertion loss of 1.24 dB and better than 23.9 dB isolation. Furthermore, based on the series inductor structure, SPDT switch can operate in the frequency range of 8-40 GHz. The active chip area of the designed SPDT switch is compact with a size of only 0.37 × 0.18 mm2.

title: VitaLLM: A Versatile and Tiny Accelerator for Mixed-Precision LLM Inference on Edge Devices.
abstract: We present VitaLLM, a mixed-precision accelerator that enables ternary-weight large language models to run efficiently on edge devices. The design combines two compute cores—a multiplier-free TINT core for ternary–INT projections and a BoothFlex core that reuses a radix-4 Booth datapath for both INT8×INT8 attention and ternary–INT—sustaining utilization without duplicating arrays. A predictive sparse attention mechanism employs a leading-one (LO) surrogate with a comparison-free top-K selector to prune key/value (KV) fetches by roughly 1−K/M for M cached tokens, confining exact attention to K candidates. System-level integration uses head-level pipelining and an absmax-based quantization barrier to standardize cross-core interfaces and overlap nonlinear reductions with linear tiles. A 16nm silicon prototype at 1GHz/0.8V achieves 72.46 tokens/s in decode and 0.88 s prefill (64 tokens) within 0.214 mm2and 120 KB on-chip memory, while reducing KV traffic and improving utilization in ablations. These results demonstrate practical BitNet b1.58 (3B) inference on edge-class platforms and provide a compact blueprint for future mixed-precision LLM accelerators.

title: A High Selectivity 28/39GHz Reconfigurable Dual-Band LNA with sub-10 mW for 5G Applications.
abstract: A reconfigurable dual-band low power low noise amplifier (LNA) for 5G millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) applications is proposed in this paper. The reconfigurable LNA is based on a two-stage amplifier with wideband input matching network. The reconfigurable operating bands are achieved by switchable capacitors. To further suppress the image frequency interference, reconfigurable resonance branches and magnetic–electric hybrid coupling are integrated into the inter-stage and output matching network, which introduce multiple transmission zeros, resulting in a high image rejection ratio. The post-layout results show that the low band has a peak gain of 20.2 dB with a 1 dB flatness within 24-30 GHz and the high band has a peak gain of 21 dB with a 0.8 dB flatness within 37-44 GHz. The dual-band image rejection ratio is better than 27 dBc with an intermediate frequency of 8 GHz. The simulated minimum NF is 2.45/3.05 dB in the low/high band mode. The proposed LNA occupies a compact core size of 0.11 mm2with a DC power consumption of 9.7 mW.

title: A Floating-Point CIM Macro Featuring Asymmetric Exponent Encoding and Adaptive Mantissa Truncation for High-Efficiency AI Edge Computing.
abstract: Floating-Point Computing-in-Memory (FP-CIM) holds significant promise for low-power AI edge computing but is limited by the dynamic range of conventional exponent encoding and the high overhead of mantissa processing. This paper presents a co-optimized architecture featuring an Asymmetric Exponent Encoding (AEE) scheme to expand dynamic range, CAM-enhanced 9T-SRAM for in-situ mantissa computation with exponent-difference-adaptive truncation(E-DAMT) , and a four-cycle sequential Binary-Coded Decimal(BCD) shifter for efficient alignment. Evaluated in 28nm CMOS simulation, the 4Kb macro occupies 0.115mm2, operates at 512MHz (0.9V), and achieves 25.9 TFLOPS/W.

title: Efficient Token Compression for the Understanding and Generation Unified MLLMs.
abstract: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) leverage a single tokenizer for both visual understanding and generation, unifying perception and synthesis within one architecture. However, to effectively perform both generation and comprehension tasks, existing methods typically rely on a large number of tokens for reasoning, which significantly hinders practical applications. Thus, a general token compression strategy is urgently required to improve MLLMs’ efficiency. In this work, we systematically examine how token compression affects model performance. We classify the mainstream tokenizers into three categories according to their different focuses: Semantic-biased, Detail-biased, and Balanced. Then, we apply three potential ways for compression at the beginning, intermediate, and final stages. Through extensive experiments, we get some interesting findings: Detail-biased tokenizers are robust to compression at the input stage but highly sensitive on the final stage, while Balanced tokenizers inherit semantic robustness that mitigates compression degradation for the final representation. These insights inspire us to design a dual-branched Balanced tokenizer, whereas we conduct compression for the Detail-biased branch at the beginning as well as for the Semantic-biased branch at the ending, achieving a win-win effect.

title: DS-eDRAM: Mode-Adaptive Dynamic-Static 2T-1C HZO eDRAM with Temperature-Aware Operation and Shared-Path Sensing for Energy-Efficient SPM in AI Accelerators.
abstract: On-chip memories in AI accelerators demand both high bandwidth and ultra-low idle power, a challenge for conventional SRAM and eDRAM. This paper proposes DS-eDRAM, a 2T-1FeCap memory switching between a high-performance dynamic mode and a near-zero-power non-volatile mode. Featuring temperature-adaptive write/refresh (TWR) and a double-margin sense amplifier (SC-DM SA), the design is validated by a 128Kb test chip in 180nm HZO-CMOS. Performance is projected from a 2Mb macro characterized via 28nm post-layout simulations. Projections show an 83× dynamic DRT improvement, while system-level evaluations of ResNet-20 estimate a 62% total energy saving, enabled by a >99% refresh power reduction.

title: Diffusion Model Based Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithm for High-Level Synthesis Design Space Exploration.
abstract: High-level synthesis (HLS) uses directives like loop unrolling and pipelining to generate hardware with different performance-resource trade-offs. However, the complex interactions between these directives make manual exploration of the vast design space highly inefficient. Automatic design space exploration (DSE) is therefore essential for finding Pareto-optimal configurations. This paper introduces a Diffusion model-based evolutionary algorithm (DEA) for HLS DSE. The DEA framework formulates evolution as a denoising process, organically integrating mutation, selection, and crossover to effectively explore the design space for high-quality solutions. Compared to state-of-the-art methods, DEA demonstrates superior performance: it reduces synthesis runs by 8.59%-28.71%, decreases synthesis runtime by 10.95%-30.11%, and improves the Average Distance to Reference Set (ADRS) metric by 83.09%-92.64%. It also achieves significant speedups of 26X-163X in algorithm runtime. These results establish DEA as a highly efficient and promising approach for HLS design space exploration.

title: A Resource-Efficient and Low-Latency Multi-Tap DFE with Soft-Decision for PAM4 Receiver.
abstract: Prevalent ADC-DSP-based PAM4 receivers make digital equalizer performance critical in AI-driven data centers. Multi-tap decision feedback equalizers (DFEs), however, are severely limited by the trade-off between hardware complexity and data latency. This paper proposes a resource-efficient and low-latency multi-tap DFE architecture, which inserts a soft-decision layer between two DFE stages. A novel low-complexity reliability function based on the Gaussian standard deviation suppresses the error propagation in soft-decision operation. To relax the timing constraint, the time-division technique segments the loop-unrolled (LU) DFE into multiple pipelined stages by inserting registers. Implemented in the SMIC 12 nm process, our architecture, to the best of our knowledge, achieves the best area-latency efficiency among previously published multi-tap DFE architectures and exhibits bit error rate (BER) performance comparable to the state-of-the-art silicon-proven design.

title: Slack-Guided Arbitration for Network-on-Chip Congestion Mitigation in Boolean Processor Array Emulation.
abstract: Boolean Processor Array (BPA) architectures enable efficient emulation of large-scale integrated circuits by mapping circuit netlists onto hardware operators. However, irregular directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) create unpredictable data transfer patterns, causing network congestion that degrades emulation performance. Traditional FIFO arbitration fails to exploit task graph topology, resulting in suboptimal network utilization. We propose a slack-guided arbitration algorithm that dynamically schedules packet transmissions using task dependencies and critical path information computed via backward BFS with iterative refinement. Evaluations on 10 industrial benchmarks and synthetic workloads show average improvements of 6.46% for netlists and 24.82% for highly dense random graph, with up to 27.35% gains in contended scenarios.
