title: A Quad-Core Series-Resonance VCO Enabled by Circular Lsecondary and Stacked Lprimary Achieving 198.9-dBc/Hz FoM at 10MHz.
abstract: This work presents a high figure-of-merit (FoM) quad-core series-resonance (SR) voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO). A circular topology is employed and optimized for the secondary inductor (Lsecondary), achieving a quality factor (Q) of 54, which significantly enhances the overall FoM. Stacked primary inductors (Lprimary) are proposed to achieve stronger magnetic coupling and shorter inter-core connections, thereby improving core synchronization and suppressing phase-noise (PN) degradation caused by core mismatch. In addition, the inductance of Lprimaryis increased due to the stacking topology, enabling a more compact primary capacitor (Cprimary) with less inductor de-Q and a smaller cross-coupled pair with reduced parasitic capacitance. The prototype SR VCO is implemented in 28-nm CMOS technology and occupies a core area of 0.43 mm2. Comprehensive electromagnetic field and post-layout circuit simulations are performed. The 18.4-GHz VCO exhibits -134.9 dBc/Hz PN and 198.5 dBc/Hz FoM at a 1 MHz offset, and -155.3 dBc/Hz PN and 198.9 dBc/Hz FoM at a 10 MHz offset (both normalized to 18 GHz), while consuming 140 mW. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this work achieves the best reported FoM among state-of-the-art SR oscillators.

title: Semantic-aware Sparsity and Adaptive Octree Partition for Efficient Deployment of Point Cloud Models on Edge Devices.
abstract: Point cloud data are widely utilized in autonomous driving and embedded intelligence; however, their inherently large yet highly sparse nature imposes significant challenges on conventional GPU architectures due to low computational and memory efficiency. This paper presents an algorithm-hardware co-optimization framework to enhance deployment efficiency on resource-constrained edge devices. First, a lightweight semantic-aware network is developed to remove more than 90% of redundant background points while maintaining detection accuracy with minimal degradation. Second, an adaptive octree-based partitioning scheme is introduced as a hardware-aware preprocessing step, effectively minimizing memory and computation overhead under resource constraints. Experiments on the KITTI dataset with the SECOND 3D backbone demonstrate up to 36.98× computational speedup and 35.68× memory access speedup over the baseline, with only a 3.6% reduction in 3D AP for the Car category. These results validate the proposed framework’s effectiveness in enabling efficient and real-time point cloud perception on edge devices.

title: A 14.3-ENOB, 600-kHz BW Third-Order NS-SAR ADC with Enhanced EF-CIFF Filter.
abstract: This paper presents a third-order noise-shaping successive approximation register (NS-SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC). An enhanced error-feedback cascade-integrator feedforward (EF-CIFF) architecture is proposed, in which a second-order CIFF filter introduces an additional pole to strengthen the noise-shaping effect. For circuit implementation, the EF-CIFF filter employs a single shared residue amplifier based on a two-stage closed-loop floating-inverter amplifier (FIA), thereby improving system robustness and energy efficiency. Implemented in a 180-nm CMOS process, post-layout simulation results demonstrate that the proposed NS-SAR ADC achieves a signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) of 87.82 dB at an oversampling ratio (OSR) of 8, corresponding to a Schreier figure of merit (FoMs) of 178.5 dB.

title: Strategic Transmission Line Upgrades of Power Systems under High Renewable Penetration.
abstract: This paper aims to enhance the robustness of power systems through upgrading specific transmission lines. We consider the responses of frequency control to renewable generation and derive the fluctuation rates of transmission lines considering the uncertainties of power injection at system buses. Then, we propose a bus criticality index based on the extent of power flow fluctuations across all transmission lines in the network induced by uncertainties at that bus. For comparison, several widely adopted centrality metrics, such as betweenness centrality, flow centrality, and clustering coefficient, are also evaluated for identifying critical transmission lines for potential upgrades. Numerical experiments on the IEEE 118-bus system demonstrate that the proposed index is the most effective in enhancing power system robustness under high penetration of renewable generation.

title: EEschematic: Multimodal-LLM Based AI Agent for Schematic Generation of Analog Circuit.
abstract: Circuit schematics play a crucial role in analog integrated circuit design, serving as the primary medium for human understanding and verification of circuit functionality. While recent large language model (LLM)-based approaches have shown promise in circuit topology generation and device sizing, most rely solely on textual representations such as SPICE netlists, which lack visual interpretability for circuit designers. To address this limitation, we propose EEschematic, an AI agent for automatic analog schematic generation based on a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM). EEschematic integrates textual, visual, and symbolic modalities to translate SPICE netlists into schematic diagrams represented in a human-editable format. The framework uses six analog substructure examples for few-shot placement and a Visual Chain-of-Thought (VCoT) strategy to iteratively refine placement and wiring, enhancing schematic clarity and symmetry. Experimental results on representative analog circuits, including a CMOS inverter, a five-transistor operational transconductance amplifier (5T-OTA), and a telescopic cascode amplifier, demonstrate that EEschematic produces schematics with high visual quality and structural correctness.

title: A Wireless Power Transfer System with Up-to-30% Efficiency Improvement based on Fully-On/Off Global Power Control and Energy Recycling.
abstract: This paper presents a 6.78-MHz wireless power transfer (WPT) system with fully-on/off global power control and energy recycling (ER) control. The proposed fully-on/off global power control reduces the transmission power during receiver (RX) freewheeling mode, thereby improving end-to-end (E2E) efficiency. The ER control provides an additional output branch that recycles resonant energy to reactivate the transmitter (TX), significantly enhancing E2E efficiency while maintaining a low output ripple. Both the TX and RX are implemented in a 180-nm CMOS process. Under a coupling coefficient of 0.2, the system achieves a 5-V regulated output, a maximum output power of 1.5 W, and a peak E2E efficiency of 72.8%. With the proposed ER control, the output ripple remains below 150 mV across the output-power range, representing a 43.6% reduction compared to the case without ER control. The simulated peak efficiency improvement reaches up to 30.6%, and the system shows instant load transient response without noticeable voltage droop or recovery time.

title: Model-Free Predictive Current Control for PMSM Drives Using Extended State Observer.
abstract: This paper addresses permanent-magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) current control under a severe inductance mismatch: the plant inductance abruptly doubles at t = 0.35 s while the controller remains configured with nominal parameters. Three control strategies are evaluated on a unified model-free deadbeat predictive current control (MF-DPCC) backbone with extended-state observer (ESO): (i) baseline ULM–ESO MF-DPCC without parameter learning, (ii) constant-forgetting-factor RLS (CFF-RLS) MF-DPCC, and (iii) variable-forgetting, bias-compensated RLS (VFF-BC-RLS) MF-DPCC with robust gating. Simulink experiments strictly follow InitFcn parameter configurations for reproducibility. Comparative analysis demonstrates that VFF-BC-RLS exhibits superior adaptive damping characteristics, effectively suppressing electromagnetic torque drift and stator current drift following the inductance jump. Results reveal significant improvements in RMS tracking error, torque overshoot reduction, and settling time compared to both CFF-RLS and the baseline approach.

title: FPGA-Based High-Parallelism ORB Feature Extraction Accelerator for Visual SLAM.
abstract: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is vital for robotic navigation, but traditional ORB-SLAM struggles on embedded devices due to high computational complexity and resource demands. This study proposes a hardware-algorithm co-optimized (Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF) ORB feature extraction accelerator to enhance real-time performance. A three-level asynchronous pipeline with an 8 Pixels Per Cycle (8 PPC) parallel strategy and a resource-balanced 8-Detection-to-1-Score design delivers near-linear speedup with minimal additional resources. We improve algorithm-hardware compatibility, using the (Rotationally Symmetric-BRIEF) RS-BRIEF descriptor to quantize rotations with a single (Digital Signal Processor) DSP and a mask-based dual-threshold Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) mechanism for synchronized feature suppression via hardware reuse. Implemented on the Xilinx KR260, our design achieves 1408 FPS in ORB feature extraction, surpassing prior works by 2.81–13.04× in speed and 6.63–18.77× in performance density. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed accelerator for efficient ORB feature extraction in SLAM systems.

title: A Sub-6GHz Balun-LNA Using Dual Feedback Gm-Boosting and Triple Path Noise Canceling Technique.
abstract: A three-stage wideband low-noise amplifier (LNA) is proposed for sub-6GHz applications. This work implements a dual-feedback mechanism, with one path improving the gain and input matching through gm-boosting of the input device, while the other leverages a triode-region PMOS to suppress the second- and third-order nonlinearities. A triple-path noise-canceling is proposed to suppress the channel thermal noise across all main amplifiers. In addition, the balun-LNA provides differential outputs with calibrated amplitude and phase errors. Fabricated in a 55-nm CMOS process, the LNA achieves a simulated gain of 21.7 dB and a 3-dB bandwidth (BW3dB) of 0.83–3.16 GHz. The minimum noise figure (NF) is 1.06 dB, and the output third-order intercept point (OIP3) reaches +11.1 dBm at 1.5 GHz. The circuit consumes 6.6 mW from a 1.2-V supply, and occupies an area of 0.55 × 0.47 mm2including RF pads.

title: Enhanced RDOQ for Dependent Quantization in VVC.
abstract: Versatile Video Coding (VVC) employs a technique known as dependent quantization (DQ), which enhances coding efficiency by flexibly switching quantizers. However, in current VVC encoder implementation, the rate-distortion optimized quantization (RDOQ) does not fully account for the impact of preceding quantizer selection and quantization index on the rate-distortion cost of subsequent coefficients. In this paper, we propose an enhanced RDOQ method that incorporates the impact of the current coefficient’s quantization on the next coefficient’s quantizer choice. By modeling the rate-distortion cost difference between the two quantizers and introducing a penalty term during RDOQ, the method optimizes quantizer transitions without significantly increasing complexity. The experimental results on VTM-23.3 show an average coding efficiency gain of 0.13% for the Y component under the All-Intra configuration and 0.20% under the Random Access configuration, with consistent gains across various video sequences and component types.

title: A Low-noise Adiabatic Energy Recovery Dynamic Comparator with Complementary Gain-Boosting Preamplifier and Push-Pull Latch.
abstract: Adiabatic energy recovery (AER) is a technique to save power in dynamic circuits by driving the transistors softly and recovering energy with a hot clock. This paper reports an AER dynamic comparator that achieves superior noise performance and energy efficiency at 250MHz-2GHz frequency. An AER complementary preamplifier with cross-coupled gain-boosting stage is designed, followed by an adiabatic push-pull strong-arm latch. Post-layout simulations in 12nm FinFET process show that it achieves an input-referred noise (IRN) of 344.4μVrmsand consumes only 24fJ/comparison running at 1GHz. This circuit shows great potential in medium-to-high speed, energy-efficient sampling and quantization circuits.

title: Improving MAC Accuracy of Pre-Aligned Floating-Point CIM Macros for Compound AI with Statistical Group Features.
abstract: Compound AI demonstrates promising potential by achieving comparable performance to full-scale neural network models using multiple smaller-scale models. Deploying compound systems on edge imposes higher demands on hardware. Computing-in-Memory (CIM) macros have shown impressive efficiency improvement, but challenges remain in their floating-point (FP) computation: pre-aligned FP-CIM suffers significant accuracy loss due to mantissa shift when applying to compound system with wide ranges of data distributions; post-aligned FP-CIM with less accuracy loss inserts exponent processing between multiplication and accumulation operations, increasing circuit complexity. This work proposes a two-mode Shift-Count-Aware (SCA) pre-aligned FP-CIM that combines pre-aligned and post-aligned FP for the first time, and improves computation accuracy based on the feature of the operand group. For exponent differences (∆E) of product within 0~21, no mantissa shift is required before multiplication, thereby avoiding multiplication accuracy loss. By adaptively configuring the working mode based on the feature of the operand group, the accuracy is further improved. Verified on ResNet-50, MobileNetV2, and ViT-B with BF16 and the group size of 128, the proposed SCA FP-CIM reduces the Top-1 accuracy loss to 0.16%, 0.37%, and 0.05%, respectively, from 0.47%, 1.41%, and 0.26% accuracy loss of the conventional pre-aligned FP-CIM.

title: A Low-Power Tunable Dynamic-Range ISFET Sensor with In-Pixel Incremental Σ∆ Quantisation.
abstract: This work presents a low-power, tunable dynamic-range ISFET sensor that integrates an in-pixel incremental sigma–delta (Σ∆) analogue-to-digital converter with an auto-reset mechanism and a clocked strong-arm comparator. Implemented in TSMC 65 nm CMOS, the pixel occupies 31 µm×36 µm and contains 23 transistors excluding the ISFET transducer. The sampling frequency is tunable from 2 kHz to 10 MHz, enabling adaptation to biochemical signals with varying amplitudes and time constants. At a 500 kHz sampling rate with a 2 pH input, the design achieves a 51 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and an effective number of bits (ENOB) of 8.2 while consuming 313 nW. The power consumption scales from 32.6 nW at 2 kHz to 5.18 µW at 10 MHz, supporting a measurable dynamic range of up to 10 pH units. The proposed compact and energy-efficient Σ∆ architecture is well suited for in-pixel quantisation in ISFET arrays, enabling real-time biochemical sensing.

title: Hardware-Efficient Image Super-Resolution for Solid-State LiDARs Using Single-Pixel Imaging.
abstract: Macropixel architectures in SPAD-based solid-state LiDARs reduce data bandwidth but significantly degrade spatial resolution. This work proposes a single-pixel-imaging-inspired super-resolution method that sequentially enables individual SPADs within each macropixel and reconstructs per-SPAD histograms using inverse Hadamard transforms. Compared to the brute force approach that sequentially activates SPADs one by one, the proposed approach provides an SNR increase in the histogram by 2.84 for both subframes and the final super-resolved depth map. The proposed approach requires only minimal hardware modification and lightweight arithmetic operations. Experiments on a commercial LiDAR dataset show that the method restores fine spatial structure in both full- and partial-histogram modes without relying on machine learning or external accelerators.

title: A Dual-Hysteresis Synthetic Current Control in a Single-Inductor Multiple-Output Converter for Dynamic Voltage Scaling and 0.02mV/mA Cross Regulation.
abstract: In an AI server power system, the server can trigger a request for the single-inductor multiple-output (SIMO) converter to execute the proposed pre-requested dynamic voltage scaling (DVS) control loop. This approach enables rapid voltage transitions, with an up-tracking rate of 227 mV/μs and a down-tracking rate of 50 mV/μs. To minimize cross-regulation, the system employs a dual-hysteresis synthetic current (DHSC) scheme, which integrates a transient enhanced compensator (TEC) and load-related window tuning (LRWT), achieving 6.4% cross-regulation during DVS tracking and just 0.02 mV/mA during load transients. Furthermore, to suppress electromagnetic interference (EMI), a frequency-locking variable gain amplifier (FL-VGA) maintains a fixed switching frequency of 2 MHz during steady-state operation in continuous conduction mode (CCM).

title: A 30Gb/s/pin PAM3 Single-Ended Transceiver with Crosstalk-Cancelling Coding for Memory Interfaces.
abstract: This paper presents a 30Gb/s/pin three-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM3) single-ended transceiver with a crosstalk cancellation coding scheme for memory interfaces. Designed for PAM3 signaling, the proposed 4D-transition-pattern-free (4DTPF) coding avoids data transition patterns with high crosstalk-induced jitter (CIJ) and thus reduces the severe crosstalk noise in high-density memory links. Impedance and ratio level mismatch (RLM) calibration as well as C-peaking equalizer are employed to further improve the signal integrity. The prototype chip demonstrates an energy efficiency of 1.35pJ/b and an active area of 0.042mm2/lane. Post-layout simulation shows a 46.2% jitter reduction at 30Gb/s/pin for the 5cm printed circuit board (PCB) channels via the 4DTPF coding. And the instrumental measurement also exhibits a jitter reduction around 43% for various data rates.

title: LLIENet: Generative Low-Light Image Enhancement Network Based on Retinex Theory.
abstract: Low-light images often suffer from color distortion, detail loss, and noise due to low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). In this paper, we propose a generative low-light image enhancement network based on Retinex theory, called LLIENet. LLIENet adopts a cross-modal data-driven, end-to-end fully convolutional architecture to achieve unified processing of brightness improvement, noise suppression, and color consistency. LLIENet consists of three core modules: decomposition, enhancement and color recovery. The decomposition module decomposes the image into luminance and reflectance components based on Retinex theory, extracting structural information to maintain detail edges and avoid over-smoothing. The enhancement module applies nonlinear adjustments to the luma component, selectively improving contrast and visibility in dark regions while preventing overexposure. Finally, the color recovery module corrects color casts and restores natural colors by learning a color mapping. A multi-loss optimization strategy ensures robust training and generalization. Experimental results demonstrate that LLIENet achieves superior performance on extremely low-light image datasets, delivering notable improvements in brightness, sharpness, and color fidelity. Moreover, LLIENet provides a viable solution to low-light imaging under challenging illumination conditions.

title: Federated LoRA with Fixed Orthogonal Basis and Dimension-wise Aggregation.
abstract: Federated learning with LoRA is widely used for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models. To address system heterogeneity, current approaches typically assign varying LoRA ranks to clients with different resources. However, these heterogeneous methods suffer from feature dilution and high communication overhead. Furthermore, they often overlook the inconsistent update directions caused by Non-IID data. To overcome these limitations, we propose a simple yet effective federated heterogeneous LoRA approach. Our method treats the LoRA’s A matrix as a fixed orthogonal encoder to pre-align low-rank subspaces. Clients exclusively learn the decoder matrix B, which enables efficient dimensionality aggregation. Experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in both convergence speed and communication efficiency.

title: Revisiting MLLM Token Technology through the Lens of Classical Visual Coding.
abstract: Classical visual coding and Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) token technology share the core objective - maximizing information fidelity while minimizing computational cost. Therefore, this paper reexamines MLLM token technology, including tokenization, token compression, and token reasoning, through the established principles of long-developed visual coding area. From this perspective, we (1) establish a unified formulation bridging token technology and visual coding, enabling a systematic, module-by-module comparative analysis; (2) synthesize bidirectional insights, exploring how visual coding principles can enhance MLLM token techniques' efficiency and robustness, and conversely, how token technology paradigms can inform the design of next-generation semantic visual codecs; (3) prospect for promising future research directions and critical unsolved challenges. In summary, this study presents the first comprehensive and structured technology comparison of MLLM token and visual coding, paving the way for more efficient multimodal models and more powerful visual codecs simultaneously.

title: Impact of AI Data Center Load Dynamics on Blackout Risk.
abstract: The rapid expansion of AI data centers introduces substantial and highly variable power demands to modern power grids, posing new challenges for system resilience. This paper examines how AI-induced load fluctuations affect blackout risk by leveraging a cascading failure simulation framework based on AC power flow and protection dynamics. The simulation results demonstrate that increasing the power demand level of AI data centers significantly elevates the probability of severe blackouts, especially during high-intensity training stages. Furthermore, decentralized deployment of AI data centers and higher generation redundancy are shown to mitigate cascading failure severity. These findings provide quantitative insights for coordinated planning between AI infrastructure siting and grid capacity expansion to enhance system resilience under growing AI electricity demand.

title: A Monolithic 5×14-Channel Cryo-CMOS Multiplexer for Scalable Control of Trapped-Ion Qubits.
abstract: Trapped-ion quantum computing offers a promising path to scalability, which relies on high-fidelity voltage control across hundreds of dynamic electrodes. However, as systems grow in complexity, traditional room-temperature control architectures face severe wiring and signal transmission bottlenecks. This work presents a monolithic cryogenic CMOS multiplexer for scalable dynamic electrode control in trapped-ion quantum processors. Fabricated in the UMC 0.162 µm HV-CMOS process, the chip integrates 210 high-voltage analog switches, enabling 14-to-70 channel multiplexing with three conduction modes: forward, reverse, and compensation. A complementary transmission gate with a resistive negative feedback mechanism stabilizes the effective VGS, suppresses RONvariation, and enhances linearity at 4 K. Measurement results at 4 K demonstrate high signal fidelity (SNR > 61 dB), low crosstalk (4 MHz), and fast switching (< 1 µs), validating its suitability for cryogenic trapped-ion systems.

title: A Linear Analog Resonate-and-Fire Neuron.
abstract: Oscillatory dynamics have recently proven highly effective in machine learning (ML), particularly through State-Space-Models (SSM) that leverage structured linear recurrences for long-range temporal processing. Resonate-and-Fire neurons capture such oscillatory behavior in a spiking framework, offering strong expressivity with sparse event-based communication. While early analog RAF circuits employed nonlinear coupling and suffered from process sensitivity, modern ML practice favors linear recurrence. In this work, we introduce a resonate-and-fire (RAF) neuron, built in 22nm Fully-Depleted Silicon-on-Insulator technology, that aligns with SSM principles while retaining the efficiency of spike-based communication. We analyze its dynamics, linearity, and resilience to Process, Voltage, and Temperature variations, and evaluate its power, performance, and area trade-offs. We map the characteristics of our circuit into a system-level simulation where our RAF neuron is utilized in a keyword-spotting task, showing that its non-idealities do not hinder performance. Our results establish RAF neurons as robust, energy-efficient computational primitives for neuromorphic hardware.

title: An Energy-Efficient 0.56-pJ/cycle AVFS System Based on a Fast Transient Response Digital LDO and a Self-Calibrating Elastic Clock.
abstract: This paper presents an energy-efficient adaptive voltage and frequency scaling (AVFS) system for high-performance processors. The system is designed based on a fast transient response digital low-dropout regulator (DLDO) and a self-calibrating elastic frequency regulator. A fully synthesizable voltage comparator is designed to provide fast voltage resolution via delay differences in DEL cells under different voltage domains. A current-hungry adaptive sampling clock (CKs) generator is designed to provide fast and slow frequencies for voltage comparison and regulation, which effectively reduces the system power. The processor frequency is regulated by a tunable ring oscillator, which is continuously self-calibrated by in-situ critical path timing detection. The proposed system is implemented and simulated in 28-nm CMOS technology, with an area of 0.025 mm2. The system exhibits a voltage droop of 88 mV and a settle time of 15 ns when the load current is increased by 90 mA with a 10 ns edge time. Compared to the baseline design, the droop magnitude and response time are reduced by 30% and 53% separately. The maximum load current and peak current efficiency are 120 mA and 99.8%, respectively. The total energy consumption of the AVFS system is 0.56 pJ/cycle at 0.8 V.

title: DQ-MappingSort: Event-Driven Low-Power Spike-Sorting with Low-Bit Spatio-Temporal Encoding and Adaptive Cluster Mapping.
abstract: High-density microelectrode arrays enable millisecond-scale observation of population spiking bute impose prohibitive bandwidth and power demands on implantable systems. This work presents DQ-MappingSort, an online spike sorting scheme optimized for event-driven and hardware-efficient operation.An always-on delta-quantization(DQ) detector approximates temporal derivatives using ternary comparisons, declaring spikes via short run-length patterns and activating an 8-bit SAR front end only when necessary. Spatio-temporal features are formed by encoding the DQ sequence around the main spike extremum(quantized by an 8-bit SAR ADC) and computing a weighted centroid across neighboring electrodes. The DQ-MappingSort clustering enginge maintains per-cluster population counts, refernce DQ codes and spatial centroids within a 2kB cluster SRAM. Wtih moderate hardware utilization, its spatial L1prefilter and low-bit Manhattan matching enable fast assignment, while a population-weighted periodic mapping merges sparse classes and accelerates centroid convergence.On Neuropixels datasets, the system achieves 99.6% accuracy(≥98% with analog front end + DQ wake-up in loop), and on Quiroga benchmark 99.5% / 95.9%(easy/difficult). The event-gated schedule, relaxed ADC precision and compact memory footprint together support μW-class SoC integration for scalable neural interfaces.

title: A Fully-Integrated Flip-Voltage-Follower LDO With Bootstrap Follower Achieving -52 dB PSRR@1MHz and 3.24 ps FoM.
abstract: This paper presents a fully-integrated flip-voltage-follower (FVF) low dropout regulator (LDO) featuring a bootstrap follower (BF), designed to concurrently optimize power supply rejection ratio (PSRR) and transient response. Along with a supper source follower, the BF reduces the input capacitance and splits the poles, and thus enhances the LDO bandwidth, which is helpful for not only fast transient response but also high PSRR. Besides, a feedforward ripple cancellation (FFRC) is achieved by introducing a RC filter at the gate terminal of the BF’s bias transistor, further enhance the PSRR. Implemented in 65 nm CMOS technology, the proposed LDO occupies 0.06 mm2including 200 pF on-chip capacitance. Measurement results demonstrate that the proposed LDO achieves a 90 mV undershoot for a load transition of 0-20 mA within 2 ns, i.e. 3.24 ps figure-of-merit, and a -52 dB PSRR at 1 MHz.

title: Communication-Aware Routerless NoC Design with Integer Linear Programming Approach.
abstract: As integration density in System-on-Chip (SoC) designs continues to increase, traditional bus-based communication architectures face severe scalability and performance limitations. Routerless Network-on-Chip (NoC) architectures, particularly those based on ring topologies, have emerged as promising alternatives due to their lower area and power overhead. However, most existing designs assume uniform communication patterns, which are inefficient for application-specific scenarios where communication demands are unevenly distributed. This paper presents a communication-aware routerless NoC design framework based on Integer Linear Programming (ILP). The framework constructs optimal ring configurations by minimizing both communication cost and ring length, while satisfying constraints on bandwidth and path diversity.

title: PIM-NoC: A NoC Architecture with In-Router Processing-in-Memory for DNN Acceleration.
abstract: With the widespread use of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) in image recognition and natural language processing, growing model size and complexity increase demands on hardware efficiency. Network-on-Chip (NoC) architectures, valued for scalability and multicore communication, offer strong potential for DNN acceleration. This paper presents PIM-NoC, a novel NoC-based architecture embedding digital processing-in-memory (PIM) units into routers. By replacing part of router buffers with computation-capable PIM arrays, PIM-NoC performs in-network multiplication, improving inference without changing the dataflow. We develop a cycle-accurate simulator in C++ that evaluates LeNet, AlexNet, VGG-16, and MobileNet-V1, showing 28.8%–37.4% speedups on lightweight models and up to 51.9% on computation-intensive networks. After synthesizing it under the TSMC 12nm CMOS technology, PIM-NoC incurs only 0.21% area and 0.29% power overhead compared to the baseline.

title: Efficient Hardware-Oriented Approximation of Mish Activation Function and Its Realization.
abstract: The Mish activation function is widely utilized in fields such as computer vision, natural language processing, and remote sensing recognition. However, its complex nonlinear transcendental function results in significant computational overhead and poses challenges for hardware deployment. Existing piecewise linear or polynomial approximation methods struggle to balance neural network model performance with hardware efficiency, as higher accuracy typically entails greater computational costs. To address this issue, a hardware-friendly Mish approximation method based on piecewise polynomials is proposed. In the method, the optimal interval partitioning and the approximation function for each interval are determined simultaneously, by combining Particle Swarm Optimization and Symbolic Regression methods, with the objective of minimizing error subject to hardware constraints. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to previous Mish approximation methods, this method improves the accuracy of the approximated Mish function by up to 72.2%, leading to an improvement in the accuracy of typical neural network models by up to 1.4%; at the same time, hardware implementation of the proposed approximated Mish function reduces delay by 66.9%, area by 60.5% and power consumption by 80.5%.

title: LMM-VSC: Ultra-Low Bitrate Video Compression with Semantic Understanding.
abstract: Recently, ultra-low bitrate video compression has become a key research field. However, existing video compression methods struggle to maintain adequate performance at ultra-low bitrates. This often manifests itself as compromised perceptual quality, including detail loss, texture blurring, and artifacts, and inconsistency between reconstructed and original videos. To address these challenges, we propose a Large Multimodal Model (LMM) powered Video Semantic Compression (LMM-VSC) method. The framework consists of: (1) a semantic information extractor, which extracts semantics from the input video, (2) a video encoder, which compresses the input video at ultra-low bitrates, and (3) a hybrid decoder, which integrates semantic information with highly compressed bitstreams. Experimental results demonstrate that under ultra-low bitrate conditions, the proposed method reduces the bitrate by 68.4% while maintaining perceptual quality comparable to the H.265 reference software.

title: A Fine-grained Workload Orchestration Framework for Processing-in-Memory Architecture.
abstract: The Processing-in-Memory (PIM) architecture provides a promising option for DNN accelerators with high performance and energy efficiency. While computation and memory access have been the primary focus, its communication performance has not been fully optimized. This work proposes a fine-grained workload orchestration framework that enables computation-communication overlap to enhance the inference performance of DNN workloads on PIM. Firstly, we introduce a simulated annealing-based partitioning algorithm to convert the layer-level workload graph into a finer-grained operation-level graph. Second, we present an operation-level list scheduling algorithm to co-schedule computation and communication tasks. Finally, we develop an integer linear programming algorithm to map the scheduled tasks onto the PIM system. The experimental results reveal that we achieve a 34% and 17% improvement in inference performance compared to the baseline methods.

title: A 16-bit SAR ADC With kT/C Noise Cancellation Using Nested Auto-Zero.
abstract: This paper presents a subrange successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC). A coarse 4.5-bit Flash ADC controls the high five bits of the fine SAR ADC through a 30-bit thermometer code, achieving high-speed subrange operation without compromising precision. A novel kT/C noise cancellation technique is introduced, which combines split-sampling with nested auto-zeroing, utilizing a nested closed-loop structure to rapidly and accurately eliminate kT/C thermal noise, offset, and flicker noise. This approach resolves issues in previous technologies, such as preamplifier saturation and the main path capacitor limiting the SAR ADC conversion speed. In addition, a redundancy-balanced non-binary capacitor array determination method is proposed, ensuring constant settling time while compensating for capacitor mismatch. Together with LSB repetition and SRM techniques, the proposed design effectively reduces the impact of comparator noise. Designed and simulated in a 180-nm CMOS BCD process, the ADC operates at 5 MS/s with a power consumption of 9.042mW and an active area of 0.64 mm2, achieving a SNDR of 91.5 dB and a Schreier FoM of 178.7 dB at Nyquist input.

title: Empirical Study of Process Reward-Guided Model Ensemble for Edge Reasoning.
abstract: Deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) for multi-step reasoning on edge devices faces significant challenges due to limited computational resources and memory constraints. While ensemble methods show promise, fixed resource allocation strategies—such as uniform beam distribution or simple majority voting—often under-utilize heterogeneous model capabilities. We empirically revisit process reward-guided dynamic allocation under resource-constrained settings, examining how step-wise feedback can inform efficient compute distribution across small models (0.5B-1.8B parameters) during beam search. Our study evaluates this approach on GSM8K (grade-school math problems) and MATH500 (competition-level mathematics), achieving 82.56% and 52.2% accuracy respectively. Bootstrap significance testing (10,000 iterations) confirms statistically significant improvements of 0.6% on GSM8K (p=0.038) and 3.6% on MATH500 (p=0.045) compared to fixed allocation baselines. This work provides empirical insights into the trade-offs between coordination overhead and inference quality in small-model ensembles.

title: NMSAcc: An Arch-Decoupled Non-Maximum Suppression Accelerator on Edge Devices.
abstract: Non-maximum suppression (NMS) plays a crucial role in the post-processing stage of many object detection algorithms. It filters out numerous bounding boxes by sequentially performing sorting and iteration. However, the high latency resulting from the serial execution constraint of the algorithm is unacceptable in edge real-time scenarios. To address this issue, we propose the Batched Transformed-NMS algorithm, which achieves high parallelism without accuracy degradation, and then design an architecture-decoupled hardware accelerator (NMSAcc) based on it. NMSAcc reduces execution time through latency overlapping and maintains data access efficiency while reducing redundant storage by leveraging a dynamic sparsity restoration technique. The proposed design is implemented on XC7K410T FPGA and in SMIC 40-nm CMOS technology. Results demonstrate that NMSAcc exhibits extremely low resource utilization (1516 LUTs, 1378 FFs and 1KB BRAMs) and achieves 11.4×/2.3× speedup compared with the CPU/GPU.

title: Self-Supervised Monocular Visual Odometry Based on Multi-View Spatio-Temporal Feature Fusion.
abstract: Learning-based visual odometry (VO) estimates the ego-motion of a camera by leveraging consistent pixel movements between pairs of consecutive image frames. Unlike most existing VOs that only concentrate on a single imaging plane, our method, MultiSTVO, utilizes the physical prior of camera motions to mine and fuse enhanced temporal motion features from multiple views. To simultaneously focus on pixel movements under various views, the Multi-View Spatio-Temporal Feature Enhancement is proposed to fully extract features sensitive to different observation views. In addition, the graph attention network-based Pose Graph Attention Refinement is also designed to achieve refined selection and fusion. This meticulous integration process helps to extract substantial and robust motion information to realize the full utilization of motion features. Experiments on KITTI / Málaga demonstrate the promising performance of MultiSTVO. Compared with state-of-the-art other methods, it achieves improvements of 28.9% and 43.1% in translation and rotation evaluations, respectively.

title: Multi-stage Superpixel-guided Mamba-based Network for Change Detection.
abstract: Remote sensing image change detection relies on accurate modeling of multi-temporal features. Existing Mamba-based methods, however, often suffer from insufficient local information and redundant computations during feature aggregation, leading to inaccurate change boundary predictions. To address these issues, we introduce a superpixel mechanism into the Mamba-based framework and propose a Multi-stage Superpixel-guided Mamba Network for Change Detection (MSPMCD). In the encoder, a superpixel aggregation module extracts structurally consistent region-level features to enhance local and global representations, while a superpixel–pixel association matrix is constructed at the pre-event stage and updated at the post-event stage to preserve bi-temporal correlations. During feature fusion, superpixel-based regional constraints and feature proxy mechanisms enable region-level bi-temporal interaction. In addition, a superpixel consistency loss enforces similarity among pixel predictions within the same superpixel, ensuring intra-superpixel consistency and improving change boundary accuracy. Experiments on multiple public datasets demonstrate that MSPMCD achieves high F1 and IoU scores.

title: Training-Free Adaptation from Visible to Thermal Domain for Learned Image Compression.
abstract: The rapid growth of machine vision applications in specialized domains, such as the thermal domain, highlights the critical need for efficient data compression solutions. Although learned image compression (LIC) models have demonstrated remarkable performance in the visible domain, their generalization capabilities to the non-visible domain remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we present a training-free adaptation framework that enables a pre-trained machine-vision-oriented codec to process thermal images effectively through the addition of lightweight pre- and post-processing modules. These modules are designed to bridge the domain gap by performing channel adaptation and aligning data distribution. Our experiments show that our method preserves both high task fidelity and superior coding efficiency. Specifically, our method achieves an average peak relative accuracy of approximately 98% in the semantic segmentation task and achieves an average 31% BD-rate gain compared to Versatile Video Coding (VVC). The proposed cross-domain adaptation method offers a unified framework for both visible and thermal domain, which is crucial for establishing a unified standard while enabling coverage of multiple modalities through a single deployment.

title: An ISFET based Multi-Modal Low-Power Chopper-Stabilised Analogue Front-End for Wearable Physiological and Sweat Monitoring.
abstract: This paper presents a multi-modal, low-power analogue front-end (AFE) integrating ion-sensitive field-effect transistor (ISFET) and biopotential sensing channels for continuous physiological monitoring in elderly care applications. The proposed capacitively coupled instrumentation amplifier (CCIA) employs a folded-cascode topology with chopper stabilisation and AC coupling to achieve low offset, low flicker noise under stringent power constraints. With a bias current of 15 µA, the amplifier achieves an open-loop gain of 83 dB and a 5 kHz bandwidth, suitable for sub-100 Hz biosignal acquisition. The CCIA achieves a CMRR of 156.4 dB and a noise efficiency factor (NEF) of 7.17. A DC servo loop (DSL) employing a switched-capacitor integrator suppresses electrode offset and ISFET drift, maintaining a DC-free output with a cut-off frequency between 0.23 Hz and 1.1 Hz across gain configurations. The amplifier provides four programmable gains (25, 32, 55, and 110) by adjusting the feedback capacitances, and demonstrates effective 1/f noise suppression through chopping at 2.4 kHz. Implemented in a 65-nm CMOS process, the prototype consumes only 18 µW (without DSL) and occupies an active area of 385 µm × 790 µm. The proposed AFE enables compact, continuous, and non-invasive acquisition of biochemical and bioelectrical signals, supporting intelligent health monitoring and early risk warning for ageing populations.

title: A Sub-50-nW Resistor-Less CMOS Current Reference Utilizing High-PSRR Voltage Biasing.
abstract: This paper presents a low-power, dual-path-trimmed, high-precision 1 μA CMOS current reference with high power and area efficiency. It first generates a proportional-to-absolute-temperature (PTAT) voltage using a novel voltage reference, which is then amplified and fed into a voltage-to-current (V–I) converter to produce a temperature-independent current. The V–I converter employs NMOS transistors biased in saturation. Dual-path trimming enables accurate 1 μA output with a low temperature coefficient. Implemented in 0.18 μm CMOS, the circuit occupies only 0.0056 mm2. Post-layout simulations show that the voltage reference achieves >60 dB power supply rejection ratio (PSRR). After dual-path trimming, the output current remains within ±10% of 1 μA, with an average temperature coefficient of 19.25 ppm/°C and line regulation of 0.08%/V. The core consumes only 46.3 nW, and the total power is 1.079 μW.

title: A Charge-Recovery Half-Bridge Gate Driver With Discrete Feedback Timing Control Achieving Over 70% Power Reduction.
abstract: Dynamic power losses in power switches significantly limit the performance of buck DC-DC converters under light load conditions. Conventional power-switch drivers reduce switching frequency at low loads to mitigate switching losses. However, this method requires more complex loop control. This paper presents a charge-recycled half-bridge driver for gallium nitride high-electron-mobility transistors (GaN HEMTs) operating at 5 MHz, with reduced dynamic losses per switching cycle. The driver utilizes two off-chip inductors to provide drive current with reduced conduction loss. The driving current can be adjusted using 3-bit digital inputs. A fully on-chip discrete feedback timing controller is developed to ensure precise timing, reduce driving losses, and maintain stability across variations in driving current and process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) conditions. This driver is designed using 0.18μm Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS technology and is tested in a 12V-1.8V buck DC-DC converter. Post-simulation analysis shows that switching loss decreases by 73.2% when the peak driving current is set to 1.1A. Additionally, it maintains a rapid slew rate of 6.84V/ns at the half-bridge switching node, with a transition time of less than 5 ns at the GaN HEMT gate.

title: Condition Monitoring of IGBT in Three-Phase Inverters Based on Convolutional Neural Network Algorithm.
abstract: As a key component of a three-phase inverter, the insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) switching device plays a critical role in ensuring system stability, making its state monitoring highly important. However, due to the complex structure of three-phase inverters, many detection methods are unable to monitor the health status of these critical components in real time. To address this issue, this paper proposes an online monitoring method based on a convolutional neural network (CNN) algorithm. This method monitors the status of key components in real time by analyzing output parameters, thereby reducing the number of required sensors and simplifying the monitoring process. The proposed method has been validated through simulation experiments on a three-phase inverter, and the corresponding experimental results are presented.

title: CML-UNet: An Adaptive Spatiotemporal Registration Network for Medical Image Sequences.
abstract: Deformable medical image registration underpins many diagnostic and therapeutic workflows. To address the complex spatiotemporal deformations induced by physiological motion in image sequences such as 4D CT, we propose CML-UNet, a registration network that jointly models large- scale spatial deformations and temporal dynamics. Built on UNet, the network introduces a new recurrent cell, CNN-Vision Mamba with Bidirectional LSTM (CM-BiLSTM), to leverage multi-frequency and time-domain features in concert. Compared with conventional CNN blocks, CM-BiLSTM unifies multi-scale parallel feature extraction and bidirectional long-range temporal modeling, enabling spatiotemporal information from both past and future frames to be jointly encoded at each stage. This design mitigates feature degradation during hierarchical propagation. In addition, we propose Adaptive Frequency Routing (AFR) that fuses high- and low-frequency features adaptively at multiple stages, guided by a frequency prior, thereby improving the overall representation. On two public 4D CT datasets, CML-UNet achieves TREs of 1.15 mm and 0.90 mm, surpassing prior methods and indicating potential for clinical application.

title: FPGA-Accelerated Fully Spectral CNNs for Real-Time Semantic Segmentation.
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are vital for computer vision but suffer from high computational costs. Fully Spectral CNNs mitigate this using Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT) and frequency-domain activations; however, large inputs and spectral self-convolutions cause significant overhead in segmentation tasks. To address this, we propose the Overlapped Partitioning Block Method (OPBM), which divides large images into smaller overlapping blocks, reducing computation while maintaining spectral efficiency. We also design an FPGA-based accelerator with parallel, pipelined computing and performance modeling for further optimization. Experiments on CamVid and Cityscapes show that OPBM achieves a 1.4×~ 2.2× speedup over the full-input spectral baseline with only 0.1% ~ 0.9% accuracy loss, and up to 8.7× speedup over traditional spatial methods, demonstrating outstanding efficiency and scalability.

title: Towards a High-Performance Capacitively Coupled Non-Contact ECG Acquisition System.
abstract: Capacitively coupled non-contact electrodes significantly enhance user comfort by eliminating the need for direct skin contact, thereby demonstrating a notable advantage in long-term biomedical monitoring. However, the inherent coupling capacitance Ccintroduces critical design challenges: it requires ultra-high input impedance Rinand low-noise performance in the front-end readout circuitry to maintain signal fidelity. Moreover, the electrode impedance is highly dependent on the dielectric properties of the coupling materials and the system is susceptible to 50 Hz/60 Hz power-line interference. To address these issues, this paper designs an flexible active electrode customized for non-contact ECG monitoring, achieving an Rinof 32 GΩ and a noise power spectral density (PSD) of 276 ${\text{n}}{{\text{V}}_{{\text{rms}}}}/\sqrt {{\text{Hz}}} $ at 1 Hz. The system incorporates an embedded two stage twin-T notch filter for effective power-line rejection. Furthermore, we systematically evaluated the impact of varying dielectric types and layer thicknesses on signal quality. Experimental results demonstrate that the performance of the cotton fabric medium is superior to that of the PU medium, signal quality demonstrates a negative correlation with the thickness (number of layers) of the cotton fabric.

title: A Reconfigurable Intracranial Multimodal Monitoring ASIC with on-chip PVT-Insensitive Waveform Generator.
abstract: This work presents a reconfigurable multimodal ASIC capable of interfacing with different types of intracranial sensors. The ASIC comprises two main functional blocks: an on-chip waveform generator and a reconfigurable readout circuit. To acquire high waveform consistency, a PVT-robust and area-efficient waveform generator is implemented on chip. By reconfiguring the feedback network to either a switched-capacitor transimpedance amplifier (SC-TIA) or a capacitively coupled instrumentation amplifier (CCIA) topology, the readout circuit flexibly measures voltage, current, and impedance. A current scaling technique has been applied to the front-end of the sensing amplifier, enabling wide dynamic-range current sensing from picoampere to milliampere levels. The proposed ASIC has been validated in the Cadence Virtuoso Environment using a 180-nm CMOS process. The waveform generator produces five programmable voltage profiles with tunable potential window and frequency, while only consumes a power of 17 μW and area of 0.36 mm2. The readout circuit provides a 15-pA resolution and 157-dB dynamic range (DR) for current sensing with >0.999 linearity.

title: MEPUF: A Lightweight and ML-Resistant Strong PUF Integrating Dual-Mode MRAM and Configurable AES for Reliable UAVs.
abstract: The rapid development of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has created an urgent need for secure data storage and reliable communication under strict resource constraints. However, existing UAV hardware still relies on static storage keys that are vulnerable to tampering or theft. This paper presents MEPUF, a lightweight and machine-learning (ML) resistant hardware security primitive, which integrates spin-orbit torque magnetic random access memory (SOT-MRAM) with a configurable advanced encryption standard (AES) core. The MRAM array serves both as memory and an entropy source, while the lightweight AES core retains encryption and enables obfuscation. Experimental results show that MEPUF achieves 50.00% uniqueness, 49.99% uniformity, and 99.28% reliability, passes NIST SP 800-22 tests, and sustains 50% prediction accuracy under advanced ML-attacks. Through complete architectural reuse, this design achieves an exponential challenge-response pair space with minimal overhead. With only 577 LUTs, 260 FFs, and 6 Kb MRAM, MEPUF provides a compact, ML-resilient, and tamper-proof hardware root of trust for next-generation UAV systems in the emerging low-altitude economy.

title: An Efficient Training Method for Memristor-Based Emergent Attractor Network.
abstract: In recent years, accelerating the Hopfield neural network with memristors has been extensively investigated. It is a kind of attractor network model widely applied to solving associative memory and combinatorial optimization problems. These approaches leveraged the strengths of emerging memristors to accelerate matrix-vector multiplication (MVM). However, they overlooked the inherent dynamics of memristors, treating them only as tunable resistors. In our previous work, we proposed a memristor-based emergent attractor network that synergistically harnesses memristor dynamics and fundamental circuit laws, reducing reliance on traditional digital circuits and improving operational speed, area efficiency, and energy efficiency. This work further analyzes the dynamic regulation of network states and introduces a gradient descent algorithm to derive synaptic weights from target attractors. By addressing key limitations of our prior research, this work establishes a complete emergent attractor network model capable of training for target configurations, thereby enhancing robustness and offering superior capacity compared to the classical Hopfield neural network, while demonstrating significant potential for neuromorphic computing and artificial intelligence (AI) applications.

title: ZeroBlade: A Spatial Similarity-aware HiSparse MLP Engine for Neural Volume Rendering.
abstract: 1Neural Volume Rendering (NVR) delivers photorealistic results but suffers from prohibitive multilayer perceptron (MLP) computation, making real-time deployment impractical on graphic processing units (GPUs) or conventional accelerators. To address this challenge, we propose HiSparse, a hierarchical sparsity framework that unifies two complementary schemes: R-Sparse Skipping for majority-zero rows and T-Sparse Encoding for near-zero truncation. By combining coarse- and fine-grained sparsity exploitation, HiSparse minimizes redundant MLP operations while preserving reconstruction fidelity. Built upon this framework, we design ZeroBlade—a spatial similarity-aware sparse MLP engine that implements HiSparse in hardware, enabling both lossless and lossy acceleration with tunable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. ZeroBlade adopts an outer-product computation flow and lightweight control logic to efficiently utilize hierarchical sparsity across NVR workloads. We implement and validate ZeroBlade on the Synopsys HAPS-80 FPGA prototype system. To evaluate its performance, the design is further synthesized using Synopsys Design Compiler under a 28 nm CMOS process. ZeroBlade achieves up to 3.4× speedup with only minor quality degradation. The synthesized core occupies 1.284 mm2 and consumes 102.8 mW at 200 MHz, achieving an energy efficiency of 24.55 TOPS/W and surpassing previous 28 nm sparse accelerators in both power and area efficiency.

title: TNNSAT: A Tree-NN Based Small-Footprint ASR Processor with Scene-Adaptive On-Chip Training.
abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems based on neural networks have shown outstanding performance in human-computer interaction. However, the environmental noise and growing number of speech categories result in degraded classification accuracy, larger model size and increased power consumption, making deployment on edge devices challenging. To address these issues, we propose TNNSAT, a Tree-NN based small footprint ASR processor with two key innovations: 1) An efficient Tree-NN architecture that achieves a 68.8% reduction in data memory and hardware reuse by 95%, while maintaining high accuracy. 2) This work features on-chip adaptive learning that supports real-time fine-tuning, enabling speaker registration and robust adaptation across various noise backgrounds. Fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS process, the prototype system demonstrates a high energy efficiency of 7.7 nJ/word. It can adapt to various noise backgrounds (11 noise types, SNR: 5 dB~clean) and support more keyword categories, achieving a 1.30× ~ 4.49× energy efficiency improvement over state-of-the-art (SOTA) solutions.

title: A Photovoltaic Energy-Harvesting Chip Featuring Self-Adaptive-Monitoring-Time MPPT.
abstract: The widespread deployment of Internet of Things (IoT) applications, such as wearable devices, environmental monitoring, smart homes, logistics tracking, and smart agriculture, has created a growing demand for lightweight devices with extended battery life. This necessitates the adoption of energy-harvesting technologies to resolve the inherent conflict between compact battery size and prolonged operational endurance. Among various energy-harvesting techniques, photovoltaic (PV) energy stands out due to its high energy density in various environment, offering a viable approach to prolong device runtime. However, as the ambient light intensity varies significantly versus environmental conditions, the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) becomes essential to improve the energy-harvesting efficiency. Conventional approaches employ the fractional open circuit voltage (FOCV) method in MPPT, which relies on a fixed predetermined monitoring time, leading to considerable energy loss versus the dynamic illumination variations. In this work, a novel FOCV technique based on self-adaptive monitoring time is proposed for MPPT, which reduces the energy loss of the PV energy-harvesting IC during the MPPT process, thereby effectively improving the overall energy conversion efficiency. Fabricated in 180nm CMOS process, the prototype chip demonstrates a 59.6% reduction in energy loss attributed to MPPT detection compared to conventional methods, achieving a measured peak efficiency of 88.2%.

title: A Non-Recovery Dynamic Range Efficiency Interference Cancellation Approach based on Unlimited Sampling Framework.
abstract: Interference poses a major challenge for Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems, particularly in uplink scenarios. When interference exceeds the dynamic range of analog-to-digital converters (ADCs), clipping distorts signals and degrades interference suppression performance. This paper proposes an interference mitigation framework based on the Unlimited Sampling Framework (USF), which reduces dynamic range demands and power consumption. Radar targets are estimated in the folded domain, and a folded least mean squares (F-LMS) scheme is developed without signal reconstruction. Measurement results indicate that our method improves dynamic range by at least 6dB, with a mean squared error (MSE) increase of no more than 1.5dB. In multi-user scenarios, our approach achieves superior bit error rate (BER) performance compared with the benchmark.

title: An 8-GS/s 8-bit 16×-Interleaved Time-Interpolator-Assisted SAR ADC in 28-nm CMOS.
abstract: The multi-bit/cycle SAR ADC, embedding flash manner in each cycle, can increase the conversion speed by several times compared to a single-bit/cycle SAR ADC. However, comparator and DAC hardware consumption grow exponentially with increasing bits per cycle, causing large input loading and area. This paper proposes a 2.6b/cycle SAR ADC with time-domain interpolation. By employing time interpolator (TIL) between comparators, 2× TD interpolation is realized. Thus, the number of comparators is reduced from 5 to 3, and only one REF-DAC is used, leading to low power consumption, small area, and low kick-back noise. To deal with metastability of TIL, a half-side direct control (HSDC) switching is proposed, which uses only one output code of TIL to control DAC settling and reduces the bit error rate (BER). Another benefit of HSDC is the reduced DAC switching energy. The detection and tolerance blocks are adopted for time offset. As a proof of concept, an 8b 16×-interleaved 2.6b/cycle SAR ADC is fabricated in 28nm CMOS process. The measurement results show that the ADC achieves a 41.9-dB SNDR and 50.8-dB SFDR at near Nyquist input. The total power consumption is 96.5 mW, which corresponds to a Walden FoM of 118.6 fJ/conv.-step.

title: DeepRevelio: Multivariate Time Series Detection for Stealthy IoT Malware via Variable-length Entropy Analysis.
abstract: Attackers are increasingly undermining recent Internet-of-Things (IoT) security advances by exploiting benign applications through various stealth techniques, such as code injections and polymorphic engines. In this work, we design a real-time, non-intrusive secure engine employing deep learning techniques for the effective detection of stealthy tactics. Specifically, our method introduces entropy analysis on multivariate Hardware Performance Counters (HPCs) time series with variable lengths to capture stealthy malware behaviors effectively. We apply 1-D Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP) and logistic regression to enhance network performance, enabling variable-length inputs and outputs processing without changing network parameters and reducing inference model resource requirements. Experimental results demonstrate DeepRevelio’s effectiveness with a 94.57% accuracy in detecting stealthy malware, surpassing the current state-of-the-art works, Deepware and Stealthminer by over 4.29% and 7.29% under the same resource constraints, respectively.

title: Live Demonstration: Real-time Event-based Daily Human Action Recognition with On-chip learning on ANP-I.
abstract: Real-time human action recognition can be used in applications ranging from elderly care monitoring to context-aware smart homes. However, current action recognition systems face two key challenges: 1) privacy risks proposed by RGB cameras, and 2) low recognition accuracy caused by the complexity and dynamic nature of real-world environments. To address these challenges, we propose a real-time even-based daily human action recognition system with on-chip learning ability. The proposed system utilizes an event camera to capture human action, inherently preserving user privacy. Furthermore, we adopt a lower power neuromorphic processor (ANP-I) and leverages its on-chip learning ability to achieve high-accuracy action recognition. The system is evaluated on six actions—standing, running, jumping, bending, sitting and falling, from daily action dataset, and achieved an overall recognition accuracy of 94%.

title: Live Demonstration: A Personalized sEMG Gesture Recognition System Based on On-Chip Learning Neuromorphic Processor.
abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG)-based human machine interface (HMI) is widely used in robotics and immersive virtual reality. However, frequent recalibration is needed to overcome signal variability and drift, which leads to significant accuracy degradation. To address the problem, we introduce a personalized EMG gesture recognition system based on an edge-side on-chip learning neuromorphic processor (ANP-I). By enabling real-time local adaptation, the system eliminates cloud-based retraining, allowing for high-speed personalization and immediate recovery from signal drift. This on-chip learning enables ANP-I to continuously learn a user’s EMG signals for 10 distinct gestures. The proposed solution ensures over 90% accuracy on five hand gestures, providing a reliable edge-based HMI solution.

title: An Injection-Locked Eight Phase Clock Generator with Edge Replacement and Injection Error Calibration Achieving -253.7dB FOMJitter-N.
abstract: This paper presents an injection-locked ring-oscillator-based multi-phase clock generator (MPCG) featuring periodic edge replacement and injection error calibration, simultaneously achieving low jitter and high phase accuracy. By replacing the noisy RO edges with clean reference clock edges, this design provides strong injection strength for effective RO noise suppression even with a low-frequency reference clock. This enables a further reduction in global clock distribution power while maintaining competitive jitter performance. Moreover, a high-accuracy injection error calibrator is proposed to separately calibrate all the non-idealities in the injection-locking process, i.e., frequency error, differential injection mismatch, and delay offset, thereby minimizing phase distortion. Implemented in 28-nm CMOS, the post-simulation results indicate that the proposed MPCG achieves 561 fs RMS jitter, -72 dBc reference spur, and <1° phase mismatch among eight phases, while supporting instant ON/OFF switching for burst-mode operation.

title: Drawbridge: Securing Early-Boot DMA Through IO Bridges.
abstract: Direct memory access (DMA) significantly improves data transfer efficiency between peripherals and main memory, sacrificing security with vulnerabilities such as code injection, memory corruption, and password leakage. Although the IOMMU provides an OS-level protection mechanism, a security gap exists during the early-boot stage before the OS can deploy IOMMU. This paper analyzes the challenges in mitigating DMA attacks during the early-boot stage and proposes Drawbridge as a countermeasure. Drawbridge is located at the IO bridge chips (i.e. south-bridge), processing PCIe packets in real time to monitor peripheral traffic. It can intercept all malicious peripheral bus operations during the early-boot stage and then safely hands over to IOMMU in the later boot stage, effectively mitigating potential peripheral-based attacks. We implemented Drawbridge in a cheap commodity FPGA. Evaluation shows that Drawbridge only incurs minimal hardware modification and very low performance overhead in the SSD benchmark.

title: Neural-Enhanced Hybrid Video Coding: Learning-Based Motion Modeling and Adaptive In-Loop Filtering.
abstract: In recent years, deep learning has shown remarkable success in computer vision, inspiring its application to video coding. Neural network-based tools have demonstrated significant potential for enhancing compression efficiency. This paper presents a hybrid video coding framework that seamlessly integrates neural network-based modules into the conventional coding architecture. A Neural network-based Virtual Reference Frame generation network (NNVRF) is proposed to improve inter prediction by modeling both local and global spatiotemporal contexts, enhancing the quality of reference frames for motion compensation. In addition, a Multi-scale Transformer-based in-loop filter (MTILF) is designed with a hierarchical feature reconstruction backbone that captures cross-scale details while reducing computational complexity. Experimental results show that, under the Random Access configuration, NNVRF and MTILF achieve BD-rate reductions of 6.50% and 9.14% over the VTM-11.0 anchor for the Y component, respectively. When both tools are combined, the framework achieves overall BD-rate savings of 11.87%, 25.51%, and 24.62% for the Y, Cb, and Cr components.

title: An End-to-End Compilation Flow with Reinforcement Learning-Guided Logic Synthesis.
abstract: High-level synthesis (HLS) enables rapid accelerator generation from high-level descriptions but lacks coordination with downstream logic synthesis (LS), limiting optimization for area, performance, and latency. This paper presents CASCADE, a customizable compiler built on MLIR that integrates HLS and LS into a unified optimization framework. CASCADE bridges high-level models to hardware through domain-aware transformations across multiple abstraction levels, including memory layout specialization, operator fusion, and polyhedral analysis. To enhance hardware mapping efficiency, CASCADE introduces a reinforcement learning (RL) guided logic synthesis exploration module that works jointly with the HLS pipeline. This module adjusts synthesis parameters such as mapping strategy, logic restructuring, and technology-specific optimization under different design constraints. By embedding this adaptive exploration into the MLIR pass pipeline, CASCADE automatically tunes transformation sequences and synthesis directives to achieve balanced trade-offs among performance, area, and latency. Experiments show that CASCADE delivers consistent speedups and improved hardware efficiency compared with state-of-the-art system-level compilers across diverse accelerators and workloads.

title: SENTRY-VQA: A Region-Aware Framework for Surveillance Video Quality Assessment.
abstract: Existing generic video quality assessment (VQA) methods, mostly designed for aesthetic-oriented user-generated content, are misaligned with the functional requirements of surveillance. In security footage, perceptual quality is task-driven: the foreground determines analytical accuracy, while the background ensures contextual reliability. To address this functional duality, we introduce SurVQA, the first subjective dataset with decoupled ratings for foreground, background, and global quality. Building upon this, we propose SENTRY-VQA, a no-reference framework with a tri-pathway architecture that models motion, context, and global perception. A gated mutual attention (GMA) module fuses complementary features to enable region-aware, perception-aligned evaluation. SENTRY-VQA achieves SRCC and PLCC values of about 0.90 across all three quality dimensions on SurVQA, surpassing existing approaches and generalizing well to user-generated videos. Together, our dataset and model establish a strong foundation for function-driven video quality assessment in surveillance applications.

title: A 0.277pW/bit Sleep 10T SRAM with Improved Read/Write SNM for Low Leakage Applications.
abstract: SRAM suffers from reduced noise margins at low supply voltages, which limits its leakage reduction capability. This paper proposed a low leakage SRAM cell with high read and write stability. A separate read port is introduced to remove read and write requirement conflicts and read disturbance. A built-in feedback-cutoff mechanism enhances writing by eliminating internal node contention during write operations. The balance between leakage suppression and operational speed is maintained by a multi-threshold design and a pull-down transistors stacking scheme. Simulation results indicate a 99.25% leakage reduction compared with 6T cell at 0.3V. It also offers 2.34×/4.22× improvements in read static noise margin (RSNM)/write margin (WM). The silicon results show a minimum leakage power of 0.277pW/bit at Vmin=0.3V while reaching a minimum access energy of 20.43fJ/bit at 0.36V.

title: A 24.5-29.5GHz Active Bidirectional Phase Shifter With Impedance-Invariant Vector Modulation Achieving 0.29°-1.4° RMS Phase Errors.
abstract: This paper presents an active bidirectional vector-sum phase shifter operating in the 24.5-29.5 GHz frequency range. The proposed phase shifter employs a bidirectional impedance-invariant vector modulation technique to achieve high-precision phase and amplitude control. A bidirectional impedance-invariant variable gain amplifier (BIIVGA) is introduced, which utilizes an equivalent capacitance compensation (ECC) technique to stabilize the input and output impedances of the variable gain amplifier (VGA), thereby effectively suppressing impedance variations caused by changes in control voltage. Fabricated in a 65 nm SOI CMOS process, the bidirectional phase shifter provides a 6-bit phase resolution over a full 360° range. At 27 GHz, the phase shifter achieves an average gain of -9.3 dB in transmit (TX) mode with RMS phase and amplitude errors as low as 0.29° and 0.34 dB, respectively. In receive (RX) mode, the average gain is -10.2 dB, with RMS phase and amplitude errors of 0.40° and 0.60 dB, respectively. The chip occupies a core area of 631 × 544 µm2and consumes 38.2 mW of DC power.

title: A Digital Baseband ASIC Targeting 99.999% Fidelity for Qubit Control and Readout with ROI-based Classification.
abstract: As superconducting qubits scale toward large-scale quantum processors, conventional room-temperature (RT) control and readout architectures introduce interconnect bottlenecks that lead to high latency. To mitigate these issues, a cryogenic circuit architecture is adopted that co-integrates control and readout circuits with qubit chips within a cryo-environment. However, this approach is constrained by refrigerator limitations, which impose stringent requirements on area and power dissipation, while high-fidelity qubit operation necessitates high spectral purity. A 28 nm bulk-CMOS digital baseband ASIC is presented for qubit control and readout, integrating a pulse modulator capable of arbitrary-envelope modulation, a readout receiver with a state classifier for reflectometry-signal preprocessing, and on-chip state classification after offline training. Key techniques include (i) a multiplier-less CORDIC-based Direct Digital Synthesis (DDS) for high-precision pulse shaping, which replaces conventional LUT-based implementations and achieves a 29.2% higher speed and a 41.54% lower area compared to conventional LUT-based DDS, with SFDR > 54dB; (ii) a dynamic Region of Interest (ROI) based data cleansing method that classifies the qubit states from a small data subset, reducing memory requirements by 89% compared to conventional threshold classification approaches, while ensuring fidelity degradation is no more than 0.32% compared to the theoretical limit.

title: A 94.6% Peak-Efficiency 2-Phase 3-Level Buck Converter with Dual-Path Flying Capacitor Balancing and Novel Pre-Charging.
abstract: This paper proposes a 2-phase 3-level Buck converter with dual-path flying capacitor voltage VCFbalancing and flying capacitor pre-charging, which eliminates the requirement for VINpower-on speed, while the main loop adopts current-mode Constant On-time (COT) control based on phase distribution. For VCFbalancing, an on-time TONloop calibration technique is proposed to eliminate TONmismatch and reduce the error of COT self-balancing. Meanwhile, by reusing the pre-charging circuit, a loop-free VCFcalibration path is designed to ensure that VCFis maintained at VIN/2. In addition, a cycle-by-cycle differential inductor current balancing circuit is designed to make the inductor currents of each phase consistent. Designed in a 0.18μm BCD process, this circuit occupies a chip area of 2 × 3mm2. The simulation results show this work achieves a peak efficiency of 94.6% and a 12W maximum output power for 12V to 0.8-2.4V conversion, while the efficiency is maintained at >85% over a wide load range from 1 A to 5 A with a recovery time within 20 μs.

title: RASLL: A Removal Attack on SAT-Resistant Logic Locking.
abstract: Logic locking techniques have emerged as an active defense against intellectual property (IP) infringement in integrated circuit design, yet attacks targeting these techniques have coevolved. This paper proposes RASLL, a novel removal attack that extracts key-connected subcircuits by tracing the output paths of key-driven gates. It then constructs the subcircuit truth tables and derives pairs of key values and input patterns that produce true outputs, enabling recovery of the original circuit. Experimental evaluations based on ISCAS’85 and ISCAS’89 benchmark circuits show that, compared to Boolean satisfiability (SAT)-based attacks, the proposed RASLL recovers the complete set of key values and corresponding input patterns for all the benchmark circuits and reduces the computation time by more than 83%, while conventional removal attacks are inapplicable due to the absence of viable targets. To the best of our knowledge, RASLL represents the first successful attack on a variant of input-dependent key-based logic locking (IDKLL) techniques.

title: Live Demonstration: An Agile FPGA-Overlayed CGRA SoC for High-Efficiency Computing.
abstract: As the demand for efficient and flexible acceleration grows in AI and embedded domains, Coarse-Grained Reconfigurable Array (CGRA) have emerged as a promising architecture that balances performance and reconfigurability. This demo presents an agile CGRA system implemented as an FPGA overlay, together with a fully automated toolchain that compiles high-level inputs into executable binaries. Visitors will experience end-to-end deployment of AI models and high-performance computing kernels on a CGRA-overlayed Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC platform, demonstrating the system’s efficiency, flexibility, and debugging capability.

title: A Highly Linear 5-Level SCDAC with Simple Control Logic for Wideband CTDSMs.
abstract: This paper proposes a high-linearity 5-level switched-capacitor digital-to-analog converters (SCDAC) for continuous-time delta-sigma modulator(CTDSM), which can mitigate nonlinearities caused by mismatch, reference voltage errors, inter symbol interference, clock jitter with extremely low power and delay overhead. The proposed SCDAC overcomes the power consumption and delay issues faced by DEM in wideband applications, and features the simplest control logic among similar designs. In this work, a 3rd-order 2MHz bandwidth CTDSM is designed in a 65nm process to validate the proposed SCDAC, achieving SFDR/SNDR of 92.7dB/ 83.1dB, power consumption of 564 uW, and FOMS/ FOMW of 178.6 dB and 12.1 fJ/conv-step.

title: Audio-Visual Synergy for High-Fidelity Portrait Animation: A Two-Stage Framework with Identity-Motion Disentanglement.
abstract: Portrait animation technology has advanced rapidly in recent years. However, the quality of the animation degrades significantly when the identity in the source image mismatches that in the driving sequence. The primary cause of this degradation is the tight coupling between identity and motion in the learned representations. This entanglement causes the driving motion to carry its own identity features, which, during the feature fusion stage, contaminate the source identity and ultimately impair the quality of the generated sequence. This limitation has prompted the exploration of multi-modal driving. The core challenge is that each modality is inherently incomplete: visual features from frames capture structure but only short-term motion, whereas audio features provide a continuous temporal guide but no structural information. Consequently, any method based on a single modality is fundamentally constrained. To address this, a novel multi-modal portrait animation framework is proposed: it first learns joint and collaborative audio-visual representations via a self-supervised framework incorporating contrastive learning and masked data modeling; second, it employs a dedicated audio-visual motion estimation module to integrate these features and infer accurate facial motion. Experiments demonstrate that our model achieves the state-of-the-art performance on the VoxCeleb and VoxCeleb2 datasets. The code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/AVS-for-Portrait-Animation-85F2.
