title: A 4.7 μW Dual-Phase Front End with Dual-Mode Buffer for Dry-Electrode ECG Acquisition.
abstract: This paper presents a power-efficient dual-phase front end for dry-electrode ECG acquisition, featuring a novel dual-mode common-mode (CM) reuse buffer that enables ultra-low power consumption of 4.7 μW. The proposed architecture comprises two non-overlapping phases: a reset phase for CM interference (CMI) suppression, and an amplification phase for high total common-mode rejection ratio (T-CMRR). The dual-mode buffer operates in high-power mode during the reset phase to drive the common-mode charge pump (CMCP), and switches to low-power mode during the amplification phase to shield capacitance and support the common-mode error amplifier (CMEA), reducing the buffer power by 90% compared to conventional always-on designs. Simulation in 180-nm CMOS, the proposed front end achieves 27 GΩ input impedance, a T-CMRR of 100 dB under 1 MΩ electrode mismatch, and a 20 Vpp CMI tolerance, and consumes only 4.7 μW, which is ten times lower than prior CMCP systems [8].

title: A Highly Linear SAR ADC Architecture with a Correction-Free Hybrid DAC.
abstract: CDAC linearity is one of the precision limitations in a SAR ADC. Given that in the SAR conversion process, the linearity requirement on the MSBs is more stringent than that on the LSBs, this work proposes to use an intrinsically linear 1-bit Delta-Sigma DAC to convert the MSBs and a CDAC without correction to convert the remaining LSBs. In this way, linearity beyond the limitation of CDAC mismatch can be achieved. The impacts of non-linearity and noise of the reconstruction filter in the 1-bit Delta-Sigma DAC are analyzed. An exemplary SAR ADC with the proposed hybrid DAC is implemented at transistor level in a 40nm CMOS process, and the simulation results verify the CDAC mismatch insensitivity of the proposed architecture.

title: A Dual-Loop Multiphase DLL with Charge-Pump-Based Duty Cycle and Phase Error Corrector.
abstract: This paper presents a dual-loop multiphase delay-locked loop (DLL) featuring low duty cycle and phase errors. To maintain a 50% duty cycle and mitigate phase errors at the outputs, a correction loop with charge pump (CP)-based duty cycle corrector (DCC) and phase error corrector (PEC) is proposed. The proposed DCC achieves a duty cycle correction range from 10% to 90% without the need for an auxiliary 50% duty cycle reference clock. In addition, the PEC is designed to mitigate phase errors caused by mismatches in the voltage-controlled delay line (VCDL) and DCC unit. Fabricated in a 130-nm CMOS process, the DLL demonstrates a maximum duty cycle error of 0.4% and a maximum phase error of 0.85° with the input duty cycle from 10% to 90%. It consumes a total power of 2.88 mW.

title: A 64GS/s 8b 64× Time-Interleaved SAR ADC Achieving 33.8dB SNDR at 26GHz in 28nm CMOS.
abstract: This paper presents a 64 GS/s 8-bit time-interleaved (TI) SAR ADC fabricated in 28-nm CMOS. A T-coil input network with two-rank hierarchical samplers extends the input bandwidth while minimizing rank-1 sampling capacitance to relax clocking requirements. Low-jitter, low-skew, and power-efficient sampling clocks are provided by a multi-phase injection-locked ring oscillator (MPILROSC). On-chip foreground analog calibration corrects sub-ADC comparator offsets, whereas residual offset, gain, and timing mismatches are compensated off-chip. The prototype ADC operates from a 0.9/1.8 V supply, achieving 33.8 dB SNDR and 39.8 dB SFDR at 26 GHz, with a core area of 0.319 mm2and a power consumption of 489 mW.

title: A Hybrid CTDT ΔΣ Direct-Digitization Analog Front-End with SAR Quantizer Reuse Zin Boosting.
abstract: This paper presents a 2nd-order hybrid continuous-time discrete-time (CTDT) delta-sigma modulator (ΔΣM) based direct-digitization analog front-end (AFE), employing a successive-approximation-register (SAR) quantizer reuse (SQR) technique to boost the input impedance (Zin). SQR provides a passive Zinboost solution, by reusing the output of the SAR quantizer to neutralize the input current via capacitor digital-to-analog converters (CDACs). Combined with chopping, the proposed AFE achieves low noise and low power consumption simultaneously. The proposed AFE is designed in a 130 nm CMOS process. Under a 1 kHz bandwidth, the peak signal-to-noise ratio (SNDR) is 95.4 dB, and the dynamic range (DR) is 98.24 dB. The SQR increases the DC Zinof the AFE from 1 MΩ to 760 MΩ.

title: A Broadband Ultra-Compact Series Doherty Power Amplifier Achieving Back-Off Efficiency Enhancement over 24-to-38GHz in 65nm Bulk CMOS.
abstract: This paper presents a series Doherty power amplifier (PA) with broadband load modulation. The proposed technique employs a stacked differential common-source auxiliary PA to enable high-efficiency voltage-mode operation at millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) frequencies. Implemented in a 65-nm bulk CMOS technology, the design achieves power back-off efficiency enhancement over 24–38 GHz, while maintaining a Psat–1 dB bandwidth across 28–38 GHz and S21–3 dB bandwidth across 29–39 GHz. Furthermore, it delivers a Psatof 22.9 dBm and a peak PAE of 24.6% at 34 GHz, with a compact core area of only 0.11 mm2.

title: Diff-Band:Bandwidth Estimation in RTC via Diffusion-Based Offline Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Accurate bandwidth estimation is crucial for optimizing quality of experience (QoE) in real-time communication (RTC) systems. While online reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise in adapting to dynamic networks, it suffers from instability, exploration risk, and high deployment cost. Offline RL mitigates these issues by learning from pre-collected trajectories, but existing methods often rely on simplistic architectures and lack efficient policy modeling. We present Diff-Band, the first diffusion-based offline RL framework that formulates bandwidth prediction as a conditional generative process. By learning a deterministic denoising policy model guided by a Q-function, Diff-Band reconstructs high-quality bandwidth decisions from expert trajectories. Experiments on both offline accuracy and online QoE for the RTC bandwidth estimation benchmark show that Diff-Band outperforms the baselines in both aspects, while remaining lightweight for real-time deployment.

title: Near-field Radar Imaging Acceleration Strategy Using Wavelet Transform and Multiscale Processing.
abstract: With the continuous advancement of millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar technology, high-resolution, high-definition and real-time near-field imaging has emerged as a new research objective. However, existing near-field SAR imaging approaches still face numerous challenges. Achieving high-resolution imaging requires optimizing and enhancing radar bandwidth, data acquisition density, and scanning aperture. This, in turn, imposes higher demands on processing speed and parallelism for computational units to enable real-time imaging capabilities. In this paper, we propose a novel multiscale decomposition imaging acceleration strategy based on the wavelet transform, which achieves parallel acceleration across multiple units while reducing the computational cost. By comparing imaging results between this method and previous algorithms using metrics such as SSIM and Jaccard, we demonstrate high-precision, rapid radar imaging of two-dimensional planes with minimal compromise in imaging quality.

title: A Low Noise Bio-potential AFE Achieving 300-mV EDO Tolerance and <20-ms-Settling with VCO-based Full Digital DC Servo Loop.
abstract: This paper presents a capacitive coupled chopper instrumentation amplifier (CCIA) for the bio-potential analog front end (AFE). The proposed AFE employs a VCO-based digital servo loop to enhance electrode DC offset (EDO) tolerance ability and achieve fast setting time without introducing extra input-referred noise (IRN). Implemented in 180nm CMOS process, the proposed AFE achieves ± 300 mV EDO tolerance range and a fast settling time of less than 20 ms, consuming 1.57 µW from a 1 V supply. Furthermore, the IRN from 0.5 Hz to 300 Hz is 0.52 µVrms with a noise efficiency factor (NEF) of 1.32 and power efficiency factor (PEF) of 1.73.

title: Robust Multichannel Autoregressive Parameter Estimation in Spatially Correlated and Impulsive Noise.
abstract: Multichannel autoregressive (MAR) models are widely used in applications such as time series analysis, spectral analysis, biomedical signal processing, etc. The extended instrumental variable (EIV) bias compensation (BC) (EBC) method, which integrates EIV with BC, is an effective method for estimating MAR under temporally white but spatially correlated measurement noise. However, it is known that AR parameter estimation is sensitive to impulsive noise leading to significantly degraded performance. This paper proposes a robust MAR estimation method for batch data using bidirectional consistency detection and iterative sample reweighting. By comparing residuals from forward and backward model fits, outliers are identified and excluded from covariance accumulation. Simulation results demonstrate significant performance improvement of the proposed method over the EIV-BC algorithm under various impulsive noise conditions.

title: Energy-Efficient Neural Video Coding via a High-Throughput Hardware Design for Pointwise Convolution and LUT-based WSiLU.
abstract: Neural video codecs such as DCVC-RT achieve high compression efficiency but typically rely on high-end GPUs, leading to prohibitive power and energy in battery-powered devices. This paper presents an energy-efficient ASIC implementation of two core DCVC-RT primitives: the pointwise (1×1) convolution and the WSiLU activation. Additionally, we introduce a hardware-friendly LUT approximation for WSiLU that preserves coding efficiency, adding only 0.40% BD-Rate when integrated into DCVC-RT. Synthesized in 40 nm at 100 MHz, the design dissipates 238.82 mW and consumes 9.33 pJ per processed sample, yielding up to 731× lower energy than software execution on a high-end GPU of the same pointwise convolution + WSiLU operation. To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first dedicated hardware designs targeting learned video compression frameworks.

title: VFE-CIM: An Algorithm-Hardware Co-Designed Computing-in-Memory Accelerator for Efficient Voxel Feature Encoding in Large-Scale Point Clouds.
abstract: LiDAR-based 3-D perception has become fundamental to autonomous driving, robotics, and UAV systems, where large-scale point-cloud object detection dominates current approaches. The voxel feature encoding (VFE) network, which transforms raw point-cloud data into voxel representations, remains a major bottleneck due to irregular memory access and tightly coupled computation, resulting in significant system latency. In this work, we propose VFE-CIM, an algorithm-hardware co-designed computing-in-memory (CIM) accelerator that addresses the latency challenge at both the algorithm and hardware levels. At the algorithmic level, an anchor-based decoupling and structured-pruning scheme enables streaming-friendly parallelism with minimal accuracy loss. At the hardware level, heterogeneous SRAM-based CIM macros combined with a locality-aware buffer manager minimize data movement and on-chip storage. On the nuScenes dataset, VFE-CIM achieves up to 1.72× speedup over state-of-the-art baselines with less than 0.3 % accuracy degradation.

title: An Efficient Hardware Accelerator for JPEG-AI Image Compression on FPGA.
abstract: JPEG-AI is a recent image compression standardization effort that employs advanced deep learning techniques to achieve superior compression performance. However, the high computational complexity of JPEG-AI poses challenges for real-time applications and the implementation on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose an efficient hardware accelerator for JPEG-AI on FPGA. A dedicated hardware architecture is designed, which includes a processing element array for neural network computations, a vector unit for diverse operations, and an efficient entropy coding module for me-tANS coding. Additionally, we propose a grouped on-chip coding scheme that enables cross-layer kernel fusion, reducing memory bandwidth requirements and improving overall system efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that our implementation achieves a decoding FPS of 74.18 for 720P images and 38.40 for 1080P images, enabling real-time decoding. It achieves a peak performance of 4.12/3.98 TOPS for en/de-coding. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to implement the inference of JPEG-AI models on FPGA in the open literature.

title: Design-Driven Exploration of MOM Capacitors for Capacitive Neural Networks.
abstract: Recent advances in capacitive network design have improved data converter performance; however, parasitic capacitances remain a key limitation to the computational accuracy and energy efficiency of capacitive neural networks. This work presents the design and analysis of a Metal-Oxide-Metal (MOM) based capacitive synapse, investigating parasitic effects across multiple existing interdigitated structures and proposing strategies for scalable, energy-efficient capacitor arrays. We demonstrate and quantify how structural variations and the aggregation of unit capacitors into larger structures introduce additional parasitic capacitances, degrading accuracy and energy efficiency. Under nominal conditions, the post-layout simulation results demonstrate excellent agreement between the analytical and simulated weighted-sum voltage node of a capacitive divider circuit in four structures and across two different methods. In contrast, a 4-bit input capacitive Artificial Neuron (AN) exhibits a deviation of 9–12% due to threshold logic and switch circuit parasitics, while energy consumption varies by approximately 1.2% between structures.

title: CoMe3D: Co-Optimizing Cache-Memory Coupling and Traffic Scheduling for Monolithic 3D Heterogeneous Systems.
abstract: Monolithic 3D (M3D) integration offers substantial vertical bandwidth for heterogeneous systems, yet conventional 2D cache-memory architectures remain constrained by NoC congestion and unified cache inefficiencies across diverse CPU-GPU workloads. This paper presents CoMe3D, a co-designed last-level cache and memory controller (LLC-MC) architecture for M3D platforms. By physically coupling LLC banks with memory controller channels via dense monolithic inter-layer vias (MIVs), CoMe3D forms direct, low-latency data paths that bypass the NoC.To enhance cache utilization, CoMe3D integrates a Dynamic Traffic Dispatch Unit (DTDU) that estimates reuse potential using lightweight address pattern tracking and workload metrics. DTDU dynamically routes traffic to cache or memory based on predicted caching benefit. Implemented on a cycle-accurate Multi2Sim-based M3D platform, CoMe3D achieves up to 2.9× speedup over a 2D baseline, with DTDU contributing up to 6.5% additional performance over conventional LRU. The results highlight CoMe3D’s effectiveness in improving cache efficiency and memory bandwidth utilization under heterogeneous workloads.

title: DocIQ: A Benchmark Dataset and Feature Fusion Network for Document Image Quality Assessment.
abstract: Document image quality assessment (DIQA) is an important component for various applications, including optical character recognition (OCR), document restoration, and the evaluation of document image processing systems. In this paper, we introduce a subjective DIQA dataset DIQA-5000. The DIQA-5000 dataset comprises 5,000 document images, generated by applying multiple document enhancement techniques to 500 real-world images with diverse distortions. Each enhanced image was rated by 15 subjects across three rating dimensions: overall quality, sharpness, and color fidelity. Furthermore, we propose a specialized no-reference DIQA model that exploits document layout features to maintain quality perception at reduced resolutions to lower computational cost. Recognizing that image quality is influenced by both low-level and high-level visual features, we designed a feature fusion module to extract and integrate multi-level features from document images. To generate multi-dimensional scores, our model employs independent quality heads for each dimension to predict score distributions, allowing it to learn distinct aspects of document image quality. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art general-purpose IQA models on both DIQA-5000 and an additional document image dataset focused on OCR accuracy.

title: QT-PUF: Quantum Tunneling Leakage Based PUF for Implantable IoMT Devices.
abstract: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) marks a shift toward decentralized healthcare, enabling continuous monitoring and personalized care through connected wearable and implantable devices. However, ensuring the trust and integrity of these devices themselves remains a major challenge, as physical compromise or counterfeiting can directly endanger patient safety, privacy, and data integrity. This work presents QT-PUF, a gate-tunneling-leakage-based physical unclonable function (PUF) that leverages quantum-mechanical gate leakage resulting from process-induced variations in standard CMOS devices. A differential readout circuit with a pseudo-resistor I-to-V frontend is proposed to convert the picoampere-level leakage variations into digital responses. Unlike existing PUFs such as those based on memory, ring oscillators, or arbiters, which are less suitable for ultralow-power IoMT devices (due to additional circuitry, power overhead, or poor stability), QT-PUF requires no external excitation or stabilization and operates under static bias. Simulation-based measurements for a 65 nm CMOS process demonstrate an entropy of 0.9999998, an FHD of 0.5001, and an average power (energy) consumption of 96.04 nW/bit (19.21 fJ/bit, respectively) at 1.2V and 35°C for the proposed PUF. It operates reliably across 0.9–1.3 V and 0–100°C with an average BER below 0.000163 across 1.0–1.3 V and 10–70°C within the operating conditions of typical implantable devices.

title: CVA6-CFI: A First Glance at RISC-V Control-Flow Integrity Extensions.
abstract: This work presents the first design, integration, and evaluation of the standard RISC-V extensions for Control-Flow Integrity (CFI). The Zicfiss and Zicfilp extensions aim at protecting the execution of a vulnerable program from control-flow hijacking attacks through the implementation of security mechanisms based on shadow stack and landing pad primitives. We introduce two independent and configurable hardware units implementing forward-edge and backward-edge control-flow protection, fully integrated into the open-source CVA6 core. Our design incurs in only 1.0% area overhead when synthesized in 22 nm FDX technology, and up to 15.6% performance overhead based on evaluation with the MiBench automotive benchmark subset. We release the complete implementation as open source.

title: Adaptive AV2 In-loop Filtering via Guided Neural Model with Vectorized Quantization.
abstract: The in-loop filter plays a key role in modern video codecs, improving frame quality by reducing compression artifacts. The next-generation AV2 codec incorporates a series of in-loop filters, e.g., the loop restoration tool, where the dual self-guided filter (DSF) is applied at the final stage to refine the reconstructed frame toward the original. Although prior works attempted to replace DSF with learning-based models for performance improvement, the bitrate increase caused by guided parameters cannot be ignored. Consequently, the current implementation adopts two fixed guidance channels and scalar quantization, which limits its efficacy. To address these issues, this paper proposes a neural self-guided filter for AV2, introducing two key techniques: (i) adaptive selection of the number of guidance channels for higher coding efficiency, and (ii) a vector quantization method for lower bitrate overhead. Our method is general and applicable to any network architecture. Experimental results on a 20 KMACs network demonstrate that it achieves an additional 0.73% (intra) and 0.52% (inter) BD-BR (Bøntegaard Delta Bit Rate) reduction over existing approaches with lower signaling overhead.

title: MOTA: Mapping and Optimization of ASIC-Accelerated TFHE Transciphering.
abstract: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) enables computation on encrypted data without decryption, preserving data confidentiality. However, encrypting large datasets directly with FHE is often impractical due to substantial ciphertext expansion and communication overhead. Transciphering offers an efficient alternative by encrypting data with a lightweight symmetric cipher (e.g., AES) and then converting it into FHE ciphertext on the server. In this work, we propose MOTA, a framework for mapping and optimization of TFHE-friendly AES transciphering on near-memory FHE accelerators. We construct a compound gate library tailored for AES logic, designed for efficient mapping onto TFHE-compatible hardware implementations. We then optimize the circuit representation through an integer linear programming (ILP) formulation built upon the compound gate library. The resulting circuits are mapped to a representative class of programmable near-memory ASIC accelerators, enabling efficient execution with reduced data movement and specialized TFHE control flow. Experimental results demonstrate that MOTA achieves significant improvements in evaluation latency over conventional TFHE-friendly AES designs.

title: Binary Descriptor Learning via Diffusion-based Feature Disentanglement.
abstract: Most of the current works learn binary descriptors by encoding features comprehensively representing complicated image contents. This contradicts the fact that different image applications rely on different levels of visual cues. Encoding all cues is thus not optimal in ensuring compactness and discriminative power. This work proposes a self-supervised method to disentangle image features into multiple levels of visual cues. We hence adaptively generate binary descriptors by encoding and binarizing the most discriminative cues for each task or dataset. The feature disentanglement is conducted based on the proposed conditional diffusion model, where different visual cues are taken as condition features of a certain block in the diffusion model. Based on disentangled features, the entropy-based binarization adopts information entropy to evaluate the discriminative power of different visual cues to a certain task.

title: Time-Area Efficient RNS Base-conversion Architecture for HPS-BFV Homomorphic Encryption using Generalized Solinas Primes.
abstract: The most expensive operation in the BFV Homomorphic Operation scheme is the tensor multiplication part of the homomorphic multiplication, as it requires polynomial multiplication of two ciphertexts without modular reduction four times. The requirement to do it without modular reduction, making the usual technique to accelerate polynomial multiplication, the Number Theoretic Transform and its inverse (NTT/INTT), cannot be used. It means that the complexity cannot be efficiently reduced from O(n2) to O(nlogn), which is very inefficient in hardware settings. The residue number system (RNS) scheme, which allows base conversion, can be used to overcome this problem, which Halevi, Polyakov, and Shoup (HPS) formalize as one of the variants of the BFV scheme. To make NTT/INTT available for polynomial operations in the homomorphic multiplication, the input ciphertexts’ base RNS must be extended from base q = {q0,q1,q2,...qk−1} to base Q, where Q = q ∪ p and p is an additional set of prime moduli p = {p0,p1,p2,...pl−1}. In this paper, we propose an efficient architecture for converting an RNS number from base q to Q, by using a specialized set of prime numbers called the Generalized Solinas Prime applied in sets of q and p. They have a small absolute Hamming weight in the Canonical Signed Digit (CSD) representation, making modular reduction on them easy to do by using add, subtract, and shift operations.

title: Modeling of an All-Mechanical In-Sensor Vibration Classifier Compatible with MEMS Implementation.
abstract: This work explores the feasibility of an electromechanical in-sensor intelligent timeseries classification system implemented using MEMS technology. The proposed architecture integrates, on a single chip, an acceleration sensing layer and a mechanical MEMS neuron for vibration features classification, eliminating the need for any digital interfacing or processing. The computing principles relies on the direct electromechanical coupling between the sensing mass and the MEMS neurons, so that capacitive transduction enables computation within the sensor itself. A neuron performs a mechanical summation of input forces followed by an electrostatically governed nonlinear activation, analogous to neural processing. Simulations of the system's constituent elements, on a toy example of classification task, demonstrate the compatibility of MEMS-based neuromorphic architectures with MEMS sensing units, paving the way for truly integrated mechanical intelligence at the edge.

title: Hardware-Aware Attractor Dynamics in Neuromorphic Systems: Compensating for Device Mismatch through Network Design.
abstract: Attractor networks and their underlying attractor dynamics represent a powerful computational primitive for implementing robust and reliable computations in neuromorphic systems. Their ability to sustain stable activity states makes them especially suitable for neuromorphic processing, where low-power, continuous-time operation is achieved by leveraging the intrinsic physics of analog circuits. However, device mismatch in analog circuits creates parameter variability that challenges traditional mean-field approaches relying on homogeneous population responses. We investigate how parameter variability affects recurrent excitatory-inhibitory networks, demonstrating that device mismatch creates heterogeneous response functions leading to distinct functional neuron classes. Our results show that systematic tuning of recurrent connectivity can compensate for hardware variability and maintain stable attractor states, with compensation strategies validated through successful implementation on mixed-signal analog/digital neuromorphic processors. We extend this framework to networks under periodic perturbations, revealing analogous functional segregation and identifying synaptic time constants as the key parameters distinguishing functional classes. Counterintuitively, networks with compensated variability prove more robust than homogeneous networks when subjected to input degradation. These findings provide practical design principles for implementing reliable attractor dynamics in analog neuromorphic hardware while leveraging parameter heterogeneity as a computational advantage.

title: Three-Independent-Gate Reconfigurable Transistors in 22 nm FDSOI for in-Sensor Time-Domain Mixed-Signal Processing.
abstract: Massively integrated embedded systems capable of sensing, computing, and communicating information are increasingly ubiquitous in modern technology. The high density of devices imposes stringent constraints on energy consumption and cost, particularly for implantable medical devices for point-of-care or drug monitoring. Time-domain mixed-signal processing offers a promising solution by combining the multi-bit information transport of analog computing with the robustness and scalability of digital circuits. Here, we propose Three-Independent-Gate Reconfigurable FETs as an efficient device primitive for time-domain information processing. These devices exhibit intrinsic current-limiting and XNOR functionalities, which can be leveraged to implement a compact voltage-controlled pulse-width modulator, the fundamental building block of this approach. The concept is validated through measurements on fabricated devices based on the 22nm process of GlobalFoundries.

title: Design of a PUF in 600-nm IGZO-TFT Flex-ICs for Secure IoT Applications.
abstract: This thesis presents an innovative Physically Unclonable Function (PUF) implemented in 600 nm Indium-Gallium-Zinc-Oxide (IGZO) Thin-Film Transistor (TFT) technology, fabri- cated on Flexible Integrated Circuits (FlexICs). The proposed architecture takes advantage of device level randomness to produce distinct and repeatable digital responses by utilizing the intrinsic Threshold Voltage (Vth) variability of IGZO TFTs as a physical entropy source. Oxide TFTs, as opposed to conventional Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS)-based implementations, enable compatibility with low temperature, large area and mechanically flexible substrates. This approach is particularly well suited for the next generation of Internet of Things (IoT) and wearable electronic systems. The circuit architecture is based on a differential current comparison mechanism, where two transistor arrays are sequentially evaluated and their discharge characteristics are compared to produce a digital output. Cadence Virtuoso transient simulations were statistically modeled using the experimentally extracted Vth distributions from manu- factured IGZO TFT matrices. This allowed for precise analysis of entropy quality and robustness. Nine National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) SP 800-22 statis- tical test suites were successfully passed by the resultant bitstreams, demonstrating high entropy and consistent randomness across several simulated instances. Additionally, transient noise simulations were performed to assess stability under process and environmental fluctuations. The bitstream demonstrated a Bit Error Ratio (BER) below 0.4% at the optimal comparator threshold. Overall, the proposed IGZO-TFT PUF demonstrates that thin-film oxide electronics can serve as a foundation for intrinsic, low cost and hardware-based security primitives, suitable for secure identification in flexible and large area electronic systems.

title: An Explainable Multi-modal Deep Learning-Enhanced Framework for Automated Depression Detection.
abstract: Depression is a severe mental health disorder requiring early screening for timely intervention and effective treatment. Traditional AI-based detection methods prioritize high classification performance on benchmark datasets but lack transparency in their reasoning processes, rendering their outputs insufficient for the rigorous standards of clinical practice. Although recent efforts have integrated deep learning models with explainability techniques, their predominant focus on elucidating the model’s reasoning process is a critical weakness. This is especially true for multi-modal decision models, where the features themselves may lack practical meaning, rendering explanations that fail to provide real transparency or align with clinicians’ diagnostic reasoning. This misalignment limits their utility in real-world medical settings. To address this gap, this work proposes an explainability-driven framework for multi-modal depression detection that extracts salient evidence across audio, text, and visual modalities, employs a large language model to transform these features into human-readable interpretations, and synthesizes them into a comprehensive clinical judgment with actionable diagnostic insights. Compared with raw predictions, the full framework yields a substantial improvement in human evaluation, with the overall mean rating rising by +2.18 points, corresponding to an approximate 44% relative enhancement in perceived report quality. Additionally, the multi-modal decision fusion can be improved by leveraging our clinically explainable evidence, the F1 can be improved by an absolute F1 gain of 0.05, corresponding to an 6% relative improvement, confirming a notable enhancement in decision reliability.

title: Enhancing Neuromorphic Pattern Selectivity for Imbalanced Data by Adapting from Homeostasis.
abstract: Neuromorphic systems are at the forefront of edgeconstrained learning applications due to their low-power and hardware-efficient mechanisms. Unsupervised neuromorphic algorithms use neurons to represent patterns within the data, commonly embedding homeostatic regulations to balance neuron firing rate and evenly distribute computational load among the available neurons. In real-world scenarios, datasets are often highly imbalanced and identification of rare features becomes critical. In such cases, homeostatic regulation encourages the algorithm to select for majority classes and become blind to the minority class. This work shows that the homeostatic assumption can be adapted within a simple Spiking Neural Network (SNN) classifier, to select for minority patterns under imbalanced, multiclass training conditions. A Base (homeostatic) and Adaptive model are first compared for a simple binary grayscale training set, demonstrating proof-of-concept. These models are then applied to the Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology (MNIST) handwritten digit dataset, under various conditions of imbalance, to demonstrate Adaptive selectivity of Class 4 and Class 9 with only 20% of their original training incidence. Challenges remain in demonstrating blanket performance improvement in terms of precision and recall as datasets become more balanced, emphasizing the criticality of initial model parameters.

title: Hardware and Software Collaborative Energy Management for A Light-powered E-ink Display.
abstract: Existing solutions for self-powered electronic devices typically use fixed-threshold under-voltage lockout (UVLO) circuits for energy buffering and release. Small-scale energy-storage systems often lack sufficient capacity to support large-scale software routines. On the other hand, large-scale energy-storage systems undergo a prolonged startup process. Additionally, a pure hardware-based UVLO lacks the capabilities of energy awareness and adaptivity. This paper introduces a hardware-software collaborative energy management (EM) scheme and validates this EM scheme using a self-powered E-ink (SP-Eink) display. At the hardware level, an energy buffer-release (EBR) circuit is utilized. This circuit provides two hardware-defined on/off thresholds. At the software level, an adaptive energy managemen (AEM) approach is designed. This approach achieves two software-tunable power-good and power-warning thresholds. The additional thresholds are created by polling the state of charge (SoC) through analog-to-digital converter (ADC) sampling. By leveraging the collaboration between the engineered hardware circuit and software routines, a SP-Eink node was developed. This SP-Eink node is also capable of bidirectionally exchanging information with a host PC. The proposed design offers a practical design guideline for the development of sustainable ambient Internet of Things (IoT) systems.

title: MX-SE: Microscaling Data Format with Super Exponent for AI edge computing.
abstract: The Microscaling (MX) format shows great potential for energy-efficient AI edge computing. However, its limited intra-block dynamic range causes significant quantization errors when processing outlier activations and weights. This paper proposes a novel MX format with a super-exponent mechanism, which improves tolerance to outliers and mitigates accuracy loss from quantization. In addition, an approximate accumulation unit is introduced to reduce energy consumption and hardware cost. Experimental results show that, on representative AI models, the proposed design improves inference accuracy by 9.8% and energy efficiency by 41.2% compared with the conventional MX implementation, and achieves a 63.2% gain in energy efficiency over the INT format.

title: An inter-channel calibration technique for the correction of all static errors in SAR ADCs.
abstract: Multi-channel systems feature several ADCs, and offset and gain errors, together with the single channel capacitive DAC mismatch, significantly degrade the overall system performance. This paper presents a foreground on-chip calibration technique to address simultaneously DAC element mismatch, gain and offset static errors in the SAR ADCs of a multi-channel system. A prototype ADC with the integrated calibration circuits has been fabricated in 22-nm CMOS FDSOI and four chips have been operated as a multi-channel system to demonstrate the proposed calibration effectiveness. It achieves 60.1 dB SNDR over 25 MHz signal bandwidth and the digital post-correction logic consumes only 20% of the overall ADC power while effecting a 24.5 dB improvement in SNDR thanks to the proposed calibration technique. The SAR ADC occupies 0.125 mm2, while the calibration circuit occupies 0.15 mm2shared among multiple channels.

title: Power-Efficient Gm-C Band-Pass Filter for Bio-Signal Acquisition.
abstract: This paper presents a power-efficient, wide dynamic range, second-order tunable Gm–C⁴ band-pass filter tailored for low-power biomedical signal processing. The design exploits MOS transistors operating in the subthreshold region to minimize power consumption. To enhance dynamic range, capacitive attenuation and bump linearization techniques are employed, while a Gyrator-C active inductor is integrated to improve the quality factor. The filter provides a tunable frequency range from 6.8 Hz to 707 Hz, suitable for physiological signals with a quality factor of 3 and a 2 dB gain. It achieves ultra-low power consumption between 4.4 nW and 234 nW, a dynamic range of 90.3 dB at 5% total harmonic distortion, and an input-referred noise below 30 μVrms. The design occupies a silicon area of 0.1 mm2in a standard 0.18 μm CMOS process with a 1.8 V supply.

title: A 198.7 μJ/token Block Diffusion LLM Processor with Mask Token Similarity-Based Activation Reuse.
abstract: This paper presents an energy-efficient diffusion-based large language model processor. Diffusion-based large language models have attained significant attention for their computational parallelism, which enables both high token generation speed and energy efficiency. However, their inherent block-based architecture still contains redundancies that can be further optimized. The proposed processor achieves high energy efficiency and low token generation latency with three key features as solutions: 1) Mask token similarity-based activation reuse (MTAR) to reduce computation energy of global prefill stage by 70.6%, 2) Continuous confidence-based mixed precision (CCMP) to allow 94.2% of the local block decoding stage workload to be processed with low-precision activation. 3) Reordering shared bit-slice core (RSBC) architecture to reduce computation energy of local block decoding stage by 46.3%. The proposed processor is implemented in 28 nm CMOS technology and achieves 32.8 TOPS peak throughput with 10.1 TOPS/W. In sum, 198.7 μJ/token highly energy-efficient diffusion-based LLM processor can be achieved on the GSM8K dataset.

title: Invulnerability Checking for Memory Protection Extensions Against Meltdown.
abstract: Intel’s Memory Protection Extensions (MPX) are designed to prevent buffer overflows by enforcing bounds checking on memory references at runtime. However, MPX has been shown to be vulnerable to Meltdown security attacks. A hardware-based mitigation was proposed to address this issue by enforcing sequencing on bounds checking, thereby preventing Meltdown. Despite this, design errors or hardware Trojans in the mitigation’s implementation can still render the microarchitecture vulnerable. We present a formal verification method to ensure that the hardware implementation of the mitigation is secure. Additionally, we identify three classes of hardware Trojans capable of compromising the mitigation. Our formal method, evaluated on multiple microarchitecture benchmarks, accurately detected both errors and Trojans in the mitigation implementation and was also able to prove when the mitigation was securely implemented.

title: A Hybrid FIR-IIR MASH DTDSM with Optimized Self-Coupling Filter for Robust Low-Amplitude Stability.
abstract: A novel hybrid FIR-IIR MASH DTDSM architecture with a self-coupling filter is proposed to address the trade-off between robustness and maximum stable amplitude in delta-sigma modulators. The central innovation stems from the simultaneous optimization of filter dynamics and bit-width allocation via convex programming, dynamically modifying the hybrid FIR-IIR transfer function under stability constraints derived from the Lee criterion. The self-coupling method merges finite and infinite impulse response elements, which results in accurate noise shaping and lower quantization noise power while preserving stability margins. The proposed method sets itself apart from traditional techniques by introducing dynamic bit-width scaling and phase compensation, which reduce harmonic distortion and group delay fluctuations. Simulation results show improved stability at low amplitudes and decreased NTF peaking, accomplished by simultaneous stability observation and coefficient adjustment. This work is particularly relevant to fields demanding precise analog-to-digital conversion with strict durability standards, including biomedical sensing and wireless communication systems.

title: Hardware-Efficient POSIT Based SVM Inference Engine for Intelligent Biomedical Systems.
abstract: Typically, in most portable health-checkup devices, the process of scanning & reporting runs concurrently, hence the demand for establishing intelligence on edge devices continues to rise. However, edge devices pose an acute shortage of resources and tighter power constraints towards achieving longer shelf life, yet faster and more real-time outcomes are desired. Hardware ML design is possibly the way forward, but a compute-intensive structure, with no compromise in accuracy levels, calls for a design innovation. Classical ML techniques, including Support Vector Machine (SVM) and others, fit better for these requirements over other dense neuron architectures of DNNs. This paper proposes an efficient, dataset-agnostic SVM inference engine using optimized Posit arithmetic for biomedical applications. Leveraging a linear SVM kernel, the design offers a lightweight alternative to neural networks and demonstrates improved efficiency and dynamic range over traditional floating-point, validated across multiple biomedical datasets from the Physionet database. Multiple Posit configurations, ranging from (8,2) to (16,4), are evaluated to explore trade-offs in precision, area, power, and performance. FPGA implementation results demonstrate 67.4% reduction in resource utilization at the cost of negligible accuracy drop. ASIC validation further confirms the benefits, showing a 25.2% reduction in silicon footprint, a 34.7% reduction in power consumption, and a slight overhead in computational delay with respect to the corresponding fixed and floating-point implementations. The work showcases a step towards determining an optimal Posit topology for the hardware engine to accelerate inference without compromising critical accuracy and diagnostic outcomes. All the design files are made freely available at [1] for further usage by the designers and research community.

title: ISAC for Intelligent Transportation: Ray-Tracing, Clutter Cancellation, and Sensing-Aided Beamforming.
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) is rapidly gaining prominence as a foundational capability for intelligent transportation systems, allowing wireless networks to perform simultaneous data transmission and environmental sensing using shared resources. However, accurate performance evaluation of ISAC sys- tems remains challenging due to complex multipath propagation, high vehicular mobility, and rapidly time-varying channel conditions. This dissertation presents a unified simulation and algorithmic framework for ISAC in vehicular scenar- ios. A three-dimensional (3D) ray-tracing simulation platform is developed using the NVIDIA Sionna RT framework to model realistic wireless channels, includ- ing multipath effects, Doppler shifts, and environmental clutter. Based on this platform, an Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM)-based radar sensing algorithm incorporating Static Clutter Cancellation (SCC) is developed to enhance vehicle range and velocity estimation performance under strong ur- ban clutter conditions. Additionally, a sensing-based trajectory prediction algo- rithm is developed to support predictive beamforming through proactive beam alignment toward moving vehicles. Simulation results demonstrate measurable improvements in localization accuracy and communication reliability under high- mobility conditions compared to reactive, non-predictive beamforming schemes. The proposed framework provides a practical toolset for assessing and develop- ing advanced ISAC solutions tailored to next-generation intelligent transportation infrastructure.

title: Rethinking ETI Sensing: Analysis, Experimental Proof, and Circuit Insights for In-Band, Magnitude-Only Motion Tracking in EEG.
abstract: Motion-induced fluctuations at the electrode–tissue interface are a dominant source of artifacts in ambulatory dry-electrode EEG. Most systems sense electrode–tissue interface impedance (ETI) out of band using kHz I/Q lock-in methods, which measure a capacitively dominated impedance that poorly reflects the sub-100 Hz interface that actually modulates EEG and imposes bandwidth and power overheads. This paper presents an in-band, magnitude-only ETI sensing method and evidence that it is the right operating point for motion awareness. We provide a compact ETI sensitivity analysis and high-frequency simulations to frame frequency regimes, then report bench measurements with dry comb electrodes under different types of controlled motion. In the EEG band (20 Hz), |Z| aligns with artifact epochs with ≈0.998 correlation, while at 1 kHz, correlations drop to 0.87–0.97 and require phase to recover. A two-tone experiment (20 Hz + 1 kHz) shows limited cross-frequency relevance: 1 kHz-derived estimates correlate only ≈0.92 with 20 Hz artifacts, versus 0.998 in band. We then discuss a simple architecture enabled by modern high-dynamic-range direct-ADC EEG front ends, which make in-band magnitude-only ETI extraction practical. In addition to the main recording ADC, the system incorporates a programmable tone generator, narrow notch filter, envelope detector, and a sub-100 Hz ultra-low-power ADC dedicated to ETI monitoring. Overall, the proposed method yields more accurate artifact estimation with substantially lower power, complexity, and data rate, enabling cheaper, always-on motion awareness for wearable EEG without inertial sensors.

title: Power Side-Channel Attacks in Nanosheet Circuits.
abstract: Pushing the boundaries of device scaling and advanced circuit design, the semiconductor industry is moving beyond FinFETs. The nanosheet field-effect transistor (NSFET) technology is among the most promising contenders, improving area efficiency and reducing power consumption. As NSFET technology progresses toward production, it becomes crucial to assess how vulnerable their power profiles are to leaking confidential information. Here, we evaluate the resilience of an advanced encryption standard (AES) circuit to power side-channel attacks (PSCAs). By using transistor-level NSFET device models and full-layout netlists with standard delay format (SDF) back-annotation, we capture realistic timing and switching activities, enabling accurate power simulations. We conduct correlation power analysis (CPA) with randomized sampling, enabling robust insights. We find that 1-sheet devices, lower supply voltages, and stronger aging consistently provide superior resilience.

title: @NTT: Algorithm-Targeted NTT hardware acceleration via design-time constant optimization.
abstract: The Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) is a critical computational bottleneck in many lattice-based post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) algorithms. By leveraging the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) algorithm, the NTT of a polynomial of degree N − 1 can be computed with a time complexity of $\mathcal{O}(N\log N)$. Hardware implementation of NTT is generally preferred over software ones, as the latter are significantly slower due to complex memory access patterns and modular arithmetic operations. Achieving maximum throughput in hardware, however, typically demands a prohibitively large number of butterfly unit instantiations. In this work, we propose @NTT, which exploits the fact that the ring parameters in these algorithms are fixed, enabling design-time constant optimization and achieving the maximum throughput of N-point NTT per clock cycle with a compact hardware footprint. Our case study on the Dilithium NTT, implemented using the TSMC 28nm library, operates at a clock frequency of 1.0 GHz with an area of 1.45 mm2. On FPGA, the design achieves a throughput-per-LUT that is 5.2× higher than the state-of-the-art.

title: An Automated Framework for Optimal Selection of Approximate Computing Units for Low-Complexity Trigonometric Transforms on FPGAs.
abstract: The optimal selection of approximate computing units towards low-complexity FPGA-based hardware architectures for approximate discrete cosine transform (ADCT) and approximate discrete Fourier transform (ADFT) are explored. The proposed methodology employs an existing library of FPGA based approximate adders to select Pareto-optimal1approximate adders for cascaded signal flow architectures found in ADCT and ADFT operations. Benefits are presented with examples from 8-point ADCT based image compression and 16-point ADFT based digital multi-beamforming applications. Examples demonstrate a nearly 25% LUT reduction in FPGA utilization compared to error-free computing, with a corresponding degradation of nearly 1 dB in terms of PSNR in image compression and 0.3 dB loss in SNR improvement in beamforming.

title: Low-Complexity Multi-beamforming with Configurable Beam Profiles via Approximate-DSFT.
abstract: Low-complexity digital multi-beamforming via multiplier-less approximations for discrete spatial Fourier transform (DSFT) is explored. The proposed approach employs an approximate-DSFT (ADSFT) which - for a uniform linear array with N antennas producing N simultaneous beams, reduces the hardware multiplier requirement from 3N2to 0 with marginal error in the beam profiles. Importantly, the proposed approach extends the previously reported approximate discrete Fourier transform (ADFT) multi-beamforming systems having fixed beam profiles to enable configurable beam profiles, where the user can obtain N simultaneous beams within a given spatial angular region. Simulations demonstrate that the multi-beam profiles are largely accurate, and approximate selection results in deviations for 8- and 16-element ULAs, with worst-case beam angle errors of 0.3° and 0.2°, and worst-case sidelobe deviations of 1.7 dB and 1.4 dB, respectively. For the same scenarios, the proposed ADSFT provides 100% reduction in multiplier complexity and 44.45% reduction in adder complexity compared to conventional multi-beamforming algorithms.

title: FPGA-Accelerated Feature Extraction for an AI-Based Automatic Modulation Classification System.
abstract: Real-time Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC) is limited by the high computational cost of deep learning models on edge devices. This work validates the feasibility of a low-cost, feature-based AMC system designed for future full hardware implementation. The system’s robustness is demonstrated through a hybrid HW/SW approach, where 59 features extracted by an FPGA IP core feed a 4-bit quantized lightweight MLP neural network classifier. The extractor’s implementation on a Zynq-7020 SoC is highly efficient (30µs latency, 107mW), and the final system achieves 85.11% mean accuracy with minimal degradation. The results validate the approach as an efficient and low-cost solution, establishing a practical path for the implementation of real-time AMC on edge devices.

title: Securing IoT with True Randomness and Side-Channel Resistant ECC: a Layered Hardware-Software Approach.
abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in critical applications requires robust hardware-based security mechanisms. Standard Pseudo-Random Number Generators (PRNGs) are vulnerable to statistical analysis and side-channel attacks (SCA) due to their deterministic nature, compromising cryptographic key integrity in resource-constrained environments. This work proposes a validated layered hardware-software security approach integrating a low-cost True Random Number Generator (TRNG) with optimized Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) for constrained IoT systems. The TRNG utilizes the intrinsic electronic noise of a transistor as the physical entropy source, captured and conditioned by an Analog and Mixed-Signal (AMS) circuit. The core contribution lies in the comprehensive integration and validation of the system of this secure chain. The noise is post-processed, achieving a high min-entropy of H∞(X) ≈ 0.9990 bits/bits, which is then used to seed the generation of 256-bit ECC keys. Crucially, the ECC scalar multiplication is implemented using the Montgomery Ladder algorithm and projective coordinates, ensuring constant-time execution – a necessary defense against power and timing SCA. This methodology provides a high-quality, rigorously validated, and low-complexity framework for generating strong cryptographic keys. We demonstrate a practical and resource-efficient security solution for IoT devices, effectively enhancing system robustness where both low-power and high assurance are paramount.

title: Residual Convolutional Neural Networks for Digital Calibration of Oversampled ADCs.
abstract: Machine learning (ML)-based calibration is rapidly emerging as an alternative to traditional digital signal processing-based calibration techniques in analog-to-digital converters (ADCs), offering greater adaptability in addressing non-idealities without prior knowledge. This work demonstrates an ML-based calibration framework on two oversampled ADCs - a second-order noise-shaping approximation register (NS-SAR) ADC and a second-order ring oscillator ADC. A residual convolutional neural network is proposed as the calibration framework that learns to suppress ADC errors directly from time-domain waveforms. Using stacked residual Conv1D blocks, the model effectively captures both local distortions and longer-range error dependencies in time series data, achieving richer feature extraction than conventional artificial neural networks used in previous works. The proposed ML framework enables strong generalization across a wide range of unseen input frequencies and varying operating conditions, and improves signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) by more than 20dB and 8dB for the two ADC test-chips.

title: IDSPfree: An FPGA-Based Intrusion Detection System with DSP-Free Design.
abstract: The rapid expansion of IoT systems and the corresponding surge in network traffic have increased the demand for efficient and low-latency Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS). Although neural network-based IDS models demonstrate strong performance in identifying malicious patterns, deploying these models on embedded systems (edge devices) remains challenging due to resource and power constraints. This work proposes IDSPfree, an FPGA-based low resource consumption and high energy-efficient system for intrusion detection. In particular, we first introduce 8-bit floating point (FP8) quantization to reduce data-width but maintain accuracy. Building on the FP8 data format, we further develop the optimized FP8 approximate multipliers and symmetric approximate activation functions. Experimental results show that IDSPfree maintains an average accuracy loss below 2% on three typical datasets. Additionally, IDSPfree achieves average performance improvements of 9.0× and 3.83×, with up to 6.13× and 9.11× energy consumption saving compared to edge CPU and edge GPU, respectively. Moreover, compared to edge-FPGA-based IDS designs, IDSPfree achieves the lowest power consumption while delivering comparable performance.

title: Experimental Lower-Bound Error for Lyapunov Exponent Estimation Using Switch-Controlled Initial Conditions.
abstract: The lower-bound error (LBE) has emerged as a versatile technique with applications ranging from rigorous simulation and the estimation of the largest Lyapunov exponent (LLE) to cryptographic systems. However, its applicability within experimental settings has not yet been established. This work presents a novel methodology for estimating the LLE of physically implemented chaotic circuits using LBE as a central metric. Two nominally identical but physically distinct circuits are initialized via switch-controlled voltage injection, ensuring reproducible initial conditions, providing sufficient grounds for applying the LBE theorem. As a result, we were able to calculate the LLE for the Jerk and Chua circuits, with values in good agreement with those reported in the literature. These findings confirm that the proposed LBE-based approach enables consistent and accurate experimental estimation of Lyapunov exponents, marking a significant step toward bridging theoretical metrics with physical implementations.

title: A Self-Adaptive Digital Control with 20 ns Precision for Zero Current Switching for Next Generation TEG-based Wearable Devices.
abstract: A Self-Adaptive Digital control based Zero Current Switching scheme (SAD-ZCS) for low power energy harvesting (EH) power management unit (PMU) is proposed. The proposed ZCS control uses a current-starving based tunable delay element, avoiding more area occupied by on-chip capacitors. A regenerative feedback based clocked comparator is employed for its high gain achieved in ZCS comparison. The SAD control can be programmed to start with an early turn-off or late turn-off of the High Side (HS) switch based on the system requirements. The designed boost converter operates from an input voltage range of 100 mV to 600 mV, regulating the output voltage at 1 V to 1.8 V (programmable). The system is designed and simulated in a standard 130 nm CMOS technology. The proposed boost converter achieves a peak converter efficiency of 97.13% for an input voltage of 400 mV.

title: VERIMLA: A Unified Framework for Verilog Generation via Multi-Level Alignment and Formal Equivalence Verification.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have exhibited remarkable capabilities in code generation for mainstream programming languages such as Python and C/C++. However, their performance in hardware description languages (HDLs) remains underexplored. Existing research typically requires commercial LLMs to generate their datasets or is limited by the model’s prior knowledge. Additionally, open-source benchmarks rely on experts to craft testbenches, making them hard to expand. To overcome these limitations, we propose a unified framework for Verilog generation that integrates training and evaluation. Its core is a multi-level alignment method that maps abstract syntax trees (ASTs) to code before task-level fine-tuning. For evaluation, we adopt a formal equivalence verification (FEV)-based workflow to simplify testing and the evaluation dataset construction. Our VERIMLA achieves state-of-the-art performance on VerilogEval under equivalent training data, with a pass@10 of 86.1% on VerilogEval-Machine and 65.4% on VerilogEval-Human. Furthermore, to evaluate generalization on more complex problems, we employ our FEV-based evaluation workflow to create a new evaluation dataset whose Verilog code has an average token length six times that of VerilogEval. VERIMLA’s high pass@1 on this challenging set confirms its ability to solve complex design tasks.

title: A Flexible 128-Channel Neural Stimulator with Dynamic Voltage Scaling and Synchronous Charge Balancing for Visual Cortical Prosthesis.
abstract: This work presents a scalable neural stimulator ASIC for visual cortical stimulation (VCS) aimed at the restoration of vision. The proposed system integrates 128 compact stimulator channels optimized for cortical implantation, enabling simultaneous multi-electrode stimulation within the visual cortex. Employing a dynamic voltage scaling (DVS) technique, the system achieves energy savings of up to 46% during concurrent multi-channel stimulation. A synchronous charge balancer (SCB) ensures accurate biphasic charge transfer while maintaining the stimulation offset voltage within ±20 mV without prolonged processing time. Implemented in a standard 180 nm CMOS process, the stimulator achieves a compact area of only 0.005 mm2per channel, supporting high-channel-count cortical electrodes and facilitating seamless integration with other functional blocks in a fully integrated system-on-chip (SoC) platform.

title: Low-Noise Digital Fractional-N PLL with Continuous-Time Band-Pass ∆Σ TDC and Two-Point Chirp Linearization.
abstract: This paper presents a 2.86–3.2 GHz digital fractional-N frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) chirp synthesizer employing a continuous-time bandpass delta-sigma time-to-digital converter (CT-BP∆Σ-TDC), which serves as the phase detector. The proposed architecture enables wide loop bandwidth operation for fast chirp generation while simultaneously maintaining low in-band phase noise, thus addressing critical challenges in modern radar and sensing applications. The synthesizer integrates several key components: a 2 GHz voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO); a multi-phase divider with phase interpolation for fine fractional frequency resolution; a high-order BP∆Σ-TDC sampled at the reference frequency with digital down-conversion to baseband; a digital loop filter; and on-chip chirp control circuitry. To overcome the fundamental loop-bandwidth limitation on achievable chirp slope, this work implements two-point modulation by combining N-path and VCO-path modulation with predistortion compensation based on a comprehensive VCO nonlinearity characterization. The 180 nm CMOS prototype achieves −120 dBc/Hz phase noise at 1 MHz offset (normalized PN: −256 dBc/Hz), a 0.6-1 MHz loop bandwidth, 2-5 MHz/µs chirp slope with a 100 kHz RMS frequency error, and −50 dBc reference spurs using phase-selection dither, while consuming 10 mW in a 0.05 mm2area. Compared to PFD/CP-based PLLs, the CT-BP∆Σ-TDC provides superior near-DC noise suppression, reduced delay-mismatch sensitivity, an extended phase detection range, and improved chirp linearity through time-scheduled loop bandwidth control without compromising stability.

title: A Noise-Shaping SAR ADC With Second-Order Input Prediction.
abstract: This paper presents a low-power noise-shaping (NS) SAR ADC with a second-order input prediction algorithm. This algorithm uses polynomial interpolation to predict the bits of the next sample. Since the ADC only needs to convert the small difference between the input signal and the predicted code, the energy per conversion and the number of bit cycles per conversion can be reduced. The prototype ADC is designed in a 130-nm CMOS process. It consumes 270 µW from a 1.2-V supply while operating at 16 MS/s. The simulated SNDR is 86.3 dB over a bandwidth of 500 kHz, corresponding to an SNDR-based Schreier figure of merit (FoM) of 179 dB.

title: Embedding Passion: A Project-Based Scaffolding Framework for Embedded Systems Education.
abstract: We present a project-based scaffolding framework for an undergraduate course in embedded systems. Four labs in the second half of the semester gradually reduce scaffolding and build toward a testable baseline, followed by an open-ended enhancement phase. Weekly take-home tasks extend the in-lab work and help students move from guided practice to independent design. Using five years of data, we observe higher pre-exam self-efficacy and a higher achievement floor among lower-quartile students. Qualitative evidence shows that more teams pursue features beyond requirements. Our evaluation is observational and context-specific; however, the sequence structure and supporting schemes are readily transferable. We contribute a compact, replicable sequence, an evaluation that triangulates perception and performance, and guidance on pacing and hinting. Future iterations will stage a large assignment and connect an early assembly artefact to the project to strengthen coherence throughout the semester.

title: An AI-Based Pareto-Driven Cost-Dimension Optimization of EMI filters for DC-DC Converters.
abstract: This paper presents an AI-based and data-oriented optimization algorithm for the synthesis of passive Electro-Magnetic Interference (EMI) filters in DC–DC converters. The algorithm minimizes both cost and occupied area (or volume) targeting specific EMI attenuation levels and ensuring system stability. It operates on commercial component datasets and exploits the mathematical properties of Pareto dominance to explore feasible design configurations. Through dominance preserving set operators, the proposed approach guarantees exact Pareto-optimality while drastically reducing computational complexity. A neural network assists the optimization process by identifying computationally feasible ranges of component parameters, thus accelerating convergence. The method is validated on two commercial DC–DC converter evaluation boards from STMicroelectronics and Texas Instruments. It demonstrates its ability to identify solutions that outperform existing reference designs in both cost and area/volume.

title: A 10-MS/s Sub-0.1-mW Power Scalable SAR ADC with 10/12-bit Reconfigurable Resolution for Portable Ultrasound Systems.
abstract: An asynchronous, reconfigurable successive-approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) for portable ultrasound systems is presented. A power- and noise-performance-scalable dynamic comparator employing a floating inverter amplifier (FIA) is proposed. Bottom-plate reconfigurable switches eliminate three-quarters of the most significant bit (MSB) capacitors, significantly reducing power consumption. A low leakage latched dynamic cell featuring reconfigurability is utilized to further improve energy efficiency. Fabricated in a 65-nm CMOS process, the proposed SAR ADC supports both 10- and 12-bit operations. In 10-bit mode, it achieves a signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) of 59.67 dB while consuming 63.42µW at 10 MS/s sampling rate. In 12-bit mode, it attains 67.50 dB SNDR with a power consumption of 99.52µW.

title: Live Demonstration: AI-Aided RF Reflectometry for Rapid Adulteration and Contamination Detection in Food Products.
abstract: This demonstration presents a portable AI-aided Radio-Frequency Reflectometry (RF-R) system for real-time detection of adulteration in high-value foods (e.g., extra-virgin olive oil or pure honey). The system combines broadband RF sensing (30 kHz–5 GHz) with machine learning to identify adulterants and estimate concentration (10–40% range) with > 95% accuracy. Visitors interactively add adulterants and observe real-time AI classification, demonstrating how electromagnetic sensing enables rapid, non-destructive and field-deployable food quality assessment.

title: A 94.3%-Efficient Battery-Less Wireless Sensor Node Featuring -0.5°C~+1°C Inaccuracy Room Temperature Two-Point Calibrated Sensor.
abstract: This paper presents a battery-less wireless sensor node that integrates energy harvesting with a room-temperature two-point calibratable temperature sensor. By utilizing ambient energy, the system eliminates the need for batteries and enables long-term, maintenance-free operation suitable for large-scale IoT deployments. The proposed temperature sensor performs offset and slope calibration entirely at room temperature using a digitally switchable resistor network, eliminating the need for costly multi-temperature testing. This approach simplifies production and improves yield without compromising accuracy. The system achieves -0.5°C~+1°C sensing inaccuracy after digital calibration and incorporates a power converter with 94.3% peak efficiency over a wide input range. Fabricated using a 130nm BCD process for the energy harvesting part and a 55nm ULP RF process for the BLE transceiver part, the platform combines energy efficiency with robust wireless performance.

title: A Discrete-Time Analog Compute Macro for Edge ML with 200 TOPS/W in CMOS 28nm.
abstract: A signed analog precision Multiply-and-Accumulate (MAC) macro, targeted for edge computing, is introduced and fabricated in CMOS 28 nm technology. Scalability of Computing-in-memory (CIM) faces challenges due to complexities in implementing high bit-precision compute units. This work addresses scalability by pushing computations to analog domain and transferring data between MAC layers in a discrete time pipelined manner, removing the need for per-cycle memory read and write operations. The proposed analog MAC circuit improves system energy-efficiency and latency by removing some of the complex operations in the conventional CIMs, such as partial-sum operations, data converters, shift and add, and memory access in multiple cycles. Due to its discrete-time nature, operation per-kernel can be scaled up as desired by tuning the supply voltage, making this work more suited for power-performance scalable Deep Neural Networks (DNNs). The proposed system achieves 200 TOPS/W and 6 GOPS per MAC in energy-efficient and high-performance modes respectively, enabling 10× and 30× improvement in energy efficiency and throughput over the state-of the-art MAC units with 8-bit operand precision.

title: S-SSHI/SECE Hybrid Circuit with Two Diodes for Piezoelectric Devices.
abstract: This paper presents a new self-powered hybrid circuit of series synchronized switch harvesting on inductor (S-SSHI) and synchronous electric charge extraction (SECE) with discrete components. The proposed circuit has two diodes and two inductors. In relatively smaller resistance range, the proposed circuit obtains larger power than a conventional S-SSHI and SECE hybrid circuit with three diodes when high forward voltage diode such as silicon diode is chosen. S-SSHI and SECE operation have been confirmed, and the output power is compared to the conventional one in simulation and in experiment.

title: Live Demonstration: Pocket-Size USB-C TRNG with Interactive GUI for High-Entropy Security.
abstract: We present a silicon-proven ring-oscillator true random number generator (RO-TRNG) in a pocket-size USB–C module that streams raw entropy to a host in real time. A lightweight Python GUI makes the source auditable, exposing live health, while the same bytes drive production workflows: key/seed generation, authenticated messaging, session re-keying, file protection, fair selection, and Monte Carlo visualisations. The platform is bus-powered, CDC/serial class, and offline, enabling dependable plug-and-show deployment. Grounded in a hybrid delay-cell RO architecture with measured robustness and adaptable operation as published in [1], the platform packages these validated properties into an auditable, pocket-size module that carries lab-grade entropy directly into real deployments.

title: A Smart Rotation-Tolerant and Self-Positioning WPT System for Freely Moving Small Animals.
abstract: This paper introduces an enhanced wireless power transmission (WPT) architecture optimized for dynamic and misaligned receivers, specifically addressing the challenges posed by tilt-induced misalignment. The system deploys phase-controlled excitation across a spatial array of transmitter coils to locally counteract angular displacement of the receiver. Targeted toward behavioral and cognitive studies on freely moving animals, the setup consists of a dual-array cage structure with transmitter plates mounted above and below the roaming area. Receiver positioning is intelligently determined using current-sensing feedback from the power drivers in conjunction with Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithms for real-time spatial classification. A phase-shift control strategy is activated in response to receiver tilt, significantly enhancing received power by optimizing magnetic field orientation. Additionally, the use of overlapping transmitter coils improves field uniformity and supports full rotational tolerance. Simulations and experimental results from a fabricated prototype confirm the system’s efficacy, demonstrating a substantial power delivery of 296 mW under 90° angular misalignment—contrasting sharply with just 1.67 μW from conventional array systems.

title: A Direct 48-1 V Three-Phase Three-Inductor Converter with 5× TON Extension and 4× V·A Metric Reduction.
abstract: This paper presents a direct 48-1 V three-phase three-inductor converter (TPTI) for data center applications. By utilizing flying capacitors (CFs) and three-phase operation, the proposed TPTI converter substantially reduces both voltage and current stresses of the power switches and the voltage swing at the switching nodes (VSW), achieving 5× ON-time (TON) extension and 4× V·A metric reduction. By employing only 12 V and 24 V power devices, the proposed converter achieves a 48-1 V conversion and a maximum output current (IO) of 10 A, featuring pseudo-soft charging/discharging of CFs, low inductor current (IL) ripple, and low output voltage (VO) ripple. The TPTI converter adopts valley current-mode constant-on-time (COT) control with a master phase mirroring technique to generate three-phase control signals. Simulation results demonstrate a peak efficiency of 91.8% and VOripple of merely 2.1 mV under 48-1 V conversion.

title: Memristive probabilistic neuron enhanced memristor-based Ising machine for efficient combinatorial optimization.
abstract: Combinatorial Optimization Problems (COPs) are prevalent across many fields and are mostly NP-hard, posing significant challenges for conventional von Neumann architectures. Ising machines offer a promising alternative by mapping COPs onto spin systems that evolve toward low-energy states. Recent efforts have implemented Ising machines using various technologies, yet silicon-based approaches often suffer from limited parallelism and high energy consumption due to data movement and complex digital sampling. In this paper, we propose a memristor-based Ising machine scheme enhanced by probabilistic neurons that enable analog in-memory annealing. By performing spin updates directly in the analog domain, our architecture eliminates the need for high-precision ADCs and integrates intrinsic stochasticity for efficient exploration of the solution space without extra cost. Our proposed scheme can be easily integrated into existing memristor-based Ising machines and achieves approximately 100% improvement in energy efficiency.

title: An Iterated Hybrid Fast Parallel FIR Filter.
abstract: This paper revisits the design and optimization of parallel fast finite impulse response (FIR) filters using polyphase decomposition and iterated fast FIR algorithms (FFAs). Parallel FIR filtering enhances computational efficiency and throughput in digital signal processing (DSP) applications by enabling the simultaneous processing of multiple input samples. We revisit a prior approach to design of fast parallel filter architectures by using the iterated FFA approach where the same primitive filter, such as 2-parallel, is iterated to design the fast parallel filter. In this paper, we present yet another novel iterated fast parallel FIR filter, referred to as the fast hybrid filter. The hybrid filter iterates a transposed 2-parallel fast FIR filter in all the inner layers and a direct-form 2-parallel fast FIR filter in the outermost layer, resulting in reduced hardware complexity. Such an iterated hybrid approach has not been presented before. We show that the hybrid fast parallel filters require less number of additions compared to prior approaches.

title: Design of a Class-J Power Amplifier with Reactive-Resistive Second Harmonic Termination for Improved Efficiency.
abstract: This paper presents a highly efficient class-J power amplifier (PA) that accounts for both resistive and reactive terminations of the second harmonic through appropriate load optimization. Initially, a non-shorted second-harmonic termination is introduced, incorporating higher-order harmonics at the drain terminal. A higher-order harmonic-terminated voltage waveform is then employed to enhance efficiency by increasing the peak voltage swing. This work focuses on designing an efficient power amplifier (PA) by exploiting the flexibility in load termination, which enables bandwidth enhancement with a tradeoff in efficiency. The simulated results are validated through fabrication and measurements. The amplifier achieves a drain efficiency of up to 70% and a gain of 10.2 dB, with a medium output power level of 34.2 dBm at the 1-dB compression point (P1dB).

title: Energy-Aware Heterogeneous Deployment of Learned Image Codecs.
abstract: Learned image compression (LIC) achieves state-of-the-art compression performance, yet practical deployments often overlook latency and energy—critical constraints for on-device pipelines and bandwidth-limited applications such as drones and satellite imaging. We address this gap with a codec-aware heterogeneous deployment partitioned at the codec’s natural bottleneck—the quantised latent—and mapped across devices: large analysis/synthesis transforms to the GPU (high parallel throughput), the compact, pipelined hyperprior to the FPGA (low-power dataflow), and entropy coding to the CPU. The system remains bit-exact with the reference codec and integrates directly with pretrained CompressAI models via exported ONNX subgraphs. Across two pretrained codecs and 1,000 test images, the heterogeneous mapping improves encoder runtime by about 10% and reduces encoder energy by 80% on average relative to GPU-only execution. For the decoder, runtime remains within 1% of the GPU while energy decreases by approximately 78%. Overall, it achieves an energy–delay product about 80% lower than GPU-only and 29% lower than FPGA-only, providing a superior latency–energy trade-off for LIC deployment.

title: A 70 GHz Differential Noise Source for Noise Figure Built-In Self-Test in 22nm FDSOI CMOS.
abstract: This paper presents an on-chip differential broadband noise source (NS) implemented as a built-in self-test (BIST) system for noise figure (NF) measurement based on the Y-factor method. The proposed NS enables accurate NF characterization of broadband differential low-noise circuits. The paper describes the measurement methodology and provides simulation results. When activated, the NS generates two noise levels, referred to as COLD and HOT, while in the OFF state it exhibits only 20 fF of parasitic capacitance. The circuit is implemented in 22nm FDSOI technology, and simulation results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of on-chip BIST-based NF measurement for differential broadband systems up to 70 GHz.
