title: Piecewise Modeling of RF Power Amplifiers using Derivative Analysis and K-Means Clusterization.
abstract: Piecewise modeling of power amplifiers (PAs) is an effective approach for handling complex amplitude and phase distortion characteristics. However, determining the optimal number of sub-models and their corresponding segmentation points is often heuristic or computationally expensive. This work introduces three data-partitioning strategies based on the derivative analysis of the AM-AM curve: (i) direct derivative-based segmentation, (ii) derivative-driven K-Means clustering in the amplitude domain, and (iii) derivative-driven K-Means clustering using the joint amplitude/phase trajectory. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed methods achieve comparable accuracy to classical grid search while reducing runtime by a factor of 400–600. Notably, the amplitude/phase trajectory approach, although not the top performer in this dataset, introduces a novel perspective that may offer significant advantages in scenarios with stronger phase distortion.

title: Algorithm-Aided Design and Verification for Multiple-Node-Upset-Recovery Latches.
abstract: In advanced CMOS technologies, integrated circuits are becoming increasingly sensitive to soft errors in radiation environments. The design process of existing latches heavily relies on electronic design automation (EDA) tools with comprehensive error-injection-based robustness verification. In this paper, algorithm-aided design and verification for robust latches are proposed and then, three algorithm-aided latches (i.e., SURLAD, DURLAD, and TURLAD) respectively providing SNU-, DNU-, and TNU-recovery are proposed. These latches are recoverable from single-node-upsets (SNUs) and multiple-node upsets (MNUs), respectively. Verification results demonstrate the robustness and advantages in terms of delay and power overhead of the proposed latches compared with state-of-the-art latches.

title: A Neural Spike Sorting Framework with Multi-Scale Slope Detection and Lite-CNN Classification.
abstract: In invasive brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), achieving accurate and efficient spike sorting is hindered by the noise sensitivity of conventional methods and the high computational overhead of deep learning approaches. This paper proposes a hardware-efficient end-to-end solution combining Multi-Scale Slope-based Spike Detection (MS-SSD) and a Lightweight CNN (Lite-CNN). MS-SSD achieves a 99.91% recall rate through band-pass filtering, slope analysis, and multi-scale thresholding, while the Lite-CNN performs fine-grained classification and noise rejection on an optimized 5-sample temporal region-of-interest (ROI). Experimental results on the public Quiroga dataset demonstrate a classification accuracy of 99.08%. Remarkably, the proposed architecture requires only 34 Multiply-Accumulate operations (MACs) and 35 parameters per classification, making it highly suitable for resource-constrained, real-time BCI applications in edge computing scenarios.

title: CADA: Chroma-aware denoising architecture for low-light RAW images.
abstract: Image denoising represents a fundamental and challenging problem in image signal processing. Despite the proliferation of deep learning-based denoising methods for real-world images, their performance significantly deteriorates under extremely low-light conditions. RAW images acquired in such environments are severely contaminated by signal-independent noise that exhibits channel-wise independent distribution. The extremely low signal-to-noise ratio prevents complete noise suppression, and the residual signal-independent noise alters the original inter-channel signal ratios in RAW data, leading to undesirable color patch artifacts. This paper introduces a two-stage denoising framework that decouples the denoising process into basic noise removal and subsequent color restoration. The proposed chroma-aware restoration block operates as a plug-and-play module that effectively eliminates color patchiness in outputs from diverse denoising backbones. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that our approach substantially alleviates color distortion in denoised images, achieving up to 0.67 dB PSNR improvement over baseline denoising networks. Furthermore, the chroma-aware architecture exhibits strong generalization capability to low-light image enhancement tasks, yielding up to 2.74 dB PSNR gain.

title: An Adaptive SMU System with Single-Shot Transient Impedance Sensing and 1 mF Capacitive Driveability.
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive source measurement unit (SMU) system that integrates single-shot transient impedance sensing technique, covering all SMU load ranges (up to 1 mF). Based on the sensing results, the system automatically selects optimal compensation capacitors and resistors according to a predefined adaptive range configuration, ensuring seamless stable operation. A 30 V rail-to-rail operational amplifier has been designed as a core component for the SMU’s adaptive measurement system, achieving 136 dB gain, 63.5 MHz GBW, and 2.7 A output driveability. The simulation results under resistive, 4.7 μF typical capacitive and 1 mF heavy capacitive loads consistently demonstrate superior accuracy and settling time compared to commercial SMUs.

title: Three-Dimensional Off-Grid Source Localization Based on Distributed Linear Array Networks.
abstract: The problem of three-dimensional (3-D) off-grid source localization based on a distributed linear array network is investigated. For wideband signals, a focusing-based off-grid localization method exploiting the group sparsity concept is proposed, where the on-grid information and the 3-D grid offsets are estimated separately. Furthermore, a dynamic-dictionary-based re-focused localization method is presented to iteratively mitigate system mismatch errors caused by both focusing and off-grid Taylor approximation. Employing a coarse grid, both methods demonstrate improved performance while maintaining low computational complexity.

title: FPGA-Based Dense-Sparse Adaptive Simulated Bifurcation Ising Machine for MAX-CUT Problems.
abstract: Combinatorial Optimization Problems (COP) are mostly arbitrary and sparse in practice. Simulated bifurcation (SB), as an emerging quantum-inspired heuristic algorithm exhibits strong performance in solving COP. However, existing SB-based Ising machines lack adaptability to sparse graphs, require excessive hardware resources, and struggle to balance convergence speed and solution quality. To address these issues, this paper proposes a fully connected FPGA-based dense-sparse adaptive SB Ising Machine (DSA-SBM) for sparse COP. DSA-SBM adopts an adaptive SB strategy rooted in saturating-growth control to balance system convergence speed and optimal solution accuracy. Its hardware features a dense-sparse adaptive architecture with compressed sparse row (CSR) format storage for 5-bit coefficient matrix and supports dynamic data allocation and adaptive matrix-spin multiplication. Implemented on Xilinx UltraScale+ XCZU7EV FPGA with 151 MHz clock frequency, it achieves 13.81× higher energy efficiency than the original dense SB Ising machine. In the 2000 spin MAX-CUT benchmark, it achieves 99.56% accuracy with an average of 0.687 ms, delivering a 123.6-170.5× speedup compared to the GPU.

title: Experimental Evaluation of a Varactor-Tuned Programmable Metasurface with Modular Electronics - Toward ASIC Integration.
abstract: Programmable metasurfaces are poised to reshape wireless communication and sensing, yet their adoption depends critically on the electronics that bias hundreds to thousands of reconfigurable elements. This paper reports measured results from a modular, 4.15 GHz programmable metasurface controlled by off-the-shelf electronics. The 256-element array achieves ~15 dB gain and ~100° beam steering, with 230 ms reconfiguration latency and 2.55 W power consumption per tile. However, some applications demand sub-100 ms and strict energy budgets. To satisfy such requirements, the manufactured prototype measurements are compared with post-layout simulations of a custom application-specific integrated circuit approach. The possibility of replacing the digital-to-analog converters with custom designed integrated circuits is explored to reduce per-tile power consumption, enabling battery or solar-powered operation and denser tiling. Latency still remains constrained if the same microcontroller-based control is used, but if a parallel control of the chips is adopted, it can reach the sub-millisecond updates required for mobile use cases. The comparison demonstrates how chip-based metasurfaces can reduce energy consumption and latency.

title: Knowledge Distillation in the QAOA Setting for Advantage on Quantum Hardware.
abstract: In this work, we investigate the application of Knowledge Distillation (KD) to the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) setting, introducing a framework to distill knowledge from a Multi-angle QAOA teacher to a standard, single-layer QAOA student. We propose three distillation schemes: count-based KD, distillation using MSE, and distillation with Huber loss for enhanced robustness. Numerical experiments on diverse graph families, including complete graphs, Erdős–Rényi graphs, complete binary trees, and random 3-regular graphs, suggest that MSE and Huber-based distillation can improve the student’s performance, while count-based KD exhibits higher variance and limited generalization. Our results indicate that KD can enable a compression of the QAOA parameter space while often maintaining competitive solution quality, providing a practical avenue for efficient deployment on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum hardware with improved training stability.

title: Adaptive Resolution and Chroma Subsampling for Energy-Efficient Video Coding.
abstract: Conventional video encoders typically employ a fixed chroma subsampling format, such as YUV420, which may not optimally reflect variations in chroma detail across different types of content. This can lead to suboptimal chroma quality and inefficiencies in bitrate allocation. We propose an Adaptive Resolution–Chroma Subsampling (ARCS) framework that jointly optimizes spatial resolution and chroma subsampling to balance perceptual quality and decoding efficiency. ARCS selects an optimal (resolution, chroma format) pair for each bitrate by maximizing a composite quality–complexity objective, while enforcing monotonicity constraints to ensure smooth transitions between representations. Experimental results using x265 show that, compared to a fixed-format encoding (YUV444), on average, ARCS achieves a 13.48 % bitrate savings and a 62.18 % reduction in decoding time, which we use as a proxy for the decoding energy, to yield the same colorVideoVDP score. The proposed framework introduces chroma adaptivity as a new control dimension for energy-efficient video streaming.

title: Content-Driven Frame-Level Bit Prediction for Rate Control in Versatile Video Coding.
abstract: Rate control allocates bits efficiently across frames to meet a target bitrate while maintaining quality. Conventional two-pass rate control (2pRC) in Versatile Video Coding (VVC) relies on analytical rate-QP models, which often fail to capture nonlinear spatial-temporal variations, causing quality instability and high complexity due to multiple trial encodes. This paper proposes a content-adaptive framework that predicts frame-level bit consumption using lightweight features from the Video Complexity Analyzer (VCA) and quantization parameters within a Random Forest regression. On ultra-high-definition sequences encoded with VVenC, the model achieves strong correlation with ground truth, yielding R2 values of 0.93, 0.88, and 0.77 for I-, P-, and B-frames, respectively. Integrated into a rate-control loop, it achieves comparable coding efficiency to 2pRC while reducing total encoding time by 33.3%. The results show that VCA-driven bit prediction provides a computationally efficient and accurate alternative to conventional rate-QP models.

title: An X-Band LC-VCO with 37% Tuning Range and Programmable KVCO in 65nm CMOS.
abstract: This brief presents a wideband LC voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) oscillating within the frequency range of 8.5 GHz to 12.3 GHz, achieving a tuning range of 37%. A varactor structure is proposed to enable the programmable KVCOfeature for wideband VCO designs, ensuring comprehensive band coverage. The VCO is fabricated in UMC-65nm low-leakage CMOS process, achieving FoM and FoMTAof 182.8 dB and 208.4 dB, respectively, occupying a compact area of 0.038 mm2using a power consumption of 2.76 mW from a 1.2-V supply.

title: A Complete Low-Duty-Cycle S/H System with 100ms Hold Time at 175°C.
abstract: A complete IC with a innovative Sample & Hold structure to be used in aggressive low-duty cycle scheme for power reduction approach is proposed. The circuit is autonomous, since it includes a fully-integrated current and frequency generator. All digital logics are current limited to reduce cross-bar current. The S/H is able to multiply the input voltage and to hold the resulting voltage for 100msec with a negligible droop rate (70mV/sec at 140°C). For extremely high temperature up to 175°C, the leakage current increase results in a droop rate of 570mV/sec that produces a maximum 5.7% error. The full circuit consumes an average current of 460nA, enabling turning-off the reference voltage generator.

title: In-Sensor Computing by Reconfigurable Field-Effect Transistors.
abstract: The rising demand for multiplexed biomarker analysis in complex disease diagnostics, such as cancer, places a premium on biosensing technologies that can process multiple biochemical information with minimal power and footprint. Current systems, however, rely on complex analog front ends that make complex signal interpretation, increase energy consumption, and limit miniaturization. In this work, we overcome these limitations with a novel circuit based on nine triple-independent-gate reconfigurable field-effect transistors (RFETs). This circuit processes three analog inputs from a biotransducer, performing, if needed, in total up to eleven combinations of logic operations (showcased four in this work) to enable integrated in-sensor computing and multiplexing. The resulting output provides a direct digital correlation with pathological conditions, offering a clear pathway for therapeutic decision-making. We validated four core logic functions through in-silico simulations using models from Global TCAD Solutions, confirming the circuit's operational principle.

title: Analogue Studies of Energy Recurrence in Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou Systems.
abstract: Analogue approach has been used for many years in the studies of non-linear systems due to the convenience and low cost profit. However, this approach has not been applied to analyse the Fermi–Pasta–Ulam–Tsingou (FPUT) system which was discovered and exhibited the phenomenon of energy recurrence in a non-linear array oscillations in 1955. Over the following decades, extensive studies have been conducted focusing on the mathematical and theoretical aspects rather than experimental results in the real world. In this work, we replicate the energy recurrence in FPUT system by designing an electrical oscillation circuitry to build a 4-oscillator FPUT system with quadratic non-linearity. We compare the experimental results with the simulation results, which exhibit similar behaviour. This confirms our successful observation of the energy recurrence phenomenon in this electrical oscillation system. These results enhance the understanding of the non-linear system and provide new inspiration for future research directions.

title: Multi-Time-Gated SPAD Array with Shared TDCs for Fluorescence-Lifetime Imaging Applications.
abstract: To investigate the mechanism and potential of multi-time-gated (MTG) single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) in fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) applications, we designed a 4×4 MTG SPAD array integrated with a shared multi-purpose delay line and two-stage time-to-digital converters. The proposed architecture enables multiple shifted detection windows to reduce the complexity of circuits and to extend the dynamic range. Post-layout simulations and preliminary measurements demonstrate a maximum detection range of ~15 ns with a timing resolution of ~30.4 ps, highlighting the potential of the proposed SPAD array for scalable and cost-effective FLIM systems.

title: A Compact Broadband Power Amplifier with High Efficiency and <1% Power-Added Efficiency Variation over 24-36 GHz.
abstract: This paper presents a compact broadband and high-efficiency power amplifier (PA) for fifth-generation (5G) new radio (NR) frequency range 2 (FR2) communications. Using a class-B PA as an example, the mechanism behind inherent power-added efficiency (PAE) non-flatness in conventional cascode architectures is analyzed. To address this, the design incorporates a parallel inter-stage inductor, which effectively mitigates non-ideal effects in traditional cascode structures. The proposed architecture improves the output impedance matching, resolving the degraded S22performance in conventional cascode PAs at saturation power (Psat). This enhancement makes the design more suitable for phased-array applications. Furthermore, a compact low-coupling transformer is implemented to minimize chip area. Designed in a 40 nm CMOS, the PA achieves 19.27 dBm Psatwith a 3 dB bandwidth spanning 21–38 GHz. Within 22.5–38 GHz, the Psatvariation remains below 1 dB. The PAE variation is maintained within2.

title: Statistical Routing Order Optimization in Global Routing.
abstract: This paper presents a statistical framework for routing order optimization in global routing. By analyzing routing outcomes across multiple benchmarks, we systematically investigate how net features correlate with optimal routing order. Our analysis reveals non-uniform patterns in wirelength sensitivity across routing stages, indicating that net ordering indeed impacts final results. With sampling data, we could reconstruct a near-optimal routing order to obtain a better routing quality. Based on these statistical insights, we then develop a lightweight machine learning model to predict this near-optimal routing orders, using the observed patterns as guiding priors. Experimental results of initial global routing demonstrate consistent wirelength improvements over baseline ordering, confirming that our statistical analysis can effectively guide routing optimization.

title: C2NoC: A Communication-Computation Coupled NoC-based Neural Network Accelerator.
abstract: The increasing complexity of Deep Neural Network (DNN) models has made Network-on-Chip (NoC) based neural network accelerators a critical platform for energy-efficient computing. However, intra-network communication latency remains a major performance bottleneck, particularly under congested conditions. To address this, this paper presents C2NoC, a Communication-Computation coupled Network-on-Chip neural network accelerator. We embed multiply-accumulate units into router virtual channels, allowing packets to perform computations during pipeline and congestion delays, effectively transforming communication latency into computation. Experimental results demonstrate that C2NoC achieves up to 24.2% reduction in inference latency under varying payload configurations. Synthesis results show that the architecture reduces area and power consumption by 18.9% and 27.6%, respectively, compared to the baseline, significantly improving both performance and energy efficiency.

title: A Low-Distortion Feedforward Delta-Sigma ADC with Nested Summation Quantizer.
abstract: Feedforward delta-sigma analog-to-digital converter (ΔΣ ADC) topologies offer high energy efficiency and wideband performance, with signal summation playing a crucial role in overall converter effectiveness. This paper introduces a novel architecture for wideband, low-distortion input-feedforward ΔΣ ADCs that achieve energy-efficient signal summation. By employing a nested first-order delta-sigma modulator operating at a sampling frequency of 32 times faster, the design facilitates 4-bit quantization. The architecture enables unattenuated signal feedforward by moving the summation node into the delta-sigma quantizer, thereby eliminating the need for active adders. This configuration supports high-speed operation of feedforward ΔΣ modulators while preventing signal leakage into the integrators. Post simulation results demonstrate that the proposed modulator achieves a peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of 95.7 dB, it consumes 5.5 µW and achieves a competitive Schreier FoM of 165.3 dB, validating effectiveness of the proposed architecture.

title: Harnessing Spatiotemporal Redundancy for Fast Diffusion Models on FPGA.
abstract: Despite the impressive generative capabilities of diffusion models, their iterative inference process is computationally intensive, hindering deployment on resource-constrained devices. Existing accelerators with static optimizations are ill-suited for the inherent non-uniformities of the denoising process, wasting computation in early stages and on infrequently updated background regions. To address this, we propose Diffusion-OPU, an algorithm-hardware co-design that systematically exploits these spatiotemporal redundancies. First, we introduce Progressive Scaling with Adaptive Reuse (PSAR), which partitions the denoising process into a coarse phase to efficiently establish global structure and a fine phase for detail refinement, reducing early-stage computational waste. Second, a saliency-aware mechanism selectively recomputes only dynamic foreground regions while reusing cached features for static backgrounds, tackling spatial redundancy at a fine-grained level. Third, our co-designed architecture materializes these algorithmic gains with a reconfigurable processing engine for multi-resolution computation and a mask-aware dataflow, guided by the saliency mechanism, to physically gate background computations and maximize throughput. Experimental results demonstrate that Diffusion-OPU outperforms the NVIDIA A100 GPU baseline, delivering up to a 2.1× speedup with negligible impact on generation quality.

title: Piezoelectric energy harvesting interface with high frequency mismatch tolerance based on a novel two-dimensional MPPT algorithm.
abstract: In piezoelectric energy harvesting, the severe attenuation of harvested energy due to frequency mismatch between the vibration source and the piezoelectric transducer poses a critical challenge. Existing wide-bandwidth designs lack the capability to autonomously adjust their parameters according to the excitation frequency. This paper proposes a piezoelectric energy harvesting system based on a novel MPPT that can self-adapt its parameters based on the excitation frequency. The MPPT employs a two-dimensional hill-climbing algorithm, utilizing a specialized power detection technique to monitor the harvested power. By incorporating the concept of acceleration into the MPPT framework, the tracking speed toward the maximum power point is significantly enhanced. The proposed system achieves a peak MPPT efficiency of 99.9% and a 3-dB bandwidth of 43 Hz, outperforming SEH by 248% in MPPT efficiency and 1204% in bandwidth, and surpassing SECE by 135% in MPPT efficiency and 253% in bandwidth. Implemented in the digital domain, the MPPT controller occupies a compact area of only 0.039 mm2while consuming merely 0.802 μW.

title: A 915MHz Wide-Input Range CMOS Rectifier With Variable Common-Mode Feedback Achieving 75.2% Peak Efficiency.
abstract: This paper presents a CMOS RF-DC rectifier that extends power-conversion efficiency (PCE) over a wide-input range by introducing an output-referenced, variable common-mode feedback (VCMFB) loop. The VCMFB circuit dynamically adjusts the PMOS gate bias by changing the common-mode feedback coefficient (β) from the rectifier output. A search scheme for VOUT-peak is designed to obtain the optimum β over a wide-input range. The proposed rectifier is fabricated in a 180-nm CMOS process, occupying an area of 0.36 mm2. Measurement results show a sensitivity of -13.9 dBm with a 1 MΩ load and a peak PCE of 75.2% at -6.8 dBm with a 3kΩ load. Furthermore, the proposed rectifier achieves a power dynamic range (PDR) of 18.3 dB with a load below 3kΩ.

title: ViMA: A Decoupled FPGA Accelerator for Vision Mamba with Resource-Space Exploration.
abstract: Vision Mamba (ViM) adapts the Mamba to images via bidirectional state-space scanning, delivering strong accuracy with lower latency and memory footprint. Recent FPGA accelerators largely optimize the original Mamba formulation, with quantization co-design and generic SSM dataflows, rather than ViM’s bidirectional scan setting, which causes difficulties for fully streaming implementations and larger resource overhead. To solve these challenges, we present ViMA, an FPGA accelerator tailored for Vision Mamba. ViMA decouples computation into a Selective SSM module and a Full-stream module with a streaming architecture. At runtime, an interleaved, time-multiplexed schedule exposes bidirectional scan parallelism without duplicating resources. We further introduce a resource-space exploration method that finds balanced configurations and enables deeper pipeline optimizations under a fixed resource budget. Implemented on a Xilinx ZCU15EG platform, ViMA achieves up to 30.2× and 2.84× higher energy efficiency than NVIDIA RTX 3090 and RTX A6000 baselines, respectively, demonstrating that decoupling and resource-space exploration are effective for ViM on edge FPGAs.

title: Multi-Retention and Bit-Level Approximate STT-MRAM for High-Efficiency AI Applications.
abstract: Magnetoresistive random-access memory (MRAM) is a strong alternative to dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) in the future main memory domain with its extremely low static power consumption and fast read/write speeds. However, existing designs fail to leverage the advantage of MRAM in the field of deep neural networks (DNNs), where data volumes are increasingly massive. In this paper, we propose a multi-retention MRAM architecture along with approximate computing (AC) based on spin-transfer torque MRAM (STT-MRAM) to improve write energy efficiency. Additionally, we put forward a fully pipelined read scheme to enhance read speed utilizing the standard array. Finally, we further optimize the approximation strategy through algorithms and conduct evaluation and validation on convolutional neural networks (CNN) and transformer-based models. The proposed architecture is evaluated using a 28 nm process combined with a SPICE model of the STT-MRAM. Simulation results indicate that the write energy consumption for activations using low data retention time is reduced by 79.8%, and the approximate strategy further reduces it by 28.3%, while the maximum model accuracy loss remains below 2.8%.

title: A Rate-Distortion-Complexity Analysis of Neural Video CODECs.
abstract: We study the decision-making process for choosing video compression systems through a rate-distortion- complexity (RDC) analysis. We use a Lagrangian cost D + λR + γC, such that choosing the best video codec among a number of candidates for an application demands selecting appropriate (λ, γ) values. Thus, we argue that an application may be associated with a (λ, γ) point, so that all possibilities of (λ, γ) span all the application space. An example streaming application was given as a case study. Furthermore, we can span the plane and compare codecs for the entire application space filled with different (λ, γ) choices. We then compared several state-of-the-art neural video codecs using the proposed metrics. Results are informative and surprising. We found that, within our RDC computation constraints, only a few neural video codecs came out as the best suited for any application, depending on where its desirable (λ, γ) lies.

title: Live Demonstration: An Efficient and Compact Visuo-Tactile Perception System.
abstract: This demonstration presents a compact visuo-tactile processing system based on the near-sensor neural network processor NS-Engine, targeting resource-constrained embedded tactile perception scenarios. The system employs a customized sensor that encodes tactile attributes into RGB images, which are then processed in real time at the near-sensor edge by the NS-Engine integrated on an FPGA platform. Leveraging a compute-in-memory(CIM) architecture and optimized system design, the solution significantly reduces physical size and power consumption while effectively overcoming the data transfer bottleneck of traditional von Neumann architectures. The solution provides an efficient and miniaturized tactile perception solution for intelligent edge devices.

title: Automatic Tuning of Effective "On" Resistance of Switches in N-path filters.
abstract: We propose a fully automated, process-, temperature- and clock-frequency- insensitive "effective on" resistance control technique for N-path filter architectures. A negative feedback-based control loop dynamically adjusts the clock generator bias until the "effective on" resistance of the N-path switches equals that of a reference resistor. This removes the necessity of calibrating the clock driver strengths to adjust for the requisite sharpness of the rise- and fall-times, which ultimately determine the out-of-band rejection of mixer-first-receivers. The proposed solution has been verified with simulations and is shown to offer an "effective on" resistance tracking across various process, temperature, and clock-frequency ranges. This helps achieve a robust, ambient condition invariant frequency response in N-path filters across a range of center frequencies.

title: Load Impedance Matching for Kinetic Energy Harvesters Operating under Displacement Constraint.
abstract: We theoretically derive the optimal load and corresponding power limits for a kinetic energy harvester based on a two-port model and with constrained displacement and experiencing harmonic input vibration (acceleration). Our results generalize both previous similar efforts of general complex load without displacement constraints, and resistive loads with displacement constraints. We give a discussion about the implications of these results for realistic implementation of optimal non-linear electrical conditioning of harvesters described by this model, such as piezoelectric kinetic energy harvesters.

title: Radiation-Hardened Circuit for Chaos-Based Characterization of Cosmic Ray Dynamics in Space Missions.
abstract: This paper presents a radiation-hardened circuit for characterizing cosmic ray dynamics using chaos theory. The proposed system identifies chaotic behavior in real time by reconstructing the Takens attractor and computing Lyapunov exponents. Experimental data include ground-based neutron flux measurements and charged particle data from the Galileo mission to Jupiter. The results indicate that cosmic ray interactions can be modeled as a deterministic chaotic system. When interacting with semiconductor devices, cosmic rays may induce single-event upsets (SEUs), observed as bit-flips in SRAM cells. The proposed circuit estimates the time intervals between SEUs, enabling a predictive fault-tolerance approach for spaceborne electronics and in situ monitoring of cosmic radiation.

title: SuperCIM: A Charge-domain CIM with 3D Parallelism Reconfigurability based on Asynchronous NoC Protocol.
abstract: Modern neural networks employing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have become fundamental to computer vision and natural language processing. However, conventional reconfigurable Computing-in-Memory (CIM) architectures suffer from approximately 30% throughput degradation caused by mismatches between channel dimensions and kernel sizes across network layers. This design enhances CNN processing efficiency through co-optimization at the circuit, architecture, and dataflow levels by integrating an energy-efficient charge-domain splice protocol with a flexible Network-on-Chip (NoC), enabling 3D-reconfigurable parallelism. Experimental results demonstrate that SuperCIM achieves a peak throughput of 2.91 TOPS with 4.44× energy efficiency compared with SOTA designs.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Compensation Pixel Circuits under Bending-Induced Degradation.
abstract: Flexible active-matrix displays face reliability challenges due to threshold-voltage (VT) shifts in thin-film transistors (TFTs) under electrical bias and mechanical bending. However, existing compensation circuit studies are often based on different device technologies and stress conditions, limiting fair comparison. This work presents a unified evaluation of representative compensation pixel circuits using identical VTdegradation models derived from experimentally measured amorphous silicon TFTs under bias stress and mechanical strain. Individual TFT measurements show that tensile bending slightly improves, while compressive bending accelerates, VT-induced current degradation by up to 30%. Circuit-level simulations reveal that ∆VT-sensing architectures achieve superior compensation and faster programming than charge-transfer designs, albeit with larger area and higher routing complexity. A figure of merit (FOM) is introduced to quantitatively assess stability, power and area efficiency, confirming that ∆VT-sensing circuits achieve the highest performance-to-complexity ratio. These insights provide design guidelines for reliable and efficient flexible AMOLED systems.

title: Subharmonic to Superharmonic Optical Injection Locking of Ring Oscillators in Standard CMOS.
abstract: Non-contact clock synchronization via external optical injection is proposed and demonstrated in a standard CMOS process. A visible-wavelength LED (523 nm) provides pulsed optical excitation that illuminates the die surface. On-chip photodiode-coupled ring oscillators recover the optical timing and use the generated photocurrent for injection locking anywhere within the die. Fundamental, subharmonic, and superharmonic locking are achieved over a 1–10 MHz span, with a maximum locking range of 21% at an average incident irradiance of 550 µW/mm2.

title: Grid-Forming Inverters for Enhancing Grid Stability via Synthetic Inertia and Damping.
abstract: The transition of power grids from systems based on synchronous generators to those integrating increasing shares of renewable energy sources (RES) reduces system inertia and challenges frequency stability, particularly in weak grids. Grid-forming (GFM) control has emerged as a key solution, enabling inverter-based resources to provide synthetic inertia and autonomous grid support. This paper proposes a method for assigning virtual inertia and damping coefficients to multiple GFM inverters in a microgrid or distribution feeder. The objective is to ensure that the aggregated dynamic response at the point of common coupling aligns with target values specified by the grid operator. The proposed method is validated through simulations on an IEEE test network.

title: An Ultra-Low Power Relaxation Oscillator for IoT Power Management Applications.
abstract: This paper presents the design of an ultra-low power relaxation oscillator for Internet-of-Things (IoT) power management applications. The new design employs a dual-comparator architecture with a novel dynamic biasing technique to minimize power consumption. The biasing of both comparators is dynamically regulated to ensure their operation only during decision-making events, substantially reducing power consumption. The proposed oscillator achieves a power consumption of only 74.6nW at a stable frequency of 1.2kHz, exhibiting a standard deviation of merely 74Hz. The new design demonstrates a 73% reduction in power compared to the conventional design. The circuit is simulated in a 65nm, 1.2V CMOS process, with all results verified by post-layout simulation.

title: Comparison of Feature Selection Methods for High-Dimensional Small Datasets.
abstract: Machine learning (ML) techniques are widely applied in healthcare, ranging from precision healthcare to thepossibility of preventive care. A general problem in clinicalstudies is the combination of high dimensionality and low samplesizes, complicating the process of extracting significant indicatorsfrom the feature set. In this paper, we compare the quality ofthree feature selection methods when the number of samplesis low compared to the number of features. The results arecompared to those of earlier research that used an optimizationprocess applied to recursive feature elimination. The two filtermethods, Anova and chi-squared, were unable to produce stableresults, whereas the embedded Lasso method showed morepromising outcomes.

title: A Ringamp-Based Low-Noise Bias Generation Technique.
abstract: This paper presents a low-noise bias generation technique utilizing a ring amplifier (ringamp). By exploiting the property of ringamps that allows fast driving when the error is high and subthreshold biasing of the output stage in steady state, a low-bandwidth operation is achieved, thereby reducing the integrated noise. The proposed technique is applied to generate a low-noise bias for the level-shifting capacitor (CLS) used in amplifiers. RC-extracted simulation of a ringamp-based closed-loop gain-of-two amplifier implemented in a 28-nm CMOS process demonstrates a 6.2× reduction in noise power on CLSacross PVT variations and a 33% reduction in amplifier power consumption compared to an amplifier with a conventional capacitor-based level shifter.

title: Exploring the Phase Noise Reduction Limits of Stacked Ring Oscillators.
abstract: Recent progress in oscillator stacking techniques has revealed its potential to achieve substantial phase noise reduction with minimal power and area overhead. Building on our previous work that introduced a four-level stacked ring oscillator employing current reuse for injection locking, this study extends the analysis to determine how many oscillators can be effectively stacked under a fixed supply voltage. The objective is to establish design guidelines, identify the practical limits of the technique, and derive analytical expressions that support these findings. In the stacked architecture, the supply current is shared while the supply voltage is divided among the oscillators, enabling simultaneous operation and phase noise improvement. Post-layout simulations in TSMC 65 nm show an average 3 dB phase noise improvement each time the number of stacked oscillators doubles, with the benefit saturating once the per-oscillator voltage drops below the device threshold. These results define the practical limits of the stacking approach and guide its optimal design.

title: Voltage-Controlled Delay Line for Precise Phase Tuning of a 10-MHz Clock in Integrated Dual Active Bridge Converters.
abstract: This paper presents the design, simulations and measurement results of an integrated Voltage-Controlled Delay Line (VCDL) to ensure reliable phase regulation in Dual Active Bridge (DAB) converters. The proposed architecture employs a current-mode delay control mechanism and an internally generated supply voltage to achieve fine phase modulation with minimal duty-cycle distortion of 1.5% for the output clock signal. Simulation and measurement results show excellent agreement, with a maximum deviation of 5% for voltage-to-phase-shift characteristics. An external trimming mechanism compensates for phase shift deviations exceeding 30% of clock period with reliable timing performance across all operating conditions. Moreover, the circuit demonstrates strong robustness against supply voltage variations in the range between 4.5 V - 5.5 V, without affecting phase shift accuracy. These features make the proposed circuit well-suited for integration in high-frequency, closed-loop control systems requiring accurate phase regulation.

title: Live Demonstration: Transformer-Based Visual Object Detection and Tracking on MPSoC.
abstract: Visual object detectors with transformers are very demanding models for hardware constrained devices such as FPGAs or custom solutions. This live demonstration shows a design that integrates our own nano version of the off-the-shelf RT-DETR transformer with a custom tracker. Our design provides a frame rate of more than 5 fps with images of 640 × 480 pixels for tracking faces on a ZCU-102 MPSoC with a drop in AP50 precision for object detection from 53.6 in floating-point representation to 51.9 with our own nano model quantized to INT8. The tracker keeps the identity of a given face for its whole trajectory while in the field of view of the camera, addressing the lack of detections at faster frame rates.

title: A Comparative Study of Multilevel PWM Techniques with Circuit Non-Idealities in Class-D Audio Power Amplifiers.
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of several multilevel pulse-width modulation (PWM) techniques and their impact on a class-D power amplifier for high-fidelity audio systems. The techniques involved in this analysis are phase (PH), phase opposition (PO), alternate phase oppositions (APO) and phase shifted carrier (PSC) disposition used with a natural-sampled PWM and for the cases of two, five and nine output levels. The analysis takes into account some non-idealities that may arise in the effective implementation of the class-D, particularly jitter and gain error of the PWM carriers, offset and rms noise of the comparators which determine the level of the signal. The system, except for the aforementioned non-idealities, is modeled as an ideal closed-loop class-D amplifier, with a 3rd order loop filter. The simulation results show that the PSC technique has the best robustness against carrier gain error and offset, while the modulation techniques are equivalent when considering the others non-idealities.

title: RC-Scaled Timing-Driven Routing: Bridging Targeted Timing Optimization and Massively.
abstract: Global routing faces dual challenges in nanometer IC design: interconnect delay dominance from technology scaling and escalating computational demands. Timing-driven approaches have been extensively explored, and recent advancements in GPU acceleration have significantly improved the scalability of global routing. However, the synergistic integration of timing optimization and GPU acceleration in global routing remains largely unstudied, leaving a critical scalability gap for modern IC timing closure. This work advances prior timing-driven methods through a GPU-accelerated framework with massive parallelism. We propose a resistance-capacitance (RC)-scaled timing cost model that enables effective optimization in massively parallel global routing flows, and a two-stage net ordering strategy that enhances global routing quality. An adaptive cost-scaling strategy is introduced in rip-up and reroute (RRR) stage to further reduce overflow. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves superior result in both timing and routability compared to the first-place router in the ISPD25 routing contest.

title: SCONE: A Practical, Constraint-Aware Plug-in for Latent Encoding in Learned DNA Storage.
abstract: DNA storage has matured from concept to practical stage, yet its integration with neural compression pipelines remains inefficient. Early DNA encoders applied redundancy-heavy constraint layers atop raw binary data-workable but primitive. Recent neural codecs compress data into learned latent representations with rich statistical structure, yet still convert these latents to DNA via naive binary-to-quaternary transcoding, discarding the entropy model's optimization. This mismatch undermines compression efficiency and complicates the encoding stack. A plug-in module that collapses latent compression and DNA encoding into a single step. SCONE performs quaternary arithmetic coding directly on the latent space in DNA bases. Its Constraint-Aware Adaptive Coding module dynamically steers the entropy encoder's learned probability distribution to enforce biochemical constraints-GC balance and homopolymer suppression-deterministically during encoding, eliminating post-hoc correction. The design preserves full reversibility and exploits the hyperprior model's learned priors without modification. Experiments show SCONE achieves near-perfect constraint satisfaction with negligible computational overhead (< 2% latency), establishing a latent-agnostic interface for end-to-end DNA-compatible learned codecs.

title: Hardware-Algorithm Co-Design of a CORDIC-based Nonlinear Unit for low-power edge RNN inference.
abstract: Nonlinear functions such as sigmoid and tanh can become major contributors to latency and energy in ultra-low-power recurrent neural network (RNN) inference, especially when executed on a general-purpose core alongside MAC accelerators. This work presents a hardware-algorithm co-design of a pipelined CORDIC-based nonlinear processing unit (NLPU) optimized for sigmoid and hyperbolic tangent computation in always-on edge AI systems. By exploiting symmetries arising from the sigmoid function, the proposed architecture achieves up to 75x area reduction compared to other CORDIC implementations while maintaining a maximum error below one LSB across the input range [-8, 8). Synthesized in 22 nm FD-SOI, the NLPU occupies 11.46k µm2and consumes 948 nW, representing up to three orders of magnitude lower power than prior works. Integrated within an RNN accelerator, it sustains 1 operation per cycle throughput and supports 8/16-bit precision modes. End-to-end evaluation on the Google Speech Commands dataset demonstrates no accuracy loss compared to full-precision inference, validating the proposed CORDIC methodology as an effective solution for energy-constrained AI applications.

title: Power-Efficient Spiking Conversion of Deep Unfolded Transformers.
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) present strong potential for power-efficient edge applications because of their sparsity and event-driven computation. However, direct training of SNNs is particularly challenging for large and customized transformers because of their non-differentiable spike dynamics. To overcome this challenge, Transformer-to-SNN conversion methods have been proposed to leverage existing architectures, but these approaches often suffer from significant performance degradation and high firing rates, which diminish the efficiency benefits of SNNs. In this paper, we propose a conversion approach inspired by the Few Spikes (FS) method and adapt it to the complex deep unfolding sparse transformer (DUST), enabling the conversion of major transformer components. We validate the proposed spiking DUST on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano platform. Experimental results show that the converted model achieves comparable reconstruction quality to the original DUST while reducing power consumption by approximately 25%, demonstrating its potential for power-efficient edge deployment.

title: TRACEFORMER: Trace-Efficient and Robust Transformer-Based Late-Fusion Side-Channel Analysis of Masked AES.
abstract: Side-channel analysis (SCA) exposes vulnerabilities in cryptographic circuits by exploiting physical leakage such as power or electromagnetic emanations. Deep learning (DL) has significantly improved SCA, but most architectures, such as CNNs, struggle to generalize under practical conditions like masking and temporal misalignment. This paper investigates a transformer-based approach that uses a pretrained BERT pathway for plaintext and a linear embedding for traces, fused for masked S-box classification. A dual-path late-fusion architecture combines trace and plaintext embeddings to predict masked AES S-box values. Experiments on ASCAD variable-key datasets show key-rank 0 recovery with only 9 traces in the aligned case and robustness under desynchronization (305 and 444 traces for desynchronization 50 and 100). We further analyze the impact of the size of the training set and the model components, showing that removing positional encoding improves performance by 18.7% and that the optimal profile size lies between 60-90k traces. The results demonstrate that attention-based models can effectively evaluate circuit leakage, providing insight into countermeasure design for secure embedded systems. PoI-optimized methods (e.g., EstraNet) achieve 5-7 traces on selected windows; under our stricter fixed-window, full-key, cross-desync protocol we reach a closely comparable 9 traces (aligned), prioritizing protocol efficiency over PoI-specific tuning.

title: A Low-Power, Single-Comparator, Differential Level-Crossing ADC.
abstract: This paper presents a low-power, clockless level-crossing analog-to-digital converter (LC-ADC) in a 65nm CMOS process for applications with sparse input signals. The proposed LC-ADC uses only one continuous-time comparator for event-driven sampling, leading to low power consumption and reduced chip area. Post-layout simulations of the LC-ADC show a peak of 6.4 ENOB for an input signal bandwidth from 5Hz to 10kHz, with a minimum average power consumption of 398nW from a 1V supply voltage.

title: Toward Generative Silicon: The Next Frontier in Open-Source and AI-Driven Analog Design.
abstract: Integrated circuit (IC) design is undergoing a noticeable shift as AI-assisted tools and code-driven layout frameworks begin to influence established workflows. Automation has reshaped digital design over the past two decades. However, analog and mixed-signal design remains largely manual and dependent on layout expertise, device intuition, and iterative refinement. In practice, analog design has become the point at which current methodologies struggle most and, therefore, the area in which new approaches are emerging first. Recent work on programmatic layout, such as gLayout, shows that expressing circuits as structured code rather than fixed geometry allows new forms of interaction, including automatic generation, refinement, and correction based on feedback. In parallel, large language models are beginning to work with design intent and constraints, not just code templates, suggesting a shift in how tools may participate in the process. This paper describes the current stage of this transition. It discusses the main technical obstacles—verification, evaluation, data availability, and trust—and argues that machine-interpretable circuit representations may be a necessary step toward more scalable design automation.

title: Jitter Reduction in Voltage Controlled Oscillators for Clocking at Cryogenic Temperature.
abstract: Operating Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor (CMOS) at cryogenic temperature offers multitude of advantages including higher device ON current, lower subthreshold leakage, superior switching characteristics, lower thermal noise floor, better digital noise margins etc. Generating high fidelity clocks at low temperature thus becomes critical for achieving high performance. The devices, however, demonstrate higher flicker noise at low temperature giving rise to higher phase noise in clock generation circuit components like voltage-controlled oscillators which further translate to higher jitter. We propose a new method of reverse body biasing to reduce the phase noise and jitter at cryogenic temperature when conventional techniques like supply voltage reduction do not yield expected returns. In this simulation study, we fit BSIM models to measured device I-V and noise data on 22nm Fully Depleted Silicon on Insulator (FDSOI) and show the improvement in the jitter and phase noise performance with our new proposed method.

title: SHAP-AAD: DeepSHAP-Guided Channel Reduction for EEG Auditory Attention Detection.
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based auditory attention detection (AAD) offers a non-invasive way to enhance hearing aids, but conventional methods rely on too many electrodes, limiting wearability and comfort. This paper presents SHAP-AAD, a two-stage framework that combines DeepSHAP-based channel selection with a lightweight temporal convolutional network (TCN) for efficient AAD using fewer channels.DeepSHAP, an explainable AI technique, is applied to a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on topographic alpha-power maps to rank channel importance, and the top-k EEG channels are used to train a compact TCN. Experiments on the DTU dataset show that using 32 channels yields comparable accuracy to the full 64-channel setup (79.21% vs. 81.06%) on average. In some cases, even 8 channels can deliver satisfactory accuracy. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of SHAP-AAD in reducing complexity while preserving high detection performance.

title: A Time-Domain Verification Framework for Digitally-Trained Op Amp and Ring-Oscillator Based Analog Spiking Neural Network.
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) implemented using analog circuits offer substantial energy efficiency compared to digital realizations, but verifying their time-domain behavior remains challenging. Analog neurons, such as op-amp and ringoscillator (RO)-based leaky integrate-and-fire models, exhibit nonlinear dynamics that can diverge from their digitally trained counterparts, particularly at high spike rates due to discretization approximations like the bilinear transform. To address these challenges, we present a time-domain verification and visualization framework that allows users to configure network architectures, neuron models, including a new RO-based neuron architecture, and spike encoding schemes, and automatically generates Simulink-based simulations that reproduce analog dynamics. The framework provides real-time visualization of spiking activity, membrane potentials, and layer-wise dynamics, enabling both educational exploration and practical debugging. Demonstrations on the Iris dataset show that the framework achieves waveform-equivalent behavior to transistor-level simulations in Cadence Spectre while providing over an order-of-magnitude speedup. By combining interactive visualization with configurable neuron models, including the novel RO neuron, the framework offers an intuitive platform for understanding and verifying analog SNNs.

A 1-tap DFE matched receiver equalization is implemented with boosted CTLE, slew rate boosting in TX. Power efficiency is achieved with merged design and layout techniques. The proposed design achieves 0.45pJ/bit power efficiency on a 5-inch channel M.2 2280 NVMe SSD product.

title: Direct Neural ADC via Level-crossing Quantization: Feasibility, Trade-Offs, and Design Guidelines.
abstract: Level-crossing (LC)-ADCs are valued for their input adaptivity in sensing biomedical systems, yet all reported implementations still rely on a preceding analog front end (AFE). This work investigates whether an LC-ADC can operate as a direct ADC with inputs tied to electrodes, i.e., without a preceding amplifier. The study is analytical rather than a circuit proposal. We develop closed-form relations linking power, noise, loop gain and bandwidth, and show that by leveraging the spectral statistical characteristics of real neural signals (containing noise, seizure events, etc.), the required LC-ADC power can be reduced by 78× to sub-µW region, demonstrating the feasibility of direct neural quantization. While noise-shaping ADCs can match this power, their fixed-rate sampling wastes energy transmitting largely redundant data during low-activity periods. Analysis of 10-hour EEG/iEEG recordings (including noise, artifacts, etc.) using an LC-ADC shows a 79% reduction in transmitted data relative to fixed-rate sampling, proportionally lowering telemetry energy. We then examine whether LC-ADCs can directly quantize high-dynamic-range (HDR) signals with large artifacts (e.g., from stimulation) and show that conventional LC-ADCs are impractical due to poor energy efficiency at high input DRs. To address this, we outline architectural strategies that combine LC adaptivity with HDR efficiency, including adaptive LC with reactive or predictive range control, and noise-shaped LC.

title: A Chopping Technique for High Input Impedance Biopotential Instrumentation Amplifiers.
abstract: This paper presents a chopping technique applied to a Current-Balancing Instrumentation Amplifier (CBIA) with overall feedback, leading to an intrinsically high Zinwithout compromising key performance metrics. The proposed technique unfolds the switching actions into two copies of the input transconductance amplifier (TCA) stage of the CBIA, providing a pathway to upconvert flicker noise using only a single chopper at the TCA output while not needing any series switches on the TCA inputs. Overall feedback in the CBIA ensures a robust operation across PVT. Furthermore, the CBIA features a passive electrode DC offset (EDO) removal scheme, and an area-efficient switched-capacitor notch filter (SC-NF) that suppresses unwanted artifacts arising from the applied chopping technique. Post-layout simulation results show that the proposed chopping technique attenuates flicker noise by ~ 20 dB across process corners, resulting in an in-band noise of 2.95 μVrmsover a 1 kHz bandwidth, while the IA achieves a sub-Hz and 50 Hz Zin> 75 GΩ and > 6 GΩ, respectively. The proposed IA consumes 6.2 μW from a 1 V supply, resulting in an NEF and PEF of 8.97 and 80.54, respectively, and occupies 0.04 mm2of area.

title: A Miniaturized In-Mouth pH Sensing System for Real-Time lntraoral Telemetry.
abstract: Dental caries is one of the most common chronic diseases worldwide, caused by acid production from bacterial metabolism of fermentable carbohydrates and affecting people of all ages. To evaluate the cariogenic and erosive properties of widely consumed food products, such as energy drinks, intraoral pH changes are measured during consumption. The gold standard for such measurements is miniaturized silicon-lithium-barium glass membrane electrodes. These electrodes allow dental plaque to form on their surface, thereby enabling in situ monitoring of pH changes in a biologically relevant environment. Due to their high impedance and susceptibility to external interference, they can currently only be measured using a large analog amplification and recording unit, which is highly limiting for study design and participant comfort, as individual measurements can take upwards of an hour. This work presents the first battery-powered, low-power wireless and wearable pH telemetry evaluation system designed for real-time intraoral pH monitoring with glass electrodes. The system comprises a miniaturized pH telemetry front-end, a neck-worn Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) node, and software tools for data acquisition, visualization, and reporting. The front end integrates with a custom dental prosthesis, directly digitizing the pH signal in the mouth and minimizing noise. The data is transmitted over BLE to a host computer, and analyzed using dedicated software that supports calibration, drift compensation, region marking, and PDF report generation. The system integrates an 8.6 by 3.3mm, 0.2g pH front-end and a 37.6g neck-worn BLE node which consume 8.89 mW to transmit data at 10 Hz to a host computer during a measurement. A five-hour continuous validation using standard calibration solutions (pH 4, 7, 10) demonstrates system stability with a drift of only 0.005 pH/min, and an effective response rate of 1.875 pH/s, confirming robust sensing and reliable wireless telemetry.

title: Compressive Light-Field Image Coding with Spatial-Angular Measurement Prediction.
abstract: Light Field (LF) images capture scene information across both spatial and angular dimensions, enabling rich 3D visual effects but producing massive data volumes. Conventional pixel-based and learning-based codecs achieve high compression efficiency but require heavy computation for reconstruction and rate-distortion (R-D) optimization at the encoder, making them impractical for resource-constrained capture environments. To address this issue, we propose an asymmetric LF compression framework operating in the measurement domain. In the proposed method, each view is reordered according to the proposed serpentine scan and projected into a low-dimensional measurement space via block compressive sensing (BCS). This process allows both spatial and angular correlations to be efficiently compressed through measurement-domain prediction without requiring pixel reconstruction. Additionally, mode decision and coding are performed directly on the measurements, eliminating iterative R-D optimization and, together with the dimensionality reduction effect of CS, significantly reducing encoder complexity. The proposed encoder demonstrated a significant speed advantage on standard LF benchmarks, achieving up to 5 times faster encoding than HEVC and over 10 times faster than VVC at a comparable visual quality of around 35.8 dB. Furthermore, the proposed serpentine scan order preserves angular adjacency, enabling stable spatial-angular prediction and improved R-D performance.

title: An FPGA-Based SoC Architecture with a RISC-V Controller for Energy-Efficient Temporal-Coding Spiking Neural Networks.
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer high energy efficiency and event-driven computation, ideal for low-power edge AI. Their hardware implementation on FPGAs, however, faces challenges due to heavy computation, large memory use, and limited flexibility. This paper proposes a compact System-on-Chip (SoC) architecture for temporal-coding SNNs, integrating a RISC-V controller with an event-driven SNN core. It replaces multipliers with bitwise operations using binarized weights, includes a spike-time sorter for active spikes, and skips non-informative events to reduce computation. The architecture runs fully on a Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA, achieving up to 16× memory reduction for weights and lowering computational overhead and latency, with 97.0% accuracy on MNIST and 88.3% on Fashion-MNIST. This self-contained design provides an efficient, scalable platform for real-time neuromorphic inference at the edge.

title: An Electrochemical Sensing SoC for Autonomous Wound Monitoring.
abstract: This paper presents the first integrated electrochemical sensing system-on-chip (SoC) for autonomous wound monitoring, integrating a custom potentiostat analog front end, 12-bit dual-slope ADC, RISC-V processor, and neural processing unit (NPU) on a single silicon die. Conventional wound monitoring approaches rely on multi-chip architectures that separate sensing from processing, resulting in high power consumption and connectivity dependencies that limit continuous wearable operation. This work achieves monolithic integration of the complete signal chain from electrochemical transduction to biomarker quantification by unifying analog sensing, digital processing, and machine learning. This integration enables wearable point-of-care wound monitoring by reducing power and connectivity requirements. Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS with a 1.5 mm × 1.0 mm die area, the SoC operates at 3.0 mW with 153 pA current resolution while performing cyclic voltammetry measurements to capture wound biomarkers including lactate, pH, and uric acid, with the integrated NPU converting electrochemical measurements into quantitative biomarker concentrations for continuous wound assessment.

title: An Ultra-Low-Power Energy-Harvesting Wireless Transmitter with Nanowatt Duty-Cycled Operation for Autonomous Sensor Networks.
abstract: This paper presents and investigates an ultra-low-power wireless transmitter (TX), fabricated in a standard 130nm BiCMOS technology for energy-harvesting sensor network applications, and demonstrates its operation when powered by a thermoelectric generator (TEG). The proposed ultra-low-power transmitter enables battery-less short-range communication while maintaining a compact feature size. To achieve low-power operation, the transmitter employs injection-locking and frequency-multiplication techniques for ultra-low-power frequency synthesis, combined with on–off keying (OOK) modulation and an integrated duty-cycling mechanism for further power reduction. Operating in the 433MHz ISM band and supplied by dual voltages of 0.25V and 0.9V, the TX delivers –21dBm output power with a continuous-mode power consumption of approximately 100µW. Under aggressive duty-cycling, the average power is reduced to the nanowatt range (≈ 150nW), enabling operation from a compact thermoelectric generator driven by a small body-to-ambient temperature difference (ΔT2. These results demonstrate a significant advancement toward fully integrated, energy-autonomous wireless transmitters for wearable and industrial Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications.

title: Resistive switching of 2D material incorporated polymer based self-healing flexible memristor.
abstract: The composition of materials have a profound influence on the distinct resistance-switching characteristics of memristors. This study involves the fabrication and characterization of a self healing memristor device with copper electrodes on a glass substrate, having Poly Vinyl Alcohol (PVA)-reduced graphene oxide (PVA-rGO) or PVA-graphene switching layers in the configurations of Cu/PVA-rGO/Cu and Cu/PVA-graphene/Cu. XRD, SEM, and FTIR analyses provided insights into the composition and morphology of the switching layers, establishing a connection between device functionality and material properties. The resistive switching and memory characteristics of the device have been explored by means of Current-voltage (I-V) measurements, log I-V curve analysis, and potentiation/depression investigations. The PVA-rGO system exhibits a lower SET voltage compared to the PVA-graphene memristor. Furthermore, LTSPICE simulations were employed to analyze switching characteristics, aiming to replicate electrical responses and verify with the experimental I-V data. The results indicate the promise of PVA-based switching layers in memristor fabrication and proposed methods to enhance device performance for practical applications.

title: GUARDIAN: A Decoupled GNN Framework for Type-aware Hardware Trojan Detection.
abstract: With increased outsourcing of intellectual property (IP) cores to third-party vendors, system-on-chip designs face heightened security risks from hardware trojans (HTs) that can compromise integrity and functionality. Prior HT detection works typically train separate deep-learning models on combinational (TRTC-TC) and sequential (TRTC-TS) trojan benchmarks from the LEDA-based Trust-Hub dataset, treating them independently and framing detection as binary classification, which fails when both trojan types coexist in a single netlist. In contrast, our proposed method employs a unified Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based model trained on a mixed dataset comprising benchmarks from both TRTC-TC and TRTC-TS, enabling multi-class classification to distinguish between benign, combinational, and sequential trojans. The approach addresses key GNN constraints and attains strong detection performance on the mixed dataset: TPR of 99.3% and 100%, TNR of 99.99% and 99.9%, and PPV of 97.9% and 97% for combinational and sequential trojans, respectively.

title: SRAM-Based Compute-in-Memory Accelerator for Linear-decay Spiking Neural Networks.
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have emerged as a biologically inspired alternative to conventional deep networks, offering event-driven and energy-efficient computation. However, their throughput remains constrained by the serial update of neuron membrane states. While many hardware accelerators and Compute-in-Memory (CIM) architectures efficiently parallelize the synaptic operation (W × I) achieving $\mathcal{O}(1)$ complexity for matrix–vector multiplication, the subsequent state update step still requires $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time to refresh all neuron membrane potentials. This mismatch makes state update the dominant latency and energy bottleneck in SNN inference. To address this challenge, we propose an SRAM-based CIM for SNN with Linear Decay Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LD-LIF) Neuron that co-optimizes algorithm and hardware. At the algorithmic level, we replace the conventional exponential membrane decay with a linear decay approximation, converting costly multiplications into simple additions while accuracy drops only around 1%. At the architectural level, we introduce an in-memory parallel update scheme that performs in-place decay directly within the SRAM array, eliminating the need for global sequential updates. Evaluated on benchmark SNN workloads, the proposed method achieves a 1.1× to 16.7× reduction of SOP energy consumption, while providing 15.9× to 69× more energy efficiency, with negligible accuracy loss relative to original decay models. This work highlights that beyond accelerating the W×I computation, optimizing state-update dynamics within CIM architectures is essential for scalable, low-power, and real-time neuromorphic processing.

title: SilentBite: A Novel LLM-based framework for Automated Hardware Trojan Insertion.
abstract: We introduce SilentBite, a novel LLM-based framework for automated hardware Trojan (HT) insertion. Our framework uses hardware description language (HDL) files to find optimal HT insertion sites by targeting rare execution regions in circuits. Specifically, the framework first chunks HDL files based on module-block declarations and extracts signal metadata. Later, it identifies infrequent code paths and analyzes optimal HT types for attacks such as cryptographic, information leakage, and performance degradation attacks. Finally, it generates tailored HT implementations with scope-aware signal filtering and determines precise HT insertion sites in the circuit. We evaluated two SilentBite variants utilizing GPT-5 and Gemini respectively on four designs including cryptographic (AES) and communication (UART-RX/TX) benchmarks. The implanted HTs consistently evaded detection, degrading the performance of state-of-the-art HT detection tools by upto 22.9%.

title: An All-MOS 1-nA Current Reference Insensitive to Process and Voltage Variations.
abstract: This paper presents a 1-nA current reference with high immunity to process and voltage variations. Based on the β-multiplier structure, the proposed reference employs MOSFETs as resistors to reduce the area. To mitigate process sensitivity, a diode-connected NMOS with cascaded 2T-cells biases the NMOS resistors' gate voltage, compensating for process variations in threshold voltage (Vth) and mobility(μ) with minimal power consumption overhead. A feedback branch, together with cascode transistors, significantly enhances power supply stability. The prototype chip, fabricated in 0.18 μm CMOS, occupies an active area of 0.018 mm2and consumes 6 nA. The measured line sensitivity is 0.04%/V over a supply voltage range from 1.5 V to 2.5 V, among the lowest in the state-of-the-art nA current references. The average output current measured across 15 chips is 1.068 nA, exhibiting a low untrimmed variation coefficient (σ/μ) of 2.96%.

title: A 6-bit 2.15-GS/s 1.05-mW Flash-Assisted Time-Domain ADC with 0.8-V supply.
abstract: This work presents a flash-assisted time-domain Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) that uses a passively-interpolated Time-to-Digital Converter (TDC) and a gain-tunable Voltage-to-Time Converter (VTC) to enhance bandwidth and reduce power consumption. The prototype ADC is implemented in a 28-nm CMOS technology and achieves a Nyquist SNDR of 32.7 dB at 2.15 GS/s consuming just 1.05 mW. The Walden figure of merit (FOMw) is 13.4 fJ/c-s.

title: A Temperature-Adaptive Bias Generator with Threshold-Voltage Compensation from 3.6 K to 410 K.
abstract: In this paper, we present a temperature-adaptive bias generator (TABG) with threshold-voltage compensation, which is capable of operating from high to deep cryogenic temperatures. The threshold voltage of metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) increases by several hundred millivolts from high to deep cryogenic temperatures, which shifts the circuit’s operating point and may even lead to functional failure. To address this challenge, we propose a compact, low-power threshold-voltage compensated temperature-adaptive bias generator. The proposed design comprises two stacked MOSFETs with specifically selected aspect ratios. One diode-connected MOSFET with an inverse aspect ratio serves as a microampere-level, low-temperature-dependence current source. The other MOSFET, of the same type but with a large aspect ratio, converts a constant bias into a temperature-adaptive bias voltage, whose temperature sensitivity is approximately equal to that of the threshold voltage. Fabricated using a 0.18 μm process, the proposed design occupies an area of 328 μm2, consumes 28 µW, and has been validated to operate in an ultra-wide temperature range from 3.6 K to 410 K.

title: A 0.156 NEF Transimpedance Amplifier with Analog-Domain Multi-Band Fusion Technique for High-sensitivity and Broadband Hydrophones.
abstract: Underwater acoustic systems employ bulky sonar devices with inherently limited bandwidth. This work addresses the fundamental sensitivity-bandwidth trade-off in piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducer (PMUT) through an innovative analog-domain multi-band fusion technique. We present a multi-channel fused transimpedance amplifier (TIA) implemented in 180-nm CMOS for high-sensitivity, broadband hydrophones. The proposed architecture combines analog-domain signal fusion with a capacitive-feedback TIA topology, achieving simultaneous area and power efficiency. When integrated with a compact 3 mm × 2 mm PMUT array, the system demonstrates 129% fractional bandwidth and 523 V/MPa sensitivity. The single-channel configuration achieves an input-referred noise (IRN) density of 10 pA/√Hz@1MHz with noise efficiency factor (NEF) of 0.093 while the triple-channel design attains a NEF of 0.156, representing an exceptional low-power solution that enables high-resolution underwater sensing.

title: A Heterogeneous Decision Spiking Transformer Accelerator with Locality-dependent KV Product Cache and Compute Pattern Reconfigurable Engine.
abstract: Embodied Artificial Intelligence (EAI) represents an emerging challenging research area which emphasizes the tight integration of perception, cognition, and actuation in real-world environments. Leveraging transformer architectures for sequential action generation has shown remarkable potential in EAI workloads. However, existing EAI accelerators struggle to meet the stringent power and accuracy requirements of embodied deployment. Neuromorphic computing, characterized by its event-driven and energy-efficient nature, offers a promising computational paradigm that aligns well with the requirements of EAI. In this work, we propose a decision spiking transformer based neuromorphic accelerator, specifically designed for EAI applications. The proposed architecture introduces a locality-dependent KV product cache, a compute-pattern reconfigurable engine and a heterogeneous core to efficiently handle the dynamic computation patterns of spiking transformers. We evaluate our design on multiple MuJoCo Gym benchmark tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that our accelerator achieves up to 10.9× improvement in energy efficiency over state-of-the-art EAI accelerators, while maintaining high task performance of 92.4, 105.3 and 101.5 average normalized score in HalfCheetah, Hopper and Walker2D, respectively. These findings highlight a feasible pathway toward neuromorphic hardware deployment for EAI.

title: A Transient-Enhanced Buck Converter Based on Capacitor Current Adaptive On-Time (CCAOT) Control.
abstract: This paper presents a transient-enhanced buck converter based on capacitor current adaptive on-time (CCAOT) control. The capacitor current modulation scheme achieves an ultra-fast transient response under load step-up conditions. However, due to its inherent control characteristics, the response during load step-down remains limited. To overcome this limitation, a transient enhancement module is introduced, which enables the converter to achieve ultra-fast load transient performance during both load step-up and step-down conditions without compromising stability. The prototype is fabricated in a 0.18 μm CMOS process, operates at a switching frequency of 2 MHz, and supports a load current range from 0.5 A to 1.5 A. The load current slew rate is 1 A/100ns.

title: A 16- ENOB 2nd order Noise-Shaping SAR ADC with Mismatch Error Shaping and Optimized Switch Charge Injection Balancing.
abstract: This paper presents a 12-bit noise-shaping (NS) successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) featuring a second-order loop filter and on-chip mismatch error shaping (MES). The design employs a fully dynamic folded-input amplifier (FIA) shared between the integration paths to achieve a compact and power-efficient architecture with a sharp noise transfer function. Top-plate sampling scheme facilitates MES implementation while reducing CDAC area. To suppress nonlinearity caused by asymmetric switching, the switch sizes are optimized to balance charge injection. The ADC decomposes classic high-order noise shaping into low-order shaping, multi-bit quantization, and MES. Implemented in 180nm CMOS, simulation results demonstrate clear second-order noise shaping and improved linearity, achieving an SNDR of 98.1 dB within a 10-kHz bandwidth, leading to a Schreier figure-of-merit (FoMs) of 177dB.

title: A Fast-Transient Buck Converter with Oversampled Multi-Phase-Ramp PWM Control.
abstract: This paper presents a voltage-mode buck converter employing an oversampled multi-phase-ramp (OSMR) PWM control technique to achieve enhanced load transient response. The proposed OSMR-PWM scheme utilizes N-phase time-interleaved ramp signals to sample level crossings with the error amplifier output, enabling rapid detection of output voltage (VOUT) transients. Unlike transient enhancement techniques, such as ripple-based control and other nonlinear methods that increase the duty cycle, the proposed technique does not alter the compensation logic of constant-frequency PWM control. It solely increases the sampling frequency, thereby mitigating the phase margin degradation caused by the zero-order hold (ZOH) effect inherent in the sampling process. Consequently, the proposed approach achieves a faster response to any load transient without introducing VOUTovershoot. In contrast to conventional voltage-mode PWM control, this approach improves transient performance by effectively boosting the loop bandwidth, without increasing the power stage switching frequency (FSW). Implemented in a 180-nm BCD process, the proposed converter was simulated as a 12:1 step-down converter operating at 1MHz FSW. The results demonstrate a 61.1% reduction in VOUTdroop (from 103.2mV to 40.1mV) under a 1A/ns load step while completely eliminating overshoots. Furthermore, it achieves an average 35% reduction in voltage droop under transient load steps applied at different points within a single switching cycle. Additionally, this work achieves a peak efficiency of 96.13% for a 12V-to-1.2V conversion.
