title: An 18-bit 97.2-μW 40-kSPS Single-Rate Scalable Switched-Capacitor Zoom ADC With Intrinsic DAC Mismatch Immunity and Tri-Level CDAC.
abstract: This paper presents an 18-bit bandwidth/power scalable single-rate switched-capacitor (SC) zoom ADC with high energy efficiency and DAC linearity. To improve in-band linearity, a 1st-order delta-sigma modulator (ΔΣM) with tri-level CDAC serves as the coarse stage to suppress interstage quantization noise leakage. An 8-tap finite impulse response (FIR) filter is employed to shape the 1.5-bit coarse data stream to a 4-bit code, thereby preserving the intrinsic linearity of the multi-bit tri-level CDAC without requiring additional mismatch error shaping (MES) or calibration techniques. Considering the delay introduced by the FIR filter and single-rate operations, correlated level shifting (CLS) assisted cascode floating inverter dynamic amplifiers (FIDAs) are utilized to achieve coarse-fine settling and further improve linearity. Fabricated in a standard 65 nm CMOS process, the prototype zoom ADC occupies an active area of 0.25 mm2and consumes 97.2-μW under a 1.2-V supply when operating at 5.12 MS/s. It achieves 95.9-dB SNDR and 116.6-dB SFDR over a 20 kHz signal bandwidth with an oversampling ratio (OSR) of 128, resulting in 179-dB SNDR-based Schreier FoM (FoMSNDR) without any calibration or DAC linearization techniques.

title: Analysis and Evolution of Dynamics in 1R Memristive Crossbars: From Sneak Currents to Analog Computing.
abstract: Memristors have shown strong potential for constructing compact and efficient computing systems. The 1R memristor crossbar offers a regular structure capable of representing multi-level memory states through analog resistance variations. While sneak currents in nanoscale memristor crossbars are often considered a challenge for reliable memory operation, this work demonstrates that they can instead be harnessed to build nonlinear dynamical systems for computation. We first explore and analyze the behavior of sneak currents in 1R memristor crossbars under different input–ground configurations, showing how these currents can be exploited to form useful dynamic responses. We then propose an evolutionary algorithm that automatically determines the assignment of input and ground signals, optimizing both their positions and timing. This strategy allows circuit synthesis without auxiliary components, relying solely on the memristor crossbar. Finally, the evolved crossbar configurations are applied to multi-task time-series prediction, showing improved accuracy and efficiency over conventional approaches. The findings confirm the promise of 1R memristor crossbars as a compact and effective platform for nonlinear dynamical computation.

title: A 28nm 143.4-322.5TOPS/W INT8 time-domain CIM macro featuring zero-weight skipping and shift-and-add embedded TDC for Deep Neural Network.
abstract: Time-domain computing-in-memory (CIM) has gained widespread attention in the acceleration of neural network due to its high energy efficiency and large signal margin. However, conventional time-domain CIM architectures face several limitations, including inefficient utilization of sparsity as well as accuracy degradation caused by PVT (process, voltage, temperature) variations, and the high energy and delay overhead of shift-and-add circuits. To address these issues, this work presents a time-domain CIM macro featuring: (1) a zero-weight skipping delay-chain structure that reduce MAC energy and delay by 88.2% and 82.5%, respectively; (2) a self-calibration circuit that reduces offset by 95%; and (3) a shift-and-add embedded time-to-digital converter (TDC) that lowers macro energy consumption and latency by 22.3% and 16.4%, respectively. Evaluation based on the implemented macro shows that when executing VGG16, ResNet-18, and GoogLeNet, the proposed design improves energy efficiency by factors of 1.68×, 2.86×, and 3.18×, and reduces latency by 63.3%, 82.9%, and 91.8%, respectively.

title: Log-Normal FPN in DVS from Bias Mismatch.
abstract: Dynamic vision sensors (DVSs) employ event-driven sparse encoding for data compression. However, DVS remains susceptible to complex noise patterns. Existing research on spatial fixed pattern noise (FPN) remains comparatively limited. While the log-normal distribution of subthreshold currents is well-established, its specific propagation into the spatial domain of DVS event outputs has remained unmapped. In this work, we bridge this gap by revealing that the event distribution across pixel array exhibits a log-normal spatial pattern. Analytical modeling demonstrates that transistor subthreshold operation induces spatially correlated log-normal distribution in the bias current. Theoretical analysis further establishes that such current mismatch propagates to event distribution through pixel bandwidth dependencies. This paper explains the critical role of pixel bias current mismatch in governing FPN in DVS. Experimental measurements confirm that FPN manifests as a lighting-modulated log-normal spatial distribution. These results advance the understanding of FPN in DVS, supporting better denoising methods based on fundamental noise mechanisms.

title: A Wireless Power and Full-duplex Data Transfer System Achieving 57.6% End-to-End Efficiency with 0X/1X Regulating Rectifier.
abstract: This paper presents a wireless power and full-duplex data transfer system for implantable medical devices (IMDs). Conventional systems could not achieve simultaneous full-duplex telemetry and single-stage 0X/1X regulation because the regulation-induced envelope variation obscures data signals. The proposed architecture employs an amplitude shift keying (ASK) demodulator immune to 0X/1X variations and synchronizes TX/RX data frames to separate the timing of the load shift keying (LSK) modulator and regulator operations. As a result, backward telemetry and regulation can operate concurrently. The proposed system achieves synchronized full-duplex communication with 1 Mbps forward and 500kbps backward data rates, and, for the first time, demonstrates concurrent 0X/1X regulation with full-duplex telemetry, attaining 57.6 % end-to-end efficiency.

title: A Passive Threshold-Voltage-Mismatch Cancellation Technique for Visual-Neuron-Inspired HDR CMOS Image Sensors.
abstract: This paper addresses the critical issue of high fixed-pattern noise (FPN) caused by source-follower threshold-voltage (Vth) mismatch in high-dynamic-range (HDR) CMOS image sensor (CIS) inspired by visual neuronal response. We propose a threshold-voltage-mismatch cancellation technique that employs a simple capacitor-based sampling network to dynamically store and cancel pixel-specific Vthoffsets during the quantization phase. This approach effectively suppresses FPN without requiring power-intensive operational amplifiers or complex digital circuitry. Pre-layout simulation results in a 180 nm CMOS process demonstrate that under significant process induced Vthvariations, the proposed technique reduces the standard deviation of output digital codes from 11.56 LSB to 1.04 LSB, achieving 91.0% suppression of Vth-induced FPN. The circuit architecture introduces zero static power overhead, making it ideally suited for high-quality bio-inspired vision sensing in ultra-low-power Internet of Things applications.

title: A 65nm 8GHz E-PPWM/FSK IR-UWB Transceiver Achieving 2.4Gb/s Data Rate and 8.6pJ/b Energy Efficiency.
abstract: This paper presents a high-data-rate impulse-radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) transceiver for brain-computer interface (BCI) systems. To address the challenges of Gb/s data transmission under strict power constraints, a hybrid modulation scheme combining differential-coded extended pulse position/width modulation (E-PPWM) and frequency shift keying (FSK) is proposed. The transmitter employs a direct up-conversion architecture with a digital-controlled oscillator (DCO), while the receiver features a dual-path regenerative demodulator that reuses key circuit blocks for both envelope and frequency detection. Implemented in 65nm CMOS, the transceiver achieves a data rate of 2.4Gb/s with a power consumption of 20.6mW, demonstrating an energy-efficient solution for high-throughput neural data transmission.

title: A Reference-Free Neural Network Architecture for ADC Nonlinearity Calibration.
abstract: This paper proposes a reference-free neural-network-based calibration scheme for mitigating nonlinearity in analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) without requiring circuit-specific knowledge, such as mismatch, gain/offset errors, and timing skew. A customized loss function derived from dynamic performance metrics enables unsupervised calibration without reference channels or ground-truth data. The calibration network employs a lightweight two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2D CNN) with residual connections and group convolution, providing both high accuracy and computational efficiency. A dedicated accelerator is implemented on a Xilinx XCZU3EG FPGA, occupying only 5.4k LUTs (6.7%) and 6.7k FFs (4.8%) of available resources. To evaluate generalization capability, a database is constructed from measurement results of five different ADCs and multiple samples of the same ADC. Experimental results demonstrate an SFDR improvement of 17.7–35.8 dB across all tested ADCs, achieved with only 4096-point input data and 3.2k network parameters.

title: Time-of-Flight Extraction Using a Partial Temporal Attention Spiking Neural Network for SPAD-based LiDAR.
abstract: This paper presents a time-of-flight (ToF) extraction method using a partial temporal attention spiking neural network (PTASNN) based on an FPGA, addressing the noise interference problem accompanying the high-gain characteristic of single-photon avalanche diodes (SPAD) in weak echo scenarios. The temporal attention (TA) module is used to enables PTASNN to adaptively identify and focus on critical temporal windows where echoes are dominant, while effectively suppressing random spike emissions induced by noise in non-informative intervals. The partial network architecture consisting of coarse stage and fine stage is proposed to obtain 18 m measurement dynamic range and 1.5 cm resolution. In the coarse stage, temporal quantization step of input spikes is set to 1 ns to obtain a rough estimation of echo time, based on which the measurement window is effectively compressed for subsequent fine stage. In the fine stage, quantization step is set to 200 ps to achieve accurate ToF extraction. Transfer learning is leveraged to reuse both pretrained weights and circuits for convolutional operations in the PTASNN. Experimental results show that when the number of accumulations is 200, the PTASNN achieves an effective ranging distance of 85 m based on sliding window segmentation strategy, with a ranging success rate of up to 80.84% and a maximum ranging nonlinearity error of 16.25 cm.

title: A Biomimetic Nanopore Memristor Model for Emulating Synaptic Plasticity in Neuromorphic Circuits.
abstract: [EN] This study presents a comprehensive circuit-based nanopore model for emulating memristive and synaptic behaviors in neuromorphic systems. A set of governing mathematical equations describing the voltage- and time-dependent ion transport dynamics within the nanopore were derived and implemented in Verilog-A, enabling seamless integration into circuit simulators such as Cadence Virtuoso for hardware-level analysis. The model reproduces key electronic characteristics, including nonlinear current¿voltage (I¿V) hysteresis and voltage-controlled resistive switching, confirming its memristive nature. Beyond conventional memristive behavior, the nanopore model exhibits biologically inspired learning mechanisms such as spike-duration-, spike-voltage-, and spike-frequency-dependent plasticity (SDDP, SVDP, SFDP), as well as paired-pulse facilitation (PPF), closely mimicking the short-term and long-term adaptation observed in biological synapses. Simulation results demonstrate how the nanopore¿s conductance dynamically evolves with variations in pulse width, amplitude, and frequency, revealing tunable memory effects and temporal learning capabilities. These findings establish the nanopore-based memristor as a promising candidate for neuromorphic computing, bio-signal processing, and cognitive hardware architectures, providing a scalable bridge between nanoscale ionic transport physics and large-scale circuit-level implementation.

title: Electrode-Dependent Gas Sensing Behavior of CNT-TiO2 Hybrids for Ethanol Detection.
abstract: The development of gas sensors with high sensitivity and reliable response characteristics is essential for detecting volatile organic compounds (VOCs) such as ethanol in industrial, medical, and environmental applications. Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are promising materials for gas sensing due to their outstanding electrical, mechanical, and chemical properties; however, their practical performance is often limited by low response levels toward specific gases. In this study, CNTs were hybridized with titanium dioxide (TiO2) to enhance their sensing performance toward ethanol. In addition, the influence of different metal electrodes on the sensing behavior of CNT-TiO2hybrid sensors was systematically investigated. The results show that TiO2hybridization significantly enhances the sensitivity of CNT-based sensors to ethanol, while the choice of electrode material strongly affects the electrical behavior and gas response characteristics. Although most electrodes primarily influence the response magnitude, certain electrodes, such as aluminum, exhibit distinctive response features. Furthermore, analysis of response and recovery times reveals notable electrode-dependent variations with no direct correlation to sensitivity, indicating that dynamic parameters provide complementary information. These findings highlight the potential of electrode engineering and multi-parameter response analysis to enhance response differentiation and support future gas discrimination strategies in CNT-TiO2–based sensing platforms.

title: Step-Down DC-DC Converters with Transient Enhancement Technique Based on Active Compensation for Large-Load Applications.
abstract: Peak current mode (PCM) DC-DC converters are popular in numerous applications because of their advantages in multiple aspects. Emerging applications such as autonomous driving and AI computing require more power supply capability and impose new design challenges to balance the performance between efficiency and transient performance. In this work, we propose a PCM step-down DC-DC regulator employing an active compensation technique to accelerate the transient response in heavy load applications without sacrificing efficiency by increasing switching frequency. A frequency doubling technique is introduced to overcome the intrinsic delay caused by switching frequency to further restrain the output variations during load-step transients. The design was prototyped and simulated using a 0.18-μm BCD process. Under a typical application case from 5V Vin to 1.2V Vout at 500kHz switching frequency, the simulation results demonstrate that with a 20A load step with 100A/μs slew rate, the new architecture improves the output droop from 56mV to 28mV, and shortens the recovery time from 55μs to 8μs.

title: Wearable System with Real-Time Electrode Quality Evaluation for Continuous Long-Term ECG Monitoring.
abstract: Degradation of ECG electrodes critically impacts the reliability of long-term cardiac monitoring. Existing systems typically fail to detect electrode deterioration until signal quality has already degraded. This paper presents an impedance-based electrode quality assessment system that operates along with ECG system. The system estimates the electrode time constant (τ) using RC decay analysis and jointly evaluates τ and interface capacitance (Cint) to identify electrode degradation. Commercial Ag/AgCl electrodes were evaluated under simulated thermal, saline, and mechanical stress conditions. Baseline parameters for the device under test (DUT), obtained by averaging measurements over 56,000 excitation cycles per minute, were τ0= 0.103± 0.018 ms and Cint,0= 57.27 nF, while degraded state values reached τmax= 1.151±0.112 ms and Cint,max= 2071.33 nF. A degradation threshold of τ > 0.206 ms (corresponding to > 5σ above the baseline) was established to generate a warning to the user. Implemented on an ESP32-C3, the system consumes 7.7mW and provides a low-cost, real-time method for monitoring electrode health. The proposed scheme is readily adaptable to a wide range of physiological sensing systems.

title: Design and Implementation of a Low Latency and Low Complexity Reed-Solomon Decoder for IEEE 802.15.4a/z IR-UWB.
abstract: The IEEE 802.15.4a/z Impulse Radio Ultra-Wideband (IR-UWB) communication standard has been widely adopted in emerging applications that require real-time responsiveness and low implementation complexity. Among the key components of an IR-UWB receiver, the Reed–Solomon (RS) decoder makes a significant contribution to the overall system latency. This paper proposes a low-latency and low-complexity RS decoder for IEEE 802.15.4a/z IR-UWB systems. Novel parallel decoding architectures are introduced, enabling high-speed RS decoding. Additionally, optimized low-complexity circuit structures are developed to minimize implementation costs. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed RS decoder achieves a 47% reduction in latency and a 30% reduction in circuit complexity compared to existing state-of-the-art designs.

title: Uncertainty-Aware H2 Control of a Wave Energy Converter Prototype.
abstract: This paper presents a data-driven robust control framework for wave energy converters. Unlike traditional model-based approaches that neglect uncertainties, the proposed method uses a data-driven model with polytopic uncertainty identified from experimental data of a Wavestar-type prototype. The control problem is cast as a convex semidefinite program with linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), enabling the synthesis of a robust H2 controller that maximises average energy capture. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed controller either outperforms or matches passive, reactive, and H-infinity strategies in energy absorption and control efficiency.

title: A Charge-Reusing Architecture for Low-Power StrongARM Latch Comparators.
abstract: This paper presents a low-power StrongARM latch comparator based on a charge-reusing architecture. The proposed design integrates two capacitor modules that alternately capture and recycle charge between clock cycles, significantly reducing the dynamic power drawn from the power supply. By exploiting this charge redistribution technique, the comparator lowers internal node voltage swings and minimizes redundant charging and discharging events without compromising functionality. Implemented in TSMC 65nm CMOS technology, the proposed design achieves an energy consumption of 17.39fJ per comparison at a 1.2V supply, which constitutes a 40% reduction compared to the conventional design. Comparative analysis demonstrates that the new architecture offers substantial energy savings over the conventional StrongARM latch, particularly under varying input differential voltages and load capacitances. The results indicate that the charge-reusing technique is a promising approach for ultra-low-power applications that utilize circuits such as ADCs or memories, requiring high energy efficiency.

title: Composit: A Dual-Precision Posit MAC and a Composite Quantisation Scheme for Accelerated Mixed-Precision Neural Network Inference.
abstract: The deployment of Neural Networks is hindered by the trade-off between computational efficiency and inference accuracy. Mixed-precision inference, which allocates numerical precision proportional to layer sensitivities of a network, offers a promising path to navigate this trade-off. However, existing number formats complicate hardware design, as supporting multiple precisions requires distinct arithmetic units, increasing silicon footprint and power consumption. This paper introduces a novel number format based on the Posit and a corresponding dual-precision Multiply-and-Accumulate (MAC) architecture. Our format decomposes values into two scaled Posit components, allowing a single, unified hardware design to operate at both high and low-precision. We also describe a Systolic Array design for dual-precision matrix multiplication and evaluate it through ASIC synthesis and Neural Network inference benchmarks. Evaluation across multiple State of the Art model architectures and datasets shows that our technique’s performance is comparable to 32-bit floating point, enabling efficient and accurate Neural Network inference on resource-constrained and powerful platforms alike.

title: Robust Floating offshore Wind Turbines State Estimation Under Covariance Mismatch and Outliers with the Adaptive Fading Extended Kalman Filter.
abstract: This paper proposes a robust Adaptive Fading Extended Kalman Filter (AF-EKF) for state estimation of a floating offshore wind turbine. It addresses the challenge of unknown state and noise covariance matrices required by the KF which may arise from disturbance, modeling/linearization errors, and other impairments, which may even be time-varying. The AF-EKF algorithm mitigates the scale uncertainty in the state and measurement noise covariance via the fading factors which is adaptively adjusted according to the observation to minimize the discrepancies in real time. A robust statistic-based method is also introduced to combat possible measurement outliers. Simulation results show that the proposed AF-EKF achieves more accurate and stable estimation compared with the standard EKF algorithm reported. It also effectively suppressed the impact of measurement outliers, which may greatly affect the operation of the conventional EKF-based method.

title: A Layer-Aware Heterogeneous SNN Accelerator Architecture for Energy-Efficient Inference on Resource-Limited FPGAs.
abstract: Deploying fully connected Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) on resource-constrained FPGAs is challenging due to irregular memory access, high control complexity, and inefficient resource utilization caused by uniform neuron processing across all layers. To address these issues, we introduce a layer-aware heterogeneous accelerator architecture guided by empirical analysis of temporal spike sparsity. Our investigation reveals that early layers exhibit stable and sparse spike patterns, while deeper layers show dynamic variability. Leveraging this insight, the first hidden layer adopts a preloaded, time-multiplexed structure to eliminate redundant memory access, whereas deeper layers retain event-driven computation to accommodate dynamic activity. A fine-grained inter-layer pipelined scheduler further enables cycle-level parallelism across layers with minimal control overhead. Implemented on a low-cost Artix-7 FPGA (Basys3) using 4-bit quantization, the proposed design achieves 98.3% accuracy on MNIST, 78.5 kFPS throughput, and 6.07 μJ/sample energy consumption—offering over 140× improvement in energy efficiency over prior SNN accelerators on the same platform. This work provides a scalable and hardware-efficient solution for real-time SNN inference at the edge.

title: 3D-TANoC: Thermal-Aware 3D LLM Accelerator with Hierarchical NoC and Operator-Aware Dataflow Mapping Strategy.
abstract: Large language models (LLM) have demonstrated unprecedented performance across natural language processing tasks. However, this comes at the cost of their huge model size. Three-dimensional (3D) LLM accelerators have shown potential to alleviate this challenge with highly integrated computation units and memory, yet critical challenges remain: 1) thermal wall caused by high power density, which significantly degrades chip performance; 2) imbalanced workloads between LLM operators that lead to high communication latency and limited throughput. To this end, this paper proposes 3D-TANoC, a heterogeneous 3D integrated (H3D) accelerator with hierarchical network-on-chip (NoC) for efficient LLM inference. The main contributions are: 1) a thermal-aware H3D memory-on-logic architecture with hierarchical NoC to balance the temperature distribution; 2) operator-aware dataflow mapping strategy that supports efficient communication to achieve high performance and throughput. Experiments on LLaMA and OPT inference demonstrate that the proposed accelerator achieves 13.85–14.80× higher energy efficiency and 12.90–13.71× speedup over the A800 GPU baseline.

title: A 454.9-kHz, 65,100-NAND2-Equivalent-Gate Flexible Cortex-M0 SoC in 3-μm LTPS TFT Technology.
abstract: Flexible electronics have attracted increasing attention for emerging applications such as wearable healthcare and bio-integrated systems. Despite recent progress in flexible microprocessors, challenges remain in achieving high operating frequency, large-scale integration, and system scalability for flexible circuits. To address these limitations, we present the design of a flexible system-on-chip (SoC) based on a 3-μm low-temperature polycrystalline silicon (LTPS) complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) thin-film transistor (TFT) technology. A comprehensive digital design methodology tailored for the LTPS process is established, including device characterization, digital standard cell library design and development, register-transfer level (RTL) design, logic synthesis, and physical implementation, with process-specific optimizations to enhance the speed, power efficiency, and reliability. Leveraging this framework, we have implemented a 32-bit programmable Cortex-M0-based SoC, integrating on-chip memory, AHB/APB bus interconnects, and multiple peripheral modules. Post-layout simulations validate that the SoC achieves a maximum operating frequency of 454.9 kHz and integrates approximately 65,100 NAND2-equivalent gates. To our knowledge, these metrics represent new benchmark for performance and integration scale for flexible circuits. This work demonstrates the feasibility of large-scale, high-performance flexible SoC design using LTPS TFT technology and provides a design paradigm to accelerate the development of sophisticated flexible systems.

title: A 64-Pixel CMOS-MEA with 8 Piezoelectric Sensor Readout Channels for Simultaneous Electrophysiology and Mechanobiology Cell Studies.
abstract: Simultaneous monitoring of cellular electrical and mechanical activity is critical for understanding complex cellular processes. Conventional readout instrumentation is developed to perform these studies separately, and lacks spatio-temporal correlation required to couple bioelectrical activity with mechanical responses in real time. This paper presents a 64-pixel, dual-parameter CMOS microelectrode array (MEA) designed for synchronous electrophysiology and mechanobiology. The chip, fabricated in a 0.18 µm CMOS process, integrates a shared, time-based readout architecture. This novel design utilizes a SAR-ADC with an in-pixel time-domain comparator for electrical sensing and a three-stage starved-inverter VCO for mechanobiological readout. Simulated results using a 1.8 V supply demonstrate an SNDR of 55.8 dB, an effective number of bits (ENOB) of 9.13, and a power consumption of 130 µW per column. This integrated platform provides a compact, low-power solution for real-time investigation of coupled bioelectrical and biomechanical signals.

title: Single-pass Anchor-based Uncertainty Quantification in Deep Neural Networks.
abstract: Uncertainty quantification has emerged as a critical research direction in machine learning, enabling the development of trustworthy and robust intelligent systems. However, many existing uncertainty estimation approaches rely on ensembles, stochastic sampling, or covariance modeling, which substantially increase computational complexity and memory requirements—hindering their applicability in embedded and circuit-level systems. To address these limitations, we propose Anchor-based Uncertainty Quantification (AUQ), a lightweight framework that models the similarity between input samples and a set of class-central anchors to estimate predictive uncertainty. By leveraging central samples extracted from the training data, the proposed method identifies well-understood and ambiguous regions of the feature space with minimal computational overhead. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets and network architectures demonstrate that AUQ provides superior uncertainty calibration and out-of-distribution detection performance, achieving competitive accuracy while maintaining high efficiency suitable for resource-constrained hardware implementations.

title: Slice-Aware Sampling in CS-based Deep Learning Brain MRI Reconstruction.
abstract: Deep Neural-based reconstruction for Compressed Sensing (CS) has emerged as a powerful approach for accelerating brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), minimizing scan duration and patient discomfort, surpassing traditional methods. Among the numerous available architectures, ADMM-CSNet stands out as one of the most effective state-of-the-art solutions. However, this approach is affected by a high standard deviation in the reconstruction accuracy. In this work, we investigate the cause of this variability. Specifically, we show that brain MRI itself has a high variability in information content, meaning that the first and last sections are relatively simple to reconstruct, while central views are more complex.To overcome this problem, we adopt the Weighted Random Sampling (WRS) strategy, enhancing both reconstruction quality and robustness. Although this is not typically applied to this kind of dataset, it allows a refinement of the ADMM-CSNet framework, directing the network’s learning process to prioritize central slices over lateral slices. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently outperforms the baseline ADMM-CSNet and other state-of-the-art methods in terms of mean achieving a 22% lower standard deviation than the original model. Finally, the experimental results on pathological MRI images further validate the efficacy of the proposed method, showing an average PSNR gain of 3 dB over the original baseline.

title: A 0.5V 72-pW Process and Temperature Compensated Voltage Reference.
abstract: This paper presents a picowatt, process and temperature-compensated voltage reference for energy-harvested IoT nodes, producing a 0.36 V output. The design eliminates trimming, startup circuit, and on-chip resistor, minimizing complexity and area. A non-loading voltage-divider enables accurate reference generation at supply voltages down to 0.5 V, ensuring robust operation under deeply scaled supplies. Furthermore, a PMOS source-follower is repurposed as a voltage summer, simplifying the architecture, reducing the active device count, and lowering power consumption. Process compensation is achieved through a device-level technique that limits output variation to a σ/μ of 0.39%, while a native-VTHtransistor (NVT) improves line sensitivity. Implemented in 180-nm CMOS technology, the circuit achieves a nominal temperature coefficient of 36.5 ppm/°C and exhibits a typical line sensitivity of 0.14%/V over a supply range of 0.5–2 V. Additionally, the circuit consumes only 72 pW at a 0.5 V supply and occupies an active area of 0.0054 mm2.

title: A 22nm Reconfigurable Systolic Array for FFT and AI Inference.
abstract: The demand for efficient and flexible computing keeps increasing across signal processing, data management, and AI workloads. This paper proposes a reconfigurable systolic array (SA) architecture supports both 32-bit fixed-point Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and 4-bit Matrix Multiplication (MatMul) for AI inference. Each Processing Element (PE) operates in dual modes, FFT or MatMul, allowing the array to dynamically switch between butterfly-based FFT execution and MAC operations for AI tasks. Conditional routing and control logic enable seamless reconfiguration, maximizing hardware reuse. Compared with separate FFT and MatMul units, the proposed design reduces the total area by 37.17%, with minimal overhead (11.23% at PE level and 9.89% at array level). A 16×16 SA prototype implemented in GF 22nm technology occupies 1.59 mm2, consumes 225.86 mW of power at 625 MHz, and achieves 1.61 TOPS/mm2area efficiency and 11.33 TOPS/W energy efficiency.

title: Graph-Structure-Aware Hyperdimensional Computing for Hardware Trojan Detection.
abstract: State-of-the-art hardware Trojan (HT) detection largely relies on machine learning (ML)–especially GNNs– whose multi-layer message passing with learnable weights incurs substantial computation. This paper proposes a graph-structure-aware hyperdimensional computing (HDC) framework for netlist-level HT detection: we modify an open-source pipeline’s feature engineering to produce HDC-compatible graph features and inject k-hop directed structure via HDC binding and bundling, markedly improving sensitivity to HT nodes. Using HDC encoding and similarity inference, the method achieves TNR 99.82%, TPR 96.99%, and F1 89.56% on Trust-HUB, comparable to mainstream GNNs, while requiring only one-shot projection and prototype aggregation, no learnable weights, and bit-level operations–yielding low training/inference cost, easy parallelism, and suitability for resource-constrained edge deployments.

title: Compiled, Parasitic-Aware MOM Capacitor Arrays Experimentally Evaluated in SAR ADC.
abstract: Capacitor arrays are widely used in mixed-signal circuitry, and crucial to overall performance. However, the trade off has to be made for capacitor arrays among the performance of area, parasitics and matching, which becomes more difficult and requires more manual efforts as the technology scales down. This paper evaluates different structures of unit Metal-Oxide-Metal (MOM) capacitors, and then proposes a novel Hilbert-based Placement and Routing (P&R) methodology to realize a compiled and compact capacitive digital-to-analog converters (CDAC) for SAR ADCs. The proposed CDACs are integrated into a 12-bit SAR ADC fabricated in a 28nm CMOS technology, with the array area reduced by 39% compared with the traditional common-centroid CDAC. The comparative measurement results show that Sandwich-Hilbert CDAC is the best candidate, achieving the SFDR of 62.00dB and SNDR of 59.01dB without calibration.

title: A Compact 0.2-19GHz Zero-IF Reconfigurable Quadrature Transmitter with Dual-Band Selection in 28nm CMOS Process.
abstract: This work presents a 0.2-19GHz zero-IF quadrature transmitter fabricated in 28nm CMOS. Compared to the conventional ultra-wideband transmitters, the proposed dual-band design (0.2-6GHz & 6-18GHz) incorporates broadband linearity enhancement techniques and a frequency staggering scheme that break the trade-off between bandwidth and output power, thereby achieving high linearity over a wideband. The proposed dual-band 50% duty cycle LO generation circuits enabled by divider and delay locked loop (DLL) for current-mode mixers, reduces the required input clock frequency and extends the LO operating frequency with low phase error. The reconfigurable baseband achieves 42dB/100-500MHz gain /bandwidth tuning range. The transmitter achieves >40dBc IRR and LO leakage suppression with 11.8-15.1dBm output power and 13.1-17.8% TX efficiency in a compact size of 1.17mm2. It achieves wide frequency coverage with high output power and efficiency in recently reported CMOS wideband transmitters.

title: Model-Free Predictive Current Control of 2-Level Voltage Source Inverter via Robust Load Estimation in Impulsive Outliers.
abstract: The paper proposes a robust Model-Free Predictive Current (MF-PC) Control algorithm for 2-level voltage source inverter applications. It employs a deadbeat controller and an online auto-regressive with exogenous input (ARX) model for time-varying load loading using a robust recursive least square (RLS) algorithm with variable forgetting factor (VFF). The proposed VFF-RLS algorithm, which is equipped with a self-calibration mechanism, offers improved adaptation during both steady-state and transient periods, leading to lower third harmonic distortion than conventional RLS algorithm with fixed forgetting factors. To safeguard the controller from possible impulsive noise in measurements, M-estimation is employed to automatically detect and mitigate the influence of impulsive outliers. This avoids the adverse effect on the outliers on the deadbeat, leading to more robust performance. The superior tracking performance, resilience to outliers, and transient response of the proposed controller is demonstrated by computer simulation.

title: A 185 dB FoMS Direct-Integration Third-Order Passive Noise-Shaping SAR ADC for Biomedical Applications.
abstract: This paper proposes a high-energy-efficiency, direct-integration third-order passive noise-shaping (NS) successive approximation register analog-to-digital converter (SAR ADC) for biomedical applications. By directly sampling the residue voltage on the integrator and connecting the integration capacitors to the comparator through a charge-pump cascade, the proposed NS SAR ADC significantly reduces quantization-noise loss during the sampling/integration process, relaxes the gain requirement of the differential input pairs, lowers comparator power consumption, and enhances noise-shaping performance. The proposed NS SAR ADC is designed based on a standard 180nm CMOS technology. Under a 1.2V power supply, the ADC achieves 87.36 dB signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) over a 55.6 kHz bandwidth at 1.78 MS/s while consuming only 9.67 μW. The corresponding Schreier figure-of-merit (FoM) is 184.96 dB and the Walden FoM is 4.6 fJ/conversion-step, offering an energy-efficient solution for ultra-low-power biomedical systems.

title: Indoor Panoramic Depth Estimation via Dual-Projection Feature Fusion and Structural Refinement.
abstract: Accurate depth estimation from indoor panoramic images is crucial for virtual reality and robotic perception. However, existing methods suffer from distortion near the poles due to equirectangular mapping and spatial discontinuities at the boundaries when using cube mapping. These issues lead to inaccuracies in the predicted indoor panoramic depth maps. We propose a multi-feature fusion framework that innovatively incorporates room structure features alongside image-based depth prediction. The framework focuses on efficiently fusing room structure information with previously extracted features to obtain more accurate depth estimates. The proposed approach outperforms the state-of-the-art methods, reducing the absolute error by 8% and the log10 by 10.7% on the Joint 2D-3D-Semantic dataset.

title: A Compact 18-bit 1-MS/s SAR ADC Using Passive-Charge-Redistributed DAC.
abstract: This paper presents a passive-charge-redistributed (PCR) technique to mitigate the reference settling issue. Unlike passive-charge-sharing (PCS) and reservoir-charge-redistributed (RCR), which alleviate the reference settling issue by requiring extra reservoir capacitors (CREF), this work differentially connects the bottom-plate of the corresponding capacitors to enable charge redistribution without CREFrequirement, thus decoupling the trade-off between the additional area consumption and kT/C noise introduced by CREF. Furthermore, the PCR eliminates the bit-weight errors and dynamic-range (DR) loss contributed by the parasitic effects in the prior RCR scheme, thus avoiding extra complex resizing. Incorporated this technique in an 18-bit SAR ADC that adopts the FIA-based comparator, the prototype in an 180-nm CMOS process achieves a 95.1-dB signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) and 113.2-dB spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) at Nyquist input, consuming 1.37 mW power at 1 MS/s, and yielding a 180.8-dB Schreier FoM (FoMS).

title: A Monolithic GaN Bidirectional Load Switch with Fast Turn-on Control and Inrush Current Protection.
abstract: A monolithic GaN bidirectional load switch (BLS) with a fast turn-on control (FTC) technique and inrush current protection is proposed in this paper. By utilizing an integrated sense-BLS, the FTC driver accurately tracks the Miller platform to achieve rapid fully turn-on the BLS without overcurrent risk. Moreover, the design introduces a 100% duty-cycle bootstrap supply adopting a pre-charged pumping capacitor, enabling the maximum 100% duty-cycle operation. The proposed GaN BLS is simulated in Cadence Virtuoso where its inrush current protection capability and fast switching performance are verified.

title: Robust and Accurate Line Following Navigation by Hybrid Infrared-Visual Modes for Mobile Robots.
abstract: With the advancement of industrial automation, mobile robots are increasingly required to perform robust and accurate line-following navigation. However, conventional single-mode approaches face limitations: infrared (IR) systems offer high precision but are susceptible to ambient light, while vision-based systems are more robust but typically less precise. This work presents a hybrid line-following navigation system that integrates both IR and visual modes to improve reliability and accuracy. The IR mode utilizes a triple-sensor array for path deviation detection, while the visual mode processes RGB images to estimate deviation angles. The system supports automatic mode switching based on environmental conditions, seamlessly transitioning to visual navigation when IR failure is detected. Experimental results show that the hybrid navigation system outperforms single-mode methods, especially in challenging scenarios such as discontinuous lines. A representative application is also demonstrated to prove its application potential, where multi-object detection and localization are combined with line following, enabling the robot to efficiently perform patrol and product recording tasks in a simulated supermarket environment.

title: A 16-Channel Monopolar-and-Bipolar Super-Reconfigurable Neurostimulation IC with Active Charge-Balancing and 12-V Voltage Compliance in Standard CMOS.
abstract: This work presents a monopolar-and-bipolar super-reconfigurable 16-channel neurostimulation IC with active charge-balancing (ACB) and on-chip power management achieving 12-V compliance voltage in a 180-nm standard CMOS process. A novel dynamically self-biased stimulation driver ensures circuit reliability while supporting monopolar-and-bipolar bimodal operations. The proposed ACB scheme allows automatic residual charge removal in a self-controlled loop with minimum system complexity overhead. A 2.2-to-3.3-V-input reconfigurable charge-pump-based power management unit is implemented to generate ±6 V outputs, which extends the stimulation compliance voltage to 12 V in bipolar modes. The peak power efficiencies of the ±6-V charge-pumps are measured to be 75.07% and 58.25%, respectively. The ACB module is measured to reduce the residue voltage to less than 2 mV for both polarities. The proposed neurostimulation IC offers exceptional reconfigurability, power efficiency, and system integrity, addressing the evolving demands of modern neuromodulation devices.

title: A sub-μVrms 64-Channel Neural Recording ASIC with Easy-Driven TDM and 16-Bit SAR ADC.
abstract: This paper presents a 64-channel time-division multiplexed (TDM) neural recording ASIC optimized for minimal area and noise in high-density interfaces. An easy-driven TDM architecture is proposed to minimize the output swing and load capacitance across recording channels while enabling multiple channels to share a single high-performance ADC, thereby significantly reducing both channel-level power consumption and overall silicon area. A segmented CDAC combined with MSB capacitor sampling is employed within a 16-bit SAR ADC to reduce both the ADC’s area and the capacitive load on its driving buffer. Each recording channel adopts a CS-CCIA cascaded with the SAR ADC, achieving low-noise performance of 0.97 μVrms (1-250 Hz) and 4.52 μVrms (1-10 kHz) IRN. SAR ADC features redundant capacitors, foreground calibration and LSB repeating to enhance linearity and precision, yielding 13.61-bit ENOB at 1.28 MS/s. Fabricated in 180 nm CMOS, the prototype achieves 0.2 mm2/channel area, offering 5%-15% higher area efficiency and 1.3×-3.5× improved noise performance compared with state-of-the-art TDM-based neural recording systems.

title: A Single Channel Two-Stage 12b 500MS/s Pipelined-SAR ADC with Reset-independent Asynchronous SAR Logic and Differential Flipped Voltage Follower Based Two-Stage Open-Loop Dynamic Amplifier.
abstract: A 12-bit single-channel two-stage pipelined-SAR ADC is proposed, which operates at 500 MS/s and achieves a Nyquist SFDR of 75.64 dB. An asynchronous clock generation circuit with separated high-and low-bit control is introduced, decoupling the reset delay paths for the most significant bits (MSBs) and least significant bits (LSBs). This eliminates the constraint of MSB settling on the LSB reset time, thereby minimizing the comparator reset time duration while ensuring proper SAR ADC conversion. Furthermore, a compact control logic layout with short latency is designed to further reduce the comparator reset time. In addition, a two-stage high-speed dynamic amplifier based on the differential flipped voltage follower (DFVF) is proposed which enhances the gain of the open-loop amplifier to 16 times under a 128 fF load while maintaining favorable linearity under large-signal conditions. Fabricated in a 28 nm process, the ADC occupies an area of 0.0164 mm2. Operating under a 1 V power supply at 500 MS/s, it consumes 6.1 mW. And it achieves a measured SNDR of 60.15dB and SFDR of 77.38 dB, with FoMw of 14.7fJ/conversion-step and FoMs of 166.3dB.

title: A Fully Digital Dynamic Vision Sensor based on Time to First Spike Encoding.
abstract: This paper presents the first fully digital asynchronous Dynamic Vision Sensor (DVS) core based on Time to First Spike (TFS) pixels. In this approach, each TFS pixel encodes the intensity of the incident light as the latency of its first spike, which is digitized using a Time to Digital Converter (TDC). The DVS core, detecting temporal contrast, is implemented through the difference of successive TFS measurements, which is compared against a programmable threshold. Any type of TFS pixel, visible or infrared, can be interfaced. The core is a digital asynchronous bundled-data circuit designed for low-power applications. Unlike conventional analog DVS circuits embedded at the pixel level, the DVS logic is externalized from the TFS pixel array, significantly improving the fill factor and reducing the area compared to a standard analog DVS. Such an image sensor provides simultaneously the TFS and DVS functionalities. Two operating modes are proposed, differing in how TFS intensities are stored and compared. Both modes were implemented in a 28nm Fully Depleted Silicon-on-Insulator Technology from STMicroelectronics. This work demonstrates the feasibility of combining TFS encoding with DVS, opening new perspectives for low-power, low-throughput imaging systems.

title: Reinforcement Learning Framework with Improved NSGA-II for Logic Synthesis.
abstract: Exponentially expanding design space in logic synthesis poses significant challenges for AI-driven high-performance computing (AI-HPC) in logic optimization. Reinforcement learning (RL), as a key of AI-HPC, performs well in searching for solutions but converges poorly, whereas heuristic algorithms converge excellently yet begin from low-quality solutions. This paper proposes a hybrid high-performance AI computing framework for FPGA logic optimization that combines RL with an improved Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). This framework integrates the strengths of both RL and NSGA-II. Specifically, an Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C) agent is employed as an initial population generator to produce a high-quality and diverse set of solutions. The improved NSGA-II, incorporating structure-aware hashing to avoid redundant evaluations, along with adaptive crossover and mutation mechanisms, is then applied to efficiently optimize multiple objectives. Compared with resyn2, evaluation results on the EPFL benchmark suite and FPGA mapping demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces the LUT-6 count by an average of 14.82% under delay constraints.

title: An Intrinsically Linear 9-Level Current-Steering DAC for Continuous-Time Delta-Sigma ADCs.
abstract: This paper presents three techniques for realizing intrinsically linear multi-level current-steering (CS) digital-to-analog converters (DACs). Two concepts are developed for 5-level DACs and one for a 9-level implementation. The first technique exploits inherent linearity using a dual-return-to-zero (Dual-RZ) architecture composed of two tri-level CS DAC unit elements. The second approach mitigates nonlinearity in return-to-zero (RZ) CS DACs through time-domain self-compensation. The third combines both concepts to realize a 9-level self-compensated intrinsically linear multi-return-to-zero (Multi-RZ) CS DAC, verified in the feedback path of a continuous-time delta-sigma modulator (CT-∆ΣM) and designed in 55 nm CMOS technology. The proposed techniques significantly improve linearity under device mismatch, showing only an 11 dB degradation in spurious free dynamic range (SFDR) in the worst case of 100 Monte-Carlo (MC) simulations. The achieved linearity is particularly advantageous for low-oversampling ratio (OSR) CT-∆ΣMs, where conventional randomization becomes impractical and existing linearization methods add excessive complexity.

title: Topology-Aware GNN Embedding with Domain Priors and Graph Policy Regularization for Balanced Multi-Objective Analog IC Design.
abstract: Analog integrated circuit (IC) sizing is challenging due to its high-dimensional parameter space, stringent design constraints, and the need to balance conflicting objectives like gain, bandwidth, power, and stability. Conventional GCN-RL frameworks often use graph neural networks (GNNs) as passive feature extractors, leading to weak coupling between topology representation and policy learning. This paper proposes a Graph-Regularized Twin-Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient framework that integrates graph-based circuit embeddings with reinforcement learning. Circuit topologies are encoded through flexible GNNs, enriched with domain-specific priors such as pole-zero distribution, gain-bandwidth product, and phase margin. The embeddings are processed by a Graph Policy Regularization (GPRO) module to enforce structural consistency and improve TD3 policy. An adaptive exploration strategy enhances sampling efficiency. SPICE-in-the-loop experiments show that GPRO-TD3 achieves faster convergence, more stable trade-offs, and superior generalization compared to vanilla TD3 and evolutionary baselines.

title: An Optimized Pre-Emphasis Spike Detector for High-Density Neural Interfaces.
abstract: Spike detection plays a core role in neural signal processing and brain-computer interfaces (BCIs). A key challenge for next-generation implantable BCIs is to develop a spike detector with low hardware cost, high performance, and adaptive adjustment capabilities. In this work, we propose a novel hardware-efficient and high-performance spike detector for implantable BCIs. The proposed design is based on adaptive pre-emphasis and fixed threshold estimation. For adaptive pre-emphasis, a short-window convolutional filter is trained via an energy ratio loss function to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the signal.We evaluated the proposed spike detection algorithm on the Wave Clus dataset, achieving an average detection accuracy of 97.95%. Even in high-noise scenarios, the accuracy remains above 95%, which ensures the reliability of the method. The detector was implemented in hardware with a sampling rate of 24 kHz and a resolution of 8 bits. A multi-channel detector based on this architecture was designed using 65 nm process, exhibiting an area efficiency of 868 μm2per channel and a power consumption of 71.8 nW per channel.

title: VIR-EH: An Ultra-Low-Power Wide-Spectrum Visible-Infrared Vision Processing Chip with On-Chip Energy Harvesting.
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-low-power wide-spectrum visible-infrared visual processing chip with on-chip energy harvesting scheme (VIR-EH) for always-on distributed vision sensor nodes. In VIR-EH, the inverter-based infrared read-out circuits and analog-digital hybrid near-sensor motion detection architecture are proposed to reduce the power consumption significantly. The power management unit (PMU) and energy scheduling strategy designed for on-chip energy harvesting enable the system to achieve ultra-low-power consumption. VIR-EH is designed in 180nm CMOS process and the simulation results show that the chip consumes 5.54 µW at a frame rate of 230 fps when executing motion detection task. The PMU of the chip can achieve an efficiency of 61.9% when supplying 795.4 nW of power to the system.

title: TSA-P: A Triple-Sparsity-Aware Reconfigurable Few-Spikes-Neuron-Based SNN Processor.
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) hold great potential for energy-efficient computing by exploiting sparse, spike-driven processing. However, existing SNN processors directly adopt the zero-input/weight dual-sparsity scheme designed for Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs), neglecting the sparsity arising from repeated identical spike trains inherent in SNNs. This limitation, coupled with workload imbalance caused by unstructured pruning, constrains overall efficiency. To address these challenges, we propose TSA-P, a triple-sparsity-aware processor based on FSN-SNNs. In addition to dual-sparsity, we identify and exploit a third form of sparsity, termed Repetition Spike Train sparsity. To leverage these three sparsity forms, TSA-P introduces three key techniques—Adjacent Spike Train Compression (ASC) scheme, Spike-driven Weight Matching (SWM) method and Repeated Spike Train Reuse (RSR) strategy—which collectively minimize computational and memory-access energy. Furthermore, a hardware-friendly unstructured pruning (HUP) algorithm and a Sparsity-Adaptive Processing Element (SAPE) engine are developed to adaptively balance computational load while improving accuracy. TSA-P also features a reconfigurable architecture supporting both convolutional and fully connected layers. Experimental results on three datasets demonstrate that TSA-P achieves comparable accuracy while significantly reducing resource usage. On the CIFAR10 dataset, TSA-P achieves energy efficiency improvements ranging from 1.70× to 342.76× over state-of-the-art SNN processors.

title: Spatio-Temporal Event Clustering for Tracking Moving Light Sources in Event-Camera Visible Light Communication.
abstract: Event cameras provide ultra-fast detection of light changes, offering strong potential for reliable visible light communication (VLC) in dynamic environments. However, accurately tracking and separating moving transmitter light sources remains challenging due to background noise and unpredictable motion. This paper proposes a generalized tracking method for moving transmitter light sources in event-camera-based VLC. The proposed method first suppresses background noise using spatial density filtering, then continuously classifies and updates each source with dynamic centroid-based tracking. Experiments show that this approach achieves stable tracking and accurate synchronization under various motion patterns, including irregular movements, demonstrating its effectiveness for dynamic VLC.

title: SGFormer-RGCN: Accurate Performance Prediction for High-Level Synthesis Design Space Exploration.
abstract: Agile hardware development creates an urgent need for rapid, accurate circuit quality prediction during high-level synthesis (HLS) design space exploration (DSE). While graph neural networks (GNNs) using control data flow graphs (CD-FGs) are popular for this, they struggle to capture long-range dependencies and can lose critical structural information with hierarchical pooling, limiting their accuracy. To overcome these issues, we propose a novel SGFormer-RGCN fusion model. It synergistically combines the global information modeling of a simplified graph transformer (SGFormer) with the local structural awareness of relational graph convolutional networks (RGCN). An innovative learnable fusion mechanism dynamically weights global and local features for flexible, efficient integration. This approach achieves breakthroughs in predicting resource utilization, critical path delay, and power consumption, reducing the average prediction error to between 2.70% and 7.18%. Our method shows significant accuracy improvements over existing approaches, providing an efficient solution for early-stage design quality assessment. Code and models are available at https://github.com/luckyu227/SGFormer-RGCN.

title: A Logic-Assisted Hybrid-Mode Ising Machine Based on a 3D Topology for 3D Path Planning.
abstract: Path planning is a fundamental task in robotics, autonomous systems, and spatial optimization, in which real-time and energy-efficient computations are crucial. Conventional digital architectures exhibit limited parallelism when exploring large search spaces, leading to challenges in power efficiency, latency, and scalability. The Ising model offers a promising hardware framework for addressing such problems through energy-minimization dynamics. The spins that represent obstacles and paths in an Ising model update simultaneously, providing substantial acceleration in large-scale pathfinding. However, existing implementations are constrained by inefficient problem mapping and are typically limited to two-dimensional (2D) scenarios. To address these challenges, this work presents a CMOS Ising machine with a three-dimensional (3D) lattice topology for efficient 3D path planning, achieving a 91.3% reduction in transistor count compared with prior work. CMOS simulations verify that the proposed system correctly solves a 16 × 16 × 16 maze within 45 iterations, consuming 8.625 μW per spin and occupying 496.31 μm2per spin.

abstract: This demonstration presents an energy-efficient System-on-Chip (SoC) for real-time correlative scan matching in 2D LiDAR Simultaneous Localization And Mapping (SLAM). Integrated into an autonomous mobile robot platform equipped with LiDAR, IMU, and wheel encoders, the ZYNQ-7020 FPGA-based SoC achieves 111.29 frames per second at 100 MHz with an energy efficiency of 7.15 mJ/frame The implemented SoC processes 500×500 probability grid maps with up to 600 LiDAR points per frame at 5 cm resolution, corresponding to a physical area of approximately 25 m × 25 m.

title: Video-Based Gait Analysis for Lumbar Disc Herniation Screening.
abstract: Video-based gait analysis is crucial for the screening and management of Lumbar Disc Herniation (LDH). Therefore, this study proposes to extract and optimize features from video to enhance the performance of LDH screening models for classifying LDH patients from healthy individuals. A framework was established to extract joint angle time-series from pose data, with features evaluated across time, frequency, and wavelet domains. An initial ablation study revealed that a baseline model utilizing 16 time-domain features (AUC=0.7464) surpassed models with more complex feature sets. To enhance performance, a two-stage optimization was conducted: XGBoost hyperparameter tuning improved the AUC to 0.7556, followed by Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), which identified a minimal subset of 6 key features. The final model, trained on these 6 features, achieved a superior average AUC of 0.7827 in 5-fold cross-validation. The study demonstrates that a concise set of interpretable time-domain features is highly effective for this clinical application, offering a reliable and computationally efficient model for LDH screening.

title: A 4GS/s 8b Time-Interleaved SAR ADC with LSB-Repeating-Based Background Offset Calibration and Adaptive-Average Residue Estimator.
abstract: This work proposes an input-independent LSB-repeating-based background offset calibration method for high-speed SAR ADCs employing ping-pong comparators. By repeating the LSB decision, it detects the offset mismatch between the two comparators and increases the overall resolution, regardless of the input signal statistics. During the LSB repeating process, a novel adaptive-average residue estimator is introduced for the repeated LSB decisions to further enhance the SNR. With the proposed techniques, a prototype 4GS/s 8b 4-channel time-interleaved ADC achieves a Walden FoM of 16.6 and 9.7fJ/conv-step with and without the reference and input buffers.

title: RRAM based CIM, PUF and True Random Number Generator for High-Security AES Encryption System.
abstract: Encryption systems based on the compute-in-memory (CIM) paradigm offer a promising foundation for secure communication in Internet of Things (IoT) devices, owing to their intrinsic resistance to electromagnetic side-channel leakage. However, existing CIM-based encryption research still faces two major challenges: (1) the risk of key exposure during transmission, and (2) the difficulty of efficiently performing complex encryption algorithms onto CIM hardware. In this work, we propose a high-security and energy-efficient Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) system based on resistive random-access memory (RRAM). By leveraging the diverse physical properties of RRAM, the key functional modules of the AES algorithm—including the Physical Unclonable Function (PUF), True Random Number Generator (TRNG), and encryption logic—are all implemented within the RRAM arrays. This enables on-chip key generation and in-situ encryption, thereby eliminating the need for external key transfer. Furthermore, a multi-array parallel operation scheme based on a hierarchical data bus network is developed to support parallelized in-memory execution of encryption and decryption, substantially reducing the hardware overhead required for AES deployment. Performance evaluation demonstrates a 68× improvement in resistance to side-channel differential power analysis (DPA) attacks, along with 29.5% higher area efficiency and 23.4% greater energy efficiency.

title: A 2.3-ns Response Time Temperature Insensitive Capacitive Level-Shifter with a Novel Active Pull-up for a 100-V Monolithic GaN Half Bridge.
abstract: This paper presents a capacitive level-shifter circuit for a 100-V monolithic 1-μm GaN-on-Si half bridge, designed to achieve the lowest and most thermally stable response time possible. The circuit employs a novel active pull-up that uses depletion transistors connected with the source to the upper supply to achieve a faster output latch commutation. The proposed design achieves rise and fall delays of 2.29 ns and 2.14 ns, respectively, with a temperature stability of 1.28 ps/°C. It can switch at 5 MHz, withstand switching node noise up to 500 V/ns, and transmit signals with the switching node at –100 V, all within an area of only 0.14 mm2.

title: A 50-ns Response Time High-Side Current Sense with a Novel Analog Level-Shifting Technique for a 100-V Monolithic 1-μm GaN-on-Si Half Bridge.
abstract: This paper presents a high-side current sense circuit for a 100-V monolithic 1-μm GaN-on-Si half bridge, designed to achieve a fast response and low power consumption. The circuit employs a novel technique based on the channel length modulation of a resistively degenerated 100-V enhancement-mode transistor to transfer the analog information from the high- to the low-voltage rail. The proposed design achieves a 50-ns response time and 99.97% accuracy under the nominal operating condition of 50-V input voltage and 10-A load current. The current sense amplifier exhibits a DC gain of 73 dB and a gain-bandwidth product of 18.6 MHz. The accuracy remains above 96.5% across a wide range of temperatures, input voltages, load currents, and device mismatches.

title: GFix: Perceptually Enhanced Gaussian Splatting Video Compression.
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enhances 3D scene reconstruction through explicit representation and fast rendering, demonstrating potential benefits for various low-level vision tasks, including video compression. However, existing 3DGS-based video codecs generally exhibit more noticeable visual artifacts and relatively low compression ratios. In this paper, we specifically target the perceptual enhancement of 3DGS-based video compression, based on the assumption that artifacts from 3DGS rendering and quantization resemble noisy latents sampled during diffusion training. Building on this premise, we propose a content-adaptive framework, GFix, comprising a streamlined, single-step diffusion model that serves as an off-the-shelf neural enhancer. Moreover, to increase compression efficiency, We propose a modulated LoRA scheme that freezes the low-rank decompositions and modulates the intermediate hidden states, thereby achieving efficient adaptation of the diffusion backbone with highly compressible updates. Experimental results show that GFix delivers strong perceptual quality enhancement, outperforming GSVC with up to 72.1% BD-rate savings in LPIPS and 21.4% in FID.

title: Performance-Reconfigurable Multi-Mode Doherty Power Amplifier Using Bias-Space Control.
abstract: This paper presents a Bias-Space Control (BSC) methodology for Doherty Power Amplifiers (DPAs) that formalizes biasing as a multidimensional control space. The proposed approach analytically links bias selection to shifts in the effective Doherty load-modulation trajectory. This allows the DPA to be operated in four distinct performance-priority modes, namely–power-priority, gain-priority, back-off-range-priority, and efficiency-priority operation, without modifying passive matching networks. A 3.2–3.4 GHz GaN DPA is designed to validate the framework, demonstrating a consistent and predictable reconfiguration of output power, gain, back-off range, and efficiency. The proposed BSC framework elevates bias control from empirical tuning to a structured system-level design methodology for adaptive RF transmitters, while requiring no hardware modifications.

title: MANBO: A Multi-Agents PPO Network-Based Optimizer Framework for Multi-Operand Adders.
abstract: The low-area and low-power design of multi-operand adders (MOAs) is of great importance in digital signal processing (DSP) and machine learning hardware. However, the highly complex prefix optimization space poses a significant challenge to identifying the optimal MOAs architecture. In this work, we propose MANBO, a Multi-Agents PPO Network-Based Optimizer framework for MOAs. Unlike prior works, MANBO transforms the pareto optimization of a single adder into the optimization of the minimum area with timing constraints. MANBO represents MOAs prefixes with matrices in which the elements represent prefix nodes. The policies are generated by multiple actor heads sharing features of MOAs prefixes to reduce the number of network parameters and enhance scalability. Experimental results demonstrate that MANBO consistently outperforms baseline methods, achieving 12.03% reductions in area within the constraint under 250MHz, providing a promising direction for intelligent hardware optimization.

title: An FPGA-Based Design of Reliable Quantized AdderNet Under Fault Injection.
abstract: AdderNet, as an energy-efficient alternative to convolutional neural networks, still suffers from incomplete quantization and vulnerability to soft errors in hardware deployment. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Fully Quantized AdderNet (FQ-AdderNet) framework and a lightweight fault-aware encoding scheme, termed FA-MEC. The proposed FQ-AdderNet achieves complete integer quantization for all modules, enabling an integer-only inference pipeline that improves hardware efficiency without sacrificing accuracy. In addition, FA-MEC provides enhanced fault tolerance with minimal redundancy, achieving the highest accuracy-to-redundancy ratio of 140.09 under high fault rates. Experimental results on an FPGA platform demonstrate that the proposed approach maintains 91.21% accuracy under 8-bit quantization, offering a reliable and efficient hardware solution for energy-constrained deep learning systems.

title: Exploring Structural and Behavioral Features for Hardware Trojan Detection at Gate Level.
abstract: Hardware Trojans are malicious design modifications to integrated circuit (IC) designs, which pose severe threats to hardware security and trust. This work proposes a novel hardware Trojan detection method at gate level by exploring structural and behavioral features and training a machine learning model for node classification. The gate-level netlist is converted into a directed graph to extract structural features for each node. A random forest algorithm is then employed to analyze feature importance, providing explainable insights into the most influential features. In addition, we transform the netlist to bench format and extract three behavioral features from the perspective of controllability and observability. A neural network model with optimized class-balanced focal loss is trained for classifying circuit nodes and identifying Trojan-infected ones. Experiments using 80 hardware Trojan benchmarks from Trust-Hub and ATTRITION show that the proposed method can successfully pinpoint Trojan-infected nodes with true positive rate (TPR), true negative rate (TNR), accuracy, and area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 99.46%, 96.56%, 96.57%, and 98.01% respectively on average.

title: BioSeek: A Design Generation Framework of Biosignal Processors with Large-Language Models for Edge Healthcare Applications.
abstract: Deep neural network (DNN)-based methodologies have shown impressive performance and robustness in the detection of abnormalities and decoding of multi-modal biosignals. While the use of DNNs provides promising classification and decoding capabilities, it also introduces significant design and cost challenges for the implementation of biomedical System on Chips (SoC). To address the increasing demand for advanced and efficient DNN-based healthcare solutions at the edge, we propose BioSeek, an agile design generation framework enhanced by cutting-edge large-language models (LLM). BioSeek offers a comprehensive solution to the design challenges associated with biosignal processors. The effectiveness of BioSeek is evaluated through the design generation of both application-specific and versatile biosignal processors, demonstrating performance that is competitive with existing solutions.

title: A Fully-Parallel Digital MRAM Computing-in-Memory Macro Featuring a High-Efficient Dynamic Adder Tree and Bit-Splitting MAC.
abstract: Digital computing in-memory (DCIM) macros, known for their high robustness, have recently attracted growing attention. However, they still face challenges of large logic overhead and low efficiency sign-bit processing in fully-parallel CIM. In this work, we propose a fully-parallel digital MRAM-CIM architecture featuring a dynamic adder tree and a bit-splitting multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) scheme. Based on a 28 nm CMOS process and voltage-gated spin-orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions (VGSOT-MTJs) devices, a 128-kb MRAM-CIM macro was simulated to validate the proposed design. The dynamic full-adder and 15-to-4 full-precision compression-based adder tree achieves 48.7% lower energy for MAC operations, while the bit-splitting approach eliminates sign-extension operations, improving computing efficiency. Furthermore, the shared voltage-divider reference cell enables compact 2T1M storage, achieving 73.96% and 64% area reduction compared with complementary cell designs. The proposed MRAM-CIM achieves energy efficiency of 96.9 TOPS/W and throughput of 2.8 TOPS at IN-8b/W-8b/OUT-22b with 0.9 V VDD. Its figure-of-merit is 3.03–5.27× higher than existing CIM macros.

title: Integrated Current and Vibration Sensing System for Condition Monitoring of a Drone Docking Station.
abstract: In this study, we present an integrated current and vibration sensing system designed to monitor drone docking station conditions using machine learning models for anomaly detection. The system also offers a plug-and-play monitoring capability with the potential to be adapted to various machinery. We developed two approaches: a long short-term memory (LSTM)-based classifier for known anomalies and an unsupervised convolutional neural network (CNN)-based autoencoder for detecting any deviations from normal operation. Validated on a real-world drone docking station, the reconstruction-based autoencoder, which does not require labeled data, achieves over 98.99% accuracy and a 98% F1-score.

title: Clipping Error Compensation for Accuracy Recovery and Throughput Improvement in Computing-in-Memory.
abstract: This paper proposes built-in self-repair (BISR) strategies for computing-in-memory (CIM) architectures to mitigate clipping errors in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and enhance overall CIM performance.First, we propose a BISR circuit that detects and compensates clipping errors in real-time. When a bitline output of the CIM approaches the upper limit of the analog-to-digital converter (ADC), a pre-stored compensation value is added to preserve inference accuracy. Second, we observe a strong correlation between clipping errors and the sum-of-weight-bits on bitlines. Based on this, we introduce a grouping scheme that records compensation values by sum-of-weight-bits ranges, reducing storage overhead while maintaining accuracy.Experiments on image classification show the proposed BISR recovers the top-1 accuracy loss to approximately 1% and improves CIM throughput by up to 3.2×. The hardware incurs only about 5% additional area relative to the CIM macro, excluding ADCs and DACs.

title: A High-Power Absorptive-Type Asymmetric SPDT Switch for Millimeter-wave Phased-Array Transceiver Front-End.
abstract: The asymmetric single-pole-double-throw (SPDT) switch is a popular component in time-division duplex (TDD) RF front-end transceivers. In the conventional reflected-type configurations, potential internal reflection may be an issue when switching between the transmitting (Tx) and the receiving (Rx) modes, due to the fact that the Tx power amplifier is connected to the highly mismatched load during Rx operation. In this paper, the high power absorptive-type asymmetric SPDT switch is thus developed for 5G new-radio (NR) frequency range 2 (FR2) n257 band applications. Implemented in the 0.15-μm GaAs pseudomorphic high-electron-mobility transistor (pHEMT) technology, the experimental results demonstrated an insertion loss of less than 3.4/1.8 dB, an isolation of better than 17.9/18.1 dB, and an input 0.1-dB compression point (P0.1dB) of 30.0/22.0 dBm from 24-30 GHz while operating in Tx/Rx mode. Compared to the conventional asymmetric configurations, the proposed one offered a better isolation with lower insertion loss in the Rx mode.

title: On the Implementation of Low-Cost Neural-Network Models for Cardiac Arrhythmia Detection.
abstract: In recent years, there have been few efforts on the development of AI models for the prediction of cardiovascular diseases. These efforts show that it is possible to train models for the prediction of critical health conditions like arrhythmia. However, such models come with high complexity that hinder their hardware implementation and use on resource constrained devices. This paper presents one of the first efforts on the implementation of low-cost models for cardiac arrhythmia detection. Starting with a state-of-the-art prediction model, we apply various optimizations including quantization-aware training, post-training quantization, and pruning, which we evaluate on an Alveo U250 FPGA. The resultant models show up to 45% power and 92.6% area reduction with only 1.6% accuracy loss compared to non-compressed models.

title: CEDAR: A Compact and Efficient Decoder Architecture for RS-RM Code in HQC.
abstract: The rapid development of quantum computing has driven a new wave of cryptographic innovation: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), a class of algorithms that resist quantum attacks. In particular, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has initiated the PQC standardization process, selecting five algorithms. Notably, HQC (the newest selection) is a code-based PQC scheme that has not been widely studied in the literature, especially with respect to its hardware acceleration. This paper follows the current trend to design CEDAR, a Compact and Efficient Decoder Architecture for Reed-Solomon Reed-Muller (RS-RM) code in HQC. We have proposed three layers of contributions in total: (i) an optimized RM decoder is designed; (ii) an efficient low-complexity RS decoder is also presented; (iii) a complete HQC decoder is implemented, along with a comprehensive evaluation (it is shown that CEDAR outperforms the existing approach). We hope this outcome will facilitate a more efficient hardware acceleration of HQC and impact the ongoing NIST PQC standardization process.

title: Universal OMA Tracker Using Sampled Envelope Feedback for Wavelength Locking of High-Speed Micro-Ring Modulators.
abstract: Wavelength locking of high-speed microring modulators (MRMs) remains a significant challenge for both academia and industry. Obtaining dynamic optical modulation amplitude (OMA) information is a critical step toward addressing this challenge, yet existing methods are constrained by modulation speed, data patterns, and modulation formats. This work presents a universal OMA tracker based on sampled envelope feedback, capable of supporting high data rates, various modulation formats, and data-pattern-agnostic operation. The design is implemented in standard 65 nm CMOS technology with 0.0784mm2chip area and 1.775mW power consumption. We successfully achieved OMA tracking for 120 Gbps PAM-4 signals and demonstrated maximum OMA wavelength locking of a 28 Gbps MRM.

title: Post-Training Quantization for Overfitted Neural Image Coding.
abstract: Overfitted neural image codecs offer a promising path to ultra-low-complexity decoding, ideal for resource-constrained hardware. However, realizing their potential requires an integer-only pipeline, a task complicated by their extreme sensitivity to post-training quantization (PTQ). To our knowledge, this is the first work to systematically address the challenges of 8-bit PTQ for such codecs. We present an effective methodology for 8-bit weight, 16-bit activation quantization, developed through a three-stage investigation. (1) We first establish that a fine-grained, per-channel quantization scheme is the essential foundation for preserving model fidelity. (2) We then use Hessian analysis to identify strong weight dependencies as the primary bottleneck and apply a dependency-aware compensation algorithm to mitigate the resulting errors. (3) To further refine the compensation process, we integrate a principled, decreasing-importance order into the quantization sequence. Our final approach reduces the rate-distortion overhead to just +2.95% BD-Rate on the Kodak dataset and +2.78% BD-Rate on the CLIC dataset, establishing a practical methodology for this sensitive codec class.
