title: Phase Noise Integration Limits for Jitter Estimation in Wireline Transmitters.
abstract: The performance of high-speed wireline transceivers is significantly affected by the broadband phase noise of their clocking modules, thus requiring accurate noise integration limits for jitter calculation. We show that the correct bounds depend upon the transmitter architecture and the simulation/measurement environment, and present results for various clocking schemes relevant to different multiplexing techniques.

title: Physics-Driven In-House Memristor Crossbar Array Model for Image Classification.
abstract: The design of memory devices for the computation of neural networks requires stationary weights to preserve accuracy in classification tasks. This work classifies CIFAR-10 images with a ResNet-18 neural network. We simulated the time evolution of the weights belonging to said network when programmed as conductance values into an in-house SrTiO3/SrCoO3memristor array. The memristors feature a decaying conductance with time whose behavior we predicted by means of experimental data and IBM’s Python toolbox, the AIHWKit. We report an end-to-end accuracy variation from 86% upon weight programming to 78% after one thousand seconds. Future work will focus on reducing conductance drift through material optimization, the study of the physics of a memristor crossbar, and the implementation of memristor-based neural network systems, for example for object tracking.

title: A RISC-V Coprocessor to Accelerate Structured Sparse-Dense Matrix Multiplications.
abstract: Machine learning algorithms are seeing an increase in data sparsity due to optimization techniques and model compression methods. However, traditional accelerators underperform in sparse workloads due to wasted computations on zero-elements. Therefore, specialized architectures are needed to accelerate sparse computations, with a close-coupling to general-purpose processors to leverage algorithm-level optimizations. This work proposes a RISC-V coprocessor to accelerate structured sparse-dense matrix multiplications with a scalable tile-based architecture that can directly be controlled through the RISC-V core using a custom instruction set. Prototyping this design on an AMD/Xilinx ZCU104 shows a lightweight design consuming less than 60 mW of dynamic power, and an analysis of its performance shows 85-100X speedup compared to CPU.

title: Closed-Loop Arrhythmia Classification with Level-Crossing Sensing and Bidirectional SNN.
abstract: This work proposes an event-driven sensing and inference framework that jointly optimizes signal acquisition and neural processing for energy-efficient, real-time Electrocardiography (ECG) analysis. Specifically, we present a closed-loop pipeline that integrates an adaptive Level-crossing Analog-to-digital Converter (LC-ADC) with a compact, fully spiking temporal back end. To validate hardware readiness, the complete signal path is implemented in Verilog RTL and synthesized in a 130 nm CMOS ASIC flow. The prototype attains 96.44% overall five-class classification accuracy and 98.02% detection accuracy on MIT–BIH dataset while consuming only 43 µW of average end-to-end power. These results are on par with recent state-of-the-art low-power arrhythmia detection systems, achieved with a lightweight (~50.3k parameter) Spiking Neural Network (SNN) and a simple ternary event interface. The combination of adaptive sensing and event-native inference makes the proposed design highly suitable for always-on, battery-constrained wearable healthcare devices.

title: A New Current Controller for Grid Following IBR Systems Using μ Transfer Functions.
abstract: Usual controllers deployed on Grid-Following Inverter Based Resource generators need several gain adjustments and lack an analytical methodology to guarantee system stability, and do not take into account transient phasorial phenomena. We propose a new integral transform called μ Transform which bears a new fundamental control theory in Dynamic Phasor space, and generates notions of Transfer Functions in that space. These Transfer Functions generalize the Laplace Transform for rotating dynamic frames, and they generalize the notions of input-output stability, as well as signal processing and controller design in Dynamic Phasor space. Using this new control theory, we propose a new current control scheme for grid-following inverter systems with theoretical and design benefits when compared to the traditional controllers, like guaranteeing system stability through a simple and intuitive assessment of input-output stability, and intuitive tuning of gain parameters using the theoretical framework of the μ Transform. The new controller guarantees zero-error in steady state due to the equivalent Final-Value Theorem for μ Transforms, which is unavailable to the conventional design.

title: Approximate DCT using Scaling Factor Optimization for Error-Resilient Applications.
abstract: Approximate discrete cosine transform (DCT) accelerators are widely employed in energy-constrained image, video, and audio processing systems, where application-specific quality requirements enable aggressive optimization. This work presents a fully synthesizable approximate DCT architecture that exploits scaling factor optimization to minimize area and energy for a specified quality target. A random forest regression model is trained to quantify the relative importance of scaling factors associated with each DCT coefficient, guiding efficient design-space exploration and selection of optimal configurations. Furthermore, activity masking is introduced to dynamically adjust the number of active DCT coefficients, allowing real-time adaptation of energy consumption to varying quality demands. The 8X8 DCT architectures implemented in a 28nm CMOS process achieve 8–35% energy reduction and 13–57% improvement in energy–delay product (EDP) compared to state-of-the-art designs at iso/higher-quality. These gains will scale substantially at the system level, where the DCT core is repeatedly invoked for block-based transforms in medium- and high-resolution image and audio processing workloads.

title: A Multi-rate 2-2 DT-CT MASH DSM Using an Embedded LPF for Easy-Driving.
abstract: This paper presents a multi-rate (MR) 2-2 discrete time (DT)-continuous time (CT) delta-sigma modulator (DSM) that employs a low-pass filter (LPF) as its front-end. The loop filter of the first stage operates in the DT domain to mitigate quantization noise (QN) leakage in MASH architectures, while the second stage operates in a power-efficient CT manner at a 4x sampling rate. To alleviate the demands on the input buffer, an RC LPF is incorporated prior to the DT loop filter, while the LPF compensation (LPFC) circuit is introduced to restore the altered noise transfer function (NTF). Moreover, the LPF also provides an in-band gain of 4, thereby mitigating the design requirements for subsequent stages. Note that the proposed architecture is more robust to RC variations when compared to a pure MR 2-2 CT MASH DSM. Theoretical analysis and further simulation results are provided to validate the proposed architecture.

title: RL-FRA: Exploration and Optimization of FPGA Routing Architectures via Model-Based Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: The routing architecture critically affects FPGA performance in terms of delay, area, and routability. However, its vast design space makes traditional heuristic or Bayesian optimization (BO) methods inefficient to explore and optimize routing architectures. In this paper, we present RL-FRA, a model-based reinforcement learning framework for efficient routing architecture exploration. RL-FRA integrates parameterized modeling, Latin hypercube sampling for initial data collection, and surrogate-based reinforcement learning optimization. Through iterative surrogate retraining and selective real evaluations, the framework converges to high-quality architectures with reduced timing cost. Experimental results show that RL-FRA achieves up to 15.9% area-delay product improvement and reduces exploration time by 33% compared to BO, demonstrating its effectiveness for FPGA routing architecture design automation.

title: A Highly-Scalable and Full-Connected SOT P-Bit Ising Annealer for Combinatorial Optimization.
abstract: Combinatorial optimization problems, which are fundamental to fields such as finance and artificial intelligence, remain challenging for classical computers due to their NP-hard nature. Ising machines have emerged as a promising physical platform that solves such problems by searching for the ground state of the Ising model. In this work, we propose an Ising machine implemented with spin-orbit torque probabilistic bits (SOT P-Bits). A scalable network of SOT MTJ-based P-Bits was constructed and a hardware-software co-calibration strategy was introduced to ensures behavioral consistency across probabilistic units. The compressed sparse row (CSR) method was applied to compress sparse weights while simultaneously optimizing the multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations. To mitigate the issue of local minima in large-scale instances, a local optimal temperature lifting (LOTL) method was employed during simulated annealing. The proposed Ising annealer comprises 1024 fully connected nodes, representing a scalable hardware implementation for solving large-scale combinatorial optimization problems. It has been experimentally evaluated and systematically verified across the device and system levels. The final results demonstrate that the system achieves significantly higher solution accuracy.

title: MPE: A Power-Efficient Edge-Device Mamba Processor with Multi-Dimensional Calculation-Compression Scheme.
abstract: The Mamba architecture has recently emerged as a prominent neural network design, enabling the development of highly competitive large language models (LLMs) with enhanced training efficiency. However, the growing computational and energy demands of Mamba-based models during inference present significant challenges. To address this, this paper proposes an energy-efficient inference processor for Mamba models, which we term the Mamba Processing Element (MPE) containing three architectural features. Firstly, MPE uses the recurrent framework and multi-head attention mechanism to find Low-correlation Assignment Pruning Optimization (LAPO) schemes in spatial models, and further reduces the computation through in-situ computation; Secondly, MPE uses the mechanism of Spatial Multi-head Attention Similarity (SMAS) to further reduce the redundancy and repeated computation in Mamba operations by searching for alternative computations and approximation mechanisms; Thirdly, MPE designs a Dynamic Parallel Compression Quantization (DPCQ) mechanism across spatial dimensions to further improve the computation speed and hardware utilization under high-dimensional weakly correlated tokens. Using 28nm CMOS synthesis tools, the proposed processor has an area of 9.14 mm2and a peak energy efficiency of 93.51TOPS/W, which is estimated to be 16.3 times that of the H100 graphics processing unit (GPU).

title: GTPE: A 28nm 33.12 TFLOPS/W GNN Training Processor with Unstructured Multi Threshold Pruning, Hybrid Multi-mode Approximate Computing and QUIRE Number System Support.
abstract: The GNN (Graph Neural Network) model has shown great potential in the field of artificial intelligence, particularly for complex intelligent problems such as path planning. This paper proposes a GNN training processor GTPE (GNN Training Processing Element) with three key features. Firstly, Unstructured Multi-Threshold Pruning (UMTP) has two thresholds are set when input data is received for filtering and pruning. The remaining data is sorted for a second pruning, followed by in-place computation with padding to reduce storage read demands. Secondly, Hybrid Multi-mode Approximate Computing (HMAC) makes Two-level caches and four types of comparison cases are used to reduce the overall computational workload. Thirdly, QUIRE Number System Support (QNSS) performs using QUIRE and POSIT-based adders and multipliers to ensure high precision under limited bit-width conditions. Using TSMC 28nm CMOS process for tape-out, the proposed GNN training processor achieves a peak energy efficiency of 33.12 TFLOPS/W. In typical training tasks, it provides a 12.56x acceleration for GNN planning algorithms using a 3D maze dataset, as well as 5.21x improvement in energy efficiency.

title: A 51-nW Feature Extraction Analog Front-End for Voice Activity Detection.
abstract: This paper presents a voice activity detection (VAD) analog front end (AFE) that uses a envelope detector and zero-crossing detector (ZCD) as acoustic feature extractor. By extracting the envelope of the speech signal, the feature bandwidth is reduced from 4 kHz to 200 Hz, greatly reducing the sampling rate requirements for ADC and digital backend. The ZCD enhances the anti-interference ability of VAD against specific noise. The proposed AFE implemented in 65 nm CMOS occupies an active area of 0.14 mm2. Post-simulation results indicate that the AFE achieves 4.6 Noise efficiency factor (NEF) while consuming 51 nW from a 1-V supply. By processing the envelope and zero crossing rate features at the digital backend, the entire VAD achieve 95.1%/91.9% speech/non-speech hit rates at 10-dB SNR with babble noise.

title: A 275pJ/bit Fully Integrated 2.4GHz DQPSK Sub-Sampling Phase-Tracking Receiver.
abstract: This paper presents an on-chip fully integrated sub-sampled phase-tracking receiver for the 2.4GHz BLE/WIFI applications. Sub-sampling and an modified (hard-limited) costas loop phase-tracking are adopted to demodulation DQPSK. Comparing with the traditional phase-tracking of the receiver. The special phase-tracking make loop bandwidth is not affected by data rate, the receiver is designed and simulated in CMOS 28nm. The proposed receiver operating at a power supply voltage of 0.9V/0.45V, the power consumption is 1126μW, and the energy efficiency is 275pJ/bit. The sensitivity is -80dBm at a data rate of 4Mbps. The figure of merit (FoM) of the proposed receiver reaches 175.5dB.

title: An Efficient Sine/Cosine Design Using Piecewise Quadratic Approximation for FOC Applications.
abstract: In this paper, we propose an efficient hardware architecture for sine and cosine computations and applied it to field-oriented control (FOC) applications. To achieve higher efficiency, we take the piecewise approximation into consideration and wisely pick out the quadratic form for our design. Only several segments are needed, much less than the linear form, while keeping a relatively small hardware complexity. To further reduce the complexity, we delicately select the endpoints to drastically decrease the required bits of subtractions, with negligible effect on the precision. The implementation results on FPGA show that compared with the open-source design of the traditional coordinate rotation digital computer (CORDIC) method, the proposed design can reduce the latency by about 80% and reach an approximately 65% reduction of hardware resource consumption while maintaining the precision. Moreover, by applying our design in the open-source FOC system, the total hardware resource consumed is reduced by about 12%.

title: AdaCGen: Heterogeneity-Aware Layer Management for Efficient KV Cache Offloading in LLMs.
abstract: The growing demand for large language models (LLMs) in long-sequence, large-batch applications intensifies memory bottlenecks from key-value (KV) cache during inference. While KV cache offloading to host memory alleviates GPU memory constraints, limited PCIe bandwidth creates severe data transfer bottlenecks during full KV cache fetching. Recent advances mitigate this issue by leveraging attention sparsity to selectively transfer only critical KV pairs, combined with prefetching to overlap computation and transfer. However, these approaches overlook heterogeneous attention sparsity across layers, thereby causing imbalanced transfer loads and suboptimal pipeline utilization. To address these computation-transfer imbalances, we propose an adaptive layer classification management strategy. By identifying transfer-dominant layers and applying computation-transfer co-optimization, our method reduces their data transfer volume by 3.56×. Experiments demonstrate up to 1.34–1.59× lower inference latency compared to state-of-the-art KV cache offloading systems.

title: In-pixel Decorrelation Time Approximation Circuit for Rapid Wide-field Dynamic Light Scattering Imaging.
abstract: Dynamic light scattering imaging (DLSI) is a wide-field optical technique that visualizes blood flow dynamics from laser-illuminated tissue. Practical systems, however, are constrained by pixel size, I/O bandwidth, and latency due to large off-sensor data transmission and per-frame offline exponential fitting. This paper propose a data-compressed DLSI method combined with binarized autocorrelators that outputs only two summed autocorrelation bins per pixel and recovers the decorrelation time constant through an analytical solution. Simulations with synthetic photon streams show that time constants over 10–100 lag bins can be estimated with MAPE <~10% when the photon detection rate per lag bin is lower than 0.70. Relative to a 5-bit, 32-bin autocorrelator, the approach reduces per-frame throughput by ~9.5×, lowers latency via rapid time-constant approximation, and yields an estimated ~4× pixel-area reduction, enabling higher resolution at constant silicon area.

abstract: Based on conventional digital foreground calibration, this work introduces an auxiliary calibration capacitor to address calibration failures in high-precision SAR ADCs caused by excessive offset voltage. A 16-bit 1-MS/s SAR ADC utilizing this structure has been implemented in 180-nm CMOS. The design also adopts an inter-segment redundancy scheme, which helps alleviate errors induced by incomplete CDAC settling.

title: Live Demo of A Bidirectional Communication Gateway for Battery-free IoT End Devices.
abstract: A large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) system comprises numerous end devices [1] . To eliminate the inconvenience of wire arrangement and battery replacement, many previous studies have proposed battery-free (BF)-IoT end devices [2] . BF-IoT end devices integrate energy harvesting (EH) modules to capture ambient energy from sources including light, wind, radio-frequency (RF) signals, and human motion, and convert these energy forms into electrical power. This characteristic eliminates the requirement for conventional power cables or batteries. However, the energy output of EH modules is typically limited and volatile. Such energy constraints restrict the effective standby duration of BF-IoT end devices. As a result, most BF-IoT end devices cannot maintain continuous online status and are not directly compatible with energy-intensive wireless technologies (e.g., WiFi). This intermittent connectivity further indicates that traditional bidirectional communication—either between BF-IoT end devices and the host device or among different BF-IoT end devices—is not feasible. For this reason, most BF-IoT devices have not been supported by commercial smart home ecosystems (e.g., Google Assistant, Apple HomeKit, Xiaomi Mijia) to date.

title: A High-Accuracy Peak Detection Algorithm Using a First-and-Last-Event Histogram with a Dual-Mode TDC for dToF Sensors.
abstract: In this paper, a high-accuracy time-gated differential-cumulation peak detection (TGDC-PD) algorithm is proposed with a first-and-last-event histogram (FLH) scheme for dToF sensors. The proposed algorithm effectively mitigates the pile-up distortion and enhances ranging accuracy. Moreover, a dual-mode multi-event time-to-digital converter (TDC) with low dead time is presented to enable first-and-last-event quantization as well as multi-event operation. The Nutt interpolation method is employed to improve TDC linearity. A novel interpolator with inherent misalignment error immunity is also introduced, eliminating the need for additional synchronization circuit. The proposed TDC is fabricated in a 0.11 μm CIS technology, achieving a 62.5 ps resolution with a conversion rate of 200 MS/s. The worst case DNL and INL are of +0.14/-0.11 LSB and +0.36/-0.08 LSB, respectively. The proposed TGDC-PD algorithm with FLH is experimentally validated through indoor ranging measurements using a digital SiPM (dSiPM) and the proposed TDC, demonstrating accurate target distance extraction at 6.5 m.

title: Adaptive Row-wise Attention Score Pruning and Compensation for Attention Acceleration.
abstract: Transformer models have become a cornerstone of modern AI applications, with the attention layer playing a critical role within each transformer block. As the computational demands of these models continue to grow, considerable research has focused on accelerating attention computation while maintaining acceptable accuracy. Among these approaches, low-precision top-k prediction is commonly used to speed up the attention layer by selecting only the largest values for the softmax operation.Despite its effectiveness, the top-k prediction method still leaves room for improvement. In this paper, we propose two complementary techniques to accelerate attention computation while preserving accuracy. First, we introduce Two-stage Adaptive Row-wise Attention Score Pruning, which carefully prunes unimportant elements in each row. Second, we present Pruning-aware Softmax Compensation, which mitigates the numerical error caused by pruning and further improves accuracy.Experimental results demonstrate that our methods achieve higher accuracy and greater computational savings compared to the conventional top-k prediction approach.

title: A 32-Gb/s Adaptive DFE with Dynamic Step SSLMS Achieving 0.9 μs Convergence.
abstract: This paper presents a 32-Gb/s wireline receiver featuring an adaptive decision-feedback equalizer (DFE). The proposed dynamic step sign–sign least mean square (DS-SSLMS) algorithm adaptively adjusts the step size based on the detected gradient magnitude, significantly reducing the adaptation time of the DFE while minimizing steady-state mean square error. Furthermore, compared to conventional LMS algorithms, DS-SSLMS incorporates historical gradient weighting to dynamically adjust the step size, which not only accelerates convergence but also effectively prevents the adaptation process from being stuck in local optima. A full receiver prototype was implemented in a 12 nm process to validate the effectiveness of the DS-SSLMS algorithm. Post simulation results demonstrate that with a PRBS31 input pattern at 32 Gbps, the adaptive DFE achieves convergence within 0.9 μs and compensates for up to -36 dB of channel loss. The total power efficiency of the receiver is 2.06 pJ/b.

title: A 0.57-pJ/bit Adaptive CTLE with Novel High-Pass Node Sampling Adaptation for Wireline Receivers in 28-nm CMOS.
abstract: This paper presents a continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE) with an adaptation technique based on highpass branch node sampling. In conventional adaptive CTLEs, sampling circuitry on the main data path introduces parasitic loading that limits bandwidth. To address this issue, the adaptive sampling point is relocated to a high-pass node within a feedforward branch. The signal at this node is proportional to the input derivative, which strongly correlates with the channel’s high-frequency loss, thus providing a reliable adaptation metric. By avoiding direct loading of the main path, this approach minimizes bandwidth degradation and reduces power consumption. Moreover, an asynchronous clock sampling method is employed to reduce power and eliminate complex clock requirements. Post-layout simulations of the design in a 28-nm CMOS process demonstrate that the equalizer consumes 18.3 mW from a 0.9-V supply, compensates for channels with up to 21 dB loss at 16 GHz, and achieves an energy efficiency of 0.57 pJ/bit.

title: An 11.5-bit ENOB 312.5kS/s Column-Parallel Two-Step Single-Slope ADC for Infrared Focal Plane Readout Circuit.
abstract: A 12-bit column-parallel two-step single-slope (TS-SS) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) is proposed for digital infrared focal plane readout circuits. The proposed TS-SS ADC divides the quantization process into coarse conversion and fine conversion, both by the SS ADC. The ADC accelerates the quantization process while suppressing kickback noise by reusing the offset-storage capacitor to shift the storage node of the coarse quantization result toward. A CDAC-based coarse ramp generator reduces settling time and suppresses glitches. The proposed ADC is implemented in a 180nm CMOS process, consuming 94.45μW and operating at 312.5KS/s sampling frequency per channel, achieving a peak SFDR of 76.95dB with a SNDR of 71.99dB and a figure of merit (FoM) of 104fJ/step.

title: Adversarially Regularized Latent Flow for Enhanced Conditional Video Generation.
abstract: We investigate a counterintuitive yet consistent phenomenon in conditional video generation. Within diffusion-based frameworks operating in perceptually aligned but compressed latent spaces, latent representations with higher image reconstruction error can paradoxically yield superior video quality after the diffusion process. This observation motivates an investigation into how distribution-level reconstruction losses influence motion-relevant latent structures. To this end, we employ the Jensen–Shannon (JS) divergence between the distributions of reconstructed and ground-truth images as the training objective. This distributional constraint encourages the latent motion predictor to emphasize motion dynamics over appearance details. Although it produces a higher reconstruction error, the resulting motion features, when projected back to the image space, enable more accurate and temporally coherent video generation. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks show consistent improvements in motion fidelity and overall video quality, attributed to enhanced spatiotemporal disentanglement and the suitability of motion-pure latent representations for diffusion-based refinement.

title: Perception-Core: Reconfigurable Energy-Efficient Domain-Specific Architecture with Multimodal Fusion for AIoT.
abstract: In emerging artificial intelligence & internet of things (AIoT) System-on-Chip (SoC) applications such as smart radar, assisted driving, and intelligent robotics, there is a critical demand to simultaneously handle computationally intensive computer vision tasks, neural network inference, high-precision signal processing, and linear algebra applications under low-power constraints. Perception-Core is a highly energy-efficient coarse-grained reconfigurable architecture (CGRA) SoC dedicated to perception computing, designed to process such multimodal data. Implemented in TSMC 28nm HPC+ process technology, it features: 1) Reconfigurable computing array with fused operator blocks that support multi-algorithm datapath and multi-precision data formats; 2) Memory virtualization strategy employing hierarchical storage, affine-coalescing memory, and data prediction modules to reduce on-chip data movement, cutting memory access bandwidth requirements by 35%; 3) Affine-reconfigurable architecture, featuring hardware-level adaptive arithmetic intensity adjustment, significantly enhancing hardware utilization efficiency in multi-task perception scenarios. Perception-Core achieves energy efficiencies of 239 GFLOPS/W (FP32) and 554 GFLOPS/W (FP16) at 28nm. Normalized comparisons show a 25.6% energy efficiency improvement over state-of-the-art designs, with expanded application scope.

title: Impact of Community Structure on Robustness of Power Systems.
abstract: Modern power grids are expanding and tightly interconnected, making cascading failures the leading cause of large blackouts and a severe threat to secure operation. Network science shows that grid topology—especially community structure—critically shapes fault propagation. This paper systematically examines how community structure affects power-system robustness against cascading failures. First, we propose simple rules to build large-scale grids ranging from random to strongly modular networks, mirroring realistic topologies. Second, a DC power-flow cascade model, coupled with Monte Carlo simulations, reproduces and statistically analyzes the post-disturbance evolution. Finally, we adopt the power-loss ratio (RBS) as an index to quantify and compare robustness, assessing how communities inhibit fault spread and explaining the causes. Results reveal that networks with stronger communities exhibit smaller average power losses and retain higher structural integrity during cascades; clear community boundaries isolate fault zones and block further spread, significantly enhancing grid robustness and resilience. This paper provides theoretical guidance and practical strategies for power grid topology design, enhancing disaster resistance.

title: Entity-Aware Graph Neural Network for Multi-Intent Spoken Language Understanding in Power Dispatch Systems.
abstract: As digital power dispatch and intelligent question answering evolve, natural-language queries in dispatch datasets increasingly involve multiple tables and fields within a single utterance, making joint modeling of multi-table intents and entity-level slots a core challenge. To address this, we propose the Entity-aware Graph Neural Network (EA-GNN), which models power-dispatch semantic parsing as multi-view intent–slot collaborative reasoning. By formulating the task as heterogeneous intent–entity graph inference constrained by table–field priors and corpus co-occurrence, EA-GNN produces schema-consistent semantic structures in a single forward pass. The framework ensures alignment between slot boundaries and database schemas through entity-level recognition and relation-aware multi-hop reasoning. Experiments on real-world power dispatch datasets verify its superior accuracy and generalization in multi-intent semantic parsing and retrieval.

title: A MASH Two-Phase Incremental ADC with High Tolerance to QN Leakage.
abstract: This paper presents a multi-stage noise shaping (MASH) two-phase incremental analog-to-digital converter (IADC). During the first phase, the IADC operates as a 2-1 MASH architecture. To achieve a higher resolution, the second phase employs a cyclic exponential-linear MASH topology. Note that the quantization noise (QN) from both stages is further resolved in the second phase, intentionally maintaining the same tolerance to QN leakage as the first phase. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed architecture offers enhanced tolerance to QN leakage compared to the prior 2-1 MASH two-phase IADC, while achieving higher resolution than a conventional 2-1 MASH IADC. Mathematical analysis and further simulation results are presented to confirm the principle of the proposed architecture.

title: A 210.6 nW FLL-based Standby Timer with Offset Compensation in 65nm CMOS for IoT Applications.
abstract: This work proposes a low-power, temperature-compensated frequency-to-voltage conversion (FVC)-based FLL as a standby timer for on-chip clock generation in compact and cost-constrained low-power IoT applications. The proposed architecture offers a viable crystal-alternative with high energy efficiency, incorporating inherent error amplifier offset cancellation and improved temperature stability compared to open-loop oscillators. A first-order RC low-pass filter inserted at the FVC feedback node effectively suppresses the ripple of the control voltage and output frequency FOUT, while comprehensive S-domain analysis verifies the loop stability. Fabricated in 65-nm CMOS, the FLL prototype generates a 2-MHz clock from a 0.6-V supply, consuming only 210.6 nW while achieving 80.2 ppm/^C stability across a temperature range of -30◦C to 70◦C. It demonstrates high energy efficiency with a figure of merit of 0.105 nW/kHz.

title: GCC-CIM: A Charge-Domain Compute-in-Memory Macro using Grouped-Row Capacitors and C-2C Ladder with Improved Multi-Bit MAC Linearity.
abstract: Analog compute-in-memory (ACIM) reduces data movement and leverages analog parallelism for efficient multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) operations. In charge-domain ACIM, grouped-row capacitors (GRC) and C-2C ladders have been proposed to execute one-shot multi-bit MACs, but practical implementations often suffer weighting imbalance and linearity loss due to unequal parasitics. This work presents a charge-domain multi-bit MAC macro with two circuit-level improvements. First, eliminating inter-group switches in GRC structure ensures that each bit-cell uses an identical input path, equalizing parasitics and improving activation weighting. Second, an asynchronous-sampling, synchronous-coupling signed C-2C ladder reduces top-/bottom-plate switching and ensures uniform output gain scaling, enhancing multi-bit weighting linearity. Implemented in 22nm CMOS, the macro performs one-shot 4W4A MAC operations. Post-layout simulations show excellent linearity (DNL2.

title: Salient-Channel-Guided Knowledge Distillation in Learned Image Compression.
abstract: In learned image compression (LIC), only a small subset of latent channels is crucial for reconstruction, while many others contribute little to visual fidelity. Conventional knowledge distillation (KD) transfers all latent features from a teacher to a student, leading to redundant supervision and limited compression benefit.We propose a salient-channel-guided knowledge distillation (SCKD) approach that focuses supervision on channels most relevant to reconstruction quality. Salient channels are identified through a lightweight masking analysis that measures the degradation when each latent channel is removed, and only these channels are used as primary distillation targets. This strategy, relying on a training-free and architecture-agnostic saliency analysis, allows the student to allocate its capacity to high-impact representations without training additional modules.Experiments on representative LIC frameworks show consistent rate–distortion improvements compared with conventional KD methods. This work is inspired by our prior study on the Invariant Salient Channel Space (ISCS), extending its insight into a practical, task-driven distillation strategy.

title: Piecewise Linear Ultra-Wideband Chirp Generators for Sub-THz FMCW Radar in 28-nm CMOS.
abstract: This paper proposes a novel piecewise approach for chirp generation in sub-THz wideband frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar systems. Two wideband piecewise linear chirp frequency generators (PLFGs) are demonstrated for a sub-THz FMCW radar: a closed-loop dual-band PLFG (DB-PLFG) which can be cascaded with frequency multipliers (×3) for short-range and a direct-synthesized quad-band PLFG (QB-PLFG) at sub-THz for long-range. The DB-PLFG includes a bandwidth (BW)-enhanced phase-locked loop (PLL) with a magnetically tuned dual-band voltage-controlled oscillator (DB-VCO) to generate two piecewise linear sub-bands from 30.1 to 42.7 GHz. The QBPLFG features multiple wideband coils, utilizing mutual inductance analysis between the resonant coils to enhance the linearity and performance, which can generate four piecewise linear sub-bands covering 73.7 to 117.8 GHz. Fabricated in 28nm CMOS and measured on the probe station, the DB-PLFG achieves 6.5 MHz RMS frequency deviation with an FoMTdown to -199.2 dBc/Hz. The QB-PLFG delivers 46.1% fractional bandwidth (FBW), 48.1 MHz RMS frequency deviation, with an FoMTdown to -197.9 dBc/Hz.

title: Analysis of Converged 3D Gaussian Splatting Solutions: Density Effects and Prediction Limits.
abstract: We investigate what structure emerges in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) solutions from standard multi-view optimization. We term these Rendering-Optimal References (RORs) and analyze their statistical properties, revealing stable patterns-log-normal scales and bimodal radiance-across diverse scenes. To understand what determines these parameters, we apply learnability probes: training predictors to reconstruct RORs from point clouds without rendering supervision. Our analysis uncovers fundamental density-stratification: dense regions exhibit geometry-correlated parameters amenable to render-free prediction, while sparse regions show systematic failure across architectures. We formalize this through variance decomposition, demonstrating that visibility heterogeneity creates covariance-dominated coupling between geometric and appearance parameters in sparse regions. This reveals RORs' dual character-geometric primitives where point clouds suffice, view synthesis primitives where multi-view constraints are essential. We provide density-aware strategies that improve training robustness and discuss architectural implications for systems that adaptively balance feed-forward prediction and rendering-based refinement.

title: A 97.63 fJ/conv-step 3 GSa/s 2-Way Time-Interleaved (TI) 3-Bit Flash ADC for Analog In-Memory Computing (IMC) Deep Learning (DL) Accelerators in 28-nm CMOS.
abstract: In analog in-memory computing (IMC) accelerators for deep learning (DL) systems, the massive deployment of column-parallel ADCs makes power and area overhead a critical concern. Leveraging recent advances in DL algorithms, the resolution requirement of ADCs in IMC systems has been reduced, thereby favoring low-resolution but highly efficient designs to sustain system-level benefits. This work presents a 2-way time-interleaved (TI) 3-bit flash ADC that avoids the need for front-end sample-and-hold (S&H), parallel-to-serial (P2S) conversion, and background calibration, while maintaining sufficient effective number of bits (ENOB) for coarse quantization, thereby achieving a balanced trade-off among power, area, and ENOB. A feedthrough-aware design exploits the alternating polarity of clock feedthrough in the interleaved architecture to suppress disturbance at the ADC input without additional circuitry. Fabricated in 28-nm CMOS, the prototype occupies an active area of 0.076 mm2, consumes 1.68 mW at 3 GSa/s, and achieves 2.52-bit ENOB with a Walden FoM of 97.63 fJ/conversion-step. These results demonstrate the suitability of the proposed ADC for large-scale deployment in IMC-based DL accelerators.

title: A Compact Current Balancing Method for Multi-Phase Buck DC -DC Converter.
abstract: This paper presents a fully integrated current balancing method for multi-phase buck converters. The proposed approach eliminates any current-sensing components. Implemented in the slave phase, it samples the low-side power MOSFETs' VDSvoltage to generate a control signal. This signal modulates the slave phase's ramp, forcing current balancing with the master phase. A sequential control circuit ensures precise operation. The method is validated in a two-phase interleaved buck converter designed in a 180nm BCD process. The current balancing circuit occupies only 0.02 mm2. Post-simulation results show it reduces the maximum current balance error from 26.57% to 2.4%. The error remains below 1% for load currents above 2 A, and reaches 0.45% at a 6 A load. The circuit also enables fast current balancing after load transients, without degrading the output voltage response.

title: Aegis-ES: Hazard-Adaptive Conformal Event-Sparse Inference for Glucose Monitoring.
abstract: Continuous noninvasive glucose monitoring on wearables faces a core tension between accuracy and on-body energy. We present Aegis-ES, an event-sparse, risk-controlled streaming framework that computes when and how much to infer. A hazard-adaptive fusion (HAF) module converts multimodal cues (meals/EDA/activity) into a fused event intensity that opens and closes adaptive windows. A decision-theoretic defer-or-compute (DoC) gate triggers heavy inference only when the expected value of computation exceeds its marginal energy, and is post-hoc calibrated with conformal risk control (CRC) to bound the risk of skipped decisions. Inside windows, a mathematically defined learned time-step pruning (LTP-Time) reduces FLOPs while preserving state consistency via closed-form k-step state-space updates. On three public datasets (BIG-IDEAs, CGMacros, OhioT1DM), Aegis-ES matches or exceeds the accuracy of an always-on heavy model (e.g., MAE@30 min 15.2 vs. 15.4 mg/dL; AUROC 0.912 vs. 0.905) while cutting daily energy by 66% (from 11,405 to 3,852 J) and heavy duty-cycle by 78% (from 1.00 to 0.22). On an MCU-class prototype, it lowers per-window latency by 29% and reduces peak memory through temporal pruning.

title: Dual Graph Feature Learning for ADHD Diagnosis: Integrating Node and Edge Information in Brain Networks.
abstract: Current graph neural network (GNN) approaches for analyzing brain functional connectivity networks (FCNs) in Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) often underutilize edge information and fail to capture dynamic node dependencies. To address these, we propose the Dual-Graph Feature Learning Network (DGFLN) for ADHD classification and biomarker discovery. Our framework constructs dual graph representations: a node graph, where multi-band amplitudes of low-frequency fluctuations (ALFF) serve as node features and both functional connectivity (FC) and node-wise relationships define edge attributes; and an edge graph derived through line graph theory, which facilitates the interchange of node and edge roles.DGFLN implements an alternating feature update mechanism with optimized graph convolution operations, facilitating hierarchical learning of node-edge relationships across network layers. Extensive experiments on the ADHD200 dataset achieve 97.3% accuracy, significantly outperforming existing methods. Additionally, gradient-based biomarker analysis identifies key regions in the bilateral limbic and default mode networks associated with ADHD, aligning with prior studies.

title: A 14-bit 4GS/s DAC Achieving 68dBc SFDR Up to 1.7GHz with Digital Pre-Distortion and Switching-Glitch Compensation in 28nm CMOS Process.
abstract: This paper presents a 14-bit, 4 GS/s current-steering digital-to-analog converter (DAC). To enhance linearity, a novel random code rotation-based digital pre-distortion technique is introduced, which quantifies the static error of each current-source bit by controlling rotation cycles during calibration. This approach corrects mismatches in current cells without requiring excessive calibration control logic or switches. Additionally, a normally-open current-source-based switching glitch compensation technique is proposed to achieve code-independent and constant switching activity with minimal hardware overhead, effectively mitigating inter-symbol interference. Post-simulation in a 28 nm CMOS process demonstrates that the DAC achieves a spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) exceeding 68 dB at 1.7 GHz output. The proposed techniques collectively improve SFDR by 13 dB across the Nyquist band.

title: A Scalable and Highly Efficient NTT Unit for Crystals-Dilithium.
abstract: Dilithium was selected by NIST for its strong security, reliability, and quantum resistance. However, its large-scale polynomial multiplication relies on the Number Theoretic Transform (NTT), which remains a critical bottleneck. Efficient NTT/INTT implementations are thus vital for secure and reliable cryptographic circuits. Existing scenario-specific NTT designs achieve high performance but lack scalability, as their cycle counts and parallelism are fixed. To address this, we propose a configurable NTT/INTT unit for Dilithium supporting multiple parallelism levels. We optimize K-RED-based modular multiplication to reduce resource usage while maintaining a short critical path for higher frequencies. In addition, a conflict-free NTT architecture with two-dimensional processing elements (2D_PEs) is introduced to exploit stage parallelism, boosting throughput while lowering resources. The proposed design delivers efficient performance trade-offs and achieves 5.8%-82.5% area-time product (ATP) improvements over state-of-the-art FPGA works.

title: HOC: Hierarchical Overlapped Communication Optimization for Parallelism in Distributed Training.
abstract: Communication accounts for a major fraction of time in large-scale model training. Existing studies mainly optimize end-to-end training, while communication efficiency itself remains underexplored. We present HOC (Hierarchical Overlapped Communication), a family of collective algorithms that decomposes global communication into intra- and inter-node phases. The core insight is to minimize traffic on bandwidth bottlenecks while maximizing overlap across bandwidth domains, thereby reducing overall completion time. HOC employs Hierarchical Decomposition to isolate bandwidth tiers, Chunked Overlap Pipelining to overlap inter- and intra-node transfers, and Adaptive Optimization through offline profiling with run-time lookup and small-message fallback for maximal bandwidth utilization. Experiments on a multi-node A100 cluster show that HOC significantly accelerates communication for large message sizes, achieving up to 1.30x, 1.18x, and 1.12x speedups over PyTorch NCCL baseline on All-Gather, Reduce-Scatter, and All-Reduce, respectively.

title: An Ultra-Low-Power, High-Output-Power and High-Sensitivity Bioelectronic Transceiver.
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-low-power, high-output-power, and high-sensitivity transceiver for implantable bioelectronic systems in a 40-nm CMOS technology. The design targets stringent power constraints by employing a wake-up scheme. The transceiver introduces a transmitter architecture based on a cascaded injection-locked ring oscillator (ILRO) and edge combiner (EC), alongside a receiver utilizing an envelope-detection demodulation technique for power reduction. The switched-capacitor power amplifier (SCPA) enables high output power through its high-efficiency characteristic, while a high-gain low-noise amplifier (LNA) ensures high-sensitivity reception. Compared with prior works, this transceiver achieves simultaneous high output power and high sensitivity within an ultra-low-power architecture, making it ideal for implantable bioelectronic applications. The proposed techniques reduce sleep-mode power consumption to 40 nW. The transmitter delivers 2.37-dBm output power with 8.2-mW consumption, and the receiver attains –64-dBm sensitivity with 200-µW consumption over a 10-meter wireless range.

title: An Efficient Fully-Pipelined Hardware Architecture for Optimized Sparse Polynomial Multiplication in CRYSTALS-Dilithium.
abstract: Efficient hardware implementations for post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) algorithms are urgently needed for practical deployment. In this paper, we introduce a fully pipelined dual-input sparse polynomial multiplication architecture specifically optimized for CRYSTALS-Dilithium, a lattice-based digital signature algorithm selected by NIST. Our FPGA design fully exploits polynomial sparsity and a five-stage pipelined architecture, achieving significant improvements in computational performance and resource utilization. Experimental results on Xilinx Artix-7 and Virtex Ultrascale+ platforms demonstrate that the proposed sparse polynomial multiplication architecture achieves optimal hardware efficiency with fewer resources. Experimental data show approximately 2× speedup compared to existing state-of-the-art solutions, along with a 61.2% reduction in resource consumption. Thus, the proposed architecture provides an efficient and resource-optimized hardware implementation for sparse polynomial multiplication in CRYSTALS-Dilithium.

title: An Integrated Wearable Electromagnetic Sensing System with Wireless Vector Readout for Noninvasive Glucose Monitoring.
abstract: Noninvasive glucose monitoring is essential for diabetes management, yet current solutions either rely on invasive measurement or lack seamless integration for practical wearable use. This paper presents an integrated wearable electromagnetic (EM) sensing system with wireless vector readout for noninvasive glucose monitoring. The system consists of a nested-architecture metamaterial-inspired EM sensor and a compact stepped-frequency continuous-wave (SFCW) readout module. The two modules are vertically stacked to form a lightweight and skin-conformal sensing platform. The nested EM sensor generates weak omnidirectional electromagnetic coupling that increases sensing coverage and enhances sensitivity to glucose-induced permittivity variations. Furthermore, the wireless readout module performs real-time gain and phase demodulation, enabling vector sensing without the need for a benchtop vector network analyzer. In-vitro experiments across glucose concentrations from 0 to 400 mg/dL demonstrate clear monotonic trends in both amplitude and phase responses, confirming the effectiveness of the presented sensing system. Consequently, the proposed system offers a promising pathway toward practical wearable solutions for noninvasive continuous diabetes monitoring.

title: A Dual-Path SSHC Rectifier with Decoupled Battery Architecture for Enhanced Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting.
abstract: Piezoelectric energy harvesting is essential for enabling self-powered wireless sensor networks in Internet of Things applications. This paper presents the first analysis of the voltage-blocking mechanism in synchronized switch harvesting on capacitors (SSHC) rectifiers, which occurs when the piezoelectric voltage magnitude exceeds a threshold determined by the transducer’s impedance characteristics. This phenomenon occurs under shock excitation or low-frequency conditions, yet has been previously overlooked in capacitor-based rectification techniques. To address this limitation, a dual-path SSHC (DSSHC) architecture is proposed, employing two parallel energy extraction paths at different voltage levels to extend the energy harvesting window. The high-voltage path handles normal operation, while the low-voltage path maintains energy transfer during voltage-blocking conditions. A decoupled dual-battery architecture eliminates charge redistribution losses between storage capacitors. Simulation results using an 8-stage implementation demonstrate 4.92% higher peak output power compared to conventional SSHC and elimination of voltage-blocking conditions.

title: Design of Symmetric Transformer-Based Quadrature Couplers.
abstract: Symmetric transformer-based quadrature couplers are designed and analyzed in this work. A systematic approach is presented to simplify the design process by correlating the physical dimensions of an interleaved transformer-based quadrature coupler to its target operating frequency and characteristic impedance through mathematical equations, bridged by its lumped-element L-C-k model. To validate the accuracy and reliability of the proposed design method, four quadrature couplers targeting 10/20/30/40 GHz were designed in 65nm CMOS following the proposed design approach. For all four designs, an insertion loss of around 3.5 dB and a phase error of <1.5°are achieved, respectively, within the ±0.5 dB bandwidth, corresponding to 5.5~11% fractional bandwidth. The comparison between the ideal model and EM simulation results demonstrates a high level of agreement. This numerical approach not only reduces the computational effort in the design process and accelerates the development cycle of a transformer-based quadrature coupler but also potentially becomes a vehicle to generate massive design examples and provide prompt decision feedback for AI-based quadrature coupler design.

title: Efficient LLM Inference on ARM via Hardware-Aware Operator Co-design and Heuristic Mixed-Precision Search.
abstract: On-device large language models (LLMs) offer low-latency response, enhanced data privacy, and personalized experience. However, their enormous parameter size and high computational demand pose severe challenges for deployment on resource-constrained edge devices such as ARM CPUs. To address this, we propose a co-design framework that integrates hardware-aware operator optimization with a heuristic mixed-precision search. We systematically optimize key Linear and Attention operators via loop tiling, high-throughput kernel implementation, and operator fusion, specifically tuned for ARM architectures. Concurrently, a heuristic search method based on a genetic algorithm is proposed to identify an optimal mixed-precision quantization scheme that balances model accuracy, memory footprint, and inference speed. Experiments on ARM devices show that our approach substantially reduces resource usage while accelerating inference. Under comparable accuracy, the optimized model consumes only 8.89% of the original memory and achieves 5.11× higher throughput in the prefill stage and 11.86× in the decode stage. Compared to state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, our framework attains higher accuracy with 4.03× greater memory reduction and a further 1.25× prefill throughput improvement.

title: A Low-Cost and High-Accuracy Bipolar Divider for Stochastic Computing.
abstract: Stochastic computing (SC) encodes real values with stochastic bitstreams, leveraging simple logic gates to implement highly efficient arithmetic circuits. The processing of signed numbers in SC usually employs a bipolar encoding format. Achieving high precision in bipolar stochastic divider circuits, however, remains a significant challenge due to the inherent limitations of current designs. To address this, this work proposes a bipolar correlation-controlled divider (BCCDIV), based on a sign-magnitude separation mechanism and a shared random number source (RNS). By optimizing the utilization of bitstream correlation, this design ensures operational accuracy while reducing hardware costs. Additionally, the hyperbolic tangent function is implemented using the proposed bipolar divider to verify its effectiveness in practical applications. Experimental results show that the mean squared error (MSE) of the proposed BCCDIV is only 4.70×10-3, which is 92.93% lower than that of the traditional Bipolar Gaines Divider (BGDIV), 13.33% lower than Bipolar Correlated Divider (BCORDIV), and 79.84% lower than bipolar in-Stream correlation-based divider (BISCBDIV), with a 10-bit RNS.

title: A Buck Converter with Mixed-Signal Computational Charge Balance Control for One-Cycle Fast Recovery.
abstract: This paper presents a voltage-mode (VM) controlled buck converter with a computational charge balance control (C-CBC) technique. The C-CBC technique overcomes the limitation of conventional one-cycle recovery techniques, which fail to work at gradual load transition, and extends its reliable operation to almost any load transition speed, achieving fast transient response simultaneously. Additionally, this paper uses adaptive ramp compensation, which not only corrects the minor output voltage deviation after the finish of the C-CBC, but also further enhances the transient response. Simulation results show that the recovery time of the proposed VM loop is reduced from 31 μs to 2.6 μs for 500 mA load step, the undershoot are reduced from 101 mV to 20 mV. When dealing with a large load step of 6 A/ns, the response time is only about 30% of that of a conventional buck converter.

title: Boosting Vector Instruction Throughput in RISC-V via a Hybrid Decoupled Architecture with VLIW-Driven Execution.
abstract: This paper addresses the instruction throughput bottleneck in traditional scalar-core-driven vector coprocessors by proposing a hybrid decoupled vector architecture driven by a Very Long Instruction Word (VLIW) scheme. The design introduces a complete workflow from task submission to synchronization: the host core configures tasks via memory-mapped CSRs, triggers execution, and is then released to achieve coarse-grained task-level parallelism; the vector coprocessor integrates hardware task scheduling, dual-buffered instruction prefetching, dynamic VLIW packing, and scalar instruction execution capabilities to support fine-grained instruction-level parallelism. Benchmarking against the Ara processor demonstrates that under short-vector scenarios (AVL=32), the proposed architecture achieves a 44% performance improvement while increasing vector unit utilization from 40.2% to 67.9%. Although the performance advantage narrows with increasing vector length, the architecture consistently outperforms traditional design in both vector unit utilization and overall performance (e.g., +3.2% perf. at AVL=512). Furthermore, it exhibits excellent area and power characteristics, comprehensively validating the design’s effectiveness.

title: A DLSK Global Phase-Shift Controlled Wireless Power Transfer System Achieving Above 90% RX Efficiency.
abstract: A global phase-shift control strategy for wireless power transfer system is proposed in this paper. Both the transmitter and the receiver can regulate the output power within a single resonant frequency by employing phase-shift control. In the receiver, the normalized phase shift (DRX) is adjusted to an appropriate value by an error amplifier. Meanwhile, a global power regulation is implemented by adjusting the phase shift of the transmitter (DTX) to constrain DRXwithin 0.5~0.8, ensuring that the receiver can maintain a high efficiency under a wide load range. To indicate whether the phase shift of the receiver is excessively high or low, a delay-load-shift-keying (DLSK) is presented. By modulating the turn-off time of the receiver, the transmitter can detect these two states to regulate transmitted power. The proposed control system is designed with 0.18μm BCD process. The output voltage is regulated to 5V with only 1.2mV voltage ripple. Simulation results show that the RX efficiency can be maintained above 90% under a load range of 15mA~150mA. Compared to the system without global phase-shift control, the light-load efficiency can be improved by about 25%.

title: SRNeRV: A Scale-wise Recursive Framework for Neural Video Representation.
abstract: Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for video representation and compression. However, existing multi-scale INR generators often suffer from significant parameter redundancy by stacking independent processing blocks for each scale. Inspired by the principle of scale self-similarity in the generation process, we propose SRNeRV, a novel scale-wise recursive framework that replaces this stacked design with a parameter-efficient shared architecture. The core of our approach is a hybrid sharing scheme derived from decoupling the processing block into a scale-specific spatial mixing module and a scale-invariant channel mixing module. We recursively apply the same shared channel mixing module, which contains the majority of the parameters, across all scales, significantly reducing the model size while preserving the crucial capacity to learn scale-specific spatial patterns. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SRNeRV achieves a significant rate-distortion performance boost, especially in INR-friendly scenarios, validating that our sharing scheme successfully amplifies the core strengths of the INR paradigm.

title: A 2-18 GHz LNA Based on Dual-mode Hybrid Coupled Frequency Response Reshaping Technique.
abstract: This paper presents a 2-18 GHz ultra-wideband low-noise amplifier (UWB LNA) with a dual-mode hybrid coupled frequency response reshaping technique, which employs gm-boosting coupled microstrip line (CMSL) to improve the first-stage gain without introducing additional noise, and series-parallel coupled inductor peaking (SPCIP) to compensate for the second-stage high-frequency gain and expand the bandwidth. This design is based on the 0.25 µm GaAs pHEMT process, and according to the test results, the LNA has an average gain of 23.5 dB over the 2-18 GHz frequency range, a gain flatness of ±0.7 dB, and a noise figure of less than 1.8 dB within the operating bandwidth, which has a significant advantage over other designs at the same frequency band. The average OP1dB is 9 dBm, and the power consumption is only 112 mW with a single power supply of 5 V, and the chip area is 1.26×1 mm2.

title: SCOPE-3D: An Energy Efficient Accelerator for Implicit Neural Representation-based Sparse-view Computed Tomography Reconstruction.
abstract: The increasing demand for portable CT and other resource-constrained clinical environments necessitates compact and low-power reconstruction systems. This paper presents 3D Self-supervised Coordinate Projection (SCOPE-3D), a low-power hardware-efficient accelerator for Sparse-View Computed Tomography (SVCT) based on Implicit Neural Representation (INR), an emerging paradigm in reconstruction. The SCOPE-3D architecture is optimized for the computational flow of our proposed INR-based SVCT reconstruction algorithm, integrating a hash encoding module, fully connected network computation arrays, and a ray accumulation module. Fabricated in a 40nm CMOS process, the SCOPE-3D chip occupies a total area of 5.74 mm2, operates at frequencies ranging from 55.6 MHz to 166.7 MHz, and consumes between 16.8 mW and 61.0 mW of power. SCOPE-3D represents a promising solution for energy-efficient SVCT rendering in embedded medical imaging systems.

title: A 240-to-945MHz 8-Phase PLL Clock Synthesizer With 1.22° Skew Calibration in 180nm HV CMOS for Closed-Loop Digital SiC/GaN Gate Driving.
abstract: This work presents a clock synthesizer for a digital gate driver application targeting a cycle-by-cycle drive profile optimization in fast-switching SiC and GaN power converters by integrating a burst-mode ADC for capturing the switching transients. Fabricated in 180nm HV CMOS, the proposed clock synthesizer achieves a timing resolution ranging down to 132ps by implementing an 8-phase time-interleaved architecture. The 8-phase clock is generated by a ring VCO inside an integer-N charge pump PLL with a wide programmable frequency range from 240MHz to 945MHz (119%). A min./max. search-based background phase skew calibration is proposed that reuses the 7-bit burst-mode ADC of the gate driver during its idle time to minimize the implementation overhead. Measurements of 5 samples demonstrate a standard deviation reduction of the phase spacing errors from 2.77° to 0.64°. A consistent calibration accuracy is achieved across the whole frequency tuning range with a maximum residual error of 1.22°.

title: High-Selectivity RF On-Chip Dual-Passband Filter With Multiple Stopband Transmission Zeros Using Through-Glass-Via Technology.
abstract: This paper reports a novel type of high-selectivity RF on-chip dual-passband filter using through-glass-via (TGV) integrated passive device (IPD) technology. Its core circuit part consists of a lumped-element signal-interference dual-path network, which features a dual-band bandpass filter (BPF) behavior with two close-to-passband transmission zeros (TZs) located at the lower and upper stopband regions and two inter-band TZs. In order to achieve an improved upper stopband with two more TZs, two in-series-cascaded LC tanks are introduced at the input and output accesses. Based on the conceived whole equivalent circuit, the design principle of the proposed RF dual-band BPF is detailed by theoretical frequency responses associated with various sets of LC components. For validation purposes, a proof-of-concept prototype of the devised RF BPF implemented in TGV IPD technology is designed and electromagnetically simulated at the 3-D layout level. The two simulated lower and upper passbands are centered at 2.86 and 7.29 GHz with minimum in-band insertion-loss levels of 0.46 and 1.95 dB, 3-dB fractional bandwidths (FBWs) of 50.6% and 6.86%, and inter-band and upper stopband suppression levels above 26.34 and 17.69 dB from 4.8 to 6.49 GHz and from 8.02 to 14.4 GHz, respectively.

title: Cryogenic Influences on Frequency Dividers and Output Buffers in Ring-Oscillator Design and Characterization.
abstract: Qubit-interfacing circuit design at 4 K is critical to system performance in many quantum-computing platforms. Cryogenic influences in silicon processes, combined with stringent power budgets, impede specification-compliant CMOS integrated circuit design at 4 K, motivating a departure from conventional design approaches. This work targets key building blocks of frequency-reference chains within qubit controllers, including ring oscillators, frequency dividers, and output buffers. Two comparable designs were implemented in a 65-nm process: a baseline standard-cell design and a 4-K-optimized custom design. Their performance is compared in terms of supply current, output frequency, and rms period jitter. Measurement results demonstrate that the non-ideal cryogenic effects observed in the standard-cell design can be mitigated through the use of low threshold voltage CMOS, comprehensive guard-ring layouts, and a simplified D-latch design. These customizations yield thermally stable frequency performance while reducing power dissipation by approximately 20 times and rms period jitter by over 19 times at sub-4 K. This work characterizes the cryogenic manifestations in standard-cell implementations and demonstrates their mitigation via a custom design, serving as a practical reference for future cryogenic CMOS developments.

title: RRAM-based CAM for Energy-Efficient In-Memory Text Compression System.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance across diverse applications, driving an explosive growth in text data for training. This surge poses critical challenges for data storage and transmission, highlighting the need for lossless text compression systems with high energy efficiency and compression ratio. In this work, we propose a resistive random-access memory (RRAM)-based content-addressable memory (CAM) for high-efficiency, high-compression text compression processing. The proposed RRAM-based CAM enables on-chip storage of large-scale dictionaries and single-cycle string matching, which is experimentally demonstrated using an 1Mb 40nm 1-transistor–1-RRAM (1T1R) chip. Experimental results on text compression and decompression demonstrate a 1224× improvement in search energy efficiency and a 49.8× reduction in search latency compared with a commercial CPU, validating the potential of RRAM-based CAMs for future in-memory compression systems.

title: A Compilation Framework for Domain Specific Multi-Chiplet Systems with Double-Layer Genetic Algorithms.
abstract: As deep learning scales, single-die inference is bounded by reticle limits, motivating heterogeneous multi-chiplet systems with AI domain-specific accelerators (DSAs). However, inter-chiplet communication degrades performance–energy efficiency and complicates deployment. To address this issue, a compilation framework is introduced to automatically optimize deployment on such systems. Unlike prior work, both activation and weight traffic are modeled, including repeated weight transfers under limited on-chip memory. The deployment is cast as combinatorial optimization with throughput- or energy- prioritized objectives. A double-layer genetic algorithm is employed to decouple task segmentation from chiplet mapping, shrinking the search space and accelerating convergence while retaining global optimality considerations. A fast event-driven evaluator is integrated to estimate throughput and energy. Given a model and hardware description, deployment strategies are produced automatically. On an 8-chiplet system, up to 30.83% higher throughput and 24.65% lower energy were achieved; on average, throughput improved by 12.26% and energy decreased by 10.87% relative to state of the art work.

title: A Low-Power FPGA Implementation of QRS Detection for Real-Time Heart Rate Monitoring.
abstract: Wearable heart rate monitoring relies on efficient QRS detection for real-time ECG analysis, yet traditional algorithms demand high computational resources, making them unsuitable for low-power platforms. We present an optimized FPGA implementation of a QRS detection algorithm using adaptive thresholding and parallel processing, achieving millijoule-level energy consumption and over 98.5% accuracy on several widely used real-world ECG datasets. The design leverages fixed-point arithmetic and a pipelined architecture to minimize latency (under 5 ms) and resource utilization (under 35% of LUTs on a Zynq-7020). Compared to software-based counterparts, our implementation achieves a 7.8–43.0× improvement in power efficiency, while maintaining clinical-grade precision, enabling operation in battery-powered wearable monitoring devices.

title: ERSRP: A 55nm 46.28 MPixels/(s·mm2) 104 FPS Efficient Real-Time Super-Resolution Processor with Layer-Fused Lightweight Engine.
abstract: This paper presents ERSRP, a 55nm Edge Real-Time Super-Resolution Processor that achieves 104 FPS at FHD resolution with a peak area efficiency of 46.28 MPixels/(s·mm2), 8.86× higher than the state-of-the-art. The processor is designed through a software-hardware co-optimization approach, addressing the low utilization, high memory demand, and workload imbalance challenges inherent in lightweight SR networks. At the algorithmic level, an Ultra-Lightweight Super-Resolution (ULSR) model is proposed that integrates depth-wise and point-wise separable blocks with a pixel-shuffle mechanism to achieve high-quality reconstruction (37.18 dB PSNR and 0.9581 SSIM on Set5) with only 5.62K parameters. At the hardware level, the ERSRP introduces a Lightweight Accelerated Engine (LAE) sup-porting a Layer Parallel Computing Scheme (LPCS) to improve lightweight operator throughput by 48.9%. A Point-wise Layer Fused Scheme (PLFS) further enhances utilization by 4.95× through inter-core and intra-core fusion without intermediate memory. Fabricated in a 55nm UMC CMOS process, the ERSRP achieves a throughput of 215.7 MPixels/s and supports 104 FPS real-time SR at FHD.

title: Transient Stability Prediction for AC Microgrids Using a Data-Driven Approach.
abstract: Transient stability assessment (TSA) is paramount for ensuring the reliability of AC microgrids comprising both grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) converters, especially in multi-machine systems subjected to large disturbances. Conventional methods including time-domain simulations, manifold-based bifurcation analysis, and the Lyapunov energy function approach, are often hampered by computational inefficiency, model complexity, or excessive conservatism. These limitations render them unsuitable for the rapid stability evaluation required in modern power electronics-dominated grids. To overcome these challenges, this paper introduces a novel data-driven framework for fast and accurate transient stability prediction. Leveraging machine learning (ML) techniques, this paper proposes a data-driven method, which bypasses the need for computationally expensive simulations and analytical approximations. The results demonstrate that our framework significantly reduces computational burden while maintaining high predictive accuracy, facilitating near real-time assessment. This work provides a practical and scalable solution for enhancing transient stability management in inverter-based AC microgrids.

title: Layer-Aware Timing-Driven Global Routing for Advanced Technology Nodes.
abstract: Routing is a critical stage for VLSI timing closure. Global routing algorithms without considering timing delay might lead to inferior solutions with timing violations. This paper proposes a timing-driven global router for advanced technology nodes. First, we present a congestion-aware layer planning method that assigns an optimal routing layer range for each critical net. Then, we design a timing-driven Steiner tree construction algorithm that generates a timing-optimal topology through a Single-Source Shortest Path (SSSP) based reconstruction. Finally, we develop a timing-constrained multi-level maze router to resolve congestion without timing degradation. Experimental results on 7nm industrial benchmarks show that, compared to an advanced commercial tool and the leading academic engine OpenROAD, our proposed routing algorithm achieves the best results on key timing metrics (WNS and TNS).

title: Parallel Critic-Free Reinforcement Learning with Direct Parameter Space Mapping for Large-Scale Analog LDO Sizing.
abstract: Traditional reinforcement learning (RL) methods for analog circuit sizing suffer from low sample efficiency, requiring extensive simulations in large-scale parameter spaces. This paper proposes a critic-free RL approach with direct parameter space mapping to significantly reduce simulation requirements. The customized environment maps actions directly to the entire parameter space, enabling rapid exploration. Advantages are computed through group-relative normalization without critic networks, ensuring accurate estimation in sparse reward distributions. The single-step configuration achieves parallel sample evaluation and policy updates, accelerating convergence. Three practical low-dropout regulators with 65-179 parameters validate the method, achieving convergence within 2.5k-5k simulations and outperforming human designs. Compared to state-of-the-art RL methods, the proposed approach achieves 5.5× –19.8× faster convergence.

title: Reliability and Optimization for Neural Network Accelerators using Value-Aware Error-Marking Pattern with Sequential Access Error Correction.
abstract: In this paper, we propose two mechanisms: value-aware error-marking pattern (VA-EMP) and sequential access error correction to relieve the effect of SA faults on NVM-based accelerators. VA-EMP serves as a low-cost and effective solution. VA-EMP reserves a specific value in the exponent (EXP) field to indicate data affected by exponent SA1 faults, enabling efficient error marking with minimal hardware overhead. Sequential access error correction exploits the inherent sequential dataflow property of neural networks, which can reduce the storage and combinational circuit overhead of SA fault correction. By integrating these two schemes, accuracy is preserved while minimizing the power and area overhead associated with the combinational circuits used for SA fault marking and correction in NVM-based accelerators. The evaluation results reveal that our proposed mechanisms can help enhance the SA fault tolerance rate up to 0.2% on the Imagenet dataset within 2% accuracy loss. Overall, our proposed mechanisms can enhance the fault resilience of NVM-based accelerators with only 3.5% hardware overhead.

title: A 196-MHz Bandwidth Transimpedance Amplifier with High Out-of-Band Rejection Employing Transmission Zeros.
abstract: This paper presents a baseband Rauch transimpedance amplifier (TIA) topology with 196-MHz bandwidth (BW) for Sub-7-GHz direct-conversion receivers (RXs). By connecting an equivalent RLC bypass network in parallel, a pair of transmission zeros around the channel bandwidth is introduced to achieve out-of-band (OOB) rapid roll-off while effectively suppressing close-in blockers. To meet the TIA's requirements for high bandwidth and excellent inband (IB) and out-of-band (OOB) linearity, the circuit incorporates a three-stage operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) to achieve high DC gain and gain–bandwidth product (GBW). Designed in 28-nm CMOS technology, the circuit occupies a 0.05-mm2area and consumes 22.5 mW of power from a 1-V supply voltage. The TIA achieves a 196-MHz baseband bandwidth, an OOB rejection of 24 dB at 3-baseband-bandwidth (BB-BW), an adjacent-channel OOB IIP3 of 46.9 dBm at 2-BB-BW, and an integrated input-referred noise (IRN) of 147.5 µVrms from 1-MHz to 196-MHz. The corresponding FoM value reaches 186.5 dBJ–1, surpassing all previous designs.

title: Layout-Aware Standard Cell Synthesis via Reparameterization Multi-Task Bayesian Optimization.
abstract: Standard cells (SCs) fundamentally influence the power, performance, and area (PPA) of digital integrated circuits. With advances in manufacturing technology and increasing integration density, traditional sequential design flows face two challenges: upstream "optimal designs" diverge from post-layout reality, and isolated design stages restrict the solution space. We introduce LASS, a Layout-Aware Standard Cell Synthesis framework. LASS addresses key challenges through (1) a multitask Gaussian process(MTGP) regression model that captures the correlation between pre- and post-layout simulation1results to transfer rich pre-layout data and enhance post-layout modeling under limited data; and (2) a reparameterization-based probabilistic improvement (RePI) acquisition function for efficient exploration in discontinuous design spaces. Experimental results show that LASS optimizes the PPA figure-of-merit (FoM) to 78% in the best case and 84% on average, compared to the X1-driven designs. Moreover, case studies confirm tangible circuit-level performance improvements, with up to 35% delay reduction.

title: FeRAM-Based Reconfigurable Strong PUF with Ultra-Low Power and Enhanced Attack Resilience.
abstract: Hardware security is critical in modern information technology, particularly with the exponential growth of in-memory AI inference scenarios and neuromorphic computing. Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs) have become a key solution for securing these devices. In this paper, we propose a PUF design that uses Ferroelectric Random-Access Memory (FeRAM) as the entropy source. FeRAM, known for its non-volatility, high read/write cycle endurance, and low power consumption, offers distinct advantages for PUF implementation. Evaluated in 180 nm CMOS technology, the results show that the 1T1C FeRAM-based PUF scheme we proposed exhibits low power consumption and high robustness and achieves a uniformity of 49.1% and a reliability of 97.6%. With a dataset of 1M Challenge-Response Pairs (CRPs), the prediction accuracy of the proposed PUF under Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES) algorithm-based attacks is 78.1%, demonstrating a 19% reduction compared to SRAM-based PUFs.

title: Topology-Mapping Co-Design for Scalable LLM Accelerators with Hierarchical Mesh-of-Trees NoC.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) demand high-bandwidth and low latency on-chip communication fabrics. This paper presents a hierarchical mesh-of-trees (MoT) network-on-chip (NoC) based on blending mesh and tree topologies, and a corresponding simulation framework to optimize the LLM workload deployment. Our topology-mapping co-design framework models a hierarchical MoT NoC system and provides integrated cost estimation, mapping optimization, and utilization analysis. Evaluation results demonstrate improved network utilization and performance of LLM inference compared to the conventional flat NoC system. We conduct design space explorations across key design aspects—mapping strategy, cluster size, and LLM dimensions—to reveal design trade-offs and extensive insights.
