title: IDEA: A Real-Time Unified Accelerator for Dual-Task Image Restoration: Dehazing and Illumination Enhancement.
abstract: High-performance image dehazing is crucial for various visual tasks, particularly in the field of embodied intelligence, where real-time processing and energy efficiency on edge devices are essential. This paper introduces a deep learning-based dehazing network, namely DIE, and its corresponding accelerator, IDEA, which are optimized to correct illumination bias. The proposed DIE features a Chunk-Wise Fused Concatenation Scheduling (CFCS) and an inter-Processing Element line buffer (ILB) mechanism to enhance data reuse, leading to a 2.24× acceleration. Additionally, a dual-task scheduling approach and a Heterogeneous Ping-Pong (HTTP) strategy are utilized to balance the workload and improve parallelism. Implemented in a 55nm process, the accelerator achieves a core area of 2.83mm2, power consumption of 192mW, and a frame rate of 72 fps at 1080p resolution. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first ASIC implementation of a deep learning–based dehazing architecture, demonstrating strong potential for low-power, high-quality visual enhancement in edge intelligence applications.

title: A 0-400MHz DDFS Based on the Multi-Level CORDIC Pipeline for Radar Applications in 65-nm CMOS Process.
abstract: This paper proposes a CORDIC phase-amplitude conversion module driven by a high-bit wide phase accumulator to implement a high-precision waveform synthesis DDFS module for Radar applications. The module supports rapid frequency loading and can achieve frequency switching within an extremely short time, making it suitable for complex multimode modulation requirements. By optimizing the CORDIC pipeline of the phase-to-amplitude conversion, the design strikes a balance between power, area and high spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR). The design is implemented using TSMC 65-nm technology. Based on post-simulation results, it achieves an SFDR of at least 80.19 dBc at a clock frequency of 1 GHz and can directly generate linear frequency modulation signals in the range of 0 to 400 MHz in the digital domain. Simulation results show that the proposed design is suitable for a wide range of high-performance radar and communication systems.

title: Interactive State Space Model with Cross-Modal Local Scanning for Depth Super-Resolution.
abstract: Guided depth super-resolution (GDSR) reconstructs HR depth maps from LR inputs with HR RGB guidance. Existing methods either model each modality independently or rely on computationally expensive attention mechanisms with quadratic complexity, hindering the establishment of efficient and semantically interactive joint representations. In this paper, we observe that feature maps from different modalities exhibit semantic-level correlations during feature extraction. This motivates us to develop a more flexible approach enabling dense, semantically-aware deep interactions between modalities. To this end, we propose a novel GDSR framework centered around the Interactive State Space Model. Specifically, we design a cross-modal local scanning mechanism that enables fine-grained semantic interactions between RGB and depth features. Leveraging the Mamba architecture, our framework achieves global modeling with linear complexity. Furthermore, a cross-modal matching transform module is introduced to enhance interactive modeling quality by utilizing representative features from both modalities. Extensive experiments demonstrate competitive performance against state-of-the-art methods.

title: Precise Hardware Trojan Localization at RTL Through Graph-Based Feature Integration.
abstract: Under a globalized semiconductor supply chain, hardware Trojans have become a significant threat to hardware security and trustworthiness. In this work, we propose a novel hardware Trojan localization method at register transfer level (RTL) using graph convolutional networks (GCNs). We integrate both static circuit structural features extracted from RTL code and dynamic behavioral features obtained through random simulation to form comprehensive node-level representations. A four-layer GCN model is then trained for classifying design nodes in RTL code and identifying the Trojan-infected ones, in which class-balanced (CB) focal loss is employed to effectively address the class imbalance issue. Experimental results using 42 RTL benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method can successfully locate Trojan-infected nodes in hardware designs with true positive rate (TPR), true negative rate (TNR), accuracy and area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 94.72%, 97.01%, 97.00% and 97.83% respectively on average.

title: SPICA: Energy-Efficient SRAM-Based Multi-Precision Multi-Mode Compute-in-Memory Accelerator for AI Inference.
abstract: Embodied artificial intelligence (EAI) and neuromorphic computing (NC) demand specialized hardware with extreme energy efficiency (EE) and low latency. The substantial energy cost associated with the large number of multiply accumulate (MAC) operations in von Neumann architectures necessitates the adoption of Compute-in-Memory (CIM) architectures. To support the multi-precision requirements, including integer (INT) and floating point (FP) computations of complex EAI models while minimizing energy cost, the POSIT format offers a promising solution as it achieves comparable accuracy to FP data with lower bit widths. In this work, we propose an efficient SRAM-based CIM accelerator supporting shared-exponent and mantissa-truncated POSIT (SEMTP) and INT MACs, achieving a balanced trade-off between EE and accuracy. Particularly for transformer workloads in EAI, the proposed mask-aware power gating scheme saves up to 17.09% of the total system power. Evaluated in 28 nm CMOS technology, this work can achieve a peak throughput of 0.54 TFLOPS and an EE of 2.2 TFLOPS/W@SEMTP, representing an 18.18× improvement over prior work. Additionally, it achieves 1.13 TOPS and 5.02 TOPS/W@INT8, 3.67 TOPS and 15.46 TOPS/W@INT4.

title: An Adaptive Sampling Frequency FOCV MPPT Based on Energy-Packet-Counting for Energy Harvesting Applications.
abstract: This paper presents a design of a discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) buck-boost converter for photovoltaic (PV) cell or thermoelectric generators (TEGs) in energy harvesting system. Based on the traditional fractional open-circuit voltage (FOCV) maximum power point tracking (MPPT) method, the proposed design integrates an energy-packet-counting-based input power detection (EPC-PD) module, which detects input power solely by monitoring switching signals, minimizing interference with the power converter’s normal operation. The proposed adaptive sampling frequency FOCV MPPT (ASF-FOCV MPPT) re-samples the open-circuit voltage (VOC) only when input power changes. Additionally, the discrete digital VOCsample-and-hold (DD-S&H) circuit eliminates the FOCV system voltage dividers or capacitors, and decouples the sampling and holding processes, reducing per-sampling open circuit time to 1 μs while achieving virtually infinite holding time. Compared with the traditional fixed-sampling-frequency FOCV MPPT, the proposed ASF-FOCV MPPT maintains high tracking efficiency under stable input power and achieves fast response when input power changes. Simulation shows an MPPT efficiency of over 97.5% (with 99.5% peak) for harvester voltage of 200 mV to 800 mV, more than 80% of point-to-point efficiency for input power of 100 μW to 10 mW (with 92% peak), and a 200μs to 600μs maximum power point update time when the input power changes.

title: A 6.12-to-8.62GHz Class-F23 VCO with Series-LC Assistance Achieving 195.9dBc/Hz FoMT at 100kHz Offset.
abstract: This paper introduces a Class F23voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) that achieves robust flicker noise suppression and a low 1/f3phase noise corner across an ultra-wide tuning range. The proposed LC-series-assisted resonator enables broadband common-mode resonance at the second harmonic using only one additional inductor, eliminating the need for manual tuning. Implemented in 40-nm CMOS, the VCO exhibits a tuning range from 6.12 to 8.62 GHz. It achieves a phase noise of -102 dBc/Hz at 100 kHz offset and a peak FoMTof 195.9 dBc/Hz. The 1/f3PN corner frequency remains below 220 kHz across the band, reaching as low as 58 kHz, within a compact area of 0.07 mm2.

title: On the Purpose of Harmonic Suppression: A Two-stage Approach Enabling ACPR Enhancement for VMbPWM-based All-Digital Transmitter.
abstract: To eliminate the excessive memory consumption and to enable the agility of the all-digital transmitter (ADT), the Viterbi-based pulse width modulation (VbPWM) and the Viterbi-based multi-bit deduction PWM (VMbPWM) are proposed to leverage the in-band signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) advantage of the mapping-based PWM (MPWM), but the two schemes demonstrate a worsened adjacent channel power ratio (ACPR) due to their insufficient harmonic suppression. By analysing the principle of MPWM, a lower ACPR bound of -33 dB is found in this work, where this result is leveraged to form a two-stage modulation scheme balancing both ACPR and SNR. Numerical simulations have suggested a 10 dB of ACPR enhancement compared with VMbPWM while decreasing the in-band SNR. The decrease of SNR turns out to be minor according to the hardware evaluation results implemented within the ZCU102 kit, and a maximum of 20 dB ACPR enhancement is presented at the cost of doubled resource consumption.

title: A Multi-Channel Bioelectric Signal Transmission Device Featuring Low-Power Design.
abstract: This paper presents a wireless bioelectrical signal transmission device with 1024 channels. Eight analog front-end (AFE) circuits with 128 channels each constitute a total of 1024 acquisition channels. The maximum sampling rate of the acquisition channel is 32kHz, and the sampled data is output with 16-bit quantization. A system on chip (SoC) based on RISC-V core serves as a data transmission device and is connected to 8 AFEs via QSPI, responsible for the automatic transmission of high-speed data streams. The maximum data rate supported by the transmission module is 524.288Mbps. The transmission device integrates three operational modes for diverse scenarios, with the capability to switch the system clock as required. The power consumption under low power consumption mode is 15.58uW. The output terminal of the transmission device is connected to the Ultra Wide Band (UWB) module for wireless transmission. The transmission device has been verified through 40nm CMOS tape-out process, and the chip size is 2.97mm x 1.98mm.

title: Malice Hides in Equivalence: Attacking Text-Image Alignment Assessment with Subtle Text Variations.
abstract: Text-Image Alignment Assessment (TIAA), which aims to automatically evaluate the alignment between an image and its textual description, has gained significant attention due to its critical role in generative text-to-image and image-to-text tasks. However, in this paper, we reveal that existing TIAA models are vulnerable to purely textual perturbations that preserve semantics. Based on this finding, we make the first attempt to attack TIAA models by modifying only the textual input, generating adversarial textual samples that retain the original semantics while significantly misleading the alignment predictions. Considerable efforts have been made to overcome the significant challenges posed by the discrete nature of the text modality. Specifically, to enable gradient-based optimization of textual input, we first introduce a Learnable Embedding Matrix (LEM) strategy and leverage Gumbel-Softmax for word-wise adversarial updating by sampling from categorical probability distributions over the vocabulary. Moreover, we employ a Lagrange relaxation strategy to incorporate the stealthiness constraint, ensuring text fluency and semantic similarity compared to the original ones, into the main attack objective. Extensive experiments have demonstrated that existing TIAA models exhibit significant vulnerabilities on white-box attack.

title: Dual 3T2R Differential SOT MRAM Array for Energy-Efficient In-Memory Computing in Deep Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Edge tasks represented by embodied intelligence require deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to adapt to real-world environments, which in turn demands high compute throughput and write bandwidth under tight energy budgets. We propose a dual 3T2R differential Spin-Orbit Torque Magnetoresistive Random-Access Memory (SOT-MRAM) compute-in-memory (CIM) array for on-device deep DRL. The bit-cell employs complementary encoding and two switchable operating modes, enabling high-precision forward inference and backpropagation. Leveraging the stochastic switching of devices, we implement a lightweight on-chip random number generator to support stochastic experience replay and policy exploration. Further, we realize a fully on-chip RL pipeline with efficient dataflow. Evaluation results show that the proposed design delivers high speed, accuracy, and robustness, achieving an energy efficiency of 28.766 TOPS/W, thereby offering a low-power, low-latency pathway for edge DRL.

title: Zero-Crossing Aligned and Self-Fill-In Chopping for IMD-Free Chopper Amplifiers.
abstract: Chopper amplifiers suffer from intermodulation distortion (IMD) arising from the interaction between the input signal and the chopping clock, mainly due to finite amplifier bandwidth that produces output spikes during clock transitions. This work proposes a zero-crossing aligned chopping technique that eliminates these spikes, and thus the resulting IMD, by aligning each chopping clock edge with the zero-crossing instant of the input signal. Implemented in a 0.18-µm CMOS process, a chopper amplifier with the proposed method achieves a 44 dB IMD reduction down to the white-noise level for a single tone near four times the chopping frequency (80 kHz), and a 31 dB IMD reduction under a two-tone 79/80 kHz test. For less stringent applications, a self-fill-in technique is also introduced, providing 14 dB IMD reduction with negligible overhead. These techniques enable IMD suppression without sacrificing offset, noise, or power, offering a practical and effective solution for next-generation precision chopper amplifiers.

title: A 8-19-GHz Current-Reused Wideband LNA With Dual Transformer Feedback.
abstract: In this paper, we present a wideband high-gain low-noise amplifier (LNA) with dual transformer feedback and current-reuse techniques. The first and second stages utilize a current-reuse technique to minimize low power consumption, while the third stage employs a cascode structure for high gain. Dual transformer feedback is applied to the first and second stages to suppress high-frequency gain roll-off, thereby extending the bandwidth. This paper proposes an improved transformer structure, which achieves compact footprint and higher coupling coefficient compared to traditional coupled-line implementations. The proposed wideband LNA is fabricated in 0.15-μm GaAs pseudomorphic high-electron-mobility transistor (pHEMT) process. The measured results show that the proposed LNA achieves a gain of 25.1 dB with a 3-dB bandwidth of 8-19 GHz. The LNA exhibits output 1 dB compression point (OP1dB) of 9 dBm, a minimum noise figure of 1.56 dB, and an S11 value of less than -10 dB across the entire operating bandwidth. The fabricated LNA consumes 84 mW and occupies a chip area of 1.13 mm2including test pads.

title: Low-Latency Scaling-Free Hyperbolic CORDIC Algorithm Based on Linear Rotation Angles and Leading-One Bit Detection.
abstract: The hyperbolic Coordinate Rotation Digital Computer (CORDIC) algorithm is the core computing unit of digital systems and has been widely used in fields such as digital signal processing and artificial intelligence. Its core advantage lies in its hardware implementation friendliness, as complex operations such as hyperbolic functions, logarithms, and exponents can be completed solely through adders and shifters, without the need for complex multipliers, significantly reducing design complexity. However, traditional hyperbolic CORDIC has obvious drawbacks. On the one hand, a fixed number of iterations generates redundant operations, resulting in excessively high latency. On the other hand, a scaling factor is introduced and an additional multiplier is required to deal with the final iteration result, further increasing hardware overhead. To solve this issue, we propose a low-latency and scaling-free hyperbolic CORDIC algorithm based on linear rotation angles and leading-one bit detection. Through MATLAB simulation, the proposed algorithm has fast convergence and high computation accuracy, with a delay reduction of 52.4% at the precision magnitude of 10−6. An example hardware implementation shows that it has an area of 11128.19µm2and a dynamic power of 7.1139mW under the 28nm CMOS technology. Compared with traditional solutions, the area-delay product (ADP) has decreased by 49.8% and the power-delay product (PDP) has decreased by 62.5%, fully adapting to low latency and low power consumption application scenarios.

title: A Compact Wide-Band RF Energy Harvesting Front-End Based on an On-Chip IMN with 51.78% Peak PCE.
abstract: This paper presents a wide-band RF energy harvesting (RFEH) front-end with an on-chip impedance matching network (IMN). Different from traditional transmission-line wide-band IMN or multi-stage/two-stage LC IMN, an improved wide-band LC IMN is proposed with a parallel circuit combination of LC in the shunt path. The parallel capacitor in the shunt arm provides a shift in the clockwise direction on the admittance trace of Smith chart and enlarges the required admittance, which plays a key role to reduce the required parallel inductance. To eliminate the impact of off-chip parasitic parameters on wide-band matching, the proposed IMN is integrated on-chip and co-optimized with the rectifier. The proposed wide-band RFEH front-end has been fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS technology. Measurement results indicate that the proposed RFEH front-end achieves an overall efficiency exceeding 40% at an input power (Pin) of 5 dBm across the 1.9 GHz to 5.1 GHz bandwidth range, with a peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 51.78% at 2.4 GHz. The total area of chip is only 387 × 375 μm2.

title: An Efficient BIST and Fault Diagnosis Circuit for TSVs.
abstract: 3D integrated circuits incorporate a high density of die-to-die(D2D) interconnects to enable functional connectivity between chiplets. The bonding process for these high-density interconnects is susceptible to manufacturing defects, which can induce various interconnect faults. To effectively test various faults, test algorithms and built-in self-test (BIST) techniques based on the Kth-aggressor fault (KAF) model are employed, but also prolong the test duration, elevates overall chip testing costs. To address this issue, this paper propose a test and diagnosis pattern generation algorithm utilizing true/complement codes. The proposed algorithm is fully compatible with the KAF model, covers ten fault types between any two inter-group TSVs, and enables concurrent fault localization and diagnosis. Furthermore, we design a BIST circuit featuring time-division multiplexing diagnosis logic, implemented based on the proposed algorithm. Compared to the current fastest scheme, the proposed method reduces the test time by approximately 10.2% for a given group of TSV interconnects.

title: Analysis of Photoreceptor Non-linearity in Dynamic Vision Sensors.
abstract: The photoreceptor circuit is the cornerstone of dynamic vision sensors (DVS), setting the performance ceiling for low-power, wide-dynamic-range neuromorphic sensing. However, under low-bias and high-illumination conditions, the circuit’s logarithmic response suffers from severe non-linearity, leading to event threshold drift. This paper provides a novel analysis that decouples the two main sources of variation: it identifies the non-linearity as originating from the logarithmic transistor’s transition from weak to strong inversion, while demonstrating that the feedback amplifier’s bias and body effect solely control the DC operating point. Based on this insight, we propose a circuit-level design methodology focused on managing the transistor’s current density by optimizing its aspect ratio, thereby constraining its operation to the ideal weak inversion region. Simulations in a 110 nm process demonstrate that this approach extends the upper limit of the linear dynamic range by over 30 dB, enabling the sensor to handle significantly higher illumination levels without distortion.

title: FNeRV: Frequency-Aware Neural Video Representations with Dynamic Spatial Guidance.
abstract: Recent advances in video compression have introduced implicit neural representation (INR) methods, achieving performance comparable to state-of-the-art codecs such as H.266/VVC. However, most existing INR approaches lack explicit modeling of frequency information and struggle to reconstruct high-frequency details. To address these limitations, we propose FNeRV, a frequency-aware neural video representation framework with dynamic spatial guidance. FNeRV incorporates a Wavelet Sub-band Frequency Loss to accurately capture spectral details, while the dynamic spatial guidance mechanism enhances reconstruction by adaptively shifting supervision from coarse to fine structures over the course of training. Experimental results show that FNeRV has superior performance compared to state-of-the-art implicit neural representation methods in video regression and video compression tasks.

title: An 8.91 nW, 1.74 ppm/°C Subthreshold CMOS-Only Voltage Reference for Temperature Sensors.
abstract: This paper presents a low-power CMOS voltage reference (VR) based on a two-stage stacked diode-connected MOS transistor (SDMT) structure, implemented entirely with MOS transistors. The VR is designed using a standard 0.18 μm CMOS process and occupies an active area of 0.029 mm2, with all transistors operating in the subthreshold region. Post-layout simulations show that the reference voltage reaches 365 mV at 27 °C, while the power consumption is only 8.91 nW. The VR exhibits a temperature coefficient of 1.74 ppm/°C across a wide temperature range from −40 °C to 125 °C. In addition, it demonstrates a line sensitivity (LS) of 0.25 %/V over a supply voltage range of 0.7 V to 1.8 V, confirming its excellent stability and ultra-low-power performance for temperature sensor applications.

title: A Low Complexity BPF Polar Decoder Design with Sensitivity-Aware LUT Compression Framework.
abstract: Addressing the critical need for polar decoders that can deliver both high throughput and superior error performance, Belief Propagation with Flipping (BPF) has been studied as an effective scheme. However, the extensive number of processing units (PEs) in traditional BPF decoders results in significant circuit area. To overcome the limitation, this work proposes a Sensitivity-Aware Look-Up Table (LUT)-based Belief Propagation with Flipping (SAL-BPF) decoder, where complex arithmetic functions are replaced by LUTs with message sensitivity analysis. This approach greatly reduces computational complexity and memory access with negligible frame error rate (FER) performance degradation. The proposed SAL-BPF polar decoder with 1024 bit length and 1/2 rate is Synthesized with 28nm CMOS technology. It shows that the proposed LUT-based processing element (PE) achieves over 44% area reduction and 17% delay savings compared with conventional arithmetic PE, with less than 0.35 dB FER performance degradation. The proposed SAL-BPF polar decoder with 6-bit quantization, achieving 1.33 GHz maximum frequency and 0.508 mm2area. It achieves an excellent trade-off between decoding performance and hardware efficiency.

title: A Low-Cost Subtractive Dither for Continuous-Time 1-Bit Delta-Sigma Modulators.
abstract: This paper presents a low-cost subtractive dither for continuous-time (CT) 1-bit Delta-Sigma Modulators (DSMs). The scheme employs a compact digital block to realize dither-based randomization, achieving idle-tone and harmonic spur suppression with negligible digital area and power overhead. The dither is injected through a Random-Delay-Insertion Feedback (RDIF) path and subtracted on a per-cycle basis at the output, resulting in a noise-shaped residual. A CT 1-bit first-order DSM integrating the proposed dither engine was fabricated in 40-nm CMOS, and the dither engine itself occupies only 28 μm2. Measured results show that enabling the RDIF path together with per-cycle subtraction suppresses spurs and restores the in-band SNR from 13.6 dB to 49.0 dB relative to the unsubtracted dither case, while introducing only a modest in-band SNR degradation of less than 3 dB compared to the non-dithered DSM baseline, indicating partial cancellation in the presence of practical nonidealities.

title: HyperNTT: An Ultra-High Throughput Number Theoretic Transform Accelerator for FHE.
abstract: As the most computationally intensive operator in fully homomorphic encryption (FHE), the number theoretic transform (NTT) critically determines FHE’s computational efficiency. In this paper, we propose HyperNTT, an ultra-high throughput NTT accelerator. Its conflict-free dataflow eliminates transposition overhead in the four-step NTT algorithm, while ping-pong buffering enables stall-free pipelined execution. We further introduce a low-cost FPGA-optimized Montgomery modular reduction circuit to minimize DSP usage without sacrificing frequency. Experiments show that HyperNTT outperforms comparable state-of-the-art designs, delivering up to a 130.2× improvement in throughput. Its overall performance, measured in area time product (ATP), is enhanced by 2.1× to 16.8×.

title: Topic-Guided and Context-Accumulated Conditions for Prompt Compression.
abstract: Prompt compression has become an essential technique for enabling large language models (LLMs) to process long-context tasks while operating within limited context windows, particularly for applications like document summarization. However, current approaches face two fundamental challenges: (1) the absence of global guidance, and (2) insufficient utilization of inter-segment dependencies. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a novel condition-guided prompt compression framework featuring two complementary conditions: (1) a topic-guided condition generated by a small auxiliary model that captures high-level semantic themes through its reasoning capabilities, and (2) a context-accumulated condition that dynamically aggregates information across multiple segments. Together, these conditions preserve document-level thematic guidance while maintaining local continuity and coherence between segments. Our comprehensive experiments across multiple summarization benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing methods under varying compression ratios, achieving superior performance in both semantic preservation and summary quality.

title: A 0.67 e-rms Temporal-Readout-Noise 80dB Intra-scene High Dynamic Range CMOS Image Sensor.
abstract: This work presents a CMOS image sensor that achieves ultra-low temporal dark noise while providing intra-scene high dynamic range (HDR) within a single exposure. Thanks to the in-pixel dual gain operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) combined with two-stage correlated double sampling (CDS), an input-referred noise of only 0.67 ${\text{e}}_{{\text{rms}}}^ - $ is achieved in high gain mode, while having an intra-scene dynamic range (DR) of 80dB in the same exposure cycle. The two identical readout chains for signal and reset level help to suppress the offset variation from the programmable-gain amplifier (PGA) and comparator, thereby reducing row noise.

title: A 10-Bit Successive Reference Approximation ADC Enabled By Switched-Capacitor Dynamic Reference Generation With Pipelined Pre-charging And Voltage Ripple Cancellation.
abstract: This paper introduces an ADC architecture that employs a cascaded switched-capacitor DC-DC chain for dynamic reference generation, realizing a successive reference approximation (SRA) technique. This approach tackles the critical challenges of exponential growth in total capacitance and power consumption encountered in traditional CDAC arrays-based ADC at higher resolutions. Furthermore, the paper proposes a pipelined pre-charging technique for fast settling and a voltage ripple cancellation scheme to enable a high sampling rate, which collectively enhance conversion speed and reduce the overall capacitor area of the proposed ADC. The prototype ADC is designed in a 0.18 µm CMOS process and occupies an active area of 0.043 mm2. At a 1.8 V supply and 5.12 MS/s sampling rate, post-layout simulation results show that the ADC achieves an SNDR of 48.9 dB and SFDR of 57.1 dB, and consumes 180 µW, resulting in a figure of merit (FoM) of 154.5 fJ/conversion-step.

title: A 90.8dB SNDR SAR ADC with a Mutual Calibration Scheme for Capacitor Array and a Dynamic-Biased Comparator.
abstract: This paper presents a synchronous, low-power Successive Approximation Register (SAR) Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) with a differential mutual calibration scheme and a low-power comparator including a two-stage dynamic biasing pre-amplifier. The proposed calibration scheme reuses the capacitor array itself and it provides a large error voltage correction range without additional hardware overhead. A dynamic biasing pre-amplifier is proposed to reduce the power consumption of the comparator while maintaining the noise and speed performance by adaptively adjusting the biasing current according to the signal amplitude. The proposed SAR ADC is designed in a 55-nm standard CMOS process with 2.5V supply and occupies an area of 0.255mm2. In post-layout simulation, it achieves a 92.9-dB Spurious-Free-Dynamic-Range (SFDR) and 90.8dB Signal-to-Noise-and-Distortion Ratio (SNDR) at 749kHz input while operating at 1.5MS/s. With a power consumption of 1.69mW, it achieves a Walden FoM (FoMw) of 39.5-fJ/conv.-step and a Schreier FoM (FoMs) of 177.3dB.

title: A Metastability-Based Reconfigurable TRNG Featuring Online Test and Auto-Calibration.
abstract: True Random Number Generators (TRNGs) are essential for secure cryptographic applications. This paper presents a TRNG that extracts entropy from the metastability (MS) of an SR latch and features built-in online testing and auto-calibration capabilities. Unlike conventional MS-based TRNGs, which typically quantize only the number of metastable oscillations, the proposed design simultaneously quantizes both the oscillation count and the precise collapse location of the metastable state. This dual quantization approach enables more efficient utilization of the entropy source, yielding enhanced randomness with minimal hardware overhead. Furthermore, the TRNG incorporates a configurable oscillation loop along with dedicated online test and auto-calibration circuits, enabling automatic reconfiguration of signal paths to minimize loop mismatch and maximize entropy generation. Implemented on a Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA, the core logic occupies only 11 LUTs and 7 flip-flops while achieving a throughput of 2.5 Mbps—outperforming state-of-the-art MS-based TRNGs. Experimental results demonstrate high-quality random bitstreams that pass all tests in the NIST SP 800-22, NIST SP 800-90B, and AIS-31 test suites, with a byte entropy of 7.9994 (bit entropy of 0.9999).

title: A 181.9-dB FoMSNDR Power/Bandwidth Scalable Fully Dynamic Discrete-Time Zoom ADC Using Gain Boost Floating Inverter Amplifiers.
abstract: This paper presents a fully dynamic discrete-time (DT) Zoom ADC using Gain Boost floating inverter amplifiers (GBFIAs) to achieve high precision and power efficiency. The proposed GBFIA enhances the gain of a single-stage cascoded FIA to nearly 80 dB, addressing the limitation of conventional FIA in high-precision DT delta-sigma modulators. A 2-bit flash ADC with multi-input comparators is utilized for quantization noise feed-forward to mitigate fuzz in Zoom ADC. Designed and simulated in 130-nm CMOS process, the proposed Zoom ADC achieves a peak SNDR of 100.3 dB and a FoMSNDRof 181.9 dB over a 20-kHz bandwidth with oversampling rate of 128, under a 1.2-V supply. Simulations indicate the proposed Zoom ADC is power/bandwidth scalable with bandwidth ranging from 2.5 kHz to 25 kHz.

title: An Edge-Pursuit Ising Machine with Programmable Local Fields and Adaptive Annealing.
abstract: Combinatorial optimization problems (COPs) play a critical role in real-world decision-making. Their NP-hard nature poses significant challenges for conventional architectures. Discrete-time (DT) Ising machines accelerate solutions but face limitations due to serial operations and annealing overheads. In contrast, continuous-time (CT) Ising machines enable broader solution space exploration through clock-free parallel iterations and analog spin states that fluctuate between -1 and +1. Prior CT designs, however, lack robust support for local magnetic fields and annealing, which limits their ability to solve complex problems. This work proposes a CT Ising machine based on even-stage ring oscillators (ESROs). It leverages an edge-pursuit mechanism to implement a 7-level programmable local field term, enabling applications such as image segmentation. Additionally, this work introduces spin-level adaptive annealing (SLAA). This approach dynamically adjusts coupling strength to transition from high-to low-temperature phases, enhancing solution quality. Simulations in 28nm at 0.4V on a 30×30 King’s graph array demonstrate high-quality solutions for max-cut and image segmentation tasks. The time-to-solution (TTS) ranges from 25-40ns, with solution quality comparable to software and energy consumption of 27-68fJ/spin.

title: A Fully-Differential Wideband Configurable Power Combiner and Splitter in 28-nm Bulk CMOS.
abstract: This paper presents a fully-differential wideband configurable power combiner and splitter. It decreases the insertion loss in conventional Wilkinson with only 1 port driven. Through even-odd mode analysis, the closed-form design equations are derived. Implemented in 28-nm bulk CMOS, this transformer-based wideband configurable Wilkinson power combiner and splitter is designed to cover 21-50 GHz operation band. The measured results demonstrate >10 dB input return loss and isolation, 0.8-1.2 dB insertion loss in combining mode, 1.9-3.1 dB insertion loss in switching mode.

title: A Low-phase-error FD-fNIRS Readout Circuit with Sub-1V Transimpedance Amplifier and LC-ADC-based Amplitude Control Loop.
abstract: Frequency-domain functional near-infrared spectroscopy (FD-fNIRS) ultilizes the propagation time and amplitude attenuation of light in tissue to quantify blood oxygen concentration. This enables more detailed monitoring of human brain activity, providing a potential solution for non-invasive and wearable brain-computer interface (BCI) devices. However, the amplitude-phase coupling effect of the comparator in the phase detector introduces phase errors, which in turn leads to inaccuracies in the measurement of light propagation time. To suppress amplitude-phase coupling effect, an amplitude control loop based on the level-crossing analog-to-digital converter (LC ADC) is employed. The utilization of the LC ADC eliminates the need for a high-speed envelope detector, thereby reducing circuit complexity and power consumption. In addition, a sub-1V transimpedance amplifier (TIA) is employed to improve energy efficiency. The proposed structure achieves a phase error of 0.11° and 12 mW power consumption.

title: A High-Efficiency Dual-Band Adaptive Power Receiver for Ultrasonic Wireless Power Transfer System Based on Dual-Frequency PMUTs.
abstract: Ultrasonic wireless power transfer (UWPT) has been demonstrated to be an important technique for wirelessly powering implantable medical devices (IMDs). Toward implantable applications, piezoelectric micromachined ultra-sonic transducers (PMUTs) have emerged as the preferred technology due to their compact size, easy integration, and multi-frequency properties. This paper presents a dual-band adaptive power receiver for a dual-frequency PMUT driven UWPT system, comprising a dual-band impedance matching network with self-tuning resonant frequency and a single-ended input half-wave rectifier with high power conversion efficiency (PCE). The dual-band impedance matching network is designed to meet the requirements of two operating frequencies for dual-frequency PMUTs. The single-ended rectifier utilizes a single-signal-triggered, multi-module cooperative startup mechanism, which significantly reduces circuit complexity, reduces power loss, and improves the startup speed of the rectifier. The proposed dual-band adaptive power receiver is designed in 0.18 m CMOS technology. The single-ended rectifier exhibits a maximum PCE of 91.8%@3MHz and 93%@9.4 MHz, while the overall receiver maintains a maximum PCE of 51.8% and 49.14% at the respective frequencies for a load of 1kΩ.

title: A Monolithic GaN Active Gate Driver Achieving 71.6% Ringing Reduction Across Various Load Currents Using A Ringing Sensor and Simplified Digital Algorithm.
abstract: The switching node ringing due to parasitic inductances and capacitances in power converters is a major source of electromagnetic interference (EMI) and reliability issues. This paper presents a closed-loop active gate driving scheme in a 400-V monolithic GaN buck converter, which consists of a 2-bit gate driver, a ringing sensor, and an adaptive controller, to reduce ringing without sacrificing power efficiency across various load currents. The 2-bit stop-and-go gate driver suppresses ringing using a pre-defined output current profile and an adaptive, fine-tuned timing determined by the adaptive controller. A ringing sensor monitors the ringing amplitude continuously. Based on the ringing sensor output, the controller uses a fast single variable algorithm to control the gate driver timing across various load currents. Implemented in a 650V monolithic GaN process, the buck converter with the proposed closed-loop adaptive gate driver achieves a ringing reduction of up to 71.6% with 1A to 5A varying load current, while consuming the same transition power loss compared to a benchmark fixed gate driver.

title: A 17-39GHz Transformer-Based Noise-Cancelling LNA with 2.7-4.3dB Noise Figure in 28nm CMOS.
abstract: This paper introduces a transformer-based dual-path noise-cancelling low-noise amplifier (LNA) operating across 17.4-to-39.5GHz in a 28nm CMOS process. Compared with classic noise-cancelling LNAs that rely on either a feedforward transformer only in the common gate (CG) amplifier or a feedback only in the common source (CS) amplifier, the proposed design employs both feedforward and feedback transformers to improve the design trade-off including noise figure and bandwidth. The LNA fabricated in a 28nm CMOS process occupies a core chip area of 0.21mm2. It achieves a 2.7-4.3dB NF within a 17.4-39.5GHz operation frequency range with 41mW power consumption at 1V power supply. The peak gain is 23dB and the S11remains below -6dB. The measured input-referred 1-dB compression point (IP1dB) and input-referred third-order intercept point (IIP3) are -14dBm and -3dBm at 32GHz, respectively.

title: Design and Analysis of Class-F23 LC-VCO with Wideband Common-Mode and Differential-Mode Impedance Control for Low Phase Noise in 65-nm CMOS.
abstract: This paper presents a 13.95-16.96 GHz low power, low phase noise (PN) LC voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) in 65 nm CMOS technology. To address the limitations of conventional harmonic tuned oscillators, whose phase noise (PN) degrades significantly across the tuning range (TR) due to narrowband harmonic impedances, a custom transformer is designed and analyzed. The proposed tank can actively contribute to ISF shaping and achieve consistent flicker noise upconversion reduction across the entire tuning range. Post-layout simulations demonstrate a phase noise (PN) of -118 dBc/Hz and a figure of merit (FoM) exceeding 187 dBc/Hz at a 1 MHz offset. The VCO occupies only 0.0306 mm2, and its PN performance makes it suitable for mm-Wave applications and next-generation wireless systems.

title: A 2-18GHz Tunable Bandpass Filter with Dual-Path Transformer Technique for Ultra-wideband Applications.
abstract: This work presents a reconfigurable bandpass filter for ultra-wideband (UWB) RF front-ends, covering the S, C, X and Ku frequency bands. The filter adopts the dual transformer wideband matching technology and can cover multiple frequency bands. The passband reconfiguration is achieved through the switched capacitor array. The insertion loss is smaller than 5 dB and the typical value is about 4 dB. The S11 is less than −10 dB. It can cover multiple frequency bands within the range of 2–18 GHz and the maximum instant 3 dB bandwidth is 11 GHz from 10 GHz to 21 GHz. For UWB applications, it can provide up to 17 dB of second-order harmonic rejection and more than 18 dB of third-order harmonic rejection.

title: A Series-Resonance VCO with Magnetic Mutual Impedance Achieving 191.9dBc/Hz FoM.
abstract: This paper presents a series-resonance (SR) voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) that leverages magnetic mutual impedance (MMI) to mitigate the critical limitation of pseudo-SR oscillators. Conventional designs based on magnetic mutual resistance (MMR) often suffer from inherent resonant frequency misalignment between the SR and parallel-resonant (PR) tanks. Such frequency misalignment degrades phase noise (PN), particularly flicker noise. This work proposes a fundamental solution by introducing an MMI-based auxiliary (AUX) tank with strong magnetic coupling, which enables synchronous frequency tuning of both tanks through a unified tuning bank. This architecture structurally mitigates the frequency misalignment and suppresses flicker noise more effectively than traditional pseudo-SR oscillators. Post-layout simulation in an SMIC 40-nm CMOS process demonstrates a phase noise of -126.4 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset and -146.5 dBc/Hz at 10 MHz offset from an 8.80-GHz carrier, with a flicker phase noise corner of 14.2 kHz. Occupying a core area of 0.123 mm2, this design achieves a peak FoM of 191.9 dBc/Hz, demonstrating the proposed MMI-based topology as a robust and competitive solution for low phase noise CMOS oscillators.

title: A 1.6-3.8 GHz Reconfigurable Transmitter with 81.5% Relative-Bandwidth PLL For FMCW Through-wall Radar Applications.
abstract: This paper presents a 1.6–3.8 GHz reconfigurable transmitter with an 81.5%-relative-bandwidth PLL and wideband PA for multi-platform (UAVs or handhelds) FMCW through-wall radar, implemented in 40 nm CMOS. The transmitter employs a power-divider-free, low-frequency-error PLL with an 8-phase ring VCO to deliver wideband chirps to both TX and RX paths, and a reconfigurable PA that uses three parallel differential cascode units and an on-chip high-coupling transformer (k=0.85) for on-chip power combining and 50 Ω impedance transformation, enabling direct antenna drive without external broadband matching. Each PA unit supports independent enable and programmable biasing from class A to class AB, allowing a system level trade off among output power, linearity, and efficiency. The PA achieves 20.1% PAE and 20.9 dBm Psat. Measured FMCW chirps maintain near 3 dB amplitude flatness across the band, with selectable TX output levels of 13.43 dBm, 10.1 dBm, and 5 dBm, and an output match of |S11| < −7 dB (−20.49 dB at 2.34 GHz). The PLL delivers multi path outputs from 1.6 to 3.8 GHz and achieves 29.6 kHz RMS frequency error, indicating a desirable trade off among bandwidth, accuracy, and area.

title: Virtual inertia and damping control strategy for AHO virtual oscillator based on RBF.
abstract: Andronov-Hopf Oscillator (AHO) control is an instantaneous current feedback method with advantages like good self-synchronization, precise power sharing, and low harmonic distortion, but it lacks adaptability under varied operating conditions and disturbances. This paper proposes an optimal control algorithm—based on an online-updating Radial Basis Function (RBF) neural network—to optimize the parameters of an improved resonant controller. With reasonable initial parameter design, the improved AHO control provides the system with optimal equivalent inertia and damping under current operating conditions. Experimental results show that, compared with the AHO controller with virtual inertia and the adaptive-adjustment virtual synchronous generator controller, the RBF-based AHO virtual inertia and damping control significantly reduces frequency overshoot and adjustment time, and effectively mitigates power systems’ frequency change rate under different operating conditions.

title: Robust Safe Tracking Control for UAVs with High-Relative-Degree Constraints via Disturbance-Observer-Based Nonlinear CBFs.
abstract: This paper addresses the safe trajectory tracking problem of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) subject to high-relative-degree safety constraints and wind disturbances. A high-order disturbance observer is developed to estimate external perturbations in real time, and the estimates, together with their error bounds, are incorporated into nonlinear control barrier functions (NCBFs) to formulate robust NCBF constraints. Following the minimally invasive approach, a robust quadratic programming (QP)–based optimal controller is designed to ensure that the UAV states remain within the safety set. The proposed method is rigorously analyzed and validated through numerical simulations.

title: Lightweight Quadrupolar Trapezoidal Coil Design with CNN-Accelerated Optimization for Misalignment-Tolerant IPT Converter.
abstract: Inductive Power Transfer (IPT) has become a pivotal technology for various applications. While diverse enhancement strategies have been explored, the magnetically coupled coil remains the ultimate determinant of system performance. Horizontal coil misalignment is particularly critical, causing coupling variations that destabilize output and degrade efficiency. Current solutions are either bulky compensation networks or complex multilayered coil geometries with limited scalability. This paper proposes a lightweight, misalignment-tolerance coil structure that merges quadrupolar trapezoidal transmit coils with a unipolar square receive coil, inherently flattening mutual-inductance variation across ±50% horizontal misalignment. To overcome time-consuming finite element analysis, we also develop a convolutional neural network (CNN) regression-prediction framework trained on multi-physics datasets, reducing design time by two orders of magnitude while preserving scalability and reusability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed CNN-based framework’s exceptional accuracy across all statistical metrics (R2, RMSE, MAE, MBE). Furthermore, the optimized prototype exhibits only 2.65 % mutual-inductance fluctuation within the targeted misalignment range.

title: A Bitwidth-Flexible Modular Multiplier with Shift-Free Accumulation for Efficient NTT Acceleration in FHE.
abstract: The Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) dominates computation time in Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE), often consuming up to 90% of execution in schemes like CKKS. Consequently, NTT performance critically determines FHE accelerator efficiency. As NTT accelerators rely on modular multipliers, their cost and performance are bottlenecked by two key issues: 1) Overflow Handling requiring large bit-widths, increasing area/cost, and 2) Serial Shifting limits the parallelization and performance of modular multipliers. This paper presents a novel hardware-software co-designed NTT accelerator addressing these limitations. First, we transform the modular multiplication algorithm to decouple shift operations, converting shift-dependent steps into precomputable constants, eliminating the serial shift bottleneck. Second, leveraging these constants, we decompose modular reduction into a set of parallelizable sub-computations. Crucially, each unit operates without reserving bits for overflow, significantly reducing latency via parallelization while simultaneously eliminating overflow-handling circuit overhead. We implement an accelerator incorporating these techniques. Experimental results demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed scheme in NTT computational performance improvement.

title: Node-Edge-Variant Distributed Graph Filter Design with Edge Sparsity.
abstract: Distributed graph filters are fundamental tools for processing signals defined on graph-structured data. To enhance their approximation accuracy for target operators under a limited number of signal exchanges, we propose a node-edge-variant graph filter that jointly incorporates node-level and edge-level parameters. Specifically, each node assigns a weight to both its connected edges and its signal aggregation process. Moreover, edge-level sparsity is explicitly considered during signal diffusion, and an efficient distributed implementation scheme is developed. The filter design problem is addressed via an alternating optimization framework, where node-level and edge-level parameters are updated separately; the latter is solved using a proximal gradient algorithm. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently achieves superior approximation accuracy in approximating both the distributed consensus operator and the exponential graph filter.

title: Mutual Information Loss for Enhancing Class-Wise Representation in Spiking Neural Networks.
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) demonstrate significant potential for energy efficiency attributable to their event-driven paradigm and sparse information representation. However, the inherent mechanism of spike generation in SNNs can be regarded as a form of lossy compression. This characteristic, compounded by the temporal refractory period, results in low information efficiency of spike trains, which in turn limits the network’s representational capacity and accuracy. To enhance information transmission efficiency, we propose a novel Mutual Information (MI) loss function inspired by information-theoretic principles. It constrains the intermediate representations of SNNs via a marginal entropy term, which promotes diverse global priors, and a conditional entropy term, which enforces intra-class stability. An effective training strategy is employed to facilitate the optimization of the MI loss, incorporating an exponent coefficient to stabilize gradients and an adaptive weighting mechanism to balance the marginal and conditional objectives. Experiments on the CIFAR-10 dataset show that our method achieves an accuracy of 95.93% with 4 time steps. Class-wise feature visualization further confirms its strong discriminative and representational capabilities.

title: A Low-Power Fractional Output Divider With Adaptive Power Control Algorithm In 28-nm CMOS.
abstract: This work presents a fractional output divider (FOD) employing an adaptive power control (APC) algorithm. Conventional calibration algorithm ignores the numerous redundant toggling during calibration, while not affecting the calibration, it increases dynamic power consumption. To address this issue, the proposed APC algorithm adaptively controls the internal blocks to eliminate the redundant toggling, thereby reducing power consumption. In addition, a dual path step scaling refinement (DPSSR) scheme is proposed to improve the spur performance at low power. Implemented in a 28-nm CMOS process, the proposed FOD covers an output range of 1.35-400 MHz. At an output frequency of 84.21 MHz, the FOD achieves −62.5 dBc spur, while consuming only 843µW from a 0.9-V supply, and the core area is 0.011 mm2.

title: Energy-Efficient All-Digital Computation-in-Memory Macro Design with CFeFET-based Booth Decoder.
abstract: The growing demand for deep neural network (DNN) accelerators has exposed the limitations of the von Neumann architecture, where the separation of memory and computation leads to excessive data movement and bandwidth constraints. Computing-in-memory (CIM) mitigates these issues by performing operations directly within memory, thereby improving energy efficiency. Compared with analog CIM, digital CIM provides superior scalability and robustness against PVT variations, yet it still suffers from large adder-tree overhead and long input interconnects. This work presents an energy-efficient all-digital CIM macro that employs the Booth algorithm to reduce partial products and alleviate adder-tree complexity. Furthermore, a complementary ferroelectric FET (CFeFET)-based Booth decoder is proposed to address the overhead introduced by Booth algorithm. To further enhance performance, a folded architecture is designed to shorten interconnect length, and voltage scaling is applied to balance speed and energy efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with prior works, the proposed CIM macro achieves up to 5.5× higher throughput and 10.1× better energy efficiency, highlighting its potential for energy-efficient all-digital CIM accelerators.

title: Low-Loss CNN Acceleration Scheme Based on Optical Network-on-Chip (ONoC).
abstract: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is widely used in image recognition, data processing, and video classification. Optical Network-on-Chip (ONoC) offers low latency, high bandwidth, and energy efficiency through Wavelength-Division Multiplexing (WDM), making it a promising platform for CNN acceleration. However, optical signal attenuation caused by multiple on-state Microring Resonators (MRs) leads to insertion loss, degrading communication quality and limiting scalability. To address this, this paper proposes two optimization methods: a communication-aware clustering algorithm that minimizes inter-group communication, and a Predictive Turn-Minimized Communication Mapping (PTMCM) algorithm that reduces path turns and on-state MRs to lower insertion loss. Additionally, an optimized multicast routing and wavelength allocation strategy is introduced. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed methods significantly reduce insertion loss and energy consumption, achieving an average insertion loss reduction of 18.4% at different network sizes, significantly improving energy efficiency.

title: Coupling and Clustering of Grid-Forming and Grid-Following Converters in Islanded Microgrids.
abstract: In an islanded microgrid containing a number of grid-forming and grid-following converters (GFMCs and GFLCs), the GFMCs splits into at least two internally synchronized clusters under a sufficiently large transient disturbance, and the GFLCs interact with these clusters to manifest diversified behaviors, e.g., being absorbed into one of the aforementioned clusters, or temporarily joining one of the clusters, or forming a new cluster alone. Such behaviors are dependent on the GFLCs’ injected reactive power, network structure and edge weights. These factors can be adjusted to absorb more GFLCs into the dominant cluster of the microgrid. These findings are verified by a modified IEEE 39-bus power grid.

title: A Scalable Cyclically Coupled Multi-phase Hybrid DC-DC Converter with Duty-Cycle Calibration for 48V Data-Center Power Delivery.
abstract: A scalable cyclically coupled hybrid (SCCH) DCDC converter is proposed for direct 48V-to-1V power delivery in data-center applications. The SCCH converter supports flexible multi-phase scalability, inherent current-sharing capability, and a sextuple reduction of inductor switching-node voltage stress, thereby achieving high-current operation and efficient power conversion. To further enhance current-sharing accuracy, a duty-cycle calibration circuit is introduced. Simulation results show that the proposed SCCH converter achieves a current-sharing mismatch within 0.9%, a peak efficiency of 91.2% under direct 48V-to-1V conversion, and a maximum output current of 30A with six phases, demonstrating its potential for 48V data-center power delivery.

title: A Hybrid RRAM-FeRAM Computing-in-Memory Architecture with Adaptive Quantization Scheme for Edge AI Devices.
abstract: Compute-in-Memory (CIM) is critical for edge AI acceleration, but single non-volatile memory (NVM)-based designs suffer from inherent trade-offs. RRAM lacks endurance and has long write latency, while FeRAM faces destructive readout. Additionally, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) weight sparsity causes redundant computations in conventional CIM. To address these, this paper proposes a hybrid RRAM-FeRAM CIM architecture with adaptive quantization scheme. Key innovations: 1) Split signed INT8 storage—2T1R RRAM for stable upper 4-bit weights, 2T1C FeRAM for fast-updating lower 4-bit weights; 2) Adaptive quantization module that switches the Flash ADC between 2/4-bit based on sparsity. The hybrid 8kb RRAM-FeRAM CIM macro shows: 32.42 TOPS/W (50% sparsity) and 74.65 TOPS/W (80% sparsity) at 25°C (TT corner), peak 87.28 TOPS/W at -40°C (SS corner). It outperforms state-of-the-art CIM macros by 3.3×–34.2× (50% sparsity) and 7.4×–76.7× (80% sparsity) in normalized energy efficiency.

title: Performance-Aware Design Space Exploration for Chiplet-Based Cortical Simulation Processors Considering Area Constraint.
abstract: Cortical simulation is limited by memory capacity and I/O bandwidth due to massive neuron counts, large fan-out, and sparse irregular connectivity. To address these constraints under a fixed total area budget, we adopt a chiplet-based solution in which a compute die is co-packaged with multiple HBM stacks on an interposer to form a tile, and many tiles are interconnected on wafer. A central question is the tile size: larger tiles concentrate more compute and SRAM but, for a fixed total area, reduce the total number of I/O lanes in the system and thus lower aggregate off-chip memory and inter-chip bandwidth; smaller tiles improve modularity and yield and increase total I/O, but raise inter-chip traffic and hop count. Motivated by this trade-off, we present a performance-aware architecture and physical co-optimization framework that explores the key design parameters. We model cortical simulation performance as the pipeline maximum of three stages: neural dynamics computing, spike routing, and synaptic information access. The framework evaluates a compact set of configurations that vary tile count, HBM stacks per tile, and the I/O split, and applies a temporal equalization principle that balances routing and synaptic access latencies. For a cortical model with 800,000 neurons, the method identifies an optimal configuration under the given constraints, achieving a 2.42× performance improvement over the average of all feasible configurations.

title: DyNeuro: A Hybrid Neuromorphic Accelerator with Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Variation Adaptations.
abstract: Neuromorphic computing hardware has emerged as a promising candidate for energy-efficient edge AI devices. By concurrently processing spatio-temporal data, these accelerators exhibit strong potential in hybrid model architectures. However, frequent variations in data fed into hardware induce significant dynamic power consumption, severely limiting the practicality of such hardware. Although exploiting the sparse nature of data enhances computational efficiency, unstructured sparsity in both activations and weights poses additional challenges, resulting in substantial inefficiencies in computation. To overcome these issues, we propose DyNeuro, a hybrid neuromorphic accelerator for both spiking neural network and artificial neural network paradigms. DyNeuro incorporates a Dynamic Valid Product Aggregator with sign-magnitude encoding to eliminate redundant multiplications and accumulations based on output sparsity, and also dynamically centralizes spatial data. In addition, a Sparsity Aware Processing Unit is designed to minimize the size of activated circuits, achieving up to 46% power savings. The General Attention-based Dynamic Manager further adapts to temporal data variations by more than 50% timestep pruning. Implemented using 28-nm technology, DyNeuro achieves a peak energy efficiency of 60.2 TOPS/W and 41.2 TSOPS/W with 8-bit weights. The inference accuracy on DVS-Gesture is 94.44%.

title: Energy Efficient Vector Gather Based on Data Serialization and Pulse Selection.
abstract: To address the issue of hardware overhead sharply increasing with vector bit width in traditional implementations of vector gather instructions, this paper proposes a hardware architecture based on time-domain computation. This architecture achieves a transition from the digital domain to the time domain through the coordinated operation of five modules: index vector extraction, delay chain, pulse selection, data serialization, and vector sampling. It serializes the transmission of source vectors via pulse timing encoding and performs synchronous sampling using index-driven pulses to complete vector gather. Test results from logic synthesis and circuit simulation on a 28nm process node demonstrate that compared to the baseline circuit, this architecture lowers power consumption by 71.3% and saves 33.1% in area. Furthermore, as vector width increases, both power consumption and area growth of this architecture remain lower than the baseline design, showcasing excellent application potential for scenarios requiring higher bit widths or constrained hardware resources.

title: WaveMamba: A Vision Backbone Synergizing Feature Extraction and Downsampling.
abstract: The paradigm of applying State Space Models (SSMs) to vision faces a dual challenge: the inefficient spatial modeling due to 1D sequence flattening and the irreversible loss of high-frequency details from downsampling. We propose WaveMamba, a novel vision backbone that resolves both challenges through a unified, frequency-centric design. WaveMamba leverages the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) as a holistic operator that simultaneously performs lossless downsampling and frequency decoupling. It decomposes feature maps into a low-frequency sub-band, capturing the core structure, and three high-frequency sub-bands containing fine details. This enables a divide and conquer strategy: a powerful Visual State-Space (VSS) block models global context on the purified low-frequency signal, while lightweight convolutions handle local patterns in the high-frequency sub-bands. On ImageNet-1K, WaveMamba-B achieves a state-of-the-art 85.4% top-1 accuracy, with its performance gains extending to object detection and semantic segmentation, where it also achieves a new state-of-the-art performance.

title: AlignLite: A Lightweight Framework for Weakly Aligned Multimodal Object Detection.
abstract: Multimodal object detection fusing visible (RGB) and infrared (IR) data enhances perception robustness against challenging conditions. However, it is hindered by weak registration, a common issue in real-world applications. Existing methods designed to handle this misalignment are computationally prohibitive for edge deployment. This paper introduces AlignLite, a framework that resolves this challenge by achieving high efficiency and offset robustness simultaneously. AlignLite is built upon an efficient shared backbone with lightweight modal extractors (MEs) for parameter economy. Its core innovation is the Semantic-Guided Fusion Pyramid (SGFP), an asymmetric strategy that bypasses naive, noise-sensitive fusion at shallow levels. This aligned P5 feature then serves as a guidance signal, propagating robustness top-down through the FPN/PAN pathway to correct shallow levels (P4, P3) with minimal overhead. Extensive experiments on the challenging DroneVehicle benchmark, known for significant weak registration, demonstrate that AlignLite achieves new state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance, reaching 86.6% mAP@50.

title: A 56Gb/s PAM-4 Transmitter with Robust DCC and Unsegmented Voltage-Mode Driver Achieving Wide-Coefficient-Tuning-Range FFE in 65nm CMOS.
abstract: For wireline transmitters (TXs), the traditional unsegmented voltage-mode driver exhibits degraded output linearity when supporting a wide tuning range of feed-forward equalizer (FFE) tap coefficients. In this paper, a switchable unsegmented voltage-mode driver slice is proposed, which adjusts the slice connection according to the required FFE tap coefficient to achieve better impedance matching. The proposed TX achieves a RLM above 98% over channels loss variation up to 10-dB loss at the Nyquist frequency. In addition, a delay-line-based duty-cycle correction (DCC) circuit is introduced to improve correction accuracy under supply voltage and temperature variations, offering up to 5× and 10× enhancements across ±12% supply and -40℃ to 125℃ temperature ranges. The proposed TX is designed in a 65-nm CMOS process, achieving an energy efficiency per channel loss at Nyquist frequency of 0.34-pJ/bit/dB with 56-Gb/s PAM4.

title: XHDC: An Adaptive Hyperdimensional Computing Accelerator with Incremental Learning.
abstract: Existing hyperdimensional computing (HDC) accelerators suffer from two main limitations: uniform retraining strategies that slow convergence and static memory allocation that prevents post-deployment learning. To overcome these challenges, we propose XHDC, an FPGA-based HDC accelerator supporting incremental learning. A confidence-aware retraining mechanism dynamically scales update intensity according to the classification margin, reducing convergence time by up to 40% and improving accuracy by up to 1.3%.A pre-allocated BRAM pool decouples physical memory from logical class binding, allowing runtime category expansion without reconfiguration while preserving over 90% of prior knowledge. XHDC thus demonstrates efficient lifelong learning for edge intelligence with negligible hardware overhead.

title: CIM-SIFT: An Efficient Compute-in-Memory Accelerator for Real-time SIFT Algorithm.
abstract: Feature extraction is fundamental for computer vision tasks and Scale-Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT) is renowned for its robust feature extraction and description capabilities under significant scale and rotational transformations. However, SIFT’s high computational workload poses challenges for deployment in embedded real-time applications. To overcome these limitations, we propose CIM-SIFT, a SRAM-based Compute-in-Memory (CIM) accelerator for efficient SIFT-based keypoint generation. Algorithmically, we replace the multi-layer Gaussian Pyramid (GP) with 2-layer sparse GP and implement direct Difference of Gaussian (DoG) through the use of pre-subtracted Gaussian kernels. In the hardware aspect, we introduce an image-stationary CIM tailored to SIFT’s dataflow, a novel row-based refreshing scheme with sparse kernel design to minimize data movement. For a video graphics array (VGA)-format (640 × 480) image, the proposed algorithm-hardware co-optimizations evaluated at 22nm demonstrate that CIM-SIFT achieves 28.54 TOPS/W energy efficiency with 2201.16 FPS without keypoint matching accuracy degradation (vs. original SIFT) tested on affine covariant feature dataset.

title: RASR: Retrieval-Augmented Super Resolution for Practical Reference-based Image Restoration.
abstract: Reference-based Super Resolution (RefSR) improves upon Single Image Super Resolution (SISR) by leveraging high-quality reference images to enhance texture fidelity and visual realism. However, a critical limitation of existing RefSR approaches is their reliance on manually curated target-reference image pairs, which severely constrains their practicality in real-world scenarios. To overcome this, we introduce Retrieval-Augmented Super Resolution (RASR), a new and practical RefSR paradigm that automatically retrieves semantically relevant high-resolution images from a reference database given only a low-quality input. This enables scalable and flexible RefSR in realistic use cases, such as enhancing mobile photos taken in environments like zoos or museums, where category-specific reference data (e.g., animals, artworks) can be readily collected or pre-curated. To facilitate research in this direction, we construct RASR-Flickr30, the first benchmark dataset designed for RASR. Unlike prior datasets with fixed target-reference pairs, RASR-Flickr30 provides per-category reference databases to support open-world retrieval. We further propose RASRNet, a strong baseline that combines a semantic reference retriever with a diffusion-based RefSR generator. It retrieves relevant references based on semantic similarity and employs a diffusion-based generator enhanced with semantic conditioning. Experiments on RASR-Flickr30 demonstrate that RASRNet consistently improves over SISR baselines, achieving +0.38 dB PSNR and -0.0131 LPIPS, while generating more realistic textures. These findings highlight retrieval augmentation as a promising direction to bridge the gap between academic RefSR research and real-world applicability.

title: A Low-power High-impedance Instrumentation Amplifier with Capacitor-calibration for Bio-sensors.
abstract: The analog front-end (AFE) in biomedical sensors requires high input impedance to suppress interference during bio-potential acquisition. This paper presents a low-power chopping-stabilized AFE with ultra-high input impe-dance. A self-adjusting variable-capacitor in the positive feed-back loop (PFL) dynamically compensates parasitic capacitan-ce, while an oscillation detection loop guides the system from instability to stability, maximizing impedance without over-compensation. A frequency ripple suppression method further mitigates input frequency fluctuations, providing accurate control signals for the variable capacitor. This capacitor decouples control and input signals, ensuring high linearity and wide tuning range. The technique achieves femtofarad-level resolution, overcoming limitations of traditional capaci-tive arrays in PFL. Fabricated in 0.18 µm CMOS, the AFE attains 46.3 GΩ input impedance at 50 Hz—83× higher than conventional designs—occupying 0.71 mm2with 40 dB mid-band gain and only 68 fF input capacitance. It also achieves low noise (0.93 μVrms) and low power consumption (3.48 μW), extending acquisition system operation. Using dry electrodes, the prototype successfully acquired high-quality EEG and ECG signals, validating its applicability to biomedical devices.

title: Design Technology Co-Optimization for Digital Compute-in-memory with Area-efficient CFET 10T3P SRAM.
abstract: A high-throughput 10T3P SRAM using a complementary FET (CFET) design, with one more pFET read port (pRP) than the 8T2P SRAM for bit-parallel operations, can increase throughput and computing efficiency at the cost of only 1.1× cell footprint. The Digital Compute-in-memory (DCIM) macro and performance modeling, including the novel design of the adder tree for the CFET 10T3P SRAM, are comprehensively studied. Multi-VTand dual rail technologies can significantly reduce SRAM read latency and short-circuit energy. Compared to the CFET 8T2P SRAM, the novel CFET 10T3P SRAM achieves 2.50X TOPS/W and 2.32X TOPS/mm2in DCIM applications.

title: Fast Response Proximity and Tactile Sensory for Safe Human-Robot Collaboration.
abstract: This paper presents a novel capacitive proximity and tactile sensory system for robotic skin aimed at enhancing safety in human-robot collaboration. The proposed flexible capacitive sensor is fabricated using copper electrodes and hydrogel, encapsulated by silicone rubber. To enable fast and accurate readout the proposed dual-mode flexible capacitive sensor, a hardware-efficient impedance demodulation method implemented on an FPGA, is introduced. This method achieves more than 99% accuracy over a measurement bandwidth of 1 kHz to 500 kHz. It supports a demodulation speed of 25 mega samples per second (MSPS) without latency. Compared with the sliding DFT, it achieves a faster response time of 0.94 ms at an excitation frequency of 10 kHz. The system has been experimentally validated in detecting both the approach and contact of a human hand.

title: A 30MHz-BW Continuous-time Delta Sigma Modulator with Reference Rotation and Time Constant Calibration in 65nm CMOS.
abstract: This paper proposes a continuous-time delta sigma modulator (CT-DSM) for factory-level wireless receiver application. To achieve advanced performance such as high SNDR and low power consumption, three techniques are adopted to address the key challenges for CT-DSM design. First, an excess loop delay (ELD) compensation method is adopted to simplify circuit implementation. Second, a Flash ADC with embedded voltage reference rotation is used to suppress the DAC element mismatch. A rotation pattern is adopted to reduce the reference settling time. Third, a time constant calibration technique is adopted for loop filter to keep the time constant invariant. Based on those techniques, a CT-DSM is designed and fabricated in 65nm CMOS process, whose core area is 0.31mm2and power consumption is 39.6mW. The measurement results prove the effectiveness of the adopted techniques.

title: A Phase Delay Comparison-Based TRNG Controlled by TDC.
abstract: True Random Number Generator (TRNG) is a critical security component that generates un-predictable random numbers based on physical entropy sources, widely used in cryptography, secure communications, and simulation. This paper proposes a TRNG based on phase delay comparison, where the phase is converted into a control signal via Time-to-Digital Converter (TDC) to implement random delay for the oscillation source. Implemented on an Artix-7 FPGA, it achieves a high 655 Mbps throughput with superior resource efficiency, enhancing security via multi-phase sampling and TDC technology.

title: An Agent Framework for Fault Recovery Planning Generation Based on Model Context Protocol.
abstract: As the complexity of power grid operations increases significantly, the requirements for efficiency and precision in decision making pertaining to distribution network fault recovery planning have become more stringent. Existing intelligent agents for fault recovery planning generation are capable of performing topology queries and power flow calculations through tool learning, yet they are hindered by nonuniform data interaction interfaces. This issue affects seamless data sharing and collaborative operation between different functional modules. Furthermore, tedious tool development and low transferability further constrain their practical application. This paper presents an interactive agent framework based on universal plug-in protocols for the generation of distribution network fault recovery plans. Functions such as topology queries and power flow calculations are integrated into this framework via a novel protocol. In the experiments, state-of-the-art mainstream large language models such as Qwen3, Gemma3, and Llama3.1 were adopted as the base large models. Interactive agents were constructed based on the proposed framework and the effectiveness of the agents was verified in scenarios including transformer query, bus query, feeder query, and power flow calculation.

title: Live Demonstration: Capacitive Proximity Imaging Array for Human-Robot Interaction and Safety.
abstract: This work presents a novel capacitive proximity sensory system for human-robot interaction and safety. The system consists of a 16×16 capacitive proximity sensor array, an analogue readout with field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-based impedance demodulation, an imaging interface and a neural network running on a laptop. The proposed demodulation method calculates impedance in real time at the analogue-to-digital converter (ADC) sampling rate of 25 mega samples per second (MSPS), producing one result per sample without requiring integer-cycle sampling. Using the reconstructed proximity images, the system recognises hand gestures above the array and distinguishes material types by sweeping the excitation frequency (physics based). The system supports proximity detection for safety and proximity imaging for interaction.

title: High Throughput LDPC Decoder with Ultra-low BER Using Hardware Sharing across Two Code Rates for IEEE Std. 802.15.3d.
abstract: This paper presents a high-throughput multi-rate LDPC decoder architecture with a simplified soft demapper, designed in compliance with the IEEE Std. 802.15.3d standard. By incorporating a re-permutation technique with hardware sharing, multi-frame interleaving, and a low-latency sorting architecture, an efficient implementation is achieved. Using the normalized min-sum algorithm, the decoder attains a BER of 10–12at SNRs of 22.4 dB for rate-14/15 and 18.6 dB for rate-thereby satisfying the specification requirements. Implemented in a 16 nm FinFET process provided by TSMC, the proposed design achieves a throughput of 128.6 Gb/s.

title: AURA: A Reconfigurable Asynchronous Spiking Processor for Low-Power Sensory Systems.
abstract: Processing weak analog signals from biomedical, environmental, and IoT sensors in a low-power event-driven manner is a major challenge, as conventional synchronous digitization wastes energy and fails to capture the fine temporal dynamics of slow and sparse natural signals. Neuromorphic computing has emerged as a promising paradigm for edge sensing; however, most state-of-the-art neuromorphic chips lack dedicated analog-to-spike interfaces, omit crucial signal conditioning such as gain control, and offer only limited flexibility, restricting their use in real-world sensing tasks. To overcome these limitations, we present AURA, a reconfigurable mixed-signal asynchronous spiking neural network (SNN) system for ultra-low-power sensing and computing. AURA integrates analog soma and synapse with on-chip analog front-end that directly encode sensory signals into spikes, reducing conversion overhead and enhancing temporal fidelity. The processor supports inter(intra)-chip communication based on four-phase handshake protocol and Address-Event Representation (AER). Online learning is enabled via reconfigurable connectivity and synaptic weight through external PC. Designed in IHP 130nm CMOS process, AURA achieves ~0.4pJ per spike (operated within 500 Hz (incl. integ.)) in simulations.

title: A 16 nm 1.60TOPS/W High Utilization DNN Accelerator with 3D Spatial Data Reuse and Efficient Shared Memory Access.
abstract: Achieving high compute utilization across a wide range of AI workloads is crucial for the efficiency of versatile DNN accelerators. This paper presents the Voltra chip and its utilization-optimised DNN accelerator architecture, which leverages 3-Dimensional (3D) spatial data reuse along with efficient and flexible shared memory access. The 3D spatial dataflow enables balanced spatial data reuse across three dimensions, improving spatial utilization by up to 2.0× compared to a conventional 2D design. Inside the shared memory access architecture, Voltra incorporates flexible data streamers that enable mixed-grained hardware data prefetching and dynamic memory allocation, further improving the temporal utilization by 2.12-2.94× and achieving 1.15-2.36× total latency speedup compared with the non-prefetching and separated memory architecture, respectively. Fabricated in 16nm technology, our chip achieves 1.60 TOPS/W peak system energy efficiency and 1.25 TOPS/mm2system area efficiency, which is competitive with state-of-the-art solutions while achieving high utilization across diverse workloads.
