title: HalF&D: A Parameter Efficient Small Object Detection Approach.
abstract: Small-object detection is a challenging problem especially in aerial imagery due to large variations in object scale, high density, and limited spatial resolution. The Focus-and-Detect (F&D) framework addresses this problem by dividing the process into two stages: a Focus stage that predicts object-dense regions, and a Detect stage that performs fine-grained detection within these focal crops. In this study, we present HalF&D, a parameter-efficient variant of the F&D framework that integrates the HaLViT (Half of the Weights are Enough) mechanism into both stages. With HalF&D, by applying parameter sharing to the challenging task of small-object detection, we achieved this task with a parameter-efficient model and examined the method’s functionality. HaLViT reduces parameters by sharing a single projection matrix and its transpose across bottleneck blocks within each residual stage. Applied to ResNet–50 in the Focus stage and ResNeXt–101–32×8d in the Detect stage, HalF&D achieves significant compression while maintaining usable accuracy on the VisDrone dataset. Specifically, the Focus network achieves 47.9% mAP@50 with a 47% parameter reduction, and the Detect network reaches 32.2% mAP with more than 70% fewer parameters. These results demonstrate that parameter sharing can substantially reduce model size while preserving the spatial precision and recognition ability in HalF&D.

title: A low-channel-crosstalk orthogonal time-division multiplexing AFE for bio-signal acquisition.
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-channel orthogonal time-division multiplexing (OTDM) analog front-end (AFE) for bio-signal acquisition with extremely low inter-channel crosstalk. Based on the TDM scheme, each channel employs orthogonal Walsh-Hadamard codes to modulate and demodulate the bio-signals, effectively suppressing inter-channel signal crosstalk. In addition, an externally biased complementary pseudo-resistor (CPR) is employed to stabilize the resistance of the PR and suppress the substrate leakage current. The proposed OTDM AFE is implemented in a standard 65 nm CMOS process, with a core area of 0.91 mm × 0.46 mm. The average power consumption per channel is 2.1 μW at a 1.2 V supply voltage. The average inter-channel crosstalk in the OTDM AFE is only 86.67 dB. The 3σ/μ of the proposed CPR is as low as 14.3%.

title: Accurate Localization of RF Signals Based on Adaptive Normalized SR System and Phase Estimation.
abstract: To enhance Radio Frequency (RF) phase detection accuracy in low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) environments, this paper proposes an Adaptive Normalized Stochastic Resonance (ANSR) system. By establishing a frequency scale mapping between high-frequency carriers and a bistable system, the proposed method utilizes an adaptive optimization model based on correlation coefficients and SNR gain to achieve parameter self-matching. Combined with quadrature demodulation and phase compensation, this approach enables high-precision phase estimation and ranging. Experimental results demonstrate that ANSR achieves positioning errors within 10 mm at SNRs as low as -18 dB, significantly outperforming traditional Matched Filter (MF) methods, which require an SNR of -2 dB. Notably, in the -20 dB to -10 dB range, ANSR reduces the average and RMS errors by 87.61% and 89.88%, respectively, compared to MF. This method provides a robust solution for precise ranging under severe noise interference.

title: A Low-Power Resonate-and-Fire Neuron with Adaptive Refractory Control for RRAM-Based Neuromorphic Computing.
abstract: Traditional Spiking Neural Network (SNN) models, such as the Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neuron, lack intrinsic resonance behaviors required for effective temporal and sequential processing. More complex models offer better biological realism but are often hardware-inefficient when implemented digitally. This paper presents a low-power Modified Balanced Resonate-and-Fire (MB-RAF) neuron with adaptive refractory control, derived from the Lotka–Volterra dynamic system. The proposed design incorporates two tunable parameters: ω, which modulates the oscillation frequency, and β, which regulates leakage. An adaptive refractory mechanism dynamically adjusts the threshold to enhance sparsity and prevent excessive firing. Implemented in 55 nm CMOS technology, the proposed MB-RAF neuron achieves ultra-low power consumption, with 25.29 µW during firing and 23.81 µW during hibernation. It is integrated with a 1024 × 128 RRAM synaptic array to form a functional hardware SNN system, demonstrating high classification accuracies on S-mnist, SHD and ECG datasets. These results highlight the MB-RAF neuron’s strong potential for compact and energy-efficient neuromorphic computing applications.

title: Phase Errors in Sub-Threshold Delay-Locked Loop.
abstract: Leakage-induced phase disturbances in the idle state of sub-threshold charge-pump DLLs are investigated. We show leakage-induced phase disturbances are periodic and non-negligible, and prevent the DLLs from locking. We further the contribution of device noise to phase disturbances is negligible as compared with that of the leakage. Single bootstrapping and double bootstrapping are proposed to minimize leakage-induced phase disturbances and their effectiveness is verified using simulation results.

title: Generic Cryogenic VLSI Design Flow and Optimization Strategies for Energy-Efficient Computing.
abstract: This article presents a generic reliable Cryo-VLSI design flow platform aimed at optimizing CMOS performance for efficient high-performance computing at cryogenic temperatures. Our approach integrates high-accurate cryogenic device models into a cryogenic-specific-optimized standard cell library, which not only ensures the conventional electronic design automation (EDA)-based VLSI design process to be utilized at cryogenic temperatures, but also enables circuit-level optimization with high efficiency. Accordingly, our post-layout simulations reveal a 27% reduction in the energy delay product (EDP) and a 33% enhancement of the clock frequency for the designed XuanTie RISC-V processor operating at 77 K.

title: A 32-Channel Neural Stimulator with 30V Supply Range and Bootstrap Charge Balancing Switches.
abstract: This paper presents a 32-channel neural stimulator with wide power supply range and novel charge balancing switches. To optimize power supply scheme, a high-voltage (HV) power management unit (PMU) is designed to handle a 6~30V supply range and generate internal voltage and current references. Facing a process limitation of LDMOS whose gate-to-source voltage (VGS) can’t exceed 5.5V, a HV level shifter is presented to both control and protect the output switch for anode current source. Besides, to realize high-accuracy charge balancing for safe neural stimulation, a bootstrap charge balancing switch is proposed with wide input range (0~25V) and constant on-state resistance. Moreover, a segmented current steering DAC with Data Weighted Averaging (DWA) mismatch shaping is adopted to generate an 8-bit-accuracy current source. Fabricated in a 0.18μm BCD process, the stimulator chip occupies 9.52mm2. It supports both monopolar and bipolar stimulation with programmable pulse width and amplitude. The charge balancing switch realizes 16mV accuracy according to the measurement result.

title: MoSim: A Modular Simulation Framework for FPGA-based Systolic CNN Accelerators.
abstract: Architectural simulators are widely used in computer architecture to explore design spaces and validate ideas before implementation. Recent works such as Scale-Sim extend this approach to convolutional neural network (CNN) accelerators, particularly systolic array-based designs. However, most target ASIC and overlook the unique resource characteristics of FPGA which is now a popular platform for CNN acceleration. To address this gap, we present MoSim, a modular, cycle-accurate simulator tailored for FPGA-based systolic CNN accelerators. MoSim models FPGA-specific resources and reports detailed performance and resource statistics to facilitate design space exploration. Evaluations on representative CNN workloads demonstrate that the simulator effectively captures FPGA-specific effects and guides practical design decisions.

title: Novel M-CNN design fostering gradual switching of InGaZnO(IGZO)-based memristive devices.
abstract: Memristive devices are promising enablers for computing-in-memory architectures, offering reduced latency and energy consumption compared to conventional designs. Among these, the memristive device-based Cellular Nonlinear Network (M-CNN) provides a compact framework for universal computing, including image processing and neuromorphic computing. In this work, we investigate the use of IGZO-based devices exhibiting gradual switching as core elements of M-CNN cells. A simulation approach based on measured I-V-characteristics is developed to evaluate device–circuit interactions. We first analyze the limitations of the conventional M-CNN cell core, where asymmetric I-V-characteristics restrict voltage levels and accelerate device degradation. To address these issues, we propose a symmetrized cell that mitigates asymmetry, intrinsically limits cell voltage, and supports differential readout. The results demonstrate that gradual switching enables reliable distinction of input current levels while ensuring stable operation and reduced power consumption, thus paving the way for robust IGZO-based M-CNN implementations.

title: Sub-Threshold DLL with Built-in Linearization and Time-Mode Proportional-Integral Locking.
abstract: This paper reports a ultra-low power sub-threshold DLL with built-in linearization and time-mode proportional-integral. The DLL consists of a sub-threshold current-starved delay line with built-in linearization, a TDC-based proportional block called pBlock and a bi-directional gated delay line time integrator-based integration block called iBlock. Bootstrapping and high threshold-voltage devices are used to ensure its proper operation and minimum power consumption of the iBlock. The DLL is designed in a TSMC 130 nm 1.2 V CMOS technology with a reduced supply voltage of 0.6 V and analyzed using Spectre with BSIM3v3 device models. Simulation results show the DLL locks to a 100 kHz reference at all PVT corners with no accumulated static phase errors. It occupies 0.0113 mm2, offers a 50-500 kHz lock range, 0.618% RMS jitter, and consumes 138 nW.

title: A 7-bit 1-GS/s Single-Channel Charge-Injection Loop-Unrolled SAR ADC with Foreground Calibration.
abstract: This paper presents a 7-bit 1 GS/s single-channel charge-injection (CI) successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital (ADC). The architecture employs a split capacitive digital-to-analog (CDAC) and charge-injection digital-to-analog (CIDAC) hybrid architecture, which exponentially reduces the area of the traditional CDAC. Meanwhile, it maintains a constant common-mode voltage in the CDAC conversion part, thus limiting the voltage swing of the CIDAC conversion part to within 0.1 V and improving the linearity of the CIDAC. It also employs Loop-unrolled(LU) SAR logic, which eliminates the need to wait for the reset of comparators and thus enhances the conversion speed. Meanwhile, a calibration mode with extensive reuse of timing logic is proposed, which overcomes the high dependence of traditional CI cell performance on process, voltage, temperature(PVT) characteristics and improves the robustness of the ADC. Designed in a 28 nm process, the ADC achieves a SNDR of 43.3 dB and a SFDR of 57.3 dB. The power consumption is 0.254 mW to achieve 2.14 fJ/conv.-step Walden figure-of-merit (FOM) .

title: PEFT: a near-memory processing-enabled heterogeneous accelerator for BatchPBS TFHE.
abstract: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is increasingly adopted for private deep neural network (DNN) inference due to its formal privacy guarantees. Torus-FHE (TFHE) supports accurate evaluation of nonlinear functions, but has to evaluate the intermediate activations one by one through bootstrapping. To address this challenge, the Batched Programmable Bootstrapping (BatchPBS) algorithm was introduced. Although it enables batched nonlinear function evaluation, we observe it still suffers from significant latency cost, primarily due to the off-chip memory access.To overcome this limitation, we propose PEFT, a heterogeneous accelerator for BatchPBS TFHE based on near-memory processing (NMP). PEFT features an optimized framework designed to minimize data movement for BatchPBS. At its core is a co-designed NMP unit that executes various modular integer arithmetic instructions, supported by an efficient data mapping scheme and execution flow. Our integrated approach significantly enhances the performance and energy efficiency of TFHE DNN inference workloads.

title: Efficient FPGA Deployment of Power-of-Two Quantized Networks via Dynamic Hierarchical Base-Exponent Offset Encoding.
abstract: Power-of-two (PoT) quantization has been proved as a promising solution for neural network deployment. However, the development of PoT is normally for efficient bit-shift computations on edge devices such as FPGAs, and the resulting natural clustering of weights is often overlooked for memory optimization. To fill this gap, we introduce Dynamic Hierarchical Base-Exponent Offset (DHBEO) to exploit this clustering. DHBEO groups PoT weights within layers and represents them using a shared base exponent plus a compact offset, thereby significantly reducing the overall weight memory footprint. Our evaluation on ResNet-18 with ImageNet demonstrates that DHBEO achieves up to a 90.62% reduction in memory usage and maintains competitive accuracy (69.42% Top-1 with a 3-bit offset), outperforming existing 5-bit PoT methods in storage efficiency. DHBEO delivers an impressive throughput of 594.52 GOP/s and a power efficiency of 127.85 GOP/s/W based on an AMD XCZU9EG FPGA.

title: A FeFET-based Approximate DCIM Integrating Multiplication and OR Addition In-Bitcell.
abstract: Digital computing-in-memory (DCIM) preserves accuracy and is robust to process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) variations, yet the adder tree dominates macro-level area and power. To reduce the adder tree cost, DCIM with approximate adders, called approximate DCIM (ADCIM), has been proposed, but the number of addition operations in adder tree has not been reduced. In this paper, we propose a ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET)-based DCIM bitcell. The proposed 2-FeFET bitcell performs two 1-bit multiplications as well as an in-bitcell OR-approximated addition simultaneously, and it can effectively replace the 1ststage adders in adder tree. As a result, when the proposed bitcell is employed for ADCIM design, nearly half of addition operations in adder tree can be performed inside 2-FeFET bitcells, thus significantly increasing area and power efficiencies. Experimental results show that the proposed ADCIM achieves 50% of area and 52.4% of power reduction over the SRAM-based DCIM baseline.

title: Live Demonstration: Circular Object Recognition with Binary-weight Spiking Neural Networks.
abstract: This proof-of-concept experiment shows that AI can recognize objects with indistinct contours, even when SNN weights are quantized and designed in binary. Circular objects can indicate either high-speed movement, such as a ball, or random, minute movements on an LCD monitor. The demo system implements a real-time, quantized SNN, which reduces the computational load of inference. Visitors can experience the real-time recognition of circular objects and observe the performance differences among SNNs with various bit weights running on PC or SoC-FPGA systems. They can also understand the power consumption differences between PCs and FPGAs.

title: Ultra-Low Latency Synchronous Integral Demodulation Technique for Eddy Current Sensor.
abstract: With the development of industrial automation, eddy current displacement sensors are playing a crucial role in precision electromechanical systems. However, the previous demodulation techniques generally have large latency, which has a significant impact on the fast response of the sensing system. This article proposes an ultra-low latency synchronous integral demodulation technique for eddy current sensor. It achieves both low latency and high SNR demodulation. The system on chip (SoC) designed in this article includes transmitter, demodulation, power management, and digital logical modules. The proposed SoC achieves 87.4 ns transmission latency and 64.1 dB SNR at 4 MHz excitation frequency. It is implemented in 110-nm CMOS process from 5 V power supply.

title: An Event-Driven Spiking Compute-In-Memory Macro based on SOT-MRAM.
abstract: The application of Magnetic Random-Access Memory (MRAM) in computing-in-memory (CIM) has gained significant attention. However, existing designs often suffer from high energy consumption due to their reliance on complex analog circuits for computation. In this work, we present a Spin-Orbit- Torque MRAM(SOT-MRAM)-based CIM macro that employs an event-driven spiking processing for high energy efficiency. The SOT-MRAM crossbar adopts a hybrid series-parallel cell structure to efficiently support matrix-vector multiplication (MVM). Signal information is (en) decoded as spikes using lightweight circuits, eliminating the need for conventional area- and powerintensive analog circuits. The SOT-MRAM macro is designed and evaluated in 28nm technology, and experimental results show that it achieves a peak energy efficiency of 243.6 TOPS/W, significantly outperforming existing designs.

title: A Strain-Gauge Readout Circuit with SAR-Based Current Calibration for Sensor Variation Compensation in Side-Button Applications.
abstract: This paper presents a multi-level side-button sensing system integrating a strain-gauge sensor with an eight-bit successive-approximation-register (SAR) current compensation scheme for stable operation despite significant sensor resistance variations caused by manufacturing and environmental fluctuations. The proposed architecture employs monotonic current-compensation cells and a common-mode cancellation amplifier that suppresses common-mode offset and converts monotonic input currents into fully differential bipolar outputs. A dual-mode capacitive trans-impedance amplifier performs current-to-voltage conversion during calibration and signal integration during readout. The proposed system, designed in a 350-nm CMOS process, effectively compensates for sensor resistance deviations and achieves 1.2-LSB calibration accuracy. The robustness of the calibration performance is verified across process corners, a wide temperature range (-45°C to 80°C), and supply voltage variations (2.7V to 3.3V) for sensing resistance above 5.88 kΩ, while consuming 0.45 mW in readout mode and 1.83 mW in calibration mode.

title: A 1.2-3.4 Gb/s Low-Power Multiphase CDR with Glitch-Free Bang-Bang Phase Detector.
abstract: This paper presents a multiphase clock and data recovery (CDR) circuit for high-speed (1.2-3.4 Gb/s) display driver ICs (DDIs) with a novel glitch-free bang-bang phase detector (BBPD). Compared to conventional BBPDs, which often suffer from sampling glitches caused by latch-delay mismatches and asynchronous data-edge interferences, the proposed BBPD employs a robust sampling network ensuring mutually exclusive data-edge valid events, thereby filtering invalid transitions and minimizing timing-induced jitter. An extensive comparison with conventional BBPDs highlights these improvements and clarifies how the proposed BBPD enhances phase detection integrity and overall stability in high-speed CDRs. Fabricated in a 0.18-μm CMOS process and integrated in a chip-on-film (COF) package along with other DDI's components, the proposed CDR demonstrates a clean output phase trajectory and an improved 97 ps output jitter (0.388 UI at 4 Gb/s) with only 20.1 mW power consumption including the equalizer power. The overall CDR performance is also validated through a comprehensive characterization using a shmoo plot across 1.4 V - 2.2 V supply voltages.

title: A 0.036mm2 Cross-Coupled Class-AB High-Voltage Amplifier with Unipolar/Bipolar Output Using 180nm BCD for Multi-Channel MEMS Drivers.
abstract: This paper presents a cross-coupled push–pull Class-AB high-voltage amplifier (HV-AMP) tailored for multi-channel MEMS driver applications. Conventional charge-pump or stacked-MOSFET approaches often introduce voltage ripple, large device overhead, and limited ability to realize both unipolar and bipolar outputs. By contrast, the proposed cross-coupled push–pull Class-AB architecture uses only six laterally diffused metal-oxide-semiconductor (LDMOS) devices to enable rail-to-rail high-voltage operation, while maintaining linear amplifier performance. This design supports reconfigurable output ranges, providing either unipolar 0–30V or bipolar ±15V output without additional biasing circuits. Implemented in a 180nm BCD process, this design occupies 0.036mm2and achieves an 85dB low-frequency gain, a 1MHz gain–bandwidth, and a 97.65V/µs slew rate. The amplifier consumes 0.65mW in unipolar mode and bipolar mode, demonstrating both high efficiency and compact area. These features make the proposed HV-AMP a promising building block for scalable, low-power, and high slew rate MEMS driver arrays.

title: Static Segment-Based Approximate Booth Multiplier with Probabilistic Error Compensation.
abstract: Approximate computing has become an efficient design method in error-tolerant applications to achieve better performance. Among various approximation techniques, truncation with error compensation is widely adopted due to its flexible compromise between error and power consumption. In this paper, two truncated Booth multipliers are proposed with static segment method based on probabilistic estimation of partial products and truncated compressing tree using simple error compensation circuit. Compared with the exact design, the proposed Booth multipliers achieve at least 36.96% of area reduction and 35.95% of power reduction. Additionally, in the application of Sobel detecting, they have acceptable performance with SSIM loss less than 3%.

title: A Self-built Continuous Temperature Compensation Circuit for Logarithmic Amplifier.
abstract: This paper presents a continuous temperature compensation circuit for trans-diode logarithmic amplifier (TDLA) to ensure the robustness and accuracy of radar sensing. Self-built and on-chip integrated, the calibration topology adopts a two-step structure to eliminate the impact on the gain of the TDLA caused by temperature-induced changes in the performance of its core BJT. Besides a traditional first-step compensation for the reverse saturation current of PN junctions, an automatically variable-gain amplifier whose gain is controlled by an adjustable body-biasing MOSFET array is utilized as a second step to mitigate the effects of the thermal voltage (VT). Simulation results show that a logarithmic amplifier equipped with this novel temperature compensation demonstrates a conversion gain deviation of less than±0.6 dB across the temperature range from -45¼C to 125¼C.

title: A LiDAR Point Cloud Dataset for Crowd Segmentation and Counting.
abstract: Accurate and privacy-preserving monitoring of dense crowds remains a critical challenge for developing robust AI-driven safety systems. While traditional video surveillance struggles with occlusions and high-density scenarios, LiDAR offers a powerful alternative by capturing rich 3D spatial information. In this work, we present a pipeline to generate synthetic LiDAR point cloud datasets that model realistic pedestrian movement and group dynamics in crowded environments. The dataset includes point-level annotations for crowd management tasks such as segmentation and counting. Multiple sensor viewpoints capture diverse crowd configurations, enabling the training and evaluation of state-of-the-art AI models under varied conditions. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of these models in segmentation and counting tasks, highlighting the dataset’s potential to advance LiDAR-based crowd perception.

title: A 241MHz/mA Low Power, Low noise Capacitively Coupled Chopper Amplifier with Integrated Feedforward Passive Ripple Reduction.
abstract: This paper presents a 180nm CMOS capacitively-coupled chopper operational amplifier (CCOPA) for precision sensing applications, achieving exceptional Gain Bandwidth Power Efficiency(GBW/Isupply), and 27 nV/√Hz input-referred noise while consuming only 9μA for a closed loop gain of 100. A key challenge in chopper amplifiers is the large output voltage ripple caused by the up-converted DC offset, which can severely limit dynamic range. To address this without the power and area overhead of conventional active feedback loops, this work integrates a feedforward passive ripple reduction technique. A parallel R-C network creates a frequency-dependent impedance that blocks the DC offset current while passing the modulated signal, achieving 59 dB of ripple attenuation. Furthermore, the paper analyzes a long-term output drift mechanism in resistively-biased CCOPAs caused by leakage currents, a critical but often overlooked issue. The design presents a power-efficient wide swing, low noise capacitively coupled amplifier for power-constrained precision sensing applications.

title: Influence of Quantizer Resolution in Gm-C Based DSM with Feedback Non-Linearity Cancellation.
abstract: Continuous-time (CT) Delta-Sigma-Modulators (DSMs) are favored for their implicit filtering and easier drivability features. While opamp-based RC integrators offer high linearity, they can exhibit low resistive input impedance in high-resolution converters. Gm-C integrators are more power efficient with high input impedance but suffer from non-linearity. This paper explores the challenges of a specific non-linearity cancellation technique applied in DSM on system-level, focusing on the quantizer finite resolution and the resulting quantization noise (QN) folding. A theoretical analysis for the extra folded noise is presented, matching with simulation results.

title: FPGA Implementation of Sketched LiDAR for a 192 × 128 SPAD Image Sensor.
abstract: This study presents an efficient field-programmable gate array (FPGA) implementation of a polynomial spline function–based statistical compression algorithm designed to address the critical challenge of massive data transfer bandwidth in emerging high-spatial-resolution single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) arrays, where data rates can reach tens of gigabytes per second. In our experiments, the proposed hardware implementation achieves a compression ratio of 512× compared with conventional histogram-based outputs, with the potential for further improvement. The algorithm is first optimized in software using fixed-point (FXP) arithmetic and look-up tables (LUTs) to eliminate explicit additions, multiplications, and non-linear operations. This enables a careful balance between accuracy and hardware resource utilization. Guided by this trade-off analysis, online sketch processing elements (SPEs) are implemented on an FPGA to directly process time-stamp streams from the SPAD sensor. The implementation is validated using a customized LiDAR setup with a 192 × 128–pixel SPAD array. This work demonstrates histogram-free online depth reconstruction with high fidelity, effectively alleviating the time-stamp transfer bottleneck of SPAD arrays and offering scalability as pixel counts continue to increase for future SPADs.

title: Neural Quantization-Aware Piecewise Linear Approximation for Nonlinear Functions on FPGA.
abstract: Nonlinear functions are widely used in neural networks but lead to high latency and area overhead in hardware implementations. NN-LUT proposed a neural network-based piecewise linear (PWL) approximation, which fits nonlinear operations via neural network and stores the coefficients in LUTs to simplify the computation logic. However, existing neural PWL methods still suffer from two key limitations: accuracy degradation due to quantization-unaware design, and considerable hardware overhead from full-width comparators for interval identification. To address these issues, we propose NQA-LUT, which fine-tunes the slope and intercept parameters through quantization-aware training, thereby improving the approximation accuracy. In addition, we introduce a hierarchical MSB-LSB interval identification strategy that avoids redundant full-width comparisons to reduce hardware overhead. FPGA implementation results show that, compared to the state-of-the-art Auto-LUT method, NQA-LUT achieves a 34.3% reduction in approximation error while reducing LUT and flip-flop (FF) usage by 5.3% and 29.5%, respectively. Code is available at https://github.com/yuffeenn/NQA-LUT.

title: Design of a Ku/K-Band Mode-Switching Reconfigurable Low-Noise Amplifier in 110-nm CMOS Technology.
abstract: This paper presents a two-stage Ku/K-Band reconfigurable low-noise amplifier (LNA) in a 110-nm CMOS process based on electrically and magnetically switchable coupled resonator (EMSCR) and mode-switching techniques. A tri-coupled transformer-based input network is co-designed with the first-stage load network to jointly exploit the gate-drain capacitance (Cgd)-induced loading effect, thereby realizing wideband input matching covering Ku/K-Band while eliminating input-network switches and minimizing noise figure degradation. The first-stage load integrates an EMSCR, which provides band-selective transimpedance gain and enhances out-of-band rejection. The second stage employs two differential switch groups to steer the excitation current of a mode-switching transformer, enabling compact implementation and stable gain-band reconfiguration. Implemented in a 110-nm CMOS process, the proposed LNA achieves simulated gains of 11 dB and 6.9 dB over 10.6-13.2 GHz and 15.5-19.4 GHz, respectively. The input return loss remains2.

title: Live Demonstration:A Reconfigurable and Self-Regulating Wearable NIRS Platform for Multi-Scenario Monitoring.
abstract: This demonstration presents a reconfigurable self-regulating wearable near-infrared spectroscopy(NIRS) detection system for non-invasive real-time monitoring of hemoglobin concentration in human tissues. The system utilizes dual-wavelength LEDs at 735 nm and 850 nm as the light source, estimating hemoglobin concentration by detecting the intensity of light irradiated onto the body and reflected back. The system is highly portable and flexible, can be worn on different parts of the body, and allows users to conveniently monitor hemoglobin concentration.

title: Edge-RamanSBL-Net: Compressed Sensing-Based Real-Time Directional Raman Qualitative Unmixing via Network Unfolding and One-Shot Training.
abstract: Raman spectroscopy enables accurate substance identification by leveraging its inherent fingerprint characteristics, yet edge-side Raman spectral qualitative unmixing analysis faces two critical challenges: traditional methods suffer from low inference efficiency and high resource consumption, while deep learning-based methods rely heavily on large-scale labeled data. So this paper proposes a Sparse Bayesian Learning (SBL) unfolded network named Edge-RamanSBL-Net (ERSN) to address the pain points. ERSN adopts a cascaded unfolded architecture with 5 SBL layers, converting the iterative optimization of SBL into the forward network to learn the mapping relationship between mxiture spectra and multiple pure components and support high-dimensional dictionary input. Through a network parameter sharing mechanism, the model weight is compressed to 6.13MB. During the training phase, a hierarchical decrement strategy is employed to decouple training sufficiency from testing flexibility, allowing inference complexity to be adjusted on demand. Experiments validated with data collected by portable instruments show that on 16 types of mixture samples (10 spectra per type), both the positive identification rate and recall rate reach 100%, with an average execution time of 40ms per spectrum (75-fold speedup). Moreover, only one 5-component mixture spectrum is required to complete One-Shot training. ERSN is an effective solution for fast and accurate Raman qualitative unmixing on edge devices.

title: RTCore: A RISC-V Processor Featuring Nested Hardware Loop Optimization for Real-time Control System.
abstract: Real-time control systems demand processors that deliver deterministic, low-latency performance under strict power and area constraints. While specialized DSPs like the TI C28x address this with custom ISAs, they are proprietary and often lack efficient support for nested loops—a critical bottleneck. This paper presents RTCore, an 8-stage single-issue RISC-V processor that overcomes these limitations. We introduce lightweight, custom ISA extensions for hardware-supported nested loops, managed by a dedicated LIFO structure that enables single-cycle context switching without pipeline stalls. Fabricated in 180nm technology, RTCore achieves a 7–47% performance improvement over the industrial TI C28x baseline while maintaining a power efficiency of 2.09–3.25 mW/MHz. Our results demonstrate that RTCore provides a compelling, efficient, and customizable alternative to proprietary DSPs for next-generation real-time control applications.

title: Breaking the Local Optima Barrier in Branch Predictor Design Space Exploration: An LLM-Based Initialization Strategy for PSO.
abstract: TAGE branch predictors deliver state-of-the-art accuracy but require complex parameter optimization across exponential design spaces. We present an LLM-guided Particle Swarm Optimization framework that transforms parameter initialization into a text-based reasoning task. Our approach generates intelligent starting points that accelerate convergence while preserving solution quality. Experimental results demonstrate 2× faster convergence and consistent performance gains across 1–64KB storage constraints, with particular strength in resource-limited scenarios. The method automatically discovers optimal architecture trade-offs and generalizes across workload patterns, offering a promising path toward automated microarchitecture optimization..

title: High-Speed Area-Efficient Adder Design with SET-MOS Technology.
abstract: This paper presents a high-speed, area-efficient adder design based on hybrid Single-Electron Transistor and MOS (SET-MOS) architectures. By utilizing the Coulomb oscillation characteristics of SETs, an integrated multi-input digital logic (a.k.a. Coulomb gate) is proposed to perform addition operations with significantly reduced area cost and improved area-delay product. In particular, we focus on design of a 2-bit adder which is implemented using only six transistors and three inverters, compared favorably with conventional CMOS counterparts. The proposed Coulomb gates are further extended to a 16-bit adder design with 70% reduction in transistor count and nearly 8% improvement in area-delay product compared to the best existing adders. This SET-MOS based approach offers a scalable and promising solution for arithmetic circuits that are widely used in IoT, edge computing, and biomedical systems.

title: RECALLS: Reinforcement Learning Enhanced Generative Model for Logic Synthesis Optimization.
abstract: Logic synthesis optimization is essential for enhancing the quality of results (QoR) of circuits by applying a sequence of structural transformations to circuit representations. This paper proposes RECALLS, a novel reinforcement learning (RL)-enhanced generative model for logic synthesis optimization. RECALLS is built upon a graph-to-sequence generative model and further fine-tuned with RL from human feedback technology. This model eliminates repetitive exploration and directly generates sequences for any specified design by inference. Experimental results demonstrate that RECALLS significantly enhances circuit QoR compared to hand-crafted transformation sequences. Furthermore, RECALLS achieves thousands of times faster than the machine learning-based methods while consistently generating sequences with comparable QoR.

title: An Energy and Area-Efficient Ternary SAR ADC with Tri-State Comparison.
abstract: This brief presents a ternary Successive Approximation Register (SAR) Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) aimed at reducing the power and area overheads while achieving speed improvement. The proposed ternary ADC is compatible with different DAC switching techniques. With the same switching techniques, the proposed ternary ADC reduces the DAC switching power consumption by 50% and the area by 66%, while achieving a 1.5x improvement in quantization speed compared to prior designs. The proposed ADC is simulated in a 40-nm CMOS technology with sampling rate of 1-GS/s and resolution of 6-bit. The simulation results achieve a 5.97 effective number of bits (ENOBs) with about 0.97-mW power consumption resulting in a FoM of 15.47fJ/conversion-step.

title: Live Demonstration: A High-Resolution Plantar with Crosstalk Compensation for Human-Machine Interaction.
abstract: This work presents a method to compensate for undesired crosstalk commonly found in crossbar pressure sensor arrays. With a cleaner pressure image, more features can be extracted for finer human–machine interface (HMI) applications. The platform comprises a custom-designed resistive plantar plate, resistance readout circuits, wireless transmission via Wi-Fi, and a battery. These components together form the plantar sensing system. A neural network deployed on a laptop compensates for crosstalk effects and visualises interactive functions. The system captures subtle foot movements in all directions and fine pressure variations from toe contacts. Leveraging these micro-pressure dynamics, visitors can experience novel interactive controls and gaming through a customised HMI.

title: InFP: A 17.97 TFLOPS/W Reconfigurable SRAM Based Computing-in-Memory Macro for BF16 MAC Operations.
abstract: As the demand for high-precision training and inference of deep neural networks (DNNs) continues to grow, floating-point (FP) compute-in-memory (CIM) architecture has emerged as an essential solution. However, in contrast to extensively studied integer (INT) CIM, the efficiency of FP-CIM still requires further enhancement. In this paper, we present an energy-efficient and area-efficient digital SRAM-based FP-CIM macro with reconfigurable peripheral logic. Specifically, we design an interleaved SRAM bank with specific weight mapping, which improves SRAM utilization and enables write-compute pipeline scheduling to maximize hardware usage. Additionally, to improve energy efficiency and reduce area requirements, we propose a reconfigurable peripheral logic equipped with a shared addition unit, conducting exponent and mantissa addition at different stages of the FP MAC operation. A 16kb SRAM CIM macro with the proposed techniques is designed in TSMC 45nm CMOS technology and occupies an area of 0.081 mm2. The simulation results show that our work achieves a peak energy efficiency of 17.97 TFLOPS/W and an area efficiency of 0.395 TFLOPS/mm2with brain-float 16 (BF16) representation.

title: A Lightweight Algorithm-Hardware Co-design for Real-Time Video Frame Interpolation.
abstract: Video Frame Interpolation (VFI) aims to generate intermediate frames between consecutive video frames to achieve smooth motion transitions. However, existing VFI methods face significant challenges including high computational complexity and suboptimal hardware resource utilization, making it difficult for real-time on-device systems. This paper presents an algorithm-hardware co-optimized framework for VFI. Specifically, a Lightweight Video Frame Interpolation Model (LVFIM) is proposed to reduce both parameter count and computational overhead. Furthermore, we develop a Low-Latency Hardware Accelerator (LLHA) featuring tile-level parallelism and a tightly-coupled computing architecture, enabling efficient pipelined execution of the architecture and achieving high computational efficiency for depthwise and pointwise convolutions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed LVFIM achieves competitive interpolation quality compared to existing frame interpolation methods on the Vimeo90K, UCF101, and Adobe240 datasets with only 40.2K parameters. Meanwhile, The hardware implementation achieves up to 2.3× improvements in throughput compared to prior video processors.

title: Physics-guided AI-Assisted Modeling of Flexible Transistors Based on Fully-Additive Printed Electronics Process.
abstract: Fully-additive printed electronics enables low-cost and flexible circuit fabrication, but severe process variations significantly degrade device uniformity and modeling accuracy. This work presents an AI-assisted modeling framework for flexible thin-film transistors (TFTs) fabricated via a fully-additive printed electronics process. To accurately capture the nonlinear current voltage characteristics of the printed transistors, a hybrid AI-assisted model is proposed, combining a physics-based trend equation with a residual neural network (RNN). The trend model provides a physically interpretable baseline describing the device’s general behavior, while the RNN learns the fine-grained residuals from experimental data. A physics-informed loss function is further incorporated to enforce smoothness and monotonicity, ensuring that the model adheres to fundamental device physics. Experimental validation on printed flexible FETs demonstrates that the proposed approach achieves high prediction accuracy and physical consistency across wide bias ranges and different bending conditions.

title: A D-band CMOS Frequency Sextupler with 1.62-dB Conversion Gain and >20-dBc HRR in 65-nm CMOS.
abstract: This paper presents a D-band frequency sextupler with high conversion gain (CG) and superior harmonic rejection (HRR), implemented in a standard 65-nm CMOS process. The proposed design leverages a source-degenerated inductor in the tripler core to efficiently enhance the third harmonic while actively suppressing lower-order undesired harmonics, thereby achieving high CG without affecting input-output matching. Additionally, a compensation capacitor integrated at the input balun minimizes reflection and ensures stable 50-Ω wideband matching. Measured at 114 GHz, the prototype achieves a remarkable peak CG of 1.62 dB and a HRR exceeding 20 dBc with only -4.8 dBm of input power, while occupying a compact core area of 670 × 210 μm2.

title: SVVHD: An Open-Source and Self-Verified Benchmark Framework for LLM Evaluation in VHDL Code Generation.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate significant potential for generating and verifying Hardware Description Languages (HDLs) in Electronic Design Automation. However, a notable gap exists in VHDL code generation compared to other HDLs, exacerbated by the absence of an open-source benchmark. To address this gap, we propose SVVHD, an open-source benchmark for evaluating LLMs on VHDL code generation. The first part of SVVHD is an evaluation dataset, constructed by translating 156 diverse Verilog problems into VHDL, employing prompt refactoring and rigorous code equivalence verification. The second part of SVVHD is a set of automated testbenches that perform functional verification of candidate VHDL designs against golden solutions within a sandbox environment. Using SVVHD, we conduct zero-shot code generation evaluations with various LLMs to establish baseline performance for the VHDL code generation domain. Subsequently, we construct both a refactored training set and a basic training set for model fine-tuning, which yield significant performance improvements. The introduction of SVVHD, combined with our fine-tuning methodology, contributes to advancing research in LLM-assisted automated VHDL design.

title: Receiver Localization for Deep-Implant Wireless Power Transfer System at 6.78MHz Using a Flexible Transmitter-Coil Array.
abstract: This paper presents a flexible wireless power transfer (WPT) system with receiver (Rx) localization algorithm based on mutual inductance measurement. The system consists of a flexible transmitter (Tx) coil array driven by GaN-based half-bridge drivers and a Rx coil. The coil-array is modelled in MATLAB to analyse the rotation of coils. A Monte Carlo-based localization algorithm is used to estimate the Rx position. Experimental results show that, even with a 48 nH mutual inductance error, the proposed algorithm achieves an average localization error of 6.75 mm. The system could locate the Rx when it is 72 mm away from the Tx array and deliver 2.92 mW to the load. These results demonstrate the robustness and practical potential of the proposed system for localization and WPT for near organ implants such as spleen and renal nerve stimulators.

title: GPA: A General-Purpose In-Memory Computing Accelerator.
abstract: In-memory computing (IMC) is considered as a promising technique to alleviate the memory wall bottleneck. Various specialized IMC-based accelerators have been proposed recently to accelerate applications in different fields. In this paper, we propose GPA, a general-purpose accelerator based on the IMC technique. GPA is a massively parallel architecture that works in single-instruction-multiple-data (SIMD) manner. It is composed of a three-level hierarchy of computation and storage units (PE-core-array), where the IMC arrays are elaborated to support various operations on both integers and floating-points. We propose four working phases to avoid the potential structural conflict problem in IMC accelerators. An instruction set is also developed for GPA as a programming interface. Compared with an NVIDIA V100 GPU, evaluation results show that GPA achieves 161.28×, 169.66×, 73.18×, and 579.16× speedups and 6.23×, 6.66×, 24.16×, and 412.37× energy savings in four different applications.

title: Development of a Photoacoustic Platform for Blood Glucose Monitoring and a Comparative Study between Signal Propagation delay and Peak-to-Peak Amplitude.
abstract: Achieving noninvasive glucose monitoring is a critical goal for diabetes management, and photoacoustic (PA) technology has emerged as a promising pathway. However, conventional PA-glucose models based on the peak-to-peak amplitude (VPP) are often compromised by environmental interference. While the signal propagation delay (TP) has shown empirical promise for more stable measurements, a foundational theoretical analysis of its robustness has been absent. This study fills this gap, first by presenting a theoretical analysis concluding that TPis inherently more robust against environmental noise than VPP, and then by providing experimental validation on a custom-built PA platform. Linear regression models for both features were established over a 0–1452 mg/dL concentration range. The resulting TPmodel demonstrated a significantly better goodness-of-fit (R2=0.874) compared to the VPPmodel (R2=0.671). Furthermore, validation on an independent dataset confirmed the TP’s superiority: Clarke Error Grid (CEG) analysis showed 100% of readings in the clinically acceptable A+B zones, starkly outperforming the 70% from the VPP-based approach. Our findings provide the first theoretical and experimental evidence for the superiority of TP, positioning it as a more robust feature for reliable noninvasive PA-based glucose monitoring.

title: A High-PSRR Pitch-Matched Ultrasound Receiver Analog Front-End with Integrated Beamforming for PMUT-Based Ultrasound Imaging.
abstract: This paper presents a high-PSRR pitch-matched ultrasound receiver analog front-end (AFE) circuit for miniaturized ultrasound imaging system based-on piezoelectric micromachined ultrasound transducer (PMUT). The AFE is designed to receive echo signals from a 9-channel 2-D PMUT array. The 9-channel AFE integrates nine low-noise amplifiers (LNAs), an analog beamforming (BF) circuit, and a programmable gain amplifier (PGA) within the 200-μm pitch channel while achieving high-PSRR and consuming low-power. A compact current-reused LNA is adopted to achieve pitch-matching. However, its power supply rejection ratio (PSRR) is inherently poor, especially in closely integrated pitch-matched AFE. To address this challenge, a high-PSRR channel-shared low-dropout regulator (LDO) is employed to power nine LNAs. The proposed LDO introduces a pre-LDO stage, significantly improving PSRR while reducing power consumption. The BF is implemented by pipelined sample-and-hold scheme to delay and sum the outputs of nine LNAs, reducing the number of PGAs. The PGA with adjustable gains of 6/12/18/24 dB implements time gain compensation. The proposed 9-channel AFE is designed in a 180nm CMOS process with a compact area of 0.0141 mm2/channel, achieving an input-referred noise of 4.08nV/√Hz@3MHz. a PSRR of 76.8dB@3MHz, and an average power consumption of 0.476 mW/channel.

title: Neural Video Compression with Domain Transfer.
abstract: Content-adaptive compression has always been a key direction in neural video coding (NVC), aiming to mitigate the domain gap between training and testing data. Such gaps often arise from distributional discrepancies between training and inference data, which may cause noticeable performance degradation when the testing content differs from the training distribution. To tackle this challenge, we propose DCVC-DT, a domain transfer enhanced neural video compression framework. Specifically, we design a lightweight online domain transfer (DT) mechanism that dynamically adapts the encoded latent representation during inference, effectively bridging the domain gap without modifying the encoder or decoder parameters. In addition, we develop a frame-level dynamic RD (Rate and Distortion) adjustment scheme that actively regulates the ratio of R and D in the loss function based on quality fluctuation, thereby improving rate-distortion performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DCVC-DT achieves up to 6.21% bitrate savings over the baseline DCVC-DC, while significantly enhancing generalization to unseen testing data and alleviating error propagation. Our code is available at https://github.com/SunnyMass/DCVC-DT.

title: A Fast Convergent Timing Mismatch Calibration for Time-Interleaved ADCs Based on Sub-sequence Weighted Autocorrelation.
abstract: A novel calibration technique with sub-sequence weighted autocorrelation-based skew detection (SWASD) for addressing timing mismatches in time-interleaved analog-to-digital converters (TIADCs) is proposed in this paper. The proposed calibration divides the sample sequence of TIADC into several sub-sequences and substitutes these for the original sequence in the autocorrelation function computation, effectively reducing the autocorrelation’s error caused by finite samples. Compared to previous approaches, this technique achieves faster convergence speed and higher accuracy while only slightly increasing hardware complexity. The proposed technique is applied to both a 12-bit 3 GS/s 4-channel TIADC model and a 12-bit 3 GS/s 4-channel commercial TIADC chip to validate its effectiveness. Simulation results show that the SFDR and SNDR are improved from 49.65dB and 45.39dB to 89.17dB and 65.35dB at fin=0.162fs. In the measurement results, the SFDR and SNDR increase from 57.34dB and 51.50dB to 73.62dB and 53.43dB.

title: Design and Implementation of a Scalable 64 p-bits Ising Computing Chip with Integrated SOT-MTJs for Efficient Computing.
abstract: The Ising machine is a specialized processor designed to solve combinatorial optimization problems (COP) by simulating spin interactions through iterative updates. Conventional CMOS-based Ising annealing relies on pseudo-random number generators, resulting in large power and area overheads and limited solution quality. To overcome these challenges, in this paper, we propose a 64 probabilistic bit (p-bit) Ising computing chip based on large-scale integration of spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions (SOT-MTJs), with read/write circuits implemented in a 110 nm CMOS process. The fully connected architecture enables flexible spin coupling and weight configuration. The highly uniform spin nodes achieve a fast computation speed of 30 ns per update, ultra-low energy consumption of 2.11 nJ/bit/update, and compact area (457 × 215 μm). When solving the Max-Cut problem, the chip reaches the optimal solution for an 8-node graph within 3 μs, leveraging the intrinsic tunable randomness of SOT-MTJs without external annealing.

title: A Two-Stage Machine Learning Assisted Calibration Scheme Achieving 73.3dB SNDR and 87dB SFDR for A 14-bit Pipelined NS-SAR ADC.
abstract: This paper presents a two-stage machine-learning-assisted calibration scheme for high resolution ADCs. This scheme includes a bit-weight-optimized linear projection (BWOLP) stage for linear correction and a Hammerstein neural network (HNN) stage for nonlinear correction. By cascading these two stages, both static and dynamic errors can be calibrated. To validate the effectiveness of this calibration scheme, a prototype pipelined multi-stage noise-shaping (MASH) SAR ADC is designed in 55-nm CMOS process. This pipelined ADC includes a first-stage 6-bit noise-shaping (NS)-SAR and a second-stage 4-bit NS-SAR, realizing second-order noise-shaping. The ADC post-layout simulation shows a signal-to-noise and distortion ratio (SNDR) of 73.3 dB and a spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) of 87 dB in a 10 MHz bandwidth with 4 mW power consumption. The proposed calibration enhances the SNDR and SFDR by 16 dB and 23 dB, respectively, with a compact parameter size of 120.

title: FABS-CIM: Unlocking A/D Conversion Bottlenecks of Bit-Serial Computing-In-Memory with Analog Shift-and-Addition and In-Situ Batch Normalization.
abstract: Computing-In-Memory (CIM) has emerged as a pivotal architecture for energy-efficient artificial intelligence inference systems. Among CIM paradigms, the bit-serial approach is particularly attractive for its inherent scalability and high area efficiency. However, its performance is severely constrained by the power and latency of numerous A/D conversions and digital shift-and-addition, alongside substantial dynamic power from iterative computations. To overcome these challenges, this work presents a fully analog bit-serial CIM architecture, named FABS-CIM. FABS-CIM introduces a switched-capacitor analog shift-and-addition unit that significantly reduces A/D conversion overhead, a low-reference charge-domain computation scheme that minimizes array dynamic power, and a low-cost readout circuit that integrates in-situ batch normalization with a time-to-digital converter. Experimental results demonstrate that FABS-CIM achieves a normalized energy efficiency of 2703.36 TOPS/W and a throughput of 277.4 GOPS, while maintaining excellent computational linearity—representing an 1.42–3.85× improvement in energy efficiency over prior designs.

title: A Power-Efficient High-Speed Residue Amplifier with Source-Driven Input.
abstract: This paper presents a power-efficient high-speed residue amplifier which can be utilized in the multiplying DAC (MDAC). We propose a push-pull source-driven input pair, significantly increasing both the small-signal transconductance and the large-signal current, hence it results in high power efficiency and high speed respectively. A novel active load based on flipped voltage follower (FVF) is also proposed to largely reduce the settling time and improve the speed. The proposed power-efficient high-speed residue amplifier achieves a GBW of 12.5 GHz and a power consumption of only 4.42mW in a 28-nm CMOS with a 1-V supply. This contributes to 180-ps 1% settling time and 16.1-kV/us slew rate, leading to a competitive small-signal and large-signal figure-of-merit (FOM).

title: Learning-enhanced Video Compression with Capability beyond VVC.
abstract: ITU-T VCEG and ISO/IEC MPEG’s Joint Video Experts Team (JVET) has issued a Call for Evidence (CfE) to study the advanced video coding technologies that could provide substantially higher compression capability than VVC standard. This paper presents one solution based on Enhanced Compression Model (ECM) by integrating two optimized learning-based coding tools: a Cost Volume–based Deep Reference Frame (CV-DRF) and a Test Time Augmentation-enhanced Neural Network Loop Filter (TTA-NNLF). The CV-DRF employs a cost volume-based video frame interpolation network to synthesize a temporally consistent reference frame that strengthens inter prediction, while the TTA-NNLF adopts a Transformer-based filter to suppress compression artifacts and improve reconstruction quality. When evaluated under the Random Access (RA) configuration on the CfE SDR RA UHD, SDR RA HD, UGC RA test sequences, relative to the CfE anchor VTM-23.11, this method achieves average BD-rate savings of 32.02%, 36.15%, and 38.39% for Y, U, and V components, respectively. These results provide concrete evidence that hybridizing ECM with modern learned modules is a promising direction for next-generation standardization beyond VVC.

title: FRRAP: A Fast-Response Reconfigurable AI Processor and Its Application in Four-Class Seizure Monitoring.
abstract: Human medical signal processing systems face significant challenges in clinical deployment, including stringent real-time constraints, limited hardware efficiency, and poor generalization. This paper presents a fast-response reconfigurable artificial intelligence processor (FRRAP) based on a coarse-grained reconfigurable architecture (CGRA), specifically designed for low-latency and energy-efficient biomedical signal processing. To validate the proposed architecture, seizure monitoring is selected as a representative application requiring minimal latency. We proposed a four-class seizure monitoring model that integrates both seizure prediction and detection functions, leveraging a task decomposition algorithm to mitigate class imbalance in the training data. The model employs a shared dual-branch neural network, achieving a classification accuracy of 94.07% on the CHB-MIT dataset with only 10.26 K parameters. Fabricated in 12 nm CMOS technology, FRRAP incorporates multi-level configuration mechanisms and dynamic instruction prefetching to enhance execution efficiency. The system achieves a seizure detection latency of 0.61 s, representing a 39% improvement over conventional ASIC-based accelerators. Enabled by a large-scale array of processing elements and on-chip memory, FRRAP supports a wide range of high-throughput medical signal processing workloads, offering the flexibility and scalability to accommodate emerging applications in real-time health monitoring and beyond.

title: WinoMobi: A General-Purpose Winograd IP for Efficient MobileNet Acceleration on Resource-Constrained FPGAs.
abstract: The efficient deployment of modern convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on resource-constrained edge devices is often hindered by the dual challenges of convolutional computational complexity and limited hardware resources. This paper presents WinoMobi, a general-purpose Winograd convolution IP tailored for MobileNet. The proposed IP adopts a unified design that maps standard convolution, depthwise convolution (DW), and pointwise convolution (PW) onto a general matrix multiplication (GEMM) engine, while integrating fully connected layer (FC) to avoid redundant overhead caused by operator isolation. Through resource reuse, optimized dataflow scheduling, and pipelined execution, WinoMobi maintains generality while significantly improving hardware efficiency and reducing arithmetic and memory overhead. Experimental results on the Zynq-7020 Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) platform demonstrate that, for MobileNet V2 deployment, relative to the pre-optimization baseline, WinoMobi reduces total system power by approximately 41.6% and cuts DSP usage to 30% of the original. Moreover, under the same platform settings, it further lowers DSP consumption by 67.8%–70.9% and system power by 12.0%–42.1% compared with prior works. These results substantiate the effectiveness of the proposed approach as a low-power, high-efficiency, and scalable solution for lightweight neural network deployment on resource-constrained FPGAs.

title: PSVS: A Parallel-Series Voltage-Sensing 1T4R RRAM Macro Achieving 15-Level Storage and 17.88 Mb/mm2 Density for LLM Inference.
abstract: The rapid expansion of Large Language Models (LLMs) has intensified the demand for high-density and low-power memory in edge AI hardware. Resistive random-access memory (RRAM) is a promising candidate. However, conventional current-sensing 1T4R arrays suffer from limited storage density and high read energy. This work presents a Parallel–Series Voltage-Sensing (PSVS) 1T4R RRAM macro capable of storing 4-bit symmetrically quantized weights, achieving 3.91-bit (15-level) effective storage per cell. The design integrates parallel–series (PS) encoding, a differential-sampling coupled (DSC) voltage-sensing amplifier, and an asymmetric transition readout to enhance the sensing margin, suppress resistance variation, and enable bidirectional reads for improved endurance. Fabricated in 28 nm CMOS, the macro attains 17.88 Mb/mm2density, 0.09 pJ/bit read energy, and a FoM of 372.9 GB/s/mm2—an 18.5× improvement over prior works. These results demonstrate a compact, robust, and energy-efficient readout solution for scalable edge LLM deployment.

title: SIMCH: Stochastic In-Memory Computing using High-Density MTJ.
abstract: In-memory computing (IMC) has emerged as a promising paradigm for data-intensive applications, as it mitigates data movement overhead and enhances computational efficiency by performing operations directly within memory arrays. Nevertheless, conventional IMC architectures face scalability and density constraints arising from the integration of complex logic circuits into memory structures. To overcome these limitations, we introduce SIMCH, an in-memory stochastic computing (IMSC) architecture that exploits stochastic magnetic tunnel junctions (sMTJs) to enable a fully digital, parallel, and probabilistic computation. By co-integrating fixed-probability sMTJs with MRAM bit cells, SIMCH achieves high-density stochastic matrix–vector multiplication without the need for analog biasing. When evaluated on hyperdimensional computing (HDC) workloads, the IMSC system demonstrates up to 6.7× higher memory density compared to an SRAM-based IMC macro and delivers a 7.7× improvement in throughput over a state-of-the-art ReRAM-based HDC accelerator, while maintaining accuracy close to the baseline.

title: Cross-Layer Evaluation for On-Chip Training of BEOL FeTFT-based CIM M3D Accelerator.
abstract: This paper presents a device-to-system cross-layer evaluation framework that enables system-level optimization of on-chip training in compute-in-memory (CIM) accelerators built with monolithic 3D (M3D) integrated ferroelectric thin film transistor (FeTFT). Our proposed framework integrates multi-physics device modeling, circuit-compatible neural network simulations to bridge device-level and system-level of design abstraction. Using a 1T1FeTFT array with back-end-of-line (BEOL) compatible amorphous-InGaZnO (a-IGZO) access transistors, we evaluate design knobs at the system-level for CIM application. Our results show that aggressive scaling of the access transistor has negligible impact on training accuracy but significantly increases energy consumption for weight reads/writes. Also, the ferroelectric (FE) polar-axis (PA) orientation beyond 60° causes a sharp drop in training accuracy due to degraded weight update behavior.

title: A Time-Division Multiplexing Dual-Band Self-Powered WuRX for WSNs.
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band architecture, which combines radio-frequency energy harvesting (RFEH) and wake-up receiver (WuRX) for wireless sensor networks (WSNs). By separating the wake-up and energy-harvesting frequency bands, the design eliminates co-channel interference (CCI), improving wake-up sensitivity. To achieve high integration, a frequency-blocking single-balun time-division multiplexing (FB-TDM) is proposed, enabling RFEH and WuRX to share antenna (ANT), matching network (MN), and balun across different frequency bands. Moreover, to address missed detection caused by TDM, discontinuity-tolerant coding and correlator are introduced. The self-powered WuRX is implemented in a 65nm CMOS process. The measurement results show that the chip can harvest RF energy at -35 dBm with a DC output exceeding 0.45V, and supports wake-up reception at -53 dBm with 100 bps data rate, 158.2 ms latency, and an energy cost of 5 nJ per activation.

title: SEP-YOLO: Fourier-Domain Feature Representation for Transparent Object Instance Segmentation.
abstract: Transparent object instance segmentation presents significant challenges in computer vision, due to the inherent properties of transparent objects, including boundary blur, low contrast, and high dependence on background context. Existing methods often fail as they depend on strong appearance cues and clear boundaries. To address these limitations, we propose SEP-YOLO, a novel framework that integrates a dual-domain collaborative mechanism for transparent object instance segmentation. Our method incorporates a Frequency Domain Detail Enhancement Module, which separates and enhances weak high-frequency boundary components via learnable complex weights. We further design a multi-scale spatial refinement stream, which consists of a Content-Aware Alignment Neck and a Multi-scale Gated Refinement Block, to ensure precise feature alignment and boundary localization in deep semantic features. We also provide high-quality instance-level annotations for the Trans10K dataset, filling the critical data gap in transparent object instance segmentation. Extensive experiments on the Trans10K and GVD datasets show that SEP-YOLO achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance.

title: ARIC: A Lightweight Reconfigurable Active Interposer with CPU-Free Configuration.
abstract: As chiplet integration technology advances, efficient design space exploration and reusable interposers have become essential for cost-effective multi-chiplet systems. However, existing approaches lack both efficient algorithmic frameworks for the exponentially expanding design space and lightweight reconfigurable hardware architectures. This paper addresses both challenges with an integrated solution. Algorithmically, we introduce a bipartite graph maximum flow optimization framework that achieves 18.5%–34.2% improvements in EDP/EDA2P for homogeneous systems, as well as 18.4%–51.8% reductions in execution time and up to 49.9× improvements in EDP for heterogeneous accelerators. Architecturally, we present ARIC, a CPU-free reconfigurable active interposer featuring a hybrid toroidal mesh and fat-tree topology, which achieves a bandwidth of 400 GB/s while reducing power consumption by 36% at 0.9 V and requires 16.5× to 53.4× fewer clock cycles for communication compared to state-of-the-art network-on-interposers architectures. The QSPI based configuration enables hot reconfiguration in less than 1ms. Designed and synthesized for 28nm CMOS technology, this approach provides an efficient solution for a variety of workloads in small-batch production.

Visitors will experience two interactive games to explore how the system locates and aligns the Rx.

title: A 3.6 GS/s 7b TI-LU 2b/cycle SAR ADC in 65 nm CMOS with Preamplifier-Level Interpolation and Shared-Reference Background Offset Calibration.
abstract: This paper presents a 3.6 GS/s 7-bit four-channel time-interleaved (TI) loop-unrolled (LU) 2b/cycle SAR ADC in 65 nm CMOS. A preamplifier-interpolated dynamic comparator with a gain-boosted preamplifier resolves three thresholds per 2b cycle using only two preamplifiers and four latches, lowering input loading and kickback. The first REFDAC precharge slot is advanced into the sampling phase, allowing the preamplifiers to compare the sampled residue against ±Vthimmediately after SIGDAC sample-and-hold, which removes idle time and shortens the critical path. A shared-reference background offset calibration equalizes per-path offsets and suppresses TI spurs. On-chip foreground analog calibration corrects inter-channel timing skew, while absolute offset and gain are compensated off-chip. Simulations show 42.58 dB SNDR and 55.65 dB SFDR near Nyquist (1.79956 GHz). The ADC draws 26.95 mW from 1.2 V and achieves Walden and Schreier figures of merit of 68.12 fJ/conv-step (FoMw) and 150.83 dB (FoMs) at Nyquist.

title: Asymmetric Read Transistor Configuration Enabled Low-Power 2T0C CAA-AOSFET Crossbar Array through Sneak Current Suppression.
abstract: The three-dimensional stacked two-transistor capacitor-less (2T0C) memory architecture based on channel-all-around amorphous oxide semiconductor field-effect transistors (CAA-AOSFETs) is a promising candidate to overcome the capacitor scaling bottleneck in future high-density DRAM. Although the decoupled read/write path of the 2T0C cell enables read operations at voltages as low as 0.1 V, its low-power potential in large-scale arrays has not been systematically investigated. This work analyzes sneak current impact on read margin and power in a 2T0C crossbar. Compared to 1T1C DRAM, 2T0C reduces read energy by 50% by eliminating restore and lowering precharge energy, yet sneak current becomes dominant. To address this, we propose and validate an asymmetric read transistor electrode configuration (AsymTEC) to suppress sneak currents at the array level. Measurement results demonstrate that in a 512-cell read bit line (RBL), a read transistor with a 0.2 V bidirectional threshold voltage difference reduces sneak current by over 80%, enabling a 4 ns RBL pull-down time at a 0.7 V read array supply voltage.

title: A 7-bit 1-GS/s Single-Channel Partial Loop-Unrolled SAR ADC Featuring Constant Input Common-Mode for Comparators in 28-nm CMOS.
abstract: This paper presents a high-speed single-channel successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) featuring constant input common-mode for comparators. The proposed ADC employs a partial loop-unrolled (LU) SAR architecture, which reduces half of the number of comparators compared to the traditional fully LU architecture. Specifically, the first four bits are converted using a conventional SAR structure that integrates a bit-dependent capacitive digital-to-analog converter (CDAC) settling technique. The remaining four bits are processed by the LU structure. One redundancy bit is incorporated to relax the requirements of the CDAC settling in the SAR structure. By utilizing an improved set-and-down switching scheme and optimized comparators, the ADC ensures that the input common-mode voltage of comparators remains constant through the whole conversion process. Implemented in a 28nm CMOS process, the ADC occupies a core circuit area of only 0.001 mm2. Post-layout simulation results demonstrate that the SNDR and SFDR are 42.51 dB and 55.94 dB with a Nyquist input, respectively, and that the power consumption is 2.06 mW, leading to a Walden figure-of-merit (FoM) of 18.9 fJ/conversion-step.

title: A Power-Efficient VCO-Based ΔΣ Modulator Achieving 175.5 dB FoMs with an Active Open-loop Integrator and Compensation-Current Linearization.
abstract: This paper presents a power-efficient second-order discrete-time (DT) VCO-based delta-sigma modulator (ΔΣM). The modulator achieves second-order noise shaping by cascading an active open-loop integrator with a VCO-based quantizer. The proposed open-loop integrator provides moderate gain to suppress loop nonlinearities and noise, while offering significantly higher power efficiency than conventional OTA-based closed-loop integrators. The second integration stage is inherently realized by the VCO quantizer, achieving an additional OTA-less noise-shaping order. A compensation-current-based linearization scheme is further introduced to mitigate the dominant third-order nonlinearity in the voltage-to-frequency characteristic of the VCO. The ADC is implemented in a standard 180 nm CMOS process and verified by simulation. It achieves a 91.7 dB peak SNDR over a 24 kHz bandwidth while consuming 102.3 μW, corresponding to a Schreier FoM of 175.5 dB.

title: Approximate Signed Multiplier Designs for Efficient CNN Inference.
abstract: Approximate multipliers have widely been explored in the hardware design of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to improve energy-efficiency. However, most existing designs are unsigned, while signed multipliers often either incur considerable hardware overhead or fail to achieve sufficiently high accuracy for CNN inference. In this work, we devise AM4CNN, a set of approximate 8-bit signed multipliers tailored for CNN inference. Specifically, two new probability-optimized approximate compressors are introduced, which are integrated with partial product truncation and speculation, effectively reducing the hardware cost. In addition, application-driven constant compensation is applied to enhance the accuracy under CNN dataflows. Experimental results in CNN applications demonstrate that the proposed multipliers achieve a favorable trade-off between efficiency and accuracy. Compared with the baseline implementation with exact multiplications, the proposed multiplier achieved 14% energy saving, with less than 0.3% and 2.0% accuracy loss on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, respectively.

title: Resonant Network Optimization and Coupling-Aware Adaptive BPSK Design for High-Speed Inductive Data Links.
abstract: This paper presents the design and optimization of a Class-E-based adaptive binary phase-shift keying (A-BPSK) wireless power and data transmission (WPDT) system operating through a near-field inductive link. The system model incorporates both power transfer and data modulation paths, and the effect of resonant network parameters on phase transition and demodulation is systematically analyzed. A complete design methodology is developed, which for the first time provides a quantitative determination of the RX parallel capacitor CRto balance demodulation stability and transient settling speed. Furthermore, a 20-phase voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO)–based phase-selection scheme is proposed to choose the optimal reference phase for downlink demodulation, thereby enhancing timing alignment and robustness. The proposed optimization achieves stable zero-voltage switching (ZVS) operation and reliable data recovery. Measurement results under 13.56 MHz carrier frequency demonstrate successful demodulation of pseudo-random binary sequences with an averaged data rate of 6.02 Mbps and a bit-error rate below 10−6.

title: A Novel PFM Control Chip with Model-Based Duty Ratio Prediction and vds-Sensed Fine Tuning for Optimal ZVS in VHF Resonant SEPIC Converters.
abstract: This paper proposes a critical duty ratio pulse frequency modulation (CDR-PFM) control IC to achieve optimal zero-voltage-switching (ZVS) in very high frequency (VHF) resonant SEPIC DC-DC converters. To mitigate the power loss–output voltage ripple tradeoff of conventional fixed-duty PFM and ON/OFF control, the proposed controller combines model-based duty ratio prediction with vds-sensed fine tuning to maintain ZVS across switching frequencies. An analytical time-domain model of the VHF SEPIC converter is developed to derive the switching-node voltage vdsat different switching frequencies fs. The zero-crossing point of vdsis used to predict the critical duty ratio for each fs. A duty ratio fine tuning scheme then dynamically adjusts the duty ratio by sensing vdsat the turn-on transition to compensate for prediction errors. The controller was fabricated in the HHGrace 180-nm BCD process and experimentally validated on a 5 V/10 W SEPIC converter with a 28 V input and switching frequency of 12.2–15.38 MHz. Compared with conventional PFM control, the proposed control method reduces power loss by up to 45% (at Po= 5 W), while compared with ON/OFF control, it achieves a maximum reduction in output voltage ripple of 90 mV (at Po= 7.5 W). Experimental results indicate that the controller reliably achieves zero-voltage-switching under various operating conditions, thereby reducing power loss and lowering output voltage ripple.

title: A 16-phase High Frequency Integrated Voltage Regulator with On-chip Current Sensing and Smooth Phase Shedding/Adding.
abstract: This paper presents a 16-phase Integrated Voltage Regulator (IVR) with smooth phase shedding/adding (SPS/A) and on-resistance(Ron) based current sensing. The proposed IVR employs peak current-mode control and utilizes a high speed and lossless current sensing scheme, thereby reducing power consumption and simultaneously minimizing the minimum on time (Ton,min). Furthermore, the proposed IVR incorporates smooth phase shedding/adding which changes the steady-state relationship between the control voltage (VC) and the inductor current (IL) to optimize light-load efficiency and reduce output voltage overshoot/undershoot during phase shedding/adding. The proposed IVR is combined with a transient acceleration circuit , which detects output voltage droop and activates all phases simultaneously. The strategy effectively mitigates the drawback of degraded transient performance inherent to phase shedding/adding operations. In simulation, the proposed IVR achieving 74.2% at full load and 90.8% peak efficiency at 12A load current when 8 phases activated. Under a load current step of 50A/60ns, the simulated maximum output voltage undershoot is 121mV, with a settling time of 350ns.

title: A 50/25/12.5 Gb/s Fast-Settling Burst-Mode Transimpedance Amplifier for 50G-PON.
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable burst-mode (BM) transimpedance amplifier (TIA), supporting triple rates of 50/25/12.5-Gb/s for both symmetrical and asymmetrical 50G-PON. Triple rate bandwidth scaling gain modes are adopted in high-gain (HG) mode while a merged bandwidth gain mode is utilized in low-gain (LG) mode. For rapid settling, a concurrent offset cancellation (OC) scheme is implemented to activate AOC and ROC loops in parallel, eliminating the cumulative delay inherent in sequential loop activation. In HG mode, the TIA achieves simulated gains of 82/85/86 dBΩ with corresponding 3-dB bandwidths of 38/13/7 GHz for 50/25/12.5 Gb/s rate, respectively. Meanwhile, in LG mode, it provides a gain of 61.5 dBΩ while extending the bandwidth to 42 GHz. Finally, the TIA achieves a record burst-mode settling time of 6.5 ns.
