title: A Pipelined NoC-Based Membrane Shortcut SNN Architecture for Low-Latency Spike Sorting.
abstract: Spike sorting, a fundamental process in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), necessitates increasingly high-throughput, low-latency, and energy-efficient computing paradigm. Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have emerged as promising candidates owing to their event-driven and low-power nature. However, the hardware performance of advanced architectures like residual SNNs is severely hindered by a long-standing challenge: the lack of an efficient multi-core communication mechanism for their critical residual connections. To bridge this gap, we propose PMS-NoC, a Pipeline Membrane Shortcut Network-on-Chip architecture that, for the first time, optimizes membrane shortcut SNN data flow on multi-core neuromorphic hardware. We introduce two key strategies: a dual-packet time-division multiplexing strategy that significantly improves pipeline efficiency, reducing spike sorting inference time by 29.37%, and a distributed multi-core pipeline synchronization strategy minimizing parallel computation errors and improving inference accuracy by 11.7%. Our FPGA prototype of PMS-NoC, utilizing a mesh router for compressed 16-bit packets, achieves high throughput of 817.9 K timesteps per second at 3.3 μs latency. This work provides a feasible and efficient hardware framework, paving the way for the deployment of advanced residual SNNs in real-time BCI systems.

title: A 4/8b High-Precision Fully-Parallel In-Sensor Computing Chip with Subthreshold Digital Pixel and Hybrid Pulse Modulation.
abstract: The growing integration of artificial intelligence in edge applications has intensified demands for high-frame-rate, low-power vision sensors, challenging conventional visual systems that separate sensing, computation and storage—an architecture limited by data movement bottlenecks which can be mitigated by sensing with computing. This work introduces a fully parallel convolutional digital pixel sensor (FPC-DPS) architecture employing a subthreshold self-ramped single-slope ADC (S3S-ADC) with self-calibrating current registers. By integrating a global nine-direction propagation PWM (G9DP-PWM) and a relaxation oscillator-based global clock pulse frequency modulation (GC-PFM) strategy, the design seamlessly merges sensing, analog-to-digital conversion, and convolution at pixel level, achieving fully parallel in-sensor computing (ISC). Simulations demonstrate dual-mode operation with 100,000 FPS in imaging mode and 30,000 FPS in convolution mode using 4b signed weights and 8b quantization, attaining 5.74 TOPS/W in energy efficiency and an iFoM of 1.54 pJ/pix•fps, offering an efficient solution for next-generation edge AI visual systems.

title: A 1.8-ns, 45fJ/bit Time-Domain Sensing Scheme with Offset-Cancelled Resistance-to-Time Converter and 10-5 BER for Digital RRAM Compute-in-Memory.
abstract: Resistive random-access memory (RRAM) is emerging as a promising solution for digital compute-in-memory (DCIM) architectures to boost the computational efficiency of edge artificial intelligence (AI), owing to its non-volatility, high density, and CMOS compatibility. However, designing high-speed, energy-efficient, and low bit error rate (BER) readout circuitry for RRAM-based DCIM remains challenging. In this paper, a low-latency and energy efficient time-domain sensing (TDS) scheme is proposed, featuring: 1) resistance-to-time converter (RTC) with offset cancellation and dynamically fixed cell current (Icell) mechanism; 2) reused symmetrically generated reference. The proposed TDS scheme realizes linear resistance-to-time conversion through capacitor coupling, while eliminating DC power consumption, thus eliminating DC power consumption and thereby reducing read latency and energy overhead. The proposed circuit is implemented and pre-simulated on a 1-Mb RRAM DCIM array using a 28 nm technology node, achieving 1.8 ns latency, 45 fJ/bit readout with 10−5BER at an on-off ratio of 1:3.

title: Near-Field Radar Imaging Motion Compensation Solution Based On STFT and PGA.
abstract: With the continuous advancement of Terahertz radar technology, high-resolution, high-definition and real-time Terahertz near-field imaging has emerged as a new research objective. However, due to the radar’s high-speed motion and the accompanying mechanical vibrations, significant motion errors are induced, which in turn substantially deteriorate the imaging quality. Conventional studies often simplify vibration to a sinusoidal model, but this assumption may not fully reflect real-world conditions. This paper proposes a more realistic perturbation model and a motion compensation scheme based on STFT and PGA, which can better address nonlinear problems. Through actual experiments and ablation studies, this paper demonstrates that this method has the advantages of fewer iterations and better imaging quality. Under the same image contrast, the algorithm proposed in this paper only requires 3 iterations. The PSNR of the imaging results of the algorithm proposed in this paper increases by approximately 3 dB.

title: Efficient LoRA-Based Weight Update Write-Back in 3D NAND Flash for Large Language Models.
abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) in non-volatile memory systems faces severe challenges of high latency, limited bandwidth, and restricted endurance. Although the Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) algorithm effectively reduces computational complexity by training only a small subset of parameters, it still requires frequent weight write-backs and the transfer of tens of gigabytes of data during distributed fine-tuning. This paper presents a LoRA-integrated 3D NAND flash architecture that enables efficient in-memory weight update through multi-string parallel programming. The proposed scheme maps LoRA’s low-rank matrices to 3D NAND array operations, allowing only two compact matrices to be transmitted while performing all weight update directly within the flash array. A sub-block array architecture is also proposed to enhance programming parallelism and reduce resistance–capacitance delay. Furthermore, a differential-pair cell structure enables bidirectional weight updating without block erase operation, thereby extending 3D NAND flash lifetime. Simulation results show a 2850× improvement in update efficiency and a 140× extension in memory lifetime compared with conventional full-parameter weight update in 3D NAND flash, achieving scalable, low-latency, and energy-efficient fine-tuning for neuromorphic AI systems.

title: A Power Efficient and Fast Response Cascode FVF LDO Using Voltage Detecting and GB Enhancing Techniques for Cryogenic Quantum Computing.
abstract: This paper presents a low power consumption, high current efficiency and fast response low-dropout voltage regulator (LDO) without external capacitors (capless) working at cryogenic temperature (4K). The flipped-voltage-follower (FVF) structure achieves large bandwidth with low power consumption. The voltage detecting unit provides not only extra current but also low voltage overshoot and undershoot when the load steps. The gain bandwidth (GB) enhancing structure with active inductors is adopted to improve loop bandwidth to realize better transient response. The proposed LDO is fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS process, occupying only 0.0026mm2. Measured results show that the LDO provides a voltage of 0.9V and a quiescent current of 15.1μA achieving current efficiency of 99.94 % and loading 25mA at 4K. It achieves 48mV undershoot and 45mV overshoot with a step of 24.95mA/10ns. The results show that the LDO can power circuits at cryogenic temperature and can be applied to large-scale quantum computers.

title: A Capacitor-Less Current-Feedback LDO with Mismatch Cancellation Using DEM and Chopping for Distributed Power Management.
abstract: This paper presents an output capacitor-less low dropout regulator (LDO) with mismatch cancellation for distributed power management. Compared with the traditional LDO, the proposed LDO has an embedded reference and uses current feedback to alleviate the limited vertical voltage margin. Dynamic element matching (DEM) and chopping techniques are adopted to reduce the mismatch between the current replication and thereby reduce the mismatch in output voltage. The LDO is implemented in a 28-nm CMOS process. Simulation results demonstrate that the quiescent power consumption is 9.6μA when power supply is 0.9V and output voltage is 0.6V. It also has 84.9mV undershoot and 70.5ns recovery time when the load steps from 100μA to 10mA in 50ns. Monte-Carlo simulations of output voltage performed on 1500 samples show that the standard deviation decreased by nearly 25 times with DEM and chopping.

title: A 12-bit 5-MS/s TMR-Free Radiation-Adaptive SAR ADC for Space Missions with 67.55-dB SNDR in 22-nm FD-SOI.
abstract: We present a Triple Modular Redundancy (TMR)-free 12-bit 5 MS/s SAR ADC in 22-nm Fully Depleted Silicon-on-Insulator (FD-SOI) for space missions where radiation levels vary widely. Robustness is engaged on demand by a mode-switchable comparator: dynamic under benign conditions and op-amp-based in harsh radiation, with a cold-redundant replica to limit total-ionizing-dose (TID)-induced drift. Fully synchronous timing bounds single-event effects (SEE) to one conversion. In dynamic mode, the prototype achieves 67.55 dB SNDR and 82.45 dB SFDR at 5 MS/s with a 300 kHz, 97.5% full-scale input, corresponding to a 56.4 fJ/conv-step Walden FoM. Heavy-ion tests at LET≈60 MeV·cm2/mg yield SEE cross sections of 1.6×10−6and 4.0×10−6cm2in op-amp-based and dynamic modes, respectively. The ADC withstands >1 Mrad(Si) without hardened libraries or TMR.

title: First Demonstration of Ternary Logic Circuits in Commercial 180-nm CMOS Technology.
abstract: Ternary logic increases information density and can reduce interconnect and gate count relative to binary designs, yet most demonstrations remain at the simulation stage or depend on emerging devices unsuitable for large-scale implementation. This paper presents, for the first time, ternary (radix-3) logic gates and arithmetic circuits implemented in a commercially available 180-nm CMOS process, covering design methodology, circuit fabrication, and experimental validation. Ternary logic gates are realized using complementary multi-threshold Si transistors, producing three well-defined logic levels with balanced noise margins. Ternary arithmetic modules, including ternary half/full adders, are proposed and realized using cycling-gate–based architectures, which effectively shorten logic depth and reduce transistor count. In addition, ternary D-type flip-flops (DFFs) are implemented to verify sequential operations. Measured results show operating frequencies up to 150 kHz—approximately 100× higher than prior work. These results confirm that ternary logic can be reliably implemented in mainstream CMOS process, establishing a practical platform for scalable ternary logic computing.

title: MMCap: Multi-Level CLIP Feature Fusion with Multiway Dynamic Dense Connections for Urban Incivility Scene Captioning.
abstract: Urban incivility scenes (e.g., littering, vandalism, disorderly parking) pose prominent challenges to urban governance and social civility. Despite remarkable progress in image captioning for natural scene description, current models are insufficient in capturing the semantically complex and socially contextualized urban incivility phenomena. To address this limitation, this study introduces image captioning techniques into civilized urban contexts, aiming to automatically identify and narratively describe incivility scenarios. Building upon our previously developed IncivilityCaps dataset, we propose MMCap, a novel model that integrates multi-level CLIP feature fusion with a multiway dynamic dense connection Transformer. Specifically, MMCap leverages hierarchical CLIP visual features and dynamic dense Transformer connections to strengthen semantic consistency and contextual reasoning across visual and textual modalities. Experimental results on the IncivilityCaps dataset demonstrate that MMCap outperforms mainstream baseline models, achieving significant improvements in both caption fluency and semantic precision. This confirms its ability to generate meaningful urban incivility descriptions, advancing multimodal intelligence for smart cities.

title: Deep Learning-based Public Template Attack against ML-DSA on ARM Microcontrollers.
abstract: The Module-Lattice-based Digital Signature Algorithm (ML-DSA), selected by NIST as the primary post-quantum signature standard, is witnessing rapid global deployment. However, its resilience against practical side-channel analysis (SCA) attacks remains insufficiently understood and evaluated. This paper introduces DL-PTA, a deep learning–based public-template attack that belongs to the non-profiling class. The proposed method employs shallow neural networks to model information leakage directly from raw power traces, eliminating the need for manual Point-of-Interest (PoI) selection. The models are trained on traces whose intermediate values are derived from publicly available signatures, without requiring access to secret keys or dedicated profiling devices, and are then applied to recover sensitive intermediates during target executions. Experimental results on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller demonstrate that the proposed DL-PTA successfully retrieves the full secret key of ML-DSA-44 using only 7,400 power traces, achieving a 50.67% reduction in data complexity (i.e., trace count) compared to previous attacks, while maintaining effectiveness across all three ML-DSA security levels.

title: A Topology-Aware Reinforcement Learning Framework for 2.4-GHz VSWR-Robust Power Amplifier Matching Network Design.
abstract: This paper presents a topology-aware reinforcement learning (TA-RL) framework for the automatic design of a 2.4-GHz VSWR-robust power amplifier (PA). This framework 1) re-models the circuit as a graph-structured environment, where the TA-RL agent learns to adjust output matching network (OMN) topology and component values to maximize efficiency and power stability under load mismatch; 2) begins with a random exploration stage and stores exploration results in an experience buffer to reduce agent learning complexity and accelerate algorithm convergence; 3) injects exploration noise into the training process to avoid local optima, which gradually decays as the agent converges to the optimal policy. Validated in 65 nm CMOS process, the TA-RL-designed PA achieves a peak power-added efficiency (PAE) of 45.7% at 10.3 dBm output power (Pout) and maintains efficiency variation within 7.2% and Poutfluctuation within 1.2 dB at VSWR = 3:1, demonstrating high robustness to VSWR variation. This work represents an AI-designed VSWR-robust PA, reducing the PAE variation from 13.5% to 7.2% compared with conventional designs, thereby validating the effectiveness of the proposed TA-RL framework.

title: MA-RQAOA: A System-Algorithm Co-Design Framework for Coherence-Limited Topological Quantum Computing.
abstract: Topological quantum computing (TQC) with Majorana zero modes (MZMs) promises scalable, fault-tolerant computation, but is severely constrained by finite coherence times (1ms) and costly non-Clifford gates. Standard hybrid algorithms like the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) are hardware-agnostic and often produce physically unrealizable solutions. To address this, we introduce the Majorana-Aware Recursive QAOA (MA-RQAOA), a system-algorithm co-design framework. MA-RQAOA embeds a hardware-aware temporal cost model directly into its classical optimization loop, formulating the task as a constrained variational search. This guarantees that the discovered quantum circuits are executable within the processor's coherence time. Through simulations on Max-Cut problems, we demonstrate that MA-RQAOA consistently identifies high-quality, feasible solutions, significantly outperforming standard approaches that are frequently invalidated by hardware constraints. Our work presents a new paradigm for developing practical quantum algorithms that are deeply integrated with the realities of physical hardware.

title: DNA-HHE: Dual-mode Near-network Accelerator for Hybrid Homomorphic Encryption on the Edge.
abstract: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) schemes (e.g., RNS-CKKS) support Privacy-Preserving Outsourced Computation (PPOC) yet face high computational latency and ciphertext expansion, especially on resource-constrained edge devices. Hybrid Homomorphic Encryption (HHE) alleviates these edge issues by using lightweight symmetric encryption (e.g., Rubato cipher for RNS-CKKS-based HHE) instead of HE for plaintext encryption, but introduces transciphering overhead on the cloud. This trade-off demands a flexible dual-mode solution. This paper presents DNA-HHE, to our knowledge the first dual-mode HHE accelerator with near-network coupling capability for edge devices. DNA-HHE unifies RNS-CKKS and Rubato support, driven by flexible instructions. For compact edge deployment, we propose three key designs: DSP-efficient modular reduction, compact multi-field-adaptive butterfly unit, and Rubato parallel scheduling with high resource sharing. Crucially, DNA-HHE is directly coupled to the NIC, handling network protocol packaging to reduce end-to-end PPOC latency by 1.09× to 1.56×. ASIC and FPGA evaluations show DNA-HHE outperforms state-of-the-art single-mode designs in both latency and area efficiency, while providing this critical dual-mode functionality.

title: A 5.7-mW 9-GHz 8-bit Twin-PI with a Digitally-Controlled Weighted Summer in 28-nm CMOS.
abstract: This paper presents an 8-bit Twin-phase interpolator (PI) implemented in 28-nm CMOS technology for high-speed clock and data recovery. To mitigate the inherent integral nonlinearity (INL) caused by the amplitude variation of the sub-PI, a digitally-controlled weighted summer, consisting of two transconductance amplifiers controlled by a look-up table (LUT), is employed to normalize output amplitudes. The proposed Twin-PI incorporates only two stages of linear amplifiers, thereby exhibiting higher supply noise tolerance and consuming less power than previous designs based on CML-to-CMOS (C2C) converters. Post-layout simulations demonstrate that the 8-bit Twin-PI achieves an INL of 0.95 LSB and a differential nonlinearity (DNL) of 0.80 LSB at TT, 50°C, and 0.9V. The Twin-PI consumes 5.7 mW when operating at 9 GHz.

title: Hierarchical Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Voltage Balancing Control for IPOS-DAB Converters.
abstract: High-performance power modules for AI-oriented power systems must achieve both high efficiency and adaptive voltage balance during multi-channel power transfer. The Input-Parallel Output-Series Dual Active Bridge (IPOS-DAB) converter, with its high voltage gain and modular scalability, has become an ideal candidate for AI power architectures. However, parameter mismatches and dynamic load disturbances can cause output voltage imbalance, leading to reduced system stability and efficiency. To address this issue, this paper proposes a voltage balancing control strategy based on Hierarchical Super-Twisting Sliding Mode (HSTSM). By introducing a hierarchical sliding-mode framework, the proposed method realizes coordinated voltage regulation among multiple modules and rapid suppression of external disturbances, thereby enhancing dynamic performance and robustness for intelligent energy regulation. Experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed strategy in maintaining voltage balance and improving transient response, demonstrating its potential for intelligent and adaptive power management in AI-oriented power and energy systems.

title: The similarity interaction mechanism optimizes multi-agents with reactive strategies*.
abstract: In complex engineering and social systems such as power grids, transportation networks, and financial systems, cooperation and coordination among multi-agents has become increasingly widespread. In these systems, agents sharing similar characteristics are more likely to cluster and form cooperative patterns, indicating that similarity plays a crucial role in the evolution of cooperation and the emergence of collective intelligence. To capture this mechanism, we investigate the evolution of reactive strategies based on the repeated prisoner’s dilemma game, and construct the dynamic interaction network through the similarity of agents, where interactions occur when the strategic distance of both agents falls within their tolerance thresholds for similarity. Our results demonstrate that cooperative strategies can be effectively favored and sustained under this similarity-driven interaction mechanism, leading to improved population-level outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of similarity-based interactions in preserving cooperation and provide new insights into the underlying mechanisms that govern cooperative behavior within complex systems.

title: DiffPCGC: Efficient Point Cloud Geometry Compression via Diffusion Models.
abstract: The rapid development of 3D data processing necessitates efficient point cloud compression techniques. Although existing learning-based point cloud geometry compression methods have achieved certain milestones in compression efficiency, they are limited by the autoencoder architecture and struggle to maintain high point cloud reconstruction quality while achieving extreme compression ratios. To address the issues, this study innovatively designs a new framework that utilizes diffusion models for point cloud geometry compression, namely DiffPCGC. We introduce the latent representation that encodes the intrinsic information of the original point cloud and employ reverse diffusion in the decoder to generate the reconstructed point cloud. Additionally, to further restore the geometric structure of the point cloud, we extract textual semantic information from projection views of the original point cloud to assist in the generation of the reconstructed point cloud. Experimental performance validates the effectiveness of our method. Compared to the existing state-of-the-art methods, our framework shows an average performance gain of 58% on D1-PSNR metric.

title: A Unified Function Processor with Integer Arithmetic Based on Piecewise Chebyshev Polynomial Approximation.
abstract: Nonlinear functions are fundamental components in widely applied AI algorithms. However, their hardware implementation presents a major challenge due to the diversity of function types and the full precision requirement (e.g., FP32), which results in significant area and energy overheads. To overcome these issues, we present a Unified Function Processor (UFP) with integer arithmetic, capable of efficiently computing a wide range of nonlinear functions with high accuracy under integer constraints. First, we propose a dynamic programming segmentation algorithm within a third-degree Chebyshev polynomial framework that optimally partitions each function into eight integer-aligned segments to minimize global quantization error. Second, a unified three-stage pipelined hardware with computation element reuse is proposed. Implemented in TSMC 28-nm HPC technology and working at 1GHz, the proposed UFP achieves up to 93.6% reductions in area compared to the state-of-the-art works, with a 79% lower energy consumption. The architecture flexibly supports all mainstream functions in AI algorithms with configurable precision and range, offering a compact and scalable solution for AI acceleration hardware.

title: A 28nm 56.45TOPS/W Hardware-software Co-optimized Sparse Accelerator for Traditional DNNs and Transformer-based LLMs.
abstract: This paper presents a 28-nm hardware-software co-optimized sparse accelerator for traditional deep neural networks and Transformer-based large language models, featuring a balanced encoding algorithm for workload balancing, a unified hybrid precision multiplier and accumulation architecture for matrix multiplication, and a parallel Computing-Fetch scheduling strategy for efficient computing. The chip operates at frequencies ranging from 100 MHz to 700 MHz and voltages between 0.75 V and 1.1 V, achieving a peak energy efficiency of 56.45 TOPS/W and a peak area efficiency of 0.85 TOPS/mm2 under 4-bit integer precision. Compared to state-of-the-art accelerators, our design achieves a 2.59×-3.56× improvement in energy efficiency and a 3.54×-5.05× improvement in area efficiency.

title: A Low-Error Approximate Logarithmic Multiplier with Symmetric LUT for Efficient DNN Training.
abstract: Training deep neural networks (DNNs) incurs high computational and energy costs. Approximate computing can lower these costs by reducing arithmetic precision, but existing approximate logarithmic multipliers introduce large errors that disturb convergence. In this work, we propose SyALM, a low-error approximate logarithmic multiplier with a compact correction look-up table (LUT) designed for efficient DNN training. SyALM refines the Mitchell approximation with a two-dimensional symmetric LUT that is calibrated to the empirical distributions of weights and activations. Simulations show a mean relative error of 0.49% across FP32, BF16, and FP16 formats. End-to-end experiments on Vision Transformers and BERT confirm that SyALM can achieve near lossless training while maintaining convergence and accuracy of the final model. Synthesis results demonstrate that, the proposed design achieves 89.1% dynamic power reduction and 82.0% area reduction compared with a Wallace-tree FP32 multiplier.

title: Unity-EDR: A Hybrid Neural-Mesh Rendering System for Efficient Visual Synthesis.
abstract: Neural rendering delivers photorealistic visual quality but remains computationally prohibitive for interactive applications. To overcome this bottleneck, we propose a real-time neural–raster fusion system that integrates neural and mesh-based rendering for efficient visual synthesis. The architecture adopts a screen-aligned fusion strategy that shares an optical center and field-of-view, enabling direct alpha blending of RGBA frames without incurring depth exchange, calibration, or warping overhead. A lightweight, multi-threaded server utility enables asynchronous communication with a neural rendering coprocessor named EDR-NR, effectively decoupling hardware rendering from the Unity host. In addition, an efficient ray-marched shadow casting method leverages the EDR-NR’s native hierarchical fine grid data structure for real-time soft-shadow approximation. Evaluation results demonstrate the system’s efficiency and seamless compatibility with standard rendering pipelines. The quad-core EDR-NR prototype implemented on an FPGA board, integrated with Unity, achieves over 200 frames per second (FPS) on the chair dataset within a mesh-based scene, demonstrating that practical, high-speed neural rendering on edge platforms is fully achievable within a commercial game engine environment.

title: A High-Precision CORDIC Architecture with Reduced-Convergence Preprocessing and Dynamic Logarithmic Bit-Width Scaling.
abstract: This paper presents a parameter-programmable coordinate rotation digital computer (CORDIC) architecture featuring dynamic logarithmic bit-width scaling (D-LBS) and a lightweight coarse-alignment preprocessing scheme, enabling full-range input support with with accumulated truncation error bounded by 0.5 LSB (least significant bit) . The key innovation lies in establishing a mathematical relationship between iteration indices and bit-width truncation via conditional right-shift operations, which suppresses quantization error accumulation and guarantees an average absolute error below 0.5 LSB. By redefining the initial micro-rotation and tightening the effective convergence range, the proposed preprocessing stage maps arbitrary input angles into the reduced convergence range using only simple region-aware logic. Implemented on an Artix-7 XC7A100TCSG324 FPGA, the design achieves a peak operating frequency of 461 MHz. At 32-bit precision, it delivers an order of magnitude lower average relative error (10−6versus 10−5) in circular mode compared to state-of-the-art parameterized CORDICs, with a 1.52× higher operating frequency. The architecture’s parameter programmability enables flexible accuracy–resource trade-offs at design time, making it particularly suitable for high-precision, low-cost FPGA-based signal processing systems.

title: FlexEdge: A Hardware-Software Co-Design for Flexible Edge Transformer Inference.
abstract: Transformers have become foundational for various applications, driving the demand for efficient inference on edge devices. Although numerous dedicated accelerators have been proposed, they struggle to keep pace with the rapid evolution of Transformer variants, primarily due to inflexible dataflows and ineffective computation-memory overlap. To address these limitations, we present FlexEdge, a hardware-software co-design framework for efficient Transformer inferences. FlexEdge hardware incorporates an accelerator with a concurrent execution pipeline that effectively overlaps computation and memory access. Complementing the hardware, the FlexEdge software stack introduces an automated dataflow optimization method, along with an analytical performance model tailored to the accelerator. Extensive evaluations across a wide range of Transformer models demonstrate that FlexEdge achieves high hardware utilization of 88.03% on average, as well as a superior area efficiency of 640 GOPS/mm2compared to state-of-the-art accelerators.

title: An Ultra-Low Quiescent Current Step-down DC-DC Converter for Heavy Load Automotive Applications.
abstract: DC-DC converters are broadly used in automotive systems where specifications such as quiescent current (IQ), efficiency, electromagnetic interference (EMI) and so forth are critical for system performance. In this work, we propose a peak current mode (PCM) DC-DC converter that combines low EMI performance together with ultra-low IQin light load conditions. An innovative frequency modulation method based on a voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) using the output of the error amplifier is proposed to achieve smooth transition from pulse-width modulation in heavy load with fixed switching frequency to pulse-frequency modulation in light load. A green mode control architecture is introduced to shutdown most of the active circuits so that minimal IQis required to maintain regulation when load is light to prolong battery life. The converter was designed and fabricated on a 180-nm BCD process with 4.4 mm2die area and flip-chip copper pillar package is employed to further reduce the EMI noise. The fabricated chip supports load current up to 10A and consumes as low as 3.8μA IQunder no load conditions, making it suitable for automotive applications.

title: An Artifact-Suppressing Neural Stimulator Using Differential Push-Pull Architecture.
abstract: This paper presents a neural stimulator that suppresses stimulus artifacts for closed-loop brain-machine interfaces. The proposed differential push-pull architecture leverages dual stimulation sources to realize artifacts cancellation at the recording site. Fabricated in a 180nm BCD process, the chip integrates timing logic, current-steering digital-to-analog converters, and high-voltage drivers— enabling the stimulator to achieve a voltage compliance of 20 V. Simulation results show the design can reduce the peak-to-peak artifact voltage from 1.2 V to 180 mV, which equals to 85% suppression. This enables robust simultaneous stimulation and recording.

title: EdgeFER: A Structure-Guided and Hardware-Friendly Framework for Dynamic Facial Expression Recognition.
abstract: Dynamic Facial Expression Recognition (DFER) is pivotal for human-computer interaction, yet state-of-the-art models, typically based on 3D CNNs or Transformers, are computationally prohibitive for resource-constrained edge devices. This creates a substantial performance gap, as existing lightweight alternatives often sacrifice the capacity to model complex temporal dynamics and lack robustness to in-the-wild variations such as pose changes and occlusions. To bridge this gap, we propose EdgeFER, a novel, lightweight framework designed to achieve an optimal balance between accuracy and on-device efficiency. EdgeFER introduces a decoupled spatio-temporal architecture: an efficient 2D CNN extracts spatial features, while a dynamic Temporal Attention Module (TAM) models temporal dependencies at a low computational cost. To enhance robustness, we introduce the Structure Guidance Module (SGM), which employs a micro-Graph Convolutional Network on facial landmarks to inject geometric priors and adaptively recalibrate spatial features with minimal overhead. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EdgeFER is over an order of magnitude more compact than existing models while achieving competitive accuracy. Deployed on an NVIDIA Jetson platform, it achieves over 35 FPS, proving its viability for real-time edge applications.

title: FPPS: An FPGA-Based Point Cloud Processing System.
abstract: Point cloud processing is a computational bottleneck in autonomous driving systems, especially for real-time applications, while energy efficiency remains a critical system constraint. This work presents FPPS, an FPGA-accelerated point cloud processing system designed to optimize the iterative closest point (ICP) algorithm, a classic cornerstone of 3D localization and perception pipelines. Evaluated on the widely used KITTI benchmark dataset, the proposed system achieves up to 35$\times$ (and a runtime-weighted average of 15.95x) speedup over a state-of-the-art CPU baseline while maintaining equivalent registration accuracy. Notably, the design improves average power efficiency by 8.58x, offering a compelling balance between performance and energy consumption. These results position FPPS as a viable solution for resource-constrained embedded autonomous platforms where both latency and power are key design priorities.

title: Energy-Efficient Acceleration of Fourier-based Transformers on RRAM-CIM via Mixed-Precision and DFT Symmetry.
abstract: The computational demands of modern Transformers pose a significant challenge to their energy-efficient deployment on edge devices. While RRAM-based computing in-memory (CIM) architectures alleviates the data movement bottleneck, the dynamic nature of the self-attention mechanisms limits RRAM’s efficiency and endurance. This work proposes a software-hardware co-design framework for the Fourier-based Transformer (FNet), which replaces attention with hardware-friendly Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) operations. Our framework introduces two key optimizations: First, guided by a sensitivity analysis that reveals DFT modules are more susceptible to quantization than feed-forward networks, we employ a mixed-precision strategy augmented with hardware-aware finetuning to maintain high accuracy. Second, we propose a novel symmetric DFT mapping strategy that exploits the matrix’s inherent conjugate symmetry, reducing DFT-related RRAM storage and computation by nearly 50%. Evaluated on the GLUE benchmarks, our framework achieves accuracy comparable to 8-bit implementations while reducing power consumption by 2.96x. Critically, compared to state-of-the-art RRAM-based Transformer accelerators, our design demonstrates a 6.1x to 25.1x improvement in energy efficiency.

title: FPGA-Accelerated Real-Time Image Reconstruction For CMOS Electrochemical Sensing Arrays.
abstract: This paper presents a real-time, high-speed decompression and image reconstruction platform for Ion-Sensitive Field-Effect Transistor (ISFET) arrays, implemented on FPGA. The system leverages compressed sensing (CS) principles and employs an Iterative Hard Thresholding (IHT) algorithm to reconstruct ISFET images from highly compressed measurements in real time. The hardware implementation reconstructs a 32×32 ISFET image from a compressed signal with a compression ratio of 4:1, achieving a peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of up to 27.49 dB. The reconstruction latency from the compressed signal input buffer to the output image buffer is 870 μs. The FPGA-based platform integrates a real-time readout and control interface for the ISFET array, along with a user-friendly visualisation interface that displays the reconstructed images dynamically. The platform constitutes a portable and energy-efficient solution for the ISFET System-on-Chip (SoC) enhanced with compressed sensing. It enables configurable image processing parameters to accommodate a range of image sensing applications.

title: A Background Calibration Technique in Rotary Travelling Wave Oscillator Based All-Digital PLL.
abstract: This paper proposes a technique to calibrate the nonlinearities in the Rotary Travelling Wave Oscillator (RTWO) based All-Digital PLL which leads to periodic errors (also known as spurious tones). The calibration technique is based on a mean adaptation algorithm that features a self-learning capability. An ADPLL with proposed calibration circuitry is designed and simulated in a TSMC 65 nm CMOS process. The 64-phase embedded PDC achieves a 2π/128 phase resolution in sampling a pseudo-differential RTWO DCO core running at 6.5 GHz. It is verified that most spurious tones are removed, and the worst spur is reduced by more than 18% (or 10 dB) to 76.9 dBc. After calibration, the in-band phase noise and RMS jitter of ADPLL achieves -117 dBc/Hz and 89.4 fs, respectively.

title: Screen-Shooting Resilient Watermarking Based on Perceptual Mask-Guided Embedding and Feature-Segmentation Decoding.
abstract: This paper proposes a novel deep learning-based screen-shooting resilient watermarking scheme designed to address the challenge of balancing robustness and imperceptibility in existing methods. We designed a perception-mask-guided encoder that directs watermark embedding into texture-rich regions and performs feature reconstruction on the stitched results to achieve deep fusion. The decoder decomposes decoded features into semantic and spatial paths, enabling collaborative compensation of semantic and spatial information to effectively separate the watermark from noise. Experiments demonstrate that this approach achieves outstanding extraction accuracy and visual concealment across various shooting distances and angles, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods. It provides effective technical support for screen content security and copyright protection.

title: A Low-complex and Dual-SPSA Digital Predistortion for MIMO Transmitters with Crosstalk.
abstract: In this article, two aspects on achieving an effective and low-complex digital predistortion (DPD) are introduced to satisfy the compensation requirements for MIMO transmitters with crosstalk. Firstly, a dual-loop architecture with coarse extraction and fine tuning for crossover and crosstalk canceling DPD is proposed to effectively compensate for the crosstalk and power amplifiers nonlinearity. Secondly, a low-complex simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation (SPSA) algorithm in both dual loops is also adopted to mitigate the computational complexity significantly. Our simulation results demonstrate that these two improvements successfully lessen the complexity and improve the DPD linearization performance.

title: CIMA: An Energy-Efficient In-Memory Accelerator Architecture based on Non-Volatile Capacitive Crossbar Array for Random Forest Inference.
abstract: The inference phase of random forest models becomes increasingly time-consuming and energy-intensive as the scale of the problem grows. However, implementing the random forest model on traditional von Neumann architecture presents significant challenges due to the complex structure of decision trees. In this work, a capacitive-based in-memory accelerator (CIMA) is proposed to accelerate random forest inference. Non-leaf nodes are mapped to a 32×32 capacitive crossbar array. Meanwhile, the branch processing elements and the maximum voltage hold circuit are designed to identify the best matching branch, outputting a one-hot code. Additionally, the decision trees are divided into subtrees to enhance the efficiency of storage resource utilization. Test and simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves an average 96× throughput improvement and 212× power reduction compared to state-of-the-art CPU-based methods.

title: A 0.1-1kbps, 9.4pJ/bit, Wake-Up Receiver with No-Standby-Clock and Level-Crossing Comparator.
abstract: This work presents a clock-less envelope detector first (ED-first) wake-up receiver (WuRX) with clock recovery (CR) and a level-crossing (LC) comparator, eliminating the always-on clock generator. This design achieves reduced standby power, flexible data rates, smaller area and fast data alignment. Fabricated in 65nm CMOS, the WuRX supports data rates of 100bps-1kbps with sensitivities up to -74dBm, 8.8MHz bandwidth and 23.2nW peak power. With over 50% standby power reduction, it demonstrates high energy efficiency for low-data-rate applications.

title: DDTST-Encoder: A Novel Dual-Domain Time-Series Transformer Encoder for Analog Circuit Fault Diagnosis.
abstract: This article presents a novel transformer-based framework for complex analog circuit fault diagnosis. As the time series obtained from circuit is rich in time-frequency information that comprehensively reflects circuit states, a dual-domain time-series transformer encoder (DDTST-Encoder) is proposed. The DDTST-Encoder is specially designed to learn discriminative features from such time series through time and frequency domain information fusion. The proposed encoder employs a dual-domain time-series embedding module to generate time domain and frequency domain matrices. In addition, a well-designed time-frequency joint attention (TFJA) mechanism is employed in our encoder to realize dual-domain information fusion. Due to the convincing capability of our encoder, a simple classifier is followed for fault classification. On the complex benchmark leapfrog filter circuit, the proposed method achieves a diagnostic accuracy of 0.9724, significantly outperforming other diagnosis methods.

title: SCASN: Sparse Cross-Attention Self-supervised Network for Endoscopic Surgical Video Desmoking.
abstract: Surgical smoke significantly impairs the visual quality of endoscopic videos, thus compromising intraoperative visibility and surgical safety. Despite recent advances, existing methods remain limited in addressing the dynamic and spatially non-uniform characteristics of surgical smoke. In this paper, we propose SCASN, a Sparse Cross-Attention Self-supervised Network for surgical video desmoking. Our method utilizes the pre-smoke (PS) frame as unaligned supervision, enabling the network to learn without paired annotations. We further incorporate a novel Sparse Cross-Attention Transformer Block (SCATB) to preserve structural details of tissues and generate visually faithful results. To facilitate evaluation, we introduce MegaClear, a surgical video desmoking dataset covering various procedures. Experiments reveal that SCASN surpasses current methods in both quantitative metrics and visual quality, particularly in dense and dynamic smoke environments.

title: A BEOL Ferroelectric FET-based Computing Unit for Digital Computing-in-Memory.
abstract: Ferroelectric FETs (FeFETs) based on BEOL metal-ferroelectric-metal (MFM) capacitors exhibit a large memory window, high write endurance, and strong process compatibility. They not only serve as a promising candidate for embedded non-volatile memory but also provide a competent platform for developing computing-in-memory (CIM) chips. While prior works have extensively investigated the memory properties of MFM-FeFETs and their analog CIM applications, their use in digital CIM (DCIM) remains relatively underexplored. In this work, n-type MFM-FeFET devices are experimentally characterized for model calibration. Building on these results, we propose lookup-table (LUT)-based computing units for DCIM using MFM-FeFETs. A design guideline for circuit-device co-design is introduced to balance trade-offs among signal margin, readout yield, and area efficiency.

title: A Time-Efficient 2D Numerical Compact Model for Dynamic Vascular Monitoring in Functional Near Infrared Spectroscopy Systems.
abstract: The small size, portability and non invasive features of functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) system position it as one of the outstanding candidates for continuous and dynamic measurement of vascular parameters, therefore enabling blood pressure (BP) monitoring. However, the nonlinearity of optical quantities collected by multiple channels from fNIRS systems makes it difficult to convert real-time data to vascular parameters (radius and depth) efficiently. This paper proposes a numerical compact model featuring a forward/inverse fast lookup table (FLUT) and a depth-adaptive calibration scheme for source-detector (S-D) channel activation. Sensitivity analysis and optimization on finite element (FEM) simulation dataset is employed to aid the method. Simulation results demonstrate its outstanding performance with 0.6 ms single inverse operation time, 0.005 mm vascular radius resolution and a 49.8 dB dynamic SNR. Compared with the full-channel model, vascular radius reconstruction time is saved by 98%. The proposed solution provides a promising platform for continuous, real-time vascular monitoring in dedicated fNIRS applications.

title: A Low Power Current Sensor with 84.6dB SNR for Battery Management System.
abstract: A low-power, low-offset sigma–delta modulator (ΣΔM) based current sensor for battery management systems (BMS) is presented in this work. The impact of offset and low-frequency noise of OTA on ΣΔM performance is analyzed, motivating the adoption of multi-level chopping techniques for precision enhancement. An integrated amplifier-chopping circuit is embedded within the OTA to suppress DC offset and 1/f noise, while an additional system-level chopping scheme further minimizes residual offset and enhances overall accuracy. The modulator employs a third-order feedforward architecture to achieve higher resolution than conventional second-order designs. Fabricated using a 0.18-μm BCD process, the prototype achieves a peak signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 84.6 dB with a total power consumption of only 130 μA, demonstrating its effectiveness for high-precision, low-power current sensing in BMS applications.

title: A High-Performance Dual-Issue RISC-V Core Addressing Data Hazard for IoT.
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel dual-issue RISC-V core for Internet of Things (IoT). The RISC-V core adopts the dual arithmetic logic units (ALU) selected bypass method proposed effectively improves performance by supporting single-cycle parallel execution of certain arithmetic instructions with the data hazards. The results of the physical design of the core using commercial tools show that the core can achieve a frequency of 1587 MHz, an area of 0.045 mm2, and a dynamic power consumption of 42.7 µW/MHz in a 28 nm CMOS process. Compared with the baseline version, the proposed core achieves a performance improvement of 10.7% in Coremark/Mhz. The Coremark and Dhrystone benchmark scores of the core are 4.32 Coremark/MHz and 2.67 DMIPS/MHz, respectively, which are 24.5% and 32.2% higher than the ARM Cortex-R5. The micro-architecture core implemented can achieve up to 56% improvement compared to the many existing state-of-the-art commercial and RISC-V cores for IoT system.

title: Sensitivity Analysis of Process Variables for Large-Scale Circuits based on Graph Attention Networks.
abstract: Process variations in advanced semiconductor technologies pose significant challenges to circuit reliability and yield, making process-variable sensitivity analysis (SA) essential. However, traditional SA methods suffer from prohibitive computational costs or insufficient accuracy, especially for large-scale circuits. In this paper, we propose a novel and scalable process-variable SA framework based on Graph Attention Network (GAT). Our key idea is to convert the circuit into a graph and train a GAT-based model to learn the complex, nonlinear mapping between process variables and circuit performance. To further enhance the scalability of our method, we introduce virtual nodes into the graph based on circuit hierarchy to improve interaction between long-range nodes in large-scale circuits. Sensitivities can be calculated using the gradient of the model’s output with respect to its inputs. Experiments on an 8-bit population counter and a 4-word-2-bit SRAM array demonstrate that our proposed method is effective in identifying critical process variables.

title: Dual-Hilbert Scan for Efficient Video-Based Gaussian Splatting Compression.
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables real-time, high-fidelity rendering, but its large data volume poses challenges for storage and transmission. Compressing 3DGS with video codecs is promising, yet its effectiveness critically depends on the 3D-to-2D mapping. Existing approaches face a trade-off: simple scans are fast but yield poor rate-distortion (RD) performance, while optimization-based methods improve RD at a high computational cost We propose a Dual-Hilbert scan algorithm that first sorts Gaussians along a 3D Hilbert curve to preserve spatial locality, then maps them onto 2D grids via a 2D Hilbert curve, producing spatially coherent, block-like layouts suitable for video compression. A parallel implementation accelerates Hilbert code generation, making the approach practical for large-scale 3DGS. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves RD performance comparable to state-of-the-art PLAS while being over 500× faster, effectively breaking the performance-complexity trade-off and enabling efficient video-based 3DGS compression.

title: CircuitS2L: Circuit Dataset Augmentation via Generative Featuring and Supervised Labeling.
abstract: Learning-based techniques are increasingly integrated into electronic design automation (EDA) tool to accelerate and improve the design process. Yet, their success depends on large, diverse circuit datasets, which are scarce due to strict data privacy and confidentiality in the semiconductor industry. To address this challenge, we propose CircuitS2L, a data augmentation framework that enables task-aware generative feature augmentation for both tabular and graph-structured circuit data, producing richer and more diverse representations. CircuitS2L also introduces a supervised label generation strategy that remains robust under limited data by training in an interpretable and task-consistent manner. This ensures that the generated features and labels align with representative downstream EDA tasks, enhancing model performance and generalizability. Evaluations across multiple downstream prediction tasks show that CircuitS2L-augmented data significantly improves prediction results, achieving up to 64% MAE reduction compared to real data alone in LLM-based downstream tasks.

title: A Configurable Energy-Efficient Dual-Mode Accelerator for DNN and SNN.
abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have achieved remarkable success in various applications but incur high power consumption due to intensive multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations. Inspired by biological neurons, spiking neural networks (SNNs) provide an energy-efficient alternative through sparse, event-driven computation. Although dedicated SNN accelerators demonstrate superior energy efficiency, they still lag behind DNNs in accuracy and computational performance. Notably, since the MAC operations in DNNs are highly similar to the synaptic integration in SNNs, a unified accelerator can efficiently support both types of networks with minimal additional hardware overhead. Motivated by this observation, this work proposed a configurable dual-mode accelerator built on a unified weight-stationary systolic array that efficiently supports both DNNs and SNNs by performing dense and spike matrix vector multiplication (GEMV) and matrix matrix matrix multiplication (GEMM) operations, maximizing hardware reuse. Implemented in TSMC 28 nm CMOS technology at a frequency of 500 MHz, the accelerator achieves energy efficiencies of 9.75 TOPS/W and 9.75 TSOPS/W for DNN and SNN workloads, respectively. Compared with existing accelerators, this corresponds to 1.9× and 2.7× the energy efficiency of previous DNN and SNN designs.

title: Energy-Efficiency Monitoring and Parallel Fault Protection BMIC for Battery Management.
abstract: This paper presents a battery-pack monitoring and protection IC (BMIC) that achieves low power consumption and high detection accuracy for battery management systems (BMS). Conventional designs suffer from sensing latency and offset accumulation, motivating a dual-path high-voltage multiplexer with an auxiliary drive structure that ensures switch cascadability and sampling precision under disordered power-up conditions. A parallel-synchronous architecture is further proposed, enabling cooperative voltage acquisition and protection decision-making through time-division multiplexed control. The BMIC supports monitoring and protection for 16 series-connected cells, featuring configurable overvoltage, undervoltage, and overcurrent protection. Fabricated in 180-nm BCD, the prototype achieves a detection error below 5 mV and operates at 294 μA, demonstrating its effectiveness for low-power, high-reliability BMS applications.

title: A Constant-Loss 6.78-MHz Wireless Power Transfer System with Hybrid Class-ED Power Amplifier for D2D Fast Charging.
abstract: This paper proposes a constant-loss (CL) wireless power transfer (WPT) system operating at 6.78 MHz for device-to-device(D2D) wireless charging applications, designed to maximize the available charging rate by fully utilizing the system’s physical thermal design. The system adopts a Series– Series (SS) compensation topology for its load-independent characteristics and a hybrid Class-ED power stage to achieve a high power rating with a low supply voltage. By monitoring both the input and output power and employing a closed-loop feedback control scheme, constant-loss charging can be maintained throughout the entire charging process. The proposed design is validated through simulation results of a wireless battery charger. The proposed CL charging scheme effectively exploits the allowable power dissipation, thereby approaching the theoretical maximum charging rate.

title: Power Delivery for Cryogenic Scalable Quantum Applications: Challenges and Opportunities.
abstract: Quantum technologies offer unprecedented capabilities in computation and secure information transfer. Their implementation requires qubits to operate at cryogenic temperatures (CT) while control and readout electronics typically still remains at room temperature (RT). As systems scale to millions of qubits, the electronics should also operate at CT to avoid a wiring bottleneck. However, wired power transfer from RT for such electronics introduces severe challenges, including thermal load between cooling stages, Joule heating, noise coupling, and wiring scalability. This paper addresses those challenges by evaluating several candidate architectures for scalable power transfer in the dilution frige: high-voltage (HV) wired power transfer, radiative wireless transfer, non-radiative wireless transfer, and a hybrid HV and non-radiative transfer. These architectures are analyzed in terms of thermal load, power loss, heating, coupling noise, power density, scalability, reliability, and complexity. Comparative analysis demonstrates the trade-offs among these architectures, while highlighting HV non-radiative transfer as a promising candidate for scalable quantum systems.

title: Horizontal-Parallel ADC-less Sparsity-Clock-Aware RRAM CIM Macro for edge AI devices.
abstract: The MAC operations essential to DNNs face significant memory wall challenges, motivating the development of Compute-in-Memory (CIM) as a promising solution. RRAM, being an emerging non-volatile memory technology, is well-suited for CIM implementations. However, existing RRAM-based CIM architectures suffer from two main limitations: (1) sensing margin (SM) degradation caused by simultaneously activating multiple vertical columns, along with the power and area overhead associated with ADCs; (2) degradation in inference accuracy under coarse-grained sparsity, and excessive control circuit costs for fine-grained sparsity handling. To address these issues, this paper presents a Horizontal-Parallel ADC-less Sparsity-Clock-Aware RRAM CIM Macro for edge AI devices. The design incorporates HPACM to enhance SM while eliminating ADCs, and employs SCAFA (Sparsity-Clock-Aware Fine-grained Architecture) to achieve full data-path fine-grained sparsity detection with minimal circuit and power overhead. Designed under 55nm CMOS technology, the macro achieves an energy efficiency of 7.37 TOPS/W@8b/8b and a peak throughput of 3.3 GOPS with a 92.25% inference accuracy.

title: Thermal-Aware 3D-IC Floorplan Based On TSV-Coordination Simulated Annealing.
abstract: With the development of high-performance circuit systems, a surge in functional modules increases wirelength and chip temperature, degrading system performance. 3D integrated circuits (3D-IC) reduce overall area and total wirelength via vertical stacking and through-silicon vias (TSV), but their design suffers from more TSVs, longer wirelength and higher temperature due to heterogeneous integration. In this paper, we propose a three-stage optimization strategy based on simulated annealing (SA): layer assignment prioritizes minimizing cross-layer TSV number; intra-layer optimization sequentially optimizes module and TSV positions; thermal optimization introduces a 3D thermal clustering index to optimize overall system temperature. Experiments on the GSRC benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can significantly reduce the number of TSVs by 4%~33% and wirelength by 1%~12%, while achieving temperature performance comparable to advanced methods.

title: TLMALS: Tiny Language-Model Enhanced ALS via Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Approximate computing is crucial for designing energy- and area-efficient hardware, yet existing methods often lack generality and global optimization capability. To overcome these limitations, we propose TLMALS-Tiny Language-Model Enhanced Approximate Logic Synthesis (ALS) via Reinforcement Learning. TLMALS represents circuits as textual sequences and employs a pretrained language model as the agent, transforming logic approximation into a language-understandable task and enabling semantic knowledge transfer from natural language to EDA. We design a bespoke tokenizer for circuit language and seamlessly embed the graph structure into the textual representation, breaking the long-standing barrier of fixed-node graphs that struggle with dynamic-node tasks. Reinforcement learning facilitates efficient exploration of approximation spaces beyond local optima. To address the weak interpretability issue of general approximate methods, a method-decoupled compensation mechanism adapts flexibly to error scenarios and restores accuracy. Experiments show that TLMALS reduces circuit area by 45.9% on average under 5% error rate.

title: A Challenge-Based-Learning System to Improve Education in Circuit and System Design.
abstract: In this paper, we present a challenge-based learning (CBL) system for education in circuit and system design. Within this system teachers implement circuit design challenges. Learners provide their own circuits as solutions. These solutions are automatically tested by the system using a test bench provided by the teacher. The test bench performs automatic measurements and derives scores based on test cases. We accumulate these scores e.g. in a figure of merit (FOM) and display them on a high score list to compare different learners’ solutions. In this way, we provide direct feedback, and engage and motivate learners in a competitive context. We implement the system using three main blocks: A Python application programming interface (API) to simulate the test benches using LTspice, a website as a user interface (UI) for teachers and learners and a database to store simulation files and data. We show, how to use the system on a circuit design example, and discuss various areas of application.
